highlights: chance to learn about Vietnam's history
pay respect to a revered leader

author: F M
title: Great Vietnam History
original_content: The grounds are large and well maintained and entry through security was pretty quick despite the number of people (went around 11am). Because of the size of the grounds, you never feel crowded. Read up  on the history of the mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh beforehand if you aren't going with a tour guide who can give you the info.
highlights: grounds are large and well maintained
entry through security was pretty quick
practical_tips: Read up on the history of the mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh beforehand

author: Niko
title: A long wait for a disappointing glimpse
original_content: The line to see Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum was ridiculously long, and the viewing itself was a quick, underwhelming experience. We felt rushed and couldn't appreciate the historical significance. There are better ways to learn about Vietnam's past.

author: Otto
title: A respectful visit
original_content: We paid our respects at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. The somber atmosphere reminded us of Vietnam's historic struggles. A place to learn and appreciate the sacrifices made for Vietnamese independence.
highlights: place to learn and appreciate the sacrifices made for Vietnamese independence

author: Ellen M
title: Worth a visit
original_content: If you want to visit inside the mausoleum and see Ho Chi Minh, you have to go in the morning. Problem is, that's when thousands and thousands of school children also go. We estimated we'd have to stand in line in the hot sun for about 3 hours to get in. Instead, we returned and visited the external grounds in the afternoon and it was peaceful and lovely. Worth a visit for the architecture, culture, and history.
practical_tips: visit the external grounds in the afternoon

author: LolaGo1
title: Feeling grateful that I was able to enter it before leaving Hanoi
original_content: Through Booking.com , I was able to book a walking tour with a  Vietnamese college student. Cost for this service was only for $5.00. Entrance to the Complex is quite restrict. We had to leave our backpack, handbags and personal stuffs at the Entrance Lockers. We were ushered in walkways that have roofs before entering the Mausoleum. Security Guards kept reminding us NOT to  take photos and keep moving. The body is an enclosed glass compartment,  with 4 guards standing around it. There are more security guards along the way. In the wide, open space infront of the mausoleum were several groups of school children who also visited the Mausoeleum. Other attractions in the Complex include the HCM Museum, Pagoda Shrine, Gardens,  Palace (closed during my visit). Recommended to visit them as well.Note: Visiting days and hours to the Mausoleum are limited. Entrance is FREE, consult with the locals regarding their opening and closing hours.Picture- taking at the other attractions in the Complex is allowed, NOT just inside the Mausoleum!
drawbacks: Security Guards kept reminding us NOT to take photos and keep moving
Entrance to the Complex is quite restrict
Picture-taking at the other attractions in the Complex is allowed, NOT just inside the Mausoleum!
highlights: Cost for this service was only for $5.00
Recommended to visit them as well
Picture-taking at the other attractions in the Complex is allowed
practical_tips: Entrance is FREE, consult with the locals regarding their opening and closing hours

author: Elsa D
title: must see in Hanoi
original_content: One of the tourist attraction in Hanoi. The place is magnificent. I did not visit inside because it was already noon (closed by 11 am). The next morning we saw the lines of people wanting to get there, my tour guide said it takes 2 hours in line to get inside. We took nice pictures just outside

author: arpitam
title: Salute to the great leader
original_content: If in Hanoi this is a place to pay a visit. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is located in the Ho Chi Minh complex, a luxuriantly large and beautiful esplanade. I was unfortunate to have landed up on a Monday (Mon & Fri closed) but had the opportunity to watch the daily morning parade.
practical_tips: check the opening days before visiting

author: The-Mong-Melbourne-Australia
title: A couple of tips for you
original_content: 10 April 2023, the mausoleum itself is still closed, so you can’t get to see, nor file past Uncle Ho’s body…. Do you have to queue to get through security, and at 1 pm on a Thursday we wait about 20 minutes so no major drama. You do NOT need to have identification so you don’t need to carry a passport like we did. Importantly, females (women not kids as far as I’m aware) have to have their shoulders covered so at minimum a T-shirt and also the knees covered or you certainly can’t wear tight shorts. If you do, they will not let you in. That said some random dudes offer to sell you scarves to cover your shoulders if you don’t have something appropriate. Whilst you can’t go into the mausoleum itself it is worthwhile having a look at Ho Chi Minh’s Stills house and other buildings on the site, you do not need to prepay you can purchase a ticket after entering security at the internal gate to get into the building area …40,000VND to get in and will take you approximately one hour or so to have a good look around, and you certainly are beautiful place so it is well worth while doing.
drawbacks: Need to cover shoulders for women
Need to purchase ticket after entering security
highlights: Approximately one hour to have a good look around
practical_tips: Go early to avoid long wait times

author: RoverP
title: A good insight into a powerful but humble leader
original_content: This is an experience not to be missed.  It is certainly very interesting but it would be a push to call it excellent.  You can only go so close to the Mausoleum itself.  The scale of the building and the security certainly reflect the esteem in which Ho-Chi-Minh is held by the Vietnamese people.  The mausoleum dominates an absolutely massive square which is devoid of any other structure.  It looks across the square to the National Assembly building as if the great leader is checking that current day leaders are not betraying the revolution.Also on the site and in much more attractive surrounds are the yellow walled official presidential residence (which Ho only used for official business) and two much more humble dwellings which Ho actually lived and worked in.  You can't go in, but you can get a good look in through glass frontages.  A good insight into a leader of the people for the people.
drawbacks: You can only go so close to the Mausoleum itself
highlights: good insight into a leader of the people

author: Chris318i
title: Arbitrarily selection of visitors
original_content: We were not allowed to enter the mausoleum, because our youngest son was too young (ten month old). The "official rule" is that kids under three are not allowed to enter the mausoleum. I'm ok with that rule, but it should be applied to all families then. Several families waiting with us brought kids below the age of three. When I asked the staff why some are allowed to go in and some not, they made up new rules. First additional rule, it's too cold for our kid. Second additional rule, the kid needs to be able to walk on its own. We were not the only ones that had to stay out. I'm really ok if there are clear rules, but from my point of view, the staff arbitrarily selects who is allowed to go in and who needs to stay out. In the end we visited the mausoleum only from the outside.
drawbacks: Not allowed to enter due to child's age
practical_tips: Check the official rule for child entry
Be prepared for inconsistent staff behavior

author: Людмила Пластинина
title: tribute and history
original_content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi is a memorable and poignant experience. The mausoleum, which is an iconic monument, has deep spiritual significance for the Vietnamese people. Inside, a solemn atmosphere and an aura of respect surround the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh.A strict dress code must be followed and respect for the location must be maintained. Be prepared to queue as the mausoleum is a popular attraction. A visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is not just a tourist activity. This is an opportunity to bear witness to a historical figure and pay tribute to a leader who left an indelible mark on Vietnam's history.

author: Asden D
title: Excellent But Time Consuming
original_content: The mausoleum is of great historic and social importance to the people of Vietnam, which in our opinion makes it well worth a visit.   However, it is worth being aware that the lines can be extremely long and it may take up to several hours to get to the inside of the mausoleum. We weren’t aware of this and visited around 8.30 am on a Sunday without having had any breakfast and it was 11 am by the time we finished seeing the mausoleum - we didn’t end up seeing the presidential place, museum, or the stilt house because we were too tired at the end of it/didn’t have the time. The time spent in the mausoleum is about 5 minutes. Our advise is don’t skip your breakfast/cuppa, come prepared to stand in the sun for few hours, and make sure you have sufficient time if you want to see everything in the complex.
practical_tips: Come prepared to stand in the sun

author: Barrie W
title: A Must Visit in Hanoi
original_content: A respectful memorial to the leader who unified the nation. Amazing legacy: overcoming foreign control. Highly revered now and an important place for understanding today’s Viet Nam.
highlights: Important place for understanding today's Viet Nam

author: Daniel K
title: Just stay away and leave the dead alone.
original_content: We were not impressed, it was a lot of employees who were angry and did not bother to help us. They gave us more, wrong information and wasted our time. I would recommend doing something else. Or get out of town as soon as possible. Definitely the city we least liked being in.
drawbacks: employees who were angry and did not bother to help us
practical_tips: get out of town as soon as possible

author: SEALS
title: I wanted to see the changing of the guard.
original_content: I visited on a tour of Hanoi city. I was told that there would be a long queue, but I entered through the gate and walked along the long corridor without stopping, and entered the huge building where Ho Chi Minh's body was kept in a refrigerated container, guarded by many guards. I was told that stopping, taking pictures, and talking were prohibited inside the building. Most of the people in line looked like they were Vietnamese. I wanted to see the changing of the guard.
drawbacks: prohibited from stopping, taking pictures, and talking inside the building
practical_tips: enter through the gate and walk along the long corridor without stopping

author: Angelo M
title: Ok
original_content: This was ok.  Nothing exciting but if you’re a history buff you might enjoy this. Keep in mind you can’t go in here wearing shorts. We tried to and were turned away and then had to buy some dead sexy pants from a street vendor so we could get in.
drawbacks: had to buy clothes to get in

author: m2347m
title: Preservation is amazing!
original_content: Visited in March. The weather was perfect. Was warm but not hot.  Lot's of people and school children but the lines go fast so dont let that intimate you. The lines stop at 11AM as it closes by 11:30AM. Closed Monday and Friday.Amazing how well preserved this guy is.  Is it plastination? Is it a wax figure? Who knows but word is he is taken to Russia for touch ups every year.  Has Russia found the fountain of youth for the dead?
practical_tips: Don't let the lines intimidate you

author: Alessandro S
title: Too many people
original_content: The mausoleum of Ho Chi Min who was president from 1945 until his death in 1969 is definitely a destination worth visiting. There is a long queue to do some kind of check at the metal detector. They put my camera in a red bag.We pay the ticket 40,000 Dong each. The guards have a particular all-white uniform because on Saturdays and Tuesdays there is a kind of special ceremony. the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a complex that includes the monumental tomb, the house, the Presidential Palace and the Museum dedicated to Ho Chi Minh. It is now considered a sacred place for all Vietnamese.The complex was built in the period from 1973 to 1975
extracted_spaces: Museum dedicated to Ho Chi Minh
practical_tips: go on Saturdays or Tuesdays for special ceremony

author: LondonFamily88
title: The queues move quickly
original_content: We are glad we had a  guide when we visited in order to navigate the security and adhere to the strict deferential protocols. The queues appear long, however, move swiftly, particularly in the mausoleum. This is on the list of things to do in Hanoi, and certainly, there was lots of respect and reverence by the Vietnamese visitors.

author: Henry E
title: A beacon of history and inspiration
original_content: The detailed sculptures were an inspiring sight, each one meticulously maintained. The mausoleum stands as a testament to the resilience and spirit of the Vietnamese people. A visit to this iconic landmark is a must for any solo traveler seeking to delve deeper into the rich tapestry of Vietnam’s past.
highlights: testament to the resilience and spirit of the Vietnamese people
practical_tips: a must for any solo traveler seeking to delve deeper into the rich tapestry of Vietnam’s past

author: Angeles Echevarria
title: YOU ONLY ENTER ESCORTED IN A GROUP. WITH SOLDIERS
original_content: The entire complex is escorted with very young soldiers dressed in white uniforms. We visit the place where the embalmed corpse of Ho Chi Min called Tio Ho is. Some Russians embalmed it and they check it from time to time.There is a guard inside the mausoleum for 24 hours, they never leave the body alone.It is located where Ho Chi Min had his modest house on stilts that can be visited on one side.
extracted_spaces: the place where the embalmed corpse of Ho Chi Min called Tio Ho is
Ho Chi Min had his modest house on stilts
drawbacks: Some Russians embalmed it and they check it from time to time
highlights: a guard inside the mausoleum for 24 hours
practical_tips: visit the place where Ho Chi Min had his modest house on stilts on one side

author: nasser
title: great leader
original_content: It was a fun day, the atmosphere was beautiful, and there was a very wonderful organization on the website to visit this remarkable person and the great leader who led the country to freedom. He deserves all the appreciation, reverence and respect.
extracted_spaces: the great leader who led the country to freedom

author: DotsGirl2
title: There is a lot to see here beside the Mausoleum
original_content: Be prepared for long lines. They do move pretty quickly. The mausoleum is based on one in Russia. Basically you go into a cooled building and file past Ho Chi Minh’s body. The interesting part is seeing how much he is loved and revered by his people. When you come out you can see the Presidential Palace he refused to live in. Then go to house no 54 where he did live  for 4 years, which is basically the servants quarters for the presidential palace. Then you can go through the stilt house that he lived in for the remainder of his life.
highlights: Seeing how much Ho Chi Minh is loved and revered by his people
practical_tips: Go to house no 54 after visiting the mausoleum

author: BrakiWorldTraveler
title: Inform yourself if you want to see Mr. HCM body
original_content: This was my second visit to Hanoi, however both times I didn't manage to see Mr. Ho Chi Minh's body in his Mausoleum, but was around in front and on other sites around the complex.So basically, you're reading tips from a traveler who didn't make it inside, but for sure will next time :-) HCM Mausoleum is within a huge space with several another sites.When entering the area you pass an airport style security check. After that you can roam freely exploring the area. You need around 2 hours min for that, excluding the Mausoleum, which visit length depends on the queueing line.Besides the Mausoleum within the complex is the Presidential Palace, One Pillar Pagoda, HCM stilt house and a Museum (small entry fees for the latter two).People here review and post pics of all these together, but I'll focus on the Mausoleum, while others you can read in respective reviews.My previous visit in 2017 was during some Vietnam holidays, so the waiting line in front was very long, some 2+ hours as I was told by police, so I gave up.This year, in Jan 2024 I put it high on my to do list saving our last day only for that.Unfortunately, I did not know the Mausoleum is NOT open every day. It's open only 4 days a week and some of these days only 8-11 AM. So, inform yourself beforehand if you want to enter it and see Mr. HCM body.All other attractions on the premises are open every day, so you still have plenty to visit.
practical_tips: Save last day for the Mausoleum

author: JanAarup
title: A tourist attraction in an authentic city
original_content: The rush of history alone makes the mausoleum and the surrounding area worth a visit.However, you probably don't go to Hanoi just to visit this.There are many other things that draw in a tourist experience that is much more authentic than the norm
drawbacks: Not the main reason to visit Hanoi
practical_tips: Go to other attractions in Hanoi for a more authentic experience

author: Lori M
title: don't miss - very respectful and tastefully executed
original_content: this was special to visit... HCM is preserved with so much dignity and reverence. the line is long but it moves very fast.
highlights: preserved with so much dignity and reverence

author: Trevor N
title: Recommend going with a guide
original_content: Definitely need a guide to explain the significance of Ho Chi Minh to the Vietnamese people as there’s no information boards or other materials. We were lucky to visit when the guard was changing, otherwise not really a lot to see. One lady in our party was wearing shorts and had to ‘hire’ a skirt from a vendor near the security gate otherwise she wasn’t going to be allowed in.
drawbacks: no information boards or other materials
not really a lot to see
had to 'hire' a skirt from a vendor near the security gate
practical_tips: Definitely need a guide to explain the significance of Ho Chi Minh to the Vietnamese people

author: Shannon
title: Strange
original_content: Large square with a security entrance into it. Keep in mind the restricted area markings, it's easy to miss as it's marked along the ground on footpaths. Recommend coming when they raise the flag but other than that this site is pretty odd.
drawbacks: easy to miss restricted area markings
highlights: recommend coming when they raise the flag
practical_tips: come when they raise the flag

author: pngocduong1
title: Pho Thin - Delicious & Huge Portions
original_content: Pho Thin 13 Lò Đúc was another great pho experience in Hanoi! My daughter recommended it from her previous trip, so we had to give it a try. I thought the pho was delicious, and the portion was huge! They definitely don’t skimp on the beef! There was so much of it! They only have one size, and it was more than enough for me. I couldn’t even finish the bowl. Definitely come hungry!

author: Maps37681545689
title: SCAM
original_content: charged us 100k for a bowl each
drawbacks: charged us 100k for a bowl each

author: deborah t
title: Great pho for lunch!
original_content: Colleagues ordered lunch for us - great Pho!  The soup was flavorful, vegetables plentiful, and portions were good.  Would visit again!

author: rara
title: Delicious local experience
original_content: It's cheap and delicious. It gives you a local mood and makes you happy to go. I was happy to see a local uncle who shared a table with me casually pass the seasoning around and teach me how to eat!

author: Edokko
title: Four shop opened in Ikebukuro
original_content:
Visit on December 7, 2025.
I went out for dinner by myself because it was a branch in Ikebukuro!
Pay at the entrance and enter. I was asked if there was any cilantro on the list when I ordered it, so I thought many people didn't want to put it in, but there was a pretty large amount of cilantro on it that I couldn't see the noodles! The noodles and soup were delicious and I finished them in no time!
drawbacks: large amount of cilantro on the noodles that I couldn't see

author: Zung H
title: A bowl of powder to wake up Hanoi's early morning
original_content: Queue up with friends for Pho Thin early in the morning, now fried beef aromas, soup is rich and refreshing. The small storefront was packed with locals, and a bite down instantly understood what "authentic" was! It's not fancy, but it's memorable, and it's definitely a taste memory that Hanoi must punch in!

author: Damian C
title: Fabulous Pho
original_content: First impressions do not do the food justice. Having been up for 24 hours our first evening in Hanoi was concluded with a trip to Pho Thin. The standard bowl is ample pho for any meer mortal and did not disappoint! Cheap, tasty and filling! 60k Vkd so about £2:80 at time of visit fantastic on any budget and a great “hole in the wall”.
practical_tips: go to Pho Thin for a cheap and tasty meal

author: Selig Getz
title: Famous Vietnam noodle
original_content: The beef pho was rich, aromatic, and hit the spot after a long flight. No fancy seats, just plastic stools and big flavor. A messy, noisy, perfect taste of real Hanoi with the whole crew.
highlights: rich, aromatic, and hit the spot

author: Adventure05703998509
title: Good pho but not the best
original_content: It's hard to understand the enthusiasm for this place. It's better than average and full of herbs, but it's not the best we've eaten.

author: Janis Yana
title: Best Pho noodle in Hanoi
original_content: The rich, savory broth and the unique stir-fried beef were unlike any pho we've ever had. Sharing this delicious bowl of noodles in such a bustling, authentic setting was the perfect Hanoi experience for us.

author: lilybt
title: Famous Four Shops (authentic)
original_content: Affiliated or unrelated stores of the same name? I arrived paying attention to this. The most famous restaurant in Hanoi, Pho Bo (beef pho) is the only item on the list, and you tell the old man at the entrance whether you want to attach quantity and oil gruel or not, and whether coriander can be added. I'm delighted to say that I've arrived soon after and added tabletop lime, chili peppers and chasing nyocum as appropriate. Beef bone and beef broth is a good soup, which fits in with crisp rice noodles and is quite delicious. The amount is not small portions like Taiwanese noodles, and it is equivalent to Japanese ramen, so you won't be unhappy.
practical_tips: add tabletop lime, chili peppers and nyocum as appropriate

author: Ines L
title: Super delicious and traditional
original_content: Super tasty pho, just like you traditionally do. It was sensationally delicious. The food was super fresh. From the outside it looks like the worst cashmere, but inside everything was clean and good.

author: 이준호
title: Special Lunch in Hanoi, Poetin
original_content: It was really attractive, with a soft, rare piece of beef in it, and the taste of cold in your mouth. The fragrant aroma stimulated the nose and was the perfect place to enjoy a quick lunch. However, it's better not to have too many expectations. The atmosphere was normal, and the service was just like that. Yet the landscapes here have a charm to make you remember! I'll think about hearing it again next time.
extracted_spaces: the perfect place to enjoy a quick lunch
highlights: the landscapes here have a charm to make you remember

author: 劉 維杰
title: Delicious Tour in Hanoi - Pho Thin
original_content: The Vietnamese food here is authentic, the soup is delicious, the rice flour is smooth and tender. Sitting in a small shop filled with Hanoi's atmosphere, it's like time is still. It's a big crowd, but the atmosphere is warm, and enjoying this meal with your lover makes us feel so happy. It's definitely worth a try!

author: Willie Cilla
title: The best Pho in Hanoi
original_content: The richest, most flavorful pho we've ever tasted. The charred onions give it that unique smoky taste you won't find elsewhere. Yes, it's basic seating and quick service, but that's part of the authentic charm. Worth queuing for!
highlights: Charred onions give it a unique smoky taste

author: Hiroshi Tanaka
title: A traditional pho specialty shop loved by locals
original_content: The lively atmosphere with the locals was also great. The soup with condensed beef flavors and chewy noodles go well together. The simple but profound taste captivated us all. This is one of the must-stop places when you visit Hanoi!
highlights: soup with condensed beef flavors and chewy noodles

author: 최선우
title: Hanoi Rice Cuisine, Portin
original_content: Portin is the northern part of Hanoi where you can feel the street food culture. A place loved by locals, always crowded with people. When you pass the front of the store, the smell of deep rice sauce that stimulates the sores will stop. Make sure to taste the rice sauce, which has a deep and nuty taste!

author: 시연차 X
title: Hanoi's local cuisine, genuine rice sauce at Poetin
original_content: We visited Poetin, a Recommendation of the locals during our Trips to Hanoi. This place is famous for its local cuisine, and I could experience it personally. After ordering a fast and efficient service, gold-heated rice sauce arrived at the table. A mixture of deep, abundant meat and soft beef was one. The atmosphere full of locals was also attractive. If you want to taste genuine Vietnamese rice in Hanoi, Poetin is a strong Recommendation. The price is reasonable and suitable for Travellers.
practical_tips: go to Poetin for genuine Vietnamese rice

author: Alfons
title: Authentic Simplicity
original_content: Don't let the crowds put you off! Pho Thin is a must-see experience in Hanoi. The place is simple, always crowded, but the service is fast. We tasted their famous pho bo tai lan: a tasty broth with tender meat, just delicious! A culinary adventure for those looking for authentic Vietnamese flavors without frills.

author: Luis L
title: Best pho
original_content: I've never had better pho than this! It was absolutely delicious, and the soup was exceptional. Everything was perfect, and it's no wonder that both tourists and locals flock to this place.

author: Sohan
title: Good Pho, terrible service.
original_content: It was a delicious bowl of Pho not gonna lie! The broth is rich and flavourful with good taste, the meat is just superior compared to other bowls of Pho I’ve had in my Vietnam adventure. But their service is really poor. I wanted Chinese bread to have with the Pho, no one spoke English and they never understood / served me.
practical_tips: go somewhere else for Chinese bread

author: Chloe
original_content: Execellent beef pho, mainly local eating here which i view as a sign it's authentic and good value. This pho is more savoury than other i had in Hanoi, I found it rich and filling. Good value for money, I would come again

author: Howard L
title: The best beef phô in Hanoi is right here, and they've been at it for 50 years!
original_content: Our tour guide who grew up around Hanoi said this was the best beef phô eatery in Hanoi and who were we to dispute that??  It's record speaks for itself - they have been in continuous business for 50 years and serve only one dish.  The beef phô bowl currently goes for 70,000 VND or $2.80 USD.  It's a flavorful and delicious phô bowl, maybe a little more oily than South Vietnamese phô but that is the style and the source of the flavor.  It's a no frills operation and you pay cash at the restaurant entrance.  It was a delightful foodie stop for us.
highlights: best beef phô eatery in Hanoi
practical_tips: pay cash at the restaurant entrance

author: Mark M
title: Just better than the same things elsewhere in VN!
original_content: We arrived at our Air BnB across the street, and hungry for lunch. We all had different things, everything tasted fresh and just better than we had had elsewhere in VN. Server was super-helpful in how to eat to get the best flavour mix.
practical_tips: ask server for help with food

author: Alex Phạm
title: Pho Hanoi
original_content: A must-try dish when you go to Hanoi is Pho. The beef pho here is still complete and with quality, the price is also very high. You should try both beef pho and chicken pho to see the difference. Chicken pho should be eaten at Pho Tien or Pho Nguyet
highlights: beef pho is complete and with quality
try both beef pho and chicken pho
practical_tips: try both beef pho and chicken pho
eat chicken pho at Pho Tien or Pho Nguyet

author: Lori M
title: not great but we couldn't find anything else suitable in that area
original_content:
not great food but location near HCM Mausoleum so convenient

937773261

went here due to its proximity to HCM Mausoleum. it was pretty meh. soup didn't have much flavor and the fried bread things were not appealing. price was ok, maybe a little high for the area bc it's in the convention center.
drawbacks: fried bread things were not appealing
practical_tips: go somewhere else for better food

author: Diarmuid Lennan
title: Exactly what it says on the tin!
original_content:
No nonsense place. Read about it so went along as I was staying nearby. The guy asked us to pay up front, no menu, no choices. Pay, enter, share a table with other patrons, served within a couple of minutes. 

The beef Pho was excellent and that’s all I was looking for. Ridiculously cheap (approx. 5€ for two) is always a plus. 

If what you want is a good meal and go on your way to do anything else, this is the place.
practical_tips: go on your way to do anything else

author: sow s
title: Best Pho in Vietnam
original_content:
After traveling through Vietnam for a month I can confidently say that this is the best Pho. 
The broth is rich and filling. Personally, I like to get the beef raw and let it cook inside the broth, u can ask for extra noodles or if you feel like it, add an egg! Gives extra richness to the broth.
Few spots to sit, mostly locals eat here. 
It is not open all day, they have a lunch shift and a dinner shift.

author: 理一郎 中
title: Fast, cheap and delicious
original_content:
Fast, delicious, and cheap.
It's crowded, but the turnover is fast.
If you pay at the entrance and sit down,
they'll bring you your pho.
If you follow the crowd and eat it, it's delicious.

author: kenichiw2015
title: My expectations were exceeded in a good way.
original_content:
This bowl of pho changed my concept of pho, with its light soup and soft, flat rice noodles.
It was rather rich and chewy, and the noodles were very satisfying.
Next time, I'd like to try topping it with a raw egg like the locals do.
practical_tips: try topping it with a raw egg like the locals do

author: bochitabi
title: Only one menu option
original_content: The menu only has beef pho, with pineapple eye as a topping. I pay the bill to the man sitting boldly next to the entrance, who boldly accepts the bill with his right hand and puts it in the stack of bills he holds in his left hand without saying thank you. The interior of the store is not exactly clean, with counter seats on the right side and long tables and chairs lined up from the center to the left. The beef and chopped green onions are boiled in the kitchen at the back of the store, and the staff pours the pho and soup into bowls and tops them with the beef and green onions, and serves them one after another. The boiled beef, crispy chopped green onions, smooth pho and mild soup were very delicious. Incidentally, the flavor of the soup is slightly different from the Ho Chi Minh store, Shinjuku store, and Ikebukuro store. The pho is not slurped like ramen or soba, but is eaten by scooping it up with chopsticks and placing it on a spoon, so it took a little time to eat. There is no water, but you can bring in drinks purchased at the store next door.
drawbacks: the interior of the store is not exactly clean
the man sitting boldly next to the entrance did not say thank you
highlights: the boiled beef was very delicious
the crispy chopped green onions were very delicious
the smooth pho and mild soup were very delicious
practical_tips: you can bring in drinks purchased at the store next door

author: angie
title: Hanoi: Vietnamese cuisine
original_content:
When I said I wanted to eat pho for breakfast, a friend who lives in Hanoi brought me here.
It seems to be a famous pho restaurant in Hanoi.

There is an older man working at the entrance, so you pay first and enter the restaurant.
If you also buy fried bread, you will be given fried bread at the entrance.
The restaurant is quite crowded...
However, there is only one type of pho on the menu, so it is served quickly.
Although the restaurant is crowded, the turnover is fast, so there is not much of a line in front of the restaurant.

The pho is served with plenty of green onions.
The soup is also very flavorful and delicious.
I ate pho at other restaurants during my stay in Vietnam, but I felt that this restaurant had the strongest soup flavor and the saltiest taste.
This restaurant changed my image of pho.

My friend paid the price, so I don't remember...
It seems to be around 300 yen.

author: Noah
title: Savoring Pho Thin's Authentic Delight
original_content: I was so eager to leave for Vietnam because this country is noted for its budget and delicious food. And it would not be a trip to Vietnam if I didn't eat Pho here. We just looked at the Google map and headed to Pho Thin, where we ordered two bowls of rare beef Pho. Pho here was so good and so Vietnam. The things in the USA stand no chance to compare to Vietnamese real Pho. I highly recommend this diner.
highlights: Pho was so good and so Vietnam
practical_tips: Go to Pho Thin for authentic Vietnamese Pho

author: Chopper44
title: Believe the hype. This place. Is amazing.
original_content:
Delicious beef Pho. High quality. Sitting at shared table, lightning fast service and really delicious beef. Tender. Full of flavour. 
2 beef pho, 2 beers and 1 coke less than £6. 
Unreal.
practical_tips: go for the shared table experience

author: CoolGuy
title: Only one option - Beef Pho!
original_content:
Been here before as I can remembered, long before covid, as brought here by my Vietnamese colleague. 

So this time i bring my Japanese colleague to come here for the pho. Yes! Beef Pho. Not chicken. You don't have a choice! Breadstick and drink needs to pay separately! Yes! two different sellers.

Nonetheless, I find that the taste is still good. But as far as i can remember, the spring onions seems to be lesser this time round as compared to last time before covid period we came.

Narrow place with only two long bench tables. Still worth a visit and try out this old shop!
drawbacks: Lesser spring onions this time round
Two different sellers for breadstick and drink

author: Tj
title: Food so good!
original_content: Very home  feeling food is delicious went here after a long day and the pho hit the spot! This is exactly what I came to Vietnam to have!
highlights: exactly what I came to have

author: Henry N
title: Great Pho
original_content: If you're a Pho lover, then you absolutely must check out this Pho restaurant! From the moment you walk in, you can smell the savory aroma of the delicious broth cooking on the stove. And once you taste it, you'll know why this is the best Pho restaurant around. The broth is rich and flavorful, with the perfect balance of spices and seasoning that creates a truly authentic taste. The beef is tender and cooked to perfection, and the noodles are perfectly cooked and add a great texture to the dish. Overall, this Pho restaurant is a must-visit for any food lover, and I can't recommend it enough!
highlights: perfect balance of spices and seasoning
tender and cooked to perfection beef

author: Matteo Conti
title: Best Pho
original_content: Simply the best Pho in Hanoi. Authentic pho at very cheap price. You absolutely have to try it if you are in old town.
practical_tips: Try it if you are in old town

author: Peter M
title: Brilliant authentic Pho packed with people who clearly seek out a taste of home
original_content:
Found this place at the end of Hardware Lane. Packed. Great Pho and very reasonable prices. Lots of add on options. 
My new Pho home in CBD

author: Travelly HN
title: Pho Thin is absolutely MUST-TRY
original_content:
Pho has many ways to prepare and Pho Thin is a MUST-TRY as their chef possesses one of the most special recipes. Pho is pre-fried with garlic, so the noodle soup is very flavorful. It would be perfect if you get fried dough soaked in Pho broth!!

Price: a bit too high for a standard bowl (but it's worthy!! Trust me)
drawbacks: Price: a bit too high for a standard bowl
highlights: the noodle soup is very flavorful
practical_tips: get fried dough soaked in Pho broth!!

author: Stephen B
title: Best pho in Vietnam
original_content: Best pho I've had in my life. Amazing. So simple, yet it was perfect. Don't think I can order pho back home again, just doesn't compare at all. The pickled garlic was so good. Tried pho several times travelling through Vietnam and this was the best, hands down. Note to travellers, you need to pay before you sit down.
highlights: Best pho I've had in my life
The pickled garlic was so good

author: Andrew
title: Pho Thin
original_content: Actually the pho is “thin” too. Anyway, nice bowl of authentic pho bo. Price is high by Vietnamese standard. Highly recommended if you like beef rice noodles with soup. Don’t forget to pair it with the mini fried fritters.
drawbacks: Price is high by Vietnamese standard
highlights: nice bowl of authentic pho bo
Highly recommended if you like beef rice noodles with soup
practical_tips: Don't forget to pair it with the mini fried fritters

author: waylandtony
title: Do one thing very well.
original_content:
Having traveled for the last month in Vietnam I have had a lot of their national dish Pho. I didn't realize it before I was here that it is widely a breakfast dish, but I had no trouble having a hot savory bowl for many a breakfast.
I was told by my daughter that Pho Thin was a must go to. They only serve Pho Bo the beef version, a large bowl of wonderfully flavorful broth with thinly sliced beef and green onions. They also serve a Vietnamese savory donut that by themselves are rather plain but when dipped or floated in the Pho was fantastic.
I would highly recommend Pho Thin for an authentic Northern Vietnamese Pho that is sure to rank with the best you have ever had.
highlights: fantastic when dipped or floated in the Pho
practical_tips: go to Pho Thin for an authentic experience

author: Sasha
title: Delicious
original_content: The pho here is wonderful, so flavourful and very quick service. Full of locals who are all friendly. Would defo recommend!

author: Larry C
title: Best Pho Ever
original_content:
Our tour guide told us about Pho Tin and we had the best Pho ever here.

The place only serves one dish and you pay as you enter (65,000 VND per bowl)  you can also order some fried dough like things if you want.  Although they only serve one type of Pho it is by far the best we have ever had.  You sit at long tables or against the wall with other patrons.  the service is quick and the place is always busy.  We stayed in Hanoi 3 days and ate here twice.

Very much worth the price.

author: Austin T
title: Pho get about it....
original_content: We visited this place off of a YouTube video highlighting Pho Thin. It’s in the French Quarter and pretty easy to find. It’s simple as in you pay first, seat yourself and someone delivers a delicious bowl of Pho...pronounced like “Fuh”, not (Fo). The soup was fresh and very good. I believe it cost something like $4-$5.00. Very reasonable.

author: bas0921
title: Doesn't look like much from the outside, but go in and enjoy!!
original_content:
Recommended from a foodie tour, so we went for it. Community seating - great opportunity to meet new people! And the food was perfect Pho!! Buy the bread (extra) from the guy selling it separately.. Delicious soaked in the Pho broth! 
The place looks like some "hole in the wall" which it is but, a great value and even better food!!
highlights: Great opportunity to meet new people
Great value and even better food
practical_tips: Buy the bread (extra) from the guy selling it separately

author: Macdarien
title: Don’t judge a book by its Cover
original_content:
Excellent Pho, one type of Pho beef and beer and soft drink. 

A great local resturant with excellent Pho, grab a bowl and enjoy the flavors.

author: Xavier
title: Good but ...
original_content:
I gave a try to this restaurant, based on the shitload of positive reviews about it.
First, it’s quite small place, you will see many locals eating at this place, which is usually a good sign.
Then to my surprise, we had to pay before we could get a seat. A staff member kept saying “money first” without properly explaining the reason. As uncommon as it was for me, I paid, then took a seat to get immediately served without a smile or even an “enjoy your meal”. Quite rude from my opinion.
An other shocking view was how dirty the place was. Trash everywhere on the ground, even if bins were near each table. That was kind of disgusting, but then I focused on my dish.
The Pho was indeed excellent, it’s far from overrated. Broth was tasty and meat was tender too. 
To conclude, if you want to go for a good local Pho, this is a place I’d recommend. For attitude, it’s an other matter, but I could give them the benefit of a doubt, even if the place wasn’t even crowded when I came.
My ratings are:
Service/hygiene 3/5
Pho 5/5
drawbacks: had to pay before getting a seat
place was dirty with trash everywhere
practical_tips: go for a good local Pho
be prepared for a potentially rude staff

author: Philip Lim
title: Hole in the wall Pho place
original_content: Pho Thin serves pho with abundant onion leaves.  Beef here is stir fried first, giving it a different flavor from the usual pho.  The place is a real hole in the wall.
drawbacks: The place is a real hole in the wall
highlights: Beef is stir fried first, giving it a different flavor

author: cracyDP
title: Delicious soup
original_content: There is only one type of beef noodle together with green onions, you only decide how many bowls you want to order. Donut is a must try. Dip the donut into the soup before you eat. The soup is delicious and I will not feel thirsty even i drink almost all the soup. Highly recommend.
practical_tips: Dip donut into soup before eating

author: Wagner Pereira
title: The best !
original_content: The best ! Have so much Pho in Hanoi but this is so good! Only one price , one dish ! The kitchen in the door ! Basic and efficient !

author: Mikaela Z
title: Worth the Money!
original_content: Delicious food at a low price point (60,000 dong=$3-4). They only speak Vietnamese here but if you order the speciality you will not be dissappointed

author: Adventure
title: Very special and delicious Phở
original_content: This place is near the center and easy to get there. They serve only one type of food which costs 60.000đ for one bowl. It is very delicious with full of meet, noodle and green onion. Their soup is fabulous and perfect tasty.
highlights: full of meet, noodle and green onion

author: dhui
title: pho @ CBD
original_content:
one may visit if you want pho badly at CBD.

the broth was intense and good.  yet the rest was average.

the way they made the pho was different with what pho was served elsewhere, one did not get those spouts and mint leaves kind of thing.  So simply broth, rice noodles and beef in the bowl.

seating was not too comfortable, good for solo quick fix.
highlights: the broth was intense and good

author: Travel for events
title: Service really slow, waited to be seated for a while
original_content: Service really slow, waited to be seated  for a while food arrived and it was vary nice, the staff did keep apologising but it never improved  the waite was ridiculous
extracted_times: waited to be seated for a while
drawbacks: waited to be seated for a while
highlights: food arrived and it was vary nice

author: LMX
title: Fabulous Beef Pho!!!
original_content: This unassuming bowl of pho will have you blown away by its clear delicious soup broth and soft rice noodles. It wont leave you feeling thirsty even after you drink the whole bowl of soup. The soup is not oily and very flavorful, combining sweetness from the beef stock, slight sour fr the add on lime and vinegared garlic, spicyness from the chilli. It was mind blowing goodness. Warm the stomach and make u yearning for more. Two types of beef was given. One was slightly on the tough side but the other was tender n sweet. No beefy taste for those who are particular. They are also not stingy with their spring onions. Loads on them floating on top. It was amazing slurping the tangy pho w the soup. Yummy goodness.
drawbacks: One type of beef was slightly tough
practical_tips: Try it early to avoid disappointment

author: Shuke Skywalker
title: Best Pho Bo
original_content:
I lived in Japan for long time, and the country is known for the food quality for any kinds of cuisines. But for pho I have to say you have to come to Vietnam and try this real stuff.
Rich beef broth with refreshing spring onion. Onky for 60K Dong.
practical_tips: Come to Vietnam and try this real stuff

author: maverikbc
title: Just hype
original_content: The greasiest broth I've ever had.  Packed, but I didn't see any foreigners.   While I appreciate the plenty of boiled green onions, and I  don't mind the greasy broth, I find it to be average.  Deducted 1 star because 60k is overpriced for it, I frankly don't understand why the Vietnamese (I couldn't tell if they were locals or domestic tourists) love this place.

author: Samuel Piette
title: Pho Thin
original_content: Being a symbol in Hanoi is definitely not an easy things to achieve. It has meet my own expectation, it's not like any other pho i've have in Hanoi. It's actually good and i would love to eat it the whole freaking day if i could

author: Max R
title: Lives up to reputation
original_content: Having heard about this place we were keen to try it. We had eaten a delicious Pho during our walking food tour a few days before, so had a reference point, but were not disappointed. More of a hearty pho than the the more delicate, spiced broth of the other version, but very solid on flavour and ingredients - many locals also there tucking in, and certainly not for the decor!

author: Joseph T
title: Worst pho of my life
original_content: This place was recommended by my cousin, but when I got there the pho didn’t even taste like pho. It was watered down and they added tons of onions to mask the non existent flavor. Asked for a donut after we saw a lot of them right out front, but the server said they were out, probably because we ordered one to share. My hotels pho was a thousand times better. This place sucks pho real!
drawbacks: pho didn’t even taste like pho
added tons of onions to mask the non existent flavor
practical_tips: ask for a donut early to avoid running out

author: SomeKent
title: Great Pho in a raw local environment
original_content:
If you want good Pho in a real local setting come here.
One item on the menu, Beef Pho, but its good. Try and get the donut thingies “phonuts”
practical_tips: try and get the donut thingies "phonuts"

author: Han K
title: Local Recommendation
original_content: It seemed like they were serving just one dish, beef pho.  Pay before you sit.  60,000 dong.  My advice: use all the condiments on the table.  My preference was with two limes, some fish sauce,  & some sort of hot sauce.  Glad that I brought my own water.
practical_tips: Use all the condiments on the table

author: Che R
title: Really good pho but ambiance may not be for everyone
original_content: It is in a small alley which a lot of people may not view as clean. I didn't mind it as much and I really enjoyed my meal there. The broth was tasty and the meat was cooked well. I thought it was really good pho and would eat there again. I did hear from a local that they weren't too fond of this place because they feel that there is fat in the broth and that this wasn't authentic pho. I really liked it anyway and would eat here again.

author: Dan B
title: Great little place!
original_content: Small, very personable. Great pho, place made me happy, highly recommend. Word of mouth recommendation from a local: spot on.

author: PAPA
title: Nice PHO!
original_content:
The most popular pho restaurant in Hanoi.
So usually the line is so long, but we went late night and we didn’t line up.
If you don’t like waiting in line, you’ll go there late night.
Pho was so tasty.
It was the best I had ever eaten.
highlights: It was the best I had ever eaten

author: Miranda
title: The best pho in Hanoi
original_content: This place makes only one type of pho and that is beef pho but it is incredible - the best i've ever had. You walk in and pay at the front, then next grab a seat and they will bring it to you. It is very busy and packed with locals so don't hesitate. Just pay and find a seat. I highly recommend if you're visiting Hanoi.

author: Samm
title: Awesome Pho!
original_content: You pay 60 vnd a bowl as you walk in. That's the only menu they have, so they will bring in. Great local experience. The beef is charcoal cooked. and has so much spring onion and a bit of cilantro. The soup is rich in flavor and aroma but not too much. This was different kind of Pho than I was used to, but is now my favorite. I saw some guys ordering 2 bowls per a person and I totally get that. It was that good.
highlights: The beef is charcoal cooked and has so much spring onion and a bit of cilantro
The soup is rich in flavor and aroma but not too much
practical_tips: Go early, as they have a limited menu and it's a popular spot

author: MightyMike_France
title: Good Pho in Hanoi
original_content:
I was suggested by a friend to try Pho Thin.
I have tried it and I can say that this is a good Pho Bo.
This is the only dish they serve.
Walk in, order, pay and go sit...soon your Pho is served.
Nice portion. Good tasty broth.
I recommend !

author: Anas A
title: Authentic food
original_content: One of the best places in Hanoi to serve the infamous pho. The place is hard to find even with navigation maps. We got help from locals to show us the location. The restaurant is narrow and packed with hungry locals. They serve only one dish and the payment is made before seating. We enjoyed the food. It was quite an experience.
practical_tips: ask locals for help with navigation

author: manki m
title: Best Pho!!
original_content: Hanoi was the starting point of our 3 week Vietnam tour (north to south) and we tried Pho Thin on our very first day. I've waited for 3 weeks and countless more pho bowls all over Vietnam to write this: the Best pho in Vietnam by far!!!! It is a must if you are in Hanoi :))

author: Hi-there-all
title: Great dinner
original_content: Very tasty spicy dinner which we enjoyed on a hot night,  didn't stop sweating.  Local street food at it's best

author: SelenaTran
title: Amazing Pho
original_content:
Dinner was fantastic. Meals were terrific and reasonably priced. The service was exceptional and a credit to the restaurant. Very welcoming, thankyou John for your hospitality .
Well done. I will be recommending to others.
highlights: meals were terrific and reasonably priced

author: grace cahyadi
title: Amazing Pho On My First Day In Hanoi
original_content:
price was 60k VND. came with friend for a quick brunch and it was amazing. the thin noodles with great beef & coriander topping will sure warm up ur body. and the beef had that smoky flavour that enhance everything 👍

u hv to eat fast cause a lot of ppl are waiting outside to get in.
drawbacks: a lot of ppl are waiting outside to get in
highlights: the thin noodles with great beef & coriander topping

author: Spkster
title: One if the better pho bo in town
original_content:
This is one of the most popular pho bo in Hanoi with tourists. Price has increased to VND60K  per bowl from VND50K in 2018.

To order, walk in through the narrow aisle and inform the person cooking how many bowls of pho bo you want and if you wish to have the "quay" or fried dough. Pay the amount asked and take the bowl of fried dough to any empty seat available inside. The noodle will be sent to you. Not much customisation available except for a bowl with no vegetable or added egg. Squeeze some lime (from the bowl on the table) and enjoy. Soak the fried dough in the broth for a satisfying meal.
practical_tips: Walk in through the narrow aisle
Soak the fried dough in the broth

author: John_Allwright
title: Holiday
original_content: Wow, we had our evening meal there the food and service is outstanding a great find highly recommended if you are in the area.

author: Eddie Gaze
title: Best pho in hanoi!
original_content:
Been searching for this place for a while. The pho is amazing! The broth is clear but full of flavour, its smokey with a hint of bbq. The greens are as fresh as they come too. 

The service is speedy and friendly it was 60,000VND so its the upper end of pho prices (it has a right to be!).
highlights: clear but full of flavour broth
practical_tips: go to this place if you like good pho

author: Carlos S
title: Insanely good
original_content:
My gf and I spent 6 nights in Hanoi. We had researched the best Pho spots beforehand but after going to Pho Thin, we just couldn’t stop going there. 

The Pho is incredible. There is only one type of Pho they serve and that’s a good thing. They have perfected their craft. 

The place is constantly busy with many locals and tourists alike.

author: Noelle Marques
title: Very tasty
original_content: Very tasty, easy to order and fast service. Really busy but you can find a place fast. The price per pho was 60,000.

author: Josie G
title: Amazing! Use the spicy sauce
original_content: Hard to know which local spots are good, clean, and worth the stop or not. This place passes all 3. Communication is made easy since they only serve one dish - beef pho. It’s delicious!! And cheap, about 40000 VND or a little less than 2 USD. Comes with all the green herbs on top too. I recommend mixing in the spicy red sauce on the table with it - adds an extra kick if you’re adventurous enough!
highlights: comes with all the green herbs on top
practical_tips: mix in the spicy red sauce on the table with it

author: Leigh-C
title: Best pho in Hanoi!
original_content: Hearty bowl of beef pho, buried under a heap of freshly chopped herbs... dip the fritters (you-tiao) in the hot soup...lip-smackingly good! 👍🏻

author: Joanna_CF
title: One of the best pho in town
original_content: This is one of the best pho I have eaten in Vietnam hanoi! The broth is good and different from the ones I have tried here. Generous portions of beef and vegetable is given. It may be hard to find as it’s not as fancy as those normal pho chains but definitely worth to try
highlights: Generous portions of beef and vegetable is given
The broth is good and different from the ones I have tried here
One of the best pho I have eaten in Vietnam
practical_tips: May be hard to find as it’s not as fancy as those normal pho chains

author: Philip L
title: one of the best pho in Hanoi!
original_content: Fresh, tasty, and fast! This is an old family operation, founded on two things: traditional pho bo and efficient turn over!

author: 49Journeyman
title: Best Pho in Hanoi!!!!!
original_content: Fantastic Pho ... will be back soon to this little gem. Without a doubt the bast you can get. Loved it!

author: Chris C
title: Be brave..!
original_content: Looks a bit scary from outside but the staff are helpful once you’re in. Order, pay then sit. The Pho arrives red hot within 3 mins. The beef is braised and tastes amazing. The broth is full of greens and flavour. £2 a bowl. Went back for more. My favourite Pho is Hanoi.
drawbacks: Looks a bit scary from outside
highlights: The beef is braised and tastes amazing
The broth is full of greens and flavour

author: David P
title: Eat where the locals eat.
original_content:
Typical single menu food place, but great value and the Pho tastes great!
A must do if you're in Hanoi.
Don't go here expecting 5 star waiter service, its as far away from that as you can get, but pay your money and get a great big bowl of your favourite Vietnamese broth.
Lip smacking good!
practical_tips: A must do if you're in Hanoi

author: Allan E
title: great pho
original_content: It is al bit out of the way..very basic..but very tasty and a great experience. Very inexpensive...$6.00 for 2 of us

author: Alex R
title: 3 stars because maybe I’m just not a pho fan
original_content:
But the beef tasted like it had spent the last 6 months chewing plastic by the side of the highway. There wasn’t much else in the pho and it was lacking in flavour. 

The restaurant was cool in a street foody kind of way. 

But take this with a pinch of salt because I’m not a soup fan either.
drawbacks: the beef tasted like it had spent the last 6 months chewing plastic by the side of the highway
There wasn’t much else in the pho and it was lacking in flavour
highlights: The restaurant was cool in a street foody kind of way

author: CT Tai
title: pho sure is good
original_content: had a couple of pho bo the week i was in hanoi. this pho bo is definitely the most tasty. i was the first customer in the morning. the warm broth in the cold morning was one of the better things in life !!!! then i went to cafe giang for egg cafe. very good !!!

author: eannineja
title: Phó sure
original_content: Not the best not the worst.  I didn’t care for the fried pastry too greasy.  But the beef phó was fine but a bit gamey....was it beef?  I kept getting ripe whiffs at first was afraid it was the soup but the breeze shifted and I realized it was just the street garbage.  Everything was beyond grimy.  I dont think the bottles of sauces have ever been wiped down.  But I wanted to give it a go because Anthony Bourdain had given it good reviews.  I wouldn’t return with so many other options.
drawbacks: bottles of sauces have never been wiped down
highlights: Anthony Bourdain had given it good reviews

author: Mayumi I
title: The greatest pho bo
original_content:
The best pho no in my life. Always crowded with both local people and tourists. Only menu is pho no. You can add raw egg or fried bread if you want. Pay first, take a sheet, then, a staff will bring your bowl to your place. 60,000VND/bowl.

美味しいですよ。混んでいると思いますが回転は早いです。わたしが訪れた時は60,000ドンでした。地元の人はテーブルの上の調味料をかなり足して食べてましたが、そのままでも十分でした。
highlights: Best pho no in my life
practical_tips: Pay first, take a sheet, then a staff will bring your bowl to your place

author: Elena Florez
title: Best Pho in Hanoi!
original_content: My partner and I really wanted to try Pho in Vietnam and this little ‘hole in the wall’ shop was the perfect place!! The pho was phenomenal and probably our favourite meal in Hanoi! We ended up going twice in the four days we were in Hanoi. I would definitely recommend giving this place a try.
extracted_spaces: this little ‘hole in the wall’ shop

author: Matteo Albania
title: Best pho in town
original_content:
Best Pho in town! The place is simple and minimal, you pay the Pho 60k and the fried sticks 10k and then you sit waiting to be served. The turnover of tables is fast so if you see it full, wait a couple of minutes.

It is a really great experience to eat in a local and typical Vietnamese place, not really a resto, more a street food place. Truly amazing! Must try if in Hanoi.
practical_tips: eat in a local and typical Vietnamese place

author: Eliza M
title: BEST Pho!!!
original_content: Well ... I had the best Pho of my life at Pho Thin. All they serve is the Beef Pho, and it’s a hole in the wall spot that was filled with locals. The broth is robust, hearty and flavorful. The price is posted at the front, the staff is nice and the service is quick. It’s on the list for a second visit during our short trip to Hanoi. Super super delicious!! You have to know what you’re doing when you specialize in one dish, and you keep your place packed!
practical_tips: know what you're doing when you specialize in one dish

author: pomodorini
title: Yummy Pho
original_content: One of our best pho experiences in Hanoi, would definitely recommend getting the basket of fried bread sticks to go along with the rich broth. The beef broth is very flavourful served with a generous serving of spring onions. Adding the lime and some chilli gives the soup an added kick. Would definitely recommend.
practical_tips: get the basket of fried bread sticks

author: Khanh
title: Good pho in a hole in the wall setting
original_content: The pho had good flavor although you can have the same at other Vietnamese restaurants.  Little to no English spoken here and service is non existent. You order, sit down and they bring you a bowl, then you pay and leave.
practical_tips: Go somewhere else for better service

author: alexapaton
title: Best beef pho ever !
original_content: This place is worth the walk out of the old quarter. Absolutely delicious, the broth is still in my memory
highlights: the broth is still in my memory

author: Justin Li
title: No fuss beef pho
original_content:
Theres only one item on the menu and that's beef pho which is 60k. You can add a basket of deep-fried breadsticks for 10k as well.

The wait was only 1-2 minutes before we were tucking into a steamy bowl of deliciousness. The broth is much more flavoursome than other northern style pho recipes, featuring a meatier taste with plenty of spring onions, garlic and coriander.
The meat itself was cut into strips, similar to what you'd expect in a stir fry.

Overall the bowl was very full of meat and noodles. Fair price for a good meal.
drawbacks: Only one item on the menu
Fair price for a good meal
practical_tips: Go early to avoid long wait

author: chienwinston
title: The best Pho I have had in Hanoi
original_content: During 5-day trip in Hanoi, my wife and I have had 10 different type of Pho. Their soup of Pho is fabulous and meat is perfect tasty. It worths you visit. In addition, nearby a famous restaurant，Bun Cha Huong Lien ， where Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain visited you won’t miss.
practical_tips: visit nearby Bun Cha Huong Lien

author: lornabroughton
title: A genuine experience and good food
original_content: It costs 55k per person for a very good bowl of pho (and that is your only choice). The surroundings are very genuine Vietnam (ie it looks somewhat like a tiny, grubby school canteen!) so don’t go if you want luxury. But it feels like a true Vietnamese dining experience with genuine local food.
practical_tips: Don't go if you want luxury

author: Heguang Z
title: Best Pho
original_content: Simple place not far from Hanoi Opera. Fairly busy with both locals and tourists. The soup has deeper flavor than most others in the area. Definitely worth a visit. Also the place is not far from Bun Cha Obama.
highlights: deeper flavor than most others in the area

author: Felix S
title: excellent portion - very simple place
original_content: This place was interesting to find. No overhead sign or something, just a small sign at the "entrance" with the cooking place next to it. The bowl of Pho was stuffed with noodles, meat and other ingredients, really a nice filling meal for little money.
highlights: nice filling meal for little money
practical_tips: look for small sign at entrance

author: Vienne Lam
title: Very good Pho. All trash on the floor.
original_content: Very good Pho with comparatively less MSG. When staff clean the table, he simply took away the bowls and wiped all the left over tissue papers on the floor. So you somewhat feel like you are eating in a pile of trash, but truly authentic local taste and experience.
drawbacks: Eating in a pile of trash
highlights: Truly authentic local taste and experience
practical_tips: Be prepared for potentially poor table cleaning

author: EddieDean99
title: Best beef Pho in Hanoi
original_content:
Hands down the best beef pho I’ve ever had. From the broth to the noodles to the meat to the veggies, everything is fantastic. The beef somehow maintains its smokey flavour. This places only serves one thing and they do it extremely well. Definitely worth the trip out of the Old Quarter to try. 

Order when you arrive and then get a seat. A bowl costs 55k and the donuts are 10k for 6 I believe.
highlights: best beef pho I’ve ever had
beef somehow maintains its smokey flavour
practical_tips: Order when you arrive and then get a seat

author: Clarence T
title: Best Pho ever!
original_content: Went there with a HanoiKids tour. The best pho I have ever eaten. Fresh local vegetables, thinly sliced beef, generous portion of rice noodles and tasty chilli sauce. All adding up to a great food experience!
highlights: best pho I have ever eaten

author: Brooks T
title: Best in Town?
original_content: Walked in. Ignored. Found a spot. Ignored. Walked to the counter. Was told to come back in 5 minutes. Went back. Ignored. Looked and was unimpressed by hygiene. Left. Service is terrible. Highly unimpressed. This place seems to be coasting on its reputation nothing more.

author: Brenna Q
title: Great pho
original_content: Googled a good pho place and was not disappointed-didn’t know we had to pay first but it was fine anyways.

author: Geraldine E
title: Delicious Pho
original_content: Very good pho. Fast and fun. Friendly atmosphere with community seating. Chopsticks and condiments on the table. You’ll have a true local experience.
practical_tips: chopsticks and condiments on the table

author: MshackW
title: Outstanding
original_content: We were in Hanoi with a tour, and went with our tour leader to have some Pho. It was fabulous. I highly recommend Pho Thin for the tourist that wants authentic Pho!!!
practical_tips: go to Pho Thin for authentic Pho

author: Jasey Ong
title: Best pho in Old Quarter!
original_content: The best pho I had in Hanoi! We try multiple outlets pho but this is just so accommodating! The soup and the beef is soo refreshing.

author: mattwalters94
title: Excellent pho
original_content: A convenient location to get a tasty bowl of pho. A great way to experience traditional Vietnamese cuisine.

author: flodahl
title: Great Pho
original_content: Go and try it at least once while you are in Hanoi! Pho using fried garlicky beef might be the best thing you will eat during your stay!
practical_tips: Go and try it at least once

author: rachy135
title: Best pho during my trip!
original_content: Easily the best pho I had during my time in Vietnam. While the service is minimal, it’s efficient! The amount of herbs they put in the soup is delicious and the broth is outstanding. Highly recommend

author: An Doan
title: A traditional noodle of Hanoi
original_content:
I have been here for several times and this is my thoughts:
1/ You pay 50, 000 VND (2,3 Usd) for your noodle.
2 /  You can seat any where with local.
3/ Add your chilli sauce, garlic, fish sauce if you like.
4/ Quick eat and go because it’s very hot and very local.
5/ Don’t expect the best service here.
6/ They only serves Beef noodle soup and it’s very good for the price.
drawbacks: Don't expect the best service here
They only serves Beef noodle soup and it's very good for the price

author: Anonymous
title: Does not taste like normal pho to me
original_content:
Yes its flavorsome, yes the beef is stir fried... but it just does not taste like 'normal' pho to me.... 

Good to try once to see what the hype is about.

Service zooming fast, pay first, find a seat (difficult at peak times a place is small). You get the food once you sit down :) 50k a bowl.. add eggs and bread sticks for a little more!
drawbacks: difficult to find a seat at peak times

author: TimothyCCS8
title: Good local Pho for Breakfast
original_content: Had it first time with couple of friends yesterday. Food is good and the dough is delicious. Price is approx VND 50,000. So far the nicest Pho I had tried. Many locals and foreigners eat there. Just have to put up with tissues on the floor.
practical_tips: put up with tissues on the floor

author: kiwilisa8
title: The only place where the food reaches the table before you do
original_content: Excellent pho, typical hole in the wall eatery, beef not as good as what you’d get in Australia but great for Vietnam. Strong flavour with lots of onions and greens.
drawbacks: beef not as good as what you’d get in Australia
highlights: Strong flavour with lots of onions and greens

author: Radu P
title: Very good pho for a cheap price
original_content: We went to this local restaurant on a recommendation from a friend. It was well worth the walk. Very good pho, big portion, with loads of noodles and tasty beef. The service was quick (although nobody spoke English) and quite cheap (45.000 VDN). Would definitely recommend as it’s off the beaten path

author: Shycourgette
title: A very good pho
original_content:
The place reminds me of Seinfeld's Soup Man. 
The guy serving is super professional and very fast. The beef broth is very tasty and comes with noodles, greens, raw egg plus pieces of beef. The only down size was that the beef was a bit overcooked.
Definitely an authentic place to try a great local dish.
highlights: comes with noodles, greens, raw egg plus pieces of beef

author: maree150765
title: Delicious!
original_content:
Amazing Pho, local restaurant. around 50,000 for the best Pho I've ever had!
Beef if really tasty and lots of spring onions.
highlights: Beef if really tasty and lots of spring onions

author: Greg D
title: The best Pho!!
original_content:
Amazing pho soup in this place, the beef broth is fantastic, the place is packed with locals.
Best pho so far in Hanoi!

author: jongjs
title: Famous, local pho place
original_content:
Another highly recommended spot but not the most amazing pho I have had. The dish itself has a lot of spring onions, which is a plus if you like them but a huge negative if you don't. I like spring onions so all is good.

The broth is pretty alright, come with this unique 'wok-hei' taste but yea, the meat can be a bit too tough. I remember the meat option was beef only, if I am not wrong. The serving itself is huge and I like that. Not the cheapest Pho option in Hanoi, but still worth trying out.

The shop itself has no signboard so keep a look out! We had it during a rainy day, the hot soup makes it felt extra nice and comforting.
drawbacks: huge negative if you don't like spring onions
meat can be a bit too tough
not the cheapest Pho option in Hanoi
highlights: hot soup makes it felt extra nice and comforting
practical_tips: keep a look out for the shop itself has no signboard

author: Rathan K
title: Amazing Pho - off the beaten track
original_content: This place is a little away from the old quarter but is worth the extra walk. It was full of locals which is always a good sign. The Pho was heaped with meat and veggies although I would have preferred a bit more noodles. Order a bowl of fried dough to soak in the broth and squeeze some limes to add an extra kick to the Pho. Would highly recommend this place for anyone is search of delicious and cheap (VND 50,000 per bowl) Pho which is frequented by locals
drawbacks: would have preferred a bit more noodles
highlights: delicious and cheap (VND 50,000 per bowl) Pho
practical_tips: Order a bowl of fried dough to soak in the broth
squeeze some limes to add an extra kick to the Pho

author: DevinFarren
title: Stability!
original_content:
The quality of the dish is quite good only this point to note:
+) Meat hard to chew
+) I can not eat fresh onion, so it's hard to eat
+) Consumers should serve a little steam
=> slightly scared because the smell of the woman sitting next to
drawbacks: I can not eat fresh onion, so it's hard to eat
Consumers should serve a little steam
highlights: The quality of the dish is quite good
practical_tips: Consumers should serve a little steam

author: mooglemoon
title: Amazed by Pho
original_content:
Located near my hotel (hilton garden inn).
Recomended by hotel's receptionist.

Just random breakfast with my family, walked around 5 minutes from my hotel.

Place was so simple with several table, sit down and ordered pho.

No expectation or anything, just want to fill my empty tummy.

Once i took the first bite, it was just WOW. I amazed, beef was tender, broth was spiced perfectly and cakwe was good.

What a great breakfast!

Will i come back? Definitly!

author: MingZhuLiu
title: Fantastic Pho
original_content:
It's simple, you step in and pay for the bowl (50 000) 
Huge bowl of pho, full of spring onions and beef. Extremely filling and absolutely delicious! Best pho in Hanoi that we had.

author: meteorite10
title: The best Pho Bo I ever had.
original_content: The best Pho Bo I ever had. The atmosphere was the another thing I really appreciated. Definitely go back again.
highlights: best Pho Bo I ever had

author: Amalia C
title: Eat like a local
original_content: The Pho was amazing!!! That is all they serve. A big bowl of yummy broth with a perfect balance of noodles, meat and veggies. You get lots of sauces on your table to add your own touch.
highlights: perfect balance of noodles, meat and veggies
lots of sauces on your table

author: Misael G
title: Still Dreaming of Pho Thin
original_content: I don't know what everyone else is saying about "just okay" but this was the best damn pho I had in Vietnam. I'm still dreaming of it - it's unique to this restaurant, as they sautéed the meat I garlic before adding it to the pho. I'd definitely go back here if I were still in Hanoi!
highlights: best damn pho I had in Vietnam
practical_tips: go back here if I were still in Hanoi

author: vivwanders
title: Okay
original_content:
Not worth extra effort to get there. But good enough if you're in the area.

Soup base a little oilier than I like, and not quite as a beefy a I wanted. And a little too much spring onion (but you can request less, I would do this next time). Beef pieces itself were good.

Lots of locals here. Easy to order as they only serve pho, owners/staff are friendly enough.
drawbacks: Not worth extra effort to get there
Soup base a little oilier than I like
Not quite as a beefy a I wanted
highlights: Easy to order as they only serve pho

author: carlosbiazotto
title: Local eatery
original_content: When in Hanoi you will probably find thousands of Pho places, which is the most traditional vietnamese dish, but this one specifically is worth the visit. It is not a tourist spot, there is only one choice of food (which is delicious) and it is very cheap. Be prepared to pay in cash as credit cards are not accepted.

author: krysten_gibson
title: Amazing Pho and Great atmosphere
original_content: It was love at first Pho. It was sooo amazing. The flavor was so good and the owners were so amazing. Smiles all around. There was a family near by us that had a baby that was crying and one of the owners took over holding and comforting the little guy so the mom could eat. Cannot wait to hopefully be back here again soon!

author: Silviactwilson
title: Awesome food!
original_content: Restaurants seem to specialize and serve a limited menu. This was limited to pho. But it was exceptional and so well priced. A perfect evening for $10 for 2 (including beer)

author: Stefanie H
title: Authentic experience
original_content: I ate here twice in my week in Hanoi. First time with a friend I was travelling with. Really fun atmosphere and pho was good. Not mind blowing. Went again when she was sick one day and loved the experience squeezing into a table of locals and enjoying my pho while I poured with sweat

author: Allyse H
title: Best pho bo I had in Ha Noi
original_content: No nonsense pho bo outfit serving up deliciousness. Best bowl of pho I've had in Vietnam yet. (And I did a lot of googling for "best pho Hanoi," followed by a lot of slurping.) Relatively lean meat, which is my preference, delicious broth, generous portions.

author: hk_asiapearl
title: The soup for the pho
original_content: Wow, as great as it can be.  The pho and the soup is great, the beef is very good too.  Too bad there's only one thing to order here, so if you are not really in the area, I recommend you not to go to this area just for this
drawbacks: not worth going out of the way for

author: HanumI
title: Not as good as I thought it will be
original_content: Not as good as I thought it will be. We went there because of the reviews and blogs but we think the taste was just average. Not really special.
drawbacks: Not as good as I thought it will be

author: oroclom
title: Worth the Visit
original_content: Pho Thin was one of those places I was pretty sceptical about (having seen reviews on youtube about it), the place was pretty dirty and run down, the staff weren't particularly friendly but if you can get your head past all that - this was one of the best bowls of Pho I've had in years. Make sure you put some of that vinegar(?) chilli sauce in and soak your fried dough bar thingies in your soup before eating. It makes ALL the difference. Worth making a trip to if you're staying in Hanoi.
highlights: one of the best bowls of Pho I've had in years
practical_tips: put some of that vinegar(?) chilli sauce in
soak your fried dough bar thingies in your soup before eating

author: Janis K
title: Delicious, authentic and cheap
original_content:
Delicious, authentic and cheap. Really hit the spot on a hungry Saturday afternoon.
Thanks for the yummy food! see again

author: morganjacob924
title: Yummy
original_content:
Delicious dish. A bit different from the old style pho with the meat being stirred fry before. The soup is a bit fatter but the mix is so good.
The price is also fix so no need to worry about being unfair with Western people
drawbacks: A bit different from the old style pho
The soup is a bit fatter

author: Travelmax71
title: Delish Pho Bo
original_content: Hands down, the best Pho Bo in Hanoi. They use  braised beef which I guess adds some taste. Always very busy ... don't give up, wait for your turn and you won't regret it!

author: Waratahers
title: Worth the visit
original_content:
We were staying in the French Quarter so only a short walk. It would be so easy to walk past as it is only a small entrance so look for the 13. We were there around 6pm so it was not too crowded, but still a few locals eating. You pay at the entrance 50,000 I asked for no beef and it was only 30,000. The no beef is not suitable for a vegetarian but I am only semi vegetarian. We were seated along the wall and served very fast. There is no explanation of what to do so jut ahead and eat. The soup was wonderful, you can add sauce but be careful as the chilli slice is hot.
As I was leaving I bought a bottle of the chilli sauce for home. Took a bit of signe language but the cook told the severs what I wanted. 
One tip is to take a drink with you, I think they had drinks for sale but we could not work out how to get one. We walked in with our own water and beer.
This is a not a relaxing sit down, but more of a local experience.
drawbacks: no explanation of what to do
no suitable options for a vegetarian
