title: A table awaits you go check it out now……
original_content: As with everything a great hidden gem for you to discover and enjoy, great looking location, superb lively atmosphere, fabulous food and really fresh. Attentive staff with great service, great value for money and very quick service. Can’t find any faults it just ticks the boxes definitely recommend eating here will check it out on next visit……Thanks guys
highlights: great value for money and very quick service
practical_tips: will check it out on next visit

author: Annie5566
title: Dont miss this place
original_content: We came for the first time today.. I can't believe we have been to Hanoi 3 times and missed this place..the food and choices were first class, and the staff so helpful .we will definitely  be back the menu is impressive.

author: Keletso G
title: Very tasty food, very homely atmosphere
original_content: Excellent food, even better service! Everything was fresh, full of flavor, and beautifully presented. Staff were so friendly and attentive. One of the best meals we had in Hanoi.
highlights: Everything was fresh, full of flavor, and beautifully presented

author: Lebo P
title: Superb!
original_content: The best food we had in Hanoi. Kevin, the owner was really wonderful to us. He was very friendly, we absolutely had a great time and really enjoyed the food.

author: Skye C
title: A great meal!
original_content: Exceptional food. Really good service.

author: poudreverte
title: Very good meal
original_content: Good meals for a reasonable price!

author: Kate T
title: The best ever seafood spring roll with butter cream - super tasty, crunchy and delicious! Everything we had was amazing!
original_content: Fantastic food! Great service!

author: S C
title: Evening meal.
original_content:
Just fantastic!!!!!! Fabulous food, fabulous service and the wine was good too!!!
If you visit Hanoi you need to check out this place. Colin and his wife will look after you. All his family work here too. 
Highly recommend!!!! 

Thank you. ☺️

author: Tim G
title: Good
original_content: Food is very good. Braised pork especially.

author: Tricia H
title: What a find!
original_content: Hanoi Oi became our go to in Hanoi. It's small so you might have to wait, but fortunately we were staying nearby so it was easy to duck back to if the wait was too long. We particularly enjoyed the Bun Cha (pork with noodles), Banh Xeo (crispy seafood pancake), Can Chua Tom (hot and sour shrimp soup) and vegeatble fried rice - served with a ton of fried garlic. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water.

author: Matt
title: Best food in Vietnam
original_content:
It’s been a long time, if ever, that I’ve been so impressed by food at a restaurant. We did a food tour and this is several levels above anything we tried. The best food we’ve had in Vietnam by a long way.

Absolutely must try, it’s honestly incredible!
highlights: The best food we've had in Vietnam by a long way

author: Louise W
title: Far better than imagined
original_content: Beyond superb, the best food by far we have eaten so far in Vietnam. The atmosphere is fresh and different and the owner explained all the dishes. We only wish we had found it sooner.
highlights: best food by far we have eaten so far in Vietnam

author: Angie Shakira M
title: Don’t miss it!!
original_content:
This is one of the best in Hanoi! Don’t miss it!!!!
Truly delicious and Kevin (the owner) is the best!!!!

author: Edward P
title: Hanoi Mixing Food
original_content: One of the best food in Hanoi! The service was amazing. The owner is in charge of the service. Try the Pork Lemongras skewer. That was a nice experience.

author: Ranjan V
title: Fabulous
original_content: It’s just amazing good. I met Kevin, the owner of this place. Such a wonderful guy. The staff is really helpful, they’ll explain how to eat and gave the best service. Ambience is good too.

author: Doudou
title: A very good address in Hanoi
original_content: We came to eat at the beginning of our stay at this restaurant and it was so delicious that we came back for our last evening. The decor is very beautiful, the musical atmosphere too, and the owner is very kind. Favorite

author: kadandra
original_content: Fantastic food, great super-friendly service, and a cozy location. We will not find a better restaurant in all of Vietnam. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

author: Jenny-Lee F
title: Perfect!
original_content: Sooooo lovely! We passed by and had to book for the next evening as it was packed. The food was the best we’ve had in Hanoi and they were incredibly welcoming to us and our two children. Thanks so much Hanoi-OI!
highlights: food was the best we’ve had in Hanoi

author: Doug S
title: World class experience…
original_content: As an award-winning internationally published food, writer, I have to say… This was by far the absolute best restaurant that we ate at during our time in Hanoi. From the ambience, to the service, to the extraordinary food, everything was top-notch! Super, super fresh! An absolute winner!

author: Ari M
title: Amazing food and service!
original_content:
Our first dinner in Hanoi and of course we had to check this place out after seeing heaps of reviews on social media before our trip!

And wow… the food here was nothing short of amazing! Service was also next level.

Word of advice — make sure you book a table as this place gets pretty packed! We actually had to leave and come back after Kevin managed to get us a table about 45 minutes later.

Thanks Kevin!

Definitely coming back again before we leave Hanoi!
drawbacks: Had to leave and come back after waiting 45 minutes for a table

author: Stefan B
title: Authentic Vietnamese food in Hanoi
original_content: We had the spring rolls with shrimp. Fantastic. My wife had the chicken pho and I had the beef pho. Incredible taste. Simply magnificent. Best regards from Germany from Martina and Stefan

author: Freya E
title: 5 stars
original_content:
Food was the best I’ve ever eaten 
Flavour was unreal
highlights: Food was the best I’ve ever eaten

author: Nicholas B
title: Our favourite restaurant in Hanoi!
original_content: We loved the food here, such friendly service a very calm atmosphere in the normally very chaotic Hanoi. This was by far our favourite restaurant in Hanoi, it was far better than other restaurants listed in the Michelin guide!
practical_tips: go to this restaurant over others listed in the Michelin guide

author: Sedef B
title: Must try restaurant

original_content: Me and my family went here relatively late (around 9:30pm) and there was no wait at all, and the staff couldn’t have been more kind and welcoming, their menu had all items translated to English with a mini description which was great for us. When the food came, my dad ordered this type of fish which you rolled into little rice rolls with rice vermicelli, mint, pineapple, green mango, cucumber and carrot, where the incredibly kind staff gave my dad a tutorial on how to roll it and was very patient with my dad and brothers questionable rolling skills. The food was absolutely incredible, the best we have had in Vietnam with the most diverse flavour base we have found and the kindest staff always willing to help and laugh and joke with you, it was truly a pleasure eating here!
practical_tips: go relatively late to avoid crowds
ask staff for help with food

author: TiVoStarfish
title: For Your Last Night in Hanoi
original_content: My husband and I looked for a nice restaurant to enjoy our final day in Vietnam. I avoided this restaurant because it looks very touristy and mostly for foreigners. I tend to want to eat where the locals eat. On a whim, we gave it a try. Truthfully, it was really great! Queen and Kevin are fabulous ambassadors of the restaurant. They go out of their way to show you how to enjoy the food and how to use the sauces on the table. Some people may not appreciate this, but it does make a difference when you take their advice. The spring rolls are not made in house so I would avoid getting those as they are store-bought. They are prepared very well, however! The items you must get are the chef’s specialty beef noodle soup, the lemongrass pork skewers, and the braised pork with rice. Those items are outstandingly delicious and burst with flavor. Email them or find them on Facebook to make a reservation for a guaranteed spot in their cozy little place. It’s an affordable meal in a comfortable location and you will certainly leave satisfied.
drawbacks: The spring rolls are not made in house
highlights: Queen and Kevin are fabulous ambassadors

author: lilybt
title: Light flavor
original_content: It is a prominent ice cream shop on the way from Opera to Hoan Kiem Lake. The food court-like space, with its large boxes and numerous sales booths, is crowded with customers from morning to night. The temperature at which the ice cream tastes delicious is said to be between 25°C and 30°C, but the light flavored range is optimized in Hanoi, where the temperature is more than half the year. As a standard, it tastes more like ice milk than ice cream, and can be eaten without resistance.
drawbacks: tastes more like ice milk than ice cream

author: tanya gupta
title: Roasted Rice Ice Cream-Unique Must Have
original_content: Don’t mistake this for a small ice cream shop- this place seems to be an institution for Hanoi. Atleast that was the impression we got from their massive ice cream arcade (parlour would not do justice to the spread) that we came across in the old quarters. I had the roasted rice ice cream and the taste was so unique and something to go back for. We paid in cash and the cashier tried to short change us that didn’t pay us the full amount but we happened to count and ask her so then she paid us- I was only able to do this cause I had read that it’s a common practice Hanoi/Vietnam for the locals to not pay back the full cash assuming most people won’t count it or know the money- which is a sad occurrence so just be careful.
drawbacks: Common practice in Hanoi/Vietnam to not pay back full cash
practical_tips: Be careful when paying in cash, locals may not pay back full amount

author: HappyBird
title: Delicious ice-cream in a charming setting
original_content:
Perhaps the most delicious, refreshing and affordable ice cream we have ever had. The ice cream is made from natural ingredients, such as coconut milk, green beans, taro, cacao and has a unique texture that is not too soft or hard. The ice cream is sold in different forms, such as cones, sticks, mochi and has a variety of flavors to suit everyone's taste. My personal favorite is the cacao flavoured ice cream popsicle, which is chocolatey, creamy and fragrant.

Kem Tràng Tiền is located in the heart of the city right next to the lake and has a spacious and cozy atmosphere, with large open areas and green plants. The staff is somewhat friendly, helpful and the service is fast and efficient. The price is very reasonable, especially for the quality and quantity of the ice cream. You can enjoy your ice cream at the shop or take it home in a box.

If you are looking for a place to enjoy a cool and tasty treat, Kem Tràng Tiền is the perfect choice. It's a part of Hanoi's identity, charm and you don't want to miss this.
practical_tips: go to Kem Tràng Tiền for a cool and tasty treat
enjoy your ice cream at the shop or take it home in a box

author: angie
title: Hanoi: Ice cream
original_content:
It was so hot that we stopped in to get something cold. 
My friend, who lives in Hanoi, was told about this place by a local who works there. 
I wondered if this was the place to buy something, but when we entered through the entrance, we were surprised at how large the place was. 
There was also a courtyard-like area, and it was crowded with many locals. 
At first glance, they seemed to sell popsicles, ice cream, soft serve ice cream, etc., and there seemed to be separate cash registers for purchasing. 
I wanted soft serve ice cream, so I bought the chocolate flavor. 
It was a mini size, but perfect for when you want to eat just a little to cool down. 
Soft serve ice cream: 15,000VND (about 90 yen) 
Cash
highlights: perfect for when you want to eat just a little to cool down

author: L Tran
title: If you are curious
original_content:
This place seems to be locals’ favorite, so we gave it a try.
When we arrived, it was very crowded, which was a good sign for quality. We picked the “Cốm” flavor. Cốm is made of sticky rice harvested young, yielding a milky, nutty flavor that is great for making desserts. We normally get our cốm from Hanoi where quality is the best. Being said, the ice cream flavor didn’t resemble real cốm. Also, there is more ice than cream. This is actually what street version of Vietnamese ice cream tastes like. I think locals go here for nostalgia, so if you are curious, give it a try, just don’t expect too much.
drawbacks: ice cream flavor didn't resemble real cốm

author: The Baobab Republic

Always.
We were told that this is one of the iconic dishes of Hanoians. The ice cream cones with some flavors are quite basic, the appearance is also basic, but there is a huge crowd to enjoy. title: Trang Tien Ice-cream
original_content:
I first hear about Trang Tien Ice-cream shop from my friend after her trip to Hanoi. She said the shop is the most famous brand for local ice-creams and she highly recommended that I go there on my upcoming trip to Hanoi. Hearing that made me very excited because who wouldn't want ice-creams on hot summer days?
When my husband and I got to Hanoi and spent time planning for the trip to Hoan Kiem Lake and The Old Quarter, we realized that the ice-cream shop is very near there. We also read reviews about the shop's menu and we found the price really cheap, only 12k VND (a bit more than 0.5 USD) for cones, and 10k VND for ice-cream sticks. It seems that the place is refurnished because we saw a photo of the shop in the past, it does look much more beautiful now.
 We got there in the afternoon, wasn't too crowded and we saw no seats to dine-in (we expected it to be like that thanks to the reviews). The place is clean and bright, the staff was very friendly and luckily she understood English. We were sweating and thirsty so we got quite a lot: 2 vanilla cones, 2 mung bean sticks and 2 young rice sticks. The cones were smaller than I thought and it was too sweet for me. I really enjoyed the other two types, especially the young rice stick. It was a bit more chewy at the end because there are actual young rice bits!! I made a video call with my friend and she was surprised at the new look of the shop.
I'll definitely come back!
highlights: young rice stick was a bit more chewy at the end

author: egblonder
title: Cheap & Mediocre
original_content: It's a Hanoi classic, but that doesn't mean it's particualrly good. It's forgettable ice cream that doesn't break the bank, mostly famous because it was the first one and it's affordable for everyone. The most interesting flavor is probably the cốm (young rice), but it's only available seasonally.
drawbacks: mostly famous because it was the first one

author: Celine A
title: Local ice cream
original_content:
Pros:
1) Location is in the old town of Hanoi near Hoan Kiem Lake and the French quarters. Nice walk going to the ice cream shop.
2) You get a taste of of how a local ice cream is. It may taste just like an ordinary vanilla ice cream in a sugar cone but to me it was such a treat.
3) No long lines when we got there in the afternoon.
4) Relatively affordable.
5) The ice cream was perfect in hot weather.

Cons:
1) It is not really a shop where you can dine-in (unless I did not explore or ask around). It only had a counter where you can order your ice cream and eat it on the street.

Overall,  this shop is highly recommended to get a taste of local ice cream.
drawbacks: It is not really a shop where you can dine-in
highlights: get a taste of local ice cream

author: mbungay
title: Ice Cream, With a Slightly Different Take
original_content: There are apparently many with the same name that are not the same.  Go to the one here:  35 Tràng Tiền, Hoàn Kiếm, Hà Nội.  It's in the back of a parking garage.  There are no cones, only ice cream bars on a stick.  My favorite was the rice flake - it's a unique flavor.  Not unique as in bad, just something you won't find anywhere else.  I really liked it.  Our tour guide said the one at the address I listed is the real Trang Tien Ice Cream that started in 1958.  After a hot day at the lake, this is the perfect treat!  And it's really cheap!

author: CM1980
title: Best ice cream in town

They basically tasted like they were made with condensed milk! Our kids loved chatting to the other local kids in the shop as they slurped their ice lollies. author: John S
title: Skip the Fanny's - Eat Ice Cream Like A Local
original_content:
I was told Fanny's was the place to get ice cream in Hanoi.  But you won't find the locals flocking to this tourist hotspot.  I was already mildly disappointed with the Fanny's in Ho Chi Mihn City. My wife and I were lucky enough to spend a day in Hanoi with two thrifty college students.  We expected to buy them a nice treat at a famous ice cream shop, only to end up on the second floor at Trang Tien Plaza.  

Trang Tien ice cream is delicious.  We purchased four ice cream bars in exotic flavors that included coconut, green tea matcha and bean.  The ice cream was delicious, but the price was even tastier.  When I did the math, the conversion priced out around forty cents per ice cream.  Compared to Fanny's, that is a give-away (expect to pay US prices at Fanny's).

The ice cream shop wasn't much on appearances or atmosphere.  But it was cheap and clean.  And a fun respite from all the walking we did that day.  Definitely a must visit if you are in central Hanoi.  Just to say you did it. (Any excuse to buy ice cream).
drawbacks: Not much on appearances or atmosphere
practical_tips: Go to Trang Tien ice cream for a cheap and delicious treat
Be prepared for US prices at Fanny's

title: Good 'Ol Churned Ice-cream
original_content: My tour guide brought me to this place to enjoy the ice cream to cool down during a hot and humid May. This ice-cream is a traditional staple of Hanoi and have been around for a long time aka. every Hanoi-an childhood memory. I don't recall the price but it was relatively cheap. In the weekend, there's always a motor bike jam in the surrounding area because of this ice-cream joint.
drawbacks: motor bike jam in the surrounding area

author: jsthouston
title: Good icecream
original_content: An institution in Ha Noi and one of its best bargains.  Expect very long lines when the weather is warm, we enjoyed a scoop on a cool day so the line was short.

author: Dorothy L
title: Famous, tasty and good price
original_content: The place is always crowded with locals. It's my second time to be there and we tried four flavours. I like the Kem Com (ice cream with rice flakes). The shop is near the Hoan Kiem so can go there have a try if you are visiting the city.
highlights: Kem Com (ice cream with rice flakes)
practical_tips: go there have a try if you are visiting the city

author: Selena K
title: Mmmm delicious!!
original_content:
Delicious and cheap! Sooooo good! A bit hard to find - that's a huge shop with cakes and stuff, but the ice cream shops are hidden in the back - you will see the queues (!!) and that's where the yummies are :)
Rate 4 out of 5 just because not all the flavours were available when we were there :(
extracted_spaces: the huge shop with cakes and stuff
drawbacks: not all the flavours were available

author: mike_4m30nd
title: Hanoi trade mark Ice Cream
original_content: Don't expect anything but an Ice cream that will make you come back again. as simple as that. wide range of ice cream, cheap, fresh, and it was just as good as sitting down on a sunny day and relaxing.

author: Omar I
title: Yummy ice cream which is very cheap!
original_content:
You know a good place when locals swarm it too for the yummy ice cream. They have set flavours like chocolate, strawberry, coconut etc but the coconut is the best in my opinion! The ice cream costs about 12k dong (dec 2016) which is about 40p! 

Regards
Omar

author: NhuBao
title: Good ice cream but bad services
original_content: I went there with my family. We bought 2 for each person. The beans are and coco flavors are the best ice creams I have ever tried. It was really cheap.  The bad thing is most staff are not friendly enough. Just buying some and walking around the  Lake to enjoy your ice cream.
drawbacks: most staff are not friendly enough
highlights: beans are and coco flavors are the best ice creams I have ever tried

author: EA_Oussov
title: Great ice cream
original_content: We were just walking by and stopped for some ice cream. Presentation was interesting as my coffee mocha was covered in something like Turkish delight and came in 3 balls but was quite nice. And coconut ice-cream was more straight forward ice cream on the stick, which was very yummy

author: maritanlinz
title: Not same like my expected
original_content: In my memory trang tien ice cream is very famous,we are decided to came here ,but the ice cream is not some my expected,not good any more.the service is very very bad,they not welcome the guest when we are attend even no any customer around.just ignore.need more training to improve

author: Evelyn
title: Unique local ice cream
original_content: I decided to give this a try based on blog recommendation. At 12,000 VND, it's worth a try and see how locals enjoy their ice cream best. I tried the vanilla as it was my flavour benchmark across all shops around the globe (if they get vanilla right, then they're alright) and I had to say that it was interesting. Do give it a try if you're in the area!
drawbacks: ice cream was not up to standard

author: Megsie A
title: Yummy
original_content: The ice cream was good not the best but nice and worth the experience. The line up is fascinating and gave us a giggle. We went here at night time and then explored the French Quarter which made for a nice night out
drawbacks: The ice cream was not the best
practical_tips: Go here at night time and explore the French Quarter

author: MilkChocChip
title: Good Ice Cream but ...
original_content:
It's not Italian gelato but the ice cream tastes good and very cheap at 12k VND for a cone. 

However, the service is really really unfriendly. I didn't have the right change ready and she grunted and pointed to the sign. Also, as others have said, it's pretty unhygienic. Scooters can drive right in and the whole place in general looks pretty dingy and dirty. There was a huge trail of melted ice cream around the floor just in front of where they were serving and customers pretty much had no choice but to stand on it to be served. Hmm!
practical_tips: be prepared to stand on melted ice cream to be served

author: irve2016
title: Nice Cool Down
original_content:
As we walked passed this place was packed, not one to miss out we ventured in.
The ice cream was extremely cheap and refreshing, however not for my palate.

author: Kisani P
title: Cool down
original_content:
We hear really good things from people at our hotel to come here. After walking around the lake we needed a cool down.
Ice cofee and coconut ice cream, taro icecream amazing.

author: viet b
title: A must visit!
original_content:
Probably one of the best ice cream places I have tried in Hanoi. It is especially nice after walking half an hour, and you're drenched in sweat because the weather is so hot. So you go and devour a cheap eat ice cream. 
We tried many flavours: Vanilla, taro, green tea mochi ice-cream, and strawberry mochi ice-cream. Their cones are delicious. Nice, light, and crispy. Would go back again and again for the mochi ice cream. Didn't get a chance to try the taro one.

author: OliverL311
title: Want to beat the heat on a budget? This place is for you
original_content:
This place is insanely popular with the locals, with loads of bikes and scooters parked inside the premises, for the riders stopping by to grab a quick ice cream before hitting the road again. 

You can get ice cream on a cone, or traditionally on a stick. We had two ice creams on a stick, each for 7000-8000VND (Crazy cheap). The coconut ice cream and green rice ice cream. Both were great. Honestly, if you don't mind the relatively dirty shop entrance, you're in for a treat whilst continuing you walk around Hanoi! And come on, Hanoi isn't the cleanest of cities already. The ice cream's definitely safe to eat! 

Great ice cream for a warm sweltering humid day in Hanoi. Definitely worth a stopover whilst walking through the old quarters!

author: TIRAMESU
title: Smelly and dirty
original_content:
I don't like this place, ice-cream is cheap however, you will have to face unfriendly staffs 
The place is full of smelly rotten ice-cream (dropped on the floor - or rubbish bin)
Fly is everywhere, even some can find them inside their ice-cream

author: TCADVs
title: Great inexpensive icecream and an experience!
original_content:
Go here after dinner grab some great coconut ice ream for next to nothing, watch out for the scooters and walk with your treat! 
This place is fun and the ice cream is good!
practical_tips: grab some great coconut ice ream for next to nothing

author: Yan Yan P
title: Terriblle staffs!!!
original_content: This is not a great place for ice cream since the staffs here are terrible. They must learn how to serve their gests in the best way such as how to answer the guest's question. The ice cream here is quite nice but staffs' attitude is very bad. There are many other places serving nicer ice cream and nice staffs.

author: Brassos
title: Hanoi institution - a must visit
original_content: You've gotta get to this place when in Hanoi. It's where all the locals come to hang out and eat icecream while sitting on their motorbikes - from young couples, teenagers and families. Try both the icy blocks of tasty kem (only 7k VND) - which come in delicious chocolate, coconut, young sticky rice - and I think another couple of flavours I didn't get to - as well as the soft serve (12k VND) which is equally delicious. You can takeaway the ice blocks too - if they can survive the weather.
highlights: delicious chocolate, coconut, young sticky rice
practical_tips: try both the icy blocks and soft serve
takeaway the ice blocks if they can survive the weather

author: Wander20
title: Worth trying
original_content: I went there after dinner and the place was very crowed with teenagers. People buy their ice cream and then stand and eat there, a really cool place to visit. The ice cream is really cheap and worth trying.

author: Mark N
title: Good
original_content: Cool place for stopping by. Really cheap for a delicious ice cream. It's just interesting whether eat inside the place on your scooter or take it out and eat when walking through the street of Hanoi. Like it.
practical_tips: eat inside the place on your scooter
take it out and eat when walking through the street

author: Happy
title: Great Local Ice Cream
original_content: This place is a hot among locals. Try all flavors. I love the coconut ice cream best. You have a choice of ice cream on a stick or on a cone. Several flavors: chocolate, green rice, vanilla, yam and coconut.
highlights: I love the coconut ice cream best

author: WBAfan
title: Heaven Nectar
original_content:
Kem (ice cream) Trang Tien (the street name) is utterly incredible! I don't think I have ever put anything quite like it into my mouth. 

There is just the perfect amount of coconut (which I am not usually a fan of) in every scoop which makes every Kem just so refreshing in the Hanoi heat. And the best part? Each ice cream costs only 12K dong. They're practically giving it away, which really makes Kem Trang Tien a philanthropic organisation.

Many of my best memories from Hanoi involve a Kem Trang Tien in each hand.

author: tiggo71
title: The pearl of Ha Noi
original_content:
This icecream was recommended to a group of us by a friend before we came to Ha Noi. We are now considering buying him a knighthood after this recommendation. 

The experience alone is brilliant, walking into a shop devoted entirely to icecream that you can drive into as well! It is incredibly busy most.of the time which demonstrates its popularity- they employ guards to help organise the masses on very busy days!! 

The icecream is coconut based and is incredibly refreshing on a hot day in Ha Noi. There are various types of icecream from lollies to Mr whippy style and the original incredible icecream. Over the space of 3 weeks in the area we must have visited the shop 10 times. 

It sounds silly but it was genuinely the highlight of Ha Noi for us! Do yourself a favour a visit this behemoth of an icecream palace.
practical_tips: visit this behemoth of an icecream palace

author: Traveller_Monkey_123
title: Cheap yummy ice cream!
original_content:
Walked by and saw numerous people rushing to get ice cream. Have never seen so many people enjoy ice cream at the same time at the same place. Service was quick despite the people.

Had the coconut and green tea flavours. Both very refreshing. The cone tasted like fortune cookies.

author: Alejandro E
title: Absolutely awsome icecream.
original_content:
I really enjoyed. Good quality icecream. Worthit trying it.
Very popular between the locals . Never seen sommany people buying icecream at the same time. An experience. Give it a try!!!

author: cutia
title: Anthropological experience
original_content:
Have you ever wondered what it's like to have ice cream in a parking lot / warehouse, with Vietnamese youngsters happily sitting on their parked motorbikes while enjoying their "kem com"?

Look no further, this is the place for you. Apart from the odd environment, this is by far the best ice cream flavor around. I know that "green rice ice cream" doesn't sound too appealing, but actually "kem com" tastes like a mix of sweet corn and coconut. Definitely worth the try!
highlights: kem com tastes like a mix of sweet corn and coconut

author: jimbothegreat
title: Nice ice cream
original_content: We saw lots of locals eating ice cream here at 9pm so thought we would give it a go.  12 dong for a single scoop cone.  We thought the cone was mouldy but apparently its sesame?  Ice cream tasted good though.  Coconutty!

author: Johnny P
title: Cheap and Good Local Ice cream
original_content: Local Ice cream in Vietnam is so special, tasty and cheap. amazing from ice cream near lake. It so cool for walk around lake with ice cream. Good

author: PacificBlackBird
title: Coconut milk ice cream in a motorcycle park!
original_content: Apparently here since 1959, and popular with every generation. 12K for a cone with one ball; they are batch prepared, and appear to have only one flavour in the garage (vanilla, but with a strong coconut taste since that's the base). More available at the adjacent Key Coffee, but without the experience. I will remember the place more than the ice cream, but good ice cream appears hard to find... Worth a visit.
highlights: good ice cream appears hard to find
practical_tips: go to Key Coffee for more options

author: CHandGT
title: Bad ice cream in a car park
original_content:
Ice cream in an underground car park. Cheap not worth going to as the ice cream is very chalky. There are 3/4 different ice cream stations serving different types of ice creams and flavours.

No idea what all the good reviews are about

author: PuzzleSolver855
title: Visit this crazy place for the experience not the ice cream
original_content: This is an underground garage that motorbikes pull into, buses expel groups of tourists and chaos ensues!  There is a 2nd level with a bathroom and a couple of seats.  Plan to just stand after you purchase your soft or hard ice cream from one of the 4 vendors spread around the garage.  Don't stop at the entryway to buy it...go on in and have the experience.  We were there before lunchtime and it was packed.  The ice cream wasn't worthy of this but who knew???
practical_tips: go on in and have the experience
don't stop at the entryway to buy it

author: chen611
title: Excellent coconut ice cream
original_content: The ice cream here are a mix between vanilla and coconut. It is creamy and icy at the same time. The mix is perfect. There is a board with names of different flavors but it is hard to tell whether you can order these other flavors.
drawbacks: hard to tell whether you can order other flavors
highlights: perfect mix of vanilla and coconut
creamy and icy at the same time
practical_tips: check the board for flavor options

author: Chattler
title: Best vanilla ice cream ever!
original_content: It's hard to describe how good the ice cream here is. I went twice and always got vanilla ice cream in a cone. Why? Because that's by far the most popular choice and it's worth it. If you like ice cream then don't miss this!
practical_tips: get vanilla ice cream in a cone

author: luiting
title: Coconut ice cream!
original_content: Super good ice cream, cheap cheap too! Took a cab there and the place was not easily spotted. Motorbikes could go in there too! It was really cool, and a good find as well!

author: harriethoughton
title: Going to miss this place!
original_content: The icecream here is so tasty that we've been going every night we've been in Hanoi! They have a fair few different flavours ranging from 7000 - 12000d each but we definitely recommend the coconut/vanilla in the sesame cone. We're usually the only tourists there but it does get busy with locals especially on weekends! Try and get a seat upstairs if you can
practical_tips: try and get a seat upstairs

author: Robert C
title: Pretty good but must have been off-peak
original_content: Besides the ice cream bars all they had were pre-made cones of coconut/vanilla flavor. Quite good with the iciness of home made. There were no crowds, thankfully. I'm not sure I'd be happy waiting in a horrendous line for this treat. If you're in the neighborhood and don't have to queue up like you're at the Hajj, then go for it.

author: Goonerfoodie
title: Delicious Ice Cream
original_content: Someone I met in Hanoi mentioned that the ice cream here is really good and when we were in the vicinity, I asked our Tour Guide to take us there. It was coconut Ice Cream and we tried almost all the flavors they had. Ice Cream was delicious. Try it with the cone.

author: Ozzy-Kunnu
title: A MUST MUST MUST HAVE...like really a MUST HAVE
original_content:
P.S. - Try anything and everything here BUT Do Not Miss their Coconut Ice Cream served in Sesame Cones...its Out of this World...something that we had not had anywhere.

Its little tricky to find this place since there are few of them, all far away and we had almost given up until we realized there is one very close to Hoan Kiem Lake (also known as Lake of the Restored Sword). Depending on which corner of lake you are it shall not take more than 6 to 15 minutes walk to reach this Ice Cream parlor. This place is MASSIVE (though, few eating joints on the same footpath as to where this humongous place is, sell candies made by this brand but suggestion is to go this place), and it's only when you reach this place you realize how famous this brand is looking at the crowd. 

Just go for anything and everything but make sure you have the coconut ice-cream in sesame cone. Their softies taste of artificial flavors and we would suggest against it but choice is yours.
highlights: Coconut Ice Cream served in Sesame Cones

author: linhvu9x
title: When you are in Hoan Kiem Lake, please quickly find Trang Tien ice cream and enjoy one scoop or a freezy cone ice cream
original_content: Trang Tien Ice Cream becomes one of famous symbols for Hanoi since 1985 so when you wander in Hoan Kiem Lake/ Sword Lake, you absolutely must try the delicious from Trang Tien cone ice cream. Yummy a lot.
highlights: delicious from Trang Tien cone ice cream
practical_tips: try the delicious from Trang Tien cone ice cream

author: adelinecms
title: Coconut Popsicle must not missed
original_content:
Situated in between the shops of Trang Tien Road.
You will not missed it coz many motorbikes are riding in & out.  There are 4 types of ice cream in the place.  They have Popsicle, Softee, Ice-cream cone & Mochi. I highly recommended the coconut Popsicle and you taste coconut bits.

author: Uday T
title: Strange place but great ice cream
original_content:
I was taken here by local friends. It is a big space and I thought we were going into a garage - lots of bikes parked in there
Lots of choice of ice cream but I decided to try a local flavour - sticky rice
This is a green ice cream - made from the October rice harvest (which is celebrated here) and it is young and green in colour
The ice cream has an unusual but delicious flavour
well worth seeking out
It is also incredibly cheap

author: Linnidity
title: Interesting local ice cream den experience
original_content: It was like an other worldly ice cream experience. There were so many motorbikes parked in rows and rows inside, outside. It kinda resembled an illegal gambling den. But no, it was just a crowd of locals getting their ice cream fix. The ice cream was cheap, at 12,000VND iirc although mine cost a bit more than that because the lady didn't have any change (told to me in vietnamese which I totally did not understand so I was bewildered as I left the queue). My friend managed to snag his for 10,000VND for the same reason. So bringing exact change is recommended. Worth a go just for the experience. Coconut ice cream was okay, a bit more icy than what I am used to. The sesame cone was yummy. Also tried the taro soft serve. I didn't fancy it that much but my friend preferred it to the original.
extracted_spaces: motorbikes parked in rows and rows inside, outside

author: Cara O
title: Unique Ice Cream cone
original_content: Loved the ice cream cone which had an Asian sesame twist to it. Ice cream itself was mediocre -  McDonald's has better.

author: Sati77
title: A must in hanoi
original_content:
The packed one is hidden inside compared to the other stalls in front  in trang tien street and seems the inner one has more ice cream types (cones, sticks, etc). Just get in and you will see a lot of locals enjoying the ice cream. I tried vanilla strawberry on cones and Mung bean i guess on sticks. Ice cream stick flavors are written in Vietnamese and staffs dont speak English, so i just picked randomly. Ones on cones had English version written for strawberry, vanilla and taro. The fourth flavor, not written in  i guess is chocolate. Both were great although i prefer ones on cones.  ice cream stick  had strong butter taste and too hard texture taking long time to soften and to finish up unless you bite them,while cone ones had very soft texture and ice cream cone had a great taste of sesame although i did not see the sesame. Maybe it was blended along with other ingredient. Ice cream stick cost 7000 to 8000 dong while cones that i had cost me 10000 dong.
Its located near hoa kim lake and also hoa lo prison. Worth a try to accompany you strolling along the area as no seats are provided on the one i visited.
drawbacks: Hard texture of ice cream stick
Long wait time to soften ice cream stick
highlights: Soft texture of ice cream cones
Great taste of sesame in ice cream cones
practical_tips: Be prepared for a long time to soften the ice cream stick

author: Joni11311
title: Local Ice-cream
original_content: Enjoy ice-cream with the locals. The place is run-down but the ice-cream is good and the price is reasonable. They have 4 flavour a hut I'm not sure what are the flavours because I don't understand the language. Hehehehe....

author: sbx7
title: A surprise find
original_content: We saw a place where lots of motorbikes were driving into, and walked in to see what was going on. Turns out to be a very popular ice cream shop. The coconut ice cream we had was very nice!
highlights: coconut ice cream was very nice

author: Tony Y
title: Quality of this local ice cream still as good as it was !
original_content: Had the coconut flavour ice-cream in my first visit to Hanoi in 1998, and learned the Vietnamese word "kem cao cap"  ..... meaning "quality ice-cream". Took it again in my recent visit in August 2015 ...... 17 years later.  Same excellent taste ....... obviously soft and "creamy" coconut flavour - local style.  Worth a try ...... different from the Western Movenpick, Baiskin Robbins, Haagen Dazs, etc...... the shop still crowded with locals especially in the evening. Do what the locals do !!!!!!!

author: WinnieTan
title: Yummy refreshing ice cream
original_content: It's a must try if u r a tourist in Hanoi. The ice cream is light and refreshing. Yes, it melts so quickly! May be it more like a sorbet with more water content than cream. Or may be it's more natural... What's also nice is the sesame cone. It has such a strong sesame taste. It compliments t coconut ice cream somehow. My 8 year old loves it too! Go try it. Yum !
drawbacks: more like a sorbet with more water content than cream
highlights: sesame cone has a strong sesame taste

author: betoecarnavalero
title: A twist from Phó and Bah My
original_content: Is a nice local restaurant full by locals, a diferent food after only phó and Bah My. The owner super kind to show the food and how to eat it

author: Life traveller
title: Nice coconut ice cream, famous among the Vietnamese
original_content: This is worth a visit, as it is a famous ice cream parlour in the centre of Hanoi. The coconut ice cream is very nice, and the sesame cone crunchy! For a famous ice cream place in a smart area of town, it is a bit of a dump! When my vietnamese friend took me there, I thought is looked like a run down garage. Perhaps I was being a bit snooty, as this is a place for the locals rather than tourists. So, if you are a tourist, then in my view worth a visit!
drawbacks: looked like a run down garage
highlights: coconut ice cream is very nice
practical_tips: go there if you are a tourist

author: travelh00ked
title: Coconut icecream in sesame cones!
original_content:
These were absolutely delicious! The ice cream was light and the cone was crisp with toasted sesame seeds. Yummm.

The only thing I didn't like was that the lady serving the ice cream didn't even wear gloves and used the same hand she used for taking payments! I ate the icecream and just the tip of the cone but the rest of it went into a trash bin (what a shame).
drawbacks: The lady serving the ice cream didn't even wear gloves and used the same hand she used for taking payments!
The rest of the cone went into a trash bin
highlights: The cone was crisp with toasted sesame seeds

author: Audrey B
title: Ice cream that's perfect for a hot day!
original_content: The ice cream was great and I would recommend it but the shop and the variety (not much) that is offered was somehow less than I was expecting after being told that it was a famous place in Hanoi.  They have the pre packaged ice cream bars in about 6-7 flavors and if you want an ice cream cone then it's just vanilla or chocolate.  On the two occasions that I was there not many people were inside and there is not much of an environment to the building itself - pretty bland.  Most people just drive up on their scooters and then take off again.  I would still say it's worth a trip there and a very nice treat on a hot day in Hanoi!

author: Art L
title: Lovely Ice Cream - must try! But eat fast!
original_content: I was here with my family (wife and 4 yr old)... i thought it was really delicious as did the 4 yr old, although my wife was less than impressed. There's no where to sit and enjoy the dessert. There's a fast moving queue with locals buying ice cream by the dozens. The ice cream melts really fast so eat it quickly. Also the price is now VND12000... get the ice cram with a cone as i thought the cone was very unique and tasted great. Lots of young locals patronize this place...
drawbacks: no where to sit and enjoy the dessert
practical_tips: get the ice cram with a cone

author: eddyphdhong
title: in fact I don't understand why vietnameses live this icecream shop
original_content: in fact I don't understand why vietnameses live this icecream shop. so and so taste. dirty and noisy shop. not clean environment. so hot and no air conditioning. they must earn big money from hanoi people but don't change so and so interior and so and do taste. but whenever my friends visited hanoi, i brought them here. cuz famous.
drawbacks: so hot and no air conditioning

author: Lee Voon F
title: Nice ice cream!
original_content:
Normally am not a fan of ice cream, but this is pretty good. I had it on 3 separate occasions during our 4 days stay in hanoi. The best part of the ice cream was the cone, which was very fresh crunchy and tasty.

Go for the vanilla flavour only, forget the others.
practical_tips: Go for the vanilla flavour only

author: 334shellyl
title: Good ice cream, no ambiance
original_content: Good vanilla ice cream cones that taste a little like coconut. It's a very popular stop for the locals. However, the establishment is a bit weird. There's nowhere to sit and it looks a bit like a parking garage. So don't go if you are looking for a nice place to eat ice cream and relax, but do go if you are simply after a good ice cream cone.
drawbacks: looks a bit like a parking garage
not a nice place to eat ice cream and relax
practical_tips: don't go if you are looking for a nice place to eat ice cream and relax
go if you are simply after a good ice cream cone

author: bigboi90
title: Fresh and natural
original_content: The most famous local brand, 50 cent for a vanilla cone is a very good deal. Not my taste but worth a try.

author: zirconiag
title: Yum yum
original_content: Is a Vietnamese Popsicle. They only have 2 flavours when we were there - vanilla and chocolate. I rather enjoy it because it wasn't too sweet.
drawbacks: Not too sweet for some people

author: Kelley H
title: Local favourite
original_content: Best place in town to get ice cream. They have different types available, the most popular being the coconut cone, as well as some fruit flavoured ice cream bars. All available for around 12k VND, it's definitely worth the cost. Grab a cone and enjoy a walk around Hoan Kiem from there!
highlights: enjoy a walk around Hoan Kiem
practical_tips: grab a cone and enjoy a walk around Hoan Kiem

author: tda7
title: Coconut icecream
original_content: Apparently a favourite with locals. The simple coconut ice cream in a cone (priced at 12000 Dong) is delicious and perfect after a good meal or a long walk (any excuse, really!). The surprise was the delicious cone it came in - delicate, fresh with a hint of sesame. Enjoy!
extracted_spaces: The simple coconut ice cream in a cone
highlights: delicious and perfect after a good meal
delicious cone it came in - delicate, fresh with a hint of sesame

author: CoolGuy
title: Cheap and nice coconut ice cream
original_content: Cheap and nice coccnut ice cream. Location is easily accessible. It is very popular with the locals.
highlights: Cheap and nice coccnut ice cream

author: Marc U
country: New York City, New York, USA
title: For Locals
original_content: This may be one of the most local ice-cream shop I have ever visited. Walking into a small open space, there are three stands – one for each type of ice cream they serve: soft serve, hard,  and on a stick. Here the locals grab an ice cream to hang out and cool off. The experience of really not feeling like a tourist and enjoying this refreshing snack on a hot and humid day may have been better than the ice cream.
drawbacks: The experience of really not feeling like a tourist and enjoying this refreshing snack on a hot and humid day may have been better than the ice cream.
highlights: really not feeling like a tourist
enjoying this refreshing snack on a hot and humid day

author: migigawa
title: A Hanoi Institution
original_content: "Kem" means ice cream, in Vietnamese, apparently, and if Hanoians have a thing fir coffee and street food, ice cream has also got to rank high up there. Kem Trang Tien is one of the best places for regular ice cream. The fancy, artisanal ice cream parlors like Fanny's may be better, and way more expensive, but KTT is the authentic local favorite. Drive straight into the place on your scooter, or climb upstairs to the balcony area and watch the locals take their ice cream seriously! Highly recommended for an energy pick-me-upper after a hot and humid day on your feet. It's a no-frills place, just go there for the great but cheap ice cream. it is located though, right on bookstore and art gallery row, near the southernmost tip of Hosn Kiem lake, near the Opera House, so it is pretty nesr where you will want to be, anyway.
practical_tips: go there for the great but cheap ice cream
drive straight into the place on your scooter
climb upstairs to the balcony area

author: Jennie D
title: Best local ice-cream :)
original_content:
"Trang Tien Ice-cream" is a local ice-cream company in Hanoi since 1958. The name 'Trang Tien Ice-cream" came from the street "Trang Tien" where the ice-cream was manufactured and sold (first location was #35 Trang Tien Street, Hoan Kiem District). "Trang Tien Ice-cream" became very popular and familiar with Hanoians. To every kids that grew up in Hanoi, "Trang Tien Ice-cream" attached and became a part of the childhoods. "Trang Tien Ice-cream" has many flavors such as: chocolate, vanilla, coconut milk young rice and the price is very cheap :)

So many placed try to make fake "Trang Tien Ice-cream"; so to get the real one you should go to No. 35 Trang Tien Street...You will have to queue for it, it may take a while but I promise it worths to try. You'll find it always crowded not only in the summer but in the winter as well. While you enjoying the ice-cream, you can take a walk in Trang Tien street where there are many local art galleries, souvenirs, book shops. You can walk to Hoan Kiem Lake or the Opera House which is only 5-10mins walk. Especially during this season Autumn comes to Winter, it's really beautiful :)
drawbacks: You will have to queue for it
practical_tips: go to No. 35 Trang Tien Street
walk to Hoan Kiem Lake or the Opera House

author: Namit1984
title: Plain, simple and delicious
original_content: This is a drive-in (or walk-in) ice cream parlor near Opera House. They serve vanilla flavored ice cream cones which is absolutely delicious. This place is thronged by locals in the evenings.

author: Kickingkyle
title: Unique experience

author: Melisa Travel
title: cheap and delicious ice cream

author: atripwithme
title: MUST-HAVE ICE CREAM FOR ICE CREAM LOVERS
original_content:
i think that this place serves one of the best ice cream cones ever. it isn't really difficult to find this place cause its near the Hoan Kiem Lake and near the famous Trang Tien Plaza with all the expensive goods. This place is so unique cause there isn't any seats for you to settle down on your ice cream but rather its a place to just buy and go or just stand around eating it. Motorbikes are the bulk of the customers here. 
Now to the juicy and yummiest bit, the ice cream~~ 
it's that good cause the ice cream feels like soft serve but doesn't look like that. It really is delish with the cone because the cones have sesame in them and they taste and smell great! It's just 12kVND for a single cone, just slightly more than 50 cents USD. 
There happens to be 3 stalls inside that sells ice cream, but the original ones are the ones that sell the cone in the center of the place, with a price of 12k VND. There is also another surprise, because they have takeaway boxes of many many flavours that are only at 40k VND. Those are called Kem Hop. 
The staff there can understand English and are more than willing to help you get your hands on those ice cream. Even better when you get it on a hot summer day like now!
highlights: soft serve but doesn't look like that

author: CocoonHanoi
title: Unique icecream place

author: vodoxus
title: Quaint little ice cream place

author: Kyle K
title: Delicious and unique local treats
original_content: We spent a week in Hanoi and visited this place on at least four occasions. Absolutely delicious and unique. The staple here is a scoop of coconut ice cream (not vanilla as stated in other reviews) in a sesame waffle cone for around 55 cents US. The ice cream itself is light and refreshing, more ice than cream based (might even be made with coconut milk) and it gives the unique sensation of being frozen solid but melting instantly in your mouth. The cone is no disappointment either, a sesame seed infused waffle cone that is crisp and tasty and compliments the coconut perfectly. It is absolutely delicious and something that must be tried in Hanoi. They also have popsicles in a variety of local flavors and soft serve but the coconut cone is the highlight. It might be my favorite ice cream ever. Seriously.
highlights: The staple here is a scoop of coconut ice cream in a sesame waffle cone for around 55 cents US
The ice cream itself is light and refreshing, more ice than cream based
practical_tips: Try the coconut cone, it's a must-try in Hanoi
Go for the coconut ice cream in a sesame waffle cone

author: Kiku C
title: A Real Local Delight!
original_content:
it's down a dingy lane with many motorbikes coming in and out, so if you're from a very developed country, and grew up with your parents telling  you not to wander down dingy alleys, you may just miss this.

There will be two queues. One is in front - those are ice cream popsicles. On the right, it's ice cream cones - give the ice cream cones a try! It's called "kem oc que" (like "creme ock kway") - it's creamy but light, and it's on a crepe. Worth every penny :)

If you go for a popsicle, there's rice, green tea, green bean and chocolate. Also worth a try. Had like 3 ice creams during my 4 days here. 

After buying your ice cream, people watch in a corner - no seats in this place, so many people bring their bikes in, and sit around on their bikes and chat while the eat.
practical_tips: give the ice cream cones a try

author: Banskali
title: THE ice-cream spot in Hanoi!
original_content:
I had to go to the place 3 times to be successful! The first time someone in the old town had told me that there was a famous ice cream parlour on the street leading to the opera and that they would have my favourite ice-cream "durian" (from that awkward, smelly Asian fruit that divides people in lovers and haters).

I could not find the place! After doing some research on the internet I went again, two days later. I realised now why I had not found it. Because it is in the indoors yard of a big building. In fact you can even take your motorbike inside. 

I felt happy and relieved. But only for a little while! They have 5 or 6 stalls where they sell their ice cream there. And NOBODY in the whole complex speaks English. And, of course, I had not taken into account that "durian" has a different name in Vietnamese! So, no joy! Nobody understood my pleading and beckoning and I had to leave empty-handed!

More research! Equipped with the Vietnamese name (sau rieng) I went there for the third time a few days later. And: no problem. I had my cone of durian ice on no time :)

Alas, I was not too carried away with its taste. Very bland and hardly any particular durian taste. I had had much better (and cheaper) ones in Thailand. But then, I also read somewhere that the durians in Vietnam generally are not as good as in the neighbouring countries.  I cannot verify that, really.

I ended up disappointed after a lot of effort. But you may be very happy with your experience. Apart from the morning hours this place is packed with Vietnamese. They obviously adore the ice...
extracted_spaces: indoors yard of a big building
drawbacks: Nobody in the whole complex speaks English
I had not taken into account that "durian" has a different name in Vietnamese
Very bland and hardly any particular durian taste
highlights: I had my cone of durian ice on no time

author: Patrick D
title: statue of King Ly Thai To
original_content: The statue of King Ly Thai To is located in Ly Thai To Garden, Dinh Tien Hoang Street , next to the town hallThis statue aims to honour King Ly Thai To (974 – 1028). ,first king who found Capital Citadel of Thang Long (Hanoi today).In February, 2003, the Hanoi Department of Culture and Information launched a contest to design the statue of King Ly Thai To. The design of sculptor Vi Thi Hoa (Vietnam Fine Arts Association) was selected from 29 other designs. The statue was cast on August  2004 and inaugurated on October 2004. This is the biggest pure bronze statue in Vietnam with weight of 34 tons , height of 10.m . The number 1010 corresponds with foundation year of the Capital Citadel of Thang Long.The octagonal estrade represents 8 directions , the statue portrays King Ly Thai To whose right hand holds Chieu doi do (Decree on the capital’s relocation) and left hand is pointed at the location to found the capital. The statute is the cultural work to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Hanoi’s liberation day (10/10/1954 – 10/10/2004) and lead-up to the 1000th anniversary of Thang Long – Hanoi (1010-
highlights: biggest pure bronze statue in Vietnam

author: bunko007
