There are many photo opportunities with ‘love’ theme set ups. If you’re brave enough, there’s a glass floor interior deck that you can walk out on and look down and over the city. A great sight of West Lake as a love heart which is cute.
practical_tips: go to the supermarket and food court before going to the observation deck

author: John M
title: Good view of the city, weather permitting
original_content: A very impressive building in any country, this is the best view of the city, weather permitting, although our night time photos were not any good. Korean owned, the boss of the company was in the news for money fraud, but no word of that in Vietnamese news!
extracted_spaces: the best view of the city
drawbacks: no word of that in Vietnamese news
our night time photos were not any good

author: chae84
title: Good view of city
original_content: I guess here is the only place where you can view the city from the top. View at night is more stunning compare in the evening/morning. We spent couples of hours until 8 where the light of the city is clearly bright. price of the ticket a bit expensive but the photo and experience is more than that.
drawbacks: price of the ticket a bit expensive
highlights: view at night is more stunning
photo and experience is more than that
practical_tips: go at night for a more stunning view

author: ArujChoudhary
title: gratified
original_content: Do get snapped by the camera on top those pics will be better anyways. Wow what a view , i grabbed a beer and sat for an hor there... u should also go for sure.

author: kimbeanz
title: Lotte Observation Deck
original_content: If you want a great view of Hanoi, this is the place!! Although it was slightly far from the Old Quarters which is where most tourists would be at, it was not bad a trip! This place would be good for seeing the sunset- hopefully it wouldn't be too cloudy during your visit. However, the price to go up is rather steep. But then again, the place is great for taking photos so it's up to you! The observation deck is good for couples to spend a little quality time together and taking photos together.
drawbacks: price to go up is rather steep
highlights: good for couples to spend quality time together

author: joel s
title: Heaven!!
original_content: Amazing view from the top!! Worth visiting if you are in Hanoi.Prefer day visit, as pics r nice and also do try burger Ar Lotte foodstall at top (reasonable price)

author: Oleksandr T
title: Great view
original_content: Absolutely amazing view from the top of Hanoi!Must visit!Could see all Hanoi like on your hand:)It costs a bit of money(around 10$), but it definitely worth it!
drawbacks: It costs a bit of money

author: Melbguy3805
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Went at night and the views of the city are great and was only 230k dong. Well worth a visit.Only downside was when trying to take a picture, the reflection of the windows was constant which was a little annoying.
drawbacks: the reflection of the windows was constant which was a little annoying
highlights: the views of the city are great

author: jlizaso
title: Awesome view
original_content: I was with my wife and we learned about the observation deck in the Lotte Center Mall so we went and checked it out.Though it is not the Burgh Al Khalifa in UAE, but the place provides a very nice overlooking view of Hanoi, I think the entrance fee is a bit pricey, never the less it was a good experience. You get a 360 view as you go around the deck and they have the scopes to zoom in to specific area of interest. There were to section with glass floors and it felt a bit scary at first and you have to take of your shoes to walk the area.It was a nice feeling after you get used to it but my wife have shaky knees that she only stayed up to the edge of the glass floor and went back. Took some good photos and we spent a bit more time until I could get a blue hour photo of the scenic view.I can recommend the place for other tourists.
drawbacks: entrance fee is a bit pricey
practical_tips: take off your shoes to walk the glass floor area

author: boonchai t
title: Staff very helpfull and good service also good view
original_content: My phone has been lost in Taxi that i use to came to Lotte Tower i know my phone is already lost after i arrive 65 floor, im tried to contact my phone because im open Roaming but unfortunate the driver unable to speak English that why the staff name “Tran Thi Quynh Huong” come and help me to be translator untill finally i get my phone back with a lot of important information data in there, she doesn’t recive my prize that make me more impress to her, and all staff there is very helpfull too by the way view up there is very super cool i can ensure you can get a great picture if you go there 65 floor.
practical_tips: Go to 65 floor for great view
Staff may be able to assist with language issues

author: leelanc2018
title: Beautiful stunning view of Hanoi.
original_content: Wow! What a beautiful stunning view of Hanoi. One of the main attractions to see whole Hanoi is at the Lotte Observation Deck.

author: bonvojaage
title: Dizzying view, but bit expensive tickets
original_content: A great place the see the whole Hanoi in a glance. Walking on the glassfloor in the 65th floor is a nice photo and selfie opportunity. We found it but difficult to find the elevator up, since it's not in the street level of Lotte Center, but in the bottom floor (...entrance is marked clearly outside the building, but not when you are inside the department store) Tickets at 230.000 VDN (about 8 Euros) felt expensive compared to the general price level in Hanoi
drawbacks: difficult to find the elevator up
tickets felt expensive compared to the general price level in Hanoi
practical_tips: entrance is marked clearly outside the building, but not when you are inside the department store

author: Matlock1lady
title: Amazing views
original_content: We went at about 9 am and had the place virtually to ourselves. A ticket purchased on the ground floor and the a lift up. They have glass floor walkouts and it took us a white to step out. We took our pictures but they insist that you have one taken ‘ free’ , but of course if you want a copy you pay. We didn’t bother as our photos were good.No time limit up there and you can get coffe and a meal if you want. I bet we stayed a couple of hours. This was one of Hanoi highlights.I found it online and we just grabbed a taxi from our hotel to get there.
drawbacks: They insist that you have one taken ‘free’ , but of course if you want a copy you pay
practical_tips: No time limit up there and you can get coffe and a meal if you want

author: Olli J.
title: Very impressive view
original_content: If you are looking for an unforgatable view through Hanoi you have to visit the Lotte tower observation deck. You can find there a bar and coffee as well but to be honest, if you’re there do the skywalk - just for those who are NOT afraid of heights :) ... highly recommended

author: Chibikiu
title: Good place to see Hanoi from above
original_content: Definitely best place to see Hanoi from above, and you can try the Sky Walk. You can get some fun facts about Hanoi which is good. However, It is more expensive for foreigner than local. And there is only some cafe here cause I expected there will be some cocktail or wine.
drawbacks: more expensive for foreigner than local
highlights: best place to see Hanoi from above

author: Cherrychan0214
title: First time to experience walking on glass on the 65th floor
original_content: if you are afraid of height, i would suggest you better not go. it is the first time i experienced to walk on the glass, clear crystal glass, on the 65th floor. it can be quite scary.pity that it was too foggy when we visited, so we did not really see the view clearly. otherwise it would be a very good experience.some of the equipments there are not working. e.g. there is a scanner that you can scan your ticket and leave your comments there plus taking your photo. but it just doens't work.there are some souvenir shops also, which is expected.afterall, it is a good place. i am also the kind of person who love going to observation deck. seems it is the only one in hanoi. don't think there are other buildings that is as tall. you can also visit the lotte mart at the basement to do some shopping, not to say the lotte department.highly recommend it.
drawbacks: did not see the view clearly due to fog

author: Widlydidly
title: Great night time view of Hanoi
original_content: We enjoyed the whole experience, went up in the evening, more romantic. The sky was clear and dark. The roads below glistened with the legendary Hanoi traffic. We did the glass box, amazing. The whole cost was cheap by UK standards. My only problem was not getting to the rooftop. Signage was very poor and the staff understandably had little English, not thier fault. I would reccommend this to visitors to Hanoi.

author: Jas L
title: Fun & thrilling experience
original_content: The view was not clear that day due to the weather but that didn't dampen our mood. We had so much fun & spent so much time just on the glass skydeck itself; walking & lying around, taking pictures from various angles, watching people trying to overcome their fear of heights by hanging onto the wall & taking one small step at a time.We also like the interactive activity where you can enter a message into the computer and it would appear on the big screen. We would then try to squeeze in to take a picture with our personalised message behind us. Overall, pleasantly surprised that we managed to spend so many hours at this place. Not cheap as compared to other attractions but worthwhile to visit & would recommend.
drawbacks: view was not clear that day due to the weather

author: AdinaHagege
title: Cool Feeling On Top of the World
original_content: Really nice views of Hanoi, cool glass-decked floor. But not a whole lot to DO--1/2 hour of fun and coolness was a bit pricey.
drawbacks: not a whole lot to DO

author: Jo D
title: Lotte Observation - excellent place to view lakes and areas of Hanoi. Glass skydeck too.
original_content: Entrance fee about £7 per person. Well worth it. We spent over an hour up on the deck; the place was very quiet - maybe only 5 other people up there with us. Great views out across the whole city, bar, coffee, gifts, photo opportunities all around as you'd expect.Two glass skydecks - one that comes with an official photographer which we didn't 'play on'.  Scary but great to do...About 65 floors up if I remember.  Recommended. Would need a taxi trip out though from Old Quarter. We walked - we should have taken a cab.
highlights: Great views out across the whole city
practical_tips: Take a taxi trip out from Old Quarter

author: Yas
title: Great view!
original_content: I went to Observation deck at around 4pm and stayed till 6.30. I am glad I chose to go  during day time as after sunset the city is not that lightened .. all you can see are the lights coming from some towers and the car lights. So it doesn’t offer a great view in the evening, although the atmosphere is still magical anyhow.i recommend the place! It is expensive compared to the entrance fees of other sights in Hanoi, but it is still affordable (10 USD). You can have drinks and snacks up there also.
drawbacks: doesn't offer a great view in the evening

author: Sungho B
title: Amazing view and experience
original_content: Recommended. Sky walk and love heart zone. beautiful view from 272m on sky. Sky walk experience was amazing..

author: DaisyEdwards222
title: Wonderful
original_content: A place to go when coming to Vietnam, I find the space here is very pleasant, very comfortable, watching Hanoi on high is great.
highlights: watching Hanoi on high is great

author: Daoni Nguyen
title: Awesome place
original_content: A place to see Hanoi in its globality, to learn about Hanoi, to see the contrast of its architecture. Treat yourself for some cool pictures!

author: stoops99
title: Spectacular views
original_content: Our daughter, who lives in Hanoi recommended a visit to the tower. We started off in the department store on the ground floor. They had 3 aisles of coffee!We caught a lift, then had to transfer to another lift to get to the rooftop on the 67th floor. We were on the roof just before sunset, and after some misty rain the sky cleared so we had spectacular views of the sunset and then the night lights of Hanoi while enjoying cocktails from the bar.We had a great evening and we were surprised at how large Hanoi actually is when viewed from above.Entry to the rooftop is free, unlike the observation deck, and the drinks from the rooftop bar were quite reasonably priced, so buying a few cocktails seemed like a better investment than the observation deck!
extracted_spaces: department store on the ground floor
highlights: spectacular views of the sunset and night lights of Hanoi
practical_tips: entry to the rooftop is free
buying a few cocktails from the rooftop bar is a good investment

author: Viet Vo
title: Beautiful Hanoi
original_content: My first time at Lotte Observation Deck and it was amazing. Decided to go up there after shopping at Lotte. But the cashier advised us to wait for 10 more minutes as the price goes down during night time and it was already dark anyways. Hard to see the whole city at night but it was still sparkling. My girlfriend and I were surely having fun exploring the sky walk, both excited and shaking at the same time. Would recommend this place to everyone.
drawbacks: Hard to see the whole city at night
highlights: having fun exploring the sky walk
practical_tips: go during night time for lower price

author: Coryy20
title: Thrilling
original_content: Wow went up to the to tower around 5pm so I could have seen day and night effects. I so was not disappointed. Wow the day was clear and u got to see Hanoi beautiful buildings from up high both day and night viewHowever the moist thrilling part of my visit was to walk on the glass...thats if you are brave enough..this was such a rush to walk out on the glass and see cars so  very small down below on the streets... really did enjoy this tower.. it reminded me a lot of one in Hong kong.. but this was more fun because of that piece of glass thst goes out of the building.Definitely a must do.
highlights: fun because of that piece of glass

title: Wow!
original_content: Great! 230,000 vnd about £8 so cheap for the the awesome views! Glass floor on 2 sides was amazing! Not as good as the viewing platform in Ho Chi Minh in my opinion but well worth a visit! Little bit out of the way, so take a taxi!
extracted_spaces: viewing platform in Ho Chi Minh
drawbacks: Little bit out of the way

author: mattnajd
title: Nice, Kinda Expensive for What It Is
original_content: Three of us went to the observatory today. It was nice. The glass floor was a cool experience and made for fun pictures. But 230,000 vnd is expensive to ride an elevator. Especially considering the cost of most other things in Vietnam. It was nice to see the city from this vantage point. But hard to relax and enjoy with the hot temperature inside the building and the kids running laps and yelling for 45 minutes straight.
highlights: nice to see the city from this vantage point

author: Benjamin B
title: Rooftop
original_content: Great location for having a great view over Hanoi. There you get the feeling, that Hanoi is not just the Old Quarter, but much more! If you want to enjoy drinks or food, the restaurant on top is all right. The prices are a bit to high for the quality of the food, but you pay for the great feeling of an open air restaurant. If you want to experience the glass balcony, you need to buy the tickets, which is absolutely recommendable, if you have never done this before.
drawbacks: prices are a bit too high for the quality of the food
practical_tips: buy tickets for the glass balcony
go to the restaurant on top for drinks or food

author: Traveller 912
title: A must when in Hanoi
original_content: A definite must when in Hanoi. Cheap entry. Amazing views! The clear glass viewing deck was scary as hell but so much fun!

author: misshazeyeyed
title: Must-do in Hanoi
original_content: When in Hanoi, visiting the Lotte Tower is an absolute must. It's a short drive from the Old Quarter (where most tourists stay) and for someone unaccustomed to Vietnam see public transport, such as myself, get yourself a driver. The Lotte Observation Deck sits over sixty floors above Hanoi and boasts breathtaking panoramic views. It's open day and night. We went at night and thoroughly recommend it. For a modest entrance fee, the observation deck offers interactive experiences for people young and old. The highlight for me was the glass skywalk, where you take your shoes off and walk right out into the night sky- not for anyone with vertigo! The Lotte tower also offers a range of eating options, so I recommend making an evening out of the experience. At the skydeck there's a fast food eatery or two, but if you delve a little deeper, you'll find award winning restaurants and bars within the Lotte tower- we went to Top Of Hanoi and had an excellent meal with stunning views.
practical_tips: make an evening out of the experience

author: NL_DINKS
title: Best 360' view over Hanoi in rooftop bat
original_content: Went with group of friendsYou really have full view over whole cityThe seats and lounge sets are very relaxed and modernPrice of drinks is as expected high for Vietnam standards, but worthwhile to see lights of the city, bridges, lakes etc
drawbacks: Price of drinks is as expected high for Vietnam standards
highlights: seats and lounge sets are very relaxed and modern

author: Traveling is a blessing
title: Beautiful night view
original_content: Went there around 625pm.The counter staff was friendly and help us to save money by telling us that the price will be half by 630pm. He told us to wait.The night view was splendid. We even took a photo at the glass floor where you can see all the way down.It is a pity that we did not manage to catch the sunset view.If you want to catch the sunset view, pay more and you can stay there from 6pm to 7pm to catch the great view.
drawbacks: did not manage to catch the sunset view
practical_tips: go early to catch sunset view
pay more to stay from 6pm to 7pm

author: Andrew M
title: Worth the effort.
original_content: I can see why you come to an observation deck as it puts the size if the city into a little perspective and where you fit in.  Sadly, Hanoi was having one of its misty days but the view was still worth the VND220,000.   This sky deck lacks the plan-o-grams of the city at each viewing location to help you orientate yourself.  That would make it so much better.  I also found the staff at the sky deck in Saigon far far far better.  Here they seemed a little distant.   The sky platform with the glass floor is quite confronting at first.  Over all we enjoyed it but it did lack some atmosphere.
highlights: puts the size of the city into perspective

author: Japai p
title: Breathtaking view
original_content: Only managed to go there on my 3rd visit to Hanoi. How i regret not going much earlierIt has amazing 360 view of Hanoi especially the one facing the Westlake.I had planned for a quick view but ended up taking my time (2 hours+) just enjoying the view and having few cups of tea.Took 2 of my boys along and yes they really enjoyed the experience.Must go place if u are around the area.For foreigners price was VND170k for kids n VND270k for adults
practical_tips: Must go place if u are around the area

author: Antoine F
title: What a point of view!
original_content: Amazing point of view. It offers a panoramic city view of Hanoï. You can realize how big the city is. Price : 230,000 VND during the day130,000 VND during the night
highlights: realize how big the city is

author: AndrewMyers1
title: Emotionally cold but with with most advances toilets on the 38th floor
original_content: After 3 days of very hot weather we decided we needed 5 star consumerism and air conditioningIt was like John Lewis upmarket with security guards and really lacking the customer care.This was expensive and not very pleasant experienceWe tried to go to 63 floor and the 'man' said it was a resteraunt  so no  quick drinkSo he informed us we could go to 38th and got in lift with usTea and couple of cocktails later we did have a great view but felt uncomfortable throughoutThe highlight was the most electronically advanced toilets Seat warmer ,front wash,back wash,dryer all controlled from a control panel next to toiletTried the oscillator button as well, but you can test that yourself There were two other buttons I was terrified they would play musicOverall the view ,the long drinks,the English books we bought and the great air conditioning make this a good two hour visit The electronic lavatory was memorable but does it count as progressThis felt like high security rather than anywhere near us customer care

author: Delilah W
title: Fab views
original_content: If you have time to kill in Hanoi then visit this place. Great views of the city- we visited in the evening and the views were spectacular. The sky walk is scary but fun.

author: Jeremy
title: Get high above it all.
original_content: On the top of the Lotte Centre is a bar high above the city. There is a nice open air vibe and DJ at night. They serve drinks and the view is really nice. A nice place to come for a break from the chaos on the street.
practical_tips: come for a break from the chaos on the street

author: Andy S
title: Skydeck
original_content: Best place to see the whole city from the top. Enter before sunset and stay there till night so you can see the city at 2 different side. Dark and light
highlights: see the whole city from the top

author: Kimbacat1
title: Vietnam trip
original_content: A must do. We went at night. Great and spectacular view of Hanoi.Floor 65. No souvenirs of the deck itself in the souvenir shop on that floor at that time. Would we go here again --- definite YES.
drawbacks: No souvenirs of the deck itself in the souvenir shop on that floor at that time

author: Andrew T
title: restaurant and rooftop bar. interesting
original_content: This was our first time up to the restaurant on level 63 and rooftop bar.  Great service and continental food.  We had a special meal well prepared of sirloin and basa that was excellent.  The view, service and ambience in the restaurant was good.  They had a live band playing at the right volume so it didn’t overwhelm the experience as many other places mess this up.  The rooftop could have been better if the original design allowed for more of a seating design on the edge for a more thrilling experience.  Anyways, it’s still a interesting panoramic view of the city.
drawbacks: The rooftop could have been better if the original design allowed for more of a seating design on the edge for a more thrilling experience.
highlights: live band playing at the right volume

author: Jordan F
title: Amazing view
original_content: We visited the observation deck right at 6:30- and it was the perfect time! We paid the lower fee, got to see the city in the light, saw the sunset, and stayed to see the city lights at night. There are 2 glass floor observation areas and they are great for photos. It is difficult to get good photos at night as there are a lot of lights on in the building and so there is a lot of reflection. If you want good photos definitely go during the day or during the sunset.
drawbacks: difficult to get good photos at night due to reflection from building lights
highlights: see the city in the light
see the city lights at night
practical_tips: go during the day or during the sunset for good photos

author: Chaarvi B
title: Great view of Hanoi, a must see!
original_content: Visited at around 530pm on a weekday. Wasn't too crowded. The evening rates were VND 130,000 for non-nationals. I think the day rates are 230,000/non-nationals. Tickets have to bought from the B1 floor of the Lotte Departmental store. It was a good time to visit, we saw the city in the day time as well as the early evening with all the lights! It definitely looks so so beautiful from that height. All the lakes and buildings look gorgeous. The glass floor are a fun experience but be warned, that it is quite scary if you don't like heights! There are also binoculars on the skydeck so can look in detail. Also a few eateries on the floor.
drawbacks: Scary if you don't like heights
practical_tips: Buy tickets from B1 floor of Lotte Departmental store
Use binoculars on skydeck for detailed view

author: lozliz7
title: Great View - loved the sky walk
original_content: We visited the observation deck early afternoon but beware it's quite a walk from Hanoi centre, particularly in the heat at this time of day! Recommend getting a taxi at least one way.When you do get there it's worth it though, what a view! Gives you some context around how big the city actually is. You can walk all the way round the floor to get a 360 degree view & there are 2 Sky Walks..... not for the faint hearted but can get you a great picture! Nice cafe on the floor too. Ps- the video in the lift makes for a unique experience !
extracted_times: heat at this time of day
drawbacks: quite a walk from Hanoi centre
highlights: gives you some context around how big the city actually is
can get you a great picture
practical_tips: get a taxi at least one way
walk all the way round the floor to get a 360 degree view

author: Wayne T
title: Great Views of Hanoi
original_content: We visited the Lotte Observation deck at around 1100 in the morning. Cost was VND 230,000 each. The entry is discounted in the evening. There were very few people visiting at the time so we practically had the place to ourselves. Views from the top were very clear allowing us to take some great photos. There are also 2 glass floors which allow a great view below...Unlike some towers I have visited, the observation level was nice and wide the entire way around so even if this was busy, I still think there would be plenty of room. There is a cafe and also a fast food restaurant. It was a nice spot to have a coffee afterwards.
highlights: nice and wide the entire way around
practically had the place to ourselves
practical_tips: go in the evening for discounted entry
consider visiting early in the morning for fewer crowds

author: fsanchezcv
title: Great spot. A must in Hanoi
original_content: The view of the city is amazing. You get a small discount if you visit after sunset, but the glare from the light inside blocks some of the views.
drawbacks: glare from the light inside blocks some of the views
highlights: view of the city is amazing
practical_tips: visit after sunset for a discount

author: Tony P
title: Beautiful views and amazing ambiance
original_content: We stayed at the Lotte for a business retreat.  While the hotel is first class all the way, the Observation Deck was something special.  The views of Hanoi were amazing.  The deck is set up very comfortably and as usual the friendly staff catered beyond our needs. We were part of a private group party and there was music, a DJ, dancers, disco lights... everything to make a great party.  One of the best parties ever... danced all night!
highlights: friendly staff catered beyond our needs

author: CHTrips
title: Lotte Observation Deck
original_content: It's away from the tourist area but a taxi ride (Uber) was only about $5. It's discounted entry after 5:30pm and you get to see excellent view of the entire city.  Also there are two area's that are suspended in the air that you can take pictures off of and lay on and take pictures.
highlights: excellent view of the entire city
two area's that are suspended in the air

author: jm
title: Birds eye view of Hanoi
original_content: Good view of Hanoi from the 65th floor of the sky deck. The view would be better if the didn't have so many lights at night, and turned down the loud music which spoils the view

author: Redviews
title: Good view point, pity about the smog
original_content: We spent a pleasant hour on the observation deck and enjoyed looking at the sights from this tower. But, Hanoi had so much smog while we were there that it was not possible to see anything at a distance. There are a couple of interactive things to do on the viewing deck and a great 'walk of faith' - basically a clear glass floor that protrudes from the main tower and allows views straight down to the ground, 65 floors below.
drawbacks: not possible to see anything at a distance

author: Tripod
title: What a shame
original_content: Lotte Management should be ashamed. Not even enough chairs, no bar stools, no entertainment and lousy drinks. Plus point is the well trained and accomondating staff who deserve a lot of credit to manage the the busy evenings. How can it be that such a large hotel with such great potential has no feeling for ambience? The Hotel Lobby dead quiet, no music, no entertainment and you feel walking into a funeral. Sorry Lotte, brush up your skills as it is not only about building a high rise building but providing genuine hospitality and ambience which the customer will pay for!

author: hannahmckay78
title: Night visit was average and overpriced
original_content: We found this place pretty underwhelming, there were only fast food restaurants and coffee shops up there which didnt make for much atmosphere. There were also bright screens everywhere which meant when you were looking out to the city the reflection of screens were very visible and took away from the view. Wonder bother going, wish we had gone to top of hanoi bar
drawbacks: only fast food restaurants and coffee shops
practical_tips: go to top of hanoi bar instead

author: Andrew V
title: Very modern, limited facilities
original_content: Get the night ticket, you'll pay less and you'll get to see Day and night versions of Hanoi. The 67th floor bar/restaurant is a seperate ticket. It wasn't crowded at all when I went at around 17:30
highlights: Get the night ticket, you'll pay less and you'll get to see Day and night versions of Hanoi

author: kirsi_nessu
title: Great view over Hanoi
original_content: Took a walk from old quarters, easy route Lifts and ticket desk is located 1BF floor one down from ground level. Tickets 230000 Not many people up on the deck. Coffee and fast food available also gift shop and possibly to take pictures on a glass floor.Btw if you are more interested to have a drink and a view top of Hanoi roof top restaurant opens 5 pm
drawbacks: Not many people up on the deck
highlights: Possibly to take pictures on a glass floor
practical_tips: Go to the rooftop restaurant for a drink and a view

author: Koen B
title: Superb place
original_content: Away from the city.   Good music and good drinks.  Prices are ok and it's a nice atmosphere. But there was no coffee because the machine was broken ?????   For such a place.  Nice for all visitors and especially business visitors. I'll come back for sure.
drawbacks: No coffee because the machine was broken

author: Theminimalistbackpacker
title: Great views and quiet
original_content: We went up at night it was great views of Hanoi at night. Standing on the sky deck is a must although it took me a while to actually get on there. Definitely worth a visit.
drawbacks: took me a while to actually get on there
highlights: great views of Hanoi at night
Standing on the sky deck is a must

author: Rhonwyn H
title: Amusing!
original_content: This was a nice way to kill the hot afternoon. It gives you a better grasp of how big Hanoi is. Plenty of places to sit and relax. There is also a Lotteria in case you get hungry. Don't forget to try the skydeck!
highlights: better grasp of how big Hanoi is
plenty of places to sit and relax
practical_tips: don't forget to try the skydeck

author: Jack_OrionYgn
title: Exhilarating Memories
original_content: We went there at night and was greeted with one of the most spectacular night views of Hanoi. The four or five features up there, be it romance or family, made our visit very much memorable. The sky walk is definitely something you have to experience! Me and my girlfriend's heart were racing when we were standing up there. Go there around 9 PM as there will be less crowds and you have plenty of time to enjoy the view.

author: Girinath
title: Exciting
original_content: The skywalk is soo awsom! Definitely have to go., the attendant gave a nice walkthrough and took lot pics. Very nice to have a freaky experience

author: Washant
title: Very scary sky deck
original_content: What a wonderful view over the city.I fully enjoyed the the calm of the observation deck. most spectacular is the sky deck completely made out of glass where you are actually stand on glass above the ground. This gifts a very weird feeling to your senses. It's absolutely a good price and I would say go! Downstairs is very good food.
highlights: sky deck completely made out of glass

author: Teresa W
title: Take the time to walk along the wall - many entrance points and you can walk as much or little as you want
original_content: An interesting art work in Hanoi - we passed it often on the bus or grab - so finally had an up close look - really enjoyed the art work

author: abella c
title: It's worth a visit.
original_content: Great initiative this mosaic wall created for the 1000 years of Hanoi. My only regret is that it is along a very busy road and that we lack back up and calm to enjoy it but it is worth the detour

author: Andibuchbar
title: Impressively long mosaic wall
original_content: Impressively long mosaic wall, Guinness book excellent. Beautiful motifs. Unfortunately unkempt and out of age. Many stones are missing

author: BorntocruiseUK
title: Stunning and goes on for miles!!!
original_content: We only got to do a short stretch of the mosaic wall but it was amazing. Each panel is so different to the next each telling their own story. Just be careful as you walk along the street as the pavements are not very wide and the traffic does move fast. Start in the middle and choose your direction of travel and you will see enough to keep you busy or start at the beginning and keep walking.I don’t think I have ever seen anything as big as this, it appears to go on and on. To think the pictures are made from little pieces of colourful tiles all carefully placed to make stunning art pieces.
highlights: each panel is so different to the next
practical_tips: start in the middle and choose your direction of travel
start at the beginning and keep walking

author: Sue M
title: Along the Dyke Wall
original_content: We saw many sections of the ceramic mosaic mural as we traveled on the main road along side of it.  It was built to commemorate the 1,000 years existence of Hanoi.  And is in the Guiness Book of World records as the longest ceramic mosaic mural.
highlights: commemorate the 1,000 years existence of Hanoi

author: Maria Eugenia A
title: Go visit
original_content: It is long and not easily accesible. It is really beautiful thought. Nice to watch, a lot of traffic around and not easy to cross the street
drawbacks: not easy to cross the street

author: Panagiotis S.
title: Amazing art wall, worth visit it!
original_content: Amazing, impressive, worth visiting. I walked about 3 km of it and took a lot of pictures. The only negative is that is along a heavy traffic road, but is a must visit in Hanoi!

author: Mug
title: Love Along the Ceramic Mile
original_content: Each tile tells a story, and we couldn't help but take silly photos matching the mural's patterns. The sunset walk here became our daily ritual, complete with street coffee and endless selfies.

author: kate
title: A colorful journey
original_content: It's a beautiful and vibrant piece of art that stretches for miles. However, we noticed it’s not well-maintained, with some tiles missing and faded sections. Despite this, it’s still a colorful and inspiring sight to see!
extracted_spaces: a beautiful and vibrant piece of art that stretches for miles

author: dianedinky
title: See it if you can
original_content: As mentioned already, the mural is not in a good location, however, it is a thing of beauty and I would have liked to see it close up.  I didn't have time to investigate but feel that at nearly 4,000 metres long there must be a part of it that is accessible on foot?Was still nice to see from our bus a few times and interesting to see the traditional narrow houses that are along this stretch that are so typical of Vietnam.

author: BrakiWorldTraveler
title: Such a pity for the location and maintenance neglect
original_content: This is the world's longest ceramic tiles mural - some call it mosaic, but imo mosaic is something else.Nevertheless, the location where it is installed was chosen so unfortunately.It's by a very busy road - the main city center throughfare which is constantly under heavy traffic.In that way you cannot see it properly as you have absolutely no desire to walk along that road. Hanoi is one of the most polluted cities in the world, so besides the previous fact, that also contributes to the mural damage, dirt and neglection. We only saw it from taxi several times.

author: Marion B
title: Yeah
original_content: Pretty ceramic wall but in front of a highway...You can't really walk in front otherwise you'll get run over.May prefer other activities in Hanoi

author: MizuhoK
title: See from distance
original_content: This mosaic art is at the north side of Long Biên station. This was the project to commemorate the county’s 1000th anniversary, started in 2007 and completed in 2010. It lasts about 6.5km, Guinness Records. We only saw mosaic art from distance. We saw from the bus on the way to hotel from AP. We saw from the bus from hotel to HaLong. The north of Long Bien station is a key point for major transport so you may come across here on during your move.We feel fine to see from distance since you cannot see the whole mosaic anyway. Rather, you can see the whole picture from distance. It’s a pretty colorful art which cheers the people.
extracted_spaces: North side of Long Biên station
drawbacks: Cannot see the whole mosaic from close up
practical_tips: Come from a distance to see the whole picture

author: Shelley M
title: unfortunate placement
original_content: A bit of a shame something this beautiful is not maintained and able to be viewed easily.  The traffic is crazy, so you dont dare cross over to check it out. Looks lovely from a distance, just in the wrong sport to be enjoyed.
drawbacks: not able to be viewed easily

author: Lee A
title: Longest ceramic road in the world
original_content: It must be a beautiful road with many meaningful pics. But it's pity that some ceramic pieces are fade and peeled of. Needs to be cared and maintained regularly .
drawbacks: some ceramic pieces are fade and peeled of
practical_tips: needs to be cared and maintained regularly

author: palawanismyhome
title: Guinness world record
original_content: The ceramic wall is about 6 kms long and was the idea of Nguyen Thu Thuy in order to hide the dykes. The ceramics come from Bat Trang, the pottery village about 10 kms away. The idea was to complete it for the Hanoi millennium in 2010, and it depicts scenes from the history of Vietnam: Phùng Nguyên culture; Đông Sơn culture; Lý dynasty; Trần dynasty; Lê dynasty and Nguyễn dynasty. It is in the record books as the longest ceramic wall.
highlights: depicts scenes from the history of Vietnam

author: srimanone
title: LONG WALL ON BUSY ROAD
original_content: This is a long wall of many designed ceramics. Poorly maintained and very busy road. Plus the walkway is very dangerous, I suggest you pass this by in a taxi or bus for easy viewings
practical_tips: pass this by in a taxi or bus for easy viewings

author: dianne c
title: beautiful walls that did not age well
original_content: It's a really long wall(at least a kilometer?) and right beside the huge busy road. It's a bit scary to walk but the mosaic designs are really nice and made well. Unfortunately it has not aged well. But it is still worth a visit, but just once.

author: Liam F
title: Conceptually impressive but difficult to experience
original_content: The mural itself is quite remarkable but the only way to see it on foot is by walking directly in front of it on a narrow path with 4 lanes of non-stop traffic right behind you. If your taxi or bus goes past it then it's nice to look at, but I don't recommend walking there.
drawbacks: walking directly in front of it on a narrow path with 4 lanes of non-stop traffic right behind you
highlights: the mural itself is quite remarkable

author: David
title: TIP: Look at the pictures rather than visit!
original_content: The mural is impossibile to appreciate on foot. It is reportedly miles long and is adjacent to a busy road. So hard to approach, and impossible to take it all in!So, id reccomend looking at the photos online rather than visiting!
drawbacks: impossible to take it all in
practical_tips: look at the photos online rather than visiting

author: Linda B
title: Amazing piece of art!
original_content: The mural is 4 miles long and holds the Guinness World Record for longest ceramic mural (2010). We were only able to view it on our way to the airport as we were leaving Vietnam after two weeks. Wish I could have visited it in person!
drawbacks: Wish I could have visited it in person!
highlights: holds the Guinness World Record for longest ceramic mural

author: David E
title: A Highlight of Hanoi
original_content: The largest mosaic in the world entrances visitors for over 10 years along Au Co, the dyke road wall. Artists from many nations and organizations completed this majestic celebration of Hanoi's 1000 year anniversary under the leadership of artist Thu Thuy,  certainly one of the finest public artists in the world.
highlights: one of the finest public artists in the world

author: dekalbill
title: Impressive Story in Mosaic Tiles
original_content: The miles long mural is worth driving along to appreciate the creative artistic work depicting the history of Hanoi.  This impressive work is dedicated to Hanoi's celebration of 1000 years.

author: Ev_kka
title: Impressive
original_content: Few kilometers long, goes around the street, we saw it many timese - on our way from the airport, etc. It is a masterpeace, be sure to see it at least from the car / motorbike.
extracted_spaces: Few kilometers long, goes around the street
practical_tips: Be sure to see it at least from the car / motorbike

author: WileyCoyote2
title: Amazingly creative,a joy to the eye
original_content: Take a taxi,stop at a convenient locationThen walk to get the best views + pictureTaxi will pick you up ,after your stroll
practical_tips: walk to get the best views

author: Vicki E
title: Pretty impressive
original_content: Lovely to look at as you are driving around.  It is the longest mosaic in the world and crafted by many people.  Awesome work.

author: chiangmaicharlies
title: Hard to see, but unforgettable if you do
original_content: We saw much of this from our taxi from the city to the airport.It would be most difficult to see this in much detail as it's on such a busy road - but we really enjoyed what we saw of it. Sadly, none of my photos from the taxi did it justice.Typical of many Hanoi streets which are now given over to a lot of artwork. Great for visitors and great for the soul.
drawbacks: difficult to see in detail due to busy road
highlights: great for visitors and great for the soul
practical_tips: take a taxi from the city to see more

author: Nejolla
title: Very nice mural
original_content: A bit overrated a tourist attraction so don't know why it is listed on trip advisor. The mural is lovely yet sits in the middle of a busy street.  Nice to pass by I guess.
drawbacks: sits in the middle of a busy street
practical_tips: don't know why it is listed on trip advisor

author: RASHIDA HUSAIN
title: 4km of amazing mosaic art work
original_content: truly very inspiring art work from all over the world. in one look it may seem like graffiti but its all amazing art work made of small tiles and mosaic. very nice.!
highlights: amazing art work made of small tiles and mosaic

author: edenxo1212
title: Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Mural
original_content: Runs along through many streets in Hanoi. Better experience if you get yourself a bike or motorbike in order to see the whole. But, if you want to have a closer look at it you should have walk on foot
drawbacks: Need a bike or motorbike to see the whole
highlights: Better experience with a bike or motorbike
practical_tips: Walk on foot for a closer look

author: Samuel Piette
title: Mural street
original_content: Those picture on the wall was the most aesthetic things you will ever seen in your life. Not like any other exhibition or art gallery, those picture has its own beauty to display

author: Brilliant Pottery
title: Handmade Walls of Tiles
original_content: Very interesting the first few meters.  Then it get a little much to see especially with the bikes and traffic.
drawbacks: get a little much to see

author: Susan M
title: Marvellous
original_content: A great attraction despite the whizzing traffic! Close to bus station so go have a look then head out to Ba Trang the ceramic village....
practical_tips: head out to Ba Trang the ceramic village

author: Raymondale
title: Very long mural
original_content: It is a very long mural,i tried to walk from the beginning,but gave up around Long Bien bridge,very long,and dont know where is the ending.if have time will continue to explore it.it is hard to take photos too,the pedestrian street too narrow,and very dangerous if take from the busy main road.i tried to take from the opposite side,but a bit far,and so many vechiles passing by,you have to wait till no vechiles and shoot.some topics of the mosaic mural are funny,come here and have a look.
drawbacks: dangerous if take from the busy main road
highlights: some topics of the mosaic mural are funny

author: Iris T
title: amazing work
original_content: It was amazing to see all different works of Mosaic and it was quite long way on the wall. I wish I had time to walk along to see them.It is worth going there to see.
drawbacks: wish I had time to walk along
highlights: amazing to see all different works of Mosaic

author: Janice M
title: Put this on your list
original_content: What a beautiful Mural. It has so much detail made from tiny glass tiles.  It goes for such a long way.  We saw it a few times from a taxi and from the back of a motorcycle.  If I had of had more time I would have walked along it to appreciate it even more.  This has taken so much time to do and is really beautiful.  There is some wall not completed, so in future years it would be good to go back and see if it has been completed.
practical_tips: go back and see if it has been completed

author: susan1819
title: Don't try to walk it
original_content: The mosaic mural was done to mark the 100th anniversary of Vietnam. It runs along a main road - so don't try to walk it! You can't miss it if you're in a bus, cab or car. There are different stories depicted in the mural. If you want to get up close to the mural, you can do so in the Old Quarter, when walking to the Wholesale market and Old Citadel gate.
highlights: Different stories depicted in the mural
practical_tips: Don't try to walk the mural
Get up close to the mural in the Old Quarter

author: Michael D
country: La Manga del Mar Menor, Spain
title: DO NOT MISS IT
original_content: We have been passed this mosaic a number of times, still not sure how long it is in total but it is long. We were also fortunate to see people adding to the mosaic.
highlights: fortunate to see people adding to the mosaic

author: AngiWong
title: Games for children
original_content: Love the mosaic along the road. It has become a game for the children to spot the country or animal or design. Intricate and beautiful

author: Tonya057
title: Pretty
original_content: Pretty , but hard to see it well, it runs along very busy street. Great work by artists all over the world.
highlights: Great work by artists all over the world

author: Aliz A.
title: Nice Highlight of Hanoi
original_content: Colourful interesting detail along a road nearby the river. Be aware the trafic. These photos were taken in unsafe conditions.  But its worth to risk;)
extracted_spaces: Colourful interesting detail along a road nearby the river

author: Colline D
title: Beautiful, well worth a look
original_content: This world record wall was gorgeous when it was first completed. On this specific trip, nevertheless, I realized many areas of the framework are missing tiles or even crumbling and cracking. Def a must see, but also hoping in many more seasons it won't have disappeared.

author: Julian E
title: The longest ever
original_content: This mural I believe is the longest in the word. I walked a few miles of it and it is just amazing to see. Well done if you walk all of it.

author: steven e
title: A real suprise
original_content: Mosaic runs  along the side of a typical very busy road. You will probably see it as you travel to Hanoi from the Airport. Impressive when you think of the work involved

author: Cristina P.
title: Wall
original_content: It s a mosaic wall that has been said is in the Records Book as the longest wall made from mosaic. A street art you can admire from any vehicle.

author: Cliff C
title: Hanoi ceramic mural wall
original_content: This wall goes for quite a few kilometres on both sides of the road and depicts the life and history of Vietnam. NO GRAFFITI!Very professional and makes a drive from/to the airport very pleasant and welcoming.

author: Pennie B
title: Very public art
original_content: Wonderful, lengthy mosaic mural tells many tales along the way. Brilliant! Saw it on several drive bys. Wish there were a fold out book to give the entire view
drawbacks: Wish there were a fold out book to give the entire view
highlights: Wonderful, lengthy mosaic mural tells many tales along the way

author: Sandra
title: walking along the Hanoi mosaic wall
original_content: I walked along the wall for 2 miles south of the Chuong Duong Bridge, took photos and lived to tell about. The sidewalk is narrow, but wide enough to step back (if you are careful) and take photos. The easiest way to get across the chaotic road next to the wall is to hire a Grab motorcycle and have him drop you next to the wall.

author: gastronaut_11
title: Extensive
original_content: Depicts Vietnam in a kaleidoscope of colour and imagination. Seems to go on forever, mostly ignored, but a great insight.

author: Nonapama
title: Good attempt at beautifying
original_content: This has transformed an otherwise sad looking concrete wall and not so interesting neighbourhood into a place of art and cultural heritage. Best to drive by as not so easy or safe to walk past.
drawbacks: not so easy or safe to walk past
highlights: place of art and cultural heritage

author: Nguyễn K
title: Smell and dirty
original_content: So sad!This ceramic road must be a symbol of Hanoi but there are too many broken parts :((Also, it was very smelly with busy trafic around there.

author: Lisa S
title: Wow better than graffiti!
original_content: We have driven by this numerous times during our stay in Hanoi.  Some very cool, colorful mosaics here.  Our local guide said it used to be graffiti on the concrete wall and then someone came up with the idea to beautify it by using mosaics and I’d say they succeeded!

author: fizzy1991
title: Drive by but don't get out of the car
original_content: This is a great mural to view along your drive in Hanoi but don't try and get out of your car to see it up close.  The traffic is so crazy here and you will get hit if you try.  Your best bet is to get in the far lane closes to the wall and take pictures as you go.  Or maybe there will be a jam up and you can see them for a longer period of time.
drawbacks: will get hit if you try to get out of your car
practical_tips: get in the far lane closes to the wall and take pictures as you go
wait for a jam up to see them for a longer period of time

author: Willem B
title: Great public art
original_content: A proud celebration of the history of the country. Not too easy to access on foot but you will see it going to the airport it Halong Bay
drawbacks: Not too easy to access on foot
highlights: A proud celebration of the history of the country
practical_tips: You will see it going to the airport

author: TessaPolis
title: Longest mosaic in the world.
original_content: Saw this on our way out of Hanoi from the car windows.  Very, very long and in a variety of artistic styles.

author: RovingSoraSon
title: Along the way
original_content: Meet this mural along the way from the airport to the city center. I didnot think it is a thing, just some fun decoration. But there are parts looks amusing and made me want to keep looking to see what is next.
drawbacks: did not think it is a thing
highlights: made me want to keep looking

author: ferretbadger
title: Intricate and Beautiful
original_content: This mural cheers up travellers along the road by providing a bit of color in an otherwise mostly gray city. It features designs from Vietnamese mythology, childrens' art, and quilt patterns and is a delight to pass by.

author: WireWrapGems2
title: Worth choosing a route that goes by this mural wall
original_content: Local artisans have created a beautiful ceramic tile wall depicting local scenes.  It is difficult to get a good picture if you are riding in a bus.  It is quite long and beautiful to see, day or night.
drawbacks: difficult to get a good picture if you are riding in a bus
highlights: beautiful ceramic tile wall depicting local scenes
practical_tips: go early to get a good picture

author: TheLeongOhana
title: A Beautiful Mural along a Busy Road
original_content: We drove by this beautiful mosaic mural on the way to the airport after a short stay in Hanoi.  It was little tough at times to take a photo from a moving van but I managed to capture a few good photos.  It was colorful and looked like a lot of effort went into the design and construction.  The mural contained a number of different themes and landmarks both local and international, like the Merlion from Singapore.  There also was quite a bit of advertisement on the mural and personally I don’t know why they allowed it.I may try to walk along part of it next time since it extends for a couple miles.
drawbacks: little tough at times to take a photo from a moving van
quite a bit of advertisement on the mural
highlights: lot of effort went into the design and construction
number of different themes and landmarks
practical_tips: try to walk along part of it next time

author: Janka K
title: Nice view qhen you ride a motorbike
original_content: This is a nice scenery when you ride a motorbike at day - I passed the wall when taking passenger seat on the Grab motorbike ride. The decorated wall is long and it's obvious that someone made an effor. I liked it a lot.

author: Elina Ermakova
title: Colourful
original_content: Together an incredibly frantic interstate, you turn up at a beautiful mural painstakingly assembled by artists which are local and a further master artist out of a number of areas across the world - a tribute to their 1000 season birthday celebration. a genuine must see in this beautiful city.
extracted_spaces: a number of areas across the world
highlights: a tribute to their 1000 season birthday celebration

author: JnVSydney
title: Best seen by car
original_content: We had planned to walk the length of Hanoi’s Ceramic mosic mural - at 3.85 km it holds the Guiness World Record the longest ceramic mosaic mural in the world.  It was created to celebrate the millenial anniversary of Hanoi and 35 artists from around the world contributed to it. Fortunately the Grab ride to a temple showed us around 60% of it from the taxi and it turns out it runs the length of a (very noisey) highway... so not ideal for gentle and enjoyable strolling.
drawbacks: not ideal for gentle and enjoyable strolling
highlights: Guiness World Record the longest ceramic mosaic mural in the world
35 artists from around the world contributed to it

author: kpiddy
title: Longest ceramic mosaic wall in the world
original_content: The Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Wall is pretty hard not to miss on a commute from the city to the Noi Bai International Airport, local and international artists came together to add colour and decorate the Red River dyke wall in preparation for the celebration of Hanoi's 1000th in 2010.  The wall has been recognised by the Guiness Book of Records as the longest ceramic mosaic wall in the world measuring just under four kilometres long.  Accessing the wall would be difficult by foot simply due to the chaotic roads, best viewed from within a vehicle.
highlights: longest ceramic mosaic wall in the world
practical_tips: best viewed from within a vehicle

author: FrequentTrooper
title: Beautiful piece of work
original_content: Not a place you can walk to and admire. If you are in a vehicle, ask the driver to slow down and enjoy the mural depicting Hanoi.
drawbacks: Not a place you can walk to and admire
practical_tips: Ask the driver to slow down

author: Laura T
title: only drove past when transferring to/from the airport, looked amazing so would love to be able to see in more detail
original_content: This colourful 4 mile long mural runs along along the Red River dike wall, following the roads of Au Co, Nghi Tam, Yen Phu, Tran Nhat Duat, Tran Quang Khai and Tran Khanh Du. Stretching along the main road leading out of Hanoi and towards the airport, so most transfers will drive past portions of the mural. Due to the very busy traffic and narrow pathways, it is recommended to view from a car or motorbike, which is what we did. Having read more reviews now though, it sounds like people are able to walk along parts of it? although the pavement must be very very narrow! Apparently, one section is next to the historic Long Bien Bridge where it may be easier to look at in more detail?This mural was created in 2010 to celebrate the 1000 year anniversary of Hanoi. Local and international artists were assigned different sections. The artwork is beautiful and creative in many different styles, showing Vietnamese ethnic and cultural motives. Listed in the Guinness World Records as the longest ceramic art road in the world. I would have liked to have been able to look at in more detail.
highlights: showing Vietnamese ethnic and cultural motives
practical_tips: view from a car or motorbike

author: Manfred H
title: interesting
original_content: Seeing there is no infrastructure ,no trains,no trams and  gridlock traffic there might have been a better way to celebrate 1000 years Hanoi however the wall is artistic and you have plenty of time admiring as u r stuck in traffic

author: Kimmie
title: Colourful Mosaic
original_content: The 2 km colourful mosaic was interesting. Showing the ancient time and how they kings shifted the capital. After visiting the different tombs and looking at the mosaic it gives one a better understanding.. awesome and worth the nice walk.

author: Sharmistha Ghosh Das
title: Interesting concept... Difficult to capture pictures though
original_content: Our Hanoi guide first showed us this Mosaic mural and mentioned about it's length and place in Guiness Book of Records. It's a very interesting concept. We actually walked along the wall but it was very difficult to capture photos of the mosaics since the pedestrian walkway is narrow and there are millions of motorbikes running next to it who hardly stop for anyone on road. Given Vietnam's reputation of bikers snatching phones, we did not want to take a risk with the phone either. But some of the murals are really nice and give a sneak peek into Vietnam's most important landmarks and culture. Worth a visit if you have some time to walk along.
drawbacks: motorbikes running next to it who hardly stop for anyone on road
highlights: nice and give a sneak peek into Vietnam's most important landmarks and culture

author: TravelingFamilyTrip
title: Pretty cool
original_content: I noticed this long mosaic wall during my cab ride to the airport.  It was pretty interesting to view it and I appreciated the work that went into it. I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to find it, but it was a nice addition to Hanoi.
drawbacks: wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to find it
highlights: appreciated the work that went into it

author: Jana
title: Long...
original_content: Interesting to see if you have time to stroll along. It's well done and very artsy and since it's close to the Old Quarter, it's easy to walk to.

author: ron b
title: 4 mile long ceramic mural that straddles Gustav Eiffel's historic Long Bien bridge
original_content: This mural was created in 2010 to celebrate the 1000 year anniversary of Hanoi, along the Red River dike wall. Apparently different artists were assigned different sections. The art work is uniformly beautiful and creative. Unfortunately the mural is on a narrow sidewalk on a very busy street so is a bit awkward to visit. One section is next to the historic Long Bien bridge, the oldest bridge across the Red River, built in 1899 by the legendary Gustav Eiffel, bombed by America but since restored, a must-see sight in Hanoi.
drawbacks: narrow sidewalk on a very busy street

author: igor Š
title: Nice mosaic work
original_content: The Mosaic Mural of Ha Noi depicts a range of fascinating themes along with its seven km length, each artistically rendered in delightful fashion. the sections range from easy to elaborate, & they evoke history, the natural world, some laughter, as well as a popular painter. The Mural is best appreciated on foot, but in case time is short, a vehicle/taxi provides a great option. Appreciate this special outdoor art exhibit! Extremely colourfully decorated' mosaic wall' lining the course to the airport for over a mile. Probably best observed from a taxi.
drawbacks: Probably best observed from a taxi
practical_tips: in case time is short, a vehicle/taxi provides a great option

author: Chris S
title: Art everywhere!

author: rlh
title: Remarkable Ceramic Artwork For The World
original_content: Vietnam’s capital city, Hanoi (a/k/a “Thang Long” its historic name which means Ascending Dragon) celebrated its 1000th anniversary as the nation’s capital on October 10, 2010. One of the standout symbols of the city’s celebration back in 2010 was the 4km+ long ceramic mosaic wall running from the An Duong border gate  to the Van Kiep border gate. It has about  6500 square meters of ceramic artwork in 21 mosaic sections that honor Vietnamese forefathers and their various dynasties, the cultures of VN’s 54 ethnic groups, and generally the history and international relations that are part of the nation’s history.  The multi-year project attracted the participation & enthusiasm of local & international artists who used many types of ceramics from craft villages throughout Vietnam to complete the wall. As part of the celebration, the Guinness World Records Organization also certified the collaborative work of art as the longest ceramic art road in the world. The wall is somewhat difficult to view as a pedestrian due to the heavy traffic alongside its length but if you do walk a portion of the route, use the sidewalk opposite the artwall (carefully avoiding the obstructions of foliage, trash, etc) to gain the best views. Again, it will be a dicey walk so remain safety conscious—-a suggestion borne from personal experience!! It is more easily and quickly viewed from a car, taxi or bus but using this means reduces the opportunity to photograph or study the ceramic art.
drawbacks: difficult to view as a pedestrian
highlights: longest ceramic art road in the world
practical_tips: use the sidewalk opposite the artwall

The main monuments and sights of the country from Hoi An and My Son to Hue are represented, as are wildlife and flora. But basically it's long and it's a mosaic.

author: Janine F
title: Adds interest to a busy city
original_content: Travelling along in a taxi is probably the only way to see this as it is along a very busy road.  Well done and good to look at instead of the tooting motorbikes and cars!
practical_tips: Travelling along in a taxi is probably the only way to see this

author: babiesquuensland
title: very well done
original_content: saw this a lot of work has gone into this and looks great, would be very hard to walk this with all the traffic
drawbacks: hard to walk with all the traffic

author: CYY_sg
title: Colourful and breaks the monotony while traveling along this road
original_content: Colourful mosaic pictures line this stretch of road. It is entertaining for people traveling here. Probably recommended only for the most hardcore fans of such an art-form if you intend to plan a visit here as part of your itinerary.
drawbacks: Probably recommended only for the most hardcore fans
if you intend to plan a visit here as part of your itinerary
highlights: Colourful mosaic pictures line this stretch of road

author: Nunngo
title: A masterpiece of community art
original_content: I had been to Hanoi twice previously, and both times admired the mural from the road in a car sitting in traffic.  When I was there in 2010 Hanoi was celebrating 1000 years.  The mural was completed as part of the 1000 year celebration.  This trip I was determined to walk the entire length of the mural and photograph as much as possible.  We walked the mural wall on two separate days, the heat was the limiting factor in not doing the entire length in one day.  There were sections that were difficult to get to given the location and the 'madness' of the traffic.  If you have the time to walk even some of the mural it is very much worthwhile viewing up close. The sections have been completed by community groups, and various local schools, including international schools.  The art work is magnificent with elaborate mosaic detail, intense colour and texture.  Unfortunately there are parts of the mural that are already damaged and worn but it is mostly intact and well worth the effort to walk in the heat and traffic.
practical_tips: walk even some of the mural

author: Wayfaring N
title: Beautiful welcome to Hanoi
original_content: Only saw it on the bus from the airport but remembered it from my last trip here because it's really unforgettable and a great taste of what vietnam is ready to offer
highlights: great taste of what vietnam is ready to offer

author: Lydia Farmer L
title: beautiful mural!
original_content: Driving along the crowded congested main road, this is a welcome and attractive sight. We passed it many times during our Hanoi stay. Going to Halong Bay, over to the Westlake district, and several shorter trips. It is a good distraction from the craziness of Vietnamese traffic!
highlights: good distraction from the craziness of Vietnamese traffic

author: Robert Q
title: Mosaic Mural on the Red River flood wall.
original_content: Hard to see without getting killed by speeding traffic, this project was completed by collage art students celebrating Vietnamese culture.  Still, seen from a distance, or form a moving taxi, it is an impressive sight.
drawbacks: Hard to see without getting killed by speeding traffic

author: firach
title: love love love this wall
original_content: read on the internet that this wall is 6.5km long and is in the World Guinness Records for being the longest ceramic mosaic wall. Couldn't walk through the whole one as it was too hot, but passing by parts of it on a motorbike gave a glimpse into the the artsy side of vietnam, as well as the things important to them, such as the recurrent drawing of a turtle and a sword in its mouth
drawbacks: Couldn't walk through the whole one

author: jenabaintheworld
title: beautiful urban art
original_content: I see this very long mural going to and from work every day.   Incredible art from ceramic tiles---and done in Ba Trung ceramic village outside Hanoi and then put on display as nice wall to beautify the roadway.    This was done to commemorate 1000 years for the city of Hanoi.    Great idea for beautiful urban art
highlights: Great idea for beautiful urban art

author: Jane D
title: in a vehicle
original_content: but looked amazing! Are there tours to see it, because it is on a busy road? I would have paid. Next time!

author: Lim T
title: Not the same as photograph
original_content: Look from the photo very nice. But actually, have many traffic that side. Look old and not really ok. Dissapointed

author: Mary M
title: Interesting mosaic
original_content: Passed this wonderful mosaic, depicting Vietnamese culture, every time we took the taxi into the old quarter.

author: NathaPushpa d
title: Very nice fine mosaic mural on one side of the road
original_content: Excellent art work using Cermic Mosaics. Very fine art work. The length of the mural is about 2km. Nicely done. This is located in a very busy road and very hard to photographed unless vehicle stops in a traffic sign. otherwise use video recording . I have done that and it has come up nicely as I have told my driver to drive slowly. Lots of hard work done by vietnamese young artists. Seems to be taken 4yrs to complete this art work. Its worth it..rather than graffiting the blank walls..it stops also doing that...Thanks for young artitic people of Vietnam..You all have done marvelous job which I have not seen any where else.

author: Shawn S
title: The world's longest piece of art
original_content: This is one of the things that makes Hanoi Hanoi. It lines one side of a very large and busy road, so it's not the easiest thing to access on foot. This mural is still expanding and has recently added an homage to Hugo Chavez of Venezuela as far West as Xuan Dieu st. There are community contributions to the design of the mural; it's obvious that students in primary schools were commissioned to contribute designs, and they are charming. The sheer variety of styles is inexhaustible, meaning you can pass by the mural many, many times and still see something new. The best way to visit the mural is to hire a taxi or xe om and tell them "Di Cham" while pointing at the mural. They'll get the  message and do what they can to drive slow while you view it.
drawbacks: not the easiest thing to access on foot
practical_tips: hire a taxi or xe om and tell them 'Di Cham'

author: AADSWJ
title: Creative
original_content: It's along roadside in main road right outside the Old Quarter.  Somehow you will pass it. It was created by those villages in trade to promote their historical handcraft skills.  Some designs are cute,  some are kiddy like. It's better than go to museums!

author: Rengarajan S
title: Mosaic mural on roadside
original_content: As you head towards the long bridge, you can see very nice mosaic artwork on either sides of the road.... very artistic and so nice to see.....It was commissioned to commemorate the millennium of Hanoi

author: AAS619
title: Nice to see from a moving car
original_content: We only saw that from the car but I really thought it was beautiful. It goes for quite a distance. I am not sure if I would recommend walking along the sidewalk, unless you desire to contemplate each piece. I liked to have a little bit of perspective and see it change, also it runs along a busy artery road and I would not care to walk around there. Having a little bit of perspective and seeing it change was enjoyable

author: sue5290
title: Such an interesting art installation
original_content: There is such much to look at as you travel along this mural. Many hands created different images of this country and it has some fascinating detail. We really enjoyed studying it and imaging the many different people who took part in it's design and installation.

author: Toni S
title: Miles of mosaics on busy streets

It was an original plan but the execution is questionable. The streets decorated are busy with car and scooters and pedestrian unfriendly and there are a few spots where one can enjoy them.

author: BrakiWorldTraveler
title: Pity it's on a busy and unattractive street

It's very long and we looked at it while going on bus tours from the hotel.I think it deserves a much better place than on this very busy and uninviting street. You can hardly approach it and walk by due to heavy traffic around.

author: Lengyelek
title: Very good initiative from the city

author: denglander
title: Loved this !

author: palawanismyhome
title: So many mosaic pieces
original_content: Construction began in 2007 of the Ceramic Mosaic Mural which stretches about 6 kms along several roads and ends at Long Bien Bridge. It was the brainchild of  journalist Nguyen Thu Thuy who won a contest for transforming the dyke system in Hanoi to this beautiful mosaic wall. It celebrates the Millennial anniversary of Hanoi which took place in 2010. Vietnamese artists, foreign embassies and cultural centers all helped to construct the wall. All the porcelain came from the village of Bat Trang, otherwise known as the pottery village. The mosaic consists of scenes from Hanoi, modern art and children's drawings, and is now in the Guinness Book of World Records as being the biggest mosaic on the planet.
highlights: celebrates the Millennial anniversary of Hanoi

author: ailenroc13
title: It's a must
original_content: I wish several cities in the world (including mine) follow this example of decorating highway walls. This one is fab, with different themes all along, so it's a real pleasure to slowly drive along (on your way to the airport) or walk along for a while(it's 4 km long) to discover the various themes. Great idea beautifully realized!
practical_tips: drive along on your way to the airport

author: Skimsa

author: Q1578LVsandrat

author: Tiddy W.

author: RaRa

author: zycieipodroze

Ceramic mosaic wall depicts the history of Vietnam throughout history and includes more than 1,000 years. author: Lorenzo R
title: Impressive
original_content: We saw this impressive wall of mosaics when we first entered the city.The aim of the mural was to transform the urban stretches of the Red River Dyke, an essential flood defence that had been subjected to illegal graffiti and advertising.The mural had been in construction since 2007 and involved 35 professional artists from Vietnam and 10 other countries

author: Djodi
title: Mosaic murals

author: Jim M

author: pngocduong1

We ended up purchasing quite a few pieces for ourselves and as gifts.It was a great experience and a nice opportunity to see something beyond the typical Hanoi attractions. beautiful silk clothes, scarves, and other items to choose from
great experience and a nice opportunity to see something beyond the typical Hanoi attractions

author: Adrian Villanueva
title: Handicraft Village

author: George E

original_content: I might have come at the wrong time of day or wrong season - but this was mid. There was a relatively pretty pagoda, and several well-painted murals to get a photo in front of. Overall the silk village made for some colourful and fun Instagram content (with all the umbrellas and murals) but did not necessarily provide a super fulfilling experience in itself. The main factory we could see into and appeared staffed and busy, but I think you'd want a guide to take you through there rather than showing yourself through.

author: Ightham1

author: michelle B

They indicated for us to come and look at them work, showed us their patterns and were happy for us to photograph...it was fascinating !! author: Mincimoo

author: Dave
title: Good prices if you want clothes/materials
original_content: As someone noted, make sure you go to the right van phuc as this is not a unique place name.Accessible by grab (and return). But yeah this is just a shopping trip to get best prices and options, was not looking for a history of silk making or something like that so think it does the trick as long as the shopping is what you want.

author: 672highf
title: Just A Shopping Trip
original_content: A very disappointing visit to Van Phuc Silk Village. My expectations where to see the production of silk from silk worm to finished product. Unfortunately the only facility for the production of silk was one example of an old working loom and some explanations of the processes by the in house guide.There are many shops/stalls selling silk products but very little of the silk for sale is manufactured in Vietnam and is readily available in any market just about anywhere in Asia. I found nothing that was unique to Vietnam.Much of the product for sale was labelled "Silk Like" and in fact was not pure silk but a blend and/or man made fibre.

author: Wanderlust3710
title: Great 1/2 day activity
original_content: We took a taxi from the old district to Van Phuc Village and shopped up a storm...  taxi ride was about $6 and takes about 45 mins....  make sure you have the Vietnamese translation for village as there is a Van Phuc street.  Prices tended to drop as we got further in....   not much for cafes but great selection of silk scarves, dresses etc.By going ourselves and not on a tour though, we didn't get to see the manufacturing process which I'm sure would have been cool...   btw most places only accept local currency

author: Jo-Ann

author: Steph B
