author: luonghongtrung
title: Parking ticket prices are too expensive.
original_content: The organization is quite methodical. The tour guide is friendly and gentle. The scene is beautiful, both majestic and lyrical. The cave is clean, long and has many exploration options.The downside is that parking tickets are too expensive.

author: Rosemary C
title: A must do trip in Ninh Binh
original_content: The boat trip, caves, grottos and temples were amazing particularly the Torii gate in the water and the last temple. One cave is 1 kilometre to go through and that was equally such an experience! The lady who rowed the boat had very little English and was lovely all the trip. I understand other places bully people with vendors arriving to sell snacks on water.  Absolutely none of this and this is not acceptable on a trip as you need to trust the person managing boat. The pink water lilies, green tea trees were an added bonus never mind the awe inspiring scenery of the limestone karsts from the boat. The day was misty rain but made no difference as there are umbrellas or bring rain poncho. Also good shoes for getting on and off boats at temples etc. Do go and visit here and be there at 9,00am as the place gets very busy later with day trips from Halong bay and Hanoi. We were there early and think this makes a big difference but not everyone plans to stay the night in the area to be able to do this .. This is a very busy organised operation but so worth the experience. It is also a busy Vietnamese tourist location. I noticed the Vietnamese when we were there do not tip the ladies rowing the boats. I know tipping is not generally standard here. However a tip of Vietnamese dollars if coming from Euro currency would make their day … it is a tough job rowing these boats and will not kill your budget much to give something.
extracted_times: day trips from Halong bay and Hanoi
drawbacks: vendors arriving to sell snacks on water
practical_tips: tip the ladies rowing the boats

author: CHARLENE G.
title: A highlight of the trip, a must do experience.
original_content: This was a highlight of the trip.  We climbed into small flatboats rowed by an oarswoman down the river through the caves.  What an awesome experience.  It is so beautiful and peaceful.  Can't say enough good about this experience. Don't miss it!

author: A D K
title: Enjoyed this boat tour but know it's crowded!
original_content: We did 3 boat tours in Ninh Binh, and this was my 2nd favorite.  We stayed in Ninh Binh 3 nights, and we rented a motorcycle from our hotel.  We had to pay 15,000 for parking.  The boat tour costs 250,000 each, and you choose from 3 different tours, based on what they offer.  We chose Tour 3 because it was recommended as the most beautiful and because it goes through a 1 km long cave passage.  Each boat holds 4 people, and they pair you up with 2 others.  If you don't wanna pair up, you can pay for the 2 other seats and have the boat to yourself.  I don't recommend this, as there are lots of other boats around and lots of people.  If you are expecting a peaceful, quiet tour, this is not it.  Tour 3 stops at 3 temples that are big and grand.  Our boat guide gave us 5-10 minutes per temple, which was enough for us.  There are 3 caves, and the caves are lit with electric lights.  There are lots of boats around with lots of people.  We were there in the winter, and it was beautiful to see all of the karsts.  That said, we were not there in the peak season, with beautiful rice fields. That would truly be spectacular.    It's noteworthy that our guide spoke a little English and pointed out things of interest to us.  He was friendly and kind. I did not note this as our favorite boat ride because of the many, many people there.  For our favorite boat ride of the 3 we took in Ninh Binh, try Linh Coc pier, which is only 1 km from the Lalita Tam Coc Resort.  At Linh Coc, the ride is only an hour.  We went about 9 am and were the only boat on the tour.  Just the 2 of us and our guide.  We only saw one other boat the entire trip, and that was a guy checking on his buffalo.  It cost 150,000 per person, and they didn't even bother making us wear life jackets.  When we went in the 3 caves, there was no electricity, but our guide handed us the flashlight.  I enjoyed this tour because we saw wild pigs (8 of them), white birds (sorry, I don't know the names), bats, buffalo, and mountain goats.  Linh Coc was my favorite tour because it was very peaceful and quiet.  No other tourists.  Also, our Linh Coc guide rowed the boat with his feet the entire hour!  So I am mentioning this in case you are looking for an alternative to Trang An or Tam Coc, which are both very popular. Please note, on both of these tours, it's expected to tip the boat guide.  Either tour you choose, I think you'll be enchanted by the natural beauty of Ninh Binh.

author: Shannon
title: Shangri-la Oasis
original_content: One of the most magical places on earth. The area has been well planned and revitalised for tourism. Great cave systems and shrines to see, with clean toilets in each area. The only negative would be the Rowers 'expect to be tipped' so aren't the most thankful when you do tip them even if you do tip a lot. Mind you they do so much rowing so do assist as most are elderly and women Rowers. Tips recommended by tour guides are 20k per passenger.
highlights: well planned and revitalised for tourism

author: Smartmart07
title: Beautiful in every way.
original_content: Incredible scenery and so serene. I chose to visit Trang An as there are three options for your tour, compared to one at Tam Coc, as it wasn’t the harvest season for the rice I chose Trang An, I certainly don’t regret my choice.

author: ruth o
title: Serene boat ride
original_content: Worth the visit. Water was clear and weather pristine. Lots to see. My teenage kids enjoyed the ride

author: Mick247
title: Cave tour 3
original_content: This is well organised and very tranquil You can just taxi here and buy a single ticket to the cave tour then walk through the tunnel to the other side you tell the gate which one of the 3 cave tours you want to go on and you’ll wait for a boat 4 in a boat so you may have to wait for someone else who wants to go on your choice (They will take 3 )All trip is done by paddle so you can help by paddling if your inclined I found locals did this especially if you have a little old lady Caves can get low in parts but truly one of a kind adventure We tipped at the end but there’s no pressure to do soTips …*Maybe a hat if its hot*Went on a boat with a local and he changed the tour to the one he wanted once onboard so be weary of that* taxi driver may want to buy your ticket for you so he can profit - just pay driver and make your own way to ticket counter*single ticket counter is the way to go, Can buy multi pass tickets at left of entry for other attractions.*You can do all 3 caves in a day if you stay local but 1 and 3 are the favourites *Before 8.30am is nice and quiet*Getting on the boat last gives you front seat into cave  (we took turns)Takes around 2 hours each trip*Not much food here for lunch etc
drawbacks: Went on a boat with a local and he changed the tour to the one he wanted once onboard
taxi driver may want to buy your ticket for you so he can profit
Not much food here for lunch etc
highlights: locals did this especially if you have a little old lady
practical_tips: Maybe a hat if its hot
Getting on the boat last gives you front seat into cave
single ticket counter is the way to go

author: christopher m
title: A great experience
original_content: Visited to get a day away from the pollution and "mentalness" of Hanoi! What a great decision that was. The trip on the lagoon was amazing: tranquil with exquisite scenery: a place of outstanding natural beauty. A truly wonderful experience.

author: Paul S
title: Still worth it despite the crowds
original_content: Is this a massive tourist trap? Yes, absolutely. It was pretty crowded even on low season, I can't imagine how bad it gets. We could always see other tourists on boats at every point of the ride. It's also fairly expensive. If you're a two then you'll need to find someone to share with before boarding, the staff are not very helpful at this and will just board others ahead of you, you need to forcefully start boarding or you'll get ignored.All that aside, it's probably worth doing anyway, the views are stunning, the 1km cave on the 3rd route is particularly impressive, there are some pagodas if you're not Pagoda'd out yet, and it manages to wow even though we'd just been on a boat in Lan Ha bay which was equally stunning. Wish there was a less touristy way of doing it, but you just have to try and forget the other hundred people on the water.
practical_tips: find someone to share with before boarding
try and forget the other hundred people on the water

author: Mike B
title: Share a boat
original_content: Yes a must do. The temple stops are a bit boring, but a chance to have a stretch. Remember the boats hold 4 people, and the charge is per boat. So stand at the ticket office and wait for another couple to share a boat with. Great adventure through the caves. No health & safety -so remember to duck !!  There is 2 different operations, the 4 per boat trip number 3 seemed the best.
practical_tips: stand at the ticket office and wait for another couple to share a boat with

author: luc d
title: i like
original_content: Attractive tourist destination not only domestically but also internationally, the management board is operating very well and has many outstanding points, the experience is extremely impressive and friendly, and the service is highly emphasized.

original_content: The scenery is breathtaking, poetic and lyrical, the service is good but not outstanding. Good price !!!!!

author: P J
title: Fantastic day trip from Ninh Binh.
original_content: We went on route 3. The trip is fantastic, you will set off in groups of 4 so please bear this in mind as you might have to share a boat. This route takes about 2 hours and goes through 3 caves the longest of which is 1 KM  in length. You will stop along the way and will be able to get refreshments and have the use of clean toilets. A truly amazing experience.
drawbacks: Might have to share a boat

author: Skram66
title: Join the visiting Vietnamese & just definitely do it. 3+hrs. Easy access from Tam Coc.
original_content: Cannot recommend enough! Would strongly suggest No3 Tour, which takes in 3 caves, the longest of which is 1 metre long. Several opportunities to get out of the boat at various pagoda islands where you can buy refreshments at some. Interaction/racing with group of Vietnamese on holiday, as well as having a couple of young Vietnamese girls in traditional Vietnam style dress only added to this wonderful experience, so don't be put off by the pictures of many tourists. Located within beautiful setting, well geared for tourists. Moped parking 15Dong. Unfortunately, you have to wear the life jackets provided. Umbrellas of various fashions, also provided. Take some fluid with you & sun protection if hot!
drawbacks: have to wear the life jackets provided
practical_tips: Take some fluid with you & sun protection if hot!

author: MartinHBE
title: Beautiful
original_content: Something so beautiful is rarely seen on this earth. You can explore various tributaries of the river in small boats. You go through "tunnels" (grottos) in a rowing boat, served by women of all ages. It is a must-see.

author: Keshav A
title: Beautiful
original_content: It's a long boat ride approx 3 hours. 4 persons to a boat. Three different routes from which you have to choose one. We took route 1 and went through amazing caves and visited a temple. Beutiful experience
practical_tips: choose one of the three routes

author: ContentedTraveller70
title: Stunningly Beautiful
original_content: We visited Trang An early this morning and were the second boat out so we were ahead of the masses when they arrived by bus load later on. The area is stunningly beautiful and photos do not do the area justice. It’s easy to see why it is UNESCO listed. Unlike the boat trip from Tam Coc the woman who rowed us did so with her arms and not her legs. She was extremely fit as she rowed four of us around for three hours with only short breaks as we visited the temples. We gave her a small tip 100,000 vnd for her hard work.

author: HRaezeina
title: Words can not describe
original_content: This is an intricate part of Vietnam. No words can truly describe how this place has charm and attraction, all come and visit

author: orrdin
title: Fun experience
original_content: This row boat tour was quite fun even in the constant rain. The rowers who are mostly women use their legs most of the time and it’s quite a spectacle to see. And on top of that the river and the caves are nice so this was a great experience. Takes a few hours.

author: Chàng Trai M
title: Trang An Grottoes

author: Gennifer L

When the ride was over, our butts and legs felt numb.It was quite fun initially and we helped to paddle the boat. After a while, the ride became boring and tiring.Will never take this boat ride again.
