author: Isabell8785
title: Stunning and unique
original_content: Absolutely beautiful trip and it wasn’t extremely full of people either! The air was very hazy but the views still stunning. Our lady who paddled us all the way did a great job!
highlights: Our lady who paddled us all the way did a great job

author: cramac
title: By boat through a marvelous landscape
original_content: The temples aren't much, except for one, but for its lotus lake. The caves are nice but nothing special. But the scenery is fantastic.

author: Kaytlynmay
title: Nice trip in Trang An
original_content: Nice experience with a super friendly boat driver and learn a lot about the culture. The scenery and boat trip to the tunnel caves is absolutely incredible with the natural mountains and temple. Will back again
extracted_spaces: boat trip to the tunnel caves
highlights: learn a lot about the culture

author: Steven H
title: A leisurely cruise on a hot day!
original_content: One of the major tourist attractions in the region,  the Trang An boat tour. We went quite early in the morning to attempt to beat the heat, it's quite a professional set-up in terms of ticketing,  on site shopping and getting to the boats. We opted for a boat to ourselves so we're required to pay double the price per person, all good, it was our choice.Ushered to the docks, were greeted by our boat rower/operator and away we went. We felt a little guilty given it was a hot day and we had about 90 mins  of rowing ahead, so we chose to pick up a paddle and help our guide.It's quite a spectacular setting,  the rivers meandering through the karsts. We went through a few caves on our journey so sometimes you need to be prepared to get down quite low. In saying that, the boat lady was very skilful in navigating the highest point in the cave. We also stopped at a couple of pagodas along the way, a chance to stretch the legs, grab a drink or ice-cream and also gives your boat lady a well earned break.All in all it was a very nice experience.
drawbacks: had to get down quite low in the caves
practical_tips: go early to beat the heat
consider paying extra for a private boat

author: Julie A
title: Absolutely Stunning! Avoid the weekends!
original_content: Stunning!  Avoid the weekends and go very early in the morning to avoid the masses. we went around 7am paid a little extra for a boat of our own and enjoyed the whole experience for two hours as the only boat on the water which was amazing!   Go to Trang rather than Tam Coc, its much nicer. Tam coc will not let you off the boat where as from Trang you can get off the boat to walk around the temples which are stunning.   Take route 2You don't need to book this trip with and agent. Just get a grab or go as we did by scooter as the drive there is stunning, theres a big car park and you can buy your tickets from the ticket office.Be very discreet but tip you rower please, they work a very long day!
drawbacks: Tam Coc will not let you off the boat
practical_tips: Go very early in the morning

author: B K
title: Trang An Boat Ride - Highlight of Ninh Binh - Amazing Experience
original_content: Trang An boat ride was the highlight of our Ninh Binh Trip.To pass through water amidst those huge structures and the variety of flora and fauna was an amazing experience.The low caves & specially the longest one (900 m) was a leap of faith for me , as someone who has fear of closed spaces.We had to duck into the floor of the boat and even then crouch real low at some of the places. But I am glad that we could have the exotic experience. The tickets are 300K VND per person . We were a family of 4 in one boat.The boats seemed primarily driven by women rowers. They take you through caves & to pagodas which are on picturesque islandsWe chose route 3 with 3 caves & 3 pagodas. It was sunny & hot.. Its better to have your own umbrellas in case you are more than 2.The boat woman provided us with 1 umbrella. We had ours too and kept ourselves stocked with water and cool drinks. The 3 hr ride is a bit physically taxing as you can’t move much in the small boat. Getting off and on the boat is a tad tricky. So we got off only on 2 islands and skipped 1.The islands and Pagodas were very beautiful. I could see toilet facilities on one of the islands.The boat woman didn’t understand or speak english. So they can’t guide much.It’s quite some hard work. In the last 1 hr, we helped her in rowing as they provide 2 extra oars in the boat. Some other guests were seen doing that too. But that’s totally voluntary obviously.I don’t know if tipping is the norm. But I thought they might be expecting it . We tipped her 100K VND & she seemed happy with it.
drawbacks: boat woman didn't understand or speak english
getting off and on the boat is a tad tricky
practical_tips: keep yourselves stocked with water and cool drinks

author: TravelingFool88005
title: A must do!
original_content: If you only have time for one boat ride, do this one.  This is spectacular!  We did the route with 9 caves and 3 pagodas.  Pro tip:  buy 4 seats so you get your own boat.
highlights: pro tip: buy 4 seats so you get your own boat
practical_tips: buy 4 seats so you get your own boat

author: leoniechinh_19
title: Amazing
original_content: Absolutely one of the most beautiful place to visit in Vietnam, boating experience with local people, 2- 3 hours to finish the trip

author: Shelley M
title: Trang An route 3
original_content: My family really enjoyed our visit here.  3 hours is a long time sitting in a hard boat, ours was closer to 2 and half hours.  We chose the route 3 to see the longest cave, see three caves and 3 pagodas.  The stops were nice to give you a break from the boat.  The 1000m cave is really worth seeing, you do have to duck quite a few times, but it was really scenic.  We didn't see a lot of other boats which was nice and helped the rower as she had 4 of us in the boat.  Noticed as we caught up and passed several boats because 2 guys helped rowing, other boats started to race - it was a bit of fun.  The rower was lovely and didn't ask for tips.  We had already decided to give her one as she didn't harass us.  A great trip, we all enjoyed the scenery.

author: ctm7944
title: Trang An Route #3
original_content: Did Trang An boat ride on a Monday morning @ 8AM, as part of a Motorcycle Tour with Pulong Tours. Cost for boat ride was 250KVND per person. 4 foreigners per boat. Got lucky, immediately connected with 3 European friends who were traveling together. We did Route #3 - 3 caves + 3 temples, including Dot Cave which is the largest/longest cave. The boat ride lasted about 2.5 hours. FYI - The other routes had many more caves + temples. The more stops for caves + temples the longer it takes. Our rower was a very nice lady who spoke a little English. She was very friendly and even took some photos of us. She did not ask for a tip, but we gave her a generous one. Also, no other boats are allowed to peddle food or trinkets on the routes; something which happens on Tam Coc boat rides. Also on Tam Coc boat rides, rowers ask for (demand) tips. Because we were early; for multiple long stretches, it was like a private tour with no other boats around.
drawbacks: other boats peddle food or trinkets

author: Jaroslav Nečas
title: Boat trip
original_content: Good but crowded experience. Attraction offers 3 boat rides between small hills, through caves around pagodas. Place could have been very calm but there were many boats going various directions.Fish in the waters are used to being fed, locals offer fodder to feed them and it's incredible how many comes to you when it's being dropped to water.
highlights: locals offer fodder to feed them

author: Nathan
title: Real Life Disney Jungle Boat Ride
original_content: We chose route 3 since it has the longest cave. The cave was pretty cool but doesn't have many defining features, very few stalactites. Also 1000m is longer than you think and when you need to duck your head a lot to stay clear of bping your head it can get a little claustrophobic. The temples were nice but since I live in China it wasn't that different from what is seen before. Around the temples there is a lot written in Chinese since that is the written language used before Vietnam's modern day alphabet. Luckily my friend is chinese and could translate for me to help me learn a lot about the history of the area. I learned a lot that way that I wouldn't have otherwise since our boat driver only spoke Vietnamese.This is one of the more touristy places we went to. We got there around 8:30AM during a holiday weekend. There were a lot of people but the area was very organized and we were never stuck in any line for very long. However, when you are in the caves it can feel a little like a pirate themed Disney ride since you are in a cave with all the boats lined up one by one.In summary I enjoyed seeing the grottoes, and the surrounding mountains were very beautiful but I don't think there is enough there to entice me to make a repeat visit. It is also pretty long, we took about 3.5 hours to complete the loop.P.S. The ducks are really cute though
drawbacks: not that different from what is seen before
not enough to entice a repeat visit

author: ajelica T
title: Great day out !!
original_content: Hot hot day to be outside but the trip was absolutely worth it. We seen some of the most beautiful moutain ever. The boat ride always fun.

author: Chris
title: Great experience
original_content: I have been here twice in the last 6 months, forts time I took the most common route and the last time route 1 with 9 caves. The place is really special and a must see if in northern vietnam. Give Halong bay a miss and come here. You get a boat with a local rower to take you along the route and give information along the way.  The rowers are not supposed to give or receive tips so make sure you give the tip before returning to the base. The rowers are badly paid and don't get enough work. Great experience better than Tam coc.
practical_tips: give the tip before returning to the base

author: India11
title: Wonderful caves
original_content: Lovely place but crowded with tourists! I was on my own so it was pot luck who I would end in a boat with. They only take groups of three or four people. I had planned to go very early to avoid crowds but as it was raining, I went later. Still rather grey but lovely place. What I loved most were the caves. Glad I chose route 3 with the longest cave.
drawbacks: pot luck who I would end in a boat with
practical_tips: choose route 3 with the longest cave

author: Phi Somchai
title: Awesome landscape
original_content: We rode the river boat to go through the Trang An landscape.   The boat ride was approximately 1.5 hours.  The scenery included limestone mountains and caves and rice fields.   Everything was very surreal and peaceful.   Some parts of the landscape was breathtaking. Overall, I enjoyed the scenery and the boat ride was very memorable.

author: majorstu
title: A great way to get into the heart of the countryside
original_content: Without a doubt this is a commercial concern, but it’s a great way to get into the heart of the waterways, caves, off the beaten track temples and countryside in this beautiful area.  It is good to see that at least some of the monies are being used to maintain the natural beauty - the waterways are clean and rubbish free, the temples and cave’s beautifully kept.  There are three possible routes to choose from - we took option 3 - each last 3 hours.  You glide the waterways in a rowing boat and get off to explore the temples - toilets and light refreshments available at stops.  Certainly our rower spoke no English so couldn’t offer any commentary but it was it was lovely to sit back and take it in.  One of the best activities we did in Ninh Binh/Tam Coc.
highlights: get into the heart of the waterways
practical_tips: glide the waterways in a rowing boat
get off to explore the temples

author: Bill B
title: Not perfect but certainly worthwhile
original_content: My wife and I took the Trang An boat tour after reading reviews comparing it favorably vs. Tam Coc,  We rode our rental bikes from our Tam Coc stay and parked them for 10k VND each at the big parking lot.It is correct that the people selling tickets to the boat ride will attempt to make you pay for a full 4-person boat if you only have two people in your party.  I overheard two Swiss women in an adjacent line being told that and quickly tapped one on the shoulder and offered to join parties with them to fill the boat.The tour is, simply put, an assembly line.  Boats are quickly filled and you're on your way down river along with dozens of others, singing, yelling to each other, etc.  It's not a quiet ride to contemplate the scenery.We took route 3 with only three caves as one of the Swiss women requested we do more open air.  That turned out to be a good idea as, after going through the first 1000 meter cave, the other two offered nothing of additional interest.Overall, the tour was a worthwhile expense and I recommend it.  I suggest you follow the advice of others to go very early or very late to minimize the crowds you'll experience.  Our guide did not ask for a tip but we gave him one anyway.  It's tough work for them and I don't believe they're paid very well.  The scenery was beautiful and worth the trip.

author: DGSmanila
title: boat tour of 2~3 relaxing hours - pictures
original_content: We took tour from Hanoi - if you can it is best to stay in Ninh Binh and explore the area in more than just 1 quick travel.It is crowded so get early possible to buy ticket - OR if you staying in the area thancome after 1PM when the crowed are off to their lunch. The boat trip is very nice. We been 4 people on 1 boat. No English and no databut the view does not need talk.Take you time at each stop for pictures.All in all a nice relaxing 2~3 hours.
practical_tips: Take time at each stop for pictures

author: Jackytantan
title: Nice tim there
original_content: Very Good experience in Trang An.  Coming back to Trang An the second tim with My friends and this tim i wan Lucky for Good weather local boa man wan so friendly

author: Hana lim
title: Nice boat rrip
original_content: It was very good trip frkn Hanoi for 1 day. We enjoyed the trip so much wirh local boat. Conbing it with Bai Dinh Pagoda was good option

author: fal3
title: Worthy of its heritage status!
original_content: Highly recommend this over the Tam Coc boat tour. The driver is pleasant but speaks little English.Went on route 3. The scenery is stunning regardless of weather. Our tour was during highly overcast skies.Extremely clean toilets. The stops and infrastructure felt a bit “Disney land” like and fake, but not to the extent that is common with most of Vietnam’s touristy areas.Lacking a decent gift shop. One exists but it contains the generic things you see everywhere.
drawbacks: stops and infrastructure felt a bit 'Disney land' like and fake
The driver is pleasant but speaks little English
highlights: The scenery is stunning regardless of weather

author: MatthewTheCoder
title: Trang An river boat tour
original_content: We went there as part of a day tour to Ninh Binh. In my tour, 3 places were visited, Hoa Lu, Trang An and Hang Mua. Trang An is must go because of the beautiful sites. The Trang An is a boat ride along a river. The boat ride is about 2 hours and rowed by a boat operator. The boat ride goes through a number caves accessible only by the boats. Some of these caves have very low ceiling and it is best to watch out for your heads! When the boat emerges out from the caves, the scenery changes from a dark cave to a bright open sight of surrounding hills. Very magnificent sight. Trang An is an UNESCO World Heritage site.Do consider tipping the boat rower. It is a 2hr boat ride means this guy or woman will be rowing for a good 2 hours to carry a small boat with 5 pax (4 tourist + 1 rower).
drawbacks: Some of these caves have very low ceiling and it is best to watch out for your heads!
practical_tips: Do consider tipping the boat rower

author: Hanzhe
title: Amazing experience
original_content: The scenery was amazing and much impressive than what I was expecting. The boat tour is a must if visiting the area. Each boat is for 4 people
highlights: much impressive than what I was expecting
a must if visiting the area

author: Chandra M
title: Magical
original_content: Did the Trang An Ecotourism Complex Tour #1 (nine caves and three spiritual places, i.e. temples)It was one of the most exhilarating experiences I've ever had, passing through these caves sometimes with only 3 feet (1 m) between the water line and the ceiling of the caves. The longest ones take the boatman 2-3 minutes to navigate. Absolutely fantastic experience, even the intermittent rain couldn't spoil this amazing adventure

author: Leannie
title: Fantastic scenery on the boat trip
original_content: We came here and paid for a 3 hour boat trip. It was a bit strange at the payment counter as the staff were charging people for a full boat of 4 people even if they were only 2, we got round this by just paying at the same time as another couple but didn't even end up getting the same boat as them. We chose route 3 and joined a Dutch couple also wanting this route, it was a sat morning and there was no waiting round. The trip is a good mix of sitting in the boat but then getting out to explore temples and stretch your legs etcThe boats start off comfy but are rather uncomfortable by the end, they need some cushioning for sure. The woman who for the rowing are amazing, they work so hard rowing the boats full of people for nearly 3 hours
drawbacks: staff were charging people for a full boat of 4 people even if they were only 2
boats start off comfy but are rather uncomfortable by the end
highlights: good mix of sitting in the boat but then getting out to explore temples and stretch your legs
the woman who for the rowing are amazing
practical_tips: pay at the same time as another couple
dress boats with cushioning for comfort

author: Andrea L
title: Incredible view
original_content: Super positive experience, despite the truly extreme heat and humidity. The climb has about 500 steps and at a certain point it splits toward two peaks: on one side Ngoa Long (Dragon Mountain), with the famous stone dragon on the ridge, on the other the peak with the pagoda.The views are incredible: from the top, a spectacular view opens up over the Ninh Binh river, surrounded by rice paddies, lotus fields, and karst mountains. It is absolutely worth the effort of the climb.An important piece of advice: be very careful if you want to reach the dragon. There were a lot of people in line on the ridge and in some spots the space to wait is narrow, precarious, and without real protection. In my opinion, it is not worth risking a fall just for a photo.Take your time, especially with the heat and humidity, and drink often: along the climb there are also small kiosks where you can stop.Tiring? Yes. But absolutely worth doing: one of the most beautiful views we have seen in Ninh Binh.
drawbacks: narrow and precarious space to wait
highlights: spectacular view over Ninh Binh river
practical_tips: be careful when reaching the dragon

author: Eline Mucha
title: Mua Cave
original_content: I loved the stunning mountains and the amazing view from the top. The climb is a little tiring, but definitely worth it for the scenery and photos.
drawbacks: The climb is a little tiring

author: jh0rnsey
title: Amazing views!
original_content: The highlight of this trip were the amazing views from the top of the 500 steep steps. You need to be fit to attempt this climb. Also you can walk on the walkways about the lotus flower fields.
extracted_spaces: walkways about the lotus flower fields
drawbacks: You need to be fit to attempt this climb
practical_tips: You need to be fit to attempt this climb

author: Jean-Emmanuel R
title: Breathtaking
original_content: A magnificent site that deserves 2 hours or even more of your time. Several points of interest are gathered in one place: several viewpoints with a panoramic view of the sumptuous surrounding landscapes, a temple at the very top (which I did not visit), caves, and several spots set up at the bottom of the mountain for photos. The entrance fee is set at 150,000 Dong, which is about $5.50, and it is well worth it.If, like us, you opt for a guided day trip from Hanoi, here is my advice:- Start directly with the climb, which is, I must admit, very physically demanding. The other photo spots at the bottom of the mountain can be done on the way back.- Once you reach halfway up the stairs, you will have the choice between turning right (toward the temple) or left. If you do not have enough time or do not have the energy to do both sides, it is better to turn left. That is where you will have a remarkable panorama of the valley with the river.- A platform is installed on the left side about a hundred steps from the summit. From this platform, you will already have a breathtaking 360-degree view. For our part, we therefore did not deem it necessary to reach the summit.
extracted_spaces: a temple at the very top
several spots set up at the bottom of the mountain for photos
highlights: panoramic view of the sumptuous surrounding landscapes
remarkable panorama of the valley with the river
practical_tips: Turn left at halfway up the stairs
Do not visit the temple if you do not have enough time or energy

author: Kristian M
title: OK view. Not too demanding.
original_content: Not really demanding to go up the stairs. A bit warm at 13:00 but thats it. Took 10 minutes. Beautiful views but not as stunning as other reviews would suggest. The lotus Lake nearby is worth s visit.
drawbacks: not as stunning as other reviews would suggest

author: mvanroy
title: Hard climb with a beautiful view as a reward!
original_content: Apart from the fact that there is a (very) small Tiger cave at the foot, the Mua caves are more a climb of 500 stairs to some beautiful viewpoints than caves. We started early (7am) to avoid the heat and the masses. We could park the bike in the parking lot at the entrance (5,000 vnd per bike). Buy a ticket (150,000 vnd pp) and then climb the stairs. Halfway you have a fork and you can either go to the dragon or to the small pagoda. Both give a beautiful view of the surroundings and each other. The steps themselves are not always easy because they are fairly irregular and high but there are some intermediate steps in the middle as an aid. The pagoda is easy to reach, the dragon requires some more climbing and scrambling (and is not for the little ones among us). In addition to this climb, there are some restaurants, some nice bonsais and a Lotus boardwalk at the complex.
drawbacks: not for the little ones among us
highlights: beautiful view of the surroundings and each other
practical_tips: go early to avoid the heat and the masses

author: hazel
title: Very beautiful.
original_content: I am very impressed with the dance. The space is beautiful and the view from above is amazing. A place not to be missed when arriving in Safe.

author: Janice L
title: Beautiful views
original_content: This moderately difficult hike is beautiful. I have osteo arthritis in my knees but was able to do it just fine. Take your time.  The views are spectacular. (I'm afraid of heights, so I took my photos below the dragon because it was a bit too scary for me). You'll get a workout and you'll lose a lot of sweaty fluid so bring a litre of water! Enjoy! YOLO!

author: Cheryl L
title: Get there before 8am - seriously.
original_content: Climbing Lying Dragon Mountain is an absolute must — but timing is everything. The steps are steep, the summit areas are small, and the photos are infinitely better without crowds in them. The gates open at 6am (really!), and if you arrive within the first couple of hours, you'll practically have the mountain to yourself. We got there at 7:30 and found it completely empty. Go then. You won't regret it.
drawbacks: The photos are infinitely better without crowds in them
highlights: Climbing Lying Dragon Mountain is an absolute must
You'll practically have the mountain to yourself

author: bbrady962
title: Great views and a good workout too!
original_content: Great views and a great workout too so you need a reasonable level of fitness. We left around 4pm so by the time we reached close to the top, it was too crowded to get to the VERY top but we didn't care. We still got up high enough to see the classic view looking in to the steep valleys below. Maybe go earlier in the day if you want to get to the very top but for for us not essential. Defo worth walking around the small lake at the bottom to cool down
drawbacks: too crowded to get to the VERY top
practical_tips: walk around the small lake at the bottom

author: roberto p
title: Breathtaking view
original_content: We were in Ninh Binh in the day from Hanoi with Nyna travel guide who accompanied us in the visit of the north of Vietnam, to get to the dragon mountain you have to climb 500 steps carved into the rock that the higher you climb the higher they become, thank goodness that the weather accompanied us during the climbing was cloudy but as in all of Vietnam very humid .Nevertheless we managed to get up to the dragon overlooking the rice fields and the forest with the river flowing .the full ride takes about 1.30 h -2h taking it easy, under a park with fountains and statues and flowers of all kinds very, very nice....
highlights: View of the dragon overlooking the rice fields and the forest
Park with fountains and statues and flowers
practical_tips: Go early to avoid humid weather
Take it easy to enjoy the view

author: Al M
title: Dangerous click bait - give it a miss
original_content: This is a manufactured click bait – visitors are supposed to see the second feature which is the shrine on top of the hill. The Dragon is a visual display which has been now adapted for tourists but there’s no structure in place – so when you get there, there’s no organised queue system– the walk around the dragon is extremely dangerous and slippery but no safety fence in place on the sides . The exit route is extremely difficult to access and so people , especially with children forced their way back down the difficult access of slipperyslippery rocks with sheer drops fit the only safety is a  bit of  rusty oil chain – there’s no official marshal around the dragon  queue  so people who don’t want to queue entered by the exit and then cause a blockage at the top – it’s an absolute disaster and a complete waste of time unless you go there very early very late -  this is probably the worst tourist trap  I’ve ever come across anywhere in the world .

author: Olivia M
title: Not for those with health issues
original_content: We attempted this climb in early afternoon and while the views are beautiful, do not attempt if you have health conditions like a heart problem or mobility issue. There are cafes before you go up and a some boardwalks around lotus flowers (which bloom in May). There is also one stall about half way up the mountain selling cold drinks.
drawbacks: attempt if you have health conditions like a heart problem or mobility issue

author: Daniel F
title: Great views
original_content: The ascent to the Dragon is exhausting (easily doable), but it is worth it, the view is lovely.The facility below is large and beautifully designed. Especially the water lily field must be great, unfortunately the water lilies were harvested during my visit.Admission costs 100000 VND, tickets can be purchased until 6.00 p.m.The scooter can be parked at the end of the road (at the entrance/ticket office) for 10000 VND.You have to be careful not to get ripped off the scooter by the pushy sellers to park with them.
drawbacks: water lilies were harvested during my visit
practical_tips: park scooter at the end of the road

author: George Severin
title: Breathtaking views.
original_content: Mua Caves is a tourist attraction in the Tam Cac region.A very nice, well-kept complex with cafe, lotus ponds and many flowers. On a rock, the "Lying Mountain Dragon", there is a pagodaand you will be rewarded with a breathtaking view of the Ngo Dong River.The path up is tedious (about 500 steps). You actually need good fitness. Below are smaller ones but also the large cave (Mua Caves). Our visit was part of an organized day tour we took.

author: Mr9xx
title: Limestone Mou
original_content: Marvel at the stunning wave-like limestone mountain landscape. Climb the 500 steps for a rewarding panoramic view truly one of the top highlights to discove

author: Lohit V
title: Speechless with the views
original_content: I’ve been to Mua Cave and it was easily one of the highlights of my trip to Ninh Binh. The climb up the stone steps is a bit of a workout, but totally worth it once you reach the top.  The panoramic view over Tam Coc with the river, rice fields, and limestone mountains is absolutely stunning—especially around sunset. It does get quite hot and crowded, so I’d recommend going early morning or late afternoon.  A must-visit spot if you’re in Ninh Binh and don’t mind a bit of climbing!

author: Anna T
title: Gain the top and widen your gaze
original_content: Taking advantage of a cloudy day, the greeting is tiring but pleasant. We climbed in 1 hour and a half making the two peaks, one with the dragon and one with the tower. There were many beautiful girls in costume with accompanying photographers, perhaps because it is Tet (Vietnamese New Year) week. Beautiful view, even if in February the colors of the different crops are missing, now at the beginning of growth or just planted. Walk ddu wooden walkways. Beautiful bonsai trees on display.

author: Ria1104
title: A Nice Hike Leading Up to a Dragon at the Top
original_content: When we first heard about the place, we thought it was some sort of cave. But in reality it was nothing like that. Mua Cave is actually a popular destination in Nihn Bin, where you can hike up a limestone mountain to get breathtaking views of the winding river, mountains and rice fields around. There is a dragon statue at the top and if you are comfortable to walk on sharp stones with a steep drop, you will enjoy a magnificent view of the Nihn Bin area.The climb can be tiring and it is advisable to wear proper shoes and exercise caution at the top near the dragon. The area at the bottom is beautifully decorated particularly the lotus field with the winding walkways. We can get cool Instagram shots in this place.
drawbacks: wear proper shoes and exercise caution at the top near the dragon
highlights: magnificent view of the Nihn Bin area

author: Sandra L
title: Lovely.
original_content: We went first thing in the morning and it was a haven of peace. A boat trip without all the crowds that are after. We did tour C, much more nature and with fewer temples. It's beautiful though it's important to know it's 3 hours. It reminds a little of Ha Long Bay on dry land.

author: Luca Magnanensi
title: The most photographed panorama
original_content: A popular attraction in the area, the site offers several things including walkways over the lotus flower field, the Mua Cave the climb to the Mountain of the Lying Dragon with its famous staircase of about 500 steps. The curious thing is that despite being called Mua Cave (literally Mua cave), almost no one visits the cave and comes home having only made the climb to the mountain... absurd, but it is the 'power' of social media. There are also some very nice bars at European prices, a SPA, a resortEntry price 100k money them, about 3.5 euros
drawbacks: Almost no one visits the cave
highlights: Walkways over the lotus flower field
Climb to the Mountain of the Lying Dragon

author: caroleen78
title: At the top of the steps
original_content: You must arrive early and climb the 489 steps to admire the view. This climb was built 15 years ago. I imagine the construction work. The steps are quite uneven and rather steep but frankly it is worth going to some trouble. I smiled because on the way it plagues in all languages on the difficulty of the course.Splendid view of the winding river and all the boats.I really advise you to take a boat to take this walk between the karst limestone rocks.We were led by a lovely lady And what’s special is that they all row with their feet She offered us on the return of the hand sewn paintings and frankly I found one very nice that I bought 7 euros Yes of course it is very touristy it builds a lot and soon it will have lost a lot of its authentic character but it is a world that moves and all we want to enjoy comfort
drawbacks: will have lost a lot of its authentic character

author: Michael W
title: Views rather than caves. (Well, one tiny cave). But for Dave’s, there are other cool places.
original_content: The steps were steep and there were a lot of them! The view was totally worth it. Go to the tail of the dragon only if you are sure footed, agile, and not disturbed by heights.
practical_tips: go to the tail of the dragon only if you are sure footed, agile

author: Designer NC
title: A fun day out
original_content: A fun experience, wear old trainers, I did it in January and would also reccomend wearing a hoody. There are lights in the caves which is helpful

author: Russell N
title: As long as you are not expecting caves you will not be disappointed.
original_content: Strange name for a place which is actually a fabulous viewpoint. The actual cave is more of an alcove but the walk to the top is worth it. At the fork in the path - go right for the pagoda or left for the dragon.On the approach road people will step out and try and scam you for parking - just swerve around them and keep going. There is parking inside the main gate (5k for a bicycle 10k for a moped). Also parking lot to the right of the main gates at the same price.
practical_tips: parking lot to the right of the main gates

author: Karyne B
title: Attention bike and motorcycle parking
original_content: Watch out for fake parking! Locals force you to park well before entering the mua caves site! They force you in a very authoritarian and borderline threatening way to park at their house and ask you for money by bike or motorcycle. Do not stop even if they will be very threatening and make you understand with threatening gestures and looks that you do not have the right to go further! It’s completely wrong there is a parking lot just to the right of the entrance to visit the site. We were stopped by two Women who were even threatening because we didn’t want to stay and we took our motorcycle back to park at the entrance of the site we were forced to threaten them in turn to call the police if they didn’t return the money they asked us for when they were not allowed to do so.They finally gave it back to us but we understood that they were not happy and surely insulted us in Vietnamese.
extracted_spaces: parking lot just to the right of the entrance
drawbacks: Locals force you to park well before entering the site
Threatening and authoritarian behavior from locals
Forced to pay money to locals for parking
practical_tips: Park at the official parking lot just to the right of the entrance
Be cautious of locals trying to force you to park elsewhere

author: Valter C
title: A climb worth the scenery.
original_content: Tiring climb of 500 steps to get to the dragon on top, but there is also the shorter option that leads to the small pagoda on the nearby hillock.Equip yourself with non-slip shoes if there is moisture or rain and even a windproof jacket, because at some point it begins to pull hard.
extracted_spaces: small pagoda on the nearby hillock

author: Enrica R
title: Visited in October with rain
original_content: I visited this place on a rainy day so I practically climbed the 500 high and slippery steps with enormous effort. From up there the view over the rice fields and the Ninh Binh valley is wonderful. Sore note that made me very angry was that you can not pay with the card and not having enough cash my husband could not go up with us. Too bad that in such a tourist place we still do not have the pos.
highlights: view over the rice fields and the Ninh Binh valley

author: MM0980
title: Exhausting climb that is worthwhile
original_content: I went there by bike. Parking bike costs 5,000 VND. Admission costs 100,000 VND. The climb was exhausting and seemed like an eternity. I went first the way to the pagoda (15 min) and then the way to the lying dragon (15 min). You can also walk a bit to the starting point. From both viewpoints you have wonderful views of nature. At the lying dragon has been a single human casserole. Nice view. It was worth it.

author: Masela Fadjar Pratiwi
title: Must visit in Ninh Binh
original_content: Hang Múa (Mua Caves) is an absolute must-visit in Ninh Binh! 🏞️✨ The hike up may be challenging with its 500 steps, but the breathtaking panoramic view at the top makes it all worth it. 🌄😍 From the peak, you get an incredible view of the Tam Coc valley, limestone karsts, and rice fields stretching as far as the eye can see.The atmosphere is peaceful, and the scenery is perfect for photos. 📸 Just be sure to wear comfortable shoes and bring water, especially on hot days! Highly recommended for nature lovers and adventure seekers. 🇻🇳⛰️

author: みるく
title: I was tired, but I climbed hard
original_content: It's called Mua Cave, so I thought it was a cave, but it was completely different. I just climb the stairs and head for the top. There are hundreds of steps, so it's best to avoid them if you're unsure of your legs. I managed to climb it while I was resting. The summit is ... fun to climb.
practical_tips: avoid them if you're unsure of your legs

author: Marika
title: Poor dog at the entrance of Mua Cave
original_content: There is a poor dog chained in a cage close to the ticket counter of Mua Cave. When you go there please bring some water or appropriate food for the dog if you can. We felt very sorry today and tried to locate the owner to talk to him but couldn’t. The dog is right at the parking space at the waterfront. Given this is a tourist attraction we might be able to help this dog together. Many thanks
drawbacks: poor dog chained in a cage
practical_tips: bring some water or appropriate food for the dog

author: mrbrentharris
title: Absolutely stunning
original_content: The views from the top of the mountain are stunning. Depending on your fitness level, it can be a challenging hike, but I highly recommend going to the top if you can. Be patient as it can get very crowded
highlights: views from the top of the mountain are stunning
practical_tips: go to the top if you can

author: juliajg93
title: 520 steps for spectacular views
original_content: We visited this venue on our Ninh Binh day trip from Hanoi, this being our last stop of the day before returning to the city.It is worth noting that the famous stairs to climb the viewpoint were built just over 10 years ago as a tourist claim, without what you see at the top having a spiritual or historical value for the locals. However, the views of the Tam Coc River from the heights are beautiful and compensate for the hard climb on foot.To climb the 520 steps it takes around 15 minutes, while the descent is done in just under 10. Between the different levels there are benches to sit on and even a place to buy water (much needed!). Shortly before reaching the top there is a small viewpoint if you do not want to get to the top of everything, where the steps are increasingly irregular. There are a couple of drinking establishments with shaded areas and fans.Perhaps I would not consider it an essential, but if you are in the area, the time accompanies and you have energy, it is worth it.

author: Autogirogiringiro
title: So much effort for the ascent but what views! Not to be missed during your stay in Tam Coc
original_content: Noticed the day before during the boat trip on the river, we decided to visit this observation point the next day and it was actually worth it. An almost adrenaline-pumping experience for the slope of the steps (appears about 600) and for the overhangs. It is therefore not recommended for those who have problems with vertigo or those who cannot engage in a rather heavy physical commitment, considering also the heat. However, at some point of the climb there are pitches, one where there is also a bar. The views are really breathtaking at both vantage points and if visibility is good you will consume a lot of memory of your smartphone. Very nice also the starting village with numerous bars and probably even a hotel inside.

author: Explorer56807302709
title: Beautiful view!
original_content: Good workout! We set the alarm at 6am and drove there by scooter. No bother for pushy people telling you where to park.We saw 3 more goats on the path up. Was not crowded and beautiful view as reward after those 500 steps!
drawbacks: pushy people telling you where to park

author: Willi S
original_content: The steep climb up Mua Cave was worth every step. From the top, we gazed at breathtaking karst landscapes stretching endlessly.@Go early :))

author: Adventure05703998509
title: Beautiful viewpoint and lotus field
original_content: The whole is made up of a photo area with cafes and a lotus field (very nice but invaded by Vietnamese for their photos but we have room to move), and a hill with 2 peaks so you can see both sides of the hill (the most interesting being the peak with the river, the highest). The highest peak ends on a not very landscaped area where one stands at dragon carving (if you have vertigo or bad shoes, avoid) which gives a very nice view.
drawbacks: invaded by Vietnamese for their photos
highlights: most interesting being the peak with the river
practical_tips: avoid if you have vertigo or bad shoes

author: absarita
title: Mua Cave
original_content: Amazing trekking session!!! Had the best lotus farm and it's very scenic Always carry a water bottle and keep hydrated.

author: Bondy Arachnid
title: Breathtaking View!
original_content: It was a challenging climb to the top of Mua Cave, but wow, the panoramic view was our reward. We felt like we were on top of the world, looking out over the stunning Ninh Binh landscape. A must-do for adventurous !

author: Rens33
title: Hot as, but fun!
original_content: We rode bicycles from Tam Coc- fairly easy commute. We arrived early and ignored the locals trying to get us to park, riding right to the gates to park there- fee 5k per bicycle.Entered the park to do the two climbs. Great views from either side of surrounding rivers and the lotus field.Although we were early- it was still very hot. Steps are high if you are not overly tall. Recommend decent footwear. We left the complex about 11am, the temp was rising and tour buses were arriving

author: lilybt
title: Small climb
original_content: Many tours from Hanoi combine Hoa Lu with a cruise on Tran An or Tam Coc, and few incorporate Mua Cave here. The stone steps are maintained, but the steps are volatile, which causes unexpected fatigue. There are two courses, one that branches off the summit course and the other that branches off halfway up the mountain, but the summit is difficult to control in the one hour given to the tour. In the final phase, people got stuck for photography, and the stone steps were narrow, so I gave up and went down to enjoy the view on the Tamcoc side.
drawbacks: difficult to control in the one hour given to the tour
highlights: enjoy the view on the Tamcoc side

author: Dominique P
title: To be done with caution
original_content: The views are magnificent both on the river that leads and on the water lily field.However, it is necessary to climb nearly 400 steps, all uneven, of variable heights and regularly too high and slippery.But if you go up, what a view. You have to choose the climb that goes to the left to see the River.
drawbacks: uneven, of variable heights and regularly too high and slippery
practical_tips: choose the climb that goes to the left

author: Rachel H
title: Stunning views and scenery, worth the sweaty climb up!
original_content: Prepare yourself for a sweaty tough climb! We are not the fittest but managed it in the heat of the afternoon with a few stops on the way and plenty of water. We were told the path to the left was trickier but with better views. There are more steps on this route but it it is only the last 10 or so that are not steps and are more of a scramble. However we weren’t fussed about being able to say we went to this bit as the the views would have been very similar and it was so crowded up there it would have been dangerous. The views from the top and the way up are stunning, just as you see in the guidebooks for Vietnam. On your way back to the car park there’s also some lovely walkways over the water and we caught some of the sunset which was very pretty. Definitely recommend making this trip when in Ninh Binh and can buy tickets at the entrance so no need to book ahead.

author: bine-ich
title: Well planned a 100% dreamlike experience
original_content: Sensational in the early morning when it is cooler and without crowds. I would only do it in dry weather for safety reasons and preferably at lotus flowering time. We were late May and it was hotter than hot, but that was the only downside. Good climbing shoes, sun protection and something to drink. And best to deposit dry extra clothes in the scooter, because after that our clothes were wet with sweat up to the underwear.

author: thomeson
title: A Breathtaking Summit Adventure with Dragon Mountain Views
original_content: Mua Cave in Ninh Binh was absolutely breathtaking! The 500-step climb to the summit was well worth it for the panoramic views of the rice fields and limestone mountains. Our guide was very helpful, and the dragon statue at the top made for fantastic photos. The cave itself was interesting, but the real highlight was the view from 'Dragon Mountain'. Make sure to go early morning to avoid the heat and crowds!

author: 1330marc
title: To do early in the morning
original_content: Beautiful. We went there at 6:30 in the morning and we were alone! The climb is not very difficult and there are risers for the highest steps. Beautiful views of the river and lotus fields. We also made the second sanctuary then the lotus fields. At 7am we only met two couples!Do not forget the mosquito spray!
drawbacks: Do not forget the mosquito spray!
practical_tips: Do not forget the mosquito spray!

author: Mike W
title: Lovely views
original_content: We cycled to Mua at 7am. We parked the tickets by the ticket booth and started the 500 plus step climb. It was already hot but there were few people around. The climb was tiring but you have the views to stop and admire. We took the left path to the dragon first and then the right to the lookout. The views are fabulous. A wonderful start to the day and a well earned breakfast.
highlights: A wonderful start to the day

author: Christine F
title: Great reward after strenuous climb
original_content: After the strenuous climb, you will be rewarded with a beautiful view over the region. If you come just in time of year when the water lily fields are blooming, it must be even more beautiful.  The stairs are still normal to walk at first, but are becoming increasingly irregular in height and depth. There are no railings, now and then you almost have to climb or shimmy along the edge. Taking a child with a child carrier on his back upwards was something we found very daring in others, as you can not walk upright at all, especially towards the end, in many places, but rather pull yourself up.
drawbacks: stairs are irregular in height and depth
difficult to walk upright at the end
highlights: beautiful when water lily fields are blooming
practical_tips: go early to see water lily fields blooming
be careful with child carriers on stairs

author: Mickey
title: BEWARE OF PARKING SCAM
original_content: As per other reviews, the motorcycle parking scam is still alive and well, operational thanks to a miserable male duo. The pair have been known to destroy bikes if you do not park in their unofficial space, but will more commonly grab bikes, pull riders off the bike, and even slash tires. The charming pair will charge unaware riders hundreds of thousands of VND to park.Being aware of this scam, we parked our bikes about 300m up the road and walked to the entrance. The actual sting is about 80m prior to the official entrance, where you can park your bike safely for 10k.I recommend parking further back along the road, before the Misery Men® to avoid conflict.Having said this the attraction itself is beautiful and well worth a visit!
drawbacks: charge hundreds of thousands of VND
practical_tips: park your bike about 300m up the road
park further back along the road, before the Misery Men

author: afroditi18
title: Awesome views
original_content: A nice way to spend an hr and a half! Stairs are steep but not dangerous (if it's dry). Amazing view! Cave definitely underwhelming. 5000 vdn for bike parking; 100K entrance fee.
practical_tips: check the weather before using the stairs

author: Kishor D
title: Amazing place
original_content: Amazing place and views with foot pedals on boats. Restaurants opposite the entrance. Go through 3 caves and ancient temples

author: corinne_prevost
title: WHAT TO DO ABSOLUTELY
original_content: A very nice place. Certainly bcp people but that is to be seen. For the steps it is difficult and we did not do the last 50 a little too dangerous for us. 66 and 75. Well, for my part, it took me two days to clear the pain in my thighs. Really the place is very beautiful and the view superb. We can walk in the lotuses which for us was not in bloom, not the period, and the route is interesting. Restaurants are not excessive and the ride is good.

author: akio9jp
title: It's tough in an hour.
original_content: It's not a cave, it's a climb. We climbed about 500 steep stone steps to the top of the mountain, Drangon, but with only an hour of free time on the tour, we decided to turn back about half way, considering our over 60th birthday health.Still, the observation space, located about 300 steps away, offered idyllic and beautiful views of rowdy boats floating in the Tamcoc River, steep cliffs and strange rocks.
drawbacks: rowdy boats floating in the Tamcoc River

author: Anne LM
title: Magnificent view, the climb is worth it
original_content: Very frequented place of tourists, climb quite difficult and dangerous. But the scenery is amazing once you get upstairs, it’s worth it and I find it a must when visiting the region. It allows you to take height and have a beautiful view of the terrestrial halong bay. At the feet you can also walk in the lotus fields (which you can see only when it is the season)
drawbacks: Climb is quite difficult and dangerous
highlights: Beautiful view of the terrestrial Halong Bay
practical_tips: Go when the lotus fields are in season

author: S&O
title: Definitely 486 steps up
original_content: This is a real highlight in the area. The two mountains with pagodas on the top should definitely be climbed. 486 steps to the dragon's tip. Then visit the cave during the descent.  Great bonsais on site and a huge walkable area with lotus plants. Top package.

author: Kay S
title: Tamoc & Mua Caves, Minh Binh tour with Cozy Vietnam
original_content: Although raining the views were amazing. I would highly recommend. But be aware of when you go as the weekends are crammed, as the locals visit aswell. The boat ride is good and the water is keep clean for once. Also beware trips with cycling as the bikes aren’t maintained, no brakes and one persons pedal fell off. The tour itself is a little disjointed but don’t let this put you off. The guides are great fun

author: Heather S
title: Amazing views from the top
original_content: Took so many photos!  The views are incredible but the steps seemed never ending!  I have to say that the steps are fairly low and not great big high things that you have to haul yourself up!  These were normal step level I think.  Once near the top, you can choose to to left or right.  We did both!  The right side goes to the small shrine and the left goes to the dragon which is not located on a path.  From the top you can just see the dragons head but people were rock climbing at their own risk to get to this dragon which was a dangerous feat and not to be done in my opinion!
drawbacks: rock climbing at their own risk

author: Mork001
title: Crowded
original_content: You get to decide at the half way mark to go to the dragon or temple routes.So slow getting up and the last few metres are ridiculous.The views are brilliant and worth the effort.
practical_tips: go to the dragon or temple routes

author: Pier F
title: Don’t miss this gem in Ninh Binh
original_content: Climbing the 500 steps rewarded us with breathtaking views of Ninh Binh’s karst landscapes—truly a couple’s dream. The adventure activities, from exploring hidden caves to cycling through lush rice fields, kept our hearts racing. Evenings were magical, with traditional cultural performances adding a touch of local charm.

author: Bel
title: Worth a visit for sure!
original_content: We loved it here…. Has a little village atmosphere about it. Although the 500 steps are steep… please note it requires a few breaks …. It is well worth the effort as the views are lovely. I was rewarded with the dragon at the top!

author: Nickola Barry
title: A breathtaking adventure for two!
original_content: Climbing the 500 steps to the top of Mua Cave was worth every effort! The panoramic views of Ninh Binh’s limestone karsts and rice fields were unforgettable. A romantic and adventurous spot for couples.

author: Bénédicte F
title: Beautiful
original_content: To be done early in the morning because less people. Be in good physical condition for the 500 steps and take water. Halfway you can buy some

author: Webster Lee
title: Ninh Binh's Natural Beauty
original_content: The stunning natural beauty left us in awe—the panoramic views from the top were simply breathtaking. The friendly local guides made our visit even more enjoyable, sharing fascinating stories and insights. The welcoming community added a special touch to our experience, making us feel at home. It was the perfect spot for a romantic adventure, and we can't wait to return. Highly recommend this magical place!
practical_tips: perfect spot for a romantic adventure

author: Alex
title: It's a nice view of the mountains. It's recommended to pick a good season and weather.
original_content: I saw a lot of reviews about lotus flowers and rice fields, but this season there are no lotus flowers, there is no rice in the rice fields, only a mountain climbing activity, it's a bit boring. The mountain is very good, some steps are high, it is very challenging to climb, the scenery is good, on the mountain you can also see people on the Sangu River on a boat tour, but the air is not good enough to see especially far, it is important to choose a good season and good weather!
drawbacks: air is not good enough to see especially far

author: Sirisha D
title: Hard but worth the climb
original_content: There are about 500 steps to reach the top. Left side peak is the highest one with the lying dragon on the top. There is no flat surface near the dragon for pictures and it’s risky with many people hanging around. Right side peak is lower one. It has the Instagram-able pagoda and the lotus pond top view. Best pics will be at the time of sunrise on a clear day.
drawbacks: risky with many people hanging around
no flat surface near the dragon for pictures
highlights: best pics will be at the time of sunrise on a clear day

author: Henry Jackson
title: Mua Caves is a great place
original_content: Mua Caves is a great place to visit with friends! The climb to the summit is challenging, but the panoramic view of the Ninh Bình valley is spectacular. Mountains and rivers look like natural paint. The atmosphere is quiet, perfect for relaxing and taking unforgettable photos. An experience not to be missed in Ninh Bình!

author: julc130
title: Mua Caves Parking Beware
original_content: Views were good. Stairs not so bad but very busy. Felt a little dangerous on the way down with all the impatient people hurrying to the bottom. Worth it though if you take your time. We were on pushbikes. When parking people try to stop you just keep riding. It’s a con. Don’t stop. We parked right near the gate and agreed 50k for 5 bicycles. They locked our bike and asked for more money when we came back down. Stand your ground and they unlocked for us. We however would not pay until we came back down which helped as no unlock, no money. Con artists but seemed inevitable. We couldn’t readily find any free marking but there may have been. For 50k it wasn’t worth a massive argument. Be warned.

author: Petitgiaco
title: A very nice point of view.
original_content: First of all go VERY early if you do not want to get into "traffic jams" on the way up. At the arrival breathtaking view but it is only if you do not have to take a ticket to wait until the "staggerers" have finished their shots with or without hat and their different poses, to take his own photo. It's become UNBEARABLE. I advise to go very early because it's really worth a look, I repeat but it doesn't quickly want a hell. It's up to you to judge according to your level of patience.
drawbacks: wait until the staggerers have finished their shots

author: aimonetti b
title: A great panorama!!
original_content: A big and beautiful effort to make (500 steps not easy to climb) but a breathtaking 360° view. Nice reward

author: Davies A
title: Amazing panoramic view
original_content: Definitely worth a visit on the top but 500 steps are no joke. If you book a tour, ask if they'll do the cave in the afternoon or not cuz around 4-5pm you'll see flock of birds flying back home! Also I hope they can do better with safety signs around. It's kinda dangerous if you go by yourself and got injured. Anyway, I'd still come back next time!
drawbacks: dangerous if you go by yourself and got injured
highlights: see flock of birds flying back home
practical_tips: ask if they'll do the cave in the afternoon

author: Anne H
title: Worth the climb !
original_content: Amazing views !   Steps were harder going down (for me anyway).    We started at 8.30am and it was perfect - less crowded and not as hot either.

author: Trina M
title: MOA CAVES
original_content: DID NINH BINH MOA CAVES (TAM COC) ITS A WORTHWHILE DAY, THEY TAKE YOU ON A SMALL BOAT. THE LADY ROWED WITH HER FEET, THE CAVES WERE REFRESHING. THE LADY PUT IT ON US FOR A TIP. WE ENJOYED THE TRIP BUT NOT THE DEMAND FOR A TIP

author: Nathalie M
title: The view from above gives chills
original_content: Rising to the top this fact!!! We will say that the view from above is worth the climb!!! I recommend!!! Have fun Go at your own pace

author: Horizon Hugo
title: Great 360 view !
original_content: This is a park where you have lotus fields , the hang mua cave , and also the lying dragon mountain. The view up there is incredible. Not very crowded in the morning , but I've heard that it's very crowded at sunset.

author: Staci B
title: Mind blowing beauty!
original_content: Unbelievable visit here. Don't rush. Climb the mountain-800 steps- bring water. Give yourself time to descend- enjoy the boat ride! Majestic area of the world not to be missed.

author: Sunil D
title: Mua caves visit
original_content: Great boat ride and the going through the small caves , ducking your heads to avoid the stalactites and traversing though a series of caves was the highlight of this trip .. a long boat ride around 2 hours though the maze of waterways ...great
highlights: ducking your heads to avoid the stalactites
traversing though a series of caves

author: JO M
title: Nice view the rest bof
original_content: It's nice but from the beginning we are put in the bath 400m before arriving at the entrance while we drive 2 ladies stand in the way to prevent us from passing and want us to go on foot (paying to leave our bikes in their garage), a few meters later it starts again with new people, and this until reaching the entrance. There we understand that in any case we will have to pay to be able to put our bikes on the side. Then the entrance is paid and gives access to a small park that leads to the steps. Given the present world and the non-maintenance of spaces, we wonder what the entrance fee is for. The view is great from above but if you want to go to the dragon you have to wait your turn to climb.
practical_tips: Go early to avoid bike parking issues
Be prepared to pay for entrance and bike parking

author: Alessandro
title: Very tiring and beautiful view
original_content: Assuming that there are about 460 damn steps and that the final part is composed of very dangerous sharp and pointed rocks, the view is very beautiful. The effort to get there is very great

author: Sue V
title: Not for the faint hearted
original_content: This was hard! Go early to beat the tours otherwise that makes it even harder. The views were spectacular and I was glad I did it. The last bit involved scrambling over the rocks at the very top and that was just too much for me (and I do like heights)
drawbacks: scrambling over the rocks at the very top was too much
practical_tips: go early to beat the tours

author: Jonathan Phan
title: Wonderful moments at Mua Caves
original_content: Visited Hang Múa cave on Friday morning. Enjoyed walking and taking photos, even with the heat and humidity. I'd rate the experience a solid 9 out of 10. Would definitely return.

author: Bngrivett
title: Go early or late
original_content: Crowded during the middle of the day probably negativity impacted on our visit.   Nice grounds and cafes.  Lotus garden next door was a nice surprise.   Wear solid shoes.
highlights: Lotus garden next door was a nice surprise

author: Abbie F
title: Parking not free
original_content: The views were incredible but there is not free parking here anymore. We went for sunset and drove straight up to the ticket office to be met with parking people slapping my bike telling me this is where I had to park and to pay 10k. I had read the reviews which instructed to ignore these people however they were not backing down. I ended up going up to the ticket office itself to ask if it's free parking to which they said no. It all felt very hostile and uncomfortable.So please take this into consideration before ignoring the parking people by the ticket office. Also the "scammers" before the actual parking were offering parking for 5k so it may be worth doing that in the future.
extracted_spaces: parking people by the ticket office
practical_tips: ignore the parking people by the ticket office

author: Cruiser13V
title: Wonderful day spent outside!
original_content: The location far beyond my expectations. Although there are a lot of pauses and a steep climb, the vistas are well worth the effort, especially in the Vietnamese heat. The entire area is worth visiting for a half-day as there is enough to do and see.

author: The_lone_rider
title: Steep steps but worth the view!
original_content: The place is set in between picturesque limestone mountains with a breathtaking view from the top of the stairs . The climb is 500 stairs and takes a while to cover given the steps are steep, there are however benches at points on the steps to help ease the journey.The view on top is a  snapshot of Ninh binh with a Vietnamese flag flying high and mighty in the wind.
practical_tips: use benches at points on the steps to help ease the journey

author: Anja S
title: Beautiful views
original_content: Beautiful views, tough climb (+-500 steps) but definitely worth it. Safety could be improved by installing handrails.
drawbacks: Safety could be improved by installing handrails
practical_tips: Go prepared for a tough climb

author: Russ Lacuata
title: Panoramic View
original_content: The climb to the top of the twin peaks is exhausting, however, the reward is worth it. The scenic panoramic view of the landscape and rice fields is amazing. An unforgettable experience.

author: Devid P.
title: The dragon on the sky….
original_content: What a journey!! We arrived early morning and we climbed till the lying dragon… what a view, what a wonderful place. 500 uneven steps are a lot… but completely worth the climb. Thanks to the weather without sun, wasn’t too hard.

author: Sashila Mahendran
title: Mua Cave and Ninh Binh visit
original_content: Daughter enjoyed the expedition and scenic view from a top.Ninh Binh is truly magicalOur tour guide Jenny was very informative and took care of us
highlights: tour guide Jenny was very informative

author: René P
title: The trip to the top is worth all the effort.
original_content: The stairs up to the dragon can be a challenge for many, and probably not suitable for people with difficulty walking.But once you stand on top of the dragon there is a fantastic view.If you have height anxiety, you should probably consider whether you want to foot right up next to the dragon.
drawbacks: stairs up to the dragon can be a challenge for many
not suitable for people with difficulty walking
practical_tips: consider whether you want to foot right up next to the dragon

author: Coyote-Travelerz
title: Hike and Enjoy the views
original_content: The journey climbing the mountain is the experience. The steps are well worn and steep, so wear comfortable footwear with a good grip. The sight can be very busy (lots of tours at once) so the earlier you can get there the fewer people you will find. Along the way and atop the mountain there are wonderful views of the surrounding valleys (even on a cloudy day).

author: Martina S
title: Wowww experience
original_content: Wonderful place with amazing views. One of the most exciting views ever seen! The long effort to face the staircase is absolutely worth it!!

author: Ovy Q
title: Nice viewpoint
original_content: I visited a cave in the morning and the ticket price was around $4. The weather was good, with sunny skies making for an amazing view. However, as we climbed the mountain, the temperature rose, and we ended up getting hot and sweaty. I believe it would have been better to visit during a cooler season.
drawbacks: would have been better to visit during a cooler season

author: Antonia
title: Nice view
original_content: Nice view from the top, but the last few stairs are very uneven and difficult. There also is not a lot of shade to take a break in. The entrance fee is 100.000 VD. If you don't have the time to make it or are not fit enough, you won't miss out on anything spectacular.
drawbacks: not a lot of shade to take a break in
practical_tips: go early if you're not fit enough

author: Ros
title: Wonder of nature
original_content: The Mua Caves are a must for those visiting Vietnam.I fell in love with it.You have to climb 500 high and bumpy steps, but when you reach the top every effort is rewarded. The panorama below is magical and surreal and gives a great sense of peace.It is absolutely necessary to have comfortable shoes and water (and maybe even a kway!)Super recommended

author: Benjamin M
title: Parking Trouble !
original_content: Great view over the lotus paddies and river from all viewpoints. Some people tried to stop us on the way, telling us there was no parking, and we had to park there.  Don't fall for it.  There is a parking just at the ticket office.  Inside and outside they charge 10k extra now.
drawbacks: Some people tried to stop us on the way, telling us there was no parking
highlights: Great view over the lotus paddies and river from all viewpoints
practical_tips: Don't fall for it.  There is a parking just at the ticket office

author: Mgh070
title: Worth it
original_content: The cave itself is not necessarily special. The surroundings are beautiful and the park neatly landscaped. Attraction is the lookout point. Five hundred steps up. Spicy in the heat but then you also have a very nice view.Worth a lot more money than Bufalo Cave!

author: PGMikk
title: Not a "should do" in a "hot day@
original_content: I arrived at Mua Cave at around 10am, at that time the sky was very clear and blue, the weather was beyond description for a perfect trip. But everything gradually turned into a nightmare when I started climbing up. We should choose to go to this place on a day with lower temperatures. As I climbed halfway up the mountain, it seemed like each step I took became heavier due to the sunlight shining down from above and the melting temperature bouncing back up from the rock below my feet, making it almost impossible to breathe. I had to rest many times even though it wasn't a very high mountain. My clothes were soaked. And believe me, if I hadn't brought electrolyte water that day, I probably would have spent the whole night camping at the summit and would have descended the mountain the next morning.If you are elderly or have a history of heart disease, it is not recommended to try. Especially on hot days.
drawbacks: Sunlight and heat made it difficult to breathe
practical_tips: Choose a day with lower temperatures
Not recommended for elderly or those with heart disease

author: Belith67
title: Best views of Vietnam
original_content: The experience in Ninh Binh has been amazing, from the climb to see the wonderful views of the river where we were then canoeed and the scenery we saw cycling throughout this area is very worth it, delighted with the experience! Highly recommended!

author: Francesca A
title: What a view
original_content: The stairs, the view, the place. This will be forever in our hearts As soon as you arrive it seems a bit of a fake/selfie place but when you start walking up the stairs and you reach the top that you understand you couldn't miss this place out

author: Sue
title: Views and steps 😀

I suggest right for medium fitness level as this is doable . Keep plenty of time on hand and do not rush . The view at top is all worth it . Went as a part of a guided tour to non bhin tam coc and mua  caves , I took a tour with “ local mint travel “ group  ( WhatsApp +84 94 925 96 75 ) who then connect with local guides and they were simply amazing . So if you up for some challenge with stunning views - go for it
highlights: good footwear and a bottle of water

keep plenty of time on hand

author: EleonoraO75
title: Mua Caves
original_content: Definitely not to be missed! Of course it is very hot and the climb is tiring but the view from the top is absolutely worth it! Better to go early in the morning or late afternoon

author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence

buy ticket to enter the premises

author: Jasmin
title: Be careful when coming down the steps!
original_content: It is indeed a beautiful place. The lotus garden was mesmerising. I’d suggest going quite early in the morning or later in the afternoon, when the sun is not yet blazing because it can really affect your experience. Going up to peak, you’d have to brace through steep steps. I’d suggest for those of you who are not too experienced with hiking/trekking, you might want to use a stick to help you keep your balance!

author: Lana Cooking Class (Tam Cốc - Ninh Bình)

original_content: It is amazing view point.the most famous tourist site in ninh binh you have to go.In june vs july,lotus lake is blooming flowers

author: Onas
title: Many steps

author: Darian P

The lady at the ticket booth said parking was not included. I was able to park my bike just outside the gate for 5000. There will be people that try to stop you way before the entrance. author: Jacky Chen

author: zardoz07

author: Nicola F
title: Lovely view but so crowded . Not what I had envisaged.
original_content: This had been one of the main places I had wanted to visit since researching a holiday to Vietnam and watching various you tube/ drone videos which looked incredible. Our visit coincided with the Vietnam independence holiday at the start of September so it was always going to be crowded. We also struggled to do a 6am climb and it was so hot that the next option was a 6pm sunset trip. So, we knew we wouldn’t be alone, but we still weren’t prepared for the masses of tourists pouring in - at least hundreds, if not thousands, all trying to get that perfect selfie! We still had some incredible views, but in a strange way I preferred my you tube vision of the place. I’d still recommend visiting, but manage your expectations , especially if visiting at a peak time. A couple of practical considerations; We cycled from Tam Coc- fairly easy and scenic bike ride/ about 20 minutes and flat  ( but I am 50+ and unfit so still struggled a bit in the heat). We encountered the bogus “ you have to park here officials “ including a man in a fake uniform jumping out and blowing a whistle. To be honest , we found him fairly good natured and we’ve just muttered we were staying at the ecolodge ( not true- but this is the hotel which has parking for bikes right next to the entrance) and he laughed and backed off. I know froma few reviews that some people have had really bad encounters with people trying to get them to park, but this seems to be relatively rare. I really wouldn’t have minded paying him twice as much to park in his patch, but I was so knackered that parking as close to the entrance as possible was a priority for me. Given my poor level of fitness I had worried if I’d make the 500 + steps. It was actually slightly easier than I had feared, partly because the sun was going down, but also because I took it slow and steady, had loads of water with me, and I seemed motivated by the  ever increasing views with every step. I ended up going up both mountains ( so more than 600 steps) but this was by accident, and if you can only manage one, when you get to the main fork, head left. I went right first, and it was far too crowded to enjoy . The left fork gives you the classic views and although I pretty much got to the top, there was an additional queue to get on the dragon itself which seemed dangerous and unnecessary to me, although I can see the attraction if it had been quieter.If you go at a busy time, also be prepared for the Vietnamese couples going up for a photoshoot. It seems to be a common thing that the women will dress up to look gorgeous whilst their partners take photographs of them for prolonged periods at every best viewpoint. There’s even a shop at the bottom which hires out beautiful costumes whilst offering free hair and makeup! I was dripping with sweat, and as far from glamorous as you can imagine, but it was hard to find a gap in their photo shoots at times to get my sweaty selfies. Interesting cultural element to see though. I was worried we’d gone too late and would be descending in the dark/ this was parly true, but necessary to avoid the extreme heat and the worst of the crowds, and the path was partly lit when going down and seemed ok. It did mean cycling back in the dark though. Overall, if I hadn’t seen the amazing clips before I’d probably have loved it, but my trip was slightly less magical and overall I found I enjoyed the lower key attractions in Vietnam much more rewarding. Id say it’s definitely worth visiting if you’re in the Nihn Bihn area, but slightly surprisingly I didn’t find it one of the highlights of our trip, so don’t fret it you can’t fit it in, and watch the amazing drone shots instead!

author: Isabell8785
title: Sweaty but worth it
original_content: You will definitley break out in even more sweat climbing those steep stairs to reach the top of the laying dragon mountain - but the views are worth it!

author: Jessica P
title: Mia caves
original_content: A good route up to the top, over 400 steps so be prepared to either take it slow or wear appropriate footwear. The views are amazing and if you are lucky enough to see the lotus in bloom, I imagine it is even better. You can walk through the flowers at the bottom over the wooden bridges. author: Laura

author: cramac
title: Panorama

author: Johan S

author: OneTrip with local

author: André K

author: B K
