original_content: Fantastic views, 1,000 steps but worth the climb. We went at sunset and it was so beautiful, breathtaking. In the summer, even going at sunset it was a hot, sweaty, strenuous climb up those steps so I don’t recommend doing this in the heat of the day. But definitely go, you won’t regret it.

author: swexplorers2018
title: Worth the climb
original_content: An outstanding experience even for 59+ age group. Be prepared to take it slowly, drink lots of water, have a hat, and enjoy the view as it's worth the climb to the top. Out guide encouraged us to rest along the way. View beautiful. A little trickier coming down but again, take your time.

author: ArvindSharma2014
title: Nice climb to.dragon mountain
original_content: This ia nice activity if you like walking and hiking. Views from dragon mountain are awesome, however, you need to climb 1000+ steps, please wear walking shoes and hydrate yourself.  It is very humid. Also,  lot of youngsters  comes for photoshot and  they take hours to get clicked in various poses. You have to ask to get one or two selfie. Dont wait ..
drawbacks: you have to ask to get one or two selfie
highlights: Views from dragon mountain are awesome

author: gregsf11
title: Not much more to say than has already been said
original_content: Not so bad as they say. 500 steps is doable. Views from the top are sublime. Just remember:Go really early to avoid the heat. The dragon is not exactly stable in parts, and the whole area around it is dodgy. Don't get into one of those "famous last selfie" compilations. And whatever they may scream at you, don't park your bike until you get inside the ticket gate. Why walk more than you have to?
drawbacks: dragon is not exactly stable in parts
whole area around it is dodgy
park your bike until you get inside the ticket gate
highlights: views from the top are sublime
practical_tips: go really early to avoid the heat
don't get into one of those famous last selfie compilations
don't park your bike until you get inside the ticket gate

author: TIT Adventure
title: Trang An boat trip and Mua viewpoint
original_content: a wonderful day trip from Hanoi to Hang Mua viewpoint & Trang An landscape with lovely team from Emirate organised by TÍT Adventure

author: Hetzel
title: Climbing up is the highlight
original_content: It was a great thing to do, is less challenging than I expected,,, the view from the top is actually so nice, I found it a bit confusing that the place is marketed as Mua Caves, however , in my personal experience, the caves aren't impressive, but the climb to the top of the mountain with the steps is a nice experience.I didn't do a tour, just went by cab with my friends. Use meter, don't accept price offer.Taxi driver will offer to wait for you to take you wherever else you are going. You can accept that, but again, with meter (meaning he will stop the meter when you arrive there, and restart it when you come back, is his choice to wait for you.I highly recommend to be there at 7 am as it just opens, temperature is nice and less exhausting, very little people...( only thing is that the little shops or stands are closed to buy drinks or so, but you are not missing out) much better barely any people...nice to go at your own pace and take pictures easily.If you have bad knees, or are very overweight, this is maybe not a good option to do.
highlights: view from the top is nice
climb to the top of the mountain with the steps is a nice experience
nice to go at your own pace and take pictures easily
practical_tips: Use meter, don't accept price offer
Be prepared for stairs and steps

author: Shelley M
title: What a view
original_content: We had a guide drop us here, so did not have to battle with the parking touts, which made our life easier.  Take your time hear and wear comfy shoes as the stairs are very steep and slippery in places.  Some steps are very high for little legs.  Its not a race to the top, stop and look around and enjoy the views, they are stunning.  May not be worth doing on a really overcast day as you wont see a great deal.  My family enjoyed this and you come to a fork in the path - left to the dragon and view of rowers in Tam Coc and we decided to do both.  There is a place to get a cold drink half way up which is really nice, they have a seat with a fan set up for the hot sticky days.  There is also places to get cold drinks and ice-cream at the bottom.  Be very careful with young children as not a lot of safety rails, but common sense applies.  Well worth the trip to the top, the views are stunning.
drawbacks: not a lot of safety rails
highlights: nice place to get a cold drink
practical_tips: stop and look around and enjoy the views
be very careful with young children

author: TheGrebes
title: Lovely climb and views ... Very persistent parking touts
original_content: Great experience. Stunning views, but a very steep climb. Relatively quiet when we were there but could be a bit dangerous if crowded as steps very steep and narrow in p!aces. A few people blocking parts of the climb getting their breath back quite awkward to safely manouver around.The parking scam is very evident and even knowing about it we still got caught out by an official looking guy in a u inform of some kind right at the entrance gate. The official parking (cycles and scooters) is inside the gate behind the ticket office. Just say NO loudly to all the touts that try to stop you on the road approaching the gate.
practical_tips: park in official parking (cycles and scooters) inside the gate behind the ticket office
say NO loudly to all the touts that try to stop you on the road approaching the gate

author: ctm7944
title: Hang Mua - Wow The Views!
original_content: Rode FREE bicycle from accommodations (Tam Coc Wonderland Bungalows). Arrived Hang Mua about 10AM (Open 6AM-7PM).Couldn't have picked a better day to have some morning sunshine. Yes, it is 500 steps. Some of the many stone steps are quite high. But, I enjoyed the challenge/exercise. Eventually you come to a fork in the road. The path to the Left goes up to the highest point (dragon). On this path is where you see the Tam Coc boats passing on the water below. This being the higher path, you can also get great photos of the Pagoda + the countryside.The Right side path leads to the Pagoda with nice views as well.Yes, the RICE fields are GREEN in April.And of course there were lots of tourists there; doing tourist things - just like me.Hang Mua entry is 100KVND. Bicycle parking 10VND.Previous TA reviews were helpful. Advised to ignore people waving me to parking. Some stand in the road and a few had on uniforms to appear as some type of official.Parked at the lot at the end of the road (on the right side), which is immediately before the ticket office.Took photos along the way to & from; people working the fields, buffalo and limestone formations etc. Very scenic!
drawbacks: Some of the many stone steps are quite high
highlights: Great photos of the Pagoda + the countryside
Scenic views of people working the fields, buffalo and limestone formations
practical_tips: Park at the lot at the end of the road
Ignore people waving you to parking

author: mabellan
title: Beautiful views
original_content: Great views. I couldn’t see a good sunset as there was a bit misty but it was totally worth it. The mountain opposite was less crowded and had a few less steps but we decided to do Mua anyway. Best in mind that you need to get a ticket and it’s cash only

author: Jaroslav Nečas
title: Spectacular views
original_content: To see fantastic views you need to walk up several hundreds steep stairs but it's definitely worth it. There are 2 peaks, higher is more crowded lesser not so much. You probably would need to wait some time to get position for good photo.

author: Thuy
title: Hang Mua should be in favorite list if you travel to Ninh Binh
original_content: This is nice place to see almost of Tam Coc from the top. Also is natural place for travelers can take photos to save memories
highlights: natural place for travelers to take photos

author: Kelly B
title: Beautiful viewpoint, but be aware of aggression and scams
original_content: The viewpoint is stunning and well worth the short climb (15 mins if you are reasonably fit) but as other reviewers have said, it's important to know what to expect regarding the parking scams on the entrance road.I had several people jump in front of my bike trying to force me to stop before the entrance gate, a woman grabbed my arm as I cycled past her and tried to pull me off my bike, and eventually ended up with 5 men surrounding my bike, screaming at me and kicking my bike very aggressively while I was still sitting on it. As a woman on my own it was intimidating and I ended up parking in their area just to diffuse the situation as I was worried they were about to hit me. Even though I was expecting some of this behaviour (from reading other reviews), I was scared and quite shaken by how furious the men were and how unsafe they made me feel.  Don't let this put you off visiting the beautiful viewpoint - but be prepared for some aggression and go with a friend for extra safety if you can.
practical_tips: go with a friend for extra safety

author: must_travel_soon_10
title: Majestic views are worth climbing the steps
original_content: There are approx. 500 steps and they lead to beautiful vistas of the surrounding areas with limestone peaks. We went mid afternoon and didn't encounter excessive crowds. The base area is also very scenic and beautiful. One of three must sees in Ninh Binh

author: Allison G
title: Beautiful viewpoint worth the stairs
original_content: Great view point worth the stairs. Very hot so bring water. There’s a scam with a man and woman with a whistle who will try to get you to park your scooter or bike and pay for parking (do not do this). Go straight to the ticket counter!
drawbacks: scam with a man and woman with a whistle who will try to get you to park your scooter or bike and pay for parking
highlights: Great view point worth the stairs
practical_tips: go straight to the ticket counter

author: Madiyya
title: A place to escape the hustle and bustle of Hanoi
original_content: This hidden gem offers stunning views of the limestone mountains and rice fields, as well as a chance to explore the mysterious caves that lie beneath. You'll need to climb 500 steps to reach the top of the mountain, but trust me, it's worth it. The view from the peak is breathtaking, especially at sunset. You'll feel like you're in a fairy tale.

author: Marta R
title: Worth every step!
original_content: We rode a scooter out in the morning. Had read earlier reviews about the parking scam but didn’t find it to be an issue this morning. There was a woman trying to wave us down, but we were able to ride past her easily.There are shops selling dresses on the street as you lead in. Wish I had taken a bit more notice as it’s traditional dress that you can wear up the steps and take some beautiful photos in. It’s only about 600,00 Duong for the dresses so if you want something extra special for your photo have a look at them. Definitely Instagram worthy. Yes there are about 1000 steps and everyone of them is worth it. Due to the beautiful nature you stop every 20-40 steps to take photos and take it all in so you don’t feel completely out of breath (a little sweaty depending on the temperature).The view at the top is magnificent and worth the effort. The dragon is not all that accessible but the view is still spectacular.

author: majorstu
title: Beautiful views - definitely a must do when in the area
original_content: Our family of 5 ( 2 adults, 3 kids - 14. 11, 8) biked from Tam Coc - a pretty steady flat ride.  Be prepared for the parking fee - a slightly irritating common feature in the area at most attractions, followed by your entrance fee.  I’ve read the parking hassle other reviewers had - we just bypassed the early offerings and parked right outside the entrance gate and paid up.  The caves were OK (nothing compared to those experienced on the Trang An boat tour), but the viewpoint makes it, with beautiful views across the lush rice paddies, waterways and towering limestone cliffs.  As in many places rubbish is a sad accompaniment as is poor maintenance, but  the view really showcases the beauty of the area.  If you’ve got reasonable fitness climbing the 500 steps takes about 15-20 minutes.
practical_tips: bypass the early offerings and park right outside the entrance gate

author: Leannie
title: Worth the steps
original_content: Came here as a family of four, and as we arrived by car we did not get any of the hassle described by previous reviewers arriving by car. Once you have paid and entered there are some nice viewing seats/swings with good views, as well as bathrooms which are fine if you bring your own toilet roll.  We started the climb to the viewing point about 4.30m, it was not too busy, we liked the fact that the stairs were very wide allowing two way traffic without it being too busy. I appreciated the many stop points on the way up for breath and taking photos. Didn't make it right to the top, but seeing as I was q hot mess by that point and have no intracranial account to add photos too that was just fine
drawbacks: hassle described by previous reviewers arriving by car
highlights: nice viewing seats/swings with good views
wide stairs allowing two way traffic
many stop points on the way up for breath and taking photos

author: Christelle Z
title: Agressive and violent people for parking in front
original_content: Very nice view but scam at the entrance on the price of parking.  2 people in fake police ask 10k VND to park motorbike/bicycle.  I refused to pay as I knew there was official parking inside.  One of the two people attacked me, he became violent and kicked my bike 3 times.  I also specify that they looked clearly in a state of intoxication, they were drinking in front of the entrance.  One of the two then wanted to hit me but the park staff intervened.  He then insulted me in Vietnamese and I ended up parking my bike in the official parking lot for 5k VND. On the other hand, no one came to help me afterwards to call the police, the park staff did not want to get involved because they were afraid of reprisals;  and when I finally found the number of the police they told me that they could not come and that I had to go to the station. Really a shame because the point of view is exceptional, but to fear for her safety in Vietnam (especially as a woman) - I pass my turn. Knowing economy relies on tourism, I don’t understand how the police doesn’t take care of this issue, it really stains my memory of Vietnam
drawbacks: Scam at the entrance on the price of parking
Attacked by fake police who were intoxicated
Park staff did not want to get involved
practical_tips: Park in the official parking lot to avoid scams

author: Yann Renaud
title: Breathtaking sceneries
original_content: Definitely a place to visit when in the area. From Tam Coc, the place is easily accessible.on bike or motorbike. When arriving, many people try to stop you in order for you to park at their place. The further you can go with your bike/motorbike, is just before the gate before the ticket office. The parking.spot.costs between 10-15kD.The entrance costs 100kD/person, and it is absolutely worth it! You will have to climb around 500 uneven stairs, made of a slippery rock. At a given point you can turn left and reach the top, with the Dragon and a wonderful view over Tam Coc, or right and have another impressive view.
drawbacks: many people try to stop you in order for you to park at their place
climb around 500 uneven stairs, made of a slippery rock
practical_tips: park your bike/motorbike just before the gate before the ticket office
turn left and reach the top for a better view

author: Davina M
title: READ THE ONE STAR REVIEWS- DANGEROUS! AVOID!
original_content: When driving up towards the entrance, locals literally stand in front of out motorbikes and forcefully tried to stop us to pay for parking. We kept swerving around them, as we knew that it was free parking through the gate. At the entrance to buy the tickets, there were two men, very aggressive, who stopped us and were screaming at us that we couldn't go through the gate to park and we had to pay them. Having been in South East Asia for a while we know not to get angry and were calmly saying to them we are going through the gate, it's free parking. They physically would not let us and the older man became so aggressive he got right in front of my face and appeared like he was ready to punch me in the face. My boyfriend got off his bike and walked through the gate to talk to the kiosk for tickets and for them to let us through. While this was happening, the same guy who I thought was going to hit me, grabbed a large metal chain and was swinging it at my boyfriends motorbike and looked like he intended to hit it and lock it up. I started yelling at him to back off, which he did before starting to get back in my face yelling. The ticket people didn't care and were super apathetic. We decided to leave, I didn't want to support people  who were so violent. Before you go here - read the one star reviews from 2019. There is a photo of the same bloke and other foreigners who did get hit, threatened with the chain and knives.
drawbacks: Aggressive locals trying to stop visitors to pay for parking
practical_tips: Read one-star reviews from 2019 to be aware of the situation
Be cautious of locals trying to stop you for parking

author: Elisabeth N
title: Taxing climb for the unfit, but the top is worth the sweat
original_content: Over 400 steps, some .5m high!!! This is not an easy climb. The stairs are all different levels, but plenty of place to rest along the way, and the view at the top is so worth the effort.
drawbacks: This is not an easy climb
highlights: The view at the top is so worth the effort
practical_tips: Plenty of place to rest along the way

author: Alex H
title: A great viewpoint of Tam Coc river
original_content: Parking with your scooter costed us 15,000. Make sure you just drive right up to the entrance and don’t use the shop vendors earlier on, no matter how much they wave at you and walk in front of your scooter.There are two viewpoints to see, one with the pagoda and one with the dragon overlooking the river. Can be done with moderate fitness and well worth the hike to the top.
drawbacks: shop vendors wave at you and walk in front of your scooter
highlights: well worth the hike to the top
practical_tips: drive right up to the entrance
don't use the shop vendors earlier on

author: Bill B
title: Do if in the area
original_content: Mua caves has a very nice entrance area leading up to the stairs.  Do ignore the people trying to flag you down as you get close to the attraction.  We simply said "No" and veered around them and they didn't bother us.  We were charged 10k each to park our bikes just outside the entrance to the attraction.  The stairs are steep and uneven so should be attempted by relatively fit people.  Gorgeous view from the top.  I recommend this attraction if you're in the area.
drawbacks: charged 10k each to park our bikes
practical_tips: ignore the people trying to flag you down

author: Polly
title: The lying dragon mountain
original_content: We cycled to the Mua Caves from our local accommodation, it is 5 vnd parking per bike. The entry fee is 100 vnd and soo worth it. When you enter the complex it is beautiful with little decorative ponds, views and swings and restaurants. It is a short walk to the start of the lying dragon mountain steps (view point). There are 500 steps, although wide, it is quite a steep ascend to the top and quite uneven. It is perfectly do able with good footwear and water and shouldn’t take too long if you have a good fitness level. The views are next level beautiful, really breathtaking. You have a view across the mountains but also down to the river where you can see the boats pass! A very rewarding climb! We would recommend getting there early to best the sun and the crowds for a more leisurely time.

author: DGSmanila
title: great view + sunset
original_content: for older guys - 500 stairs are not so easy as you might think :-)the climb is nice and the view from top is rewarding.We finished the day there so the sunset view is beautiful.
drawbacks: 500 stairs are not so easy as you might think
highlights: the view from top is rewarding

author: fal3
title: Great views at the top
original_content: We went in December so we couldn’t enjoy the green rice field’s however the view was still nice but rather brown. The steps are a bit slippery are poorly maintained. Weird given you pay a decent amount to get in. Overall I would consider this a must do in the Ninh Binh area along with the Trang An boat tour. It’s the only place here that gives a high vantage point.
drawbacks: pay a decent amount to get in
practical_tips: consider this a must do in the Ninh Binh area
along with the Trang An boat tour

author: Rickiray
title: Amazing views and worth it
original_content: The hike up isnt to tough, i would say moderate fitness you will be fine. We went for sunrise on a sunny day and were not disappointed, spectacular. WARNING about the parking area if you come by scooter or bicycle. Vendors will try to get you to park in their spots. There is parking inside the gate but it is limited   So the vendors outside do provide a needed service. Unfortunately they are way over aggresive and some not all that honest. They charge 15000 dong for a scooter “it is 10000 inside the gate”. A couple gave buddy 150000 dong by mistake and soon realized it he and pretended not to know what they were taking about. A big argument but it was pointless he didnt give back any change. We were parked in his stall and the scooter was still there when we got back so thats a plus. A shame as you could tell his parking spot is taken care of, it is the one on the right just as you reach the gate. They will jump right out in front of you and yell to get you into their stall. Be aware and try not to be intimidated.

author: Chris
title: Go for the top!
original_content: Every step on those 500 stairs we’ll get you closer to magnificent views! A very good exercise I’d do every day. Go early to avoid the tours coming from Hanoi. Also do the little Peak too, so you’ll have a better view of the tallest one.

author: MatthewTheCoder
title: Mua caves - day trip
original_content: We visited this site as part of the Ninh Binh day tours which cover Hoa Lu, Trang An and Mua caves.Mua caves has to be highlight of the 3 sites as part of the Ninh Binh day tour package. There are about 500 steps to the top. There are 2 climbs, one climb will lead you to a small feature token pagoda (not one where it can house people). The other climb is to the Dragon. The Dragon climb has a statue of Goddess of Mercy in front of the dragon's head.Some of the stairs are quiet steep. The overall climb can be a bit strenuous physically and that we were instructed by the tour guide to be back in the bus after 40 mins did not help.There were many tourists in this site. It is impossible when we were there to take a photo without someone being it it. There was also a queue on the way up the top of the Dragon peak.If you are short of time, the Dragon climb is better one, it is higher and has more challenging steps.The 40min given to us by the tour guide was simply not enough. I would spend perhaps 2 hours for this site alone, to adequately cover both peaks, catch your breath and enjoy the scenery. Pros: High recommended for the physical activity and the view at the top of the climb.  One of the many reasons to visit Ninh Binh.Cons: Too many tourists. There is literally a human traffic jam on the way up the 2 peaks.
drawbacks: Human traffic jam on the way up the 2 peaks
Not enough time to adequately cover both peaks
highlights: High recommended for the physical activity and the view at the top of the climb
practical_tips: Spend at least 2 hours to adequately cover both peaks

author: Long H
title: Amazing view from Mua Cave
original_content: Mua Cave is so amazing, we had a great time to enjoy the panoramic view of Ninh BInh. 500 steps to reach the peak of mountain, definitely worth visiting. In the next visit, we will travel in the lotus season, cant' wait

author: Lorna M
title: A TIP I WAS GLAD TO KNOW!
original_content: Great view definitely worth the trip altough the locals as you the road that leads down to it run out pretending/demanding you park your bikes and pay. They blow whistles to look official and almost stand in your way not letting you by but make sure you just say no and keep driving past them until you get right upto the entrance. No matter how much they insist keep going. And then do not pay more than 5/10 thousand to park your bike (motorbike) bicycles should be less, either inside the gates at the official place which is 10 or you can haggle the guys at the entrance to 5/10. I seen some people paying 300/500! Or if you don't want to pay at all park before you turn onto the road somewhere and walk 5/10 minutes down the road and in.

author: Jocelyn C
title: Worth the climb
original_content: Our group of seven aged 13-60+ visited Hang Mua. We all climbed to the peak. The views were worth the 400+ steps with great photo opportunities. The grounds and surrounds are lovely. It was quiet the morning we visited.

author: alison
title: Loved it . If you want an authentic nature outing this is it .
original_content: We visited Van Long Nature Reserve early in the morning after our driver suggested it would be cooler and give us the best chance of spotting wildlife. We knew that seeing the endangered Delacour’s langur wasn’t guaranteed, and honestly, after gliding through the wetlands on the peaceful bamboo boat, we had already decided the trip was worthwhile regardless.The scenery was beautiful and incredibly calm, with towering limestone . Then our boat rower quietly pointed towards the rocks, and we were lucky enough to spot not just one langur, but a whole group of nine. It was a special moment and the icing on the cake of an already memorable visit.Van Long is a little further out than some of the more popular attractions around Ninh Binh, but that is part of its charm. It felt uncrowded, natural and unspoilt. If you’re looking for a quieter experience and appreciate nature, we would highly recommend making the effort to visit.
highlights: spotting a whole group of nine endangered Delacour’s langur

author: Meeling W
title: Peaceful Escape
original_content: Van Long Nature Reserve was one of the most peaceful and beautiful experiences of our trip. We went early in the morning, and the setting was absolutely stunning—calm water, dramatic limestone karsts, and a quiet stillness that made everything feel untouched.Our rower gently guided us through the reserve, taking her time and happily stopping whenever we wanted to take photos. She was warm and friendly, which made the experience even more enjoyable. Along the way, we were lucky enough to spot Delacour’s langurs, along with a variety of birds, fish, and other wildlife—such a special moment in such a serene environment.What really stood out was how quiet and uncrowded it was. We had done Tràng An a few days earlier, which was beautiful in its own way, but Van Long felt far more peaceful and authentic, with very few other boats around.We were staying nearby at a homestay and simply biked over, which made the whole experience feel even more relaxed and immersive. On the way back, we stopped at a close by open-air restaurant for a cold beer - a perfect way to end the morning.If you’re looking for a tranquil, less touristy alternative with incredible scenery and wildlife, Van Long Nature Reserve is absolutely worth visiting.
highlights: stunning setting with calm water, dramatic limestone karsts, and quiet stillness
spot Delacour’s langurs, along with a variety of birds, fish, and other wildlife
practical_tips: dress codes not mentioned, but recommend wearing comfortable shoes for biking
consider stopping at a close by open-air restaurant for a cold beer on the way back

author: Cory V
title: Beautiful place to visit
original_content: Got to see the monkeys which is rare so we feel very privileged. Was a great experience.

author: Jackie O
title: Natural beauty
original_content: Pleasant, picturesque boat ride. No pressure from our guide who rowed the whole way, stopping for photos. A wonderful experience. Check in advance that you can get a return Grab. Luckily our driver waited for us. Tip the boat guide & your driver (100,000 each seems fair)
practical_tips: Check in advance that you can get a return Grab
Tip the boat guide & your driver (100,000 each seems fair)

author: karin_caethoven
title: Beautiful nature!
original_content: Beautiful nature, much more authentic than Trang An, if you love natural beauty. Much smaller scale. Boat tour takes about 1.5 hours. White-rumped langurs: check!
highlights: Much more authentic than Trang An

author: ThomasPUK
title: Nice views with sunset.
original_content: No crowds. Ticket 100,000 per person. Only saw a few birds and no other while life but vet beautiful scenery. Our rower & the staff at the dock/pier, demand extra money/tips at the end of the trip and become agitated  if they don’t get what they want.
drawbacks: become agitated if they don’t get what they want

author: Josh G
title: Not the best reserve for wildlife watching
original_content: Went to the reserve in the hope for seeing some birds and/or monkeys.The entrance to the reserve is just an archway where the boat rides go from and it is not well signposted.The boat rides are ok going through the wetland, didn’t see many birds or no monkeys though.Lasts about an hour and after that there isn’t anything to do (you can walk along the perimeter which is on a busy road)Overall ok but underwhelming if you want to spend a while watching animals.
drawbacks: didn't see many birds or no monkeys

author: Jesper M
title: Wonderful experience, less tourists
original_content: We went there day after sailing at Thrang An. This experience was far better for us. - We were nearly alone, far less tourists, hence the water was absolutely calm- we had the boat for ourselves- it was cheaper- we also saw the monkeys*only note is that the ticket office is not really obvious to find*
drawbacks: ticket office is not really obvious to find

author: Hugo L
title: The rower asks to row with him and no birds or monkeys seen.
original_content: The view is pretty, but no more than Trang An or Tam Coc. It's certainly cheaper, but it's also further from Ninh Binh and Tam Coc, what you save in entrance fees you'll pay for gasoline and scooter rental. Not all rowers speak English, ours did not speak English, so no explanation. We've only seen storks. No other birds and no monkeys. The rower asks us to help him row...
drawbacks: Further from Ninh Binh and Tam Coc
practical_tips: Go early to avoid traffic and save on gasoline and scooter rental

author: Duncan W
title: Quite and peaceful
original_content: We did the boat trip through the wetland with the primary purpose of seeing birds.  Despite the misty day, we did see quite a few (including many Storks/Openbill up on the cliffs).  We visited the cave.  Very scenic.  We started out alone but there were soon other boats on the water but these weren't a problem.  The only negative was that they seemed over keen for a big tip at the conclusion.
drawbacks: over keen for a big tip

author: Lucy F
title: Beautiful and quiet
original_content: Beautiful quiet way to explore Ninh Binh. Stunning scenery. Very few boats in the water. Totally unspoilt.  Boats are east to hire

author: Fradj Did
title: Why choose Vietnam
original_content: We stayed 10 unforgettable days in Vietnam with the agency Authentik , we will not forget an exceptional and professional tour operator Mr Nguyen Thang Victor who prepared us a nature tour in the heart of large landscapes and without forgetting his team especially the Guide Nguyễn Minh Tuấn and his driver who accompanied us throughout the trip with care and kindness.

author: Andria F
title: So peaceful
original_content: Absolutely beautiful and so quiet after Trang  An. Only a few boats on the river so you could hear all the wildlife. Little cave at the end where you turn round and come back.  Lasts about an hour. Well worth doing if in the area.

author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
title: A scenic boat ride
original_content: Very leisure boat ride along the river. It was a pretty long journey as it took us around 1.5hrs to and fro sailing through the river. The boat lady was rowing the boat using her feet which was an amazing feat. Along the river, we passed by many scenic sites and paid fields. Do wear a hat if possible as it can get really hot in the summer. Thankfully the boat lady offered us an umbrella which was really useful. During the boat ride, we passed through some limestone caves as well. A must do in ninh binh.
drawbacks: it can get really hot in the summer
practical_tips: boat lady offered us an umbrella

author: Matthew L
title: Sit back and Chill
original_content: Expectations are funny things. If you were expecting to see monkeys or defined bird watching success by how many birds there were then you could easily be disappointed. We really enjoyed this boat trip. We heard the monkeys and might have seen the  tail of a departing one. The bird life was scarce but beautiful and what is not too like about being paddled around a wetland. The trip was a peaceful contrast to the Tràng An experience- we were almost the only boat  there. Coming across some locals diving for clams was a highlight. Tràng an was spectacular- this was quite beautiful in an understated way. I would go again.

author: Ellie M
title: Beat the crowds!
original_content: Van Long Wetland was an amazing boat trip, 1 hr for $100,000 each.Only 3-4 other boats on the water. Many times we were the only boat we could see. Felt like having a private tour of the beautiful rock formations and water.We did a similar boat tour at Trang An, where there were hundreds of boats and unfortunately it was not peaceful at all.I would recommend Van Long, for a more private & less touristy option!Apparently there are free walks you can do instead of the boat ride, but we couldn't find where to access those
practical_tips: go to Van Long Wetland for a more private & less touristy option
look for free walks instead of the boat ride

author: ボボ
title: Touring the Wetlands
original_content: You can tour the wetlands on a bamboo boat. You can see many wild birds and strange rock formations. If you're lucky, you may see a mother and her baby monkeys.

author: jay w
title: Van Long nature reserve.
original_content: Van Long nature reserve is a less crowded option to explore near Ninh Binh very peaceful boat trip. An alternative to Tam Coc.
practical_tips: go to Van Long nature reserve as an alternative to Tam Coc

author: Chris H
title: Natural reserve
original_content: If you are interested in the natural world then this is a lovely experience. More rustic than the more commercial boat trips but the wildlife is better. Binoculars would be useful.
drawbacks: the more commercial boat trips is more polished

author: DaveO
title: Just Ok
original_content: Van Long wetlands boat trip didn't meet my expectations. One hour gentle row among the cliffs. You don't get far from the road - we were in sight of the road for half the time. Saw distant monkeys. The main impression of cranes were the industrial kind (pic). To avoid the crowds, i went late,  got started on rowboat at 16:10, one of the last boats out. We were always in sight of other boats, sometimes a mini armada. There was no feeling of remote jungle.  I thought the Tam Coc and Trang An boat trips were better - more crowded but better scenery. Boats cost minimum 200k, or 100k per person, whichever is greater. Plenty of boats carried 3 touristos.As a friendless solo it was thus, quite expensive for me. The location on google and maps.me is problematic. If going by scooter, aim for Gia Van: the dock is at the top (north) end of that village. Loads of restaurants, shops etc. Driving via Trang An is by far the most pleasant route. I wish I'd gone earlier in the day and driven more of the little roads heading in to the karst from around GV - they were more promising, as yoozh, than the tourist destination. I never seem to learn.
drawbacks: in sight of the road for half the time
practical_tips: drive via Trang An for a pleasant route
aim for Gia Van for dock location

author: BellaDonna
title: Relax day
original_content: Lovely relaxed boat trip, but saw no monkeys and very few birds. Nice area for cycling and the food in the restaurant is excellent

author: Guide53752047682
title: Amazing time
original_content: We went here instead of Tam coc and Trang An as wildlife is more for us and we were not disappointed. Took a private car from Tam Coc.Our lady boat rower was lovely and when she knew we loved wildlife and were not there for Instagram selfies she slowed down and stopped at all the little animals and birds that we could see this included Langurs, we had them right next to the boat for about half an hour, we could not believe how lucky we were. She never rushed us to move on. She even got excited at seeing them so close.
highlights: got to see Langurs right next to the boat
practical_tips: ask the boat rower to slow down for wildlife

author: seeking.4.endorphine
title: Fantastic bird watching and wildlife tour with Luc Nguyen
original_content: The Van Long Nature Reserve is part of the dry Halong Bay, but fortunately has not yet been discovered by mass tourism. We were here in the low season (beginning of November) and it was very quiet. We really enjoyed the boat trip. The landscape, the peace, the isolation, the wildlife make the trip a unique experience.We booked our tour through ecoguidevietnam. With the help of our tour guide, Luc, we were able to see the rare Delacour langurs of Vân Long Nature Reserve. Fortunately, Luc is also a professional birdwatcher/ornithologist, so we were able to do extensive bird watching (White-browed Crake, Cinnamon and Yellow Bittern, Black Bittern, Pheasant-tailed Jacana, Bonellii’s Eagle, Egrets, Herons, etc.).We tipped the rower after the trip, which she was very happy about.We also went to Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park with Luc. It was also a very nice tour.Thank you Luc, we will recommend you!

author: Bodil M
title: Great experience
original_content: Peaceful paddle- boat tour through this rare and wonderful nature. Was lucky to see a monkey sitting anong the trees and also a little snake. But more than that was the peacefulnes gliding through the nature this way the best.  We only met a few other tourists here.

author: kenny.
title: Peaceful boat ride away from tourists
original_content: Brought here by Ninh bình private day trip from Ha Noi as alternative boat ride in Trang an. Very calm, peaceful wetland surrounded by huge mountain range. On the ride we saw varieties of birds. We only met 2 other boats on the way back. Our guide said as it located a bit far from all the main sights in Ninh Binh so no tourist buses around. We didn’t see the langurs here but we heard the sound of them. So if you have time, recommend do this boat tour.
practical_tips: Do this boat tour if you have time

author: sensable
title: Worth for the boat trip
original_content: This is a very unique place in the world. The boat trip to find the delacour langur is peaceful and very nice. The accommodations and food are limited but you can make the most of it.
extracted_spaces: The boat trip to find the delacour langur
highlights: peaceful and very nice boat trip

author: Rahul K
title: Simply breathtaking natural beauty
original_content: We were lucky to stay near this place and we could simply go near the reserve in the morning for a walk and it’s breathtakingly beautiful…Whole road goes along the reserve for almost 16 kms and it’s sheer cliff side looks beautiful… It’s amazing how calms and beautiful it is…There are birds around and this is an ideal self space for anyone…Enjoy riding your cycle or have a good walk when you are here
practical_tips: go near the reserve for a walk
ride your cycle or have a good walk

author: Geraint L
title: Let your troubles drift away....
original_content: A great way to spend an hour in the peace & quiet of gently being rowed through the dramatic scenary.We were lucky enough to see a monkey, climbing uo one of the sheer cliffs & then a real treat, a kingfisher, we saw a flash of blue as it flew away & then were lucky that it landed close by to give us a photo to treasure.Be sure to tip your boat capt well, they earn their money thats for sure

author: lorenzocaratti
title: Disappointment
original_content: Looking up lonely island, we thought it would be a great place to visit. The price is ok but the experience left us bored. The boat lady asked us money at the end (no added stuff). We gave her a tip and she continued to ask for more. Lost its spirit... honestly, we've seen much more beautiful with identical landscapes in the northern-eastern parts of vietnam.
drawbacks: boat lady asked us money at the end

author: Alu-Poo
title: Not that many birds
original_content: We mainly went here to see birds. There were a few, but not many. The boat ride is very nice, ending in a cave. Beautiful landscape and once in a while a bird taking off (they are very shy). We haven't seen the monkeys. There are not many tourists here, making it a quiet experience. We were a couple and had our own boat. Tam Coc and Trang An are much busier. We spent three days in Ninh Binh and had the time to visit this. However, if you have only time for one boat ride, I would recommend Trang An or Tam Coc. On the Trang An boat ride we have seen about the same number of species of birds as here in Van Long.
practical_tips: go to Trang An or Tam Coc if you only have time for one boat ride

author: aurelieche2016
title: Beautiful, relaxing experience
original_content: Definitely one of our highlights of the trip. I visited this place with my husband and during our visit to Van Long Nature Reserve we got to see beautiful reflections in the waters and the prettiest water lilies. Definitely a must for lovers of flowers :)

author: Jean D
title: Poetic Scenery
original_content: Perfect for a romantic couple getaway! My wife and I really enjoyed it, and we recommend to do this trip in the late afternoon for amazing sunset views
practical_tips: do this trip in the late afternoon

author: RG02
title: Well worth visiting and quieter than either Trang An or Tam Coc
original_content: It was a dull day when we visited but that didn’t spoil our enjoyment of Van Long. Our lady rower spoke a little English and took the time to explain much that we saw as we went around. Several boats overtook us as we were rowed at a more leisurely pace but this meant we could take in so much more. We came to what looked like the turning point in our journey, all of the boats ahead went briefly inside a cave before coming back out for the return journey. We entered the cave expecting to do the same but were told  ‘heads down’ as we ventured further in, soon we saw some light ahead, this was our ‘exit’. We had come through into a beautiful, quiet oasis, no other boats around us. A circular route through some lovely scenery brought us back to the point to re-enter the cave before continuing back to our starting point via a different waterway. The only disappointment was that we didn’t see any langur monkeys as we had been told they were in the area. A lovely different trip, do it if you can spare some time.
highlights: our lady rower spoke a little English
took the time to explain much that we saw
practical_tips: do it if you can spare some time

author: Henry_Chloe
title: Memorable moment...
original_content: Luckily we chose this place in the best season! Getting on the sampan, all we need to do was relaxing and admiring the scene along the river.We had wonderful time on the late Valentine’s Day...

author: Jacky R
title: Not many monkeys
original_content: Nice boat trip with nice scenery. The Langurs weren’t very accommodating as they were far away from the boat and there were only four of them but we also saw some interesting birds including a Kingfisher.

author: anikgupta_virgo
title: Average experience for me but maybe good for others.
original_content: I went to Van long Nature reserve with more expectations than what i had in reality. i already had similar experience hence it was not surprising or very good for me. but few fellow travellers enjoyed it.

author: Cameron Y
title: Peaceful ride thru the waterways
original_content: Shorter boat ride than the others in Tam Coc and Trang An. OK if you have spare time. Boat ride is about 1hr
drawbacks: Shorter boat ride compared to others
practical_tips: Go if you have spare time

author: Josefer M
title: The landscape Amazing
original_content: You will appreciate the most hiding gardens and wild treasures that one of the most beautiful areas of Vietnam give you to fulfil the senses. The have trails and hiking unforgettables the prices very reasonables and the culinary culture  wonderful.

author: Rico
title: Natural with Wildlife!
original_content: Of all the river rowboat rides that we took around Ninh Binh, we agreed that this one was our favorite because of the Wildlife and nature. We saw so many fish and snails in the water and it was truly a natural setting nothing manmade or built except of course the little rustic rowboats. We had a wonderful guide, she couldn’t speak to us but, she showed up the monkeys in the trees, the snails and their pink larvae, fishes and seaweeds. She took us through a very tight cave and around about back out. It was a very memorable trip. I think for that it was the best.
practical_tips: Go early to see the monkeys in the trees

author: Oerderan
title: A place of extraordinary natural beauty
original_content: There are a few boat tours on offer in and around Ninh Binh, but as we had already explored the Phong Nha Cave by boat recently, we figured that it would be difficult to trump, so we were looking for something a bit different. The Ramsar listed Van Long Wetland Nature Reserve proved to be a wise choice. My 15 year old son and I did some reading up on the site and we were keen to see the critically endangered Delacour’s langurs in the wild. The spectacular backdrop and proximity to our accommodation was an added bonus.However, it wasn’t all smooth sailing. We specifically asked the tour operators on shore to see the monkeys, in the hope we would be assigned a guide with a talent for finding them. Amazingly, the various guides on the Wetland shore attempted to spot the monkeys by eye hundreds of metres away on their limestone karst homes.After launching into the wetlands, our guide, worryingly rowed directly toward an area where motorised equipment was being used to conduct weeding in the conservation area. I think it’s great that efforts are being made to prevent weeds from taking over the wetlands, but what hope would we have in spotting the langurs with all of this commotion? I’m not a monkey expert, but I was certain that the monkey spotting expedition was not going to reap any rewards for us. And that’s where this story takes a turn. Our guide seemed to be heading back toward our boat launch when he took a change in direction. We suddenly found ourselves alone in the wetlands and in relative tranquility despite only having left the noisy weeders 5-10 minutes earlier. And then suddenly a langur family appeared at the base of the limestone karst outcrop. After an initial flurry of amateur photographing, we sat back and watched the langur family slowly ascend the limestone cliff face foraging as they went, as the sun slowly set over the wetlands. Sheer beauty! It’s also worth mentioning here that tips are expected by the guides, which caught us off guard. It’s not in my homeland’s custom to give tips and I thought that of Vietnam as well, until we tried bidding farewell to our guide. I fumbled the tip giving process and was unable to appease my guide.Lastly, I wish there were an interpretation centre at the Van Long Wetland Nature Reserve. It’s natural assets definitely deserve it and may help bolster their conservation efforts.
drawbacks: Motorised equipment being used to conduct weeding in the conservation area
highlights: Seeing the critically endangered Delacour's langurs in the wild
Sheer beauty of the langur family ascending the limestone cliff face
practical_tips: Go early to avoid motorised equipment
Be prepared to give tips to the guides

author: John W
title: A magical afternoon.
original_content: Three of us shared a rental car and driver to get here and we shared the same boat to explore the marshes. Arriving a little early, we took a walk along the levee from which we could look down on the wetland and see many of the birds. But when we got on the boat, our perspective changed and we saw new birds, some close up, which our boatwoman pointed out for us. What she lacked in English she made up for in good nature and sharp eyes. Having crossed the wetland she piloted us up a channel into the limestone massif. Suddenly she cried "Monkey!" and there they were, four rare and striking black and white Delacour langurs on the cliff face. She gave us plenty of time to watch before turning back. Even then we weren't finished; we saw another group of five adult and three young langurs on the way back. And we saw flights of egrets come in to the marsh to roost.We started our boat ride at 3.30 pm and saw the first langurs at 4 pm, just the time we had been told that they become active. Our smiling cheerful boat lady didn't even hint at the tip she so richly deserved.
highlights: saw rare and striking black and white Delacour langurs
saw flights of egrets come in to the marsh to roost
practical_tips: go early to see langurs become active

author: Andrew_J_Berry
title: Get there early
original_content: A great place to visit, but go early to avoid the crowds. Small boats rowed by locals take you through a sample of the wetland reserve. Very peaceful as you listen to the gentle paddling and soak up the scenery.

author: srvctraveler
title: Fabulous natural area that remains only lightly discovered - A must see before others find it.
original_content: This is a beautiful nature preserve in Ninh Binh province that hasn't been discovered and over-run with tourists like Trang An and Tam Coc.  Similar natural features, but smaller scale, and the boat tours are still run by the locals on a small scale.  We went out in a small bamboo boat paddled by a friendly young woman who made conversation in her limited English and our limited vietnamese, but she taught us the names of birds, pulled snails out of the water to show us. We saw quite a few water birds, including storks, though we didn't get to see the Langurs who are native to the area (we think we heard some vocalizing however).  Most of the other visitors were Vietnamese families and groups on a sunday outing, all of whom, including the children, wanted to greet us.  Unlike Trang An and Tam Coc, we didn't feel pressured to buy anything or tip, though we were delighted to tip this young woman who had given us such a pleasurable visit.

author: Neil R
title: Canoeing in the w ilderness
original_content: Probably the best thing we did in Ninh Binh. Hire the local boatsmen to take a trip within the reserve and explore caves and nature in all its glory. wonderful way to spend a morning
highlights: wonderful way to spend a morning
explore caves and nature in all its glory

author: thong pham
title: It was a great place that really happen with ecotourism. The place combining of the water, limestone like a paiting
original_content: Van Long NR is a place that you can see Delacour langur - an endemic species which is only 250 individuals left in the world. Enjoying with the water, limestone on a very simple boat that for sure you never experience before.

author: Zuzka123
title: Spectacular views without hordes of tourists
original_content: Possibly not as picturesque as the nearby Trang An reserve…but also not with gazillions of tourists. It was around 40 degrees when we visited with our seven year old son, so a 90mins boat trip instead of 3 to 4 hours at Trang An was far more manageable. Van Long reserve gave us a good peek into this world of narrow waterways and floating mountains.We didn’t see any monkeys, which was a shame, but the tranquility and peacefulness of this spectacular place were worth it. I felt really bad for the woman rowing our boat, she was quite old and it was so hot I worried she might just have a heart attack...
highlights: Good peek into the world of narrow waterways and floating mountains
practical_tips: Consider visiting when it's not as hot
Be mindful of the boat rower's well-being

author: khoalegend
title: It take a lot of time but useless
original_content: If you had visit all the site of ninh binh & want to discover, Van Long is the last scene. Its popular after king kong film. The price of ticket is 2$ for 1 hour boat trip. If you had seen Trang An sightseeing, van long cant compared with it
drawbacks: Cannot compared with Trang An sightseeing
practical_tips: Go to Van Long after visiting other Ninh Binh sites

author: vocalisa
title: still a hidden gem
original_content: a natural habitat of the endangered Delacour langurs, a species of primates you find in the North East just outside the UNESCO landscape complex. An ensemble of rocks surrounded by water which is declared a wetland nature reserve, home of rare species of birds and other animals. Especially in the mornings and sunny afternoons you can very often watch the monkeys climbing on the rocks searching for their diet of leaves.  A visit in the late afternoon will often reward you with an impressive sunset and the view onto the storks and egrets returning to their sleeping places on the trees near the rocks. Recently a new hotel with restaurant opened opposite the ticket booth, otherwise the setting is still modest and simple and just adorable and different every time and every season. My favourite. Try to avoid grumpy looking rowers. Tip the friendly ones with 50 k per boat.
extracted_spaces: natural habitat of the endangered Delacour langurs
ensemble of rocks surrounded by water
highlights: watch the monkeys climbing on the rocks searching for their diet of leaves
view onto the storks and egrets returning to their sleeping places
practical_tips: try to avoid grumpy looking rowers
tip the friendly ones with 50 k per boat

author: DiNg|photographer
title: It's good for a day out of city
original_content: We went to Van Long last week. The tickets were 100k vnd for 2 people. The tour is 1 hour with boat (2 people 1 bat) among the Van Long natures. The sightseeing is ok but not as great as Trang An or Tam Coc, however, with people who like things be more natured would love this place. The boater suggested us to take another 1 hour tour (he said new tour) to a quite area (good view) with charge 100k vnd. We were ok. The view looks very good. It looks like a small valley compare to Nho Que (in Ha Giang). Everything is ok until the boater charged us 250k vnd. He said 200k vnd for the tour and 50k it is for the tips. We sai we bought tickets for 100k and we gave him 200k. He looks not so happy. And at the beginning, he looks surprise when we gave him the tickets. So I am not sure, will the tickets are paid for the services or not.

author: LinhVu
title: Yes - Yes - Yes
original_content: Unlike the very crowded Trang An, at Van Long Nature Reserve we can have more time for ourselves to enjoy the nature, the quietness & if we’re lucky enough we can see langurs in the nature by our own eyes. The area has 3 different routes 1-2-3 hours depends on our time availability, we choose the 1-hour route & it covered an appropriate scale. Do give some tips to the boat ladies/men, about US$2/passenger (or VND50k)
highlights: see langurs in the nature by our own eyes
practical_tips: give some tips to the boat ladies/men

author: Irish_Food_Dude
title: Peaceful
original_content: We did this tour with 3 small kids (3, 5 & 8), we took 2 boats so the overall cost was 100k VND per boat. We tipped 50k per boat as the rowers were so good with the kids - they gave them turns rowing, went to the banks to pick flowers, took photos of our family & taught us how to sing Happy Birthday in Vietnamese!!Scenery is nothing like Trang An, much more simple, but we went first thing in the morning (around 9am) and had the river to ourselves so it was perfectly quiet except for the wildlife.The cave was really cool but luckily we did this tour before Trang An so we didn’t have a benchmark for cool caves!If you’re selecting just one boat tour I’d recommend Trang An as the preferred one but I’m glad we did both.
drawbacks: Scenery is nothing like Trang An, much more simple
highlights: rowers were so good with the kids
perfectly quiet except for the wildlife
practical_tips: go first thing in the morning
select just one boat tour, I'd recommend Trang An

author: winter
title: Disappointed
original_content: Little bit disappointed in this area where i expect it will be nice trip. Ticket is 60,000 vnd for boat trip and 20,000 vnd for sightseeing. boat trip is quite short and not much to see on the side of the river, the  cave is tiny and look average. The rower did their job but keep pushy about tips. Overall I wont be back.
drawbacks: the rower did their job but keep pushy about tips

author: Varun_723
title: 1 Hour Of Relaxation
original_content: My wife and I spent an hour being rowed around the Van Long Nature Reserve. This boat ride is much shorter than the one in Trang An, with the latter being closer to 3 hours. If you're planning on visiting both places, I recommend you do Van Long first, and then Trang An so you don't set the bar too high. Van Long doesn't have an awful lot to look at, whereas Trang An does. If you're looking for a scenic ride, this probably isn't the one for you. It's still worth checking out as you get to see storks up close (depending on the time of the day). Just buy a drink or some snacks from the shops nearby and make the best of the trip. The rower will ask you for a tip upon completion of the ride, but considering the exchange rate, a tip doesn't cost much. My tour guide recommended a tip of no more than 100,000 dong. If they ask for more, refuse.
drawbacks: Not a lot to look at
practical_tips: Refuse if asked for more than 100,000 dong

author: suzieslapcabbage
title: A tranquil piece of paradise
original_content: A great value excursion throughout a beautiful wetland. Our boat rower took us on what looked like one of the less used waterways, meaning we were the only boat (just the two of us and the rower) most of the time; it was so quiet, tranquil and beautiful. The scenery is amazing with the beautiful limestone mountains, caves, birds, fish, baby snails, and flora. We we’re very lucky to see the rare (endangered) Delacour’s Langur, 5 in fact. Our rower stopped the boat and we sat for 10+ minutes watching these beautiful monkeys jump, swing and move around in front of us (wish we had our binoculars). Van Long Nature Reserve was more than we expected, so glad we went there.

author: Max
title: Nice and a bit off the track
original_content: Beautiful views and is probably less busy compared to Trang An and Tam Coc boat trips. BUT you should still go on a boat trip in Trang An, too! Did both and preferred Trang An. But I think I only preferred Trang An because the scenery is nicer and because I was lucky that my boat was the only one at the time (which is absolutely unbelieveable but true). At peak time Trang An and Tam Coc boat tours are soooo crowded that for those who are crowd-o-phobic travellers might prefer Van Long which is beautiful as well.
practical_tips: go on a boat trip in Trang An

author: Albywon
title: Peaceful
original_content: Despite the large number of other boats near you it is still possible to enjoy this landscape. We managed to find peace and it was a beautiful day to float through the area.

author: Susan L
title: beautiful
original_content: We decided to take this day trip from Hanoi in conjunction with a trip to Trang An/Bai Dinh and am so glad we did. The largest temple and pagoda in Vietnam as well as the beautiful natural surroundings make this destination not to be missed. I would say it is easily on par with Halong Bay!
highlights: largest temple and pagoda in Vietnam
practical_tips: take a day trip from Hanoi
visit in conjunction with Trang An/Bai Dinh

author: Lya_amar
title: Hidden Gem of Ninh Binh
original_content: Far far away from city, crowds, pollution. Great way to connect your soul with nature.. :) About 30min motorbike ride from Ninh Binh to Van Long Nature Reserve.. 100k dong for 1 hour boat ride.. Love this place :)
highlights: great way to escape city, crowds, pollution

author: Mark C
title: Peaceful Boat Trip to Enjoy Nature Reserve
original_content: Took the boat trip to observe the langur primates and watch birds. Very worthwhile visit.Beautiful scenery.

author: E J J
title: Ethereal Wonder
original_content: This boat ride definitely has that other worldly feel to it. Such beauty in silence and nature. Spotted many water birds and monkeys. Loved the majesty of the place, and the lack of crowds jostling for position. A moment of peace and tranquillity.

author: Naestchen
title: Wonderful boat trip through the reserve
original_content: We were staying at the Emeralda Hotel and booked a trip with them to go on a bike and a boat tour. We cycled a lot through the area next to the Van Long Nature Reserve and enjoyed the beautiful view. After having visited a temple we went back to the starting point of the boat trips and took a one hour long trip on a wooden boat. The lady who navigated us was nice although she did not really speak English. The landscape consisting of the mountains, the water and the cage is amazing! We'd definitely recommend the trip!
drawbacks: The lady who navigated us was nice although she did not really speak English.
highlights: amazing landscape consisting of the mountains, the water and the cage
practical_tips: book a trip with the Emeralda Hotel
go on a bike and a boat tour

author: boscobobbie
title: Peaceful, otherworldly, beautiful
original_content: Much quieter than the Trang An Grottoes, Cranes, frogs, monkeys on the hillsides. Bullrushes and caves, misty mountains and birdsong. An enchanting boat ride, guides responsive and helpful. Evening ride recommended.

author: Coco
title: SO quiet and nice
original_content: SO quiet and nice whereas the other places are crowded! Views are beautiful and we saw monkeys on the rocks...and birds! Perfect

author: Lee A D
title: Second best thing to do in Bình Minh
original_content: We loved Trang An but also really enjoyed this Nature Preserve.  Long path beside it as well that we used with a tandem. Highly recommend the peace and raw nature of this large place.
practical_tips: use the long path beside it

author: Lee Đặng
title: Traveling to Van Long swamp in Ninh Binh
original_content: Van Long natural reservation area is away from Ha Noi about 80km, which is located at the Northeast, Gia Vien district, Ninh Bình Province. This is the most abundant place for ecosystem that is the residence of many flora and fauna such as: Fish, Bird, stork and more than 40 kinds of Delacour’s Langur.Besides, Van Long ecotourism destination has great scene of mountain and river, tourists can sit on the old bamboo boat and enjoy the simple and peaceful view.After traveling through the mountain, tourists can visit the Fish Cave, which is one of the most beautiful cave here with the romantic scene, small valley and the mountain surround. If lucky, tourists can see some langurs sitting on the trees.
highlights: great scene of mountain and river
romantic scene, small valley and the mountain surround
practical_tips: sit on the old bamboo boat and enjoy the simple and peaceful view

author: Kassa
title: spotted 8 langur in the wild!
original_content: lovely boat ride, quiet, beautiful waterways and we were very lucky to see the Langur.  Tickets for the boat are inexpensive but the boat driver will hassle for the same again in a cash tip at the end!
practical_tips: buy tickets in advance to avoid hassle

author: youbloodytourist
title: Less crowds, more atmosphere!
original_content: Out of all three of the 'boat' experiences in Ninh Binh province (Tam Coc and Trang An) being the other two, this one was the quietest. That alone makes it worthwhile! Less to see than Trang An, but less commercial / more authentic.
drawbacks: Less to see than Trang An
highlights: Quietest of the three boat experiences

author: Wanderlustsimone
title: The scenery is stunning!
original_content: That's one thing you can't deny, how incredibly beautiful your surroundings are, and for me, that made the trip worth it, that's why I was there! however, I thought we would get to stop off at some of the pagodas, like others did, but we didn't stop once. We were taking it in turns rowing between my partner and I and the couple sat behind us. The lady rowing at the back gave us questionnaires about half way through which gave me a red flag, because it said 'did your guide ask for a tip?' to which we put no at the time. I knew that If a company thought to give a questionnaire on a small BOAT trip. Something dodgy was happening. The woman proceeded towards the end of the tour to point at her hands and ask for a tip. If it wasn't for the fact she'd conned us into filling that questionnaire out before she asks for a tip which I presume isn't allowed, I would have gladly tipped without being asked. Still go, just be aware!
drawbacks: questionnaire on a small BOAT trip
practical_tips: be aware of guides asking for tips

author: LA4man
title: Get up early and look for Delacour's Langur
original_content: I had the privilege of visiting Van Long twice in 2018.  The first time we woke up very early and did a boat ride at Van Long. The cost is about $2 for an hour of rigorous paddling by the boatsman (or woman as is often the case).  We were the first people out for the day, and were fortunate to see three (3!!) of the very endangered Delacour's Langur (white bottomed monkey) eating in the trees on the cliffs and running along  the cliff tops.  Stunning!  The second time I took the boat later in the morning and was not so lucky to see the monkeys.  However, the next day I got up early, took a bike from the hotel, and rode along the levy (to the left as you face the river once you ride up the street from the small town).  Voila! I was able to see one monkey running along the cliff, and the bike ride was AMAZING.   If you turn right at the river you'll see a monstrous building in the distance which is a mega-cathedral being built by a very rich local businessman.  While it's still a nice ride, I prefer the left and more of natural view.  Enjoy!
drawbacks: Not seeing the monkeys on the second visit
practical_tips: Go early for a better chance of seeing the monkeys
Take a bike from the hotel for a scenic ride

author: matamatablondie
title: No monkeys!
original_content: If you are expecting to see monkeys you will be disappointed - not sure if this is promoted officially, however the map provided by our homestay states this had wild monkeys.  It was a beautiful scenic boat ride however you do not get off the boat unlike Trang An boat tour which I would recommend over this even at 4 times the price. Very authentic - be ready for a sore butt. You will be expected to tip 50,000 VND.
practical_tips: go to Trang An boat tour

author: Louise
title: Not bad but...
original_content: We were the first customers of the day, nice and early to try to spot the birds. We saw a few, but not as many as we'd hoped. The scenery was beautiful, however, I was almost constantly tapped on my shoulder by the lady rowing the boat, to let me know how hard she was working and that her hands were calloused. We gave her 20k Dong  tip (over 50% of the price of the ride) and she gave it back, saying it wasn't enough. This is totally unacceptable in my opinion. She even got a friend of hers to run after us, asking for more money!Sadly, that ruined the trip for us.
drawbacks: not as many birds as hoped
lady rowing the boat tapped on shoulder
highlights: calloused hands of the lady rowing the boat

author: John K
title: Good place for bird watching
original_content: Although this place is a bit of a drive from Ninh Binh, it's worth a visit if you're interested in wetlands habitat. Upon arrival I paid 10k to park my motor bike and 60k for entrance fee/boat ticket. It's a bit confusing, but you have to walk across the road and down some steps to reach the boats. Boats are meant for 2 adults, no more. The early part of the paddle is where we saw the most birds, in the open area before we reached the cliffs. The portion adjacent to the cliffs offered beautiful views of the sheer limestone cliffs. Very peaceful, as we paddled along, just the swish of the oars. We went through one short and very dark cave (with low headroom!) then paddled around in a big arc and back through the cave. Overall the trip was about 90 minutes.

author: Gavin C
title: Langur monkeys!
original_content: We took note of previous reviews and went later in they day (arrived at 4pm) and it ticked all the boxes. Saw plenty of bird life, insects and best of all langur monkeys climbing the rock face near the entrance to the cave - counted at least a dozen and even a baby. Our rower (man) was excellent and waited patiently until they had all disappeared, in fact was almost as excited as we were at seeing them so we tipped him 100,000 as he also slowed the boat when nearing birds so as not to scare them. He seemed very happy with the tip and no scowls at all   We went on a Sunday which is when all the bridal couples seem to go as well which is quite hilarious with all the poses and shouting cameramen. This was only at the end , the rest of the ride was extremely peaceful with only one other boat sighted.

We could view them for ten minutes leaping across rocks and descending from trees. The boatman was extremely helpful, and also when we asked in case there was monkeys, he loked for a couple of mins and spotted them for us. At the turnaround point within the cave, the boatman requested for the camera of ours plus required many pictures for us. In case you're staying at Emerald you do not have to book their bike tour in case you do not wish to as it's just a short hike. We feel this's an interesting spot to visit

title: Misty day boat ride with the parents
original_content: The boat ride was nice through the Van Long reserve. It wasn't too long of a trip and the old lady paddling was friendly and would point to different birds and say their names in Vietnamese. It's usual custom to give a tip at the end say ~100K. We ended up winding back into the mouth of a small cave and double-backed. Overall, it was about an hour long trip.I would NOT recommend motorbiking or going around Van Long though, as the truth is a sad reality. In the front is this beautiful facade of nature and wildlife but behind is just trash mounds and industrial plants, lumber yards, massive mining pits, construction and polluted landfills.
highlights: point to different birds and say their names in Vietnamese

author: Jan-Olof O
title: Well worth a visit!
original_content: The manager at Vancouver hotel arranged for a private car to Van Long Nature reserve. I did go to see the Delacour langur in Van Long Nature reserve. There is an entrance of 60 000 Dong and a fee for the boat as well, I paid 100 000 Dong for the boat! You step into a small bamboo boat and a woman rows you into the reserve. You will follow a water canal into the mountains, at the mountains there is a 180 degree bend and a new canal behind the mountains you see from the entrance to the reserve. The journey will end up at a small cave maybe fifty meters deep which will be visited! When returning out from the cave we did see langurs up in the mountains on the left hind side of the boat. This is a little bit far away so look carefully and you might spot the Delacour langurs. There are also different kind of birds in this reserve.
practical_tips: Pay attention to the 180 degree bend

author: 795suzie
title: Peaceful Ride UNTIL the end
original_content: We were lucky to be the first boat on the water for the morning. It was very peaceful and we did get to see some monkeys in the trees. We had just come back from a 4 day trek further north where the scenery was spectacular, so the scenery was ok in comparison. What really ruined it was when the lady began continually saying, "souvenir, souvenir," as we neared the end of the ride (we weren't sure what she meant). The ride was only 50 000 VND per person and we were prepared to give a 75,000 tip but once we handed it to her we soon realised it was not enough. Her tone became hostile and then a male who worked for this organisation came over on his sampan and started shouting aggressively at us and held out 100 000 VND. I felt if we didn't give more we would continue to be harassed. We had wished we hadn't taken this sampan cruise,it was the worst experience we had on our three week tour of Vietnam. This was the only time during the three weeks we felt harassed and expected to tip an amount that matched the price for the cruise. Very disappointing.
drawbacks: the lady began continually saying, "souvenir, souvenir,"

author: DRGilbert
title: An idyllic cruise through a peaceful setting with monkeys to boot
original_content: It was late afternoon when we boarded our sampan for a leisurely cruise through the Van Long Nature Reserve. It was very peaceful as our oarsman pushed us along flooded rice fields beside rocky peaks. He stopped once, pointing excitedly toward the summit where we spotted a large Vietnamese monkey scampering along the rocks. A little further down the stream we entered the mouth of a small cave and then did a u-turn to return to the vanishing daylight. Soon we were back where we started. A an hour-long trip, well worthwhile.

It is a nice and quiet scenery if you are not surrounded by hundreds of koreans/Chinese, but we also weren't impressed too much. I think we should have chosen Trang An over Van Long...
