author: Eric M
title: Air pollution in the area is hazardous to health
original_content: There are numerous cement factories that can be clearly seen from the reserve. These factories are sending clouds of silica dust into the air and the Nature Reserve is perpetually shrouded in a silica dust cloud. So bad is this that everything is covered in a layer of fine dust, from stall displays, coffee shop tables etc.This is a "dead" reserve. Riding out on the row boat, you can clearly see a suspension of fine dust on the surface and in the water itself. Not surprising, there are no fish or any living creatures alive in the water. In fact, in almost 2 hours spent on the row boat, we only spotted one fish. I photograph wildlife, and given the abundant flora in this swampy ecosystem, there should be an abundance of birds and other wildlife, but in truth, we only say 2-3 birds. And this is all the wildlife we saw throughout the boat trip.Sad to say, the ecosystem of Van Long is long destroyed. You risk your health being here.
drawbacks: Silica dust cloud perpetually shrouding the reserve
No fish or living creatures in the water
practical_tips: Avoid visiting due to health risks

author: engrob84
title: Serene
original_content: This place totally exceeded expectations. It’s so peaceful. It’s very cheap and there are so few visitors.

author: Expl0rer007
title: DELIGHTFUL
original_content: Van Long is a real delight.  Slipping gently along the waterways between the reed beds is restful and tranquil as the oarsman dips his oars into the reflective waters and nudges the sampan along.  Soaring limestone peaks brood like sentinels, keeping a watchful eye on your progress as the landscape changes by the minute.  Seeing a fish eagle and two Delacour's Langur were added bonuses.  The trip on the water is justification itself.  Highly recommended.  Go early, though, especially in the summer, when it can get very busy and noisy.

author: tonytD9568SZ
title: Beautiful river ride in a nature preserve
original_content: Preserve is located next to a canal and on the other side of a dike .most views will be of Karsts but building cranes can be seen in the distance on other side of canal so no total feeling of nature. 50.000VND/PPBoat trip is about an hour. If you have to choose between this  and Trang An. It depends...I'd say the latter. Yes this is less crowded and yes you'll see some birds and maybe a monkey or two but as far as total experience of boating the cavesI'd say Trang An.
drawbacks: building cranes can be seen in the distance
highlights: see some birds and maybe a monkey or two
practical_tips: If you have to choose between this and Trang An

author: varun_mukthi
title: An absolute must-do
original_content: This was a complete surprise. We went for a boat ride and it was completely mesmerising. Absolutely taken by surprise how picturesque and un-spoilt this place was. The people rowing the boat were excellent. Quietly went about their jobs and didn't ask for any tips. Off the beaten track and highly recommend it.

author: exquisitektc
title: Comparable to Trang An but Still Different
original_content: We started off the day by going for a quiet boat ride here. Our tour guide said that he pays the boat operators to go left while everyone else goes right but we are not certain that this is accurate information. Our two boats were the only boats out that day but probably because it was Tet. At any rate, the scenery here is different from Trang An. Whereas Trang An offered multiple cave experiences, this offered a gorgeous view of the lush waterscape and landscape, complete with beautiful white crane-looking birds, rare monkeys, and the peace and quiet that Trang An did not quite offer. If you only have time for one boat ride, it would be tough to choose. Van Long is surely a snippet and mere fraction of what Trang An offers. Either way, if you have time for both then we recommend touring both. If you have a little time on your hands, then Van Long is pleasing. If you have about three or more hours to spare then Trang An is worth the time. If peace and quiet is not your thing then this experience might not be for you.Also, make sure your tour guide doesn't jump on the boat with you. The nature reserve is best observed with two per boat, not including the boat operator of course.The negative part of this experience is that tipping our boat operator 50,000 was not enough. He literally stalked us to the car talking to our tour guide in Vietnamese with a tone that sounded like he was upset. Eventually, our tour guide pulled out 100,000 and gave it to him then he went away.Also, the two vendors near the parking lot sell cotton table covers that cannot be found elsewhere in NB. If you are looking for nice cotton gifts, these might certainly be for you. Our friend negotiated 800,000 for three. Great deal!
drawbacks: tipping the boat operator was not enough
the boat operator stalked us to the car
the vendors near the parking lot sell overpriced cotton table covers
highlights: gorgeous view of the lush waterscape and landscape
practical_tips: tour both Van Long and Trang An
make sure your tour guide doesn't jump on the boat with you

author: P F
title: Beautiful landscape!
original_content: Great spot that is well worth the visit. Rent the row boats and travel the river to experience the natural caves, wildlife and newly built temples. Go on a day when it’s not crowded for a truly peaceful nature experience. You’ll take a ton of photos of the beautiful mountains.
practical_tips: go on a day when it's not crowded

author: Marla R
title: Family trip 2018
original_content: You can get on a boat and have a rower take you through the wetlands/reserve. So beautiful to get up close to the mountains.

author: jaypep1
title: Lots of Nature
original_content: This is a stunning Wetlands Nature Reserve. All year round there is wildlife. The boat tours last about 1 hour and cost 80,000₫. Feb.2018. You buy the tickets from across the road on Gia Van Street at the ticket booth in the car park, behind the souvenir shops. Parking was free. If your into wildlife or just great scenery then it's well worth a visit. There is also a very large old Cathedral near by. The best photos I save for myself.
practical_tips: buy tickets from across the road

author: sanu
title: Better than trang ah, quite secluded and peaceful boating.
original_content: We skipped trang ah boating and came here and didn’t regret. The 1 hour boating was great with lot of birds, the view was not good for being a rainy day.
drawbacks: The view was not good for being a rainy day
highlights: The 1 hour boating was great with lot of birds

author: duncan_KS
title: Scenic and serene
original_content: When we planned to include this place as part of our private day trip, the tour operator told us this will be repetition as we will also cover Trang An boat trip in the same day, but we insisted. Glad that we made the decision as Van Long gave very different favour if compare with Trang An.We went to Van Long around 4pm, the atmosphere was very serene and reflection from the water was very clear to give many photograph opportunities.  We saw a lots of birds and impressive sunset. However, we couldn't witness the rare monkey species that we looked forward in Van Long. The boat ride was very relax. It will be great if the boatman doesn't ask us to give him specific amount of tip at the end of boat ride.
drawbacks: couldn't witness the rare monkey species
boatman asking for specific amount of tip

author: Dieset
title: The boat trip is a must
original_content: Just enjoy the fantastic boat trip through the caves and along the river. Amazing to see the way people were rowining the boats.

author: Raaj1976
title: Beautiful place with awesome views
original_content: This location is peaceful and mesmerizing. We enjoyed the journey and had all the fun with beautiful weather and joyful family time.

author: Adventure beyond imagination
title: Unforgettable experience
original_content: We decided to go there in order to avoid the crowds. While we arrived there nobody else was around. The boat trip was so fantastic and we were literally alone in the middle of the wonderful scenery.
extracted_spaces: the middle of the wonderful scenery
highlights: the boat trip was so fantastic

author: amclean2016
title: Pouring with rain
original_content: The fact hat we were caught in the tail end of a typhoon and torrential rains did not deter us to take the boat trip at Van Long Nature Reserve. Now and again the rain let up a bit and we managed to get some pictures of the beautiful surroundings.  Well worth going.
drawbacks: caught in the tail end of a typhoon and torrential rains

author: Hayles7
title: Pleasant my way to spend an hour
original_content: And that’s about it.  We walked up from our hotel and got our tickets (50,000 dang a head) and stepped into the small wooden boat.  Our rower skulled her way thru the reed lined waterway to a cave and back. Whilst it was relaxing we did not see that much of particular interest. Took about a hour. Our rower added nothing to our trip.All in all pretty much a do about nothing - until we got back to the dock and they wanted tipped. One lady actually asked for 1.0m dang and we chased her.Hopefully tomorrow we see something more impressive.
drawbacks: did not see that much of particular interest
our rower added nothing to our trip

author: kyy0te
title: A pleasant evening boat ride looking for endangered langurs
original_content: We felt very privileged to actually see a couple of langurs at a great distance. The boat ride itself was relaxing through the reeds with waterfowl in a river lined with steep mountains.
practical_tips: go early for better langur sightings

author: Grace B
title: Incredibly Beautiful & Quiet
original_content: We cycled here from our hostel in Tam Con - easy to reach. We didn't know what to expect as we'd read it can be quite a tourist trap but it was far from that! Only a couple of tourists around. The boat holds 4 people and a rower takes you around for about 3 hours - you can help her if you'd like! The scenery was absolutely breath taking!! You get dropped off at locations to walk around and explore and then hop back on the boat. we don't know anything about bird watching so can't comment on that but we did see monkeys!The rower asks for tips during the end of the trip - considering the whole trip costs £2 it isn't much to ask!
extracted_spaces: locations to walk around and explore
drawbacks: can be quite a tourist trap

author: Erica B
title: Very unassuming and easy to miss
original_content: We spent 2 hours driving around looking for the boats when we realized(after asking someone) that they were at the dock we saw 2 hours prior. When you pull off the main road (at the sign that says Van long restaurant) you drive to the end of the road. At the end of the road there is a pavilion on the right by some vendors selling crap which you buy your ticket. Then you walk up to the boat dock (2 pagoda pavilions) on the water.Overall the boat tour was ok for the value, but Trang an was much better! Don't go in the middle of the day either because there was no shade! Also, our guide was bargaining with me for a bigger tip after we gave her a 40% tip!! She didn't realize how much we gave her since it was American money.
drawbacks: guide bargaining for a bigger tip
no shade in the middle of the day
highlights: boat tour was ok for the value
practical_tips: don't go in the middle of the day

author: Faustine F
title: To do! No tourists, not expensive, beautiful
original_content: We highly recommend this boat tour as there are no tourists at all, the nature and landscapes are incredible, you get into one cave, awesome.

author: Olgalaaaa
title: Tranquil
original_content: Visited van long with a friend and had a closer look at the beautiful mountain. Sadly, were not able to do bird watching bc of the weather. Nice place but try to improve the rental boats.
drawbacks: were not able to do bird watching bc of the weather
try to improve the rental boats
practical_tips: try to improve the rental boats

author: JetHopper 71
title: "Peaceful and Tranquil scenery"
original_content: A great way to see rural Vietnam in a boat..The reserve is not as touristy as Tam Coc...Worth the trip to be amongst the limestone mountains...This area is ideal for keen bird watchers.
highlights: great way to see rural Vietnam
worth the trip to be amongst the limestone mountains

author: Amy M
title: Peaceful and atmospheric
original_content: We went at the end of the day to catch the sunset, it was really quiet and scenic. The boats are quite old and the guy bringing us around was pushy about a tip but otherwise great experience.

author: Sonnycolin
title: Beautiful wetland reserve
original_content: Didnt go with a boat because I hate Those people agressivly asking for tips etc. Went there on my scooter and drove all the way around in. Takes about 30-45 min but really worth it!

author: Risha D
title: not as touristy
original_content: if you are looking to do a boat ride in Tam Coc, this is further away but definitely worth the drive. it's quiet and you'll even spot some critically endangered monkeys that are mainly found in Van Long.

author: Karen C
title: So peaceful and beautiful
original_content: Stunning scenery and not too many tourists either. Really pretty boat trip through the long grass, passing egrets, water fowl, butterflies and dragonflies. The grotto was lovely and when we emerged my boat lady was pointing to monkeys on the cliff but I didn't manage to see them. Still had a great time.

author: Katarina B
title: Nice boat trip
original_content: I arrived at about 4pm on a Monday afternoon and took a boat trip for about 1 hour. It was a bit shorter than usual because the water was too high to go through the cave towards the end of the route. It was very peaceful - I didn't see any other boats for most of the trip. The scenery was quite beautiful but perhaps not quite as stunning as Trang An. Unfortunately I didn't see any monkeys or many birds during my trip - however just as I was leaving, around 5pm, some flocks of birds were arriving back at the wetlands for the evening. It looked like there were other visitors who had just started their boat ride, so it seems like you can continue to get boat rides at that time, despite the official advice being that Van Long closes at 5 (maybe that's just the ticket office, but the boats continue to accept rides?)  I would recommend showing up at more like 430-445 so that you see more birdlife (this might vary a bit depending on time of year due to differing sunset times though!)
drawbacks: water was too high to go through the cave
didn't see any monkeys or many birds

author: Peter L
title: Amazing nature
original_content: I think that all of the area around Ninh Binh is a little bit under rated by western tourists. That is a shame because it is one of the most beautiful part of Vietnam. On the other hand, lack of tourist crowds is a blessing for backpackers soul .
highlights: one of the most beautiful part of Vietnam

author: spikeymires
title: Stunning and Peaceful
original_content: A sampan boat trip (2 people per boat)  around the Van Long Nature Reserve is one of the most relaxing 1 or 2 hours that you will have. You will see all kinds of flora and fauna, many fish and birds and maybe even some langur. There are lots of caves to see on your route and you may even recognise some local scenery from the latest King Kong movie.
highlights: see all kinds of flora and fauna

author: ClaireBrianNZ
title: Stunning reserve to view late afternoon
original_content: We were staying nearby at the Emeralda and walked to the Reserve very late afternoon.  Thought it would be too late for a boat ride but a lovely lady took us for an hour just on sunset. So it couldn't have been more beautiful lighting and we were virtually the only people there.  One of those magical moments you remember.

author: happyface255
title: Just lovely
original_content: Chose to do this trip as Tam Coc is reknown for pushy en route vendors plying their wares and boat operators demanding tips (not that I wouldn't have been happy to oblige. They row with their feet and that's no small feat). However as a solo traveller I can feel very pressured & stressed at times when that happens, hence my decision to go elsewhere). This was day two of a two day motorcycle tour with Toan Tours (blimmin brilliant) and the very peaceful, serene 1 hour boat ride was l. I didn't see any monkeys but in all fairness wasn't expecting to, and rush hour on the river was a delightful change from Hanoi or HCMC😄Highly recommend this trip and worth the journey out their, especially as pillion passenger on motorbike, as you get to experience the beauty of the rural landscape and local life en route.
highlights: delightful change from Hanoi or HCMC
practical_tips: go elsewhere if you're a solo traveller
experience the beauty of the rural landscape and local life en route

author: jenabaintheworld
title: nice for boating, but Tam Coc area offers more
original_content: We visited both Tam Coc and Van Long area in July.    Van Long is supposed to have many birds and monkeys, but we didn't see many birds and no monkeys.    The caves in Tam Coc are a real plus, plus pagodas/etc nearby.

author: 3166Lolo
title: Serene but all good impressions fully disappeared by aggressive sales approach and continuously asking for tip
original_content: The boat tour of 1.5 hours was relaxed and nice.In the middle of the tours, the ladies tried to sell all kind of stuff in the boat and were even a bit aggressive that we did not buy more although we did buy something.On the way back she started to ask for tip, and asked us all the time to row as she was tired. Our children were in a separate boat, and that lady behaved unkind on the way back as the children did not buy anything.After the tour there was a possibility to by photo. If you refuse they are also very aggressive.Although the cave is very nice, the total has given us a very bad feeling and is not representing the kindness of the people of Vietnam. We would not recommend.
drawbacks: Ladies were aggressive in selling stuff
practical_tips: Refuse photo purchase to avoid aggression

author: jenngreglyon
title: Beautiful
original_content: Big highlight. Very quiet and peaceful with wonderful wildlife, butterflies and stunning scenery. Highly recommended.

author: Sandriawan
title: Good, but not gonna go back
original_content: Very beautiful landscape. The boat trip was nice and memorable. Boat driver even let me do his job for a while.We entered a cave but didn't go all the way through it. Probably because it's too small.Boat trip was about 60 mins. In the end, I gave VND30.000 as a tip but he askedme for VND50.000. So the actual money you need to prepare is VND150.000.I'm okay with paying VND150.000 but with VND50.000 as a hidden fee. Well, it happens almost anywhere in Vietnam which could make the tourism fail to fulfil their potential.
drawbacks: didn't go all the way through it
highlights: boat trip was nice and memorable
boat driver even let me do his job for a while

author: Pano R
title: Heaven on Earth
original_content: OMG, there is no better word to describe this place. I love it so much. In my opinion, this place is much better than the famous Trang An as it is quieter. Local people are so honest and friendly. No other selling activities as reviewed from other places.I know people have different opinions, my view is that it is still worth to visit. Totally different feeling. If you are into photograph, definitely this place is easier to capture all beauty in the frame.My other family members visited it at about 4-5pm when all the birds/cranes flew home... spectacular view!!!
highlights: Local people are so honest and friendly
Easier to capture all beauty in the frame

author: Ollie S
title: Super chilled.
original_content: This was a really nice chilled boat journey between the limestone karsts. It might be because its not peak season but it was very quiet when we go there, barely any other tourists. I've heard this place is a little less touristic than the boat journey in the centre of Tam Coc hence why we chose this one.  You pay 50,000 for the boat at the ticket office then its a 2 minute walk away. I think for the best experience you should go in 2's so we took 2 boats since there was 4 of us.  The lady who rowed the boat didn't speak great English but this wasn't a problem, we where just happy enough to soak in the scenery and try to spot the illusive wildlife!  At one point we stopped as one of the boat guides had spotted a Delacour's langu. It took us a long time to spot it, we almost thought the guide was having us on but eventually it moved and we where able to see it.  You're also taken into a small cave.  We didn't spot much wildlife but the boat ride itself was very tranquil and calming.  We tipped our boat guides once we got off the boats. They hadn't asked but I've read it's always good practice to tip these people as they don't earn a great deal.  If you wan't maybe a less busy boat ride then this would be the one. I can't speak from experience as I haven't taken the other from the centre though.

author: Katelyn B
title: Pretty sights!
original_content: It was a nice, quiet boat ride. We really liked it especially since it was more quiet than the others that we experienced. We were lucky to spot some endemic monkeys and observe them for a while. The people working there were very nice and offered us a lot of lotus flower seeds that we could eat during the boat ride. If you're looking for adventure or more grandiose sights, this might not be for you, but we enjoyed it a lot.
practical_tips: go if you want a quiet experience

author: olga7916
title: Not worth a separate visit
original_content: Nice scenery but not worth a separate visit if you'd been to Halong bay. It's much more  genuine there. The trip was about 1,5 h, very slow and the boat lady was trying to sell us different stuff and then the ladies on the other boats were pushing everyone to buy snacks and drinks for the boat people. At the end of the trip the boat lady was quite aggressively pushing us for the tip. The trip costs 120 000/ person + 150 000/boat. You have even to buy or rent an umbrella or sun hat since it's usually very hot and sunny. Feels like it's been a way too much commercialised comparing to other places in Vietnam there we've been.
drawbacks: The boat lady was trying to sell us different stuff
The ladies on the other boats were pushing everyone to buy snacks and drinks for the boat people
The boat lady was quite aggressively pushing us for the tip
practical_tips: Dress codes: Bring umbrella or rent sun hat

author: Melbournian_Sunlover
title: A must do for a less touristy experience!
original_content: We stayed at The Emeralda, just up the road from this reserve and so we walked to it and took the boat ride offered. At 50,000 Dong per person, it was incredibly cheap. Our 69 years old rower was brilliant. She didn't miss a beat and the whole trip went for about an hour. My husband is an avid photographer and whenever she saw him trying to capture a shot, she would slow down or edge closer to what he was looking at through the lens. She pointed out the very hard to spot black and white monkeys and although there was a boat about 75 metres in front of us, she kept enough distance so that we felt like we were all alone there. It is such a beautiful, quiet, peaceful place and the scenery is stunning. We had such a good time that we decided not to do the more touristy Tam Coc and Na Trang. Van Long was perfect!
highlights: Our 69 years old rower was brilliant.
She pointed out the very hard to spot black and white monkeys

author: Peter Reynolds
title: Great row boat ride
original_content: Such a great relaxing experience being rowed along the river. The wildlife is awesome and I've never seen so many colours of dragon fly.It costs 100k doing for the boat ride. I would put plenty of sun cream on and make sure you take water as it can get mega hot with little breeze. And def take a hat. The guide couldn't speak any English but that was not a problem as he showed us everything and was really friendly and nice, even took the time to show us a fishing cage with a little crab. 10/10 would crab again.
practical_tips: put plenty of sun cream on

author: CHH-pretoria
title: Nice boat trip very relaxing
original_content: Nice boat trip - boats are very small however and two large westerners are definitely the limit and no room to move. Remember a poncho if it looks as if it may rain. pretty scenery and relaxing to travel through the lotus flowers.
practical_tips: Remember a poncho if it looks as if it may rain

author: Kelly H
title: Mind-blowing experience of a lifetime
original_content: Hard to put this experience into words. Being rowed down the river by a local woman in a traditional boat, spotting bird life in an incredible landscape just so serene. If you're lucky you'll get the chance to see what is likely to be the last viable wild population of langurs in Vietnam.
practical_tips: get the chance to see the last viable wild population of langurs

author: Space C0y0te
title: Well worth it. Super chill.
original_content: After two days of natural wonders we ended on this. Excellent experience. 100,000 dong per person ($5 usd) but make sure and tip your boat captain. Our boat dude was a really nice guy (my friend speaks Vietnamese so was able to communicate). Beautiful lake. He waded the boat so we could find lotus flowers. He took us to see a family of monkeys and a family of ducks. I thought this might be similar to Tam Coc and Trang An but it wasn't! Slightly different landscape and the caves were much larger and cooler (literally). Don't skip this.

author: 547sarinn
title: Better than Tam Coc
original_content: We were staying at the Emaralda Resort and Van Long was just a 5 minute walk so we decided to do it. But the place surely surprised us. Here's what's great about it:1) Less commercialised 2) Better looking Rice paddy fields 3) Cheaper yet more scenic 4) You get to see Langurs in their natural habitat 5) Just one cave but its darker and lower in height so you really have to dunk your way through: great experience 6) No one pestering you to buy the boatman a coke!7) The fauna is a lot better ( the Lotus plants are beautiful!)When it gets hot, the boatman rows into a dense lotus plantation and plucks out a huge leaf for you to put on as a hat Overall a much richer experience. Great ride for the photographers!It's a 90 minute ride and costs about 20000 per person. Ok to tip the boatman about 50k to 100k depending on your experience
highlights: You get to see Langurs in their natural habitat
No one pestering you to buy the boatman a coke!
The fauna is a lot better ( the Lotus plants are beautiful!)
practical_tips: Tip the boatman about 50k to 100k depending on your experience

author: TravelBug_GH
title: Van Long & Bai Dinh Pagoda
original_content: I went with my parents, sister, and brother-in-law on a tour to Van Long Nature Reserve & Bai Dinh Pagoda with HVG Travel Companion and it was absolutely great! Our guide spoke English very well and gave us a lot of information. The Van Long Nature Reserve was beautiful! It was definitely hot! The Bai Dinh Pagoda was huge! Lots of steps, but worth it.
highlights: Our guide spoke English very well
The Van Long Nature Reserve was beautiful!

author: DgSolo
title: Want a break and soak in the real Viernam , cycle through rice paddies in peace and tranquility
original_content: I decided to cycle around this area, very little traffic, you get to experience local cuisine if you chose too .  Soul cleansing cycling Through the miles of rice paddies, was very humid and hot, so a sudden downpour was so welcome, you feel like dancing in the rain as scenery is so tranquil. I did not take the boat ride and was sorry I did not, this excursion is recommended for people wanting to get away from main stream activities
drawbacks: did not take the boat ride
practical_tips: get away from main stream activities

author: Kira P
title: amazing view, 1.5 hour boat ride
original_content: we really enjoyed the boatride, it was 100.000 dong for one boat for two persons, so 50.000 each. we even saw a monkey on our way back to the „pier”! we didn't knew that the boat-paddlers expect a tip after the ride, we had nothing but 10.000 dong in our pockets and they were really angry and wanted more money. so prepare yourself with more cash than we did to spare you some uncomfortable vietnamese shoutings.
extracted_times: 100.000 dong for one boat for two persons
drawbacks: boat-paddlers expect a tip after the ride
highlights: saw a monkey on our way back

author: Elizabeth Q
title: Fascinating
original_content: Sadly we didn't have long to spend here but we took an hour's boat trip in one of the little boats rowed by a Vietnamese lady on the waterways around the limestone hills where we saw monkeys at play. Also we went through the most incredible cave with a perfect reflection in the water.
drawbacks: we didn't have long to spend here
highlights: went through the most incredible cave

author: Simone M
title: Nice!
original_content: Worth at least 3 hours to visit. I suggest to go in the afternoon in order to watch the birds coming back to the park (around 5 in April). There are different caves in the park. I recommend the first you find on the way. You need to go up to almost 500 steps but at the top the view is awesome!

author: manhchu
title: One of the best place to visit in Ninh Binh
original_content: Van Long wetland area worth a visit once you in Ninh Binhthis area was not crowded like Tam Coc or Trang An, but the landscape was beautiful once you get here you will buy a ticket to get on a sampan (the price was much lower than in Tam Coc or Trang An), the local people will take you go along the lake, where you can enjoy the water, flora and fauna, if you were lucky you can see a school of birds or even some special lungars, they jumping on the mountain, the landscape here was as beautiful as in Tam Coc, there was river surround the moutain, the locals will take you to a cave there you can see some stalactites falling from the cave roof with different size and formation, they were very beauty.The total time to finish the trip was almost 2 hours, this place was one of some place the film Kong skull island was make a footagein general this was one of the best places to visit in Ninh Binh (avoid crowded area)I totaly recommended to visit
highlights: enjoy the water, flora and fauna
see a school of birds or even some special lungars
practical_tips: go to Van Long wetland area

author: HappyBingo
title: Serene boat ride lovely scenery
original_content: Our 2nd boat ride after the one at Trang An. Compared to Trang An where our family of 5, 2 boys 6 & 3 plus Grandma, could fit on 1 boat, at Van Long Nature Reserve we had to split to 2 boats. Again, beautiful scenery as we slowing drifted along. At the turning point, we enter a cave and u-turn back out, not as dramatic as the caves at Trang An. Our young boys enjoyed helping with the rowing. A relaxing boat ride through stunning landscape.
highlights: young boys enjoyed helping with the rowing

author: michel p
title: this was cool to do
original_content: very interesting tour  to do on that Van long Nature reserve, local people that row boat with their feet, cave to see, very relaxing and beautiful to see.

author: Aussiebeccyc
title: A must!
original_content: Unspoilt area. Stunning landscape. Away from the large crowds. Grab your bike and ride along the reserve and be sure to do the boat trip to the cave.
practical_tips: grab your bike and ride along the reserve
do the boat trip to the cave

author: Katherine B
title: Amazing senery
original_content: This was a stop on our 1 week tour in Northern Vietnam. We took an hour long boat ride through the marsh land around the beautiful rock formations. The boat guides were amazing, pointing out different animals and trying to use the French they knew to interact with us. Our little one (2yrs) wanted to change boats a few times so they stopped and lined up the boats so he could swap boats and sit with dad.

author: Kanaena
title: Nice way to relax
original_content: This is a good way to relax and maybe a good way to end your time in Nihn Bihn. Its quiet, a bit out of the way and not as busy as the trang an grottos. We did a lot of cycling, its a must to see the beauty of the rice paddies and karsts. So this boat ride was a good was to let our sore muscles relax.
practical_tips: cycle through the rice paddies and karsts

author: Josine T
title: Loved this boat ride with the 'surprise' cave!!
original_content: We very much enjoyed the tranquility of this 2.5 hour boat ride through the wetlands. Beautiful scenery, quiet, with only a few other small boats gliding along. We only saw some birds, no other wildlife, but that did not matter much, since the environment was so gorgeous. The biggest surprise was when we entered a fairly long cave, went right through it, did a large loop and back through the cave again...pitch black and a little spooky but very exciting.... absolutely worth a visit!

author: B f
title: Van Long water land
original_content: It's very  special land -mountain - water area. Because it's reserved land, it's wild with many special type of monkey leaving in the cocky mountains. It spectacularly beautiful in July - August when wild lotus blossom open. It's also good place to view many thousand of birds flocking back to the pond late winter afternoon.
highlights: view many thousand of birds flocking back

author: shesgottogo
title: Go at dusk or dawn to see the langur monkeys
original_content: Go at dusk or dawn to see the langur monkeys. We went in at 5 pm (Feb) and had just the two boats of us, saw plenty of storks and  Langurs on top of the Karst!
highlights: saw plenty of storks and Langurs

author: Carolyn A
title: Beautiful setting
original_content: We cycled through villages and were then rowed across the still and shallow waters to the caves in the limestone rocks.  The boats are very flimsy and the boat trip very slow . Interesting trip

author: Garrett B
title: Off the beaten track in Ninh Binh
original_content: My interest preferred somewhere really authentic and off the beaten path places in Ninh Binh rather than the normal route travelers else go on. So I just had a wonderful day with the guide Ducivan through Ultimate Hanoi Adventures which organized a guided private tour for me. And Van Long nature reserve was our choice. By the 2 hour drive from Hanoi (85 km far from Hanoi). Upon arrival, we spent a 1.5 hour boat ride, here I got to catch many birds and rare monkeys and got stunning views of landscape and rural life. Along with a river, water was so clear that it looks like a mirror reflecting mountains, grottoes and the sky and then we cycle around Keng Ga village before enjoying the hot spring bath here. This Van Long nature reserve is completely untouched. It was fun and great.
highlights: stunning views of landscape and rural life
caught many birds and rare monkeys

author: Merlouis
title: Wonderful experience
original_content: Was rowed along for a two hour trip up this lake to see the beautiful limestone hills. Very relaxing. Had to deal with a photographer and hawkers selling snacks and souvenirs but did not detract too much. Paddled mostly by using their feet which was fascinating in itself. Very busy - perhaps too many tourists.
highlights: paddled mostly by using their feet

author: Simon317
title: Not a must!!!!!!!!!
original_content: If you plan to visit Halong Bay a visit to Van Long nature reserve is not needed. Nice Limestone formations and caves but this does not justify the trip from Hanoi.
drawbacks: does not justify the trip from Hanoi
practical_tips: Do not visit if you plan to visit Halong Bay

author: onemoreholiday
title: This was special
original_content: This was one of the best experiences in our two weeks in Vietnam.  The wetlands are viewed by a two hour row in small boats the local people do the rowing deciding their time between this tourist activity and farming you are taken at a leisurely pace through the wetlands stoping occasionally to see the wildlife - mainly long tailed monkeys the vegetation is interspersed with vertical rock formations reminiscent of How Long bay and at one point you go into a low (but not too low) cave tunnel.  The best thing is that unlike How Long bay this place is not over run with tourists so you can enjoy the peace and tranquillity of the place.Well worth discovering before enforce everyone else does.

author: Bart N
title: Serene and beautiful
original_content: This place is a bit further away from Tam coc than the other boat tour places. Which makes it much better in my opinion since there won't be hundreds of tourists waiting in line to get into a boat. Its about a 17 km drive on a motorbike using the highway (really boring) The entrance fee is much lower. We payed 100k in total for 2 people including the boat (excl the tip ofcourse) We had a lovely lady rowing us through these beautiful waters. She spoke little english but was full enthousiasme and made every effort to make it a great boat trip (stopped when she saw me raise the camera to make a picture etc) Because of this and her keen eye sight we spend about 2 hours on the boat and had the place to our selves after the other boats had over taken us. Coming back to her keen eye sight we saw about 8 of the monkeys, even though the other groups had missed them :) really awesome. We ofc took a few pictures with er at the end and gave her a 100k tip for her great efforts/ service. Highly recommend going to this place if you're like me and don't want to be in a group of 40 other tourists.
drawbacks: hundreds of tourists waiting in line
really boring drive on the highway
highlights: lovely lady rowing us through beautiful waters
practical_tips: tip the rower for great service

author: worldtraveler189
title: Peaceful, quiet, beautiful
original_content: Beautiful!  Such a break from the craziness of Vietnam.  Amazing boat ride into nature.  Many birds, a chance to see some VERY rare monkeys, lots of water life.  I recommend a bike along the dyke for many views before or after.  We rented bikes at the Emeralda resort (we were guests).  Really nice.
practical_tips: Rent bikes at the Emeralda resort
Take a bike along the dyke for many views

author: shirleymtravels
title: Delacour’s langur
original_content: This was the second boat trip we did in the Ninh Binh area. It is difficult to decide which one was the best they were quite different and both spectacular.There were just the two of us in the boat on this trip.It is a much quieter trip than the Trang An trip.The scenery is again breathtaking.Highlight of the trip was we stopped and saw a group of the endangered Delacour’s langurs. It really was amazing.
highlights: saw a group of the endangered Delacour’s langurs

author: Mr9xx
title: Lovely Cathedral
original_content: Charming old architecture with a serene atmosphere, beautifully combining traditional Vietnamese and French influences. A place worth visiting.
highlights: beautifully combining traditional Vietnamese and French influences

author: abra n
title: Sunny day exploring the stone-church!
original_content: Amazing church with wonderful architect. We have learnt a lot about the history of Vietnam and Catholic community which gave us some insights of the little country by the East-Sea (words of my guide).
highlights: learnt a lot about the history of Vietnam and Catholic community

author: Alessandro S
title: Nice surprise
original_content: Visit the complex which is very large. The Cathedral was built during the colonial period (1892) and the works for its construction were personally supervised by Father Peter Tran Luc, whose tomb is located near the structure.In 1954 Ho Chi Minh's communists occupied the area and ordered the Catholics to leave. As a result, the cathedral was closed and abandoned for several years and during the war it was seriously damaged by American bombing.Today it represents a point of reference for the numerous Catholic Christians present in this area of the country
drawbacks: The cathedral was closed and abandoned for several years
The cathedral was seriously damaged by American bombing
highlights: A point of reference for the numerous Catholic Christians present in this area of the country

author: Ron
title: Nice Church
original_content: Great history place for Catholic tradidions, French Church in the North of Vietnam. If you go to Ninh Binh, must visit for Christian
extracted_spaces: French Church in the North of Vietnam
highlights: Great history place for Catholic traditions
practical_tips: If you go to Ninh Binh, must visit

author: Joyce S
title: One of a kind Asian-Western cathedral
original_content: If you love heritage buildings, architecture and visiting cathedrals, this place is not to be missed. It is 2 hours away from Hanoi city, peaceful place to explore about 1 hour especially if you love photography.

author: kellyandrewtomas
title: oversized church in undersized town
original_content: As a fairly small nondescript town in Vietnam you wouldn't expect Phat Diem to have such an impressive cathedral. It was both the size and style that kept me wandering the grounds for about 1 hour. While I was there it is peaceful. Overall I would say it has been maintained well with only a few areas needing repair and no rubbish.

author: Quang Kiet Le
title: Beautiful blend of Vietnamese culture and Western religion
original_content: It took us more than 2 hours travelling from Hanoi. Phat Diem Cathedral actually consisted of one big church and 4 smaller ones surrounding. The churches were beautifully blended of the traditional Vietnamese culture and architecture and the Western religion reflecting in every single corner. Highly recommended to register a short tour with the sister at the Information Centre to understand more about the history.
highlights: beautifully blended of traditional Vietnamese culture and architecture
practical_tips: register a short tour with the sister at the Information Centre

author: srvctraveler
title: Fascinating fusion of Chinese and Catholic traditions.
original_content: Great architecture and a fascinating history giving insight into the role of the French and the Catholic Church in this part of Vietnam.

author: Gustave S
title: Worth the detour if you like architecture but ...
original_content: The place feels serene if not in desolation.  Only one of the four chapel is still in use, the others have been converted to what seems to be classes.  You are free to roam the area which is a nice way to visit at your own pace.  The grounds are nice but the buildings are in need of tender love and care (TLC).Most display a serious amount of grime and a good power washer would do wonders.  Still a nice place to see but I fear the future will not be kind to it.The interior of the cathedral is also very dusty, the golden leaves and ornaments are not maintained.  It seems like they don’t bother with maintaining the cathedral at all.In my opinion they should charge a fee for entrance except for mass and locals and take better care of the buildings.I am glad I went to see it, gave to the maintenance box but I wish the Church would take better care of it.People like to see historical buildings, give them a better experience so more people will want to come and visit them.
drawbacks: buildings are in need of tender love and care (TLC)
display a serious amount of grime
interior of the cathedral is also very dusty
highlights: nice way to visit at your own pace
practical_tips: charge a fee for entrance except for mass and locals
take better care of the buildings

author: FrankSteve
title: A Place Between Heaven and Earth
original_content: Visiting the cathedral was an unforgettable highlight of our trip to Vietnam. The architecture is stunning, the atmosphere peaceful, and the gardens beautiful. The structures and grounds exude a vibrant and unique history. A blending of European and Vietnamese design, with pagoda style roofs, the cathedral was designed in 1892 by Father Tran Luc, a Vietnamese priest. Graham Greene featured the cathedral in a memorable scene of The Quiet American. We spent several hours exploring the place, in awe of everything we saw, and will surely return to Vietnam to see the cathedral again.

author: Carla Christina
title: Very Beautiful - Worth the Visit
original_content: It may be further away from all the other attractions but definitely worth the visits if you are interested in the olden buildings. The architecture is very unique and the scenery is lovely. I would recommend to choose a cooler day to visit as the sun can be quite harsh in the hot summer months.
practical_tips: choose a cooler day to visit

author: Sunny K
title: Mix of European and Vietnamese Architecture
original_content: Its really beautiful and well preserved! A unique blend of European and Vietnamese Architecture and not to be missed if you are in Ninh Binh or TamCoc. It is built with pagoda type roofs in traditional Vietnamese temple architecture.The Cathedral is big and there are also small churches in the same complex. Some are not used and some are still being used. Its 35 km from TamCoc and can be easily reached on motorbike. Just follow Google Map.
highlights: unique blend of European and Vietnamese Architecture
practical_tips: can be easily reached on motorbike

author: planetawdrodze
title: It was more than I've expected
original_content: This cathedral is just amazing. It was far more what ive expected. If you have time to come here - do it. We took a motorbike from Ninh Binh and got there, see cathedral and came back.
practical_tips: take a motorbike from Ninh Binh

author: girlgirl66
title: Beautiful architecture, large grounds, Vietnamese influence
original_content: I could see the toll of time on the stone walls of all the buildings here and I marvel at how it remains strong over the years. The carvings are so deep and intricate that they stand out at night. The interior has a lot of wood elements and is obviously influenced by Vietnamese compared to St Joseph’s Cathedral in Hanoi Old Quarter. I also like the large grounds that appears linked to what seemed like a community house and also how the faith had spilled over into what appears to be a lake with statue of worship in the middle. Everything is so wonderful and lovely here. I strongly recommend tourists to walk around the Kim Son District that is surrounding this beautiful place of worship.
extracted_spaces: St Joseph's Cathedral in Hanoi Old Quarter
highlights: stone walls of all the buildings remain strong over the years
carvings are so deep and intricate that they stand out at night
large grounds with a community house and a lake with a statue of worship
practical_tips: walk around the Kim Son District

author: Peter V
title: A stunning monument
original_content: This cathedral is a stunning combination of sino vietnanese styke mixed with gothic. Itbiscan enormousvcomplex. FathervSix ( sau) started it. Itbgained world renown being described in graham greenebs ThecQuietvAmerican and was also filmed. For rc beliversveven an extra must see. We regard thos on par with another fatastic cathedral that of so kien, formerly khe sonbetween hanoi and ninh binh. That is in gothoc style, built in 1852,finished 1882 andvis mentioned in thevtravel exploitsvodvdrvhocquerd. Both mustvsee forvhidtoryband architecture buffs as well as rc believers.
extracted_spaces: so kien, formerly khe sonbetween hanoi and ninh binh
highlights: stunning combination of sino vietnamese style mixed with gothic

author: Elisabeth K
title: Worth the long way
original_content: The way from Tam Coc to Phat Diem by motobike takes quite a while (1h), but it's totally worth it!! We enjoyed walking through the cathedral's area... many little chapels. It's a quiet place, only with some people visiting. Nearby we found a cute coffeeshop that serves great vietnamese coffee and mangoshake!

author: Daoni Nguyen
title: Unique architecture and peaceful environment
original_content: The architecture is amazing (mix of western and eastern). This site is the capital of catholicism in Vietnam. The space is very open and there’s a nice garden with statues.
highlights: a mix of western and eastern

author: BobsWorth1
title: Very nice place to visit
original_content: I visited today and it is well worth a visit if you are in Ninh Binh. You can take the number 2 bus from Ninh Binh bus station (Ben xe Ninh Binh) which is located about halfway between the train station and the centre of town. It only costs 25000 VND each way. No need to buy a ticket in the station, just pay the conductor on the bus. Journey time to Phat Diem is around 45 mins - 1 hour depending on the traffic.The bus will drop you off at a junction on the main road (Duong 10), outside a large yellow and black coloured electronics shop called The Gioi Di Dong). Look down the street to the side of the shop and you’ll see the cathedral at the bottom. To get the bus back to Ninh Binh, just stand opposite the electronics shop and flag it down like you would a taxi. Free entry and there are plenty of cafes in and around the area.
practical_tips: pay the conductor on the bus
flag it down like a taxi

author: jaypep1
title: Worth a Visit
original_content: I liked this place. The cathedral was quite impressive with its wooden beams. Unfortunately you can't take photos inside. The cathedral is surrounded by four smaller churches and a stone chapel. There is also a statue of Jesus Christ on an island at the front of the cathedral. Various statues and grottoes. Cost: FREE. At the back of the cathedral is a museum but it was closed when I was there. Not many tourists or touts this time of year. The best photos are for myself.
extracted_spaces: island at the front of the cathedral

author: jewel838c
title: Off the beaten path but worth a visit
original_content: Phat Diem Cathedral is slightly off the beaten path and takes about 30 minutes drive from Ninh Binh.  I think it is  definitely worth the visit. The architecture is unique - you could call it a chur-goda because it it had architectural elements that made it a pagoda more than a church.  But it was beautiful nevertheless. Some of the side chapels had some gaudy lights but if if you look past that you can still see the uniqueness of the Asian motifs in the original decoration, wood carving  and stone carving. When doing our research we stumbled on a website that described the Catholic churches and cathedrals in Ninh Binh and the neighboring province of Nam Dinh.  Some of these churches were beautiful Gothic, European style churches.  Unfortunately we didn't have time to visit so decided that we could only see Phat Diem Cathedral for this trip.  But I think a pilgrimage visit to the other churches in Nam Dinh would be well worth it in the future.
highlights: Asian motifs in the original decoration, wood carving and stone carving
practical_tips: pilgrimage visit to the other churches in Nam Dinh would be well worth it in the future

author: wildfirejc
title: Go for Mass, Nothing else worth it
original_content: The whole complex has an air of neglect. However the mass was nice. Fortunately I am Roman Catholic so even if the service was in Vietnamese, I enjoyed it. Lots of people though - very noisy. The stone temple was rather neglected.

author: Hung N
title: Peaceful Historical Place
original_content: Because we stay near Tam Coc, so it's really far to come here. Nevertheless, it would be wonderful to visit and study about memorable historical period of Catholic in Vietnam.This place is not big, not taking much time to go around, but with the peaceful atmosphere, just sit down and enjoy the place is good enough to us
highlights: memorable historical period of Catholic in Vietnam

author: Pham G
title: It's a historical place
original_content: It's a historical and religious place, that is not commercialized. There are several cathedrals in one place and all are well-maintained.

author: Buiduong
title: Biggest and beautiful cathedral in north Vietnam
original_content: I visited this place when travelling to Ninh Binh. Our group passed by it and deciced to stop to visit. We were very interested in the ancient architecture of this cathedral and spacious area,...Even it is too hot outside but when we step inside this, we feel we are in fridge, indeed

author: Phuong V
title: Nice Cathedral to visit in cool weather, not Summer
original_content: This is peacefull place for us to visit, we went there everytime we go to Ninh Binh :-), for hot weather, it d better not go there at noon as it's so unpleasant because of the heat, surrounded is stone, so you will feel headeach after few minutes.we come there when the weather is cool ( not in June to August). Have a nice time there.
practical_tips: go there when the weather is cool

author: HappyBingo
title: Unique architecture
original_content: We visited Phat Diem Cathedral as part of a tour of Ninh Binh. It was a rainy day but that didn't diminish the uniqueness of the architecture. A mix of East meets West, we were also interested in the story of Father Six who helped build this place. Interesting.

author: rajucnair
title: 16th century cathedral
original_content: Very peaceful place. well maintained cathedral where even now mass takes place everyday. special mass on sunday

author: Josine T
title: Very nice buildings and worth a visit!
original_content: Beautiful stone buildings to have a look at and grtounds to admire. Very different to other religious buildings seen in Vietnam and worth a visit!
highlights: different to other religious buildings seen in Vietnam

author: jakehands78
title: A pleasant surprise!
original_content: This isn't your average Catholic Cathedral. Once you arrive you will be amazed how Father Six constructed it fuzing both eastern and western beliefs into one. The chapel to the left of the cathedral shows a clear example of this with a Ying Yang symbol covered by the heart of christ. It's worth getting a tour guide to show you more fascinating details of this cathedral. If you walk through the gates, on the right hand side theres a small reception. Inside you'll find tour guide who can speak English, Italian or french. We were very happy with our tour and couldn't believe it was completely free,though we did give a donation at the end.

author: Đôi Lời M
title: Vatican in Vietnam
original_content: It is one of the most beautiful and ancient churchs in Vietnam. It has unique architecture, linking between Easterm and Westerm architecture.

author: Hoàng Yen
title: nice structures
original_content: I went there on Sunday January here i had occassion to see the Sunday Pray.I went around to understand the history and structures

author: Mathieu L
title: Worth the detour for a picture
original_content: The cathedral is beautiful for it's special architecture that we are not used to see for a christian building.  It has an asian style of architecture which make it unique.  There is nothing to do there but take some pictures and hang around the site.

author: Alexis D
title: Stunning
original_content: I love this place. Have been there 4 or 5 times already, and I find it absolutely incredible. If you like architecture, dont miss it: this mix of Asian and European style is unique in the world. The pillars only, made on ironwood, deserve a visit. And the trip from Ninh Binh reveals a beautiful landscape along a canal.

author: Jodi R
title: Quite spectacular
original_content: Make sure you don't visit at mass time because they close the tower and you won't be able to visit the top of the church.  It is an interesting place to visit, particularly if you are Catholic.
drawbacks: won't be able to visit the top of the church

author: T S
title: Spectacular Craftmanship
original_content: Unbelievable woodworking skills employed at this cathedral. We spent about an hour walking around. Was definitely the highlight of our tour that day.

author: Ryan Cao
title: Stunning destination
original_content: I was here for a whole morning to discover the architecture and stories behind those constructions. You definitely need a local guide to tell you about those things. There are some restricted areas that's you couldn't visit because of the religious regulations. Hope you have a good trips.

author: lavasi
title: Beautiful world heritage
original_content: Knowing it's an old church, I didn't expect to see a historic place that is stunning in architechture, particularly the main timber structure, built in the early colonial period.The surrounding is also well preserved, only the eyesore things are the colorful banners hanging here and there.
drawbacks: colorful banners hanging here and there

author: KevanEastYorkshire
title: Interesting Place
original_content: Spent a number of hours with a guide walking around the Cathedral. Seeing the bell from close up (gate/door opened by a nun) was good.Lots to see in around the site although its a bit of a drive from Ninh Binh.
drawbacks: a bit of a drive from Ninh Binh
highlights: Seeing the bell from close up
Lots to see in around the site

author: Strabo
title: Fascinating
original_content: It is rather out of the way but we enjoyed it - to see the melding of eastern and western architecture of the cathedral and its surrounding buildings. Cannot be compared with the European cathedrals or duomos in terms of scale, grandeur. But if we consider it was built in a very poor third world country then, it is indeed very unique and an architectural feat for the time.
highlights: melding of eastern and western architecture

author: Peter C
title: A surprise cathedral
original_content: Although quite a long way from Ninh Binh town it is worth visiting and perhaps combining with a visit to another site. We combined it with Mru Caves and hired a car and driver. The cathedral has very unusual architecture and looks more like a temple than a church. We visited at Christmas so it was attractively decked out with lots of lights and cribs.  It's connections with Graham Greene add to the interest.
highlights: attractively decked out with lots of lights and cribs
practical_tips: combine with a visit to another site

author: DevonCatLady
title: Very glad to have seen the interior
original_content: The interior of this cathedral is quite unexpected, unless you have seen photos.  I had, and so I turned up with my tripod, only to discover no photography whatsoever is permitted, even though we were the only people there.  It was quite a long drive to get there from where we were staying, and although I am very glad to have seen it, you probably need to be visiting something else in the area to make it worth while.
practical_tips: consider visiting with other attractions in the area

author: pinkdisguise
title: Interesting architecture
original_content: Found this to be an unexpected highlight of our trip to the Ninh Binh area. We really only came because we had a few hours to spend before our train left and Ninh Binh itself is void of anything interesting for tourists.Unlike most other churches in Vietnam, Phat Diem does not pretend to look like a copy of the Notre Dame cathedral. Instead, it is much more like an Asian temple. Beside the main cathedral building, there is a separate bell tower, plus 4 smaller chapels and 2 grottoes representing Bethlehem and Lourdes. There's not a lot of written information (found out later that at the church shop there's a little guid book), but the place looks beautiful and was a delight to visit.It takes around 45 min from the centre of Ninh Binh to get there (45km); we ordered a private car through our hotel. There are also tour packages available which include a visit to the cathedral with a visit to one of the nature parks in the area.
drawbacks: void of anything interesting for tourists
not a lot of written information
practical_tips: order a private car through your hotel

author: GohYH93
title: Old catholic church
original_content: Visited this old Catholic church of 1876-1899AD. Surprised by the large Catholic population in Kim Son. Ninh Binh.Now church is still in used by the locals. But applying for world UNESCO heritage.VERY peaceful place with cool weather now.Do get there early so to enter the cathedral.

author: arapuni
title: Interesting blend of Asian European Architecture
original_content: This complex incorporates Asian architecture very skilfully with european cathedral architecture to create a very pleasing style.  The complex was quiet and peaceful, although that may have been because we were there late in the afternoon.  The main cathedral is high ceilinged and one can visualize a european cathedral.  The smaller chapels in the complex look more like temples.  The statuary contained depictions of saints, but also included asian symbols.
practical_tips: visit late in the afternoon for a peaceful experience

author: TravelPause
title: Harmonic blend of architecture and religions
original_content: Perhaps it was the time of day but we arrived towards sunset and really enjoyed our perambulations around the cathedral and its many smaller buildings. (I'm not sure that it does shut at 5pm - comment in earlier post -  because we were still wandering around at the time of evening bell ringing). Intriguing blend of western and eastern architecture, including statues adorning rooftops which celebrated both religions. The  main cathedral is an impressive size, the interior finished in wood including the 52 massive single tree (yellow poincianas) trunks used for its main pillars. Locals were praying and outside a family was making an offering and prayers at one of the grottoes - once again a peculiar mixture of Asian and western religious artefacts. Walking around we did find plaques on inner walls explaining more of the history. When the massive bell in the tower chimed evensong it was beautiful... Sometimes the beauty of places like this can't be absorbed and appreciated in a 10 minute skip-around... and there's no point comparing them to their European counterparts either...have to remember its a blend of eastern simplicity and western reverence...take your time to observe the details in the carvings, the woodwork, the anomalies of east meets west. Watch the locals who are visiting it as their church. Sit and ponder... I'm not religious but this place had a really calming  energy..
highlights: Intriguing blend of western and eastern architecture
Impressive size of the main cathedral
practical_tips: Take your time to observe the details in the carvings, the woodwork, the anomalies of east meets west
Watch the locals who are visiting it as their church

author: BensonYap
title: Interesting architecture
original_content: The wood carvings in one of the chapel is exquisite. The cathedral and chapels are all relatively well-preserved. Interesting to see the blend of Far East and European designs on the buildings. Worth a trip from Ninh Binh!
highlights: blend of Far East and European designs
practical_tips: Worth a trip from Ninh Binh!

author: Mirek a Petra N
title: Surprising place
original_content: It is around 30 km from ninh binh, it is popular site for Vietnamese people to visit. It looks like temple but is old Catholic Church with great chapels, wood carvings and big belltower. We went there on motorbike taxi.

author: Andrew P
title: Not worth the 35 km trip out
original_content: Maybe it's just because I've traveled through Europe and have seen lots of churches, but there was nothing spectacular about seeing this place in my opinion, especially given that its out of the way and all you can really do is look at the outside of the buildings, which aren't necessarily in the greatest shape. 15 mins and you're done for something incredibly mediocre.

author: Anna M
title: Impressive Cathedral!
original_content: It is quite far from Ninh Binh (28km) but it was a nice trip. We were the only tourists there. Due to that fact some people actually walked up to us and wanted to take photos which was funny. the cathedral itself was very impressive, a mix between european and asian decoration.
highlights: the cathedral itself was very impressive
a mix between european and asian decoration

author: Txell D
title: Little treasure
original_content: If you are in Ninh Binh, just go! Peaceful and delicated cathedral, diferent of other cathedrals we have seen in Vietnam. A little treasure. We went there by motorbike from Tam Coc. Check route and you can go and come back by diferent routes and enjoy the countryside.
practical_tips: Go by motorbike from Tam Coc
Check route and go and come back by different routes

author: Vnvet68
title: A big part of Vietnamese history here........
original_content: Vietnam has a long history of Catholic influence due to the French colonolization. It is interesting to travel in the Vietnamese countryside and see enclaves of Christians scattered here and there. Phat Diem is a great example of this. A very interesting stop in Vietnam's vast and varied history.
highlights: interesting stop in Vietnam's vast and varied history

author: Georgina W
title: Interesting mix of East meets West in Cathedral architecture.
original_content: A surprising number of churches,including Phat Diem Cathedral,clustered in one area.A must to visit for those interested in church architecture,and history. A large complex of Tower and Chapels,and large wooden Cathedral.A tour of complex can be arranged,by English speaking guide,eager to"brush up"on their English skills. Will need transport from Ninh Binh,but picturesque drive.
practical_tips: Will need transport from Ninh Binh

author: shaynamin
title: Breathtaking
original_content: Amazing architecture, would definitely recommend a visit for any who like ornate or interesting buildings. Guided tours are available to give you an insight into the history of the cathedral.

author: Patrick T
title: Great
original_content: It's really a unique cathedral. They after 5 chapels surrounding the cathedral. One of the must see chapel is know as the stone chapel. The chapel is made of satin all around from floor up. The cathedral is facing a lake and inside is make by wood. Truly beautiful. Must see!!! author: E3242OSrobm

author: Danzelho
title: A must for architecture and history lover. Go!
original_content: Speeding off to Phat Diem Cathedral on a motorbike which is located in the Kim Son district. It was refreshing riding without much traffic and without any rules. Even if there are any rules on the road, it is pretty much dictate by the user. I have to agree that the noises from the excessive horn are terrible but it does serve as a great way to signal the driver in front that you are passing through or making a turn. It wasn't a very complicated journey, as we were travelling on one straight dusty road most of the time with farmlands, houses or catholic cemeteries by the side, however i am very certain we will be lost if we didn't have a google map. Take Nguyen Cong Tru Road (QL10). It is a straight route, and you will be spending most of your time riding on this route. Approximately 24km later, you will face a T or should i say Y junction with a river in front of you. At this junction turn right and carry riding on QL10. 3km later After make a final right turn into a small lane with a few potholes, and you will reach the compound of the Phat Diem Cathedral. The total distance from Ninh Binh train station to the cathedral is less than 30km. If you are riding or driving on your own, it will be good to save a offline google map since the entrance to the cathedral is a small road and you might miss it. However the cathedral is very famous in this district so ask around if you are unsure and i believe the locals will be able to point you correct way.The cathedral looks impressive and took 24 years to built, with the exterior totally in concrete and the interior made of wood. The cathedral exhibit a unique mix of Christian gothic style of architectural and Vietnamese pagoda structure. I was pretty surprised when i walk past one of the chapel and heard people chanting instead of singing hymns. Incense was also used as a form of worshiped in the cathedral which was predominantly an Asian tradition. It was an interesting mix of religion and culture. We were in Ninh Binh for one full day and we decided to visit Tam Coc, Mua cave in the morning and Phat Diem in the afternoon. If you are on a tight schedule, maybe it will not be wise for you to visit Phat Diem Cathedral due to the long distance. I have read quite a bit about the cathedral hence decided to head there. If you love unique architecture, history and riding on the outskirt of a town. Go, you will enjoy it. Just plan one whole afternoon for it so that you wouldn't have to rush and still have time to reach back before the sun set. Do take note that The Phat Diem Cathedral close at 5.00pm local time.I have included the cathedral website in the tripadvisor review, if you are Interested to know more about it. Not sure if they will show it. Drop me a message if you need more information. Cheers.

interesting mix of religion and culture
unique architecture, history and riding on the outskirt of a town
practical_tips: ask around if you are unsure
plan one whole afternoon for it

author: Jamshaid F
title: Spiritual Beauty and serenity
original_content: Stone Church, as locals called it, is a grand structure of its own class located in Kim Sơn District of Ninh Bình Province. Construction is vastly made of stone and enormous wooden pillars are carved out of single trees. It was cloudy and drizzling when we visited this marvelous monument. The wonderful weather and overall ambience further added to its silent beauty.  Phat Diem Cathedral is typical example of European structure, though it was designed by a local priest, known as Father Sau, in eighteen century. The Cathedrals was not untouched by country’s resistance against a foreign aggression. A Bombing in 1972 devastated a major portion of the church while the Cathedrals got tilted. Despite of the war the restoration work was carried on straight away and damaged was undone.

author: hugo64
title: Piece of history
original_content: About 30 mins from Ninh Binh through a part of Vietnam that seems totally untouristed.I think our driver and guide also found it interesting as it`s not really part of the tourist trail.Phat Diem  Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral built of stone but with a beautiful wooden roof. It is a mixture of European and Vietnamese, built using traditional Vietnamese temple architecture. It was built of stone and wood in 24 years. There were also several other chapels and a shrine of the Virgin Mary. Father Six, the man responsible for its construction, while devout in his Catholicism, had a great sense of Vietnamese tradition and culture. It was he who ensured Phat Diem Cathedral was distinctly Vietnamese in character. He was central both to the architecture and engineering of the project.In 1951, Graham Greene stood from the cathedral bell-tower and witnessed raging battles between Ho Chi Minh’s Viet Minh forces and French colonial forces. He included the experience in his famous novel, The Quiet American.   In 1953, French shells hit the structure damaging the roof and 1972, American bombs fell across the complex flattening one of the surrounding chapels and severely damaging the main cathedral structure. The local community has rallied to repair the cathedral and repairs are still going on.The number of churches in this area is surprising and many of them wouldn`t look out of place in Paris although the Cathedral would!
drawbacks: severely damaging the main cathedral structure
American bombs fell across the complex
highlights: mixture of European and Vietnamese architecture

title: Too many people
original_content: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital is certainly an interesting place from a historical point of view and is worth a visit if you are in Ninh Binh. Unfortunately, however, our experience was strongly affected by the huge number of people present.There are so many organized groups, practically all with their own guide in tow, and at times it even becomes difficult to move in the spaces and get close to the temples. The amount of people is truly impressive and, in my opinion, makes you lose almost completely the charm of the place.It is a shame especially because some of the buildings are places of worship, but with hundreds of people entering and exiting continuously, guides talking and groups crowding, it is very difficult to perceive any atmosphere of contemplation or religiosity.To this are added numerous vendors who try to offer practically everything and who, in some cases, we found rather insistent.In conclusion, Hoa Lư is certainly interesting and important for understanding the history of Vietnam, but mass tourism has reached such a level as to seriously compromise the visiting experience. Probably, by managing to arrive very early or at a less crowded time, the feeling would be completely different.
drawbacks: difficult to move in the spaces and get close to the temples
mass tourism has reached such a level as to seriously compromise the visiting experience
highlights: interesting place from a historical point of view
worth a visit if you are in Ninh Binh
important for understanding the history of Vietnam
practical_tips: visit at a less crowded time

author: PavalikaV
title: Past Glory
original_content: One can give a pass. Nothing spectacular, but for the large complex, though fairly neatly maintained. Indeed if one is TamCoc area, better option would be to do the circuit of Trang An boat ride, then the Bai Dinh Pagoda, Hao Lu Ancient Capital or just take rest in the afternoon; head up to Hao Lu Old Town, which is very similar to Hoi An in its environment.
practical_tips: do the circuit of Trang An boat ride
head up to Hao Lu Old Town

author: Mr9xx
title: Hoa Lu
original_content: The site features two main temples dedicated to King Le Dai Hanh and King Dinh Bo Linh. While some of the older structures may be less visually appealing, it is still a worthwhile place to visit.
drawbacks: some of the older structures may be less visually appealing

author: TravelingFoodie
title: Nothing special
original_content: We visited Hoa Lu Ancient Capital and found it to be an interesting and atmospheric historical site. The temples are well kept and set among limestone scenery, creating a calm, traditional feel. It’s easy to walk around and learn about Vietnam’s early history. Not the most dramatic attraction in the area, but a worthwhile cultural stop in Ninh Binh.
drawbacks: Not the most dramatic attraction in the area

author: Emily
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Very well maintained & preserved.Beautiful shrines & temples. Limited written information, but we had a guide to fill in the gaps.Did get quite busy, and be prepared if wearing revealing clothes you will need to cover up with provided fabric.
practical_tips: Be prepared if wearing revealing clothes

author: みるく
title: It's a laid-back ancient city.
original_content: Chan An and Hoa Loo came here for an optional tour. It was fun to ride a little bike before coming here. This one was well maintained and easy to walk. It's hot with not much sun, so parasols, hats and drinks are essential.

author: lilybt
title: Taste of Ancient Capitals
original_content: Major destinations that can be visited on day tours from Hanoi are "Ha Long Bay Cruise" and "Ninh Binh". The former is a natural heritage site famous for its landscape of steep islands in the bay, while the latter is a mixed heritage site consisting of landscapes and ruins of ancient capitals, also known as "Haron Bay on Land". While many visitors to either may choose the prominent former, they chose the latter because of the flexibility of time and itinerary, and were caught up in the unusual occurrence of being separated from the guide at the arrival point of the river cruise.The first stop is the Hoa Lu ruins, where the Đồng dynasty briefly established the capital before the transfer of the capital to Tân Long, and almost no original structures remain, but it has a unique landscape as a historical heritage.
drawbacks: being separated from the guide at the arrival point of the river cruise
highlights: unique landscape as a historical heritage
practical_tips: consider visiting Ninh Binh for flexibility

author: GhostofMars
title: Disappointing. Could be so much more.
original_content: This could be so much better. The temple they have is good enough, but unfortunately there’s not much else other than an open field. There was a small museum but it only had a few items. They really could turn this into something special showing what has been unearthed here. The confusing map for he area doesn’t help. Don’t get a bicycle from the street vendors. It is unnecessary. In the end didn’t spend much time here.
practical_tips: don't get a bicycle from the street vendors

author: May G
title: Beautiful illumination to visit in the evening
original_content: A visit in the evening to enjoy the illumination, it is small and perhaps does not deserve a detour. There is a bustling market with local produce sales and traditional dishes in the evening.

author: akio9jp
title: Capital 1,000 years ago
original_content: Hoa Lu became the capital of Vietnam in 968, when it gained independence from the Southern Han of China, but only functioned as the capital for 42 years, as the capital was moved to Thang Long (now Hanoi) in 1,010. We were able to visit historical buildings, including ancient temples and the ruins of royal palaces.

title: Skip. Lots of pushy sales people and it’s kind of in the middle of no where. Not worth the trouble

I would avoid Unlv’s you really just have so much time in ninh binh where you wanted to see every single thing. Skip the Hoa Lu Ancient Town
