author: Gus b
title: Not worth it. Too much hassle.
original_content: Not worth the fuss. On your way in you will try to be scammed into parking, just ignore them. Ticket price is 20,000 and once you walk towards entrance you’ll be harassed by people trying to get you to rent a bike, again you do NOT need to rent a bike as it’s no way near the 2 hour walk they claim. We walked up some stairs to a cool view but that was about it.Wouldn’t recommend tbh.
drawbacks: harassed by people trying to rent a bike
practical_tips: ignore people trying to scam you into parking

author: Marriet d
title: Scam! Avoid 'free parking' ahead of Hoa Lu's entrance
original_content: Parking scams are everywhere around Ninh Binh. No need to be unpleasant to anyone, but do be strong and continue to your destination with confidence.Your first stop is the ticket booth on the main road's right hand side.Next you'll drive your scooter/bicycle/motorbike across the street  (and ever-so-slightly back the way you came) into Hoa Lu. Present your ticket as you ride through the gate where everyone's entering on foot. If your experience is like mine, five or six scammers will tell you to stop or park where they want you to park. Now's a good time to show off your ice cold nerves! Give the bike some gas and head for the entrance. If you ask employees of Hoa Lu about parking, they'll tell you to do exactly what you want to do, which is park inside the complex for free.
drawbacks: Parking scams are everywhere around Ninh Binh
highlights: parking inside the complex for free
practical_tips: be strong and continue to your destination with confidence
park inside the complex for free

author: Mark
title: Important historic site for Vietnamese but not a lot to see. Unpleasant, pushy 'free parking' scammers outside.
original_content: Undoubtedly an historic site from the Vietnamese point of view but there's not really much to see. It's in a pleasant, green area not far from Trang An. We hired a motor scooter from our accommodation close to Tam Coc and took the scenic route through Hang Mua, which follows the river and is a nice quiet road. This road emerges not far from Trang An where we spent the morning on a boat trip. Don't be scammed by the 'free parking' places close to the entrance to the 'ancient capital' - they tell you that it's not permitted to take a motor scooter on to the site but, it is. Then they want you to hire a bike to go round it but the bikes are pretty clunky. We agree with other reviewers who recommend cycling from Tam Coc if you have the energy. Then you can use your own bike to ride around the site. Anyway, back to the ancient city: there's some typical old architecture and quite an extensive series of small roads winding through the village - pleasant but not really interesting. So, in conclusion, visit if you want to tick it off but don't worry if you miss out - just look at the pictures online. Enough said?
practical_tips: don't be scammed by the 'free parking' places
cycle from Tam Coc if you have the energy
use your own bike to ride around the site

author: Catherine F
title: Interesting site to visit for a couple of hours
original_content: We enjoyed our visit to Hoa Lu. We drove by scooter and parked (for free) outside and hired bicycles to visit the different locations within the city. If you are staying in Tam Coc or Trang An and have access to a decent bicycle, I would recommend cycling to Hoa Lu from your hotel and using that bicycle as the ones available there are very basic. You can walk around the site, but if it's a hot day, cycling is better as it is a fairly large site. You are not given a map (and there are just a few on signboards in the centre of the site) and the signage isnt great so make the most of your unintended detours. It is easy to.cycle out of the site onto the main road, so keep Google maps to hand.
highlights: easy to cycle out of the site onto the main road

author: Sashila Mahendran
title: Hoa Lu Ancient Citadel
original_content: Hoa Lu Ancient citadel brought to life by our tour guide Jenny.Very interesting historical stories retold during our excursion.Jenny got everyone in the bus well acquainted

author: Coyote-Travelerz
title: Disappointing, but interesting
original_content: Of the 3 sites on our tour, this was the least interesting.I want to stress this is not a bad place to visit, but there are not many buildings to visit, can be large crowds, and leaves a lot to the imagination. Unless you are a true diehard history buff, you may not get too much from here, making it a waste of your time to visit versus other places in the area.
drawbacks: leaves a lot to the imagination

author: EleonoraO75
title: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital
original_content: Not having much time and since we also had a visit to the Hue Citadel planned, we only saw two temples. Maybe they aren't the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam but I'm still happy I went. To be done only if you have a lot of time available!
drawbacks: not the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam
practical_tips: only if you have a lot of time available

author: Sonje M
title: Disappointing experience
original_content: I was very excited to visit Vietnam’s ancient capital as I’m fascinated with history. However, the experience was extremely disappointing to us, so much so that we did a quick speed walk through the place and cut our visit short. It seems like people are living on the grounds and there is debris and old discarded items lying around in places such as an old billboard/signage, ladder chair, scrubbing brush, etc. It seemed like we accidentally walked into someone's messy backyard. There are also scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”. There are two entrances and it seems locals are using it as a shortcut. This really does not help to transport you to by gone eras.Although the entry fee is not very high, it feels like a bit of a rip off to pay to enter a place with so-called historical importance where people live (and display their debris) and scooters a free to drive like it any other road. There are other much more interesting place that are much better looked after that is completely free to enter.If you have an exceptional imagination I guess it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago.
drawbacks: people are living on the grounds
debris and old discarded items lying around
scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”
practical_tips: If you have an exceptional imagination it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago

author: LaNyonsaise
title: Few remains to see.
original_content: There’s not a lot to see so it doesn’t take long to walk to a couple of temples. The entry ticket is only 20VND and there are some drinks stands nearby.

author: Jkim SNieva
title: Hoa Lu, Vietnam's former Capital
original_content: It was a short but sweet visit. I think the reason why our family had a great time visiting the site is that we did it through a packaged tour of Nin Binh, and so we had a guided tour of the place (kudos to our great guide Hoa!). The place has such a fascinating story and though it doesn't loo grand, its ancient vibes made up for it. The gardens are well kept and there's a pond with fishes. It would be a nice place to roam around.

author: Phi Somchai
title: Well maintained and spacious
original_content: The ancient city is spread over a large area.  We crossed the bridge and walk through the main entrance of the walled city.   The main highlights that remained in the city were the temples and gardens.  They were well maintained.  There were many historical events relating to this city, so it is recommended to read up about this place for a better understanding before the visit.
practical_tips: read up about this place for a better understanding before the visit

author: Eamon G
title: Just keep on riding by.
original_content: Road to & past this so called historic place and then kept on going ! Not worth going into the bull #&-! that goes on outside the entrance which is enough to put off  any sane tourist. With a location with apparent historical importance you would think again the authorities would crack down on it, if they want tourists to enjoy the visit. And I stood around for a further 10 mins just to watch further shenanigans unfold.
extracted_spaces: Road to & past this so called historic place
drawbacks: bull #&-! that goes on outside the entrance

author: hm777
title: Interesting site, but not a smooth experience
original_content: The site itself is not large and does not take much time to go around. It was very pretty and interesting, even if there were not many English explanations. (e.g. I still have no idea what a "dragon's bed" is, despite attempting to google it).It was a rather chaotic experience, however. Once we entered, the people at the clothing stand were loudly shouting at, and literally chasing, all the people wearing shorts, trying to get them to cover up. There were unfortunately so many people wearing shorts that this meant continuous shouting. There were people on motorcycles saying we needed to hire one/take a ride with them to get around the site (definitely not; it was small). It was unclear where the site began and ended. Finally, we walked up a long flight of steep steps to the left of the entrance to see the emperors tomb and were scammed into buying incense at 10,000 dong each by a lady who lit it in front of us despite us saying "no".
extracted_times: not much time to go around
drawbacks: people at the clothing stand were loudly shouting and chasing people wearing shorts
highlights: the site itself is very pretty and interesting
even if there were not many English explanations
practical_tips: don't hire motorcycles to get around the site

author: Liesel
title: Dissapointed
original_content: While the history and beauty are enjoyable, I'm afraid there were too many negatives for us. Thousands of people. Difficulty getting through very large tour groups who hold everybody else up in order to take their group photos. Paid an entry fee per person but then were demanded additional fee each time we needed to use the toilet once we were inside. Be warned to cover your shoulders and knees to enter (they have clothing wraps to borrow if you don't come prepared). No English explanation boards to explain what we were looking at. People jump in front of our motorbike in order to stop us and told us free bike parking. Then on return to the bike, told us we had to eat there because we parked there.

practical_tips: cover your shoulders and knees to enter

title: Skip this one

Had a bad experience where 2 of them agreed to take my husband and me on a quick tour of the ancient capital with stops across all key landmarks inside for 70k VND  but once we completed the trip they asked for more and created a nuisance.

author: digitalroc
title: Ancient Capital
original_content: The Hoa Lu Ancient Capital was part of the group itinerary that I was on, so normally I would not have made a visit here.  Although we only stayed an hour, so it wasn’t too bad to gain a history lesson about the Ancient Capital of Hoa Lu.
drawbacks: not too bad to gain a history lesson
highlights: gain a history lesson about the Ancient Capital of Hoa Lu

author: Teresa
title: not much to see
original_content: I went here and there is not much here it looks like the rest of Asia. Was not rely worth coming. Might be good if you are new in Asia.

author: Durga M
title: Nothing much to see
original_content: We went to the ancient capital in Hao lu city there is nothing great about the place an ancient place renovated couple of times the tour guide explained the story of the king and its history.
highlights: the tour guide explained the story of the king and its history

author: green_gecko917
title: Pleasant ride there, nice for an hour or so.
original_content: Giving this 4 stars mainly because the bicycle ride there (about 16km one way) from where we stayed in Tam Coc was spectacular. The ancient capital itself is ok - I'd probably give it 3 stars. Take your bicycles (or motorbikes etc) inside. You are allowed.  We even saw cars in there. Don't park at the "free parking" across the road as they would likely just hold your bikes for ransom afterwards. They were fairly aggressive trying to get us to park but we refused. It is also extremely hot in July so walking through this place would not be pleasant.You can actually get in for free if you go in the other way. There is a main gate where you pay, and then you go straight a few hundred meters towards the first temple and turn right before going in. If you keep going that way, it just turns into a little street that opens up into the town. We might have gone that way if we had known about this "secret" entrance.You can spend maybe 1 hour here, but lots more time cycling around nearby attractions and views.
practical_tips: avoid parking at 'free parking' across the road
go in the other way for free entrance

author: Vietnamese Dinner Experience in Tam Coc
title: Where can learn history
original_content: I often send my children here at least once a year at the beginning of the year or summer holidays to visit and learn about the history of King Dinh and Le's life in Vietnam. The space here is spacious and airy, we can enjoy as a sunny, windy picnic and immerse in nature.
extracted_spaces: King Dinh and Le's life in Vietnam
highlights: enjoy as a sunny, windy picnic

author: Shimnik
title: One day - more than enough
original_content: If you think to spend more than 2 days in Hoa Lu (Tam Coc), think about it twice. There is not much to see and do except 2 temples dedicated to the first emperors, rice fields, boat ride and cycling on an old bike. Everything can be realized in one day!

can be realized in one day
highlights: 2 temples dedicated to the first emperors

title: Quick Stop

title: Most visitors would not be interested in this cultural visit

author: Alice W
title: Don't bother
original_content: This site is fake artifacts and not worth the detour. Luckily we motor cycled there and got out quick. I would hate to have been on an organised tour. The touts here are also particularly pushy. We are pretty used to them and generally a friendly no (khong) with a smile is OK.  But these touts were agressive. Even tried to get AUD off us. When we said we didn't carry they tried to sell us an Australian $5 note. They also were forcibly placing hats on my head too, they were just scammy and rude. Avoid stress, avoid this site.

Then they want you to hire a bike to go round it but the bikes are pretty clunky. We agree with other reviewers who recommend cycling from Tam Coc if you have the energy. Then you can use your own bike to ride around the site. Anyway, back to the ancient city: there's some typical old architecture and quite an extensive series of small roads winding through the village - pleasant but not really interesting. So, in conclusion, visit if you want to tick it off but don't worry if you miss out - just look at the pictures online. Enough said?
practical_tips: don't be scammed by the 'free parking' places
cycle from Tam Coc if you have the energy
use your own bike to ride around the site

author: Catherine F
title: Interesting site to visit for a couple of hours
original_content: We enjoyed our visit to Hoa Lu. We drove by scooter and parked (for free) outside and hired bicycles to visit the different locations within the city. If you are staying in Tam Coc or Trang An and have access to a decent bicycle, I would recommend cycling to Hoa Lu from your hotel and using that bicycle as the ones available there are very basic. You can walk around the site, but if it's a hot day, cycling is better as it is a fairly large site. You are not given a map (and there are just a few on signboards in the centre of the site) and the signage isnt great so make the most of your unintended detours. It is easy to.cycle out of the site onto the main road, so keep Google maps to hand.
highlights: easy to cycle out of the site onto the main road

author: Sashila Mahendran
title: Hoa Lu Ancient Citadel
original_content: Hoa Lu Ancient citadel brought to life by our tour guide Jenny.Very interesting historical stories retold during our excursion.Jenny got everyone in the bus well acquainted

author: Coyote-Travelerz
title: Disappointing, but interesting
original_content: Of the 3 sites on our tour, this was the least interesting.I want to stress this is not a bad place to visit, but there are not many buildings to visit, can be large crowds, and leaves a lot to the imagination. Unless you are a true diehard history buff, you may not get too much from here, making it a waste of your time to visit versus other places in the area.
drawbacks: leaves a lot to the imagination

author: EleonoraO75
title: Hoa Lư Ancient Capital
original_content: Not having much time and since we also had a visit to the Hue Citadel planned, we only saw two temples. Maybe they aren't the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam but I'm still happy I went. To be done only if you have a lot of time available!
drawbacks: not the most beautiful we saw in Vietnam

author: Sonje M
title: Disappointing experience
original_content: I was very excited to visit Vietnam’s ancient capital as I’m fascinated with history. However, the experience was extremely disappointing to us, so much so that we did a quick speed walk through the place and cut our visit short. It seems like people are living on the grounds and there is debris and old discarded items lying around in places such as an old billboard/signage, ladder chair, scrubbing brush, etc. It seemed like we accidentally walked into someone's messy backyard. There are also scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”. There are two entrances and it seems locals are using it as a shortcut. This really does not help to transport you to by gone eras.Although the entry fee is not very high, it feels like a bit of a rip off to pay to enter a place with so-called historical importance where people live (and display their debris) and scooters a free to drive like it any other road. There are other much more interesting place that are much better looked after that is completely free to enter.If you have an exceptional imagination I guess it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago.
drawbacks: people are living on the grounds
debris and old discarded items lying around
scooters driving around in the “ancient capital”
practical_tips: If you have an exceptional imagination it still mildly interesting to imagine how it might have been like years ago

author: LaNyonsaise

original_content: There’s not a lot to see so it doesn’t take long to walk to a couple of temples. The entry ticket is only 20VND and there are some drinks stands nearby.

author: Jkim SNieva

The place has such a fascinating story and though it doesn't loo grand, its ancient vibes made up for it. The gardens are well kept and there's a pond with fishes. It would be a nice place to roam around.

author: Phi Somchai

The main highlights that remained in the city were the temples and gardens.  They were well maintained.  There were many historical events relating to this city, so it is recommended to read up about this place for a better understanding before the visit.

Not worth going into the bull #&-! that goes on outside the entrance which is enough to put off  any sane tourist. With a location with apparent historical importance you would think again the authorities would crack down on it, if they want tourists to enjoy the visit. author: hm777
title: Interesting site, but not a smooth experience
original_content: The site itself is not large and does not take much time to go around. It was very pretty and interesting, even if there were not many English explanations. (e.g. I still have no idea what a "dragon's bed" is, despite attempting to google it).It was a rather chaotic experience, however. Once we entered, the people at the clothing stand were loudly shouting at, and literally chasing, all the people wearing shorts, trying to get them to cover up. There were unfortunately so many people wearing shorts that this meant continuous shouting. There were people on motorcycles saying we needed to hire one/take a ride with them to get around the site (definitely not; it was small). It was unclear where the site began and ended. Finally, we walked up a long flight of steep steps to the left of the entrance to see the emperors tomb and were scammed into buying incense at 10,000 dong each by a lady who lit it in front of us despite us saying "no".

author: digitalroc

author: green_gecko917
title: Pleasant ride there, nice for an hour or so.
original_content: Giving this 4 stars mainly because the bicycle ride there (about 16km one way) from where we stayed in Tam Coc was spectacular. The ancient capital itself is ok - I'd probably give it 3 stars. Take your bicycles (or motorbikes etc) inside. You are allowed.  We even saw cars in there. Don't park at the "free parking" across the road as they would likely just hold your bikes for ransom afterwards. They were fairly aggressive trying to get us to park but we refused. It is also extremely hot in July so walking through this place would not be pleasant.You can actually get in for free if you go in the other way. There is a main gate where you pay, and then you go straight a few hundred meters towards the first temple and turn right before going in. If you keep going that way, it just turns into a little street that opens up into the town. We might have gone that way if we had known about this "secret" entrance.You can spend maybe 1 hour here, but lots more time cycling around nearby attractions and views.
practical_tips: avoid parking at 'free parking' across the road
go in the other way for free entrance

author: Vietnamese Dinner Experience in Tam Coc
title: Where can learn history

author: Adrienne G
title: Incredible hidden gem, still some love in the world
original_content: An amazing experience! Well worth the entry fee and the slightly long drive from Tam Cok. The team there do an incredible job saving bears that are victims of the horrific bear bile trade. We were so lucky to see a bear super close (he just turned his head as I took the photo but he was looking straight at us and clearly as curious as we were!) Feeding time is at 4pm which is your best chance to see the bears and you can either watch from the sky walk by yourself for only 50,000 Dong or join a tour for a bit more. Thao in the visitor house was so helpful and kind and gave us all the information we needed. She was an absolute gem! Four Paws is the project that funds and runs the rescue centre. I can’t commend them all there enough for the incredible work they do to rescue the bears who are treated so appallingly by humanity. Clearly there is still some love in the world.
highlights: so lucky to see a bear super close
Thao in the visitor house was so helpful and kind
practical_tips: watch from the sky walk for 50,000 Dong or join a tour

author: Elaine
title: A great day out with bears
original_content: They begin with a comprehensive and touching film about the bears. There is a sky walk overlooking the bear enclosures. Then the guide will take you on a more comprehensive walk at ground level for the full experience. They use earpieces so that the bears are not frightened by noise. These are frail bears who have suffered in the past but are flourishing now rescued and treated well. An uplifting experience and well worth the ticket. The onside restaurant is also very good.
highlights: guide will take you on a more comprehensive walk

author: Veronika R
title: Musst see!
original_content: Beautiful place for rescued bears, with high professional care they deserve.The stories of the bears are very sad. But it's very educational and nice to see that there are changes in progress and people who really care.Go. Enjoy the bears and support the sanctuary.
highlights: nice to see changes in progress

author: Wanderer03451888431
title: Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh Vietnam
original_content: This sanctuary (not a zoo) was established to rescue Asiatic Black and Sun bears from bile milking ( used in Chinese medicine) and hunting. The sanctuary has dedicated staff that work tirelessly for the welfare of theses bears that have been victims of much cruelty in their lives. If you love bears and are passionate about supporting authentic organisations like Four Paws- Bear Sanctuary then you will enjoy seeing the bears being looked after on this amazing site. We did the immersive tour with a member of staff who walked around showing us the food preparation areas and talking with great knowledge about how try to balance their diets whilst offering stimulating ways for the bears to find food. All staff were very knowledgeable and passionate about the bears. This was the best experience and tour we have had in Vietnam and would highly recommend it. The government fully support the excellent work being done to protect these bears and offer them a peaceful life

author: Katie
title: Worthwhile trip

Staff also had amazing English skills- definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area! Sadly we didn’t have time to do a full tour but imagine it would be great if you have the time!
drawbacks: we didn’t have time to do a full tour
highlights: Staff are very passionate about helping the bears
Staff also had amazing English skills

author: JUDY M
title: Great work done here..highly recommend
original_content: Highly recommend this place.  Our guide was so enthusiastic... she loves those bears.  Very informative and spoke very clear English. Great work on education as a means of stopping the illegal trapping of bears and, worse, bile extraction.  Do take the full tour ..so worth it
highlights: education on stopping bear trapping and bile extraction

author: Offmefarm
title: Best day!
original_content: Best day of all in Vietnam! 4 Paws is doing amazing work to rehabilitate the bears they so lovingly care for and importantly, to educate about safe alternatives to bear bile- reduce demand and less bear farms will follow. A couple of things to help those wishing to visit:1. Book a tour directly with the centre before you go and take a cab there. We arrived early but the first tour was booked out so we went on to the endangered primate and turtle centre in Cuc Phuong NP which is also excellent. The tour guide we had at both centres were so knowledgeable and passionate2. Buy well priced souvenirs to support the centre3. Have an excellent lunch in the restaurantSpread the news and have an uplifting albeit sad day
highlights: Educating about safe alternatives to bear bile
practical_tips: Book a tour directly with the centre
Have an excellent lunch in the restaurant

author: Bussereau A
title: Go there!!
original_content: We chose the first formula with a one-hour tour of the sanctuary with a great Ha guide!It was exciting and we had the chance to see all the bears in their enclosures. We could see how fulfilled they were and finally free to self-determination.Education was one of the most important levers it is essential to relay the actions of free paws with this project.We also understood what was at stake for bear owners and why they started wanting to sell their bile.There is still a lot of work to be done in Vietnam but the progress is significant and 46 bears live under care as a result of torture and will end their lives here. So they need us. The capacity of the center is 100 bears so there are still many bears to free from their ordeal. It is a pleasure to see them evolve after the terrible images of their previous living conditions. A very important visit, do not hesitate a second.

author: Alexandra F
title: Well worth the visit to support their efforts in rescuing bears from the bile trade industry in Asia
original_content: It was a very eye opening and unique experience. The staff recognise each of the bears by name and their favourite foods 😭 I did the immersive tour which was 250k and included a guided sanctuary tour and self guided access to the sky bridge which stretches over the enclosures. The tour begins with a short video outlining the sanctuary and its efforts. The staff are so caring and respectful of the bears and their individual needs. Tragic to find out that all of the bear residents spent a minimum of 15 years in captivity in cages no bigger than a large dog crate.
drawbacks: all of the bear residents spent a minimum of 15 years in captivity in cages no bigger than a large dog crate
highlights: staff recognise each of the bears by name and their favourite foods
caring and respectful of the bears and their individual needs

author: Татьяна Т
title: Best thing I've seen in Ninh Binh
original_content: Having visited almost all the main attractions of Ninh Binh, I can safely say - this place has become the most memorable for me. Definitely worth your attention.My husband and I came here just to see the bears, and we thought we'd spend a little time here. But in the end, they stayed for almost three hours - so interesting.The area is very large and green. We walked long distances over the suspension bridge above the spacious enclosures and watched the bears. There are many of them here, and everyone has their own habits: someone plays, someone relaxes, someone explores the territory. You can watch them for a very long time - it's really fascinating.They gave us a tour and told us about the shelter. Particularly touching was the fact that the staff explained in detail how the bears got here and the difficulties they had experienced before. Now they have a safe place to be cared for.The staff here are incredibly friendly and sympathetic. You can see that people genuinely love their work and treat the bears with great care and warmth. They are also very attentive to visitors and happy to share knowledge.If you're in Ninh Binh, be sure to come. Not only will you have a good time here, but you will also learn a lot about animal rescue

author: USUKAU
title: Great place doing great work
original_content: Great insight into the work done to help these animals.  We organised a car and driver to take us from our hotel.  The sanctuary offers three types of admission - we opted for the one that includes a tour of the sanctuary.  This was the correct choice!  Our guide showed us around the facility and shared information about the many bears we saw.  We then watched a short film, had a break at the cafe (additional cost but inexpensive) and then went to the tree walk to watch them give the bears lunch.  The tour was far and away the best way to see and learn about the bears.  Entry including the tour was 250k (less than $15 Aud) which goes to help support the bears.  Highly recommend for anyone who likes animals
highlights: Great insight into the work done to help these animals
The tour was far and away the best way to see and learn about the bears
Entry including the tour was 250k (less than $15 Aud) which goes to help support the bears
practical_tips: Opt for the tour of the sanctuary
Go to the tree walk to watch them give the bears lunch

author: Matthew C
title: Fantastic work that needs our support and help
original_content: What a great morning we had at this sanctuary. We opted for the full tour, this gave us a guided walk around the enclosures with our guide that answered our questions as we walked. We stopped off at the food preparation area and were lucky to see a few bears (it is set up for the bears rather than for tourists viewing them so you might not see anything), we then watched a film about the sanctuary, the work they do and they very sad situation lots of bears are still in in Vietnam who continue to be kept at bear farms even though its illegal to extract the bile. We then had a self guided walk on a glass walkway. Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.
highlights: self guided walk on a glass walkway
practical_tips: visit if you are in the area

author: Karen - Veiled Valley
title: Well managed sanctuary, not easy to sight bears
original_content: The bear sanctuary is a great place for the bears. They are well taken care of, well protected. They live in a rather natural habitat with lots of space and flora. Food is hidden so that they can use their hunting skills. They are not forced to be in front of visitors. However, because of the protection for the bears, there is really no guarantee that you would see the bear close up or in action. For the cheaper tickets, you can only walk on the sky bridge, which is not that long of a walk. For the guided tours, they also have long movies / talking before and after, which can be boring for young children. It is a very well maintained place. I appreciate their mission and work. It will probably be very fun to volunteer at the place. In terms of bear sighting, it is not as spectacular.

boring for young children due to long movies/talking
cheaper tickets only allow walking on sky bridge

volunteering may be a fun option

author: JamesXX_007
title: This is not to be missed
original_content: This is not to be missed. Well organized as we had a private guide for just under an hour.  I tip my hat to the government of Vietnam for leading the way in helping bears.

author: Jarod S

The work at the sanctuary is awe-inspiring, as they have nearly eradicated bear farms in Vietnam. They even helped us book a ride back to Hanoi when we were having issues finding one.

There is still a long way to go so that the law against these illegal practices can be fully applied. The Vietnamese government supports this project. Chapeau for the patience and care of all employees.
highlights: patience and care of all employees

author: sarpor
title: Excellent day visit
original_content: I am in complete admiration of the people who work here, who have a clear love for the bears in their care. After such a horrific start in life, these bears now spend their days at what is effectively the best version of a 5 star resort. The staff are very knowledgeable and committed to helping the bears’ mentally and physically. Quality enclosures too. I opted for the 250,000k ticket and with this you get to see into the back areas including the kitchen, vets and enrichment.  I arrived about 9am , just after the first feed so the bears were still actively looking for food as I wandered along the skywalk. Then heading bad and joined my tour about 9:45. This took us to other areas to see different bears and ended a couple of hours later. I had lunch at the onsite restaurant (there’s an enclosure opposite and two bears sat and watched me eat lunch). Then I headed back to the skywalk about 1pm to see the bears called back home so that the caretakers can then put their food out. Shortly after the bears were allowed back out and I watched them forage for a while. Excellent day and if I was ever back here I would return. Cannot recommend this place enough.
highlights: clear love for the bears in their care
practical_tips: arrive early to see the bears actively looking for food

author: tanzania2009186361
title: Bear sanctuary - and absolute must
original_content: Absolutely inspiring visit. The staff knowledge of these rescued bears, their psychological and physical needs, was very apparent. Also a reminder of how much damage we as hu.ans do to our fellow creatures.
extracted_spaces: The sanctuary where the rescued bears are kept
highlights: Staff knowledge of rescued bears' needs

author: Gerda V
title: Impressive.
original_content: Great reception. The bears have plenty of space and are well cared for.  They've come from hell to heaven.  The guide knew a lot to tell.  Highly recommended for every animal lover.

author: Rens33
title: Great complex
original_content: Complex is great. Guides are very knowledgeable and you can tell they have a real love and passion for the bears rescued. We visited early on a very hot day. Not ideal for bear watching- but we did still see some.  Recommend the full tour for 250k.We got a grab out to the sanctuary, but needed them to call us a taxi to return to Tam Coc as no drivers were accepting.
highlights: you can tell they have a real love and passion for the bears rescued

author: Tim Anderson
title: Well worth a visit
original_content: Our visit to the sanctuary was amazing, the tour guides were very knowledgeable and spoke good English. Our guide on the 21/5/2025 for the 1.30 pm tour was great, although we could not remember her name unfortunately.The short film we were shown was produced quite well and also very informative.The bear feeding times are 9am, 1pm and 4pm I believe, it is best to begin your guided tour (if you chose that option) around 30 minutes after feeding time as this is when the bears will be most active. The sanctuary provide hats and umbrellas for sun protection if necessary.It's great to see how much work is currently being done caring for these bears and  rescuing bears still in captivity.
highlights: short film was produced quite well and informative
great to see how much work is currently being done caring for these bears
practical_tips: begin your guided tour around 30 minutes after feeding time
sanctuary provide hats and umbrellas for sun protection

author: Phil R
title: A truly Worthy Cause
original_content: We did the full tour which I recommend as the best way to experience this sanctuary.  The pace was good, we saw lots of bears an learnt all about the inhumanity shown towards these bears before they were saved.  A truly worthwhile visit and cause.  hank you Four Paws
highlights: learnt all about the inhumanity shown towards these bears

author: Andrea
title: Absolutely fantastic and educative tour, please support this hard work the team makes by saving bears
original_content: Huge thanks for everyone for this hard work! This is amazing what you do for the bears. Animal cruelty needs to end, we have absolutely no right to exploit them! I went to the immersive tour and it was totally worth it. I got so many more information, it was so educative. Thank you for this amazing experience. It was actually one of the best programmes I have taken part in while staying in Ninh Binh. THANK YOU!

author: James A
title: Excellent location for conservation
original_content: I cycled to the bear sanctuary on a warm but rainy day in early July and found it to be a real highlight on the Ninh Binh area. Four Paws are doing excellent work and I really enjoyed the ambience and beautiful surroundings of the sanctuary. I think I would recommend a visit as a highlight of my time in Ninh Binh.
practical_tips: visit as a highlight of my time in Ninh Binh

author: Naomi B
title: Support the bears - great on a rainy day
original_content: We were looking for an outing on a rainy day in Ninh Binh and this sanctuary came up on my search. The bears like the drizzling  rain so we saw plenty from the skywalk. I recommend the guided tour, Ninh provides insights about the individual bears and you get to walk in the lower level near the enclosure. Plus the funds are going to care for the rescued bears.
highlights: walk in the lower level near the enclosure

author: jbschmor
title: An important and good place to visit in Ninh Binh
original_content: My driver from Tam Coc suggested going here and I am very glad that I did.  This place is well worth your time.  It begins with a short film that in some places may be difficult for some viewers to take.  But the information is important.  What I really like about this place is that the emphasis is on education, not on photo opps with the bears.  I learned a lot and I got to see some beautiful bears who are being well taken care of and protected.
drawbacks: some viewers may find the short film difficult to take
highlights: beautiful bears being well taken care of and protected

author: Narelle Z
title: Highly recommend visiting and supporting this bear sanctuary. So special!
original_content: We love visiting the Bear Sanctuary. The Moon bears were so beautiful, and it's just very special what they do there. If you love animals this is a must see. Such a great sanctuary to support too!

author: Darragh O
title: Do the Immersive tour. 250k. You won't regret it!
original_content: Excellent experience. They do amazing work to rescue bears from cruel bile farming practices.They offer three tours. 50k to self guide yourself through a "skywalk" viewing platform which has three viewings houses with written information about the bears in the viewable enclosures.150k for a guided tour of the skywalk viewing platform where a member of staff gives further info about the day to day running of the sanctuary and info about bile farming.250k for the "immersive experience". We did this one and it is absolutely worth the extra cost!! Do not hesitate. You get access to the viewing platform yourself for as long as you want. Immersive tours start at irregular intervals depending on how many people are they and if the staff are free. For this tour, then bring you for a walk along the pathways between the various enclosures where you can easily see the bears only metres from where you stand, through the enclosure fences. We had Ninh and she was very knowledgeable and had great English and explained all about the sanctuary, bile farming and knew a lot about each individual bear. It is clear the staff really care about the bears as they know them by name.10/10 would thoroughly recommend this experience!!
highlights: clear the staff really care about the bears

author: CJ
title: Four paws! Great work with bears
original_content: I recommend visiting the bear sanctuary to learn about the work that Four Paws and their team is doing to prevent the ill-treatment of bears and the harvesting of bear bile for medicinal purposes. I went there on a Thursday afternoon and there were only a 6 other guests. Entry to the sanctuary starts from 50,000VD for the skywalk (basically you get access to view the bears and sanctuary from several others enclosed platforms) and progress up to 150,000 and 250,000VD which includes a dedicated guide and tour of the premises (you get to go into the sanctuary), an overview of the history of bears in Vietnam, key information about some of the bears that are currently at the sanctuary, and an educational video at the end.The venue is modern and there is a nice vegetarian cafe with a great drink selection. I got an iced coffee and it was amazing! Reasonably priced! I am staying at a Homestay near the Bai Định Pagoda. It’s about a 20minute drive away. I ended up using a rental scooter to get here and had to drive on dirt roads but still made it. It is recommended that you have a 2WD to get up the road but I saw a lot in d scoters parked up which May have belonged to workers. You can also use Grab and I did run into another couple that got a ride from a Luxury Van and loaded their mountain bikes into the back of it. I enjoyed it, saw heaps of bears, learnt a lot and felt good about my fees going back into a good cause. It also beats going to the usual tourist places around here and the queues and waiting times to see the same things.
highlights: Learned about the work of Four Paws
practical_tips: Use a 2WD to get up the road
Use Grab or a Luxury Van for transportation

author: Amélie L
title: Best experience in Ninh binh bear sanctuary
original_content: The Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh is truly an incredible place! They rescue bears from the horrific cruelty of bear bile farming, giving them a second chance at a happy and healthy life. Seeing these rescued bears thriving in a safe, natural environment is both heartwarming and inspiring.The staff here are absolutely amazing—kind, passionate, and deeply dedicated to their mission. They take the time to educate visitors about the realities of bile farming and the importance of conservation efforts. Their hard work and commitment have already saved so many bears, giving them the care and freedom they deserve.Visiting this sanctuary is a must for anyone who cares about animal welfare. It’s not just a place to see bears; it’s a place of hope, healing, and change. I highly recommend supporting this wonderful organization in any way you can.Thank you to the entire team for the incredible work you do you are all so amazing ❤️❤️Also a special thanks for Trang ! She is so passionate and was an incredible guide toward the sanctuary 🥰!!
extracted_spaces: The Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh
highlights: Seeing these rescued bears thriving in a safe, natural environment is both heartwarming and inspiring.
The staff here are absolutely amazing—kind, passionate, and deeply dedicated to their mission.
Visiting this sanctuary is a must for anyone who cares about animal welfare.
practical_tips: Support this wonderful organization in any way you can.
Go early to get a good guide like Trang.

author: Fearless546825
title: Nihn bihn bear sanctuary, amazing.....
original_content: An amazing organisation doing some incredible work for these poor  bears here in Vietnam and around the world. Please go and visit and learn about the horrible bear bile farming industry,  knowledge is key to stop this cruelty.There are different entrance fees ranging from 50.000d to 250.000. I recommend paying the 250.000 getting a full guided tour from the carer's there and access around the complex .Should be advertised more in Tam Coc and surrounding areas so more tourists know that wonderful place is here....
practical_tips: pay the 250.000 fee for a full guided tour
advertise more in Tam Coc and surrounding areas

author: Mae G
title: Memorable visit
original_content: Highly worthwhile visit. The bears are all so well cared for. Would recommend the tour option to learn more about the day to day operations of the sanctuary. Very informative tour guide also.

author: sueanne_nicol
title: Worthwhile visit
original_content: Fabulous sanctuary with great set up for the bears- so much effort put into the bear's enrichment, relationships and wellbeing.Unfortunately we arrived too early for the guided tour, but the skydeck had great installations and was very informative.The park is being expanded and is definately worth the visit.Great shop and cafe too.
drawbacks: arrived too early for the guided tour
highlights: great set up for the bears

author: James O
title: Worthy cause we'll worth a half day visit
original_content: This sanctuary is little known and about 30 km fron Tam Coc with a number of separate compounds housing a varying number of bears.There are 2 options available for viewing the bears, both of which include a skywalk and the more expensive tour (only an extra $4), includes a walk on the service roads around the compounds, which may or may not increase your viewing chances.Both trips commence with an educational talk and finish with a video of the work the sanctuary does.Obviously, how many bears you see and how close you get to the bears is at the will of the bears themselves. However, planning your visit around one of the 3 daily feeding times increases your chances of some interaction,  09.00, 13.00, and 16.00.There were a number of families visiting during our time there, and the children seemed very excited.It's a worthy cause well worth a half day visit with all  the moneyspent going directly to the care of the bears.
drawbacks: how many bears you see and how close you get to the bears is at the will of the bears themselves
highlights: a worthy cause well worth a half day visit
practical_tips: plan your visit around one of the 3 daily feeding times

author: HJ
title: A great cause and 1/2 day trip
original_content: We had a lovely visit to the bear sanctuary, it's a little out of the way and not very well known but it is worth the trip to support such a good cause and see the bears happy and healthy. We did the immersive tour and would recommend it, you visit the sky walk and watch the bears as well as having a private tour closer to the spacious enclosures whilst learning about the charity and why it is needed and how they help. It finishes with a film about the sanctuary.

author: Davies A
title: Worth half a day trip
original_content: The place is not very big with many activities but worth a visit, and make sure you chose a guided tour so you can see bears on the way. At first they suggest us it's free to walk to their glass bridges to find bear, but I feel grateful that we chose a guide trip, or else we won't know which area to look for bear on the bridge. The guide provide a lot of knowledge and we saw lots of bear on the way so it was a successful. Also don't forget to buy some souvenir to support their organisation helping more unfortunate creatures like these.
highlights: saw lots of bear on the way

author: Lynn W
title: Save the Bears
original_content: Very well run Sanctuary.Well run, good tour & information. So sad what us humans have done & still do to the beautiful animals of this planet. These Sanctuaries save as many as they can, to at least give them a safe & well looked after rest of their life after such torture.Very important to support these Sanctuaries & learn from our old bad ways & stop it happening in the future.
drawbacks: sad what us humans have done & still do to the beautiful animals of this planet
highlights: save as many as they can
practical_tips: support these Sanctuaries & learn from our old bad ways

author: Claire H
title: A place to visit if you care about animals.
original_content: A place where rescued bears can live out their lives in peace and happiness. It’s a lovely place to see and learn about how they are being rescued. It is however, also very difficult to hear about the stories of their captivity but I saw this as a way to engage with the issue and provide funds to them directly once I’m back home. It’s operated by Four Paws registered charity and the quality input is evident. I just wish all the bears could be freed!
drawbacks: difficult to hear about the stories of their captivity
highlights: lovely place to see and learn about how they are being rescued
practical_tips: provide funds to them directly once I’m back home

author: Pamela B
title: Fascinating yet sad visit
original_content: Amazing place where staff are totally dedicated to the care of the bears rescued from bile farms.  Definitely worth booking in advance for the full visit which lasts around 2 hours then after that you are free to spend as long as you want there. We felt we could have stayed all day but stayed around three and half hours. Probably best done on your own with scooter or a driver then you can stay as long as you want
highlights: staff are totally dedicated to the care of the bears
practical_tips: best done on your own with scooter or a driver

author: Valerie S
title: Very impressive rescue facility for Asian bears
original_content: I did not know much about the bear bile trade before my husband and I went to this incredible place in Ninh Binh for rescued bears. I highly recommend going on a guided tour to get to see the bears up close. The tour was very informative and I couldn’t help, but cry for those bears still suffering on bear bile farms. I bought as many awesome items from the gift shop that I could fit into my luggage. I will continue to support the Four Paws animal organization now that I’ve returned home and was able to look up all the great work they have done already to help animals around the world. Look forward to following Four Paws online to see what they accomplish next!

author: Sue V
title: Support the work of this great place
original_content: We took a guided tour, which was very informative and interesting. The cruel treatment these animals have suffered is heart breaking. But the enclosures they live in now are top rate and their treatment excellent. We were very happy to be supporting this charity.
drawbacks: cruel treatment these animals have suffered

author: Kaz
title: An organisation doing fantastic work
original_content: Did the tour learning about these poor bears and where they have come from.  This organisation are doing amazing work and the bears are really well cared for.  A worthwhile experience to learn about them.  We had a lovely lunch there and bought a few things from the gift shop, proceeds going to the bears
highlights: the bears are well cared for
practical_tips: buy something from the gift shop

author: sixpence04
title: A beautiful experience. Must visit!
original_content: One of the biggest highlights of our trip to Vietnam! These bears have been through heartbreaking things and are now being cared for so beautifully. You can tell the staff really do care. Definitely do the guided tour to learn more and see these gorgeous animals up close. The cafe also has some lovely options. You absolutely have to visit if you're in the area!
practical_tips: visit if you're in the area

author: Anna C
title: Impressive sanctuary doing great work!
original_content: Great to visit, enlightening, Vietnam is very proactive and the care of the rescued bears is admirable, now if only China & South Korea will ban it too.
drawbacks: China & South Korea will ban it too
highlights: the care of the rescued bears is admirable

author: Pippa
title: Amazing
original_content: An amazing place doing amazing work. So glad we decided to come and visit the sanctuary, you can really see how much the staff care for the bears. We did the immersive experience which I'd highly recommend as we got to see quite a few of the bears even though it was a very hot day. Definitely a must do if you are visiting Ninh Binh
highlights: see quite a few of the bears

author: Jan M
title: Bear visit on a wet day.
original_content: On a rainy day we decided to visit the bear sanctuary, it was well worth it and we saw quite a few bears. They are doing a great job there.

author: Anne M
title: Great afternoon out
original_content: Great experience, learn about how they rescue bears and take care of them. Staff are friendly and welcoming and willing to share knowledge about what they do. Bears are fed around 1pm so good to time for that
highlights: learn about bear rescue and care
practical_tips: time visit around 1pm to see bears being fed

author: Inspire40202899371
title: Incredible Experience and Must Do in Ninh Binh
original_content: Incredible experience and so uplifting to see all of the hard work they are doing and the thoughtfulness they put into the enclosures and the day to day lives of the bears to give them enrichment and a better life.

author: Laura L
title: An extraordinary experience, to do absolutely!
original_content: A wonderful experience, it was very exciting visit this center and see with how much love and dedication these suffering animals are cared for and protected. I chose the "immerse" program in order to have a complete information about this activity. The ideal time of visit is 9 am, book before you go. The center is a bit isolated and there are no buses, from Ninh Binh you can reach in an hour by taxi.agree with the driver also the return because you will not find transport in that area.
highlights: animals are cared for and protected
practical_tips: agree with the driver for return

author: MathildaS
title: Recommended. Should not be missing from the Vietnam trip!
original_content: The facility was very professional, the leadership great. Definitely worth a visit even with children. Keep it up!!!

author: Antonia
title: Amazing!
original_content: This is an amazing sanctuary! The bears have a lot of space and are very well taken care of. You can really tell all the love and affection the staff has for them. You get a great view of the bears from the Skywalk, but if you want more information and support the sanctuary even more, I highly recommend booking the guided tour for 250.000 VD. You can just book the tour when you arrive, no need to book it in advance. The best time to see them is after they had their food (8am, 1pm, and in the evening) There is also a nice vegetarian bistro onsite for a delicious snack.Thank you to the lovely staff for giving these bears a new life!
highlights: bears have a lot of space
staff has love and affection for the bears
great view of the bears from the Skywalk
practical_tips: book the guided tour for 250.000 VD
book the tour when you arrive, no need to book in advance
visit after they had their food

author: Bauerin
title: The bears' past gets under their skin
original_content: We had booked a tour for the late morning and a good English speaking lady told us about the bears whose background can impart a lot of knowledge.Because of the heat we hardly saw bears, but for us the visit was worth it. The bears have a terrible past and are cared for here in very large natural enclosures.Finally, there was a movie to watch.Something is really being done here for animal welfare by Western standards, and a visit helps maintain the station.Card payment is possible and a vegetarian restaurant is also on site.
drawbacks: hardly saw bears due to heat

author: tomerw94
title: Amazing
original_content: We took the guided tour and the lady explained us widely about the place and answered our questions. She and the rest of the staff were nice and easy the understand.It seem like they really give the bears the best condition possible. We been there on a day woth good weather. They can give you umbrellas for the tour if you need.We were lucky to see many bears from a short distance through the fence. At 1 place we saw 8 of them at the same time, but we were told it is considered really lucky.
highlights: nice and easy to understand staff
lucky to see many bears from a short distance
practical_tips: ask for umbrellas for the tour if needed

author: Navigate544160
title: Great place - make time to visit
original_content: We visited July 24 after reading reviews on TripAdvisor and so glad we did, this is a beautiful place, spotlessly clean and well maintained doing great work for the 45 bears they have rescued. Lovely staff who are really knowledgeable about the bears and the bile trade. We are so glad we came to visit and see the work Four Paws is doing here.
practical_tips: visit after reading reviews on TripAdvisor

author: Trail56165823723
title: A true sanctuary for these beautiful bears
original_content: This is a true sanctuary. You can feel the love and care for these bears from all of the staff. Their work and advocacy for protecting bears from bile farming is inspiring. The skywalk is an incredible way to view the enclosures - with the enclosures so big it can be hard to spot the bears. I recommend doing the full guided tour for behind the scenes viewing and different angles to view the enclosures and bears. Come later in the day when it’s not so hot for the bears or they’ll mostly be hiding in the bushes and hard to see
drawbacks: mostly be hiding in the bushes
highlights: love and care for these bears
incredible way to view the enclosures

author: bobby
title: Life changing experience
original_content: We visited a bear sanctuary 🐻 which I have to say is the most ethical sanctuary I’ve ever been to. The list of rules and regulations were long and rightly so, in fact it was a privilege and not a given right to see any bears at all. No loud noises. No calling their names. No strong fragrances.No touching the fences. The lists went on, and I couldn’t have been happier for it. The enclosures are built for them and their comfort not tourists and bratty children smashing on glass walls that you’d typically see at a zoo. In fact out of 47 bears we only managed to see 3 as they roam freely as they please. The footage and facts we were shown on each bear was absolutely heart breaking, in fact I cried so hard a volunteer even offered me a hug.  Honestly if you have the chance to go. GO and support the work they do
drawbacks: bratty children smashing on glass walls
only managed to see 3 bears out of 47
highlights: most ethical sanctuary I've ever been to
enclosures are built for the bears' comfort
footage and facts were heart breaking
practical_tips: go and support the work they do

author: Daydream4444
title: Beautiful sanctuary
original_content: Such a wonderful place for the bears with a cruel, sad past. The Sanctuary is has quite great enclosures. The bears are doing very well. The guides are very professional and very informative. With admission the sanctuary supported and therefore highly recommended. These bears desperately need our support.

author: Wim V
title: Suporting a good foundation
original_content: Very nice experience, you have 3 options i will recomand the option with a guide. The passion of everybody that works here Day and night is incredible. It gives a very good feeling to suport a foundation like this. Also the bears are super cute, definitely when you see where they came from.
highlights: The passion of everybody that works here
Supporting a foundation like this gives a good feeling
practical_tips: Consider taking an option with a guide

author: Darin Merchant
title: Inspiring and absolutely worth it
original_content: We traveled to the sanctuary with a Grab from Ninh Binh. When we arrived there were very few people there and we decided to book the full tour which included watching a movie, visiting the sanctuary and doing the skywalk. Our guide was very passionate about the bears and their rescue and she could answer any and all questions we had. After the tour we had a delicious meal and finished it off with a fresh coconut coffee :) Absolutely worth it - they do such inspiring work!!
highlights: guide was very passionate about the bears and their rescue

author: zahra
title: Great Experience
original_content: Such a heart warming experience! They take care of the bears very well - The tour was great and well organized. Walking around the sanctuary felt peaceful and inspiring. Do visit the sanctuary if you have the chance.The food there is very yummy as well!
practical_tips: do visit the sanctuary if you have the chance

author: Paul D
title: A great place, a passionate team and beautiful creatures
original_content: Managed to get up to the Bear Sanctuary today, an amazing place full of passionate and dedicated people all trying their best to protect these beautiful creatures.The pre tour video almost brought me to tears but seeing the success and heart warming stories throughout my time there feeled me with hope and confidence for the future. A big shout out to our guide Nim, an absolute angel ❤️🙏Take the time out of your day to visit, a great place and an even better cause.
practical_tips: Take the time out of your day to visit

author: tess
title: Nice experience!!
original_content: I really enjoyed seeing how they take care of the bears at this bear sanctuary!! It is very interesting and certainly not a tourist attraction

author: David W
title: Great place to visit
original_content: This place was amazing in size & the care they give these rescued bears is outstanding would recommend this for anyone. The drive getting there is half the fun.
highlights: the care they give these rescued bears is outstanding

author: charbar93
title: Must visit for animal welfare lovers
original_content: This was such an incredible place. You can really see how well they take care of the bears, and do this in a very respectful way with the visitors. There is a lot of educational information which helped guests understand why this sanctuary is necessary. The scenery is also very beautiful. I would highly recommend visiting here and donating even a small amount to the sanctuary if you can! :)

author: Taïna R
title: Amazing experience
original_content: We loved the experience! Such a good cause and caring team! We strongly recommend to visit the sanctuary! We need more sanctuaries like that to protect animals from abuses!

author: Christine K
title: Watching the bears at play
original_content: We arrived at 9.30 am and the sanctuary was very quiet. Bears had been fed, so they were active in their enclosures. Walked the skywalk with a guide and had some great views of the bears playing, swimming, and resting. All the guides are very passionate about the bears having a better life now. Watched a 30 minute film that documents how they were treated whilst having bile collected. So cruel. But now they are being treated with love and respect. We highly recommend visiting Four Paws Bear Sanctuary.
highlights: great views of the bears playing, swimming, and resting
All the guides are very passionate about the bears having a better life now

author: Oscardog16
title: Well worth a visit.
original_content: Very nice sanctuary environment to care for bears who were so cruelly treated when being used for bile milking.The enclosures were full of trees and tall grass as well as enrichment structures. The bears were fed 3 times a day and were free to roam their area or go into their buildings.We rode a motorbike from Tam Coc, and it was easy to find.  It took approximately 50 minutes. A taxi from Tam Coc would have been about US$10 each way.We were shown an introductory video before being guided around the perimeter of some of the enclosures. We were then able to walk along the skywalk and could see into several of the enclosures. The cost was 250k VND and it appears there are no fixed times for tours, they are on demand.  We emailed the sanctuary enquiring about tour times, but we did not receive a reply. We arrived at about 1pm watched the video and joined a tour at 1.30 p.m.It was well worth the travel time to visit, and we will return when the Tiger sanctuary is opened. It is now under construction and is expected to finished by the end of 2024.
drawbacks: did not receive a reply to email inquiry
highlights: enclosures with trees and tall grass
practical_tips: email the sanctuary in advance to inquire about tour times
consider taking a motorbike from Tam Coc

author: Edwina
title: Wonderful sanctuary doing very good rehab work with the bears
original_content: Fantastic experience to see the good work being done to rescue bears from bile farming. We did the guided tour for 250k VND and well worth it. There is also a cheaper option to self tour for 50k. The sanctuary has a great vegetarian restaurant. Plan your visit to allow for lunch to support the cause. The mango smoothies are like gelato. So yummy.
highlights: cheaper option to self tour for 50k
practical_tips: plan your visit to allow for lunch to support the cause

author: maryjan2015
title: Such amazing work done here
original_content: They are doing such great work here.  It was a very touching experience to visit and hear how the bears are rescued and rehabilitated.  It was well worth the hour drive from Tam Coc.  If you’re looking for something different to do while in the area, I highly recommend.
practical_tips: look for something different to do

author: Jacky Chen
title: Suitable for children
original_content: Suitable for families taking young children out to play. A bit far from the center, not many activities. Easy to find location.........:::::::..........

author: Pathfinder674120
title: Great experience to see these wonderful bears.
original_content: What a great experience to see these gorgeous bears in person, so happy to see them finally living their best lives. We were given a welcome drink on arrival, then a guided tour of the facility to see the bears up close, wonderful to see how well the bears are cared for 🫶 highly recommended 👍

author: Sophia
title: Very great facility! Anytime again!
original_content: Absolutely recommended! A total of 45 bears are housed in the rescue center. Due to time constraints, we only did the skywalk (50,000 vnd) and still saw about 8 bears. author: Meg H

author: Marshall Presnick
title: Four Paws Bear Sanctuary
original_content: I was really happy to discover this place after living in Ninh Binh for a year. I've lived in Vietnam since 2011 and had heard only of the bear rescue in Tam Dao, so I was surprised to see signs for this bear sanctuary when I moved to Ninh Binh. When they recently updated their signs, I knew it was still a going concern and took my mom there when she was visiting. We had a great time, and a great tour. The facilities are very impressive - turns out the bears that are rescued and sent to Tam Dao then come and spend the rest of their lives in the comfort of the facilities here. The installations do a good job of educating visitors about the immoral and damaging trade in bear bile - and even more importantly, give the bears who have been caught up in this nefarious practice by poachers and trappers a place to live out their days in peace. We saw a ton of bears on our tour and they all seem happy to be safe and well-fed. I recommend for all ages, a great cause well executed.

After this, we were shown around the site and were lucky enough to see several bears very close up as they snuffled around in their enclosures. Our guide told us all about the bears, their tragic experiences and the amazing work the sanctuary is doing to rehabilitate them. We enjoyed a lovely lunch before watching the bears head in for their own meals from the skywalk. The whole experience was wonderful and every staff member we met was clearly passionate about the bears they care for and keen to share more about their cause. author: Antonia C
title: Must-do in Northern Vietnam
original_content: The highlight of my trip to Vietnam, and absolutely worth a day trip from Hanoi. I've been supporting Four Paws for years but to see their work in action, rescuing bears in desperate need from the bear bile industry, is something truly moving and awe-inspiring. The sanctuary itself is incredible, with large enclosures tailored perfectly to meet the needs of the rescued bears, informative educational facilities and a lovely restaurant serving great-value vegetarian food and drink for visitors. The staff are so friendly, dedicated and passionate, with a clear love for the bears and the critical work they do. There are a few options for how to spend your visit, ranging in price from 50K VND to 250K VND, with the latter package including a 45- minute guided sanctuary tour, self-guided skywalk experience (there are informative boards, videos and interactive activities throughout, as well as a gorgeous view over the enclosures and sanctuary) and viewing of a beautiful 30-minute film about the bears and sanctuary life in the air-conditioned presentation room. If making the trip from Hanoi, I'd strongly advise taking advantage of the centre's recommended driving service, Quang Anh Limosine. I arranged my own means of transport on the way there, being a bus company to Ninh Binh and a taxi for the remainder of my journey, but used Quang Anh's transportation service on the way back to Hanoi. This was a much better option, not only being more efficient and well organised but also much cheaper (200K VND, compared to the 750K VND I paid for the bus and taxi). If you're in Northern Vietnam, don't miss the chance to visit and support the work of this wonderful sanctuary. I won't be forgetting the incredible impact my visit had upon me anytime soon.
highlights: seeing the work of Four Paws in action
practical_tips: take advantage of the centre's recommended driving service, Quang Anh Limosine
go early to make the most of your visit

author: Buccaneer W
title: Brilliant, welcoming and insightful experience
original_content: I first heard of Four Paws Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh through a recommendation of a local who works at Save Vietnams Wildlife (another great place to visit!) I went alone, as a solo traveler, and was warmly welcomed at the front gate. Staff spoke good English and were absolutely lovely. I did a guided tour, which lasted about 45mins for 150.000 VND (about £5 in the UK). My guide was super knowledgeable and took me on a whole journey of how Four Paws has grown and it’s mission to protect and rescue bears in Vietnam from bile farming (a horrible practise I didn’t know about till my visit at the sanctuary). I was taken around al the enclosures and told stories about the individuals and general information about the bear species. As well as a look into the kitchen space and enrichment area where they create toys for the bears to encourage natural behaviours and improve welfare. The Sky walk gives you a whole other perspective of the sanctuary with a Birds Eye view of the enclosures. A great way to see the bears hidden from ground view. I would highly recommend visiting Ninh Binh Bear Sanctuary! 😊
