author: Harriet
title: Wonderful day out at fantastically run bear sanctuary.
original_content: Such a wonderful day out at a beautiful and quiet location. The Ninh Binh bear sanctuary rescues Asian Black Bears from captivity, illegal trade and bile farming. There are currently 46 bears here that you can see living freely in their large enriched enclosure. We went on the skyline walk and had a really informative (if sad!) tour which was excellently done! Also wonderful veggie food at fantastic prices!! Definitely reccommend!!

author: annabellewp
title: An eye opening wholesome experience! A must visit when in Ninh Binh 🤍
original_content: A must visit when going to Ninh Binh! I’m so glad we made the journey a little further out from where we were staying to visit this place. Our guide was SO passionate about the bears and rescuing them it really made the whole experience that much more enjoyable being guided around by someone who clearly cares so much about them. Such an interesting, heartbreaking, wholesome and eye opening day! Thank you ☺️

author: BikergirlzRock
title: Moon bears💖
original_content: We enjoyed our stop at the bear sanctuary.  Do the tour. You will learn a lot about the traditions that put moon bears at risk.  We really enjoyed our time!
highlights: learn a lot about the traditions that put moon bears at risk

author: madebooCalifornia
title: An absolute must-see!
original_content: This sanctuary is a hidden gem in the Ninh Binh area. It doesn’t get the attention it richly deserves. The facility is first rate, and they are doing amazing work to rescue moon bears from the cruel and disgusting bile trade. Be sure to do the guided tour. It’s well worth the minimal cost and the proceeds support the important work they’re doing. A++++

author: Tiara S
title: A must visit in Ninh Binh
original_content: We got the tour option which gave us an insight to how the bears were taken care of and the kinds of conditions they were rescued from. Recommend visiting here as they are doing great work and all the staff are very passionate about the work they do!

author: Laura M
title: Perfect day out
original_content: Paid for the guided tour was 150k and worth every Dong. Enjoyed learning about the bears and their history. Also enjoyed a vegetarian lunch which I would recommend!
highlights: enjoyed learning about the bears and their history

author: Leannie
title: Make time for the guided tour to not be disappointed
original_content: We were a bit pressed for time when we got here and so opted for the self guided tour as the assisted tour was another hour wait. It was a very short tour where you can go up the skywalk and look down on where some of the bears are but the self guided tour meant you were unable to walk around the perimeter and therefore probably have seen more bears.The other thing that was not great was the skywalk is one of the selling points but a good deal of the view is obscured by trees and overgrown bushes, I think they could be kept better maintained to aid the viewing.

author: Lisette W
title: Please visit!
original_content: We found this sanctuary through Tripadvisor and were very happy we went. When we got there we were very surprised by how well it all looks and how friendly the people are. It’s still not very known by visitors of the area. We got a wonderful private tour and a lot of interesting information about Moon bears. It’s also a reality check on how terrible these animals can be treated. Wonderful how they dedicate themselves to the welfare of Moon bears and the education on how these animals should be treated.
highlights: dedicate themselves to the welfare of Moon bears

author: Jolu T
title: No.1 place to go in Ninh Binh!!!!!
original_content: No.1 place to go when traveling to Ninh Binh!🖤 More people need to know about this wonderful place! We had a full tour (which was only 150,000d, basically £5, per person!!) of the sanctuary, learning everything there is to know about the bears that have been saved, their backgrounds and how they are given the best quality of life now.Our tour guide was so knowledgeable, giving us an intimate tour and showing us behind the scenes including the food preparation and quarantine area housing two young cubs (the latter from a distance of course!). We saw many bears during our tour, they were playing together and climbing trees in their big enclosures; it was such a special experience to be able to see these abused animals living naturally and in a way as close to wild as can be. The skywalk adds another level to the experience, and we watched as the bears were fed in the evening, which was fantastic!The reception/restaurant/gift shop/bathroom areas were all 5 star, with excellent cleanliness and service levels. If you’re travelling anywhere near Ninh Binh, take the short drive out to this sanctuary, it’ll be the best and most rewarding thing you’ll do here!P.S A note to the South African guy visiting the sanctuary from Germany, representing Four Paws, while we were there - Please be more respectful to the staff at the sanctuary, and if you are talking about business, best not to do it in front of paying customers!
drawbacks: Please be more respectful to the staff at the sanctuary
highlights: intimate tour and showing us behind the scenes
saw many bears during our tour, they were playing together and climbing trees in their big enclosures
practical_tips: take the short drive out to this sanctuary

author: Nippi0815
title: Worth to visit
original_content: Very nice institution.It was very interesting.The people there are very passionated.The work they do is really important.I would recommend it 😉

author: Jasmina A
title: Amazing place!!!
original_content: This place is amazing!!! You have to visit! They Care so so much for the Beats and the food and drinks are great aß Well. Please Go and give Them a little Tip. All the Money is for the Beats!!
highlights: They Care so so much for the Beats
practical_tips: Go and give Them a little Tip

author: Mai Le
title: A wonderful trip
original_content: I had no idea of how crude the bears were treated in Vietnam untill I went to this Sanctuary.  Seeing the violence those bears suffered have made my heart broken. Therefore, I feel heartwarming when I know they are safed and happy now in this sanctuary. You guys had done a wonderful job!! Keep it going!!!
drawbacks: The bears were treated crudely in Vietnam
highlights: The bears are safe and happy now
The staff had done a wonderful job

author: Brigid W
title: Bears!
original_content: After a disappointing morning trying to see the animals at Cuc Phuong and failing, it was lovely to come here and see these absolutely stunning animals being so well cared for after having such horrible lives. I appreciate how much effort they put in to ensure that the bears have the best life from now on and I LOVE that the sanctuary creates employment for local people too! Keep doing what you're doing! I loved visiting and will be back next weekend with a friend!!

author: Brigitte G
title: A MUST-VISIT attraction near Cuc Phuong National Park
original_content: Visiting the FOUR PAWS Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh was one of the highlights of our two-week trip to Vietnam. The facility is nothing short of marvellous and the people there work SO HARD to ensure a good experience for the bears and visitors alike. Our guide there was by far one of the most knowledgeable we have encountered in all of Vietnam, and she provided a rich description of the bear bile situation in Asia, and a heart-warming (yet realistic) tour of the sanctuary. Also, the food in the restaurant was SO GOOD! Our tour guide ordered for us ahead of our arrival and I think we basically had one of each dish on the menu, and some off-menu dishes too. Everything was so delicious and fresh, and vegan, too. One of the best meals we had in the country - surprising as this is quite a remote area! The gift shop features local artists and original crafts you won't find elsewhere. Perfect for authentic souvenirs. If you are planning on visiting Cuc Phuong National Park, I strongly recommend you stop here as well. The tour is free and it will help you understand an important part of the wildlife conservation movement in Vietnam. THANK YOU to all volunteers and workers of the sanctuary. Your efforts are noticed and appreciated all around the world.
extracted_spaces: FOUR PAWS Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh
highlights: one of the highlights of our two-week trip to Vietnam
the facility is nothing short of marvellous
one of the best meals we had in the country
practical_tips: stop here as well if you are planning on visiting Cuc Phuong National Park

author: Odyssey06307974425
title: Ninh Binh Bear Sanctuary
original_content: We had visited other sanctuarys in the area earlier in the day and were left a little disappointed.We arrived at the Bear Sanctuary later in the afternoon and were welcomed by very friendly and knowledgeable staff. We did the tour (parts very sad hearing about the bears previous treatment but life so much better for them now). So pleased that we stopped and did tour - the highlight of our Ninh Binh stay. Late afternoon a good time as feeding time and able to see bears foraging for food their keepers had hidden around the grounds. Thank you to the sanctuary for the wonderful work you do.  Garry & Anne Adcock. Australia
highlights: highlight of our Ninh Binh stay

author: chris-dusty
title: Great New Bear Sanctuary
original_content: Very well set up facilities for both bears and visitors. Lovely food (for the humans) and interesting tour. Well worth the visit.

author: Florian K
title: Must visit if you are around Ninh Binh
original_content: Really worth the visit :) Definitely take a scooter to get there as the landscape on the way is beautiful. The Bear Sanctuary is really interesting, the guides are very helpful and tell you a lot of information about the bears. Their English is also great!
highlights: tell you a lot of information about the bears
practical_tips: take a scooter to get there

author: villytod
title: Great Experience!
original_content: We had a fun day out visiting the Bear Sanctuary. We went around feeding time (1:30 pm) so got to see all the bears outside. It was also sad to learn about bile production, but necessary to understand why this sanctuary is doing such good work!
drawbacks: sad to learn about bile production
highlights: got to see all the bears outside

author: Jakub D
title: A nice place to visit
original_content: Me and my girlfriend Miška made a motorbike trip there from Cosy Son hotel near Ninh Bình.. though it seems like far place to go and no worth visiting from there I must say that THIS really touched me in possitive  way and it was definitely one our best experience around Ninh Bình.I did not know what to expect how we were getting closer and closer - it is cut off the city, but when we arrived I understood why and was glad for it. When we arrived a really kind young lady told us what’s going on this place, showed us interesting videos of bears and stuff. Our guide tour started after 1:00 pm so we had some time to take a lunch. Food you can choose from menu there is not overpriced at all how would you expect. We both love meat meals but we tried a vegetarian meals and it was amazing ! Nice and kind service.Our lady guide took us around pavilions and showed us bears and how they care about them. And one would never say that it’s not a simple thing. You can also buy some nice environment-friendly-made souvenirs to support this organisation.I really appreciate what these guys are doing for these poor animals and I recommend everyone to visit this Sanctuary and support it. Thanks a lot guys, wish you all the best !
highlights: Really touched me in positive way
One of our best experiences around Ninh Bình

author: Tony S
title: A meaningful experience
original_content: We went to visit the sanctuary for half a day.  We were shown the videos about the bears suffered in bear farms then they were rescued to live a happy life. Then your heart will move with happiness witnessing the bears playing happily in the natural area. Had an absolutely delicious vegan meal with fried tofu, fried sweet potato, fried mungbean pancake (highly recommend). Very interesting souvenir shops with many affordable items that are local produced.  It is a must destination when you are in Ninh Binh. Compared to Cuc Phuong national park, this place is more peaceful and it is better organized to prioritize the wellness of the bears. Four Paws org. did a well done job here!

author: Trang Peji
title: The best bear sanctuary i've ever seen before.
original_content: The staff are extremely friendly. Those bears look so free and happy.I had a great experience. I will visit again.

author: JLM41
title: Amazing place, doing amazing work
original_content: Visited the sanctuary in Ninh Binh today as we are on vacation in Vietnam and we donate to Four Paws. What a fantastic place and amazing people. we were so touched by the incredible stories about the bears.   I am so proud to support this worthy cause. Keep up the good work and thanks for the tour you gave us. ❤️❤️❤️❤️

author: Adamjanis
title: Be Bear Aware 🐻
original_content: We saw the signs for the bear sanctuary while riding around Ninh Binh on a motorbike, and followed our guts to check it out... We're really glad we did! You can watch the bears for free from an informational viewing deck, but I would highly recommend the tour. The wonderful guide took us to the 4 different bear enclosures and the bear kitchen where they  prepare all of the food. There's a lot of information about how they are mistreated and the efforts to save them... They're doing some great work there! And the food (for humans) is delicious. Hands down, the best coffee we had in Vietnam!

author: Josephineburrows
title: Must see, beautiful rescue bears
original_content: We had an amazing time here!! We scooted out from our accomodation in Trang An and it was a lovely scenic ride. We ate lunch at the Bear Sanctuary (delicious, recommend sesame cake for dessert!). We had a guided tour of the bear sanctuary at 1.30pm (recommend going 9-10.30 or 1-2.30 as that is feeding time). Our tour guide was brilliant and is involved in rescuing the bears. She explained the bile extraction and gave lots of information on the individual characteristics of the bears (like favourite food, their bear friends).The people here do amazing work! I recommend visiting and doing the tour, eating lunch and buying souvenirs to support them :)
practical_tips: buy souvenirs to support the sanctuary

author: Patty041994
title: Great place for all animal lovers!
original_content: We visited the sanctuary during our stay in Ninh Binh. It’s easy to go there by scooter. I would really recommend to book a tour to learn more about the bears and the sanctuary. The staff was awesome and we had some delicious vegan lunch there. It was a great visit and I would definitely go there again.Keep up the good work! :-)

author: Misst
title: Excellent - very informative and nice to see bears
original_content: We enjoyed our time at the sanctuary for bears who were used to extract bike. It was very educational but also we walked around and saw the bears playing and eating, heard about their stories and saw their food being made. It was really enjoyed by the teens. Good cafe/gift shop too.
highlights: saw the bears playing and eating

author: Dirk H v
title: Sustainable sanctuary with friendly staff
original_content: Very good, informative and attractive spot. Well organised.Good restaurant.Sustainable premisses.Lots of information in the situation of bile bears.

author: ND
title: Amazing place with beautiful bears
original_content: The bear sanctuary is a must see if you're in Vietnam. Not only is it educational , but it also has the most beautiful rescue bears of all ages ,with incredible stories. It was so lovely to see the bears being able to just be bears again, playing and swimming etc.. I could spend all day watching them! There's also a restaurant with delicious food and friendly staff working at the sanctuary, who are happy to answer any questions. I would love to go again if I am ever back in Vietnam.
highlights: lovely to see the bears being able to just be bears again

author: Rose
title: Great place to visit
original_content: Everything about this place is good. Staff, facilities for bears, ability to see the day to day life of both bears and humans, food in their cafe and goods in their shop.I would recommend anyone to go there whether or not you have children. The staff are so lovely and informative and very happy to show you around. I enjoyed this much more than the Ninh Binh caves.

food in their cafe and goods in their shop

author: Paula P
title: A must: Rescued bears and beautiful scenery!
original_content: A visit to BEAR SANCTUARY Ninh Binh is not only educational but also emotional to see former bile bears finally enjoying their life. It was great to see the bears frolicking in their huge natural enclosures with great care of the amazing FP Viet team. I would highly recommend a visit! P.S: the restaurant has extremely yummy food.

great care of the amazing FP Viet team

author: Joost
title: Beautiful sanctuary with helpfull people
original_content: It is a beautiful place and the people are willing to give you all the information you need. Big facility with a lot of bear and there is also a restaurant.
highlights: willing to give you all the information you need

author: Marie P
title: Great visit to a worthy cause
original_content: We added our visit to the Bear Sanctuary after a day at Cuc Phuong National Park. We received a warm welcome to the centre, which has free entry and were given excellent explanations from Hang (we hope we've remembered your name correctly) who obviously really cared about the bears and our visit. We didn't eat anything at the centre (but the food looked great, especially as it is all vegetarian) but did have a delicious coffee.The bears have huge enclosures and are well looked after.I recommend spending around an hour here to find out about the work they are doing and support the cause.

author: ChiaraBren
title: Good cause, good people
original_content: I didn't even know about the problem of bile bears still being kept at farms around Vietnam. It was grueling to see the fate of so many bears that are being kept in this small cages for all their life!Saving them is an important act of humanity. The Bear sanctuary in Ninh Binh does an amazing job, the bears are really happy in their new home! Thanks for the tour and the great gift shop!
drawbacks: bile bears still being kept at farms around Vietnam
small cages for all their life
highlights: Bear sanctuary in Ninh Binh does an amazing job
bears are really happy in their new home

author: Erik A
title: Very interesting and important!
original_content: It was such an interesting visit with loads of information. We had no clue this was a thing in Vietnam, they are doing a great job!

author: ogg16
title: Bears like Pumpkin ~ Who Knew?!
original_content: Four Paws was quite difficult to find but I’m so glad we persevered. The life stories of the bears are utterly heartbreaking but now they are living their best bear lives. The staff are so friendly and seemed genuinely pleased to see us. The full tour (please take it and please spend the money) was informative and full of surprises and my guide spoke perfect English. The cafe is new, spotless and very reasonable. They are looking to rescue 100 bears. I hope they get to this number as soon as they can.
highlights: life stories of the bears are utterly heartbreaking
staff are so friendly and seemed genuinely pleased to see us
full tour was informative and full of surprises

author: petervM2898HG
title: Great initiative tonsave these beautifull bears
original_content: Great people that trying to save these beautifull bears from extinction in Vietnam. Go visit them so they get supported in changing the way the Vietnamese people think about these bears
highlights: trying to save these beautifull bears from extinction

author: F.C./SUI
title: Fantastic work for the animals
original_content: We visited the new and very beautiful bear sanctuary in this very big and natural area. The staff there is so very friendly and we really felt that they work with passion for giving the bears a better life. They informed us about their area, the rescued bears with their horrible histories and the work they do in this sanctuary.In addition, the shop and the restaurant were so very nice. Many handcraft souvenirs - local made staff are there to sell. The food is delicious and vegetarian for sure. We are so happy that we saw their work. Please donate for this company, every cent helps to give the animals a better life.
highlights: passion for giving bears a better life

author: SH Seah
title: Great place to observe bears and support the cause!!
original_content: We stumbled onto this sanctuary after seeing a sign " Bear Sanctuary 29km this way". When we arrived, we had to wait awhile (there's a vegan cafe so pretty good place to chill) before the tour started. The tour was really educational, even my guide and driver came along to learn more about the bear bile industry and why these bears needed to be rescued. The bears were allowed to forage and exhibit natural behaviours in their sanctuary, and the staff and volunteers really cared for them. Highly recommended!PS: There is a primate sanctuary and a tortoise sanctuary nearby in the national park as well and you can complete all of them in about half day.
highlights: allowed to forage and exhibit natural behaviours

author: Dan G
title: Fascinating, heartbreaking and uplifting
original_content: I went to the Sanctuary with some friends while we were staying in the nearby Cuc Phuong National Park. We had a great, detailed tour of the centre, where we got to see the bears in their enclosures, see where they get medical care and meet the dedicated staff who look after them. We had a fascinating tour of the kitchens where teams of people prepare the huge quantities of food the animals need. I found the story of how the bears were treated by bile farmers heartbreaking - it brought tears to my eyes just thinking about how anyone could treat animals like that - one bear had had her paws chopped off to be used in a traditional medicine! However, it was so great to see the rescued bears relaxing in the sun and enjoying being outside - sometimes for the first time in their lives. We saw one bear who, the keepers said, would stay outside even when it was pouring with rain, just because he had spent his whole life in a cage in a dark room and wanted to stay in the light.There was a great little shop where I got some souvenirs and a journal, and I left the sanctuary feeling very glad that there were dedicated, passionate people in the world trying to help these animals and stop this horrible practice - a bright light of compassion amidst the gloom.I would totally recommend making a visit if you're in the area, and supporting the Four Paws charity in this important, valuable work. Five stars from me!
drawbacks: bile farmers treating animals in a horrible way
highlights: rescued bears relaxing in the sun
practical_tips: visit if you're in the area

author: FloatIntoTheMystic
title: Animal Lovers: Don’t Miss Out!
original_content: My friend and I visited Four Paws Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh and were very surprised to learn about the horrific conditions these bile bears were living in before they were rescued. Our guide was very informative and answered all our questions with integrity and passion for animal welfare. I’ll admit I held back tears several times hearing stories of individual bears and how they live in a vegetative state. However, it was wonderful to see these rescued bears out roaming in their enclosures, living the beat possible life they can. They looked very happy at the sanctuary. We were guided throughout the facility and even got to see the kitchen where staff was preparing meals for the bears. This was my favorite activity we did in the area as I found it eye-opening and inspirational to help organizations like Four Paws.

author: Ashley H
title: Incredible place!
original_content: Went here with a friend and learned about the sad truth of what happens everyday in a life of a bile bear. I left in tears wishing I could do more for these bears who are tortured every day just for bile that apparently is believed to be medicinal. This is a place where the bears get a second chance to live a normal life. Amazing bears! Amazing staff! Thank you for all you do!!

author: frangipansi91
title: Remember it's not a zoo
original_content: Our visit to the Bear Sanctuary in Ninh Binh was beautiful. They are doing a great job fighting everyday to rescue all the bears that are still in captivity. We were lucky to see three of the bears playing aroung in the pool and climbing trees. Please remember it is not a zoo, so don't expect to find the bears showing off for you. Thanfully in this place they have a home where they can enjoy life with no pressure at all, that meaning among other things "being ready" for human visitors ;)
drawbacks: don't expect to find the bears showing off for you
highlights: great job fighting everyday to rescue all the bears
see three of the bears playing aroung in the pool and climbing trees
practical_tips: don't expect to find the bears showing off for you

author: Helen
title: Important bear rescue centre
original_content: The sanctuary rescues bears who have been taken and kept in captivity, and abused for use in traditional medicine.We had a very interesting and informative tour of the sanctuary - very sad to hear of what the bears have been through during their lives, but lovely to see them being well looked after now.
drawbacks: bears have been through during their lives
highlights: bears being well looked after now

author: Jean Gaetan G
title: Great! Hard to find though, on maps, look for "Four Paws Viet"
original_content: Not easy to find, so on your phone, look for "Four Paws Viet"The initiative is heart-warming, the staff so nice, the place is cozy and also nice to take a break/coffee/lunch. Everything is done with care and affection, and you can sense a very heartfelt initiative. A must in Ninh Binh!
practical_tips: look for 'Four Paws Viet' on your phone

author: MaximeLecl
title: Fantastic and informative visit thanks to the staff !
original_content: First let me say that this is place is for rescued bears and is nothing like a zoo.The staff of the bear sanctuary is not only doing a great job guiding in the sanctuary and educating the people about the bear situation in Vietnam but they also study the behavior of the bears, establish the right diet for them, improve their ability to walk, and make them progressively reuse their claws, tooth and sense of smell (I'm not saying how so you can discover it during your visit).The stories of the bears are frankly depressing but that's the sad reality.Also, they will never be released back in the wild but this sanctuary is a true chance for them to now live a peaceful life.The staff is passionate about what they do and it's fair to say that the bears look happy and relaxed. They are really charming!They love sunny weather but even on a rainy day we were lucky to spot them.Feeding times are 8am, 1pm and 4pm.If you plan to visit, it's best to give a quick call to check if they have a guide available.The sanctuary is very close to Cuc Phuong National Park so if you are visiting the national park you can stop for 1-2hrs there.To the team working there: keep up with the great work!
drawbacks: The stories of the bears are frankly depressing
highlights: The staff is passionate about what they do
The bears look happy and relaxed
practical_tips: Give a quick call to check if they have a guide available
Stop for 1-2hrs if visiting Cuc Phuong National Park

author: jasanna2019
title: Such an important place!
original_content: We didn’t know about the sanctuary but it was suggested and I’m so glad we went. Our 3 children especially learnt so much and were shocked by what happens to bears. Our 10 year old decided straight away that we had to spend money on souvenirs so we could support your work. It really had an impact. We loved our lunch and were very impressed with your facilities. A great experience and one that we hope more can see and learn from.
practical_tips: spend money on souvenirs to support their work

author: Tara Q
title: Learned a lot!
original_content: One of The very kind employees walked us around and gave us a ton of information on the bears, was very interesting and I learned a lot! Had no idea about the bear situation in SE Asia.

author: jennA
title: Wonderful Visit
original_content: We visited the Bear Sanctuary yesterday and had not booked a tour but the staff were great and accommodating. Our tour guide (we did not get her name unfortunately) was very knowledgable and passionate about the plight of the bears. Very sad the damage humans do to these magnificent creatures.We need to apply pressure to Governments in Asian countries to make this practice illegal. It is illegal to draw bile from bears in Vietnam but not illegal to keep bears in tiny horrid cages. And Ofcourse why else to keep a bear without taking bile. China as always has no animal welfare laws and still legal to abuse all animals. We must continue pressure for change.
drawbacks: damage humans do to these magnificent creatures
highlights: very knowledgable and passionate tour guide
practical_tips: apply pressure to Governments in Asian countries to make this practice illegal

author: O L
title: Unique and important
original_content: This sanctuary is so important. We learned that there are still more then 1000 bears captured and abused in Vietnam. The place is new and and built in such quality we never witnessed in vietnam! The staff is very knowledgeable and the tour we had was eye opening and interesting. You get to see the bears (which are so cute) and hear about their sad stories. You also got to visit the kitchen (which is cleaner than most of the restaurants kitchens we saw in Vietnam!) and learn what the bears eat and how to make soup for them :) There’s also a cute and cheap gift shop and a really (really!) tasty vegetarian restaurant inside. This is still an unknown place as it opened its gates to tourists only a few months ago. Go visit!
practical_tips: open to tourists only a few months ago

author: Seana07
title: Amazing work rescuing bears, great place to visit
original_content: Located near the entrance to the national Park Four Paws bear sanctuary is doing amazing work in offering refuge to bear’s that were rescued from the abhorrent bear bile farming industry.   He’s beers are now allowed to roam free and act like bears. Tour was great and informative. The staff there is very kind and truly do seem to enjoy the work, giving great stories of the Bears background. Great for solo travelers or traveling with families.
practical_tips: great for solo travelers or traveling with families

author: Cecco_Rivolta
title: Two truly beautiful days
original_content: Beautiful place. On the first day, we took a bike ride around the town of Tam Coc, traveling along paths in the middle of the ponds and limestone formations that characterize the area. By bicycle, we reached and visited the Bich Dong pagoda, and in the afternoon, we reached the Hang Mua viewpoint, from the top of which you can admire a stunning panorama.On the second day, we took a boat tour starting from Trang An. Very nice tour, stunning views, including spotting monkeys a few meters from the boat.Tip: in the rainy season, boat tour routes might be limited due to the higher water level, which could in some cases obstruct the cave passages between one stretch of the river and the next.
drawbacks: boat tour routes might be limited due to the higher water level
highlights: spotting monkeys a few meters from the boat
practical_tips: in the rainy season, boat tour routes might be limited due to the higher water level

author: Sightsee28950251738
title: Three cups.
original_content: I prefer to go by boat but I like to take pictures at Tam Cok port in the old lake area. There are beautiful northern bridges.

author: Viet Experiences Travel
title: Tam Coc - Bich Dong: Worth the hype? Absolutely.
original_content: Floating down the Ngo Dong River surrounded by massive limestone cliffs and ripe, golden rice fields feels like stepping right into a painting. Watching the locals expertly row the boats with their feet is incredible. Plus, the ancient cave pagoda at Bich Dong has the most photogenic stone bridge in Vietnam.
highlights: watching the locals expertly row the boats with their feet

author: vfmen
title: A must-do
original_content: A very beautiful experience to be able to navigate peacefully on this river.There were very few people, and we felt almost alone.The landscapes are surprising, and our rower, at 72 years old, was charming.Honestly, I could not have done what she did during those 2 hours.I highly recommend it

author: Noemie
title: Nice discovery
original_content: Great discovery and very friendly people. Really nice.

author: Noemie
title: Beautiful! Things to do once in a lifetime
original_content: Superb discovery of the terrestrial Halong Bay. Lots of people on the boats but not much to climb see the view, whichd is just beautiful
drawbacks: Lots of people on the boats

author: Daniel F
title: Beautiful boat tour through rice fields and karst landscape
original_content: I only made the boat trip for 250,000 VND, without the trips to the temples. The ticket office is not located at the starting point of the boat tour in the middle of Tam Coc, but you will be driven from this very place with winem small, yellow vehicle for free to the ticket office (about 5 min drive).The boats are rowing boats that can accommodate 3-4 people.The boat tour offers very nice views of the charming area. The body of water passes through rice fields lined with high and steep karst rocks and through caves and lasts around 1.5 hours. If you're lucky, you can spot mountain goats climbing.On the return journey, drivers offer embroidered images for sale.If you have enough time, I recommend not only doing this boat tour, but also the one at Trang An.
drawbacks: Ticket office not located at starting point
practical_tips: Go to ticket office for free
Buy embroidered images on return journey

author: George Severin
title: Mass tourism but a "must".
original_content: Ninh Binh is a province in North Vietnam famous for its Trang An landscape. We were also in the community of Tam Coc and booked an organized day tour. The tour included a boat trip on the Ngo Dong River. Very nice, slow boat trip in the middle of a beautiful and interesting landscape of rocks, pagodas and caves. The journey took 2 hours. And yes, it is very touristy, it is about mass tourism actually but everything is very well organized.We have not experienced any of these negative experiences from pushy saleswomen. Our day tour was well organized, the guide very competent and this tour in itself not necessarily favorable for Vietnamese standards (about 50.-€ p.P.) and it is something you do once in a lifetime.
highlights: beautiful and interesting landscape of rocks, pagodas and caves

author: Lavender
title: Beautiful scenery, to much pushing sales
original_content: We took a 1,5 hour boat ride in Tam Coc and it was ok. If you have the time, I would reccomend. But know that the place you buy tickets is far from the entrance to the boat ride (free trolley transport), and they push a lot of sales on you that felt very off for us. Both the person «feet-rowing» and especially a woman taking pictures of us, printed and that was so difficult to get to understand that we didn’t want the pictures and never asked for them.
drawbacks: place you buy tickets is far from the entrance
push a lot of sales on you
woman taking pictures of us without asking

author: ppp
title: Incredible foot-rowing but prepare for a rushed ride
original_content: Pros: The ticketing experience is quick and efficient. Hardly any queue to get a boat. Get to see a unique rowing technique (with the feet). You can get a package that includes some temple tours. Cons: Our boat person just wanted to get it over with as quick as possible. Didn't stop at any of the piers (which were listed in the map). To be fair, this was probably because there was a queue of boats going up and down the place. It's as though you're part of some amusement park ride. On the way back, she tried to sell us some local paintings and was very pushy about tipping.
drawbacks: boat person was in a hurry
practical_tips: get a package with temple tours

author: Lohit V
title: Lovely moments in the most beautiful place in Vietnam
original_content: Took a boat ride in Tam Coc and it was such a peaceful and scenic experience. Floating along the river surrounded by limestone mountains and rice fields felt almost unreal. Passing through the caves was a unique highlight.  The ride is slow and relaxing, perfect if you just want to enjoy nature and take photos. It can get a bit busy, but it never felt too overwhelming.  Definitely one of the must-do experiences in Ninh Binh simple, calm, and very beautiful.
highlights: perfect if you just want to enjoy nature and take photos

author: Huckleberry W
title: Great ride but beware of photographers
original_content: Nice experience. Went early to avoid crowds and heat. Watch out for photographers in boats who will take your picture and then print off a whole album of photos and demand payment. Also be prepared for boat rowers to push souvenirs (hidden away in bucket with lid) and demand a tip in a pushy way. The ride itself was amazing but these things soured the experience a little. We did the combo tour that included two temples and a cave and we’re glad we did the package deal as we ticked off a bunch of things we wanted to do in Tam Coc all in one go.
drawbacks: boat rowers pushing souvenirs and demanding a tip
practical_tips: go early to avoid crowds and heat

author: Mr9xx
title: Waive Mou
original_content: Loved the purple lotus flowers!Taking a boat to see the landscape with beautiful limestone mountains was amazing.The river feels wild and natural in the best way.Definitely worth

author: Luca Magnanensi
title: Tam Coc is the place to stay
original_content: My wife and I stayed at Tam Coc 4 nights and I must say that the choice was spot on, it is located in the most convenient spot to visit the main attractions of the area and its small town offers great tranquility, but also some tourist services that make the holiday more relaxing and nice

author: caroleen78
title: Attraction n1
original_content: Taking a tam side boat is probably the most popular attraction 2 on a boat and you leave for 1h30 of ride.the particularities of men and women sail with their legs.I've never seen this before it's very sporty really and they do it with great ease The landscapes are beautiful limestone karst rocks and water everywhere it is the terrestrial Ninh Binh for taste of Along Bay.You will see water lilies pass under tunnels with beautiful colors.So yes it is very touristic but it supports whole families.They will propose on the return of very pretty embroidered photo frames, you are not obliged of course but it is handmade and handmade. May this nature remain intact

author: Conny Bob
title: Vietnam’s most enchanting gem!
original_content: Absolutely breathtaking—this place left us utterly spellbound! Without a doubt, one of the most stunning gems in all of Vietnam. A must-see that will steal your heart!

author: user0255
title: Could have been a nice memory
original_content: initially, I actually quite enjoyed it and thought, I'd do this again or recommend it to others. while the cave was impressive and memorable, there was something even more memorable, with a sour taste. the boat 'driver''s incessant want for money. at the start, she was nice and all, pointing out parts of scenery and smiling, even complimenting us. now i wonder if that's out of the goodness of her heart or to make us open our wallets more. at a point in the tour, she stopped at what seemed like a dead end to try and sell us souviners. initially me and my dad said no, since we didn't want nor need any, but she kept pressuring us and there was no where to run, so we gave in and bought a magnet for 50k dong, which is really expensive. after that, she still wasnt satisfied, still trying to sell us other stuff, which were all terribly overpriced. at that point, i was already quite irritated, but tried to sympathise, but it left me upset for the remainder of the ride. just when i thought the money-making tricks were over, at the end of the boat ride she asked for a tip. well, its not uncommon in vietnam, but we had already bought overpriced souviners, and tried refusing, but she was adamant. we caved in and passed her 20k dong, which to out shock, she insisted on 100k dong. i was so appalled, never had i seen someone blatantly ask for so much. at that point, i was already looking forward to getting off, so much as to half standing up before she even stopped at the end. i was genuinely angry and if not for the boat 'driver', this would have been a great memory. the 2 out of 5 was for the scenery. it really was nice, with the mountains and caves, which i enjoyed. i even saw a few ducks and goats.
extracted_times: at a point in the tour
highlights: pointing out parts of scenery and smiling

author: Nita H
title: Tam Coc boat ride
original_content: The water lilies were in full bloom, and the boat ride went through a beautiful part of the river. Our rower, a middle-aged lady, seemed to be in a hurry to finish our boat ride, and quickly turned the boat after emerging from a cave, instead of parking the boat to let us disembark at one of the very beautiful stop-overs. I protested, and she reluctantly turned the boat again. I was disgusted and furious, as we had paid for the whole of this trip. She later tried to sell us a picture album, then demanded a tip-- I refused all her efforts, as she had tried to cheat us. The area passed was truly beautiful, the electric car ride was less exciting. And, yes, the Tamcoc ride is prettier than the Trang An ride, though Trang An is much better organised.
drawbacks: rower seemed to be in a hurry

author: Jim Gralton
title: Highly Scenic but real risks -- need to take care
original_content: This is a magical area with a scenic boat trip, a stiff 500 step climb to top of Dragon Mountain as well as a cycle trip along very flat, varied and very attractive countryside.The boat trip was serene though wonderful scenery. Well worth it and breath-taking which included a series of cave passageways. The trips are well ordered and regulated. However many of the boat-people expected their passengers to buy pictures / souvenirs and provide tips. They can be persistent but can be resisted.Climbing Dragon Mountain is a challenge. Most of the steps were smooth, well maintained and safe to climb but there were some uneven spots which were a risk especially coming down and in the wet. As well good climbing footwear should be mandatory.There seems little regulation of the numbers climbing the Mountain which must be a real risk at time.At the top there is a pleasant viewing spot but the dragon is on a separate craggy, rocky outcrop. This can get over-congested and must be potentially very dangerous especially in wet weather with people wearing sandals, crocs and other inappropriate footwear. This need much stronger regulation.
drawbacks: boat-people expected their passengers to buy pictures / souvenirs and provide tips
some uneven spots which were a risk especially coming down and in the wet
little regulation of the numbers climbing the Mountain
practical_tips: good climbing footwear should be mandatory

author: Patricia
title: Very nice surroundings
original_content: The tour is beautiful, and although it is ultra touristic we found it quite authentic, within what we can fit.A huge catch is that it is very difficult to understand how tickets are taken out. Where supposedly the ticket office is only sell you a tour with stops included, if you only want the tour by the river you have to board an electric bus that takes you to another ticket office three minutes away where they sell you only the tour. But as much as we asked, no one explained how we had what to do and for a moment they were taken away from us. I think they should improve this point quite a bit. The people carrying the boats continue to paddle with their feet, and the surroundings are beautiful, in some parts it is impressive. The boatwoman was quite friendly, at the last moment she offered to buy some sheets but it was nothing heavy, and asked us for the tip, but nothing happens, enters into the experience and we thought we would give it to her. We also expected everything to be full of street vendors, but just one person offered us a photo at first, we said no and he didn’t insist. Maybe this was because we did it very early in the morning, maybe later there are more vendors. The duration is 1h 30min long or so, it is worth it. We liked it better than Trang An. If I had to do one of them again, it would be this one, although I know that people prefer the other one because they visit more things.
drawbacks: difficult to understand how tickets are taken out
people carrying the boats continue to paddle with their feet
practical_tips: go early to avoid street vendors

author: Emily
title: Amazing Experience, but be careful with some sales tactics
original_content: Boat ride was so beautiful & peaceful.Quite long at about 1.5 hours but very much enjoyed it; stunning scenery & wildlife.  Boat itself was well maintained & very stable; driver very good also.They did try to sell items to us, and my friends did report some hard tactics; also very direct about tip at the end. Photographer also available, but my friends reported changing prices & hard tactics again - so be prepared.
practical_tips: Be prepared for hard tactics from photographers

author: misterfuss
title: scenic and not a tourist trap
original_content: We purchased only the boat ride.  The boat ride was a very good and without any of the negative experiences in old reviews.  The price is standardized now, with a ticket office some distance away from the boats.  The rower did not stop halfway through and try to negotiate a higher fare, as warned in older reviews.  A boat approached to take our picture for money, but it was very soft sell and easy to refuse.  Be sure to wear a protective hat, possibly bring a sun umbrella, and wear plenty of mosquito repellent.  Use sun block, because the river is not in the shade.  Expect to give your rower a tip when dropped off at the dock.  I asked at our hotel beforehand to know what was an appropriate amount.     Halfway through the experience the boat turns back and retraces the first half of the journey.  There’s one particular section where the summit of Mua Cave / Lying Dragon Mountain is visible.  On another section going through a valley with steep limestone walls monkeys were calling out to each other.  During our visit in early May, the vegetation along the river was just starting to turn yellow green, as seen in the famous promotional photos.     One stop along the journey is allowed and included in the price, but that is not communicated well.  We stopped at Dinh May (Cloud Peak).  There is a sign for Dinh May (Cloud Peak) after passing through the first cave.  Once we knew the location, we waited until the return journey to request the stop.  It is a hike up some stairs to an elevated look out over Tam Coc river and very scenic.   Reading reviews, I was really torn between the Tam Coc and Tràng An boat rides.  For our short overnight visit to Ninh Binh, I has very happy with my choice of the Tam Coc boat ride.
drawbacks: One stop along the journey is allowed and included in the price, but that is not communicated well.
highlights: The boat ride was a very good and without any of the negative experiences in old reviews.
The rower did not stop halfway through and try to negotiate a higher fare, as warned in older reviews.
The vegetation along the river was just starting to turn yellow green, as seen in the famous promotional photos.
practical_tips: Give your rower a tip when dropped off at the dock

author: Wendell Wiggins

author: tig68er
title: Beautiful Tam Coc - but don't visit in a tour group!
original_content: Tam Coc was an amazing place and we could have spent so much longer here enjoying the unique beauty of the landscapes.  Being on an organised trip though this wasn't possible but next time would stay in accommodation at Tam Coc and spend the time exploring the beautiful little town that it is. We did the boat trip through the caves and up the river for a way but this is where the disadvantage of being on an organised tour was a downside in that the majority rules what happens.  Sadly most tour participants only wanted a 1 hour ride which didn't get us into the iconic open river plain area at all and we turned around and went back. author: Xuan Son Travel

author: Luca A

author: Liliane M
title: MUST SEE PLACE IN TAM COC
original_content: Recognized as the land Halong Bay and it is.The walk runs on the Ngo Dong River between mountains with rice paddies on both sides although in January it cannot be seen.The typical sampan boat ride in which the gentleman paddles with his feet and lasts about an hour.During the tour you cross three caves but beware of the head, bend down to enter them.It seems to me a must-see place and very beautiful.I recommend it.

author: Webster Lee
title: Tam Coc's scenic waters
original_content: The unique geological formations and tranquil river cruises made for a mesmerizing experience. We drifted through stunning limestone karsts and lush rice paddies, feeling truly connected to nature. The peaceful ambiance was perfect for a romantic escape, and the local boat guides added a touch of charm with their warm hospitality.

author: Brigida C
title: Tam Coc River
original_content: Very nice landscape, the boat ride was amazing passing thru the limestone caves.A UNESCO heritage site.Enjoyed watching the localpeople planting rice alongside the river.It was one of the greatest trip for me.

author: Cassidy D
title: One of our favourite places
original_content: Absolutely loved our time in Tam Coc! It has a chill vibe and the perfect place to relax and adventure the surrounding landscapes for 3 or 4 days.We took the overnight train from Da Nang to Ninh Binh and arrived around 4am. Definitely set an alarm as it’s wasn’t super clear we were arriving. We easily got a taxi to Tam Coc at that time. Found it helpful to check with our local hotel via WhatsApp what the estimated fee would be to avoid being overcharged (we paid 100k VND).Stayed at Tam Coc Victoria Hotel in the centre of town. The rooms were great (comfy beds) and the owners were lovely and accommodating.Highly recommend hiring bicycles from your local hotel to explore the surrounding areas. We paid 50k for a full day hire and 25k for a half day the following day. We explored a lot on bike and loved the freedom of going down random roads to see where it leads - pretty safe as two females. We did take a grab taxi to Trang An as it was a little further from our accommodation.For an amazing viewpoint, make sure you climb Mua Caves (it wasn’t as hard as we expected). You can easily take a grab or it took us around 20-25 minutes to bike from the centre of town. To avoid the crowds we decided to climb at sunrise. The park opens at 6am, but we arrived around 5:40am and could get in earlier. Entrance fee was 100k and paid 5k to park the bikes. We didn’t get hassled at this time with parking scammers (apparently a thing).Food recommendations:- Hoang Viet Restaurant (across from the Tam Coc boats) has the best rotisserie duck and good + cheap draft beer that costs around 7k.- Madam Loan does a great Banh xeo (a local savoury pancake).
highlights: Great rooms at Tam Coc Victoria Hotel
practical_tips: Check with local hotel for taxi fees
Hire bicycles for a full day
Climb Mua Caves at sunrise to avoid crowds

author: Pinopineda
title: Despite everything it deserves to be seen
original_content: It starts from a pond that seems artificial inside a Resort and at first it leaves a bit 'disoriented but as you go up the river nature takes over, you are in a limestone canyon covered with vegetation and on the sides the rice cultivation. The boats are actually aluminum and not bamboo but are max for 3 people and therefore reduces crowding at least on the boat. As for the presence of tourists depends on the period and time. I was lucky enough to have a few moments when we were alone sailing the river and the lady rowing had a chat with the boats that occasionally met. You also cross caves on the water which makes the trip suggestive, we were about an hour and a half sailing but there is also the possibility to go ashore, depending on the tour you choose. A bad thing I noticed here in northern Vietnam is the request for tips and the sale of photos and souvenirs (directly on the boat) this habit came with mass tourism. Many criticize this tour but we really enjoyed it, we saw herons, ducks, turtles, fish, fishermen and farmers preparing rice fields. The peculiarity here is that they row with their feet seated while in other places of excursions they rowed standing and using their hands.
highlights: saw herons, ducks, turtles, fish, fishermen and farmers preparing rice fields

author: Petitgiaco
title: Absolutely unmissable 👌
original_content: The walk on the Ngo Dong River is truly a magical boat moment and a dream on the meanders of the NGO Dong River. Go very early between 7 and 9am because after groups can spoil the visual tranquility of the place. No rice in December, it is rather from February to April but the water lilies dot pink spots throughout the walk. The price is 250,000 Vnd and for Western tourists a boat for 2..... "they are heavier"“The skipper” earns half theprices and sometimes only does it once every 3 days ... too many boats ( 1000) for the number of tourists in this season. Finally it was unforgettable even if the sun god was not on the date.
