Be firm when saying no to requests

author: DAG4
title: Great attraction
original_content: One of the best attraction we had in Vietnam. We took the boat riding between the gorge and trough the caves, it was outstanding experience. It was also nice to see how so many woman and old people from the comminute get income from this attraction and how it nicely combine with the surrounded nature

author: Jinn N
title: Great trip in Tam coc and Hoà lu
original_content: Tam coc is so beautiful. Boat trip was very nice and the local people were friendly. Cycling is very interesting

author: nour n
title: Overall great
original_content: Very helping staff, our guide Bao was extremely nice and funny, and managed for us to still have a beautiful day despite a violent storm! The journey is rather well planned, we get to see and do a lot of stuff in just one day. Would definitely recommend for short-stay people.
highlights: guide Bao was extremely nice and funny
practical_tips: Would definitely recommend for short-stay people

author: Alu-Poo
title: Loved it
original_content: This is a beautiful boat ride. We went in July so it looked not like rice fields at all, everything was green. There are lots of tourists doing this one. We were a couple and got our own boat. Luckily we had 3 days in Ninh Binh so could do several things. Don't go too late as there will be shadows everywhere from the setting sun.  I loved this boat ride but liked the one at Trang An even better.
drawbacks: shadows everywhere from the setting sun

author: Viviane V
title: Disappointing
original_content: Very disappointing walk on the river Tam Cuoc. Certainly their way of rowing is fun, but here everything is trade and if you do not buy the sellers become aggressive. The landscape is not extraordinary, this site does not reflect the terrestrial Ha Long Bay. Choose the Tran An boat ride, a little more expensive but so much more faithful to the clichés of the terrestrial Ha Long Bay and there no forced sale.
practical_tips: Choose the Tran An boat ride

author: TheLeongOhana
title: Beautiful But Hot
original_content: I was part of a tour which had the two hour boat ride preselected.  I was so glad it was the last activity of the trip since I used up quite a bit of energy climbing up the mountains by Mua Caves.  Our group was split into groups of threes but the boat could fit up to four (maybe five or six depending on the size of the child).  Everyone was required to wear life vests but as we cruised the river not everyone had them on after they left the dock.These were metal boats and my only complaint was that my butt was tired from all that sitting.   Nicer if some padding was available.  There was a pattern in how we had to sit in the boat and our rower got a little excited when we shifted out of our position for any length of time.  Apply lots of sunscreen, use sunglasses and wear a hat or take an umbrella if you are on the afternoon boat rides as the sun got pretty intense.Be amazed by the feet rowing prowess of your guide.  It was a lot of effort to row three grown men around.The scenery was quite amazing and beautiful.  I could see why Kong Skull Island had chosen this area as one of it shooting locations.  Snack boats were available at the turnaround point.  Prices were not cheap but a cold drink and fruit was good after the first hour in the sun.Remember to tip generously at the end.
highlights: feet rowing prowess of your guide
practical_tips: wear a hat or take an umbrella

author: camuche123
title: Nice Scenary
original_content: I understand why people name it Halong Bay territory. Impressing site. The boat take 90min so a bit long as it is not super comfortable if tou have long legs and back issue.
drawbacks: not super comfortable if tou have long legs and back issue

author: Vietnam Escape Tour Travel
title: Beautiful place to visit around Hanoi
original_content: Tam Coc is so beautiful with nature like Halong Bay but there are nice local people and daily life.2 days in Tam Coc will be really nice to stay overnight in Tam Coc.i have been to Tam Coc many times but i still want to go there when i have time to come back.Just come back to Tam Coc after reopening. There are most Vietnamese now.This period is good time for rice field.

author: Dirk W
title: Foot rowing
original_content: I guess the only silver lining to this dreadful Covid affair is that we were the only boat when we went "foot rowing" through the "three caves valley" in Tam Coc. In normal times there are dozens at the time. It is a peaceful experience through a very picturesque landscape. Worth the excursion.

author: Kirina A
title: Shorter boat tour
original_content: I did a boat tour in Tam Coc during my 1 day private tour with Chookies tours. They recommended Tam Coc because it is shorter (1,5h - private 2 person boat) than Trang An (3-4h <ith 5 people on the boat) and the views are the same. I enjoyed it, I think it's a good tour when you're only in Ninh Bin for one day. There are a lot of tourists and people try to sell you food, flowers and pictures, but I declined and they went away quickly. The tour was 120k and you're expected to give a small (50k) tip to your rower.
drawbacks: Aggressive vendors trying to sell food, flowers, and pictures
highlights: Good tour for a short visit
practical_tips: Be prepared for vendors trying to sell things

author: McKenzie
title: Tam Coc Boar Tour
original_content: We did the Tam Coc Boat Tour through the three caves. The scenery was beautiful and the boat driver was very kind. The tour for 2 of us in a boat was 390,000 VNDBeware of the “market” after the last cave. They try to sell snacks and drinks, and if you refuse they will suggest you buy one as a tip for your driver. Although we were happy to do so, we are not sure this was actually beneficial to our driver as he did not pick what he wanted nor did he drink the drink. Also note that the drivers expect a tip on this tour. We had no problem with this, but tipping is not customary in most places in Vietnam so this is something to keep in mind.
drawbacks: They try to sell snacks and drinks
Drivers expect a tip on this tour
highlights: The boat driver was very kind
practical_tips: Beware of the market after the last cave
Tipping is not customary in most places in Vietnam

author: Louie Boracay
title: Must do in Hanoi
original_content: I love this tour though the traveler is very far but you were able to see beautiful mountains go biking in the rice field with tourist the lunch is also good it has lots of vegetarian options and the Tour is well organized
practical_tips: go biking in the rice field

author: JSTrip_77
title: Stunning Natural Beauty
original_content: We've done the caves at Trang An several times now but this was our first visit to Tam Coc. It was truly a spectacular experience. Due to COVID, they will charge a "surcharge" if you want more than two adults and two small children in a boat. (They seem to charge both Vietnamese and foreigners an extra fee. No, it makes no sense...but what can you do?)  The two hour trip was lots of fun. The really sweet and kind woman paddled with her feet which I'd heard of but never seen. (This was featured on one of the seasons of the US version of The Amazing Race.)  I would highly recommend this tour. But, in high season, Trang An might "feel" less crowded as it's more spread out.
drawbacks: COVID surcharge for extra adults and children
highlights: Sweet and kind woman paddled with her feet

author: TravelinGypsey
title: Canoe Tours by Tam Coc-Bich Dong
original_content: Beautiful!!! Absolutely Gorgeous!! Pictures don’t do it justice! This place is awesome!! The sweet ladies who paddle you in the canoes are the kindest and are very hard working- please be generous to them and consider tipping! This place offers multiple options of the canoe ride you would like to take and all of them are gorgeous views! They let you out along the way as well to view and walk around the beautiful and interesting temples (there are also restrooms- if you do a long tour as well) it goes fast though as your immersed in the beauty of Ninh Binh! Highly highly recommend doing this tour- it’s a must and main thing you should seek to do while in Nihn Binh! Price is excellent and well worth the experience!! Follow @travelingypsey on Instagram for more travel tips & pictures on GoogleMaps as well! Tam Coc-Bich Dong (Picture below with info)
practical_tips: Take a long tour to see more temples and restrooms

author: Bart Och
title: My favourite place in Vietnam
original_content: Tam Coc is beautiful! I stayed in Chezbeo Valley Bungalow and it was such a wonderful place! So close to the small but lovely town centre as well as Hang Mua where you can easily spend a day!
extracted_spaces: the small but lovely town centre
practical_tips: spend a day at Hang Mua

author: amanda5805
title: Fantastic ride, incredible views & horrible guide
original_content: We arrived here around 2pm. It was starting to get a little grey out but was the perfect temperature for going down the river. We were told to grab lifejackets and get in line to get on a boat. It was just the 2 of us plus the rower. Which was nice now they are small. Some boats had 3-4 people in them. There was a lot of people here but the line up moved very quickly. The ride is about 2 hours and the rower rows most of the time with their feet. Pretty incredible to see. You will pass threw 3 water caves complexes Sang Cave, Toi Cave & Ba Goit Cave. The river runs along side other limestone mountains and rice fields. The tour is not a loop but has a turn around point. So you pretty much see everything twice. The way back can be a little boring and very uncomfortable. There is people along the way taking pictures if you want to purchase them later as well as boats selling food & beverages. Our boat guide didn’t say 2 words to us. After trying many time we actually assumed she couldn't speak English. Then in last 5mins she just repeated tip for me? Then when we tried to give her a $5usd tip  she got mad (in English) that it wasn’t more and demanded $10usd. On the bus before we arrival we asked our Tour guide what a good tip would be he said to tip $2usd per boat. He also told us that they would give us information along the way and point things out. Our boat guide talked on her phone quite a bit and if she was not on the phone she would talk to other paddlers passing by. Other guides would allow the people on the boat to attempt paddling with either their arms or feet. So we really $5usd was generous. back on the bus others on our tour said their guide talked to them the whole time. Others on our tour were threatened at the halfway/ turn around mark that she wanted $5usd a person and she wanted it now or she was going to leave them there (they had 3 people onboard).Even with it being a little boring and uncomfortable it is worth doing. So much stunning beauty. It was such a highlight of Ninh Binh.
drawbacks: Our boat guide didn’t say 2 words to us.
She got mad (in English) that it wasn’t more and demanded $10usd.
Other guides would allow the people on the boat to attempt paddling with either their arms or feet.
highlights: You will pass threw 3 water caves complexes Sang Cave, Toi Cave & Ba Goit Cave.

author: Rafe Wood
title: Largely popular but still a Hidden Gem
original_content: If you can deal with the buses of Chinese tourists you will have a blast at this place. The scenery and water blew me away at Tam Coc and once you get out onto the water is surprisingly peaceful. This was a place and travel experience that really exceeded my expectations!!

author: Patrick N
title: Calm and beautiful scenery.
original_content: About two hours by car from Hanoi, you will discover this very nice site with boat ride, walk (instead of bike) to have more time to stroll and take pictures. The limestone studs covered with vegetation, the rice fields, and the Mood are perfect to forget the hectic pace of the capital.
highlights: perfect to forget the hectic pace of the capital
practical_tips: walk instead of bike to have more time to stroll and take pictures

author: Desezole
title: Nice route
original_content: We really liked this part of Vietnam. Very nice site. The boat ride with the rower was perfect... at first! Beautiful setting, no one smiling at us much, very nice with us and our daughters until halfway through where she takes out a basket of things to buy, insisting that we buy. We end up buying some souvenirs, not enough according to her, the whole return is done in silence, dissatisfied, then on arrival, we give a tip that is not yet enough! So we got a little disenchanted with that, too bad...
drawbacks: The rower insisted on selling us souvenirs halfway through the boat ride.
The return was done in silence, dissatisfied.
We felt disenchanted with the experience.
highlights: The boat ride was perfect at first.
The staff were nice with us and our daughters until halfway through.
practical_tips: Be prepared to buy souvenirs from the rower.

author: AgiBebi
title: Beautiful nature scenery
original_content: We took a boat trip alog the river to the three caves. Nature here is stunning. It is recommended to take some kind of protection against the sun. Beautiful rice fileds along the way.

author: Hana C
title: Unbelieveable views
original_content: Literally standing on a pier looking at the view and I couldn't believe my eyes. Spectacular place to hang out and explore on a scooter.

author: CrunchyCracker
title: Exploitation
original_content: We already paid a lot of admission for the conditions in Vietnam. On the water several ladies on boats met us, where we were to buy food for our boatwoman for 100,000 VND. Like many other boaters, our wife is also deliberately headed for such a kiosk boat, so we couldn't get around negotiating with the kiosk woman. When we refused the overpriced food and decided to give our wife 50,000 VND in cash so that she has more of it, she accepted it ungratefully and wanted another 50,000 VND so that she ended up earning another 100,000 VND through us. So we had to pay not only the overpriced entrance fee, but also 100,000 VND just for our boatwoman as a tip.
drawbacks: had to pay 100,000 VND as a tip

author: Yves
title: Distracting
original_content: Full day from Hanoi, Rice, small boat , bike ride . Beautiful scenery. Definitely very touristy.

author: Lily P
title: Beautiful place
original_content: I had a local boat with my boyfriend, we are so excited to go there.The locals took us along the river,  the two sides are rice fields. I was like going back to the village, everything was peaceful. I love it.It just unfortunately cloudy weather. We will be back again.

author: Magnus Ø
title: Good place
original_content: Good place and beautiful Nature. Unfortunately we went there while it was cloudy. But still a Nice and cozy place.
drawbacks: went there while it was cloudy

author: TMOH8
title: A great centre from which to explore Nimh Bình region
original_content: We called in here as part of a day long trip to the region from Hanoi. There's plenty to see around here, in fact we wished that we'd booked an overnight stay and would recommend others to consider the same.The town itself has a number of restaurants and places to stay. The attraction is the surrounding countryside and, if you want, you can hire bicycles (we did) and I believe scooters.About a mile beyond the town centre is a river where you can hire a boat and lady who rows. They'll take you on a wonderful two hour river trip, past incredible scenery and through two or three low level caves.I'd certainly recommend a visit if you have time and inclination.
extracted_spaces: a river about a mile beyond the town centre

author: TombRaider62
title: A must do in Ninh Binh
original_content: I have done this tour before in another year in January and it was cold and the rice just planted, thus brown but it was still a must do. Now I have come back in late February and the rice is growing and showing a bit green. I’d say March would be perfect. You can pay for a boat as a solo and pay the extra or this time 2 persons and boat. Cost 350,000d. I usually do not tip as it is not a Vietnamese custom (or my country)but I thought I would tip our boat girl because of the physical effort they need. I gave her 50,000d before reaching the end of the trip so that other women would not see. Then as we returned and were getting out of the boat, the woman who met the boat on the steps (not knowing I spoke Vietnamese) asked her ‘did you get a tip?’ And the young boat girl said ‘yes, 50,000d’. So I’m guessing that the young girl didn’t get to keep the tip and rather they must collect all the tips and I’m not sure how they distribute it but I now know the money doesn’t go to the rower. Hence I’m back to my “no tip’ rule. Anyways definitely a must do and totally different from Trang An.
drawbacks: rower didn't get to keep the tip
highlights: rice growing and showing a bit green
practical_tips: pay for a boat as a solo or with a group

author: Alan
title: Boat tour not worth it, pressured to buy things and add tip
original_content: The boat tour was ok, you get to go through 4 caves and enjoy the views. However, I would not recommend it as you get forced to buy things and are asked to provide a tip.The Trang An boat tour is much better, with more to see and no annoying staff to deal with.When we went through the last of 4 caves, there are half a dozen boats waiting there and will grab onto your boat to sell you refreshments. They don't take no for an answer and will overcharge you for junk. They ask you to buy it for the rower, but why don't I just give money to the rower instead? I would advise you to ask the boat operator to turn around after the 3rd cave as there isn't really anything else worth seeing to avoid these people.Also, at the end of our trip, we were asked to provide a tip and after giving them a good tip they didnt even say anything.The government should really step in to enforce better customer service at these places. Otherwise they will lose customers.Avoid this place. Trang An boat tours were much better.
practical_tips: ask the boat operator to turn around after the 3rd cave
give money to the rower instead

author: Alexandra
title: A case pf possible immaturity
original_content: Tam Coc Garden hotel is indeed an invitation to dream; and indeed you will have to “fill in the “gaps” because this fabulous location has so much potential. However, when you read reviews and replies from the administration that go way back to 2018, and still see many of the same problems going on... it feels a bit discouraging.The area is so visually idilic that it sells by itself. Rooms are right on top of the rice paddies, with their aquatic life of frogs and dragon flies... We are used to frogs, so we do not mind the loud late night chatter, but if you are a light sleeper, or city dweller may be bring earplugs. Cooler nights are more silent. And of course it will be extremely humid. Even the toilet paper. It comes with the location. Nothing can be done.The staff is delightful, Vietnamese people are mostly sweet and smilie. But unless you speak Vietnamese, communication is a great challenge. Also because gestures seem different too. At Tam Coc, some dishes were very tasty, but the photos you see on the web site and menu are there for “marketing purposes” so I was explained. That food is not what you will get. Breakfast is not very good, in my opinion, and I shall tell you why:There are thousands of tiny black flies all over the hotel, food is not “net-dome” protected. We heard complains of this much before... The person in charge of making your eggs, sometimes someone with a chef hat, sometimes a boy... unluckily a simple omelette seems to be a huge mystery.  Do not worry, a kind of weird tortilla will keep you fixed. In a country famous for its coffee, hotels should keep some of the good stuff. Not so much here, where coffee is rather bad. Close by in Ninh Binh milk flows, but, may be I am wrong, in Tom Coc milk does not seem splendid, but rather “long life” stuff. Do not take this point particular from me, as I do not have proof of this.Hygiene, masks to prevent spraying food in the times of Corona, well... it took time to convince the young manager that it was pertinent to maximize precautions. But I wonder what happens behind doors in the kitchen. We did not see staff rubbing alcohol on their hand. Teapots and plates held by the rim... and you wonder... In any case after we talked to the manager a bottle of alcohol and masks were on the front desk... The fridge in the room was noisy, sometimes disconnected. The hot water finishes in a jiffy.We found the toilet, every day filled with little ants.This hotel claims to be in the “vein” of ecology awareness, but small plastic bottles is the container of your water. We found dozens of fish floating on the water on the rice paddy, just a few meters from the room and pieces rubbish everywhere. It was not windy. It is possible that this has nothing to do with the hotel, but still, water is always water, right? We believe that we are always on a learning process, so about certain things we also have to allow time to mature. However the guest does not care about their learning process. We are here to enjoy, feel pampered, find coherence, honesty and quality of produce and service. Now, if you are not a foodie, you do not care so much about this nonsense of masks, you sleep like a log, and do not mind to see some dead fish floating near by, this is definitely the place for you!
drawbacks: loud late night chatter from frogs
tiny black flies all over the hotel
questionable hygiene practices in the kitchen
highlights: Vietnamese people are mostly sweet and smiling
practical_tips: don't expect good food or coffee

author: Jennie
title: Do this in one day, ideally on a sunny day, be aware of scams
original_content: We went during early Feb, which meant it was more foggy and cold. Due to the poor food choices and the poor weather, we left a night early and it was the correct decision in hindsight. Pros:- Tam Coc Boat ride was beautiful and peaceful when we went - during off season, and also during the coronavirus outbreak. - Cycling around Tam Coc was nice, with not much traffic and a pleasant countryside view. - Hang Mua Pagoda: the steps are uneven, some of them very high. If you have any mobility issues be wary, especially in the rain. The view on top was foggy for us but I can imagine it being beautiful on a sunny day. Even on this day of poor weather, there were quite a few people who were smoking (?!?!) on the way up, climbing on places where it was signed no climbing, and the bugs at the top were quite impressive. Cons:- Food: After being to Hanoi and being amazed by street food at cheap prices, Tam Coc food was a shock. It is entirely catered to Western tourists: extensive menu, expensive prices. Usually, in a city or town, there would be at least a few local joints that serve popular local food and specialised in 1-2 meals maximum and would be freshly made and delicious. I did not understand the stunning TripAdvisor ratings for some of these restaurants. One of the banh mi we had at a supposedly highly rated restaurant used old bread, unseasoned pork mince, no sauce, at double the price of excellent banh mi places in other areas. My vegetable stir fry at another place was unseasoned again. Rice was old. A roast duck was overcooked, chewy, and the glaze had colour but no flavour. I ordered a pork noodle soup dish at yet another place and was served packet ramen with a few pieces of meat. I noticed other diners ordered "Stir fry" which also used ramen packet noodles. - The exploitation of boat workers: rowers in Tam Coc were paid minimally and quotas of boat rowing were imposed on them so they cannot rely on this for full-time income. One of the rowers I spoke to was a lovely gentleman whose family was living in Tam Coc for 9 generations. It really broke my heart to see the corporations who own the land profiting off the locals who do the leg work (literally, as rowers use their legs to row). - Weather: Do not go in winter if you plan to climb Hang Mua, you will not see anything and will be attacked by mosquitoes the entire way. The boat ride was was nice, only a little foggy, but absolutely freezing. - Extremely touristy: Natural attractions in Vietnam which attract tourists seem to also attract tacky plastic decorations in an attempt to make the place more bright and colourful. I do not understand the need to create more plastic waste in a country that already has issues with waste removal.- Scams: I understand that this is a way of earning just that bit of extra income for struggling families, however, I do not think being dishonest is the right way to do it. In our hotel at a buffet breakfast, we were approached by a lady who started off which the usual "Hi, where are you from? How long you plan to stay in Vietnam" before telling us that she rents out excellent scooters for VND 150K and any scooter anyone else rents for 100K is of poor quality. Anyway, this was obviously a scam, but I would have thought I would be safe in my hotel buffet breakfast to not be approached. Shame on the hotel for letting her do this to guests.  Other scams to be aware: parking scams, where you cycle towards a touristy attraction and attempt to be stopped by locals who charge you a fee to park your bike (just keep cycling until you reach your destination), boat ride scam - where the rower turns you directly into the "floating market" while on the boat ride and you are heavily "encouraged" to buy goods. You will need to say no repeatedly. Then you are asked to buy a beer for your rower (the beer is obviously not drunk by the rower and the money is split). If you want to help your rower, you can tip him/her. My opinion is that you only need to do 1 boat ride, as the scenery is pretty much the same.
drawbacks: Uneven steps at Hang Mua Pagoda
highlights: Tam Coc Boat ride was beautiful and peaceful
Cycling around Tam Coc was nice
View on top of Hang Mua Pagoda was foggy but could be beautiful on a sunny day
practical_tips: Go early to avoid fog and cold
Avoid Hang Mua Pagoda in winter
Be wary of scams at touristy attractions
Tip your rower if you want to help

author: Stephie Cyr
title: Friendly little town sitting in mountains on a lake
original_content: Perched between mountains and a lake. Healthy happy ambiance. Locals do laps around the lake at sunrise, everyone greets you good morning. Nice slow pace, clean air (except for little pockets of burnings which sadly seem everywhere in Asia.I wish there comes water refill stations and bamboo straws soon. 🙏 You can take a tranquil boat tour on river.We enjoyed heaps of local foods, walking around town and getting massages.Great way to break up the trip from Phong Nha to Halong BayWe stay at Tam Coc Mountain Lake Bungalow and loved it. Very hospitable and cheerful family run business. Some of the best pillow top mattresses in VietnamLove the warm hospitality, eye contact and greetings everywhere. Such a warm friendly little town.
highlights: locals do laps around the lake at sunrise

author: IsaEliCl
title: Stunning ❤️
original_content: I believe is one of the most beautiful places that I’ve ever visited and I’ve traveled quite a lot... is just heavenly to see the limestone mountains while you’re on the boat... the locals row with their feet!! You should definitely add this place to your “day trip” from Ha Noi or at least stay for 1 night. I liked it more than Halong Bay actually... is just breathtaking...
practical_tips: add this place to your 'day trip' from Ha Noi

author: swissgirl_7
title: Glad we chose Tam Coc over Ninh Binh
original_content: Ninh Binh is an unattractive city sprawled over quite a large area, so Tam Coc is definitely the better place to base a stay in this area. It has a main town centre full of bars, shops and restaurants and maintains a villagey feel to it. It’s no longer a hidden gem or secret tip as it’s full of tourists of all ages and nationalities but it never felt crowded nor overwhelming.
practical_tips: base a stay in Tam Coc

author: christinegonzalez079
title: An informative and visually beautiful stay
original_content: It seems to me that Trang An is less touristy than Tam Coc. Many caves, rice fields, mountains and beautiful pagoda! To enjoy the scenery, you can rent a bike or take a boat trip.

author: SupratimPal
title: River & Caves
original_content: Who would have thought to cover, or uncover, three caves in a river? This was a perfect getaway amid drizzles!

author: mike_piercy
title: Rice and frogs
original_content: The hotel is out in the countryside, surrounded by rice fields full of noisy frogs. Bird watchers will enjoy the storks and herons chasing the frogs. It's a delightful setting and the gardens are beautiful. The swimming pool was cold in mid February but happily there were no mosquitoes.

author: Vish
title: Such Beautiful landscape
original_content: Had a wonderful time there. With the hike on the two peaks, the cycle across that beautiful landscape and little boat trip with local. You just need to experience it. Also the local food at lunch time was nice.Things I still would like to change was the tip on the boat service and the local selling stuff at half way. Feel like being forced to buy stuff for the sailor + had to give them a minimum of asking tips. Seems it was well planned.

author: isabella h
title: beautiful
original_content: It’s beautiful. Surrounded by mountains, not too busy, easy to get to places (by scooter or bike). If you’re staying in Ninh Binh, would recommend staying here instead :)

author: Angela S
title: Boat trip
original_content: We really enjoyed our boat trip along the river. There are amazing views of the mountains and rice fields,  and we saw kingfishers,  egrets,  storks and mountain goats. There were half a dozen boats on the river when we arrived at 10.30 am but this did not detract from the peace and beauty of the place. Yes there were boat vendors but you can say "no", and yes we did tip our rower but seeing as he had just spent 1.5 hours rowing us along the river,  a couple of dollars didn't seem unreasonable. Happy to recommend.

author: alanbently64
title: Boat ride with caves
original_content: We didn’t have to queue long for the tam coc boat ride. It was D390,000 for the two of us (about £13) and the boat ride was just us and the chap rowing. We went along the river with lots of other people in boats under caves and saw lots of karst mountains and birds feeding in the rice paddies. There must have been a hundred or more other boats though it is tet when a lot of Vietnamese take their holidays. It was restful and fairly interesting. There were hawkers on boats selling stuff quite insistently and we have our rower a tip. It was ok but not amazing.
drawbacks: hawkers on boats selling stuff quite insistently

author: XavierNY
title: Nice Views
original_content: I did this on a self made day trip from Hanoi, with Mua Caves as well, I rented a motorbike. I went on a rainy day and there were no other boats in the water, it was so nice and beautiful. Paid 400k for 2 people, 1 boat and a parking fee for the bike. (1.5 hours) Like others, they do try to sell you stuff but just say no if you want or bargain like crazy and you can get things for super cheap. They also demand a tip at the end (they reminded me at the beginning and end), but only give if you want.
drawbacks: They try to sell you stuff
They demand a tip at the end
highlights: It was so nice and beautiful
You can get things for super cheap

author: Emilie G
title: Nice boat trip
original_content: We enjoyed this boat trip of about an hour and a half. The scenaries are pleasant as it is such a nice area. It is fun to go through caves. We did not experience any scam. Only one boat tried to sell us things and we said to our rower we were not interested and he kept rowing straight away. He did not ask for tips ever. We paid 150k vnd for the boat, plus a ticket of 120k vnd per person. A bit expensive but still a nice experience.

author: lovisaduvander
title: Best place to live
original_content: If you want to do all the activities in Ninh Binh, I suggest staying in Tam coc! Definitely better cause you’ll be close to a lot! A very cozy little town and even if you have a day you don’t do anything it’s very nice lite stroll around the town! Rent a scooter and drive around from tam coc is definitely the beat option! A lot more peaceful that Ninh Binh centre!

author: Tom
title: Very nice
original_content: I see the scenery here so great the air is also fresh, I also shoot quite a lot of photos here really beautiful

author: litterkati
title: It is a 5 star only if you are sitting in the first boat before 8 am
original_content: We went there before 8 am (open from 7 am) and the experience was amazing: no other boots on the way there and the nature was waking up in front of our eyes (many birds were hunting for breakfast). When we entered a cave we did not see anything and did not hear anything. Purely amazing.HOWEVER: on the way back roaring people were loudly chatting, many boats came close to each other. Boats with the purpose of selling some snacks and drinks also arrived (they are colleagues so your roaring person will stop for a couple of minutes letting them pushing their products to you).Therefore tourists starting after us lacked the true nature experience. Believe me: it is not the same.TAM COC VS TRANG ANWe did both, both were beautiful and exciting. Of course there are some slight differences between the routes, you can find great blog posts around the topic of which to choose based on your preferences.Trang An:They focus on a definitely better service compared to Tam Coc, they try to avoid the annoying factors of Tam Coc: more transparent pricing, no selling people on the way and there is even a paper based feedback form at the end of the route with the question of whether the roaring person asked for a tip. So they control them not to ask for a tip. As a result, it is a more relaxing place, I think popularity is high similarly to Tam Coc.Especially if you cannot make it before 8 am in Tam coc, I would definitely recommend Trang An. We did that starting at 10 am and due to the fact that they have 3 routes the crowd split in 3 ways.
drawbacks: boats came close to each other
practical_tips: avoid Tam Coc if you can't make it before 8 am

author: theresabryson65
title: Boat ride
original_content: This was a short boat ride but the oarsman stopped when we wanted so we could take photos. It was lovely scenery and charming people.

author: nilintentum_reliquit
title: Wonderful boat trip
original_content: The 6 kilometres 90 minutes return boat ride has your jaw dragging along by the shear beauty of the landscape. Very peaceful and the perfect way to try and take in what Mother Nature has created. Very easy to find a boat once you have purchased the official fixed price ticket.Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful.
highlights: perfect way to take in what Mother Nature has created
practical_tips: buy the official fixed price ticket

author: Peter
title: Nice view but a lot of room to improve
original_content: No questions Tam Coc is a nice place to visit but I am reviewing from tour management perspective.- they should build in the tips to the ticket price so we don’t have to be scammed like being forced visitors to buy drink and food for the rower ( we don’t mind but we don’t want to be forced and pay a high price for their food) and asking higher tips at the end. It is ok to build in tips to improve the wage for the rowers. - over 1-2 hour on the small boat without the backrest is very tough for your back ..you won’t feel it the first 1/2 hour - so many worldwide visitors per day and they don’t have a decent restroom. One old restroom that is smelly and disgusting..I don’t want to mention more..all the money that they bring in should be able to build a decent restroom- no organized method on how to boarding boat..every one just stand there wondering how to boarding ...I hope the TamCoc marketing team will take these suggestions to improve services for visitors and for local rowers as well ..and make this a world class place ..
drawbacks: Forced visitors to buy drink and food for the rower
Asking higher tips at the end
practical_tips: Build in tips to the ticket price
Organized method on how to boarding boat

author: Lilianpp
title: Very nice site very nice but questionable commercial practice
original_content: The site and fabulous, we navigate in the village, through the rice fields then we pass in 3 caves. Impressive! The only negative point: before returning to the starting point we get to a point where we are almost forced to buy food for us and the rower with a price worthy of the best rackets (150,000 Dong for 1 mango 1 drink and crakers!) And just before arriving the piroguier asking for his tip!We had planned to give before starting the walk but there was a little too much! It was a shame because the site really deserves the detour! To conclude do not take food on the way and tip the piroguier and that is all!
drawbacks: piroguier asking for tip before arrival
practical_tips: don't take food on the way
tip the piroguier at the end

author: digitalroc
title: Go before rice fields are harvested
original_content: I went here in the off season knowing that the rice fields had already been harvested, however the scenery was still beautiful.  I think it would be more spectacular if you go before the harvesting of the rice to see something even more picturesque.  The row boat ride was very interesting as we went into three separate caves.
drawbacks: The scenery might be more spectacular if visited before the harvesting of the rice
highlights: The row boat ride was very interesting
practical_tips: Visit before the harvesting of the rice for a more picturesque view

author: Simon C
title: The view is amazing
original_content: I took a boat trip to Tam Coc and bike ride around the area and totally loved it. Amazing landscapes with mountains and river (not the right time for rice paddies).

author: Barney T
title: Amazing view
original_content: Amazing view, it’s a great walk. Take some water with you, and go for it! :) especially the sunset is amazing. You can go for a boat trip as well, which is better in the morning.
practical_tips: go for a boat trip in the morning

author: Ashish J
title: Beautiful Place
original_content: We cycled around and had a good boat trip. Views are amazing. You can easily spend a couple of hours looking at the nice views. Highly recommended if you have a day to spare in Hanoi. The boat trip will take about an hour and it is hard work for the rowers. They appreciate a tip at the end. Some of the photos do not do justice to this place. You have to be there and see it and appreciate how beautiful the place is.
drawbacks: some of the photos do not do justice
practical_tips: tip the rowers at the end

author: Sarah
title: Beautiful Tam Coc
original_content: Tam Coc is really beautiful! I am glad we went there during during our trip to Hanoi, I thought it won't like it because I already went to Halong Bay.

author: adikartono
title: Beautiful place
original_content: It was a day trip from Hanoi which includes both Hao Lu and Tam Coc. In Tam Coc, we cycled as well as took the small sampan boat to enjoy the scenery. It is a really beautiful place with amazing scenery of the limestone mountain. The boat ride was extremely relaxing. Highly recommended!
highlights: amazing scenery of the limestone mountain

author: Vivek K
title: Tam con visit
original_content: It's a wonderful destination ,very peaceful and quite . The boat ride under the caves was amazing and very thrilling . We claimed a mountain there and did a lot of shopping
highlights: boat ride under the caves was amazing and very thrilling

author: C Anderberg
title: No transparency
original_content: The total fee for admission and a boat for me and my husband was $390k, which is about the same as Trang An.  The ride itself was lovely, though shorter than Trang An. All of this was fine...until the scams started. Boats are situated at the end the route, peddling food. They will guilt-trip you to buy food for your rower. We saw multiple other guests cave into the pressure, and their rower didn’t even touch the food the entire way back. Towards the end of the trip, the rower asked for a tip and we gave her 10k, but she refused it and was angry. This is a horrible way to treat tourists. The rowers at Trang An, on the other hand, refused tips and there were surveys at the end of the ride to ensure consistency of service. We really appreciated the professionalism there. To the operators of this tour: pay your rowers a fair price and do not guilt trip your guests. Build tips into the fee and don’t treat your customers like walking wallets. Would advise to skip this and just stick to Trang An.
drawbacks: rowers will guilt-trip you to buy food
practical_tips: skip this and just stick to Trang An
pay your rowers a fair price

author: Rahul K
title: amazing boat ride through a serene environment
original_content: we went on a clody day it was cool and perfect and very relaxing. was an hour long boat ride surrounded by mountains covered with green trees. it was amazing to see them row with their legs never seen that. at the end before they take a u turn beware of the people selling overpriced things they try to sell stuff to u or prey on your sympathies to convince u to buy for your boatman. try putting your legs in the cool water if u are sitting the front. highly recommend this.
highlights: amazing to see them row with their legs
practical_tips: try putting your legs in the cool water if u are sitting the front
beware of the people selling overpriced things

author: happyhok
title: The scenery and nature is nice
original_content: I like particularly the visit to Mua caves , the view is fantastic there and there is also a pagoda to visit. Lodging is basic here and can’t expect city standard but good enough for foreign tourists .

author: Manuel Pereira
title: Very nice hotel in the middle of the mountains
original_content: I´ve stayed for 2 nights in this hotel and it has amazing mountains around it! One of my favorites places in Vietnam. You can cruise around the area with the bikes they provide and after you return you can enjoy the scenic pool! Highly recommended!
practical_tips: cruise around the area with the bikes they provide

author: fede127
title: Boat trip
original_content: Visitable with a day trip from Hanoi. You cross a river that in some periods is bordered by flowering plantations. The boats are driven almost all by women who row with their feet and wear the typical hats.The view on a sunny day is spectacular

author: hweeying
title: Worth the trip
original_content: Booked the trip from Klook. The tour including the lunch and it was really good. After lunch walked to the river bank to start the boat trip. The trip took 90 min but may be longer. The mountain scene is beautiful. Our tour guide told us to give tips usd$1 to the boatman. The boat woman asked for more tips when I already passed her usd$2 (we are 2 ppl) so I just ignore her. Visited on Dec 2019.
drawbacks: boat woman asked for more tips
practical_tips: give tips usd$1 to the boatman

author: rggg
title: Stunning landscapes and long boat ride !!
original_content: Why is it so good:-1. Landscapes are stunning. Mountains, river, the cold wind, peace, caves....makes it for a surreal experience.2. Boat ride lasts nearly 1.5 hours...giving you ample time to soak in the scenery and appreciate the nature's beauty3. A single oarman/woman rows the boat non-stop for nearly 1.5 hours and their stamina is just 'wow'What could have been better:-1. If you have taken the bus tour from a travel agent or through Klook...they would waste your time with 2-3 unnecessary stops, with not so good lunch and a visit to a pagoda. Frankly, you can do this tour in half a day then a normal full day event.2. You can hire a private car (from Klook or travel agents) and come directly to Tam Coc and buy a boat ride directly through the ticket counter. That would easily save you 3-4 hours. 3. Lunch was ok but not great...they sell it by saying authentic Vietnamese food but in my opinion...it can be easily skipped.
highlights: ample time to soak in the scenery
practical_tips: do this tour in half a day
buy a boat ride directly through the ticket counter

author: Alison T
title: Nice boat trip but poor customer service
original_content: Just take note that after you paid for the standard fare, the counter staff will pass you 75,000VND (from our fare) to be passed to the boatman.  Guess this was the boatman’s “salary”.  The ride was scene & we even spotted goats on the mountain.  Just as other tourists who had commented, the locals on the boats really hard sell us drinks but we declined & they were not happy. There were photographers on their boats to take many pictures for tourists. One such photographers kept taking many pictures of us & we have to tell her politely it was enough.  The boatman stopped the boat before we reached the jetty & asked directly for tip. They expected nothing lesser than 100,000VND.  Once we reached the land we were handed our 8 photos & cost about 16,800VND per piece. We just bought it since we wanted a happy trip.  But, the Vietnam tourism board should do something about the attitude & service of the boatman. On another note, the boatman at Trang An didn’t ask for the tip & we were more than happy to tip the boatman willingly.
drawbacks: Locals on the boats hard sell drinks
Attitude and service of the boatman
practical_tips: Decline drinks from locals on the boats

author: Kerry L
title: Beautiful Scenery
original_content: Even though it was misty this morning, the scenery was amazing.  The sun tried to get through the mist - worth coming even when the weather isn't really sunny.  It is very peaceful to be rowed down the river and listen to the birds and duck when you go into the river caves - and of course gaze at the mountains in the distance
practical_tips: go even when the weather isn't really sunny

author: Sightsee28950251738
title: Moving the pagoda
original_content: The ancient temple though small but located in the mountain is very beautiful, in front of the temple is the rock bridge north through the stream there are many beautiful enough flowers.

author: Sunshine21059507876
title: Loosing my hat
original_content: Today I lost my hat in an electric car in the Parc and dear Linh and Anh from the customer service found my hat back!Amazingly and so very kind and helpfull and me happy again. Thank you so much. Greeting from Mr. Ben from The Netherlands.
highlights: customer service found my hat back
practical_tips: go to customer service if you lose something

author: thanhtamspa tam cốc
title: We came close to family.
original_content: The ancient temple , beautiful landscape is very ancient . Very encouraging you should come.

author: elaine a
title: Beautiful calm place
original_content: This was our 1st stop on our 1 st day in Nihn Bihn so we were there before the crowds built up visually stunning you need to cover knees & shoulders as it’s a temple & there’s quite a lot of steps to get to the top winding through the mountain but totally worth it was a great welcome to the heat & humidity of Vietnam lol

author: Matthew W
title: Much quieter than Mua Cave and far more magical
original_content: Our visit to the bich dong pagoda was amazing and a pleasant suprise. We cycled there from tam coc through the beautiful rice fields and quieter lanes. On arrival there was a designated space for parking of bikes (a little expensive at 150k vnd for 2, but entry to the pagoda is free).It was a beautiful time of day as the sun was beginning to set, and while there were plenty of people around it didn't feel too busy like many of the other places in the ninh binh area (for example the 500 steps up Mua Cave). It is set in an area with stunning scenery, and the short walk up to the main pagoda was lovely.We were very pleasantly surprised by the extra walk up through the cave and up to the very top where there is another shrine with beautiful views. It felt very calm at the top as it was set on the other side of the hill to all of the hustle and bustle.This is definitely a must visit!!

author: Mr9xx
title: So tourist
original_content: The old pagoda has now been renovated and elevated to attract more tourists.The pagoda itself is quite impressive, but there is a parking fee of 20,000 VND per vehicle.From here, you can see the old temple and even a corner view of Phong Nha Cave.Nature used to be home to many monkeys in this area before, but they seem to have disappeared due to human activity. I wonder where they live now.There is not much else to see here.
drawbacks: Parking fee of 20,000 VND per vehicle
Monkeys seem to have disappeared due to human activity
highlights: Corner view of Phong Nha Cave
practical_tips: Go early to avoid parking fee

author: Luca Magnanensi
title: To see
original_content: Very ancient pagoda and set in a cave, a short climb up steps allows you to reach it. Must-see attractions

author: TravelingFoodie
title: Pretty good
original_content: We visited Bich Dong Pagoda and found it to be a very peaceful and scenic place. Built into limestone cliffs with small cave temples and stone steps, it has a calm, atmospheric feel. The walk up is short and easy, with nice views along the way. Not a large site, but a quiet and worthwhile stop when exploring Ninh Binh.

author: georga
title: Be careful of the parking fee!
original_content: When you arrive there will be men dressed up in military looking uniforms with armbands directing  you to park. DO NOT PAY 50K DONG FOR PARKING! They are not actual officials. We only paid 5k each to park our bicycle whereas other people paid 50k.  The pagodas are set in the lovely mountainside. Sadly there was limited information about the history of the site so we had to look it up ourselves. There are entertaining signs about the laws of cause and effect that are worth reading.
drawbacks: Limited information about the history of the site
highlights: Entertaining signs about the laws of cause and effect
practical_tips: Do not pay 50K DONG for parking
Look up the history of the site beforehand

author: Aussie Boomers T
title: Just go
original_content: Worth the visit, I climbed the stairs to the temple not too difficult. Easy to go via grab or Veit fast electric car or scooter. Food and sovoniors available Free to enter if you want to inside the temple they supply clothes to cover knees and shoulders.
practical_tips: Go via Grab or Veit fast electric car or scooter
Free to enter if you want to inside the temple

author: Ell Belllll
title: Beautiful views
original_content: I really enjoyed this. The view from the top is worth the trek up. The trek up is manageable and there is a lot of tree cover that will shield you from the sun. 10/10 would recommend. It’s free!

author: Greg R
title: Pagoda Temple.
original_content: Fascinating.  Deep sense of history.  The steps were manageable with spectacular views from the third Pagoda.We loved it.

author: Marsoan
title: Underwhelming experience
original_content: Quite an underwhelming site. Pushy people at the entrance. Not a lot to see. We were fooled by a men on one side of the site and ended up in a cave not lighten and full of bats. Beware. Totally unsafe to go there (see photo). That said, the bike ride to get there and the surroundings are charming.

author: Liam B
title: Great free attraction don’t listen to bad reviews who clearly didn’t take the steps up to the other 2 temples!
original_content: This is an awesome visit! Don’t listen to other poor reviews who clearly didn’t explore the whole site. Hawkers were nothing to worry about (just ignore) and we parked our bicycles outside a cafe in the square for free and ignored the parking “official” (not an official). The temple built into the cave is amazing and a lovely tranquil site. They also provide leg coverings (skirt) if you come in shorts which is super handy when coming via bicycle and allows tourists to be respectful (just make sure you have a tshirt covering shoulders as per normal regulations for religious sites). This is a great visit, don’t miss it! And it’s free!

author: vivi234
title: i wouldnt miss it
original_content: it takes like 40 minutes if you want to go all the way up and its worth it ....nice insta photos there too...nise views from above ...easy route ;)

author: Sunshine E
title: Good free trip .
original_content: Free!!! A few steps to walk up but far better than expected and we did it in the rain! I think those saying there’s nothing to see maybe didn’t venture past the bridge! Once you get to the pagoda, make sure you take the tiny passage way on the left, into the cave, which then takes you to another pagoda area. (See photo) The worst thing about this trip was the instagramming!!!
drawbacks: Nothing to see (if you don't venture past the bridge)
highlights: Tiny passage way on the left
practical_tips: Make sure to take the tiny passage way on the left

author: alessandra_biondi3
title: The Jade Pagoda
original_content: In the protected area of the Unesco Heritage we visited, not far from Ninh Binh and Tam Coc (paddy fields and caves), the Bich Dong Pagoda, we got there by bike. In fact they are three pagodas, called "Jade or Green Pearl pagodas". The place breathes spirituality because it is inherent in a suggestive place between the waters and close to the mountains. It dates back to 1428 under the reign of Emperor Ly Thai To, later Buddhist monks rebuilt it in three different bodies on three levels: lower, central, upper. The three pagodas have a particular curved roof like a boat, the atmosphere is sacred, incense is burned... Honestly I struggled to climb the levels because there are steps without handrails, but it's worth it.
practical_tips: be prepared for steps without handrails

author: S&O
title: Beautiful 3-storey complex in the mountain
original_content: Beautiful, old, 3rd floor temple complex in the mountain. Wear sturdy footwear in damp conditions. Parking right in front of the start of the complex.
practical_tips: Wear sturdy footwear in damp conditions
Parking right in front of the start of the complex

author: Heather S
title: Some steps very big so be careful
original_content: We went here on a “package” from the boat tour.  You could just do the boat trip from Tam Coc for 250K Dong or for an additional 100K Dong you could have a little yellow bus tour to some temples.  As I wanted to see this pagoda it made sense to do this.  The steps were hard in places as they were so big but in my opinion was worth the time and effort.  There were 3 or 4 hawkers at the entrance selling trinkets but they didn’t bother us.  Lovely trip!
drawbacks: the steps were hard in places
practical_tips: do the boat trip from Tam Coc for 250K Dong
for an additional 100K Dong you could have a little yellow bus tour to some temples

author: Liliane M
title: PRETTY PAGODA IN AN IDYLLIC PLACE
original_content: Its name means emerald cave and is named after the lush vegetation that surrounds it.It is located on three levels to which you have to climb through stone steps. The tour is not suitable for everyone.You go inside and appear, altars, cave.The views from above are beautiful.
drawbacks: The tour is not suitable for everyone

author: chloe h
title: Pushy people, be aware
original_content: Lovely place but scammers and pushy locals ruined the experience somewhat.Got there and was waved into a parking area by official looking locals. Turned out to be a scam where the lady would not let us past unless we paid 50k vnd each. Turned out we could have parked for free a few meters further along.Then when coming down the steps (there are quite a few) one of the ladies grabbed my arm to 'help' me down and would not let go. She wanted me to buy something. Said no like 20 times and had to quickly walk away as she was forcefully insistent. Didn't stay long after that.
drawbacks: scammers and pushy locals ruined the experience
forced to pay 50k vnd each for parking
forcefully insistent locals trying to sell something
practical_tips: park for free a few meters further along
be cautious of locals trying to scam you

author: Sirisha D
title: Beautiful Pagoda
original_content: Beautiful pagoda with some temples inside. Few areas are not accessible. The boards mention that there is a cave temple from inside the pagoda area. But no body knew about it. Visit if you have more time to spend. Beware of the sellers
drawbacks: no body knew about the cave temple
highlights: Visit if you have more time to spend

author: Mr. Y
title: Tam Coc's Secret
original_content: The morning after I stayed overnight near Tam Coc, I rented a bike and was introduced as a sightseeing spot that can be done in about two hours round trip at the hotel. I wasn't expecting that much, but it's a better place than I thought.After going through the gate in the photo, I went up the stairs endlessly, and the main hall? Just when you thought you'd reached it, the road continued up through the cave behind it, and from the top you had a beautiful view of the rocky mountains.
highlights: beautiful view of the rocky mountains

author: ArpitaS
title: The route and the destination- both were amazing.
original_content: Just the kind of place where one would want to go for some quiet and peace. We cycled to this place from our accommodation and the entire route was beautiful with water lilies on side of the road and the limestone hills at the horizon. This three layer Pagoda is so serene. But it is also a religious place and hopefully visitors keep that in mind.
drawbacks: visitors not keeping the place in mind as a religious site
practical_tips: be respectful of the place as a religious site

author: Anita Rosaleh
title: Very picturesque pagoda
original_content: Beautiful pagoda with some temples inside the cave. Free entrance, prepare for some mosquitoes repellent so you won’t get eaten alive! There’re few sellers that could be quite pushy but they just need to make a living so just politely said weren’t interested. We parked our bicycles at Gao coffee bar and restaurant across the street that had the best salt coffee we’ve had!
practical_tips: Park bicycles at Gao coffee bar and restaurant

author: Henry Jackson
title: The Bich Dong Temple
original_content: Bich Dong Temple is a very nice and quiet place. The surrounding landscapes are picturesque with limestone mountains and green fields. The temple is built inside a cave, creating a very special and mysterious atmosphere. My friends and I enjoyed visiting each floor of the temple, each with its own unique beauty, perfect for taking magnificent photos. The atmosphere is serene and relaxing, ideal for finding peace and admiring the beauty of nature.

author: Monriqui
title: If you've gone to Trang An grottoes don't bother with this spot
original_content: Unless you love pagodas/temples this place is a waste of time. It is just a small bridge over water. If you are doing or have done Trang An Grottoes then you would of seen far better things there than you would here.Waste of time, only good thing is it's free
drawbacks: only a small bridge over water
practical_tips: go to Trang An Grottoes instead

author: Inspire33077069886
title: Excellent
original_content: Great place with every possible activity, as boat trips, cyclists, trekking tours, cultural program, as well as sightseeing of pagoda and temple. Good opportunity to meet new friends. Nature and surroundings are excellent.
practical_tips: good opportunity to meet new friends

author: Lynn W
title: Beautiful
original_content: Beautiful place. Lots of stone stairs if you want to get to the top. But the Pagoda in all the pics is easy to get to. Worth the effort to get as high as you can manage.
practical_tips: Get to the Pagoda in all the pics is easy to get to

author: Claires travels and tips
title: Enjoyed walking through and up the steps to the top.It was free to get in
original_content: Enjoyed walking through and up the steps to the top.It was free to get in but the parking security at yhllthe front wanted 10vnd for parking. Its ok unless you want to park just away from the entrance free.Worth the trip on our bikes
practical_tips: park just away from the entrance free

author: Anja S
title: Beautiful, but not the most beautiful
original_content: Very busy, not the nicest pagoda around. Route to it though nice. Dress codes of covered shoulders and knees are observed by almost no one and no comments are made by the supervisors.
drawbacks: Dress codes of covered shoulders and knees are observed by almost no one
practical_tips: Dress codes of covered shoulders and knees are observed by almost no one and no comments are made by the supervisors

author: M W
title: Bich Dong Pagoda
original_content: Absolutely loved this old, authentic and absolutely beautiful mountain Shrine. Each tier was very different and gave spectacular views. Very peaceful feel at the top. My favorite Shrine out of lots visited.

author: Veba1980
title: Nice Pagoda
original_content: We visited this pagoda as part of our day tour in Ninh Binh. We had a rainy day ... the place and surroundings are beautiful landscapes ... pity that we ended up soaking wet ... I recommend having a change of clothes, an umbrella, good shoes and especially rain ponchos ... the super rain jacket kept me dry only the top ...
drawbacks: pity that we ended up soaking wet

author: Chris B
title: Worth a visit while in Tam Coc
original_content: It is a small Pagoda just outside of the village. We cycled there and it took about five minutes. The pagoda is very peaceful and was quiet while we were there. There are steps that take you above the pagoda, not too difficult and then there are nice views and an opportunity to have a boat tour. We did not go on this one but it was a nice setting.
highlights: opportunity to have a boat tour

author: Roam20716917383
title: Worth a bike ride
original_content: Lovely place and easy to walk around. Very serene and well looked after. Good for a bike ride if staying in Tam Coc and to look around the area.

author: Fearless64523150081
title: Stunningly Beautiful.
original_content: Stunningly Beautiful. Well worth the trip, highly recommend .Try and climb the steps for a wonderful view from the top.

author: Dante
title: Get the boat through the small cave
original_content: The pagoda is ok, but our highlight was the boat tour. Next to the pagoda you can walk up a hill to see a small valley, from there you can take a boat through a dark cave full of bats. Not touristy at all and hence in our opinion a better experience than the Trang an boat tour (it was too crowded).

author: Mark T
title: Quiet and peaceful (once you get past the crowd of Instagram tourists)
original_content: Worth dropping by. Don’t be an Instagram tourist & take your happy snap outside with a crowd behind you. Take the time to quietly walk around and enjoy this place
highlights: quietly walk around and enjoy this place
practical_tips: take your happy snap outside with a crowd behind you

author: Chris318i
title: Nice pagoda close to Tam Coc
original_content: Nice pagoda close to Tam Coc. The pagoda is free of charge, but you need to pay for the parking of your bicycle or scooter. From our point of view the Bich Dong Pagoda is worth a visit.
drawbacks: You need to pay for the parking of your bicycle or scooter

author: Arcade05
title: A very good time
original_content: Very beautiful place with places of prayer spread throughout the mountain. A very beautiful walk. Very pleasant place. At the top we arrive at a promontory with a very beautiful view

author: Voyageur
title: Great for the view and history
original_content: We were lucky enough to be accompanied by a French guide, who explained the whole history of this pagoda to us.It's great, there are three rooms, the Buddha room, all the way to the female Buddha room.You have to climb about a hundred steps, but the view is absolutely splendid.
practical_tips: go with a guide for explanations

author: Alessandro S
title: Located just outside Ninh Binh
original_content: The site which is located in a beautiful countryside area a few kilometers from the famous Ninh Binh is a site that is quite frequented by tourists but there are not many people and therefore, even if not exceptional, it is happy to visit.

author: DotsGirl2
title: Three shrines on three levels
original_content: The first pagoda is unusual as it has three roof levels. You then climb to the second pagoda which is smaller and then you climb up some more to a much smaller pagoda. The view is very nice

author: HkkS
title: Bundle with Tam Coc and free 2 ways ride.
original_content: Worth spending some time here, nothing to see or do but if you want to see a cave and ring a bell inside a cave. This is the place you can do it. But please be mindful since this is still a holy site. Since it is free from you purchasing the Tan Coc ride, so just visit it. You can get a free ride 2 ways from Tam Coc for free too.
highlights: ring a bell inside a cave
practical_tips: get a free ride 2 ways from Tam Coc

author: view54
title: Pretty pagoda in the mountain
original_content: To have. Historic pagoda. Nice place.The most interesting thing is the boat ride in the mountains. It's incredible.

author: Nguyễn Thị D
title: Very happy
original_content: Beautifull.Bich Dong Pagoda will forever be a beautiful miracle combining nature and people to form a unique architectural complex, imbued with Vietnamese village culture./.
highlights: beautiful miracle combining nature and people

author: axcosmos
title: To do
original_content: Superb place. If you come by bike, negotiate 5000 dong for parking, no more, unless you are very generous.

author: Skram66
title: Tam Coc, Ninh Binh treasure; oldest pagoda in Ninh Binh I'm told
original_content: Slightly off the beaten track, a short 5-10mminute cycle ride from Tam Coc Amanda Villas, this beautiful secluded oldest pagoda in Ninh Binh is definitely worth a visit. One of my top visits while travelling from North to South Vietnam. Fabulous views from the top. Would recommend the Gao Restaurant, situated in the car park (red & yellow signage, on your right hand side) wherr you can go park you bike, great area to sit & have a nice cool drink, admire the view & soak up the relaxed ambience. Decent climb which takes you through an unlit cave...watch out for uneven surfaces.
practical_tips: sit & have a nice cool drink
admire the view & soak up the relaxed ambience

author: Mel W
title: Closes at 4.30 or before
original_content: The outside was quite nice, but it apparently closes at 4.30 or before even though they accept parking tickets. Probably worth a visit
drawbacks: accepts parking tickets but closes early

author: orrdin
title: Very interesting
original_content: The pagoda is partially dug into the mountain and has several levels so the whole climb and view experience was fun and it was interesting to learn about the local religion.

author: Mélanie M
title: Magnificent
original_content: Magnificent place between nature and structure, you would think that the pagoda grew in the middle of the mountain!You have to climb quite a bit to get to the top but it was worth it!

author: cramac
title: Good experience
original_content: I reached the place on foot from Tam Coc. It's 4 km there and back, but the sultry heat is suffocating. The 5 stars are for the experience rather than for the pagoda because the whole landscape in its context is worth the effort
highlights: the whole landscape in its context is worth the effort

author: Ali_Royal_2015
title: Tranquil and beautiful at sunset
original_content: We cycled to the pagoda and arrived around 4:30pm. It was very quiet on the road in and we didn’t encounter any hassle or issues, just paid the 10k each to leave our bikes in the official small covered parking area just passed the entrance walkway. There is no entrance fee but remember to save your parking receipt to collect your bike and show you paid when you return. We seemed to arrive at the perfect time as there was hardly anyone there which was perfect as it was easy to relax and enjoy the tranquility of the place without crowds. I took a large sarong to wrap around my shoulders and knees when walking through the temples. The scenery is really beautiful and the temples are interesting to walk between, they felt very calm and spiritual. It definitely made a big difference experiencing the peaceful vibe with hardly any other people around. I would recommend going early morning or later in the afternoon when it’s slightly cooler and less busy.

author: OneTrip with local
title: A peaceful pagoda surrounded by trees
original_content: Bich Dong Pagoda is a peaceful pagoda surrounded by trees and beautiful greenery. If you visit during the summer, you can see many lotus flowers.Originally constructed in 1428 during the reign of Emperor Ly Thai To, Bich Dong Pagoda was a small pagoda nestled in Ngu Nhac Mountain.In 1705, Buddhist monks Tri Kien and Tri The discovered the pagoda and reconstructed it into three levels: the Lower Pagoda (Ha Pagoda), the Middle Pagoda (Trung Pagoda), and the Upper Pagoda (Thuong Pagoda).In 1774, Lord Trinh Sam of Dang Ngoai (Outer Land) visited the pagoda and was impressed by the breathtaking panoramic view of nature. The pagoda caught his attention, and he named it Bich Dong (Green Pearl Cave) Pagoda.

author: Julie A
title: Lovely!
original_content: This is well  worth a visit.  Make sure you go right to the top as there is a cave temple and we were privileged  to be welcomed in to watch the prayers and thanks gving. It was really very special. Beautiful little place to spend a couple of hours. Car park available  for bikes or scooters.
highlights: watch the prayers and thanks gving
beautiful little place to spend a couple of hours
practical_tips: car park available for bikes or scooters

author: Shelley M
title: Unique
original_content: I had read about the parking issues and we had gone with a guide, so didn't have to deal with that but did see a group of cyclists getting annoyed about being harassed.  So do your homework, ask your accommodation how much is correct and stick to your guns.  It is worth seeing in my opinion, I'm not a religious site person, but being 3 levels built into a limestone mountain peeked my interest.  The surrounding area is really lovely too.  Lots of goats wandering around and it really is quite beautiful.
drawbacks: cyclists getting annoyed about being harassed
practical_tips: ask your accommodation how much is correct

author: ctm7944
title: Bich Dong Pagoda
original_content: Rode bicycle from Tam Coc Wonderland Bungalows to Bich Dong Pagoda. 25KVND Bike parking. Go to the left side of the Pagoda for a hike up to a Temple and Cave. If you go around the right side. You will see a green oasis. There is a small lake with boat ride operated by a family. Then followed a narrow path, which resembles a game trail. Encountered a couple of goat families eating along the trail. This leads to a hike up the side of the mountain for some very nice views.
highlights: hike up to a Temple and Cave
practical_tips: Go to the left side of the Pagoda for a hike up to a Temple and Cave
If you go around the right side, you will see a green oasis

author: Jaroslav Nečas
title: Piece of history
original_content: I am not fan religious sites but this place look magical even thought construction works were in progress during my visit. Small pagoda is surrounded by water between characteristic hills in Tam Coc area.

author: EarlyRetirementAbroad
title: A rainy day activity
original_content: A nice activity for the rainy day. Since the weather was bad, we didn't see a lot of people at the Pagoda. We slowly walked around the ground level of the  complex but didn't climb the steps because of rain and slippery steps.It is a nice well maintained complex with peaceful vibes. However, the sellers at the parking lot are aggressive and it is better to go directly to the Pagoda without paying any attention to them.
drawbacks: aggressive sellers at the parking lot
didn't see a lot of people
practical_tips: go directly to the Pagoda without paying attention to the sellers

author: Viet Exquisite Travel
title: Lovely pagoda with beautiful nature surroundings.
original_content: We visited the pagoda in a day of May, we arrived so early in the morning so the pagoda was nearly empty with just few small group of local visitors. We actually love the old structure of the pagoda and the beauty of the surrounding nature.

author: devina1991
title: Still a enjoyable visit on a rainy day
original_content: We  visited early in the morning and it was raining continuously and yet it was enjoyable to explore this site and there were no visitors and it was calm and peaceful, the surrounding is very beautiful with mountains and lake. There was no entrance fee and parking was also  free as there was nobody  at the parking lot.

author: Polly
title: Peaceful and beautiful
original_content: Beautiful area with temples and a pagoda and view points to explore. You can park your bikes etc for a small fee. There are a few small stall holders in the area. Very peaceful and beautiful, definitely recommend visiting at a quieter for a more peaceful experience. We enjoyed taking the path around the right hand side of the lake where you can climbs up some steps and descend down into a pretty valley with a small body of water and a cave.
extracted_spaces: path around the right hand side
extracted_times: quieter for a more peaceful experience
practical_tips: visit at a quieter time for a more peaceful experience
park your bikes for a small fee

author: Yann Renaud
title: Impressive temple, built.directly on the mountains
original_content: Nice temple built in the mountains. It is pretty impressive to see. The entrance is free, but the gate closes at 5pm.The place is accessible.on a bike (10-15 minutes). Parking it will cost you 5kD per bike, but they will try to raise it 10kD.
drawbacks: Parking will cost you 5kD per bike, they will try to raise it 10kD

author: Alex H
title: Unfriendly parking attendants
original_content: Be careful when visiting here as they try to rip you off when you are parking your bicycle or scooter. At first one man tried to charge us 50,000, but when I refused he got angry and started waving a ticket in my face. I asked another tourist how much they paid to park their bicycle, and they had paid 20,000. The man heard me ask this so demanded I then paid 30,000 (different price) because a scooter was more expensive than the bicycle. Eventually we gave in because he was being very aggressive and wouldn’t leave us alone.The pagoda itself isn’t great at all, and there are way better ones throughout Vietnam, so I’d say it’s barely even worth coming here.
drawbacks: parking staff tried to rip us off
practical_tips: be careful when parking your bicycle or scooter
don't pay the first price they ask for

author: fal3
title: Average
original_content: Neither good nor bad. The scenery is okay and it’s close to the main centre of Tam Coc. The temples themselves are rather boring but it’s a worth a visit if you have time.
drawbacks: The temples themselves are rather boring
highlights: it's a worth a visit if you have time

author: Jo G
title: Put off by the parking harassment
original_content: My husband and I biked to the pagoda, It seemed like such a lovely peaceful place ruined by some guys blowing whistles rushing in front of us and pointing to where he wanted us to park our bikes and telling us we needed to pay.  It totally put us off - starting to feel that everyone just wants money out of you. It would have been nice to have a drink at one of the coffee shops there but we took a photo then turned around and left. Really put a damper on visiting what looked like a beautiful place. I would happily pay an entry fee to know it went to the upkeep of these temples but not to line the pocket of some random.
drawbacks: some guys blowing whistles rushing in front of us and pointing to where he wanted us to park our bikes and telling us we needed to pay
starting to feel that everyone just wants money out of you
It would have been nice to have a drink at one of the coffee shops there
highlights: It seemed like such a lovely peaceful place
It would have been nice to have a drink at one of the coffee shops there
