author: LizzieB
title: A definite see.
original_content: Beautiful place to visit! Goats on the mountain, bats in cave, great view  Beware of people dressed in uniforms, charging you parking fee.
drawbacks: people dressed in uniforms charging you parking fee

author: Miguel M
title: Fake Parkings - Park inside
original_content: BE AWARE OF FAKE PARKINGWe cycled here and about approx 500 meters from entrance, the  scammers will start to tell you you must park here and there.Just ignore them.As you approach to the entrance, there is a small bridge to the main gate. You will find a parking, and more aggressive (just yelling, nothing else) saying the same: you have to park here, you can enter to temple, waving a red flag to you like if you were Hamilton on a F1 race. And using whistles. They are funny to be honest. Just ignore them, cross the bridge and take your bike inside the pagoda courtyard. Park it there. If they keep yelling just tell them to bring you an official ticket or to point to you a sign stating you cannot park inside.. they will yell, but nothing else.  Tell them to keep their hands away from yourself. Then they will tell you people is praying and more bullsh1t so you feel bad for entering to courtyard. In this case, tell them they are the ones not respecting the sacred place by telling and trying to scam. Also remind them that karma will act upon them and in next afterlife they will become døg guardians to learn loyalty.    PS: Pagoda is nice lol
drawbacks: Scammers trying to sell fake parking
practical_tips: Ignore scammers and park inside the pagoda courtyard
Tell attendants to bring an official ticket or point to a sign
Remind them to respect the sacred place

author: 630ph_ngl
title: Worth for visiting
original_content: The place is very pretty, it takes less than an hour to visit. The bat cave is worth it. Nice Vietnamese architecture

author: TonyB
title: Surrounded by beautiful nature
original_content: We came here during a quite heavy rain and it was a magical feeling, I’m happy we did because the place was almost empty and as I just read from other people reporting about scammers this time they weren’t there to be seen. Highly recommend, the temple has some really beautiful nature surrounding it.

author: hm777
title: Beautiful intriguing temple
original_content: Beautiful temple. We arrived at 6-7 AM and it was almost empty of tourists. The temple complex past the front gate only opened at 7 AM (actually slightlylater), and from inside there, there were 2 paths up to further sections of the temple in the mountain (up steep stairs). The left one of those paths was open, and led to a pitch black cave with a shrine inside it. Very amazing experience. The other path was never opened before we left at around 8. We travelled by bicycle and ended up leaving it in a nearby shop in exchange for buying a coconut (30/40,000 dong) before we left. I have read that there is free parking, but I'm not sure where that was. There was an undercover shelter for parking immediately opposite the main temple gate, but not sure if that was paid or not.
drawbacks: pitch black cave (may be a drawback for some)
practical_tips: parking may be paid or free

author: Yvette F
title: Pagoda lovely, people not
original_content: We were staying in the hotel next door to the pagoda and watched daily the  vendors and “parking attendants” hassle people arriving. We found this to be the case at most of the beautiful sites in the area and it has really put us off. We understand that the last couple of years have been awful for the locals, but this is not the way to do tourism. We would be more likely to walk in their shops or park in their spaces if we were greeted with a welcoming smile. Having just come from thailand, where everyone is so friendly, it was a huge disappointment. It’s fortunate the the staff at Tam Coc le Montagne were so welcoming and friendly which made up for it.
drawbacks: not the way to do tourism
not greeted with a welcoming smile
highlights: staff at Tam Coc le Montagne were so welcoming and friendly

author: Tom
title: Beware of Parking Scammers.
original_content: The pagoda/temple itself is beautiful however the experience was soiled by the scammers who try to demand money from you to park there. Upon arrival (bicycles) we were greeted by a woman who ran in front of me blowing a whistle and waking a red flag directing me into a secluded entranceway. I could see bikes parked in another location so I refused and headed towards the obviously free area. She was very persistent and kept shouting ‘No no no’ and directed me to her area. I refused and parked my bike and headed into the pagoda. Once finished I walked back to my bike where I was greeted by a man wearing an all green uniform and cap (similar to that of the police but obviously not) and demanded money. I refused and he became angry and kept pointing at a yellow badge stuck to his arm which said something in Vietnamese. Obviously this was nothing official at all but this was the impression he was trying to give. I asked him to show me a sign on the tourist information boards that said I needed to pay and he then started spitting on the floor near us and shouting. I still refused and he became even more hostile. To de-escalate the situation I paid him 10,000 Dong and left.As I was leaving a group of three young girls returned to their bikes and he did the same. I told them to get on their bikes and ride away as he was about to scam them. To which they did as he tried to grab their bikes and stop them from leaving. Definitely worth a visit but please be careful.
drawbacks: Scammers try to demand money from you to park
Unofficial and unmarked staff trying to scam visitors
practical_tips: Be careful of scammers and unofficial staff

author: Karl D
title: DO NOT PAY FOR THE PARKING!!
original_content: This is just a warning to anyone parking bikes /motorbikes... When you arrive there is a little pay parking area straight ahead... Drive in and past this area... You will have to walk back out past the scanners asking for money but just ignore them...
drawbacks: parking bikes/motorbikes can be a problem
scanners asking for money can be ignored

author: Nixoid
title: Okay temple with parking scammers
original_content: The temple is ok, but parking scammers at the gate ruin the experience. You can park one block before and walk in for free.
drawbacks: parking scammers at the gate ruin the experience
practical_tips: park one block before and walk in for free

author: Alu-Poo
title: Worth a visit
original_content: The entrance to the temple at the lake is really beuatiful. We went and looked at the temple etc. It's very nice but not worth to drive hours to see. But if you stay in Tam Coc it's definitely worth to visit. You can cycle there from Tam Coc town.  Instead to walk through the gate to see the temple  you can walk around the lake on the right side and then climb up the hill. You end up between hills in a very beautiful landscape, most likely alone as people don't go that way.
drawbacks: not worth to drive hours to see
practical_tips: cycle there from Tam Coc town
walk around the lake on the right side and then climb up the hill

author: Aidan W
title: Ridiculous
original_content: Motorcycle scam in front of the entrance where they ask for ridiculous amounts of money to park your bike… also wasn’t allowed in because i wore shorts, wouldn’t have been a problem if we hadn’t witnessed a whole other group of tourists all in shorts and sleeveless t-shirts making pictures just stroll on by…Entrance was nice.
drawbacks: Motorcycle scam in front of the entrance where they ask for ridiculous amounts of money to park your bike
wasn't allowed in because i wore shorts
witnessed a whole other group of tourists all in shorts and sleeveless t-shirts making pictures just stroll on by

author: Dirk W
title: 3 temples
original_content: The pagoda is an easy walk from the centre of Ninh Binh, up some steep stairs. Enter over a small bridge through a nice gate, then proceed to the first 2 temples ; the third one is tucked behind the second. A pleasant walk and sightseeing after a day exploring the fields and waterways.

author: Le monde de Chris
title: Should Go
original_content: It is quite and gorgeous. There are 3 temples in Bich Dong Pagoda ( Low, Middle, High) You can easily find a way to the Low and Middle one. The third one, however, is hidden behind the middle temple. You need to find a way to Dark Cave, which is next to the Middle Temple (it quite hard to notice it) . Go along the dark cave until you reach the end of the road. Trust me, you won't regret. I think it really cool and worth it. Visit here if you have time. It Free by the way.
drawbacks: It's hard to notice the Dark Cave
highlights: It's really cool and worth it
practical_tips: Go along the dark cave until you reach the end of the road
Visit here if you have time

author: Charlene T
title: Should check it out if you have time
original_content: There is a small alley beside the small temple in the second picture which will lead you to a hidden temple in the cave. I found it really cool and it also will lead you to another temple.

author: Celine A
title: Wonderful place
original_content: The place is beautiful, the stairs are sometimes scary but it's worth it. I was lucky to be alone there, usually, it's quite croudy

author: Rafe Wood
title: Decent Pagoda
original_content: Bich Dong is worth going to if you have ample time in Ninh Binh but if you are short on time stick to the main attractions.Overall the entrance is very cool and worth a few photos but the pagado itself is under whelming. The views are ok considering the walk up is slighly strenuous and time consuming.
drawbacks: walk up is slightly strenuous and time consuming

author: frida27pierre16
title: Very beautiful
original_content: This was a nice place to visit but not for handicap people or people who can not so good clim on not so good stairs

author: silvergeck0
title: Serene atmosphere
original_content: Very unadorned and humble pagoda that still has a monk living in/working from it. Fascinating peep into their everyday life, slightly spoilt by the people in your face selling highly over priced items
drawbacks: people in your face selling highly over priced items
highlights: fascinating peep into their everyday life

author: aljax83
title: Was ok, nice views
original_content: Was alright. Apparently you can leave your bikes anywhere but we chose to leave them at the entrance and pay 10k per bike. Don’t try and ride them over the bridge into the pagoda... like some stupid tourists tried to do 🙄It’s all a bit run down but has some nice views. You can walk around the back and up some steps for a good view. Be respectful and if it says don’t wear shorts in the temple DON’T WEAR SHORTS. It might not be religious to you but be respectful. So many people aren’t it’s disgraceful.

author: TMOH8
title: Interesting pagoda in wonderful scenery
original_content: We throughly enjoyed our visit here. The pagodas themselves are set on several levels and I'd say that it's worth the effort climbing to see them as they themselves are interesting per se but the views of the surrounding scenery make it a double win.I'd recommend a visit.

author: Wanderer
title: Peaceful
original_content: Peaceful temple overlooking rice fields. Access via a small stone bridge, then a few steps up the mountain. Once you reach the second sanctuary, continue around it through a cave unto the next flight of easy stairs. Beautiful view at the top!
practical_tips: Access via a small stone bridge
Continue around it through a cave unto the next flight of easy stairs

author: Alan
title: Not much to see
original_content: We biked here from our hotel, had to pay for parking at the entrance. If you are willing to try, maybe park a minute walk from the entrance so you don't have to pay a parking fee.The attraction itself was rather small, there wasn't much to see at all.
practical_tips: park a minute walk from the entrance to avoid parking fee

author: swissgirl_7
title: Lovely pagoda in very atmospheric surroundings
original_content: We cycled here from our home stay in Tam Coc without knowing what to expect. Expect to pay to park your bikes 10’000VND but the pagodas are free. The location is beautiful. There are two routes up the “mountain” to see the upper pagoda, the steps are relatively well done and the view at the top is nice.The pagodas are very rustic and unadorned and make a nice change from the heavily decorated ones we’ve seen. Simple, almost monastic atmosphere and very pleased we visited.
practical_tips: expect to pay to park your bikes

author: lovisaduvander
title: What hides inside
original_content: This place is definitely something you NEED to put on your “things to see-list”. It doesn’t look like much when you first get there even if it looks amazing by the entrance. But wow when you go inside and up the stairs you will be amazed. It’s like a hidden temple INSIDE the mountain. Like literally carved out and build inside. It’s definitely worth going up to see it. It never ends and it’s just really cool to see how it’s made. You can’t see it from the outside so it’s very good hidden! Worth seeing definitely!

author: Emilie G
title: A hidden jem
original_content: We enjoyed the visit of this pagoda a lot as we found it pretty as much as the scenary around it. We walk to it from Tam Coc but we would recommend to cycle as it is a bit far. There are different pagodas, the last one is in a cave. Free of charge. Enjoy!
highlights: pretty as much as the scenary around it

author: theresabryson65
title: Visit December 2019
original_content: This was an excellent experience and our guide was very knowledgeable, She went at our pace and explained things well, her command of English was excellent. A very positive experience.

author: Miksyd
title: A must see
original_content: One of the nicest Pagoda we visited in Vietnam, and surprising... but I won’t tell why to not spoil it 😉 When we when there we had no info about it and it was pretty spectacular. Just don’t forget to walk behind the Pagoda on the 2nd level.
practical_tips: walk behind the Pagoda on the 2nd level

author: nilintentum_reliquit
title: Peaceful setting
original_content: 3 kilometres from town this makes a pleasant bike ride. The setting in the hills is very serene and whilst the temple itself is nothing unique it is worth a look.Thanks for the vote if you found this review helpful.
drawbacks: the temple itself is nothing unique
highlights: the setting in the hills is very serene

author: NtshuaL
title: Beautiful!
original_content: Very nice place, but if you bike there, you'll be charged to park your bike. We went in the afternoon and there wasn't a lot of people. However, at this time of the year, there were no water lilies either.

author: Rico
title: Authentic Pagoda
original_content: After the morning enjoying Tam Coc we went to the Bich Dong Pagoda. Not a huge site, it doesn’t take as long to explore the temple and cave above and behind but it definitely felt and looked authentic and ancient. It is worth a visit while you are there. We got a lot of interesting photos.
highlights: felt and looked authentic and ancient
got a lot of interesting photos

author: Rob B
title: Go and see it on your bicycle
original_content: Its so easy to cycle around this area and visit these amazing places. It’s obviously best viewed without any noisy tourists. We actually just sat and waited for a noisy group to leave and then enjoyed it quietly. Most people are only there for 15 minutes.

author: Josephine Magda... M
title: Centuries old pagoda
original_content: This place is nestled in a quiet corner of Tam Coc. It involves a series of steep steps to view the 2nd and 3rd levels of the temple. However for those who are not able to climb stairs, you can still view the temple on the lower ground and capture some beautiful photos of the surrounding area.
highlights: beautiful photos of the surrounding area
practical_tips: view the temple on the lower ground

author: switchedoff
title: Lovely bike ride from Tam Coc village pretty surroundings.
original_content: Nice pagoda, pretty surroundings of course.  Will be prettiest in Summer when the lotus is abundant.  Parking available for bikes (motor and pedal) and some cars.  A few tourist stalls and some women selling massages out front.  The best views are from up very high, loads of steep steps.
practical_tips: parking available for bikes and cars

author: TCav
title: Simply, Breathtaking...
original_content: The pagoda itself is amazing to see, with the history entailed behind the buildings and caves. However, when you get to the other side, the view and peacefulness of the surroundings... only birds and baby goats to be heard... is incredible. I just had to FaceTime my parents back in the UK to show them the views, forgetting about the time difference of 7 hours, and waking them up, even they didn’t care when I showed them.Definitely a place to visit on your travels!

author: bobnrobyn
title: Busy
original_content: Loved the scramble up and through  the caves to the top temple . Fine views over the lotus pond . Quiet busy with lots of noisy tourists spoiling the peace . Visit early if you can .
drawbacks: lots of noisy tourists spoiling the peace
highlights: scramble up and through the caves

author: Ogy Kovachev
title: So huge in the rock
original_content: A great in-the-rock monastery. Be aware of the slippery stairs and a stray dog who likes to bite your trousers without notice :)
drawbacks: stray dog who likes to bite your trousers
practical_tips: be aware of the slippery stairs

author: Hellie27
title: Nothing special
original_content: In my opinion it is not worth climbing up the stairs, there is not a lot to see and the view was blocked by trees. The entrance gate is rather beautiful, I would recommend coming here when the lotus flowers are in bloom because the pond is huge and filled with flowers. Not sure when that would be the case, now in November they were all dead.
practical_tips: come when lotus flowers are in bloom

author: Abi R
title: Beautiful pagoda & cave
original_content: Beautiful pagoda with ponds around - we went when it was off season so didn’t get to see the blossomed lotus flowers however can imagine this would have been a beautiful site! There is a small cave inside and a viewpoint at the top. Worth a visit here whilst in Ninh Binh / Tam coc. A lot of parking for motorbikes / bikes right outside too for 10,000VND.
drawbacks: did not get to see the blossomed lotus flowers
practical_tips: go when in season for lotus flowers

author: carolofberks
title: Interesting
original_content: Worth a visit while in Tam  Coc - beware that the official place for parking cycles/mopeds is not ‘official’ ,just a safe place - pay no more than 10,000 per bike
drawbacks: beware that the official place for parking cycles/mopeds is not 'official'
practical_tips: pay no more than 10,000 per bike

author: Megan and Allan
title: Worth it
original_content: Cycled there from Tam Coc. 2 easy kilometres. Parking for bikes was straight out the front. Multi level with a few stairs, well worth the visit
practical_tips: Parking for bikes was straight out the front

author: Maylis P
title: Hidden beautiful cave !
original_content: The Pagoda is ok, but the place touristic. If you want to escape it and discover a hidden cave with a private guide, here is the way ! Do not cross the bridge to go to the pagoda , but continue to go along the water on the right. Leave the pagoda walls on your left to go around the pagoda. Then walk 10mîn (up and down stairs) to arrive at a nice lac. The owner of the place propose to visit a cave (10000 dong, 20min). No light inside, he will guide you with his own and explain everything (in Vietnam’s !)! The best cave I have seen and a great off the beaten tourist track experience
highlights: great off the beaten tourist track experience
practical_tips: Do not cross the bridge to go to the pagoda
Leave the pagoda walls on your left to go around the pagoda

author: Joanne P
title: FREE OF CHARGE
original_content: The place got parking for motorcycles at 20k, free of charge. Nice caves and Temples with pond outside. Stairs to climb about 15mins in all. Love this place a lot!
practical_tips: parking for motorcycles at 20k, free of charge

author: Barry W
title: Charming Pagoda
original_content: A nice peacefull pagoda. Entrance fee is free but you will have to pay to park  your  bicycle or motor bike. The Pagoda is about 5klm from Tam Coc town an easy bicycle ride. You walk through a lovely entrance gate into the grounds of the temple which is spread in  multiple levels and you walk though a bat cave to reach the top. There is stair climbing but not too taxing. Best time is  early before the tourist buses arrive and not so cowded. One dissapointing thing was the lotus pond in the front was dry. How good would it look in full bloom. Overall a good place to visit
drawbacks: lotus pond in the front was dry

author: Jennifer
title: Nice little site
original_content: Cute little temple site with multiple temples.  As always, lots of stairs, but not too taxing.  Enjoyed the quite calm and beautiful area.

author: Chamodi Sandeepa
title: Bich Dong Pagoda
original_content: We were staying at Tam Coc Happy Home and we cycled 2km among beautiful rice fields to reach there. The place we left our bicycles charged us 10,000VND where in Hang Mua they only charged us 5000VND. We went there on 02nd of October. This was one attraction I was really looking forward to visiting. But I was disappointed to see the lotus pond appeared in all the photos dried out. It was the lotus pond which made the place more romantic. With the pond dried it lost its charm. But the entrance gate was still magnificent. There were some shrines dedicated to the Lord Buddha. After climbing some steps there was another shrine with a cave. The place felt cool and relaxing. I wish the lotus pond will be in full bloom when you get there.
extracted_spaces: shrines dedicated to the Lord Buddha
drawbacks: lotus pond appeared in all the photos dried out

author: Hang Do
title: Very beautiful and unique pagoda
original_content: This place is awesome, it took me quite a lot to arrive here by taxi but the entrance fee is free. I had an experience entering a cave that full of bats. It was kind of scary but also very interesting. We took some great photos, definitely will comeback again if we have chance.

author: JayandNicholas
title: Beautiful
original_content: No entrance fee. Beautiful Pagoda with great views as you walk up and through caves full of bats. We were lucky there were not many tourists at the time of our visit and got some great photos. It's normal to pay a small fee when parking you bike, it's not a scam and is a very small price to pay, not worth getting upset over.
drawbacks: pay a small fee when parking you bike

author: DerriQ
title: Really stunning
original_content: Beautiful pagoda. Hard to get a good pic of just the pagoda when we were there as it was quite busy at 4pm yest afternoon.  We didn't clinb it all, just had a look inside and in the temple on this first level.  Was interesting to learn about the female monks who live there.
drawbacks: Hard to get a good pic
highlights: interesting to learn about the female monks

author: Travelling_Guy38
title: Cool place
original_content: Pagoda built in to a cliff with a climb up the hill to the top bit. You also pass through a bat cave which is really cool. The views are also good. It's near enough to Tam Coc to cycle to.
highlights: bat cave which is really cool

author: Anna H
title: Beatiful little pagoda
original_content: Has a fascinating cave with bats. I suggest bringing a torch or using one on your phone for dark areas. Entry is free. So worth visiting!
practical_tips: bring a torch or use one on your phone for dark areas

author: Yumitim F
title: Best temple in Tam Coc
original_content: It's gorgeous and in condition that is good. Not simply the front entrance with a lot of individuals taking photographs for the Instagram of theirs but additionally in case you go up or inside to the stairs close to it, simply really daring. Place that is great to check out!

author: Glenn
title: Gorgeous , Entry and parking are both free!
original_content: The partner of mine and I chose to go out right here, which was well worth the hype. Very awesome entry and also when youve climbed the steps to the temple, go behind, and also youll locate a huge cave and that results in yet another temple. The great spot in general and also extremely scenic.Look out for the natives. For starters, its no cost to go into the pagoda. Dont fall for anybody asking for cash and entry fees.Secondly, parking. Its free. Theres a big parking area on arrival, but you will find locals who'll attempt to point you right into a secluded area, blowing whistles and heading you there. We pulled in but seen on the maps. Me app that we had been using that's recommended parking was no cost and never to spend. We then realized we were getting cheated whenever they demanded 50.000 dongs. To park a motorcycle is normally 5 10.000 dong. 50.000 was crazy. We turned the bike around and then told them we werent paying, for the cost to miraculously be lowered to 20.000 dongs. I shook the head of mine at the partner of mine, remained tight, and also told them we werent paying. They started to be distressed and attempted to fight us leaving but later on received the photograph that we werent paying. We left the parking area only a brief walk out of there and parked at the restaurants a minute down the highway, in which a neighborhood female told us parking was totally free. In order to thank her, we stayed and also had a drink at her shop... instead offer cash for her services and integrity than to those which are blatantly attempting to rip you off. It doesnt matter it isnt considerably they're trying to rip you off by, its the idea of being cheated that is downright terrible. So dont fall for it!
extracted_times: a brief walk out of there
practical_tips: don't fall for anyone asking for cash and entry fees

author: glb1971
title: Don 't be so afraid of a little scam
original_content: The pagoda is a charming little place, well worth the visit.There are many reviewers complaining about a guy with a whistle asking for money to park your bike. This is true, it is an old man who apparently bought a whistle and some sort of uniform and rather convincingly orders bikers into his bike shelter. We parked our bikes (9) with him for 50.000, hardly any bargaining needed. This amounts to about 2 dollars. If it is worth that much to you, by all means park your bike 100m further down the road and walk, but you could also show a little appreciation for his little scam and pay a sum that amounts to a small fraction of your next meal so he can earn a modest living. Whistle back at him and you will get a smile :-)
drawbacks: guy with a whistle asking for money to park your bike
practical_tips: park your bike 100m further down the road and walk
show a little appreciation for his little scam and pay a sum that amounts to a small fraction of your next meal

author: Parker Thomas
title: My favorite place in Ninh Binh
original_content: Go in the morning before 10am and enjoy this place all to yourself. I love it the best because you wind your up and through the caves to different encounters with Buddha. Enjoy the bats, and go to the top. Worth every step.Also take the path by the bike parking as it is an adventure you will enjoy!
highlights: enjoy this place all to yourself
practical_tips: take the path by the bike parking

author: JP F
title: Nice highlight
original_content: Beautiful scenery. I love the gate with the lotus field the most. Free entrance and don't be forced to buy anything. Please throw your trash in the bin!!
drawbacks: don't be forced to buy anything
Please throw your trash in the bin!!

author: Enid
title: Watch out!
original_content: Today we went to the Beach Dong pagoda. The pagoda and temple are OK. BUT.... big warning for the awful people. We we're "greeted" be a man with a whistle.... He was yelling and pointing, but not a word was understandable. His point though was clear. No parking for bikes unless with him and if you pay him. We learnes from the Mua Cave that this is a big scam. So we refused. He wouldn't let it go but was really clear that he couldn't do anything. He was quite intimidating enough when we parked our bikes (for free) he kept standing there. He watched us the whole time. His friend was laughing at us and making all sort of signs at us. After te pagoda visit (which we maked very short) my friends bike was not OK. They've been tampering with it. The pagoda is not nice enough for this kind of behavior from the people. I don't recommend it.

author: Charlotte
title: Average as pagodas go
original_content: Lovely location with lots of waterlillies around and cute little bridge to cross water to enter. Pagoda itself not that flash and not worth the drive unless you're staying nearby or have time to kill. Very pushy locals for parking payment and also purchasing offerings and trinkets
drawbacks: Very pushy locals for parking payment

author: Isabel B
title: Nice to visit
original_content: It’s nice to visit as the surroundings to get here are lovely. You don’t need much time here. We visited as we were doing a day of exploring on scooters.

author: Sathilde
title: Nice view to discover the landscape
original_content: We came by bike, we've paid a parking (20 000 pax, it's quite expensive...) but the entrance is free.You have to climb to the top if you want to appreciate the view. Also, at the entrance, you can admire waterlilies.
practical_tips: climb to the top for view

author: Factsnotfiction62
title: You don’t need too long herr
original_content: We enjoyed Bích Dong.It is much smaller than other pagadas in Ninh Bing but nonetheless worth a visit if you’re in Tam Coc.There are three temples built into the mountain as you make your way up the stone steps. There is also a cave with hundreds of bats in!The entrance arch is impressive, set on s pond filled with hundreds of water lilies.There are signs around asking for people to be dressed appropriately (although we saw several people with bare shoulders and short shorts on).
drawbacks: people with bare shoulders and short shorts on
highlights: three temples built into the mountain

author: Zuzka Trojka
title: nice a small pagoda
original_content: Really nice buddha pagoda, It easy to get there. Rent a motorbike or bike or if you want you can walk:) its about 2km from Tam COC centre.You have to pay for parking. Entrance is free.
drawbacks: You have to pay for parking

author: Varun_723
title: One of the nicest pagodas in Ninh Binh
original_content: The Bich Dong Pagoda is a good way to spend an hour. Ideally try to visit with someone who knows the history, or you'll just be looking around without understanding the significance. This pagoda is one of the few that haven't been 'revamped' aka completely rebuilt by the government so it still maintains it's old charm and character. There's a few different levels, each with a different shrine. There's also a large cave which leads you to the top, it can be full of bats depending on the time of year but they just hang from the ceiling and stay out of your way.The pagoda is free to visit, so don't believe anyone trying to sell you an entrance ticket. Depending on the weather, you may want to carry an umbrella or a raincoat as there isn't much cover.
drawbacks: looking around without understanding the significance
bats depending on the time of year
practical_tips: try to visit with someone who knows the history
carry an umbrella or a raincoat

author: Christine B.
title: Unusual pagoda
original_content: This is a beautiful and unusual pagoda because of its location inside and on either side of a cave. We visited all three levels and the views from the top are amazing!
highlights: views from the top are amazing

author: Jessica A
title: Nice area to explore - beware con artists though!
original_content: We were charged for motorbike parking as well as an entrance fee, only to find out that this Pagoda is actually free to visit. It has a beautiful entrance and some nice views, and if you walk through the parking area to the other side of the lake you can explore a lovely rice paddy area (after going up and down some steps). Supposedly there is a cave there, too. There is also a toilet this way!
drawbacks: steps to explore rice paddy area
practical_tips: walk through the parking area to the other side of the lake
go up and down some steps to explore rice paddy area

author: Lavender
title: Beautiful Pagoda
original_content: We rent a bicycle, visited this amazing place. It was not crowded, very quiet with temple on the top.

author: Don C
title: If in the Area a must visit
original_content: If you are in the area this is a must visit. I wouldn't go out of my way for it.  Nice grounds and an interesting Buddhist Pagoda.
drawbacks: wouldn't go out of my way for it

author: Pickleinwimbledon
title: Walk around the lake and behind for better views
original_content: We avoided the parking scammers by parking on the side about 100m before the entrance. The site was very crowded with coach tours so taking advice from other travellers we took the path to the right of the bridge and walked through the bike parking and around the lake. The path  then climbs up  over a hill with stunning views onto a small lake. Down the other side was a guy with a torch who will take you into a cave for a fee. We declined. Other than that,  the place was deserted and stunningly beautiful. So much better than shoving your way through the selfie obsessed tour parties.
practical_tips: park on the side about 100m before the entrance
take the path to the right of the bridge

author: Fred F
title: Nice but comes with tricksters
original_content: We went here on our mopeds and parking is crazy. The women are really rude and put us off. I would park outside for free and walk in, you dont have to pay to go in which is good. It is a nice setting and interesting inside, great story behind it about 2 buddhas that built it. Little walk up to the caves which is good. Go to the toilet before as the lady demands payment for hideous facilities. It's nice but comes with little tricksters.
practical_tips: park outside for free and walk in

author: hfffoman
title: Ancient pagoda in a beautiful setting
original_content: Although it isn't a huge pagoda it is one of the most interesting, set in the mountains and bearing an atmosphere of age and decay. The surroundings are beautiful and you can easily enjoy a walking around for an hour so after seeing the pagoda.
practical_tips: go for a walk around for an hour

author: AnniK0210
title: Definitely worth visiting
original_content: It's a nice pagoda that's definitely worth a visit. If you're short on time in the area It wouldn't be my first choice.

author: Lya_amar
title: Cute Old Pagoda
original_content: Road to Bich Dong Pagoda is stunning :) Filled with rice fields on both side of the road is real treat for those who visiting this place.. Can stop by to take great pictures.. The Pagoda is small but cute and amazing place to take good photos :)
highlights: cute and amazing place to take good photos
practical_tips: stop by to take great pictures

author: Sam E
title: Great place
original_content: We walked here from our Hotel in Tam Coc.  I think it took us 45 minutes each way, if that.  A bicycle would have been ideal.  However with walking, we didn't suffer parking issues.  I don't think we had anyone trying to scam us to pay to get in, we just walked straight on over the walkway.  Bich Dong Pagoda was my favourite Temple.  Well worth spending a good hour or more at, as there really is so much to see.  Explore this place and enjoy it.   There are restaurants etc to buy food / drink at, so you could easily while away an afternoon here.  Also a couple of other attractions very close by that we never had the time for.
highlights: Explore the place and enjoy it

author: limedex
title: Small lovely temple with great view
original_content: Behind the temple there is a scenic location, with pond and rice fields. It is a lovely surprise especially near sunset. Beautiful little sanctuary.

author: Johannes R
title: Cute temple
original_content: It’s such a nice temple in the cave and outside. Definitely nice to see when you’re around Tam Coc!!

author: Jason Reeve
title: A great old pagoda to visit.
original_content: Bich Dong Pagoda dates back to 1428 and It’s a really beautiful place to visit. I would recommend going with a tour guide as the locals who hang around the entrance are well known for scams & thefts on unaware travellers – this is probably good advice for most of Vietnam’s tourist hotspots anyway. Lots of stairs to climb to reach all areas but the view is great and if you keep an eye out, you'll see mountain goats up on the higher areas of the mountains.
practical_tips: keep an eye out for mountain goats

author: Travelglorious
title: Watch out for the locals that patrol Bich Dong! Unfortunately, scammers and thieves are amongst them.
original_content: As already mentioned by other reviews, there is a parking scam here, but also worse. We too had whistles blown and raised voices directed at us as we decided to turn our bicycles around and park down the road. One man wearing an official looking hat and blowing a whistle also decided to grab hold of me demanding an entrance ticket! Entrance is FREE. We probably would have paid the 10k dong fee for the privilege of parking our bicycle under a tin roof, but the hassle that accompanied doing that just totally put us off! They hurled abuse at us as we cycled off to a nearby restaurant where a nice lady said we could park for free. We bought a few items from her on our return.  Anyway, the temple itself is pretty astonishing and definitely worth the short cycle ride from town. It was even more fantastic when we discovered a dark passageway that looks like it leads to nowhere, but in fact enters a cave complex leading to another temple higher up the mountain. We really enjoyed it, so we would definitely recommend a visit.However, as we left we noticed there was a disturbance between some local ladies offering massage and a group of tourists. It transpired the local ladies had offered an elderly female tourist a massage for $1, but then stole the change from a $50 note. This also happened to another tourist whilst we were there and despite the respective groups alerting their tour guides, the conclusion they made was that nothing could be done, but perhaps to take photos of the offending group and report to police later on. So, my advice.......definitely worth a visit, but just be on guard and watch out for the below!
extracted_spaces: a cave complex leading to another temple higher up the mountain
highlights: the temple itself is pretty astonishing
a dark passageway that looks like it leads to nowhere
a cave complex leading to another temple higher up the mountain
practical_tips: be on guard and watch out for the below

author: infinityonhigh
title: Best temple in Tam Coc
original_content: It is absolutely beautiful and in good condition. Not only the front entrance with plenty people taking photos for their Instagram but also if you go inside or up the stairs right next to it, just very adventurous. Great place to visit!

author: Laura H
title: Beautiful but don’t fall for the scammers! Entrance and parking are both free!
original_content: Myself and my partner decided to venture out here and it was worth the hype. Pretty cool entrance and once you’ve climbed the steps to the temple, go behind and you’ll find a giant cave which leads to another temple. Really cool place overall and incredibly scenic.Watch out for the locals. Firstly, it’s free to enter the pagoda. Don’t fall for anyone asking for money or entrance fee’s. Secondly, parking. It’s free. There’s a large parking area on arrival but there are locals who will try and direct you into a secluded area, blowing whistles and directing you there. We pulled in but noticed on the maps.me app that we were using that is suggested parking was free and not to pay. We then realised we were definitely being scammed when they demanded 50.000 dong. Parking a bike is usually 5-10.000 dong. 50.000 was outrageous. We turned the bike around and told them we weren’t paying, for the price to miraculously be lowered to 20.000 dong. I shook my head at my partner, remained firm and told them we weren’t paying. They became frustrated and tried to resist us leaving but eventually got the picture that we weren’t paying. We came out of the parking area just a short walk from there and parked at the restaurants a minute down the road, where a local woman told us parking was free. To thank her, we stayed and had a drink at her shop... rather give money for her honesty and services than to those that are blatantly trying to rip you off. It doesn’t matter that it isn’t much they’re trying to rip you off by, it’s the principle of being scammed which is downright awful. So don’t fall for it!
drawbacks: locals trying to direct you to a secluded area
highlights: giant cave leading to another temple
practical_tips: parking is free in the suggested area
don't fall for locals trying to scam you

author: Kally Q
title: Interesting place
original_content: Interesting temple with a cave behind it.Beware of toilet at the parking area. It has no running water or cubicles between each squatting toilet. The old lady will yell at you to pay 10k Dong when you exit. We ended up only giving 5k. Do not fall for the expensive toilet scam. Avoid the toilet, use the bushes instead.
drawbacks: No running water in the toilet
Cubicles between squatting toilets are missing
Old lady yelling at visitors to pay 10k Dong
practical_tips: Avoid the toilet and use the bushes instead
Be cautious of the expensive toilet scam

author: William O
title: Nice if you have some extra time to spend
original_content: Nice when in the area and when you have some time left to spend, not worth much more. Disliked the very obnoxious people at the entrance gate. Trying to sell things in a way we have (luckily) not experienced at other places in Vietnam. Also wonder why one would buy a squirrel at such a place.. as they have several locked in very, very tiny cages.
drawbacks: obnoxious people at the entrance gate
practical_tips: avoid buying things at the entrance gate

author: Katiej
title: Great place to visit
original_content: This is a great place to go and see, lovely surroundings and views a bit of a climb up but not hard. worth going to see it.The only negative point to add is we arrived with bikes and were promptly told we had to park in a certain area and pay which wasn't cheap, we bartered the price down in the end but they were very rude.
drawbacks: we had to park in a certain area and pay
highlights: great place to go and see

author: thedud31
title: Worth the visit
original_content: I went past this on the way to the bird park and it’s definitely worth calling in on. The ancient pagoda is nestled in some stunning scenery. 50,000vnd to park your bike

author: EddieDean99
title: Worth checking out if you’re cruising around Ninh Binh
original_content: Interesting place to check out if you’re cruising around Ninh Binh. I especially enjoyed the pagoda that is dug into the side of the cave. It was cool to walk behind it through the cave and around to the top. I read that you can climb the rocks past the no climbing sign to get a better view of the landscape below, but we opted not to.Make sure to take the path beyond the parking area to climb up and then back down into a valley with a large pond. Very picturesque and serene. A local man living there tried to get us to pay him to take us into the nearby caves, but it didn’t seem very safe for a variety of reasons. Maybe it would have been fine, but we got what we came for. There wasn’t many people there while we were, so it was easy to walk around and explore at your own pace. As we were leaving, a tour bus unloaded and there was probably 50 people all lined up and grouped together. If you find yourself there when that happens, maybe grab a kitkat or something and wait it out. Note on parking: There’s only one place to park. A lady will give you an official looking ticket stub, but I imagine it’s a scam like most of the other places in the area. She asked for 50k and I tried to hand her 10k. She motioned for more, so we settled on 13k. Small price to pay not to have your bike messed with I suppose. Make sure to keep the parking voucher as she does ask for it when you leave. I’ve also read that sometimes people will try to charge you an entry fee. We did not experience that. There’s definitely no fee to visit the pagoda. A lady did try to sell us what appeared to be a wombat it a cage though.
drawbacks: local man tried to scam them
highlights: cool to walk behind the pagoda
easy to walk around and explore
practical_tips: go early to avoid tour buses
parking scam to be aware of

author: Kacy W
title: Climbing Past the Path...
original_content: The signs say don’t climb on the rocks after the path stops. I can neither confirm nor deny that we climbed on the karst limestone, but let me say that if one were to do this, be careful if it starts raining. It may be harder to get down than it was to get up. The main path goes through three temples: the bottom, middle, and top, as you ascent the mountain. The path stops at the top temple, which is built into the mountain. It’s very impressive and spooky inside the carved out chamber in the rock. It was either free to get in, or we couldn’t find where to pay.
drawbacks: it may be harder to get down than it was to get up
highlights: the path stops at the top temple
the top temple is very impressive and spooky inside the carved out chamber in the rock
practical_tips: be careful if it starts raining

author: aniceglassofred
title: Stopped off on a tour of the area...its beautiful
original_content: It's free and it's gorgeous.  All a bit run down too but that sort of adds to the mystery and different worldly feel of the place.  Less than an hour is fine but you could spend longer if you want to take it all in.  There are a few people hanging about that will pretend to help you up the steps but just ignore them and they will go away.  Be careful though... steps can be slippy and as its not really been modernised for tourists. Overall I thought it was beautiful.

author: iamkayoh
title: Small place, just a quick walk around.
original_content: If you are going to the Bird Valley, do drop by this Bich Dong Pagoda. Pretty small place. Most iconic would be the little bridge to the main gate that you will see if everyone’s posts. Other than that, there is a small temple at the top, pretty amazing though, without modern cranes, I would imagine people had physically carried up the Buddha statues manually. Great work.

author: nyusual
title: Temple on three levels
original_content: A temple in the mountains on three levels. Requires some steep climbing but the serene atmosphere is refreshing. However the sights pale in comparison to what you have at Mua cave. If you see lot of buses, avoid the place. This temple has some steep climbing to do and also walk through a cave (it's lit up). We visited in August on a rainy day, wet with no crowds, just after the rains.
drawbacks: sights pale in comparison to Mua cave
avoid the place if you see lot of buses
practical_tips: avoid the place if you see lot of buses
visit on a rainy day for no crowds

author: UNNIMAYA
title: Charming cluster of Cave Temples and Peaceful Monastery
original_content: This monastery built on the side of Bich Dong mountain, has some interesting cave temples in three levels built against the mountain. The views from the top are good - but not as impressive as the views from higher Mua caves.Included in most Ninh Binh itineraries, this peaceful place can get swamped by bus loads of tourists - this could make your visit suffocating. There are souvenir shops, restaurants, cold drinks vendors and parking attendants (apparently to scam you more than taking care of your parked vehicle) outside the monastery complex.
drawbacks: scam you more than taking care of your parked vehicle

author: leashyjelly
title: Come early and avoid crowds
original_content: It was interesting and worth a visit for sure but not worth coming to if your on a tight schedule. Tour buses full of people come in the afternoon which disturbs the peace. Nice drive from tam coc. Parking is most definitely 10k, the man at parking will try and over charge you but tell him “no, 10 thousand” and he wont argue. Be wary of locals trying to charge entrance fee illegally. It is free to enter! There is also a nice lake, with the owner of the shack offering paid tour of a small cave (we didnt go in so cannot comment) if you walk through the bike parking and round the lily pads you will see some stairs.
drawbacks: Tour buses full of people come in the afternoon which disturbs the peace
Be wary of locals trying to charge entrance fee illegally
practical_tips: Tell the parking man 'no, 10 thousand' and he won't argue

author: Amy L
title: Nice area
original_content: The temples are not overly exciting but it’s an interesting place and it’s free so worth going if it’s near you. Don’t pay for parking, locals try to get you into their huts just park in big car park on street. Dont forgot to go around the back too there’s a lovely viewpoint and little area that gorgeous. It’s not where you go in the main entrance but around the side, you could easily miss it! We also ate in Aroma Indian before we left which was amazing so we had a lovely evening there
practical_tips: park in big car park on street
go around the back to find viewpoint

author: Jess D
title: Neat place but a few issues
original_content: When we first arrived, the local wanting us to pay for parking quoted 50,000VND. This is ridiculous. Start walking away when he quotes this price and he'll lower it. Or park next to the shop in the bigger lot and don't pay at all, especially if you have a bicycle. Don't be afraid to haggle, the prices aren't set by any means. It's just a guy wanting to extort the tourists. The pagoda itself is very nice and scenic. If you have a bit of climbing ability and good shoes, climb past the last pagoda (ignore the sign that says don't climb but be very careful on the rocks. There's no helicopter evacuation out here). If you're a really good person, bring a plastic bag and pick up the garbage that you find. It's disgusting up there and extremely disappointing that tourists would ruin the landscape like that. Do your part, enjoy the scenery and the history, and help maintain its beauty.
drawbacks: Extortion by local wanting to extort tourists
Garbage and litter on the pagoda
highlights: Pagoda is very nice and scenic
Climbing past the last pagoda is a good experience
practical_tips: Park next to the shop in the bigger lot and don't pay
Bring a plastic bag to pick up garbage

author: Shaun_A_M
title: Buddhist Temple in Tam Coc
original_content: This charming cluster of cave temples is a couple of kilometres north of Tam Coc. The Lower Pagoda is located at the base, from which 100 steps lead to the Middle Pagoda, where there's a shorter but steep ascent to the Upper Pagoda. Inside each cave temple, looming statues peer from the haze of burning incense. Outside offers incredible countryside views.

author: shiraziwine
title: would be nice to visit but not really fascinating
original_content: This Pagoda is not a real must see of the city but i recommend you to see if you are in Ninh Binh. the hill, temples and the place are making a nice complex.

author: nellielim
title: Lovely Buddhist temple
original_content: We were hanging around the crossroads a short distance away and noticed people walking across the lotus lake. We walked down the road and discovered this old Buddhist temple complex of three pagodas set into the mountainside. The entrance was reached by a long walkway across a large lake of lotus blooms. The walk up the hillside was not difficult. Once at the top, lovely views of the surrounding countryside could be seen. We were glad we visited this temple as it made up for the disappointment of Tam Coc. Entrance to this temple is free.
highlights: lovely views of the surrounding countryside
made up for the disappointment of Tam Coc

author: FactotumDellaCitta
title: Beautiful complex on hillside
original_content: The Bich Dong Pagoda is a complex of three pagodas, built into a hillside, with sets of stone steps connecting the pagodas.  As one ascents, one is treated to great views of the surrounding countryside.
highlights: great views of the surrounding countryside

author: Ma R
title: Loved this placr
original_content: Amazing temples set within caves in beautiful countryside quite near all the other attractions. I’m very Glad I didn’t miss this!

author: Lor6969
title: Careful not to pay more than you should!
original_content: Nice motorcycle ride to get to this Pagoda. This is 3 temples in the mountain. The entrance is beautiful. Parking for motorcycle is 20000dong. Free entry! Careful the guy at the parking place wanted us to pay 50000 dong each person. I told him we will not pay it and then he said : oh you did not do the boat trip? Then he did let us go!
drawbacks: Guy at the parking place wanted us to pay 50000 dong each person
Had to argue about parking fee

author: Wenyo91
title: Ignore the warnings. Go to the top of the pagoda.
original_content: Things to note: - Entrance to the pagoda is free. - Parking for bicycle is free, although my boyfriend and I bought ice cream and drinks from the lady who owns the middle stall at the beginning and at the end of the visit.- When you get to the top of the temple, there’s a warning sign which says “do not climb”, ignore that. Initially, I thought it was disrespectful and wanted to skip that but a local man asked us to climb up and we didn’t regret. The view at the top of the mountain was phenomenal! See the photo attached. Just be warned that the climb is at your own risk.
highlights: view at the top of the mountain was phenomenal
practical_tips: ignore the do not climb warning sign
buy ice cream and drinks from the lady who owns the middle stall

author: iliketomoveandsee
title: Beautiful place ruined my "parking officials"
original_content: We rode our bicycles out here from our hotel in Tam Coc, and it took around 15 minutes. On arrival, we were whistled at by a local telling us we must park our bikes on their private grounds or else we cannot go into the Pagoda, and they also demand money. We would have paid, but we were told by another local who was conducting bike tours that it's causing them chaos and stopping them from being able to take their tours there. The locals guarding the area are rude to everyone. I'm sure people would be happy to pay if they could communicate a little in English, and were polite to people. No need to scream and shout at people in Vietnamese.

author: YanVa
title: Great, but beware of the dog!!!
original_content: We went at noon, it was very hot. But there were no other tourists because of it. The caves can cool you down. It's a beautiful sacred place. But beware, my friends went in a wrong building and there was a dog and they got really scared when he chased them.
drawbacks: got really scared when he chased them

author: cherry_streets
title: beautiful place, but crowded and locals attempt to rip you off
original_content: We came by motor bike and parked our motorbike under a tent by the pagoda. The lady charged us 50k dong, and then tried to sell us entrance tickets while the place is free entrance. We got ripped off on the parking price... We unfortunately came at the time where there were tour buses which ruined the peacefulness of the place for us... Try going early morning or evening if you are an independent traveller.
drawbacks: Got ripped off on parking price
highlights: Try going early morning or evening

author: KellyS3210
title: Peaceful and serene
original_content: A pretty collection of very old looking temples, and it is free to enter! First you pass through an impressive gate over a bridge surrounded by water lilies. You walk up several sets of stairs to get to the top temple (including a cave - you’ll need a torch). We saw several people walking up the mountain behind the top temple - there’s a sign saying do not climb, ignore this (!) and climb up anyway - you’ll be rewarded with stunning views. Do take care as it is not a designated path and you will be clambering on rocks, but it is doable. Overall, worth a visit, and takes around an hour.

author: Megin v
title: Be prepared to take some really cool pictures at this Pagoda!
original_content: We decided to walk to this Pagoda from Tam Coc town. Which was actually quite a walk in the heat but led us through nice surroundings and green rice fields. Reaching this Pagoda was a reward though!
drawbacks: quite a walk in the heat

author: Resgol
title: Surprisingly Beautiful
original_content: We came to the pagoda with no expectations. We just took our rented bicycle and got there. We've had enough pagodas...We were therefor surprised to find out that this pagoda is an ancient one and that's it's partly carved into the stones. The path is slightly flooded but the depth is 10cm so there's no problem crossing it (although locals offer tourists to pass those 30m with a motorcycle or a boat to keep them dry). Another local sold us tickets for VND 10k which were probably fake.The temple is small but beautiful. A lady prayer who prayed and sang added to the atmosphere.

author: tifasch
title: One of the most beatiful temples
original_content: The temple is beautifully build on the mountain so that you have to climb stairs to see all of it. Parts of the buildings are inside caves which look amazing! And the view is very nice. The way to get there from Tam Coc leads through nice rice fields.

author: UK việt
title: Happy moments
original_content: On our way to Bird valley we stopped to explore Bích Dong. A stone bridge leads to a pagoda and is the start of a magical journey through caves to a view point across the countryside.

author: KaladinT
title: Nice quick stop in Tam Coc
original_content: If youre cycling or scootering around Tam Coc, this place is a very accessable stop to spend half an hour or so.Theres quite a few steps up to the top but very manageable and youre rewarded with some nice views. We also got roped into making a donation to a guy who gave us incense sticks. Shouldve seen that coming really, but as theres no entrance fee it's okay.
drawbacks: got roped into making a donation

author: Gayathri_SG
title: Steep steps to Pagoda
original_content: We clicked Mua Cave in the morning, so could not climb the steep steps in the pagoda. We did manage to go until half the distance.
drawbacks: could not climb the steep steps
highlights: managed to go until half the distance

author: native-travels
title: Temple built into the mountain
original_content: Be sure to climb to the top of the temple. Ignore the sign that says do not climb and make your way up. The view is well worth a careful ascent.
practical_tips: ignore the sign that says do not climb

author: Nemo N
title: Exciting bike trip to the countryside
original_content: We stay in Tam Coc homestay and it is really easy to take a biking to Bich Dong pagoda. The bike trip go through the golden rice paddy and this peaceful scenery countryside help us totally relax, getaway from hustle and bustle Ho CHi Minh city. The pagoda with thousand of lotus flowers blossom. We are really lucky to catch all that beautiful things.
practical_tips: visit during lotus flower blossom season

author: Blackwater190
title: Hidden Temples in a moderate climb
original_content: Just a short taxi ride or cycle out of Ninh Binh to this interesting Temple complex set into small mountain. The entrance to Bich Dong is over a walkway across a lily pond through an ornate gate.  Then gradual walk up to the 1st Temple.  Then it is moderatly steep set of steps to Temple number 2.  This is were you start to get some views into the valley.  Go around behind this temple will take you up a steeper set of stairs inside a limestone cave (steep but manegeable) past a small shrine and through an opening onto a large rock platform overlooking a view between limestone hills across to rice paddies in the distance.  Well worth the moderate effort and a unique experience.  Take water as it can get hot and humid.
highlights: overlooking a view between limestone hills

author: TheBlackleys
title: Very enjoyable
original_content: We enjoyed visiting the temples here but the best part was a walk we found through the valley on one side which was just gorgeous and then on the other side when you leave if you turn left towards the toilets you can walk around the rice paddies which is also nice.

author: Joe B
title: Pagoda built along side a mountain
original_content: Located a short distance from Tam Coc this pagoda is built alongside a hill. There are three sections built on different levels. The climb up the stairs is step and good walking shoes are recommended, the service of a guide is not required. If you visit the pagoda by bicycle expect to pay a small fee for parking. (peanuts)
drawbacks: the climb up the stairs is step
highlights: three sections built on different levels
practical_tips: expect to pay a small fee for parking

author: Elizabeth Q
title: Worth the climb
original_content: This is an amazing place with pagodas built inside the mountain. Be aware though, there are a huge number of steep steps, but for those able to make the climb, the experience is worth it.

author: Stanis Cataldo
title: Pretty cool, don’t get fooled!
original_content: Pretty cool temple, this was our first stop and I’d definitely recommend! There’s the main path to the top through a cave, which I definitely recommend doing! There’s another path that looks like it’s closed to visitors, but you can go to it through the back, there are no temples here, but since there’s no one else around you can get some cool pictures!As others have mentioned do not pay the scammers in the entrance! We paid 20K each only to realize later it should’ve been free! They’ll go to the extent of even moving your bike so that you’re forced to pay, but you absolutely don’t have to (unless you’d like to give a tip).
drawbacks: paid 20K each only to realize later it should've been free
highlights: main path to the top through a cave
practical_tips: do not pay the scammers in the entrance
go to the back for pictures

author: ginsengNewYork
title: STUNNING! DO WALK TO THE TOP!
original_content: Consists of three pagodas, each one on a different level ascending a karst mountain. To reach the second level you climb a set of stairs. To reach the third level, you go through a huge cave lit by lights and then climb some more stairs. The surrounding landscape is beautiful and the pagodas are  actual working worship places!We just don't understand all the complaining about the small scams, knowing that 10 000vnd are worth about 50 cents!!! In Vietnam, people make about 300$ a month, and have little social advantages (they pay for their kids schooling, even in grammar school, for hospital, etc, and are fanned to the teeth with the government corruption), so don't be so harsh to judge their little scams...

author: ooocasey
title: A nice place ruined by SCAMMERS
original_content: There is a lady who will rip you off- she charged me 25,000 dong to enter but my host at my hostel said it was supposed to be FREE after I got back.  I was also charged 20,000 dong parking fee- but I should have parked down the road and walked over.  DONT GET RIPPED OFF by these DISHONEST low-life people!  how awful.
practical_tips: park down the road and walk over
check with your host for free entry

author: Sally M
title: Three levels of cool scenery
original_content: First, pay attention to all the reviews and avoid paying fake entrance/overpriced parking fees to the people by the entrance. The temples themselves are typical of Vietnam, but the setting is worth seeing and it's fascinating to contemplate the work that went into carving these monuments into the mountain. Doesn't need more than 45 minutes to explore. There's another (free) walk off to the right of the entrance to the pagodas that is also very worthwhile, through rice paddies and past caves down the river.
highlights: work that went into carving these monuments

author: SirGaw
title: History amid amazing surroundings
original_content: Located only a 5 minute taxi ride from Tam Coc is the amazing Bich Dong Pagoda.Set in various caves and niches in the Karst peaks, the pagoda is an important place of worship for the Buddhist followers. the climb all the way to the uppermost lookout is a little tough. Steps vary in height and at times there are no hand holds - please watch your steps. The view and the experience far outweigh any discomfort.Close to the entrance is a drink/food/souvenir stand, but be aware of the roving 'ladies' who give your back a rub down - the service is NOT free and payment is expected. You may need to be assertive and tell them to stop.
drawbacks: Steps vary in height and at times there are no hand holds
the service is NOT free and payment is expected
highlights: the view and the experience far outweigh any discomfort
practical_tips: be aware of the roving 'ladies' who give your back a rub down

author: CareerBreakAdventure
title: Intentional Tourist Motorbike Tire Puncture
original_content: I wanted to warn all travelers about intentional tourist motorbike tire puncture.  It happened to us in Tam Coc while our motor bike was parked in the Danh thắng Tam Cốc - Bích Động parking lot.  We visited the temple and were greeted by a lady parking lot attendant who handed us an official looking ticket for parking and said we needed to pay 10,000 dong for parking. This is probably correct, but then she said we also needed to pay her 50,000 dong per person for entry into the temple. This is a stated free temple, so we told her no. After a while she gave up, gave us the hush hush sign like she was letting us sneak in so don’t tell anyone. While we were in the temple, someone poked a hole in the side wall of our tire. We nearly got to the main part of town before we abruptly stopped, noting a completely flat back tire.  Luckily neither of us were hurt and we did not cause an accident with others.  “Luckily” there was motor bike mechanic nearby.  The puncture hole was on a new tire on the sidewalk near the rim.  Highly suspicious indeed as we had not hit or run over anything.  We had the mechanic shop call our hotel where we rented the bikes and they helped us to change out the tire for 420,000 dong.  The hotel charged us 125,000 dong since this was a criminal act that they have seen frequently which we reluctantly paid.  Per the hotel owner, there are people who will slash traveler tires out of spite or if they don’t get to steal your money. Seriously... I wouldn’t recommended going to this temple anyways, but definitely don’t use the official scammer parking lot out front.
extracted_spaces: Danh thắng Tam Cốc - Bích Động parking lot
highlights: luckily there was a motor bike mechanic nearby
hotel staff helped change the tire
practical_tips: don't use the official parking lot

author: Harriet D
title: Off the beaten track
original_content: Be aware - do not park your bike/scooter close to the entrance as there is a lady who will try and charge you for parking and will move/hide your bike if you do not pay. This pagoda is lovely. A nice walk to the top and if you go round through the temple into the dark cave you arrive at a nice view - use the torch on your phone to navigate the dark cave.Go out of the pagoda and around to the left and you’ll find another path up another track. We walked up and over to a small lake and there was a short walk. Nice place to listen to the frogs and experience ‘quiet’, not many/any other people around.
drawbacks: Lady trying to charge for parking
highlights: Nice view from the dark cave
practical_tips: Use torch on phone to navigate dark cave
Go out of pagoda and around to the left for another path

author: Marissa H
title: Go for the valley behind the mountain!
original_content: First of all, THERE IS NO ENTRANCE FEE, please be aware of fake entrance tickets. We were approached by people asking 50,000 entrance fee per person, but we knew entrance was supposed to be free so we just said we would pay 10,000 for parking our motorbike. They still asked for 10,000 per person, but we said we were parking only 1 bike, so we’ll pay once.  We gave them 10,000, received our parking ticket and went our merry way. We were a bit concerned they would dump our motorbike in the water, or that we would have difficulty getting it back but we left without an issue. The road through the rice fields in Tam Coc are gorgeous. The pagodas are pretty cool, I would probably give it 3 stars if it weren’t for the beautiful valley you can walk through behind the mountain. Instead of walking over the bridge towards the gate, walk through the motorbike parking, around the lake and follow the stairs up. You can walk the entire way through the valley, and it is STUNNING. It was so quiet and peaceful, this was actually one of my favorite things we did in Ninh Binh. It was raining and we still loved it.Would definitely recommend visiting this place! Go do the pagodas in the mountain first, and don’t miss the valley behind the mountain.
drawbacks: approached by people asking 50,000 entrance fee per person
concerned they would dump our motorbike in the water

author: Ryan V
title: Definitely worth a visit
original_content: This was one of the best things we did in the Ninh Binh area. While Tam Coc was clogged with day-tripping tourists from Hanoi, all jostling to climb aboard the boats in the center of town, Bich Dong was relatively peaceful and the temple was well integrated into the area's natural beauty. The temple is set into the mountainside in three levels and you'll need to climb some fairly steep stairs to reach the top. Perhaps not the best attraction for those with mobility issues. It's not the most ornate or colorful temple you'll ever seen, but that's really the point - the surrounding mountains provide the beauty.It's only a fifteen minute bicycle ride from Tam Coc, so there's really no reason not to visit during your stay there. Walking through the three levels of the temple won't take up more than an hour of your time, but you could spend all day cycling through the nearby rice fields.One thing to note: if you come by bicycle or motorbike you will be directed to a covered parking area. If you leave your bike here, you'll be charged somewhere between 5,000 and 50,000 dong. Instead, grab a coffee at one of the cafes that are 100 meters or so up the road. Leave your bike here and avoid the parking fee. If anyone tries to charge you an entry fee to the pagoda, it's just a local trying to scam you. This is a religious site and there is no fee to enter. However, as a sign of respect, you should cover your knees and shoulders as you would at any other temple in Southeast Asia. It's not required, but it would show some cultural sensitivity.
drawbacks: not the most ornate or colorful temple
highlights: well integrated into the area's natural beauty
practical_tips: grab a coffee at one of the cafes up the road

title: Hands-Down Best Ancient Temples in Ninh Binh
original_content: If we had only one chance to go back to NB to visit a temple/pagoda, this would absolutely be it! It is a real shame that this temple is not rated more highly.Our party of four had never seen anything like this gorgeous series of temples and pagodas before. The temples and pagodas are built into this limestone mountain. Each level up takes you around or through a temple in order to get to another, higher level temple. Just absolutely gorgeous.Highly recommend wearing shoes to this temple and walking slowly. The bridge just to get to the entrance alone is quite slippery. Also, we recommend buying incense sticks from the woman at the front selling them. Good blessings just for offering incense sticks. I paid 5,000 Dong for this, not the 10,000 she was asking.Hope you enjoy your visit!

author: Sigrid Hilpert
title: Lan Ha Bay – A Peaceful and Stunning Alternative to Ha Long
original_content: I spent a full day exploring Lan Ha Bay during my stay in Cat Ba Island, and it turned out to be one of my favourite experiences in Vietnam. The bay is incredibly beautiful, with towering limestone karsts rising from calm emerald water, but what really stood out to me was how peaceful it felt. Unlike Ha Long Bay, which can get crowded with boats and tours, Lan Ha Bay has a slower, more relaxed atmosphere — you can actually hear the water, the birds, and the wind.We joined a small boat tour that included kayaking through hidden lagoons and quiet caves. Paddling under narrow rock arches and discovering secluded little beaches felt almost magical. The water was so clear that we even stopped for a swim. Lunch was served on the boat, featuring fresh seafood from the area — simple but delicious.If you enjoy nature and want the same dramatic scenery as Ha Long Bay without the busy crowds, Lan Ha Bay is perfect. It’s stunning, serene, and feels just a little bit more special because it remains less commercialized. I’d highly recommend it to anyone visiting Cat Ba.

We took a cruise with Vega Travel on the Unicharm — you can read my review if you're interested — and it was a great experience.

author: Roger E
title: Cruise in Halongbay
original_content: Our trip in Halong Bay with the cruise ship was an amazing experience that we will remember for a long time. The ship offered a perfect combination of relaxation, adventure and first-class service.Kayaking gave us a chance to get close to the magnificent nature, where we explored the majestic limestone cliffs and the calm waters. The Thai Chi lesson on deck at dawn was a magical start to the day and a relaxing moment that gave energy and focus. The excursion with traditional rowing boats gave us a deeper insight into the local culture and a unique opportunity to enjoy the beautiful surroundings in an authentic environment.The service on board was outstanding, and we would especially like to highlight Linh Chi, who really made our stay extra special. Her friendly and professional approach, attention to detail and willingness to always help made our trip even more memorable.We highly recommend this trip to anyone who wants to experience Halong Bay in the best way. Since the weather was great doesn't make things any worse.

author: Ingamar A
title: Lan Ha Bay, a hidden gem!

author: Kellen G

author: Analiese E

author: Émilie Moreau

author: Rhianon Hughes

author: vip_foodie
title: Must Try Overnight Cruise Experience in Vietnam
original_content: We opted for the luxury Lan Ha Bay cruise of 1 night and 2 days over Halong Bay as it is relatively less crowded and it offers same views and activities as Halong Bay. It cost us 110 USD per person and it was totally worth it. This included pickup from Hanoi and later drop off as well. We were picked up early in the morning and first reached the cruise point. There was a small breakfast stop on the way. We were taken to the main cruise boat via a small boat and offered the welcome lunch and drink. They had good number of Vegetarian options as well. We then checked into our room which was nothing less than a luxury with such great views. We headed for a Kayaking event and afterwards did swimming and enjoyed the jacuzzi. In the evening, there was a spring rolls cooking class in which we learnt and then made ourselves. The sunset was magical from the cruise. During the dinner, we were offered a four course meal keeping in mind our dietary recommendations. The dinner was absolutely delicious. We witnessed the local costumes show and the bamboo dance. Then we did the fishing and relaxed with herbal foot bath. All these activities were included in the package. Spa facilities were also available at extra charges. Next day started with a Tai Chi class and then visit to nearby caves in a small wooden boat. This experience was also quite nice. We then checked out and had an early lunch. Finally with a heavy heart, we bid goodbye to this cruise experience.
highlights: same views and activities as Halong Bay
practical_tips: opt for the luxury Lan Ha Bay cruise for less crowded experience
check the package for included activities

author: Russell N
title: One of our best experiences in Vietnam - not to be missed.
original_content: We did the full day hike with a guide (you could easily do this hike without a guide - the path is very obvious), however I would recommend a guide because what would otherwise be a pleasant walk through the jungle becomes an educational experience. Phuc (our guide) was able to spot and then describe the behaviour of a number of animals that we would have simply have walked past without noticing. He also had an in-depth knowledge of the uses of many plant species including my favourite: the colourful and appetising looking, one time fruit. So named because you only get to eat it once - as it is fatal. The hike is strenuous and requires the use of hands to scramble over the rocky stretches - trainers are sufficient when it is dry but would advise against it in the rain (to provide context we are moderately fit 60 year olds). After 'summiting' the 5 peaks on the route we stopped for lunch at Viet Hi village.  Here you have the opportunity to have fish nibble the skin off your feet while you are nibbling on your overpriced lunch. We were then provided with bicycles to explore the fields around the village (which is itself in an amazing setting) and then enjoyed a downhill ride to the harbour where a speed boat took us out to a floating fishing village. Included in our tour was the use of kayaks to paddle around the various bays and inlets of Lan Ha Bay as the sun started to set - magical. The speed boat then took us back to the jetty with a golf cart transfer to our hotel. ps Keep an eye out on the way back as we were lucky enough to see a troop of the critically endangered golden-headed langurs on an island.All of the above (excluding lunch) was $21! One of the best days we have had during our multiple visits to Vietnam.
highlights: opportunity to see critically endangered golden-headed langurs
practical_tips: consider hiring a guide for a more educational experience
