author: Domien F
title: Past glory
original_content: Faded glory, poorly maintained, pictures from the past. The only part that is still fun is the view point. Nice climb but there are more spectacular views.

author: Ashlyne N
title: Great place for a hike
original_content: If you’re looking to get in some hiking and great views while on the Dolan of Cat Ba this is a must visit! It gets busier as the day goes on so I suggest getting here in the morning. Your park pass gives you entry to the hiking trails and caves within the park. The smog is quite bad in the winter months it seems so the views are quite obstructed.
drawbacks: smog is quite bad in the winter months

author: Antonio Rodríguez
title: A hidden refuge
original_content: We enjoyed a quiet atmosphere and found picturesque viewpoints that left us breathless. This offbeat destination is perfect for couples looking to escape the bustle and connect with nature. Highly recommended!

author: Catriona Boston
title: Nature's Beauty
original_content: Cat Ba National Park was a breath of fresh air for us. We hiked through stunning landscapes and enjoyed breathtaking views. The trails were a bit challenging, but totally worth it.

author: Marie Dubois
title: Spectacular hike in the jungle
original_content: Hiking trails offer breathtaking views of the bay. We had the chance to spot langur monkeys. The guide was passionate and shared a lot of information about the local wildlife. Not to be missed!

author: Giffard U
title: Jungle Adventures
original_content: The challenging climb to the viewpoint was totally worth it - the panoramic views of limestone cliffs and the bay were breathtaking. Spotted some rare langur monkeys too! The well-marked trails and knowledgeable local guide made our adventure perfect. Pack plenty of water and good hiking shoes!

author: Horizon Hugo
title: Nice trek and beautoful view
original_content: It's a nice activity to do in cat ba. You can do a trek of 2h to go forth and back. You will have an amazing view over the national park. 80% of the path is with concrete or rocks stairs, the last 20% is more complex and very steep , but doable for kids and senior ( we've seen a lot of groups ) You don't need to book the most expensive ticket to do that the second one at 120k is already enough and with that one you can also go to the famous cave 500m from there.
drawbacks: The last 20% is more complex and very steep
highlights: Amazing view over the national park
practical_tips: Don't need to book the most expensive ticket
Second one at 120k is already enough

author: aline
title: Ngu Lam Peak
original_content: Prepare hiking boots, a hat and water because it climbs to Ngu Lam Peak, very nice view.It is especially for the peak that the park is worth visitingYou can hike in the park. We wanted to go to the frog pond but we met people who told us that it had no interest, poor pond with a frog a crab and snakes.Be careful not to pay 160,000, it's a scam.Trung Trang cave is included in the price at 120000 that is to be done.You won't see monkeys or deer.Luckily, a lizard, a squirrel and a snake

author: Deane Pendreigh
title: Total immersion in nature!
original_content: Trails through the jungle led us to spectacular views of the bay. We had the chance to see langur monkeys and a unique flora. The local guide shared fascinating stories about the ecosystem.

author: Laurio
title: A wild romance in the jungle
original_content: The trails were challenging but rewarding, leading us to breathtaking viewpoints over limestone cliffs and the emerald bay. Spotted some rare langurs from afar - what luck! The local guide shared fascinating stories about the park's ecosystem. Despite the humidity, it was a perfect adventure for us nature-loving lovebirds.

author: Rodrigo
title: Serene exploration
original_content: The quiet atmosphere of the park allowed us to disconnect from the daily bustle and connect with nature in its purest form. We walked well-maintained trails, observing the rich biodiversity and enjoying moments of peace.

author: Hoang Nguyen
title: A weirdly beautiful place

author: Atlante Walte
title: Hidden gem!
original_content: The unique geological formations were stunning, especially the limestone karsts. We appreciated the local community involvement in conservation efforts. This park offers a perfect blend of nature and culture.

author: Lana C
title: Hiking in Cat Ba national park

I highly recommend bringing plenty or water, a fan and an umbrella if you can. The heat in Vietnam at this time of the year could be intense.
drawbacks: heat in Vietnam at this time of the year could be intense
highlights: views from the top were breathtaking

author: Agatha C
title: The view is better than the picture!
original_content: Intense and great hiking! It is only 1,5km but you feel it 💪🏼. The trails are doable, exotic plants and trees and if you are lucky enough and go quite can find different types of animals. You don’t need to rent a bike 🚲 from the entrance to the beginning of the trail is only 500 mts. The parking 🅿️  outside is 🆓 .

author: Luisa R
title: Take the tour through the views
original_content: We hired a car with the hotel that took the 4 of us there and arranged the pickup time. The short excursion is worth it. Climb a peak and see beautiful views of the National Park mountains

author: Leannie

The view from the top is amazing, just ensure you have adequate footwear and plenty of water.The national park entrance fee of 160k seemed steep by Vietnam standards, and it didn't really feel like much money had been ploughed into it, the entrance looked quite dated and signs where they were available were very faded.

national park entrance fee of 160k seemed steep

adequate footwear and plenty of water

author: Busby Bordie
title: Discovering Cat Ba's natural wonders
original_content: We explored Cat Ba National Park and were struck by its unique geological formations, shaped by millions of years of erosion. The panoramic ocean views from the summit are breathtaking, offering a glimpse into the park's stunning biodiversity. With scenic hiking trails and opportunities to spot rare wildlife, Cat Ba is a must-visit destination for nature-loving couples. Don't miss the chance to experience its natural beauty!
practical_tips: Don't miss the chance to experience its natural beauty!

author: ellen m

original_content: Ridden on a scooter from the town of cat ba about 18 km away to the park. Fine to do your own business. The monkeys are still rare to see but it was a nice trip up to the viewpoint (and heavy).

author: Barthélemy J
title: Very nice views
original_content: I hiked with Mario, the guide. I've been traveling alone for 2 months, and I think it's been the best day of my entire trip. Mario is very nice, super smiling. We had a good laugh.Hiking is quite difficult, but doable. Quite slippery with moisture and mud. The views are beautiful. We stayed 30 minutes at the top so beautiful. I highly recommend.

author: Stephen K
title: The Real Jungle with Rio
original_content: Is there an option for 6 stars? The extra star would be for Mario (Rio). He made this trek the most enjoyable experience my daughter and I had in Vietnam. He is friendly, kind, and his English is impeccable. He was looking out for us the entire trek, carrying our water (literally) without asking, pointing out the little critters along the way, and giving us a hand up when the ground was especially slippery. He took photos and videos the entire time, and sent them to me within hours of ending our trek. He did all of this in flip flops/slides! Much respect for his kind humanity and his fitness! Now the trek. My goodness it was awesome! If you’re looking for REAL jungle, this is it. You start by picking up a trekking stick of bamboo or hard wood at the start of the trail. The path was clear but not carved out and made easy. The mud is thick in spots, threatening but never actually sucking the shoes off our feet. There is natural vines and trees to provide some stability on the big steps, and an electrical cable running up the trail in spots when natural options are not available. The sights are stunning and wild, and the sounds are deafening with bird songs and critters. The hike up the mountain is a tough, leg blasting experience, but this (almost) 50 year old man in reasonable but not great shape had no problem getting to the top. Once there, the views are absolutely worth the sweat and effort. You look out over Ha Long Bay and the craggy mountains carving the sky. A quick rest (or longer if you like), and then it’s down again. Mario leads the way down, just in case you slip.  Like all treks, going up is physically difficult, and coming down is easier but technically more difficult. Before you hit the jungle, there is a short cycle ride through some villages and rural landscapes. You end the ride at a restaurant where you have a rest, a drink, and a fish massage. This is where you put your feet in a huge fish tank filled with hundreds (thousands) of fish (10 cm or so) who nibble (no teeth) on your feet and lower legs. This is quite the experience, and very ticklish! My daughter and I were laughing uncontrollably until we got used to it. It also made your feet feel fantastic afterwards. This same spot is where you end up after the big hike, for a great meal, drinks, and socializing with your group and others. If you’re a dog lover there are little pups to pet and (secretly) give scraps to. Cute little buggers. After the meal, it’s off again for another, much shorter hike to a cave that appears untouched and not ‘civilized’ like most other caves you see on tours in Vietnam. In fact, it was Mario’s first time to this particular cave. This trek is shorter, but parts are actually more intense than the first, with some climbing as some of the ‘steps’ are too tall to just step up. Still not an issue, and the rock with its natural holes and crevices giving you multiple options. Once you’re done with the cave, you loop back to the little restaurant for another beverage break, and then it’s back on the bike for the ride back to the port where you catch the boat.The boat itself is decent, the crew is great (Ryan leads this part, and is just as personable as Rio, and his English is also fantastic). Dinner onboard was excellent, beer and other bevvies cheap and cold, and we kayaked, swam, and even jumped from the top deck of the boat for a much needed cool off/rinse. If you are looking for a good, reasonably tough but achievable trek through the jungle, with a confidant and personable guide, do not hesitate, book this immediately. I’ve never given a review like this before, but Mario and the tour deserve it and much more. Thank you Rio for giving my daughter and I the best experience we had in Vietnam. This will be a lifelong, cherished memory for both of us. 🙏🏼
highlights: deafening with bird songs and critters
views are absolutely worth the sweat and effort

author: Kathi M.
title: Beautiful view
original_content: We were in the national park in February, it was low season and therefore not very busy.Entry fee per person 80,000 VNDParking space for scooters 5,000 VNDToilets are available at the entrance.We hiked to the viewing point, which is signposted.The path up is sometimes very strenuous and there are not only very high steps but you have to really climb the last part. Sturdy shoes and enough water are recommended.You have a wonderful view from the top. It is definitely worth it.When you get back down, towards the exit, you can observe and see lots of butterflies.
drawbacks: path up is sometimes very strenuous
last part is a real climb
practical_tips: sturdy shoes and enough water are recommended

author: Chris318i
title: Great view from the peak
original_content: I visited Cat Ba National Park with my wife and kids (10 months, 3 and 6 years old) to climb the peak. The hike is a little challenging, especially with kids. Besides the great view from the peak there is not that much to see. Still, the peak and the view there are worth the hike.

author: Fai D
title: Best experience
original_content: We had an amazing experience with Cat Ba Local! The consultation and support by Judy was excellent and helped us find the best hike and kayak option for our needs. Highly recommend this trekking!
practical_tips: go with a guide like Judy

author: Jos B
title: Great, anazing hike and tour
original_content: We booked the jungle trekkingtour with boattour Lan Hai bay at the end. It was very well organized and We had a great tourguide Van! He speaks very good english and knows everything about the nature. He tells you a lot about Vietnam. We climbed up & down over steps, rocks and slipery ground, but Van was always close and very helpfull. We are 62 years old and in a normal condiotion.  It's a tough trekking tour but very beautifull. We had good diner in a little Village, a nice biketour to the little harbour, where we got on a local boat through the beautifull bay.  We had also good kayaking  and a lovely swimm. We recommend highly Van and this tour.
practical_tips: book the jungle trekking tour with boattour Lan Hai bay
go with a good tourguide like Van

author: Viet Exquisite Travel
title: Cat Ba National Park - worth visiting
original_content: We spent 3 days on Cat Ba Island and half-day trekking at Cat Ba national park. With the entrance fee as 80.000 Vietnam dong, you can visit the forest part, climb to Ngu Lam Peak and  Trung Trang Cave. The hike to the top of Ngu Lam Peak is really nice and takes about 45min one way with quite steep stairs. The view from Trung Trang cave is breathtaking, too.
highlights: The hike to the top of Ngu Lam Peak is really nice
The view from Trung Trang cave is breathtaking
practical_tips: The entrance fee is 80.000 Vietnam dong

author: Blake
title: Hike through the wood and to a peak
original_content: At the cost of only 80,000 VND, you can enter into this lovely national preserve.  With the options of a few trails you can hike to the peak which has breath taking views.  For my partner and I, it took us about 2 hours to make it from the entrance of the park, to the peak and back again.  I would highly recommend to bring plenty of water.  The trail necessary is not long but is mostly uphill while walking in sharp rock.  Closed toed boots are recommended as well.  There are other attractions in the park but due to our visit in the off season these were not open.  Safe travels!!
drawbacks: closed to other attractions in the off season

author: lpgarralon
title: Superb walk
original_content: Great walk a good difference in altitude be careful of the parking lot on the left when arriving to escape it's a thief with his smile avoid eating soup etc even drink a little coffee to really flee

author: Megan S
title: Not Worth The Time & Unwelcoming Staff
original_content: The national park itself was lovely- small, quaint and lots of stairs. There were bicycle rentals that the woman insisted to not rent to us (which was translated by an English speaking worker). Although unless you would want to ride the bike to the start of the trail, it would’ve been pointless as it was a quick 5-10min walk from the ticket booth. But still, the gesture was rude to not allow us to rent bicycles.The trail was narrow and felt like any other hike path in humid climates. I think the main event would’ve been the views at the top…We unfortunately decided not to climb to the top as another traveling couple shared that they saw snakes on the route. 😂😂😂 However, I don’t think the views would’ve altered my 1 star rating.There was a museum of taxidermy animals just across the ticket booth area. It was a good 5min of self-guided entertainment… no workers inside, no bathrooms to be found.Regarding transportation- We took a taxi here that our hotel coordinated for us, which included a stop to the hospital caves prior (those caves are worth a visit!). Our taxi somehow abandoned us at this last stop lol… either we wrapped up the trail too quickly or he ran a very long errand. Our phones didn’t have service and the workers were rude about trying to help us- suddenly the English speaker could speak English. I sensed that we were not welcomed at that park from the start..After about 45min just waiting by the main entrance, we were able to flag a taxi.Just an overall disappointing experience. I would NOT recommend this as an attraction to intentionally put on your travel itinerary- the entry may be cheap, but the time is not worth the visit when there are so many other gorgeous (and hospitable) spots nearby.

author: Hong Van Cruise
title: View from above
original_content: This is one of the places not to be missed when coming to Cat Ba. Admire the natural beauty from above. Standing from Ngu Lam peak, you can see Lan Ha Bay and admire the preserved canopy of perennial trees. Worth a try.

author: KingCong Travel
title: Place that attracts tourists.
original_content: I am a Taxi driver and a local tour guide working on Cat Ba Island. I often bring foreign tourists to this location because the natural scenery is very beautiful.

author: Seaside
title: A Natural Wonder
original_content: Located on Cat Ba Island in Hai Phong province, Viet Nam, the park covers an area of 263 square kilometers and hosts a rich biodiversity of plants and animals. You can explore the park by hiking, biking, kayaking or taking a boat tour. Along the way, you will see stunning landscapes of forests, mountains, caves and beaches. You will also encounter some of the rarest species in the world, such as the Cat Ba langur, the golden-headed langur and the white-headed langur. The park is also home to many other mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians. Cat Ba National Park is a must-see for anyone who loves nature and adventure.
highlights: stunning landscapes of forests, mountains, caves and beaches
many other mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians

author: Julia
title: 14km hike to Viet Hai plus boat ride is tough work but one of the best days you’ll have, if that’s your thing
original_content: We did the 14k hike to Viet hai and it made for one of my favourite days of our trip. So much nature to see, and look out for the dried up ancient lake on your left hand side early on. Some lovely views towards the end. There’s a fair bit of up and down, and the ground is very uneven at times, so be prepared for that. One bit of advice: you’ll need to book a boat in advance to take you back to Cat Ba, or once you get to Viet Hai village. We didn’t realise and luckily a group of various hikers of us spoke to the owner of the village cafe at Viet Hai village, just past the park gates on the other side, and she called a boat for us. We chose the slow boat for 600k, so we could enjoy the views, which takes an hour or so. We paid an extra few k so that we could stop and go for a swim on a secluded beach.  There’s also a faster boat for 800-1M ish. Recommend this whole day so much, it was big smiles from start to finish.
drawbacks: need to book a boat in advance
highlights: big smiles from start to finish
practical_tips: choose the slow boat for better views
stop and go for a swim on a secluded beach

author: ctm7944
title: Cat Ba NP - Ngu Lam Trail
original_content: Rented motorbike from accommodations. First visited Trung Tram Cave. Then drove 2km to Ngu Lam. I purchased a ticket at Trung Tram for both (80KVND). But, you can purchase tickets separately, at each place, as well (40KVND each). Parking @ Ngu Lam is 10KVND: pay the attendant. The trek to the peak is strenuous in parts, with lots of stairs and stone steps which can be a little slippery. No flip flops please!The forest landscapes are quite scenic. And there are a couple of lookout points.
drawbacks: lots of stairs and stone steps

author: Jaroslav Nečas
title: Hikers welcomed
original_content: Small but lovely national park includes well maintained hike paths leading to hills with wonderful views and several caves. Entrance fee is cheap.

author: JanBorn2Love
title: Nice place to visit
original_content: Catba National Park is a paradise for nature lovers. The hiking trails offer breathtaking views, the caves are magnificent, and the park is home to rare and endangered species. It's a must-visit for an unforgettable experience in Vietnam.

author: Kent Traveller
title: Avoid - dirty - neglected and totally not worth paying to see.
original_content: What a disappointment. The whole place should be closed to the public until it’s had some investment and is fit for people to visit again. It is run down, dirty , shabby and totally neglected. Some parts are strewn with rubbish and rubble. To have to pay money to get in is an insult. It’s stated that the entrance fee goes towards upkeep, improvements and maintenance. There is clearly none of that happening here. We’ve been travelling through Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam since January and this is by far the worst “attraction “ that we have visited. The toilet facilities are filthy and smell is nauseating. To be honest though , my whole impression of Cat Ba island is pretty much the same as with this place. Thank goodness I’ve only spent 3 days here. Never again.
drawbacks: run down, dirty , shabby and totally neglected
Some parts are strewn with rubbish and rubble
toilet facilities are filthy and smell is nauseating
practical_tips: avoid visiting until it's had some investment and is fit for people to visit again

author: Joly Stephen
title: Test for our physical and mental endurance
original_content: This hiking trails are very good. This gives you a perfect nature feeling. Steep climbing up/down ways will test you physically and mentally. If you go with friends or couples it's gives you opportunity to help and guide each other.
drawbacks: steep climbing up/down ways will test you physically and mentally
highlights: opportunity to help and guide each other

author: Callum W
title: Be warned! dangerous and intense trekking!
original_content: Be Warned! This is a extremely dangerous trip especially when slippery!The guide did take care and look out for us but I would definitely recommend only doing this if you are happy to climb straight up sharp rock faces and walk through dense jungle, no paths.Feel like this was not stressed enough before booking.
practical_tips: only do this if you are happy to climb straight up sharp rock faces and walk through dense jungle

author: oren t
title: Best agency in cat ba
original_content: Kat ba local  agency are The greatest agency in Cat Ba!!! They are really professional, kind, have exellent location and their english is perfect.

author: Alu-Poo
title: Beautiful forest
original_content: If you are staying on Cat Ba Island for a couple of days this is definitely worth a visit to get an impression of the forest on the steep rocks. We took a taxi to the park. We chose the path to climb Ngu Lam peak - which is what most people do. The path is excellent, all done with rocks and concrete. There were no leeches. However, it is going up quite a bit, involving many stairs. I would not recommend sandals, but huge hiking boots are not necessary. There is a small building on top from which you have a phantastic 360 degree view. The path goes a little bit further from there to another peak where you also have a nice view. Then it goes back down more or less the same way. Just follow the arrows, no map needed. We didn't see many animals, certainly not the famous monkeys. The forest is too dense and the birds to shy. The few birds we saw were at the bottom near the houses - the ones that used to people. The park entrance ticket is also valid for a cave 1 km down the road. Tell your taxi (if it is also taking you back) in advance that you will also see the cave. Ours tried to get more money for that. The cave has some nice spots in it and is worth a visit. It won't take long at all. The entire trip tooks us about 4.5 hours.
practical_tips: tell taxi driver about cave visit

author: Mel B
title: Fun for the fit
original_content: The view from the top is amazing. Getting to the top ... phew.As a background on me, I'm not an overly fit person so if you are, and planning to do this hike then go for it. However.. I struggled, the first leg of the hike was the hardest, due to fending off the mosquito's rather unsuccessfully. Once you get higher it gets cooler but you are already three layers deep from your own sweat that doesn't evaporate because it's a jungle. Basically I'm saying, it's not leisurely walk, it's hard work and honestly if I had heeded warnings about gyming before coming to vietnam i may have a differnt opinion. The view is spectacular at the peak and worth it but honestly as a representative of the less athletic types, I was just sat there with my inhaler, smiling briefly at the view and looking down at my impending return trek.Don't be like me.Be fitter 😂
practical_tips: heed warnings about gyming before coming

author: Michael
title: Amazing island
original_content: Had a good time in Cát Bà with our friends we had a lovely trekking, biking and kayaking tours with Blue Swimmer Adventures. Overral we enjoyed our time here very much

author: Vivian B
title: Worth a visit if you’re at Cat Ba Island
original_content: We spent 3 days on Cat Ba Island & loved it there.  We hiked up to the lookout area at Cat Ba National Park.The forest (jungle) is gorgeous.  The climb is fairly strenuous, so I wouldn’t recommend it if you have a physical disability.  We enjoyed it & felt like we deserved our nice cold drink at the end!  Take a bottle of water, sunscreen & mosquito spray.

author: Barbara W
title: Trek to the top
original_content: Our guide Luu, took us to the National Park and trek to the peak, they said it was easy! Let’s say it was challenging in parts, but we made in and lovely view at the top.

author: Beth
title: So. Many. Stairs.
original_content: I was promised this was a nice easy walk. Lies! Hundreds and thousands of steep  slippery stairs! At one point it's no more than jumbled rocks tou have to clamber over. Nice views from the top but I wouldn't say it was worth the clamber up. Other than that we couldnt find any of the other stuff to do here, butterfly area etc was non existent. I think it was 80,000 dong to visit too.

author: Jerome B
title: Very Nice Island Visit
original_content: Visited Cat Ba Island as part of a cruise on Halong Bay - very interesting a picturesque.  Clearly catering to tourists but still pretty good.

author: Pieter S
title: Very beautiful! Unprofessional
original_content: It is a nice hike to the top of the mountain. It is quite sporty with a climb that takes around 45 minutes to get up and 30 minutes to get back down. Be careful, there are almost no bars to hold on to and it can be very slippery. When we went back around 16:00 ‘o clock it was getting pretty dark on the road back. I would recommend not going up after 15:00 or 15:30 at the latest. Then you have the time to go up, make some pictures and get back safely with still some light in the forest. When we got back at the reception around 16:30 we saw some tourist going up, which I thought was very irresponsible from the park and it looked like they were just after the money. If this wouldn’t have happened, totally 5 stars. Besides that I can totally recommend! Such a nice view!! Be aware that the platform on the top is not the actual top... the mountain (that is in the way of your panaroma view) is the real top! Enjoy!!
drawbacks: almost no bars to hold on to
going up after 15:00 or 15:30 at the latest
practical_tips: get back safely with still some light in the forest

author: Luuk H
title: Nice viewpoint
original_content: We drove to the park by motorbike (25min from cat ba town). Easy hike (steps, just the final bit is somewhat steep and slippery when wet) to the viewpoint. Took us around 40min. Great 360 view, probably even better with clear skies. With entrance ticket (80000) you also get access to the nearby cave.
drawbacks: somewhat steep and slippery when wet
highlights: probably even better with clear skies

author: Frans R

author: ClaudiaW

highlights: view from the top is pretty amazing

author: HrFruJensen

original_content: One of the Best views i ever has seen. The hike is challeging, but rewarding. Nature is beautifull. The toilet is a giant anthill tho.

highlights: One of the Best views i ever has seen
The hike is challeging, but rewarding

author: Gunnar M

original_content: We took the ferry to Cat Ba Island and a local bus to the National Park. The hike to the top is really nice and takes about 45min one way! At some points it is very difficult and strenuous. You better wear walking shoes and bring water. The view from the top is amazing. Thecentrance is very ceap. They have some food sellers and restrooms on sight!

author: labdhi s
title: Awesome hike and great view
original_content: If you are looking for a 360 view of the island this is a good reason to hike. The hike itself is beautiful. I would recommend  hiring the scooter and taking the less known road from the other side of island to reach. You have to pay 5000 VND for parking at the park and the cave. The ticket of 40000 VND includes the Cave entrance. I would recommend  doing both.
