author: Magnus W
title: Yeah let’s do this
original_content: If you are looking for a great hike this is it and If you are in ok shape it takes less than 1h to go up. But on the way to Dinh Ngu Lam.  Make a stop at Trong Trang Cave and invest 30 min. You won’t be disappointed. Great Cave.  You pay the entrees fee to the park there and just show the tickets as you enter the park later on.
practical_tips: Make a stop at Trong Trang Cave
Show tickets as you enter the park later on

author: Lukas
title: Viet Hai hike
original_content: A review for people who want to do the "long hike" to Viet Hai village which is not so hard and you definitely don't need a guide. Take a first local bus departuring from the center of Cat Ba town (right opposite the harbour's "welcome" sign) at 8 am. One trip costs 30000 VND. When you reach the park, pay 80k VND for the access.The trail is easy to follow, there are many red arrows showing the way. I recommend you to have Maps.me downloaded just in case, it shows the entire 12 km long trail. 8 km to Viet Hai, 4 more to reach the port. A few more details about difficulty of the trail. Up to Frog pond it's very easy - forest walkway with some stairs. The toughest part comes after frog pond, it's like 30-45 minutes of uphill/downhill rocky terrain. Be ready for some sharp rocks, a few tricky parts, use your hands where necessary. You DO need proper hiking or trail running shoes. All in all you should be able to reach the port in 3-4 hours, depending on your shape. Unfortunately, the second part - Viet Hai to the port - is just asphalt, quite boring but surrounded by quite nice mountains. Keep in mind that you want to get to the port before 12:45 if you want take the only afternoon public boat going back to Cat Ba town. It costs only 50k VND (buy a ticket on the boat) and really departures at 12:45, not at 13:00 as you can hear from some local people. Name of the public boat is Do Viet Hai (see the picture below), it was the ugliest boat in the harbour, easy to spot :) You can sit outside on the upper floor and enjoy beatiful views of Lan Ha bay, you should reach Ben Bao port in about one hour. There you can grab a bike or simply walk to Cat Ba town, it's only 1 km.My rating of the trail itself is 3/3.5 stars. Go for it if you like hiking, just don't have too high expectations.
highlights: beautiful views of Lan Ha bay
proper hiking or trail running shoes

author: Catherine W
title: Full hike to Viet Hai village
original_content: Decided thanks to other reviewers to walk this route without a guide - followed the advice and took the local bus (from opposite the large ‘welcome’ sign by the harbour) to the national park around 8am. A few things we thought would be useful to share on top of the information from previous reviewers:The path is easy to follow mostly, but we experienced two places where we got temporarily lost:1) At the bottom of the first proper decline you leave the ‘bush’ into more of a clearing with long grass / plants, and two overgrown paths forking left and right. We took the left but after a minute it seemed to fade; fortunately we spied the more formed stone path to the right of us through trees. Therefore I assume the correct way would have been the right hand fork2) After the last long descent down the rocky cliff/ boulder sections (more below) close to Viet Hai, you reach a clearing with a couple of paths going left and right - no arrows or anything - we took the left one and wandered through some scrub bushes until eventually we reached a path with a large green sign pointing either to a cave (right) or back the way we came. We took the unmarked left option and eventually popped out by the Bungalows as we were meant to!Timings: we reached Viet Hai in just over 2.5 hours, and walked on to the harbour in a further 45 mins - c3 hours 15 - plenty of time to make the 1pm boat (brown wooden boat pay on board). We’re fit enough and hike a fair amount but this walk is challenging - the terrain is incredibly uneven on the back half of the walk and you scramble up and down and across steep boulder and small cliff sections, often needing to use arms as well as legs to transverse. Anyone with ankle or knee complaints or pregnant women should possibly think twice before undertaking this - I almost twisted my ankle and stumbled several times. No way would I advise wearing flip flops!All in all a fun experience being alone in the jungle and wandering back to the port but not without its challenges!
drawbacks: scramble up and down and across steep boulder and small cliff sections
almost twisted my ankle and stumbled several times
highlights: fun experience being alone in the jungle

author: Sally J
title: Viet Hai Hike
original_content: Such a lovely hike through the National Park! The way is pretty well marked with signs and red arrows although a map is useful in places. There's quite a lot of scrambling towards the end but, if you're used to hiking, it's nothing too extreme. For anybody who's not, the guides seemed like a good option. We met a few groups/guides along the way and they looked they were enjoying themselves. It was easy to organise a boat in the lovely village of Viet Hai to take us back to Cat Ba town (if only we had stayed in Viet Hai!). It took us about 4.5 hours to complete the hike, and was roughly 12 km one way on a mixture of paved path, forest track and a few pretty steep rock faces.
drawbacks: not suitable for those not used to hiking
highlights: well marked with signs and red arrows
practical_tips: organise a boat in Viet Hai

author: Mcneilco
title: Very beautiful park.
original_content: We did the climb, literally climb, to see above the canopy and felt that it was very well worth it. The path is tricky with a scramble at the top but great rewards for the effort.
drawbacks: The path is tricky with a scramble at the top
practical_tips: go prepared for a scramble at the top

author: Bari_Rabarbari
title: Amazing views
original_content: It is really 'must' when you are on Cat Ba Island. We reached the top and the view was breathtaking.

author: revelation21.6@outlook.com
title: Fantastic place, well sign posted for solo trekking, don't miss the navy viewpoint near the caves
original_content: Fantastic place, well sign posted for solo trekking and easy path to follow, don't miss the navy viewpoint near the caves.. It's hard work but worth itDidn't see any monkeys, but saw loads of interesting (and slightly terrifying) spiders, as well as exciting birds, butterflies, lizards and squirrelsGreat placeAdvice; if you hire motorbike to get here, only fill 1/2 tank petrolI gave my bike back with nearly a full tank, even after a longish ride finding the sunsetAnd petrol isn't cheap in the island
drawbacks: Petrol isn't cheap in the island
highlights: Loads of interesting (and slightly terrifying) spiders
Exciting birds, butterflies, lizards and squirrels
practical_tips: Don't hire motorbike to get here

author: Eden V
title: An amazing and challenging experience
original_content: There is a short and long route, for the sake of time we chose the short route.This route is equally challenging, climbing the stairs is very challenging and worth the view you see when you reach the top.
drawbacks: climbing the stairs is very challenging
highlights: worth the view you see when you reach the top
practical_tips: choose the short route for the sake of time

author: totolapraline
title: Beautiful and Varied
original_content: A very very nice park, with both stunning views on the water and delightful treks through the center of the island.Highly, highly recommend both day cruises and renting motorbikes. Only downside is a lack of visible wildlife.

author: delaenag
title: Good hike
original_content: We wanted to do the Frog Pond hike so rented motobikes to get there (which felt pretty safe to drive there as there wasn't tons of traffic) but we got there just before 2 and were told we had to arrive by 1 to do the Frog Pond (which is meant to be 4-5 hours) so instead we did the 2 hour hike which was also surprisingly nice and beautiful.  It is full of steps and once you're at the top you can go up to the very top of the next hill for an even better view.
drawbacks: Had to arrive by 1 to do the Frog Pond
highlights: Even better view from the top
practical_tips: Arrive early to do the Frog Pond hike
Rent motobikes to get to the Frog Pond

author: Prince_Brand999
title: Worth a visit!
original_content: Really amazing place  everyone gies to Cat Ba because of the Bay cruises but the Park area should not be left out by any chance! Would reccommend doing the longer hije to Viet Ha village, it is a little demanding hike that goes over 5 hills but it is worth it, the jungle sights are breath taking!
practical_tips: do the longer hike to Viet Ha village

author: Maxine M
title: Cat Ba Vietnam
original_content: We enjoyed our stay in Cat Ba. Nice little island with some great cafe’s for authentic food. Good idea to hire a motorcycle and see more of the island about $10 for 4hours.

author: Andrew
title: Hard on the legs but great view
original_content: We walked to the lookout in the National Park and it was tough going for us as it can be quite steep in places and we had to stop a few times to catch our breath however the view is great when reaching the top.
drawbacks: had to stop a few times to catch our breath
highlights: view is great when reaching the top

author: Hannah L
title: A treacherous but rewarding hike/climb
original_content: An enjoyable hike through forests for a lovely, if a little underwhelming view of the top of the forest. It’s certainly a challenge and not something I’d recommend to anyone under-confident in their footing or fitness, but it’s good fun, and you’ll see some wildlife if you look- we saw lots of butterflies, a little snake, some birds of prey and lots of frog, sadly no monkeys though lots do reside here apparently. Definitely get a guide, as it’s hard to find your way around. We paid $25 each for a pick up and guide with Signature travels. That also got us lunch and a cycle through the hills and a boat trip back. The bus was late and the guide couldn’t speak a great deal of English but you’ll find this a lot in Cat Ba.
drawbacks: hard to find your way around
guide couldn't speak a great deal of English
practical_tips: pay $25 each for a pick up and guide with Signature travels

author: Ela D
title: Breathtaking
original_content: Amazing view from the top. The untouched nature and mountains are breathtaking. For the hike I would recommend sneakers and don’t forget your mosquito spray!

author: Brigit
title: Hard climb up to the top
original_content: It was very hot and steamy and we found the climb extremely hard just to get up there and get a bit of a view of the surrounding area. Wouldn't do it again just for that. There are no animals to be seen apart from some butterflies and the odd squirrel. Interesting also that apparently they have just doubled the price for the entrance fee about 6 months ago from 40.000 VND to 80.000 VND.The whole park doesn't seem to be looked after at all. Have seen much better National Parks in other parts of the world.
drawbacks: the park doesn't seem to be looked after

author: Jayhappygolucky
title: I’m not in terrible shape but I thought the climb was challenging.
original_content: I’m glad I did it but some reviewers made it look like a walk in the park. (Haha) It was hot and the views were beautiful. Saw lots of butterflies. When I checked my phone it said I climbed 68 flights of stairs. Perhaps iPhone pedometers are not that accurate but it felt like a lot. The stairs were pretty steep and I would not recommend the hike if it rains or if you are wearing flip flops.

author: Tom M
title: Worth the hike
original_content: Challenging walk up the hill to the peak, more due to the heat rather than the gradient, but well worth it when you reach the top for a great view across the beautiful green landscape.

author: dencasrutkova
title: Ammazing nature
original_content: This place is a “must see” if you visit this island and love nature! There are beautiful view spots that will take your breath away once you are on the top! And if you book a night in the hostel in the park, no entry fees  to the park or the caves to be paid! :)
practical_tips: book a night in the hostel in the park

author: Jeanette H
title: Good views
original_content: After a hot climb you are rewarded with very good views! If you have the time then book a guide to show you more.

author: yvonnewedden
title: Independent trip to the national park
original_content: We were taken to the national park by our daughter currently staying on the island, it was a hard walk through the jungle type area in what felt like 40+ temperature and high humidity. Small path with lots of steep steps and a scramble at the last leg to the view point. Well worth the effort but not for those who struggle with the heat as exercise as it is hard to to. So proud I made it
practical_tips: not for those who struggle with the heat

author: Lee C
title: Take plenty of water
original_content: Me and my partner headed to the national park on our final day on Cat Ba and I have to say we wasn’t disappointed, there are several route options that you can chose from based on length of time you wish to be at the park for but the person on the desk at the entrance to the national park will explain all the options in great detail to you.My partner and I enjoy a good walk and the national park is just that - although it’s quite a tough hike at certain points, and as I said in the heading bring plenty of water as it gets extremely humid in the dense forest sections. It’s all worth it once you see the views though..

author: Nir A
title: Stunning view but very dirty
original_content: I had half a day to spend.Went to this stunning park.The area is very tropical and gives you the feeling you are alone in the jungle.There is a nice but steep hike up to a stunning viewpoint (a must do but dont forget water and a long breath before you start climbing).The only thing is.... the hiking area was full of empty bottles and lots of rubbish (so sad, this is a truly nature valued place which is not preserved properly).
drawbacks: hiking area was full of empty bottles and lots of rubbish
practical_tips: take a long breath before climbing

author: Gobnait o lunacy
title: Nice park, spoilt by messy island.
original_content: Just bought a ticket at the entrance and self guided around. Signage is a bit wanting in places, one notice board completely obscured with stickers placed there by tourists.Tourists. Don't do this ffsCan't get over the rubbish discarded by tourists, bins are provided so there's no excuse people. The road leading to the park area has a massive landfill and rubbish is generally strewn around Cat Ba as a whole. Vietnam would seriously want to look at the way it manages a national park island. Domestic rubbish and builders rubble everywhere.It's a nice hike through jungle with great lookout areas (again, spoiled by rubbish and tourist stickers and scrawlings). Enclosed shoes or boots are recommended rather that flip flops.
drawbacks: Signage is a bit wanting in places
Domestic rubbish and builders rubble everywhere
practical_tips: Enclosed shoes or boots are recommended rather than flip flops

author: Shanka M
title: Fantastic tropical setting and spooky caves
original_content: The entry fee has recently gone up to this place and it's a bit of a hassle to get here from Cat Bah Town, but the lush green forest and multi chamber cave complete with bats (and completely isolated) are well worth the effort. We only did the short trek, but based on that, the long trek would have been a real adventure. We went early and had the place to ourselves for a bit. Fantastic views as you climb.
drawbacks: entry fee has recently gone up

author: Samwisegam
title: Tough but worth it
original_content: We paid $20 USD for a guided trek. This included the bus to the National Park, entry fee, lunch and the boat back. It was about 10km through the jungle and then 5km flat to the harbour after lunch. The sign posts in the park aren't very clear and some of the routes we took were scrambles which we wouldn't have thought were the right way to go so we are glad we had a guide. He pointed out various animals along the way and provided us all with anti leech spray. We were the only 2 in our group of 10 not wearing walking shoes which would have been ok if it was dry but as it was wet our trainers just didn't have the best grip and parts were really slippy. Take plenty of water and mosquito repellant with you. We did 4 peaks in total before arriving at the village for lunch. You need to have some relative fitness to complete the trek we did as the heat and humidity can really have an effect on you plus some of the scrambles were a bit tricky but the views are worth every step.
drawbacks: sign posts in the park aren't very clear
some of the routes we took were scrambles

author: bris2lrocks
title: Don't forget your deet!
original_content: We did and couldn't take a rest on the way up because the mosquitos would set in.  That said it was a good hike to the top and well worth the effort. Great views from the top and we heard lemurs on the way back down. There were hundreds of butterflies of different species and birds singing in the canopies. Plus with your ticket you get in to the trung trang cave for free, which is also worth a visit.
practical_tips: get in to the trung trang cave for free

author: planetawdrodze
title: Nice
original_content: There are some trails in the park so if you have more time to discover cat ba island than only seeing the bay, you can go there. On some of them guide will be useless.
practical_tips: Go to the park for more trails

author: HightowerSF
title: Mountain hike with amazing mountain views
original_content: It takes about an hour to hike up to the mountain peak, semi technical difficulty, lots of steps. The views of surrounding mountains are really nice.
highlights: views of surrounding mountains are really nice

author: cbcb60
title: Great hike - a little challenging in places but well worth it for the views!
original_content: We did the short hike (40k dong each) up to the two peaks and it was a 2 hour round trip, allowing for a bit of a break and some photos at the top. We were told at the entrance that it takes about 1 hour to climb up but we did it in about 45 minutes. I wouldn't call us fit but we do walk a lot, and we managed it just fine. A couple of the sections towards the top are very steep and change from proper steps to more of a rocky scramble, but they're both quite short so it's not bad. I'd definitely recommend wearing shoes with some good grip as the ground and rocks are quite slippy in places even when dry. Don't forget water! Try to do it on a clear day - the views are very impressive!
practical_tips: try to do it on a clear day

author: Suzanne M
title: We did the hike to the lookout
original_content: Small fee to get in the park, nice trail up the mountain and fabulous look out at top, entry fee also includes visiting caves.
practical_tips: entry fee also includes visiting caves

author: Harriet F
title: Worth the climb
original_content: Amazing place and views. Well worth the climb! At the gate they say the whole thing will take up to 2 hours but you can climb both peaks and stop at the top and get back in about an hour. We were however charged 80,000vnd when online it said 40,000vnd. Might have been due to Tet but have extra cash just in case.
practical_tips: Have extra cash just in case

author: Dr Z
title: Great hike!
original_content: The 2 hour hike was tough, but the views at the top were definitely worth it. Take a picture of at the map at the bottom to avoid some dead-end trails.
practical_tips: take a picture of the map at the bottom to avoid dead-end trails

author: Nina O
title: Very nice view on top
original_content: Beautiful view over the green hills/mountains at the viewpoint and top (few minutes more to get there). They said it takes you 1 hr to get to the top, but in 30-40 minutes it is possible for faster walkers.
drawbacks: They said it takes you 1 hr to get to the top

author: Wanderlustsimone
title: Tiring but worth it!
original_content: We somehow followed the signs at the beginning of the park wrong and took a detour up. The views here are stunning! Try and go on a clear day, the park closes at 5pm, takes you approx 45 mins to walk up, 30 mins to walk down, so don't go any later than 3pm so you get as much time as possible at the TWO viewpoints up. It's a steep climb at times so wear comfortable ealking/hiking shoes and take water up with you. Had a great day in this park 10/10

author: Doves Q
title: Great Trekking
original_content: If you are ready for trekking this tour is a must . A very nice walk through trees and nature , I saw huge plant leafs that I never saw before . The walk is not easy but not to hard too you need to wear a good boots / shoes to be comfortable and don't forget to take water with you . Recommended to start Trekking early in the morning to avoid lot of other people do the same trekking route .
drawbacks: You need to wear a good boots/shoes to be comfortable
highlights: Saw huge plant leafs that I never saw before
practical_tips: Start trekking early in the morning

author: #wattersadventure
title: Great if you are ready for a hike
original_content: We weren’t the most fit people, but we made it to the top with some struggle! We lost one in the group on the way up and we were definitely challenged but we made it to the top!! The view took my breath away.

author: Sven E
title: Choose the rigt time for a visit!
original_content: Nice short and easy trekking tour up to the viewpoint. Takes about an hour (one Way). A lot of tourists especially young loud backpackers who are not able to behave mindfully and enjoy the sound of nature in a respectful way. Recommendation: start trekking as early as possible. Get there on your own motorbike or bicycle!
drawbacks: young loud backpackers who are not able to behave mindfully and enjoy the sound of nature in a respectful way
highlights: start trekking as early as possible
practical_tips: start trekking as early as possible
Get there on your own motorbike or bicycle!

author: PnP Wiz
title: Cat Ba National Park - Nature Scene - Lots of Hike
original_content: Cat Ba National Park is a small park with a nature scene of trees, plants, and flowers.  The flower valley is located right next to the park, and it is very small valley for pictures.  Prepare for a 1Km hike from the bottom to the top of the mountain.  There is a path with steps to walk and climb up to the top.  It is a little bit of adventure of hiking.  Along the hiking, you will see lots of identified and labeled trees, plants, and flowers.  You need to wear comfortable shoes and bring water.  You can have a good hike and workout after you finish from the bottom to the top of the mountain.  The park just have nature scenery and nothing else, and you cannot camping or stay there over night.  It is not recommended to go during summer because of mosquitos and hot.  It is recommended to visit, but it is not a must see place.

author: puchka
title: Unique
original_content: The boatman took us through the islands to show us the unique rock structures and caves.  We rowed through one of the larger caves and saw the duck caves so low only ducks could swim through.  The islands comprise the National park and protected against poachers.

author: theflyingcrab
title: Well wroth doing
original_content: The peaks take about 40 minutes to hike up to on easily marked trails and the views are truly stunning and worth the effort.

author: Erica G
title: Worth to go
original_content: Only know some people called this place 'Jurassic Park' after trekking. This park is awesome and if you wanna experience the jungle walk then don't miss this place! Good shoes is a must and expect lots of walking, climbing and pass through the route with full of plants and grasses! I was joining the 1 day trekking which trekking (and climbed) for 8 km and visited the Viet Hai Village following with the cycling to harbour and boat trip (passed by beautiful Lan Har Bay) back to shore... Wonderful experience and scenery! Love it!

author: Jane M
title: Great half day hike
original_content: We booked our hike through Cat Ba ventures. Our guide Tuan was extremely informative. We learned about the flora and fauna of the parl plus some history relating to the war. A good hike, go in the morning before it gets too hot. We are fairly fit seniors so were able to reach the summit!
practical_tips: go in the morning before it gets too hot

author: Ginnyleeinwonderland
title: It's a good day to climb
original_content: bought the tickets and with those tickets, I could go into the National Park and then go into Trung Trang cave. It took about 1 hour to go to the top then 1 hour to go back. Trung Trang cave was located in another place which was about 1-2km from the National Park.The government allowed people to make some stairs into the National Park for the tourists to visit and to protect plants and animals. In that way, they could collect some money to maintain, research and protect plants and animals. The price of the ticket was not expensive, it was actually cheap. It was not sunny anymore because there were many trees there to cover the sun, so I could hide under the trees to prevent myself from getting sunburn. The forest was really nice and quiet. Sometime it was slippery but I was lucky to not fall down. Up to the top, the view was amazing. It was not the area to see the sea but I could see the whole area with many high mountains, they were really high like they could reach to the sky. The clouds were so close like they were touching the top of those mountains. I met another friendly dog who decided to follow me to the higher top. It took about 10 minutes to go to the higher top. The way up there was quite hard. One of my friend told me that whenever we climb up to the mountain, as long as we could find a place to step in, we were ok. Up to the higher top, it was wonderful. I could see more, more high mountains, small villages in valleys and lakes.
highlights: the forest was really nice and quiet
I could see more, more high mountains, small villages in valleys and lakes

author: geoffNelson
title: Track to lookout
original_content: If you enjoy climbing things and have never seen trees before then the walk is OK, otherwise it is just a hard climb up a concrete path and steps through a litter strewn area of fairly average forest. The view from the top is good but you can see other equally impressive views just riding around the island. I saw better forest near the entrance to the park with less constant noise from all the other tourists. I think if I went back I would try the walk to frog pond as it sounds a bit more enjoyable.
practical_tips: try the walk to frog pond

author: RomanPod
title: Easy trekking
original_content: Beautiful trek in the national park, there is an entrance fee about 2 USD, no need in any additional guides, if you can step in to the jungle and a climb a little - its a nice experience for a half day tour. You can go by taxi, its about 300.000 both ways from Cat Ba.
drawbacks: no need in any additional guides
practical_tips: its about 300.000 both ways from Cat Ba

author: 300trina
title: Worth it!
original_content: It's a bit of a climb and can get quite busy but great view, loved it!Apparently I have to write min 100 characters, wow, that's annoying

author: jack w
title: Good but busy
original_content: A group of us spent an afternoon here for a walkabout. The scenary and views are breathtaking, but the heat can get a bit much so lots of water was essential. The mosquitos picked up as we left, but lots of deet and it wasn't too bad. Definately worth a trip, and lots of photo opportunities throughout. would recommend!

author: Caramea L
title: Beautiful location
original_content: 3 hours walk with an amazing view. We also saw spiders and a huge snake (2 meter) if your legs ain’t good. Than this isn’t such a good idea. Don’t forget 2 liter water to bring for your friend and yourself
drawbacks: Than this isn’t such a good idea

author: Binemaan
title: Oasis of green, paradise!
original_content: Great (but very hot) to hike.Quiet place with amazing green mountain scenery and lovely views. Make sure you have good protection for mosquitos, we were sweating the repellent away. And it was only 8:30 am.

author: Ariane VdB
title: Nice trail!
original_content: We had a great time, the view at the end was definitely worth the trip! There is a full panoramic view!! Buy water at the lady in the beginning of the trip. She said she was the cheapest and she was. Make sure to bring at least 1L of water, is would recommend 1.5L. And be careful during rain season when it gets very slippery. A must do!
highlights: view at the end was definitely worth the trip
practical_tips: buy water at the lady in the beginning of the trip

author: Gleb P
title: walk to the pick
original_content: we had 1 day hike to the pickit was really nice.45 min if you are in good shape you get to the top. very nice view over the island.there is a lake near the restaurant at the entrance so you can jump in and refresh yourself.nice and easy day tour
extracted_spaces: lake near the restaurant at the entrance
highlights: very nice view over the island

author: Simon L
title: Beautiful hike!
original_content: Me and my two teens did this hike in 1 hour and 20 minutes including 15- 20 minutes brake at the two viewpoints.There's a great view from the top, but unfortunately like the rest of Vietnam, far too much garbage on the trail.We saw chipmunks on our way.
drawbacks: far too much garbage on the trail

author: Housam Elkouteini
title: Nice hike
original_content: We went there on a rental motorbike. After paying the entry fees there is a bathroom you can use after entering the national park and later there is a small shop then the hike starts. It took us around one hour to reach to the very top and 20 min to go down (running) it was fun and the weather helped alot. It was also a good exercise but we did not see any animals while going up. There were couple at the entrance inside cages only

author: KGLeeds
title: A lovely way to spend an afternoon
original_content: This is a beautiful place to walk and spend a few hours. The trek is clearly marked and easy to follow, although it can be slippy after rain. There is a nice cafe to get a drink at the beginning (or end) of the trails.

author: Thomas L
title: As you want
original_content: We did a trek for 13 km across the national park with a guide. First 5 km was easy and partially prepared with steps placed here and there. The second half was proper jungle trekking, with “junge noise”, slippery trail and sharp rocks. So if you are up for a good trek you will have to do the whole trail.

author: Niklas G
title: Hot, humid, great
original_content: Bring water, lots of water. Bring decent shoes. Hire a guide of some sort and go in a hike. Don't forget some Good old endurance either, 'cause there är some hills to climb. A lot of sweat and panting, but if you aren't averse to that sort of thing then it is well worth it! Lush green scenery, primary jungle and some nice views at the end, if you make it to Viet Hai village, which we recommend.

author: Wei C
title: Hot humid hike
original_content: We came here to hike to Ngu Lam Peak. Definitely a morning hike, but I must admit, this is the most uncomfortable hikes I've done due to the weather and environment. Once you get to the top, it has quite a mountainous view. It seems like the country is trying to promote people to hike more, as they have very well directed signs and paved trails.What was more exciting was actually the scooter ride to the National Park!
drawbacks: uncomfortable hikes due to weather and environment
highlights: well directed signs and paved trails

author: Freemanhp
title: Great to trek in the rain forest
original_content: Situated 15km to the North West of Cat Ba Island.Cat Ba National Park is also home to 20 species of mammals, 69 species of birds, 20 species of reptiles and amphibians, 11 species of frogs. Seventy bird species have been spotted here, including hawks, hornbills and cuckoos. Many of these animals are listed in the Red Book and under tight protection. The most notable of all is Vooc (white headed monkeys), which can only be found on Cat Ba Island.various species of rare wood trees and one of the rarest tree is Kim Giao , the material to make chopsticks for the Kings. It is said that Kim Giao chopstick will turn into another colour  when it touches poisoned food.There are some good hiking trails here, including a hard core 8km route up to a mountain summit. There are a lot of cave, lake, challeng and even undiscovered point here to experience. You can join tour with Cat Ba Green Trail Travel - the local tour operator on the island.
extracted_times: 8km route up to a mountain summit
practical_tips: join tour with Cat Ba Green Trail Travel

author: Tracy C
title: Stunning View!
original_content: My friend and I got a taxi via Asia Outdoors to the entrance of the national park and where we started the trek to the peak. It may have been humid and rainy and there were mosquitoes, but that view at the top of the canopy was breath-taking and peaceful. It took two hours round trip. The trek can be a little challenging (i.e. slippery steps and a little maneuvering over rocks) so bring some good shoes and water for it. There are shops and stores before the start in case you need to stock up. But definitely bring 40,000 VND for entrance and the taxi we booked cost 350,000 VND. All in all, well worth the money!

author: sanjnaseralvo
title: Worth the hike
original_content: You will sweat and get your clothes dirty, but it is worth the view! Loads of steps and some parts are practically climbing (but we also saw people in sandals do it)

author: Ann Georgina
title: Breathtaking. Literally. haha
original_content: Was hesitant at first because I know Im not that fit to do climb but then... was surprised that I was able to make it. Like the view from top was just amazing and fulfilling. I am happy I made it safely all the way. You can take your time easily. Some steps are challenging but you will make it. Better wear a proper shoes or sandals to climb the steps. And yeah kinda bit sad because there were litters on the top for sure from the tourist who had their bottle waters and just left it there. Stupid tourist. Please dont be one. Dont leave your garbage only footprints and good memories. I wish they will have a clean up all the areas and be more strict to the people who are coming up.
highlights: view from top was just amazing and fulfilling
able to make it safely all the way
practical_tips: wear a proper shoes or sandals to climb the steps
dont leave your garbage only footprints and good memories

author: NYCtoSF
title: Good to see while in Cat Ba
original_content: We did the short hike/trek loop up to the top viewing point. You will see the limestone cliffs (but no views of the bay) - still beautiful with the lush green mountains surrounding you. Entry was 40VNDpp + 5VND parking per motorbike (as is custom in Vietnam). Take a big water with you as it gets hot despite being in the shade. I would not recommend if you are not in shape and recommend wearing decent shoes (slip on sneakers are fine). We did not see much garbage (which is a plus) and the park was not crowded on a Friday morning.

author: Acelynn Abel D
title: Beautiful place but too many people with bad attitude
original_content: A great forest and mountainous area but may be this is high season of tourism, people rush here like waterfall, throw garbage everywhere every path and climb to trees to take photos even when those trees are weak.
drawbacks: climb to trees to take photos even when those trees are weak

author: Helena N
title: Easy hike, Nice view up top
original_content: From Cat ba town centre, it's around 70-80K Vnd taxi round trip to the entrance. You will need to ask for them to wait for you for around 2 hours, and call the taxi guy 15 min before you get back to the entrance. The entrance fee is 40K Vnd/person. The view up top is very nice. Lots of things to see on the way up there as well.
drawbacks: You will need to ask for them to wait for you for around 2 hours
highlights: The view up top is very nice
Lots of things to see on the way up there
practical_tips: Ask for them to wait for you for around 2 hours
Call the taxi guy 15 min before you get back to the entrance

author: Murray M
title: Disgusting spectacle
original_content: Shortly after entering the park we were confronted with the sorry sight of some monkeys keep in completely abject conditions. A sterile cage with zero stimulation bar a few branches, no water/food source and littered with garbage people had thought it amusing to push through the cages. People were aggravating the animals and found it funny when they became distressed. I am further astonished having tried to contact the park director about this disgrace that he is an advocate of bio diversity yet allows this to happen. Apart from that the park was full of litter sadly.
drawbacks: monkeys kept in completely abject conditions

author: Rachael P
title: National Park... more like a national disgrace
original_content: Visited today in an attempt to get away from the raw sewage and the polluted dump which is Cat Ba town (If I ate fish you couldnt pay me to eat it here.) Firstly and most importantly, the National Park near entrance has three caged monkeys in the most despicable conditions. No food. No water. No stimulation. Filthy cages. Full of rubbish that utterly ignorant visitors have pushed through to try to taunt the monkeys. I have never seen any creature look so sad and desperate. I approached someone who worked at the entry office and expressed my disgust at the situation. They told me they were "rescued" which they obviously arent. From other reviews it seems they have been there since 2016. Sadly this is a representation of the disgusting way this culture treats their animals. Needless to say I will be reporting this to Humane Society International, although I am unsure as to how far they can go in helping. Secondly, there is no conservation or effort to upkeep this park. Rubbish everywhere and complete disrepect for the environment. God knows where the money goes from the thousands of entry fees. The only good thing are the views at the top of the park but marred but loud locals playing music and shouting. This island could be paradise but sadly has been destroyed. Don't go.
drawbacks: Three caged monkeys in despicable conditions
No food, water, or stimulation for the monkeys

author: Elke S
title: Not recommended
original_content: Unfortunately not recommendable:  the place is not maintained, dirty, staff not focused on service  -  a disgrace for the good idea of an ecological responsible place and attitude

author: Marissa H
title: Stunning views, fun hike up
original_content: We had a great time driving to the park on motorbike and hiking up to the peak for some spectacular views. It actually took us two tries: the first day it was raining and it was really too dangerous to hike up. The rocks were slippery and half of the path was under water. The second day the skies had cleared up and it was much better.According to the map at the entrance there are different ways to climb up. We took the stairs on the right in the beginning of the climb, then stuck left. This way we did the harder, rockier path up (which was a lot easier than climbing them down) and the easier, mostly stairs way down by following the exit signs. On our hike up we were surrounded by the sounds of jungle animals. We saw a gigantic centipede, crabs, and lots of birds and butterflies. The views at the top are spectacular! Definitely worth walking another 5 minutes past the first view point to the second view point. It’s highly recommend to wear closed shoes, although most of it is paved stairway there are some sections of just jagged rocks. We started climbing around 9am and only saw two other couples, but on our way down we saw a lot more people, including some tours. We paid 40,000 for the short hike and 5,000 for parking the motorbike. Parking is guarded, we saw large backpacks on some of the motorbikes so it’s seemed pretty safe to store luggage as well. One final thing, it’s very calm and serene at the top. However, there were a bunch of American tourists that very being very loud and obnoxious. They also launched a drone, and it made SO MUCH NOISE. Please be considerate of the environment and other tourists, drones are cool but there is a time and place, sometimes it really sucks to ruin the calmness and serenity like that for others.
drawbacks: half of the path was under water
highlights: calm and serene at the top
practical_tips: consider the environment and other tourists

author: Ulrika T
title: Trekking in a beautiful landscape
original_content: Bring good shoes and water, sometimes climbing up hills with sharp rocks if you take the longest tour. Really good sceneries.
drawbacks: climbing up hills with sharp rocks

author: Paige B
title: A nice hike for a beautiful view
original_content: Took the hike up to the peak. Cost was 40,000 VND/person and it took about 30-40 minutes up & 20-30 minutes down (I should note that I do hike often). The hike itself is very beautiful and quite easy as the majority of the path is paved; however, I would recommend wearing running shoes. There are some spots (closer to the peak) that do require you to climb on sharp rocks. Another tip- pack your own water! You will need it as it gets very hot and the stands that sell it definitely up-charge!The view at the top of the mountain is breathtaking. I thought it was well worth the hike! However, when I did reach the top (around 11AM), it was very busy & loud, which somewhat took away from the serenity of the place. Nonetheless, I think it is a hike worth doing!

author: WeLikeHols
title: A must when in Cat Ba!
original_content: Took a taxi here for approx 160,000VND from the pier (confirmed price before getting in). Not much further than hospital cave. The climb is approx an hour from entrance to the top of the mountain. It’s quite steep and hundreds of steps so take plenty of water and use bug spray. The climb to the top was worth the sweat because the view is out of this world, pure beauty. Wear good shoes and you will get hot.
highlights: View is out of this world

author: emstravel13
title: Breathtaking views from the top of the Ngu Lam Peak. Horrible zoo enclosure.
original_content: What a breath taking view from the top of the Peak!About a 1.5 hour walk to the top takes you initially to the look out spot and then you can climb further up to the very peak. Definitely worth it! The walk on the way up was fine, a little sweaty! So bring water for sure and maybe a snack for the top. We were told by a group coming down from the top that the 'down' route was far easier than the signposted 'up' route! So we did this which was easy. There's a bar at the bottom of the hill serving drinks and food. One thing that really worried us was the 'zoo' area near the entrance of the park. Although signposted in English as a 'Temporary rescue area' it was clear that there was nothing about these tiny cages that were temporary or suggested a place of rescue. 3 distressed monkeys paced up and down their tiny enclosures, it was heartbreaking to see. We asked the lady at the entrance what was happening to these monkeys and made it evident how worried we were- she dismissed our question and wouldn't give us a clear answer.
extracted_spaces: bar at the bottom of the hill
zoo area near the entrance of the park
drawbacks: distressed monkeys paced up and down their tiny enclosures
dismissed our question and wouldn't give us a clear answer
highlights: breath taking view from the top
practical_tips: maybe a snack for the top
go down the route that's not signposted

author: Tavodog
title: Breathtaking Views! Just beautiful!
original_content: Rented A scooter and had a phenomenal day touring Canon Park, Hosital Cave....but the best was the view from the peak at the National Park.  Food footwear will save you a bruised bug toe or twisted ankle.  The hike in was relatively steep and uneven.  Well worth the effort though!
drawbacks: bruised bug toe or twisted ankle
hike in was relatively steep and uneven

author: patrykpielorz
title: Hike through the jungle
original_content: The Cat Ba national park has two main routes, with one route hard to find and a longer walking distance and a shorter one from the main entrance. We tried first to find the entrance to the big tour but we couldnt find it. So we went on the short but still beatiful route trough the jungle and endet at the top of a mountain with an incredible view! It was really easy to hike and a guide was not necessary. All in all a very nice halfway tour when you explore the island by bike.

author: T de G
title: Pleasant park
original_content: Nice park with beautiful nature. Rent a scooter and enjoy the views, the caves (we recommend Trung Trang!!) and the coastline. Good 2h hike (there and back) from the park's entrance.

author: HannaBarbera
title: Nice view, short trekkin
original_content: Short trekking, nice nature, so quite. We were In Ferbruar- in low season. Without tourist- little fogy- but so majestic.

author: Sightseer757020
title: Lovely
original_content: We rented motorbikes and came here, the walk is pretty steep, lits of steps but we loved it, the view is amazing from the top. Restaurant left a little to be desired but the walk makes up for it.
drawbacks: Restaurant left a little to be desired
highlights: the view is amazing from the top

author: Tayla Alderson
title: Beautiful national park
original_content: Wow oh wow! Beautiful national park, we went bike riding around the park and visited a lovely village that was incredible to see. A must do experience

author: navtombros
title: Pleasant Walk - Great Views
original_content: Was not expecting to see wildlife based on others reviews, but was pleasantly surprised - you just have to keep your eyes and ears open! There are clouds of colorful butterflies during the day, as well as skinks, chipmunks, squirrels, deer, herons and a few smaller birds. All you need is a bit of patience. The hike to the viewpoint is a bit steep, but thankfully it isn't too long of a hike. The views at the top are gorgeous, a great place to have lunch if you've brought food. Definitely visit if you're in the area, this was our first time walking through a forest in Vietnam - it was neat seeing all the interesting caves, rocks, and vine-like trees. Photos attached!
drawbacks: hike to the viewpoint is a bit steep
practical_tips: keep your eyes and ears open

author: Kat T
title: Long trek is for enthusiasts only
original_content: We got a boat from Ben Beo wharf to Viet harbour and then did the 4 hour trek via Viet Hai village to the park entrance on the other side. We got a taxi back. If you came to Cat Ba for the views, this is not a good option as you are in dense forest for much of the time and cant see beyond the trees. It is a tough walk. Not much of it is flat and it is rocky under foot. In the middle section you are scrambling over sharp pointed rocks.We had to buy tickets for Lan Ha bay, Viet Hai village and the national park. There were no animals or bird life in the forest. The village is not attractive.I enjoyed it, but my husband felt that spending hours seeing the same undergrowth was not a good use of time and he would have preferred to hire a scooter to see the scenery.
drawbacks: no animals or bird life in the forest
highlights: scenic views (if you hire a scooter)
practical_tips: hire a scooter to see the scenery
buy tickets for Lan Ha bay, Viet Hai village and the national park

author: Olyndia
title: Quick hike
original_content: Well worth the sweat to see the beautiful view. It does get a bit gnarly with some rocks so good footwear is recommended - probably covered in sneakers. It took four of us reasonably fit people 45 minutes up and about 30 down.

author: Thang Pham
title: Nice trekking route
original_content: There are 2 routes: long trek and a short ones. I recommend the long trek to Viethai: an unique village. It takes about 4 hours to get there.
practical_tips: recommend the long trek to Viethai

author: mafischl
title: Very cool
original_content: We love National Parks, so I don't claim to be impartial. We went into the park twice. Once on land once on a bamboo boat. Both times were great. On the second visit we went through a cave after seeing monkeys climbing on the cliffs

author: Kelly O
title: Great visit; here are some important details we wish we'd had (especially about transport back!)
original_content: Couldn't find many details ahead of time on practical details. Here's some stuff we found out while there. Getting there: take the pink bus (pay 30,000d per person) from the Cat Ba ferry terminal up to the park. It seems to leave every hour on the hour starting at 8am. Let the driver know to let you off in the national park.Entry fee: 80,000d to do the long hike (to Viet Hai village) or 40,000d to do the short hike up to the peak. They told us we had to start the long hike before 10am to ensure we'd be done and not stranded in Viet Hai. However, we met people later that day who started at 10:30am.Length of time/distance: We saw everything from 14km to 18km written. Our iPhones said about 10.5 miles total. We hiked to Viet Hai, lazed around for 15 minutes, and walked to the quay/port. Took us just over 4.5 hours and we're two young, in shape people. Saw people of all ages and abilities doing it though!Boat back to Ben Beo (note: they won't take you to Cat Ba town because it's around the tip of the island; you can walk 15 mins to town or take a 10,000d taxi/scooter): We paid 75,000d per person for the boat (negotiated down from 400,000d per person - yikes!) but then the guy made us wait about an hour and 15 minutes to "get more people on the boat" even though the initial agreement was we'd wait 30 minutes until 3pm. Majority of independent hikers and group tours arrived at 3:15-3:20 and we finally left after 3:30. It was a nightmare. They know you're stuck there and will rip you off or make you wait. Don't plan to end early because you'll probably be stuck until after 3 anyway, as boat owners clearly know that's when the tours come through.
practical_tips: Take the pink bus from Cat Ba ferry terminal
Let the driver know to let you off in the national park
Be prepared for long wait times

author: J V
title: Short but nice visit
original_content: Awesome views all around . Nice to just ride a moped and then go for a swim, can't wait to visit again
highlights: Nice to just ride a moped

author: N K
title: Absolutely gorgeous
original_content: Go. Rent a motorbike. Cheap! (Don't be afraid. They are all automatic and are like riding a bike.) Get your butt to Cat Ba National Park. Park your bike by the entrance to Frog Lake and hike in. Then ride back to town and up to Canon Fort for sunset. Your welcome.
practical_tips: Park your bike by the entrance to Frog Lake
Ride back to town and up to Canon Fort for sunset

author: BillericayBaz
title: Stunning views from the top
original_content: This is a demanding climb - you need to be reasonably fit - and the ground is not very even, so good shoes recommended. But the views at the top were worth it.
highlights: views at the top were worth it

author: Wandering Traveler
title: Decent park & hike
original_content: Half of Cat Ba is covered by a National Park, which is home to the highly endangered Cat Ba langur. The island has a wide variety of natural ecosystems, both marine and terrestrial, leading to incredibly high rates of biodiversity. Types of natural habitats found on Cat Ba Archipelago include limestone karsts, tropical limestone forests, coral reefs, mangrove and sea grass beds, lagoons, beaches, caves, and willow swamp forests. Cát Bà National Park is a World Heritage Site designated as a biosphere reserve in northern Vietnam. The park is part of Cát Bà Island in Hạ Long Bay and is administered by the city of Haiphong. The park covers about 263 square kilometres (102 sq mi) and comprising 173 square kilometres (67 sq mi) of land and 90 square kilometres (35 sq mi) of inshore water.The hike covered a Distance: 3.5km (2.2 miles)Highest Elevation: 296mAgain this is a trail in a third world country, sometimes you had a sidewalks, steps and a handrail. Other times you are on your own.
drawbacks: Sometimes you had a sidewalks, steps and a handrail. Other times you are on your own.
practical_tips: Be prepared for uneven terrain and lack of infrastructure

author: Des C
title: Worth the walk.
original_content: This is really a must do if able. The walk, as mentioned, is quite steep- do not wear flip flops. The only thought would be pay attention to the route, signs are not as clear as one would hope. All this aside, the view is simply amazing. Don't stop at the little hut, walk the extra 10 minutes to the very top, totally worth it.
drawbacks: signs are not as clear as one would hope
practical_tips: walk the extra 10 minutes to the very top

author: Jurriaan-de-Jong
title: Makes you work for it!
original_content: A 50-minute steep climb through a forest full of mosquitoes to get to the top, and still he gives this 5 stars? Why!?Well, the view is why! That, combined with the fact walking is the only option (so no throngs of lazy, noisy tourists). Totally worth it :D

author: Brendan W
title: Don't Miss It!
original_content: Hiking  through  the  tropical jungle and caves "Breath - Taking"...I would go again just to see the caves one more time!
practical_tips: go again just to see the caves one more time

author: Ashish G
title: Nice hike and Mesmerizing view
original_content: A must go place in Cat Ba, the entry fees is 40k VND and it's absolutely worth it. The hike is through dense tropical jungle on limestone mountains in the heat and humidity which makes it a little tough. But as it not a long trail, it can be easily managed. In the end there is a point 100 m further of the small shelter. Please go till there as it is the absolute end and the Ngu Lam Peak. From there you will see entire island and the view is breathtaking which will make you forget all the tiring hike.
drawbacks: hike is through dense tropical jungle

author: meg t
title: Animal cruelty and litter everywhere
original_content: This place should be a haven for animals - we saw so much beautiful wildlife on our walk however our day was ruined by the monkeys in cages that are clearly for tourists however it is claimed they are "temporary". If this was true the monkeys would not have been there since 2016 and their cages would not be full of litter. They are suffering in barren environments with no food. There is also a lot of litter along the paths because many tourists love to ruin what should be a beautiful park.
drawbacks: monkeys in cages suffering in barren environments with no food
practical_tips: go early to avoid litter and monkeys in cages
dress codes not mentioned but consider dressing for a walk in a park

author: johnnie j
title: Natural beauty at its best
original_content: Wildlife, stunning scenery, fantastic Seafood and breathtakingly beautiful. Also visited  the military hospital cave and cannon fort also..... A very good reminder of the futility of war and the ingenuity of man.

author: Rik C
title: Push yourself to the top!
original_content: We got 2 motorbike taxis to takes us there, wait for us and drive us back to Cat Ba City for 300.000 dong total. Which felt like a good price.Entry to the park is a okay price not expensive. From there you just walk the route, as there is only one. If your lucky you can see dears, monkeys and other animals as you enter te park.Hiking is a struggle, at least it was for me. But getting to the top was wel worth it! I even went for the second top which is about 5/10 minuts furter and hit the green pole. I am not saying this is a must do in Cat Ba, but is was one of the most exciting things I did on the island!One last note: please take care of your own garbage and don't destroy this bit of nature even further.Found this review useful? getting to the top was well worth it
one of the most exciting things I did on the island

don't destroy this bit of nature even further

author: Lewis B
title: Amazing views
original_content: The park is located approximately 20 minutes outside of the main strip on motorbike, I'm sure you could do this as a tour or arrange a taxi to take you and wait to bring you back as there isn't any taxis at the park. Entrance is 40 000 and worth every penny.The walk is about an hour to the viewing point which is breathtaking once here you will be able to see another mountain peak just next to you which is higher and provides even better views this is about another 5/10 mins walk be sure to do this as is definitely worth it !  Make sure to wear good trainers as can be very slippery in places and also take plenty of water.

author: 640minniey
title: Nice trekking with an awesome guide
original_content: It is easy to get to the top since the route is quite clear with signs. Some parts may be a bit slippery especially with rain. Our guide Alan is the highlight. He is funny and takes great photos; and he also shows us some special species in the woods.Still fine without a guide though.
drawbacks: parts may be a bit slippery especially with rain
highlights: Our guide Alan is the highlight. He is funny and takes great photos; and he also shows us some special species in the woods
practical_tips: Still fine without a guide though

author: ewuchka
title: Hike to Viet Hai village
original_content: Unlike what you can read in the guide, or what they tell you in the travel agencies, this hike can be easily done on your own.We took the public bus from Cat Ba Town in the morning, around 8.00 am (I guess the time may vary a bit, as we were waiting till the bus was full). Price around 20 000/person.At the entrance to the national park, you need to buy a ticket - there were about 4 options for hikes, the Viet Hai is the longest one and costs 40 000/person.The first part of the hike is on the road, later you enter to the jungle, but the path is always visible and there are signs as well. It is mostly uphill or downhill, walking on the tree roots, for hikers nothing difficult. In the maps.me application you can see the whole route.Towards the end of the hike there is a cave, you can go through the cave to the other side and then continue to the village, which is more touristic, but there are options where to eat/drink something. Generally a pleasant, quiet place.From the village, you can continue walking some 5 km more to the harbour, on the weekdays there is a public boat at 13.00 which would take you back to Cat Ba Town, however not on weekends (therefore our trip back was slightly more expensive, 80 000/person on a private boat).We spent 4,5 hours walking more or less, doing some short stops on the way. Watch out for leeches (although it is not really possible :-)).For hikers a recommendable trip.
practical_tips: buy a ticket at the entrance

author: Paweł M
title: Nice place
original_content: Take short walk to view point, straight path to the top. No need to take a guide for short one, but for the one to viet hai maybe better to take organized trip
practical_tips: no need to take a guide for short one
take organized trip for the one to viet hai

author: Jlo
title: Fantastic view

Anyway, I like that its a bit challenging.The view from the top is very nice and for this I give it 4 stars.
drawbacks: some of the steps are slippery and sharp
highlights: view from the top is very nice

author: Murli K
title: Must visit park in Cat Ba
original_content: Equatorial, damp, dense forest and moderately difficult hike.  Take insect repellants; pleanty of them.  Watch out for leeches.  Do not miss the hospital cave on the way up.  The hike is moderate difficult but slippery.  The last 5 minutes is steep and rocky
drawbacks: The last 5 minutes is steep and rocky
highlights: Do not miss the hospital cave on the way up

author: drwols
title: Fantastic hike up to Ngu Lam
original_content: Me and my girlfriend hiked up here on a day which we hired a scooter on Cat Ba island. We were glad that we didn't organise a tour to here, as the peak is easily accessible by yourself! The scenery is beautiful once you reach the top so don't forget your camera. Most of the walk was pretty gentle, but the final stretch got fairly steep but not impossible. There is a restaurant at the start of the path to Ngu Lam (not at the entrance of the National Park).Well worth visiting for the views!

author: littleme493
title: Good hike
original_content: The hike itself is good and worth the recommended 2hours to be spent on it. However the park seems like it once was an attraction that the government or someone put money into but since then they have stop therefore it's somewhat run down. Needs some time and money spent on it and it could be a real attraction

author: Loïc L
title: A MUST!
original_content: If you are visiting Cat Ba island, it is absolutely essential you take a couple of hours to go to Cat Ba national park!!! The view you get from the top point is the most stunning view you will probably ever live to see!!
practical_tips: go to Cat Ba national park

author: OlafRotterdam
title: Amazing views
original_content: The view from the viewing platform (40 minute walk from the entrance) is worth the climb. What an amazing view over green Cat Ba island. Entrance is 40.000 and parking is 5.000. Signs to the top are not always clear but you wont get lost.
drawbacks: Signs to the top are not always clear
highlights: The view from the viewing platform is worth the climb
What an amazing view over green Cat Ba island

author: Chloe B
title: Beautiful views but poorly kept and animal cruelty
original_content: We did the short 1 hour or so trek and the views were beautiful. BUT and a very big but, deers are kept in a small fenced area and the saddest thing was 3 monkeys kept in extremely small dirty cages with tons of flies swarming. They were starving with no food or water and as soon as we showed a sign of food they put their hands out of the cage. The cages have old bottles and old scraps of food tourists have given the poor animals. One monkey was walking backwards and forwards in the cage GOING INSANE and was doing this for the whole 4 hours we were at the park. Truly heartbreaking. We tried to find somebody to say this was unacceptable but there was nobody in sight when we left. Please can people who visit this park have some heart and report it to the workers and hopefully something will be done. Also the park is so poorly maintained with rubbish overflowing the bins and in all of the visible landscape. Call yourself a nature reserve.. MOST DEFINITELY NOT A NATURE RESERVE ! SORT IT OUT.
drawbacks: deers kept in small fenced area
monkeys kept in extremely small dirty cages
poorly maintained with rubbish overflowing the bins
practical_tips: try to find somebody to say this was unacceptable

author: Tom R
title: Average, but important for the Langurs. Go without a guide.
original_content: We walked the longer trail that ends at the sea, we did not go with a guide.Lonely Planet calls it "hardcore", but it was about moderate difficulty. You end up walking over a series of hills, so it's tough on the thighs, but the trail is well marked, mostly paved, and I think it's unlikely you'll get lost. Yes, rain would make it more difficult, but not significantly so. There is no scrambling, or anything else that goes beyond walking, involved. Therefore, in my view a guide is unnecessary for most, and you may have a better experience avoiding the group tours from Cat Ba. You can organise the boat back yourself for about 300k per boat. In terms of appeal, this was a nice walk, but by no means special. It's great to trek through dense jungle landscape, the fig trees in particular are beautiful, and I enjoyed going up and down the rocky hills. If you want amazing vista views though, I suggest doing something else on the island. If you're coming to see the Langurs, I suggest bringing all the lucky charms you can. If you're on Cat Ba for a few days, this is worth doing, and it was a nice way to get some fresh air and exercise on a pretty walk. But it's not a must for most.
drawbacks: unlikely to get amazing vista views
highlights: great to trek through dense jungle landscape
practical_tips: organise the boat back yourself for about 300k per boat
bring all the lucky charms you can

author: Ella M
title: Amazing!!!
original_content: Hire a scooter from your hostel in Cat Ba (130k for a full day, inc petrol) and go!! 5k for parking and then 40k to get in    The view from the top of the hike is the best mountain view I have seen in a very long time. 100% recommend doing it. We went in spring so there were lovely flowers and it wasn't scorching hot yet either.
highlights: best mountain view I have seen in a very long time
practical_tips: Hire a scooter from your hostel

author: Spliffer
title: Not much but okay
original_content: The short trek in the national park is about one hour up and a bit faster down. The park is not very beautiful because of a lot of garbage around, but the nature and fresh air is lovely! Some times you need to climb a bit to reach the top, but it's doable. The view was okay, mostly mountain tops but I think on a not so cloudy day it would be very nice.
highlights: the nature and fresh air is lovely
on a not so cloudy day it would be very nice

author: batsauce
title: A nice hike to a beautiful vista
original_content: We really enjoyed our hike to a mountain top peak. It was mildly strenuous and very rewarding. The trail was very well maintained. The view was incredible. Takes a little more than an hour. Highly recommended

author: alittlelucky13
title: Please Free the Monkeys from CRUELTY
original_content: I have never been more saddened than I was to see the Monkeys in the cages living in their own excrement. They are fed rotting scraps. We got fruit from local vendors and their hands shook while eating it as they are starving!!!! This is not acceptable. Free them to mo key island. Anywhere but here. So horrific. They have no water. Clearly a Male and Female adult and a juvenile female. They are obviously breed for tourism. They have an abundance of veggies growing in patches beside them. Pumpkins rotting on the ground uneaten yet nothing is given to these poor animals! An atrocity you see and do not act on you are condoning. Please, help these beautiful animals!!!!!!
drawbacks: Animals living in their own excrement

author: Sabrina G
title: Monkeys are VERY poorly treated - extremely sad
original_content: Our tour guide took us to see monkeys right by the entrance. He told us they were there to be treated and would be released in another island or they would die there, because there are hunters that shoot them. Seems very unlikely that hunters would go into a national park. But also, we thought they looked horrible, and the cages were very dirty. We got some fruits from a nearby vendor and fed them. They were starving. It was heartbreaking to see that. I wish I could upload the video here.The monkeys are pacing constantly from one side to another, a sign of stress.I understand that perhaps they don't have a lot of funds, but in this case, they absolutely NEED TO RELEASE THEM to the wild. They should not keep monkeys in the cage just for tourist's fun. IT'S OUTRAGEOUS.Who should I contact to get help? PS. The trekking is great and nice views, but I cannot pass this fact.

author: Dunolde
title: Easy without guide
original_content: In Cat Ba town they are going to convince you to book a tour with guide but its far more expensive and not necesary. You can take a bus called qh green,it cost 30000dong, ask to stop at National Park entrance. There you need to buy ticket entrance for 80000dong. The path starts easy but it gets quite difficult without boots. There are arrows and panels, you will not get lost. Then you arrive to Viet Hai village where you can have lunch and book a boat with somebody (or do it in the harbour). We payed 200000 for two people but sharing the boat with vietnamese. If you are alone you will need to pay more I suppose. They asked 400000 in the beginning of course...and the boat its going to be also a small tour in Lan Ha Bay, very nice. You get off at ben Beo harbour and you just need to walk to at Cat Ba town.
highlights: nice boat tour in Lan Ha Bay
easy to navigate with arrows and panels
practical_tips: take a bus called qh green
buy ticket entrance at National Park entrance
book a boat with somebody in Viet Hai village

author: Samu Mattila
title: Definately worth to visit
original_content: We went there by scooter. It was very easy to find and we would recommend to visit here by yourself. Parking costs a little + the entrance fee, but it is worth it. The park was very silent and not crowded (we visited park in the morning). The route to the top is marked well. It was quite a hard climb, sometimes there were stairs but often only sharp rocks. So if you are not in decent shape, you should consider well before climbing to the top. The views are magnificent and well worth it.

author: Jitin K
title: Must go attraction in Cat Ba
original_content: If you are in Cat Ba, don't miss this. I am not exactly sure but the entree fee was about 50-80,000 VND per person depending on the route. The hike might seem a little long but the view at the top is absolutely worth the hike. It does require some uphill climbing and stairs. We biked here from Cat Ba town. Also visited hospital caves along the way.

author: rachmdavies
title: Lovely views and hike
original_content: This made our trip to Cat Ba worth it. Would recommend you get a tour guide - some of the trails are not very obvious.
drawbacks: some of the trails are not very obvious
highlights: made our trip to Cat Ba worth it

author: Enkidu-backpacker
title: beautiful landscape and good light exercise
original_content: we did rent motorbike from our hostel (80k vnd) and ride till national park. the road is fun and you will arrive to entrance which costs 40k vnd. there are two different tracks which the short one takes around 30min up and 30min down. you gonna have actual jungle tracking after 10min (after walking to end of asphalt road) there would be mid-light climbing near the end of the way. you can have a great view from up the tower or walk 6-7min further to higher summit. great for taking picture and enjoying fresh air ( even you might got some air pollution during winter). another tracking route is longer 9 locals said it takes 4 hours go and 4 back) which we didnt try.
practical_tips: Rent a motorbike from the hostel
Bring a map or guide for the longer track

author: Sander8011
title: Amazing views from the top
original_content: We took the path to the viewpoint, which is getting harder to climb towards the end. You are however rewarded with 360' view of the island. Do not forget to move to the final viewpoint which is after the tower: views here are best!

author: Jay K
title: A must if you have time on CatBa!
original_content: Save cash by hiring a scooter and riding out to the park yourself, at the gate expect to pay the small fee of 40.000vnd.Once entering you have a few locals with stalls offering drinks and snacks.There's a little area at the bottom with recovering monkeys and also some deer.The hike up the mountain is approximately 4km which doesn't sound a great deal, but it's hard work in some places! Defiantly bring drinks and your camera, as once you reach the summit after 4km of jungle you are treated to some of the best views in Vietnam!  On the way down I was also treated to the sight of a giant oriental squirrel!! With Mosquitos present, I'd rub some repellent in before entering the jungle!

author: Lars L
title: One of the best views of Vietnam
original_content: A 45 min walk uphill to the summit and then an extra 10 to the next one. The view is amazing and worth the walk. It is uphill so some level of fitness is required but you don't need to be superman either.
drawbacks: some level of fitness is required

author: Thomas
title: Great
original_content: This is a very nice place to take a hike and see some very beautiful views. There is a trip that takes about an hour or so up (and about 45 minutes back down) that takes you to the top of some hills where you have an amazing 360 degree viewpoint. The one downside to the park is that there os plenty trash laying around. I don't know how people can actually visit a protected area and just dump their plastic bottles and candybar wrappings everywhere but it brakes your hart to see it... idiots
drawbacks: people dumping their plastic bottles and candybar wrappings everywhere

author: teacherpaja
title: A must see in Cat Ba!
original_content: We've rented a motorbike, parked it near the entrance and then hiked to the top of the mountain - it took us about 1 hour to get there and the view was amazing! You can get a refreshment at the entrance, the lady is very nice. Take comfortable shoes with you.Půjčili jsme si motorku, zaparkovali u vchodu a tůra na vrcholek hor nám trvala cca hodinu. Výhled byl úžasný! U vchodu si můžete koupit občerstvení, paní prodavačka je moc milá. Doporučuji pohodlné boty.

author: Adam L
title: Short walk, amazing view, definitely worth checking out!
original_content: Me and some friends rented some scooters and headed to the national park, was around a 15 minute drive from our hostel. The entry fee wasn't that much for what you actually saw. They said it takes an hour to reach the top but if you're quick and fit you can probably do it in less, there's a decent path and steps virtually the whole way, it's a relatively easy but quite long walk, bring a big bottle of water and maybe some snacks,  although you can buy them outside. The view from each of the highest points is definitely worth the money and the walk,  mountains as far as the eye can see, was really breathtaking and nice way to spend a few hours of the day, I'd recommend it to anyone who thinks they can make the walk.
highlights: view from each of the highest points
mountains as far as the eye can see
practical_tips: bring a big bottle of water

author: Jackie Y
title: Short hike rewarding view!
original_content: We took the shorter route, takes about 45 mins going up to the peak! Past few hundred meters can be quite tough, but other than that just follow the path. Bring mosquito repellent! 1L of water at least! Also, no need for guided tour, just get a scooter and do it yourself!
drawbacks: Past few hundred meters can be quite tough
practical_tips: get a scooter and do it yourself

author: sarasarina808
title: So worth it. Gorgeous.

We hiked in the heat of the day and it still wasn't too bad because the trees provide shade almost the whole way. The view is incredible. You don't need a guide even though many reviews say you do. practical_tips: rent a motorbike to get to the park

author: Aleksandra B
title: Very nice tour

author: robeja32
title: Cheap price but fun
original_content: We visited to Cat Ba National Park. We hired a motorbike for the day! The price is so cheap, 40k VND, and were fairly well done. Driving car in VietNam is not easy but it's still ok. It's mostly just stairs. The views were incredible, hightly recommend
drawbacks: Driving car in VietNam is not easy

author: Blue Swimmer

author: Anh Khoi hotel

author: kevint61
title: A beautiful discovery of The Cave of Dragons

Sea Blue Swimmer Adventure for this unique and truly unusual adventure

author: aleisha Willis

author: Lucy Stewart

author: Huyen Tram

author: Nguyen Tu

author: Harvey Holmes

author: June Bennet

place where you can marvel for hours

author: Nguyen Thao

author: Vlade D

author: Đinh Phương Hà

author: Vũ Thu Uyên

author: Mỹ Phương

author: Đào Anh Vũ

practical_tips: spend a long time admiring the rock formations

author: Hélène Meyer

author: Anh Khoi hotel

original_content: Beautiful discovery of the Otter Valley by kayak to explore plovers and mangroves. We really liked this outdoor day. We advise you to visit this beautiful area that is really off the beaten track

author: kevint61
title: Best trip ever to Catba island
original_content: We had a lovely and relaxing experience going on a tour with Blue Swimmer to explore Thien Long cave and Ao Coi otter valley ! Our guide is knowledgeable, kind  and very informative . There is enough time to explore all the highlights. The lunch at Green Mangrove restaurant is tasty and yummy. We highly recommend Blue Swimmer company!
extracted_times: enough time to explore all the highlights

author: Nam N
title: Discovery of the otter valley and mangroves in Ao Coi

highlights: beautiful stand-up paddle and kayak ride

author: tung
title: Magnifique cave
original_content: Excellent day to explore mangrove forest in Áo Coi valley and Thiên Long cave with our local guide Toàn. We loved the boat trip along the mangrove forests, the motorbike trips and the cave . Amazing day for all of us
highlights: boat trip along the mangrove forests

author: Nam N
title: Excellent hidden gem on Catba island
original_content: Booked a day tour with small group to explore Thien Long cave which is accessible by boat, the trip along mangrove forest to reach this stunning cave is just beautiful and so green. We're the only tourists here to explore this unforgetten cave with our local guide Toan. We highly loved this visit and recommended it to everyone while you have free time in Catba island

author: Long Catba Kayak🦅
title: Amazing hidden cave in Phu Long village
original_content: Had a wonderful day exploring Phulong mangrove forests and Ao Coi valley by small bamboo boat and kayaking . We was impressed by the beauty of the stalatites and stalagmites of this wonderful cave still unkown by most of tourists. It’s worth every penny . Highly appreciated
highlights: beauty of the stalatites and stalagmites

author: Frank

Our tour guide Liam from Blue Swimmer really added to the entertainment as well as giving us lots of information about mangroves forest, ecosystems, Phu Long village, Ao Coi valley and Catba natural park. Our small group managed the tour without any problems. The journey along Phu Long river was really scenic and relaxing. highlights: tour guide Liam was entertaining and informative
practical_tips: a degree of fitness is necessary

author: Phil R

practical_tips: check if the hospital cave is open

author: Marjorie S
