highlights: Great insight into how the hospital operated during the war
Our tour guide was very knowledgable
spoke excellent english and answered our questions

author: Tanja G
title: History
original_content: Every person should visit the hospital museum, to understand what means the War. Specifically way how they hide patients and people.

author: Achiel Cattoir
title: Hospital cave
original_content: Very interesting trip but a pity there is no extra information. For the price I thought it was a bit too small and with too little information.

author: Shanee
title: Fabulous experience. Definitely worth visiting.
original_content: This was an amazing experience. To think that these caves were built in three years to take care of the soldiers during the war is unbelievable. Well worth a visit.

author: LaLouise13
title: Historically valuable
original_content: Vietnam's best-kept secret..... a military hospital that helped hundreds of wounded soldiers during the Vietnam War. And the Americans had no idea of its existence!

author: mazda3langley
title: Go! It IS worth the visit
original_content: Totally enjoyed our time there.  We had a nice young man join us and explain everything to us!  We didn’t ask him too, he just did, which was nice of him.  Worth going!  Disagree with previous person.  You get what you put into it!  These are very hard working people who do their best to explain how things were.  We were humbled to be there!
practical_tips: You get what you put into it!

author: Virginie
title: Not worth the visit

There are no explanation about when it was in operation, about how many people were working there or how many people were treated. Some rooms have a name but for others we don’t even know how they were used. The 3rd floor is not accessible right now. Definitely a poor visit for us.
drawbacks: no explanation about when it was in operation
no explanation about how many people were working there or how many people were treated
some rooms have a name but for others we don’t even know how they were used

author: Shakeyjack
title: Interesting visit to a historic sight
original_content: This was part of the half day hiking tour with Cat Ba Ventures. I didn’t know what to expect on this part, our guide was able to give an overview and explanation of all of the rooms. The models and furniture are a bit basic but do help with understanding. The guide was able to offer some personal family experiences of the war which gave a much better insight, without which the museum alone lacks some interpretation of what you are seeing. This is a great attraction and could be better.
drawbacks: models and furniture are a bit basic
lacks some interpretation of what you are seeing
highlights: our guide was able to give an overview and explanation of all of the rooms
the guide was able to offer some personal family experiences of the war

author: falcon38
title: An essential Catba trip. Loved it
original_content: A great way to spend an hour or two. A hidden gem of a visit. Was expecting little due to poor reviews but we loved it. Paid £10 for a return taxi with the driver waiting for two hours. Some reviews say no issue getting a taxi back but it was deserted when we went. 40000VND pp. Have to climb 50ish well maintained steps to entrance. A few models enhance the visit. Fascinating visit.great street cafe opposite with super value drinks.
drawbacks: some reviews say no issue getting a taxi back but it was deserted when we went
highlights: great street cafe opposite with super value drinks

author: jaap d
title: Impressive piece of history.
original_content: Easily accessible cave. If you are interested in the dark side of Cat Ba, definitely check it out. Only takes you half an hour. Little explanation but much imagination is not required. Impressive and terrifying.
practical_tips: Check it out if you are interested in the dark side of Cat Ba

author: Eva EG

original_content: Interesting for the history the cave/shelter holds, not as a cave per se. Unbelievable that it was a field hospital that performed operations!The cave is completely hidden from the sky and even from the road if there were no signs.
drawbacks: not as a cave per se
highlights: unbelievable that it was a field hospital

author: Sarah V
title: Not so impressive
original_content: Not so impressive - looks more like a big bunker with a few neglected props in it. You can surely skip this one.

author: Ita_Traveller

author: Silvia V

author: Manu Jain
title: Beautiful
original_content: Its a super nice and beautiful cave near cat ba national park and the price is included in the price for park ticket

author: JSTrip_77
title: Fascinating Legacy of War
original_content: Hospital Cave is really interesting to see. But, it would be nice if there was some additional signage or information about the site. We were even traveling with Vietnamese friends so the issue was language but lack of a sense of value in telling the story of the cave. But, even without a great deal of explanation, it's totally worth visiting the cave just to see the scale and the organization of this hospital. It's in three levels and even has a swimming pool! There are some mannequins set up that bring some life to the place even without signage. Of note, this place is accessible at the top of some very steep steps!
drawbacks: lack of signage or information about the site

author: Beth
title: Could do with a spruce up
original_content: Most the rooms are empty or just have a bed frame in them. Very little to no information about what the rooms housed, what happened here etc. We could only guess it was from the Vietnam America war? Fair few steep slippery steps to climb up too. Bonus that the loo had loo roll. Bazinga.
drawbacks: Very little to no information about what the rooms housed

author: Irina P

author: Barbara W
title: Hospital Cave

author: Rico

I liked the next Cave we visited much more.

author: Billy W

author: ClaudiaW

author: Tiffany L
title: Crappy tourist trap, complete waste of time!
original_content: Don’t understand any of the rave reviews. We were made to pay $5k for parking our scooter when we could’ve just parked it down the road for free. It costed $40k per person to enter the hospital cave, hindsight not a huge amount of money, but the fact we paid money for crap was annoying. You can choose to hire a guide (ticket collector) who recited a script, unable to answer any questions. Script was along the lines of “this was the treatment room... this was the bathroom... this was where patients slept”. He did not provide any history of the cave, and the tour lasted approximately 10 minutes. You can choose to tip him, or not. We chose to tip $10k Đông. The cave consisted of literally empty, refurbished concrete rooms. And by empty, they were literally empty with just a light bulb and some rubbish. There were no information or photos to accompany the “history” of this place. For example, in the “staff bedrooms”, there were unassembled beds (still in their packages) in a pile against the wall. The cave entrance had weird mannequins in army outfits stacked on tables, where the ticket collectors sat playing on their phones and ate their lunch. There were dead rats in the water tank. Only the first 2 floors of the cave was accessible to visit, the top floor was off limits. Don’t waste your time here, absolute tourist trap. Head 10 minutes up the road towards the national park to Trưng trang cave - which was 100 times better.
drawbacks: Paid $40k per person to enter the hospital cave
Guide recited a script without answering questions
practical_tips: Head 10 minutes up the road towards the national park to Trưng trang cave

author: Kimberly S
title: Bad - unethical
original_content: Monkey Island in Cat Ba would not be on my recommendation list. We were taken here on a cruise package during our time on Cat Ba island (just a note it was not in the itinerary so we were unaware we would be stopping here) - we went with serenity cruises day trip but I think a lot of the cruises actually do stop off here so keep that in mind when booking tours. The macaques on this island were not native to the island - they were moved from Thailand to Vietnam (Cat ba) for tourism purposes which ethically is quite questionable. The island itself does not have the resources to sustain the number of macaques on the island and they rely heavily on the tourism to maintain numbers of 60+ without tourism (the tour guides and tourist feeding them) the numbers drop to 20-30 (we were told this by the guides as well, I don’t think he realised the impact of this). The tour guides take cookies and things to feed the macaques and there was a lot of teasing, chasing, splashing the macaques which again really isn’t ethical. It causes the animals to first not be afraid of humans, therefore not having any personal space and also showing a lot of aggression towards the guides and visitors once the food is no longer available. We were really disappointed to see this happening and we refused to go onto the island. Reading reviews there have been quite a few injuries caused by the macaques to people - needing hospital visits and rabies treatment. We were just hoping the this review discourages anyone from taking the risk and also helps hopefully prevent the ongoing unethical treatment of the macaques on this island. The guides hopefully will learn that this is not an ethical way of interacting with wildlife and this is unsafe for visitors.
drawbacks: The macaques on this island were not native to the island - they were moved from Thailand to Vietnam (Cat ba) for tourism purposes which ethically is quite questionable.

author: Andrew D
title: Great location, but everything else is poor
original_content: Monkey Island is a great location, but overall it is a pretty disappointing experience and poor value for money considering the prices being asked. Some of the staff were personally really friendly and helpful, so I would like to be able to recommend it for this reason, but I just can’t.The overall impression is of a place that is poorly kept and which no one really cares about. It is a bit rundown and needs some serious investment, but I could forgive that. What isn’t forgivable are the things that wouldn’t really require much investment, or any at all, but no one seems to care about. Two examples:1.	The Food. The food is inexplicably bad, which considering you have no other options is a bit of a problem. And it’s the Vietnamese food that is most disappointing. You can forgive rubbish western food, but the supposedly Vietnamese food wasn’t really Vietnamese (more generic Asian) and was bland, non-descript and utterly underwhelming. This is the only place in two weeks in Vietnam that we had a bad meal. What made it more frustrating was that when the staff sat down to eat they appeared to be eating much authentic Vietnamese food of the kind served everywhere else, cooked with care and with fresh ingredients. It looked like the staff were getting much better food than the customers! And they either don’t realise this, or don’t care, or perhaps it’s a deliberate policy. It’s very odd. The tables in the restaurant were also noticeably dirty. The chef who was cooking people’s eggs for breakfast was comically miserable and scowled at everybody. 2.	Uncomfortable beach loungers with no cushions. The one thing there really is to do on Monkey Island is to lie in the sun on the beach. The beach itself isn’t great, but the location is stunning. I could have laid here all day, but you can’t because the wooden beach loungers are incredibly uncomfortable and there are – inexplicably – no cushions for the loungers. It wouldn't take much thought or investment to fix this. It's just basic customer care.The pick up from Cat Ba Island was also really poor. We waited around for 2.5 hours having been told (by the transit organised by the resort) that a boat would be there in 15 minutes. When we finally got there, we saw a couple who had been waiting with us at the quay as well, but who had been picked up two hours earlier. Nobody acknowledged this, nobody apologised. Vietnam is the most amazing place. Monkey Island resort is so unrepresentative of the welcome, the good food and the good hospitality we received everywhere else.

I hope that this post spursthe island owners to actionbefore a tragedy occurs. +++Frank Hickey, writer of theDancing Max Royster crime storiesabout the world's only ballroomdancing detective.

Useless advice from guides to be careful of monkeys

author: MrBoleo
title: where are monkeys
original_content: The beach is not one of those picture perfect ones. There’s a bar selling cold drinks. Oh, and you can climb to the top, from there you will have a nice view of the bay. It’s not an easy climb
drawbacks: not one of those picture perfect ones
practical_tips: go to the bar for cold drinks

author: Lee B
title: Only barely average .
original_content: We went there as part of an otherwise fantastic tour day with Alibaba tours . We only visited the one side of the island so cannot comment on the resort .The climb itself was too tough for we two 70 year olds - made it half way so that we had views in both directions - ok , but nothing much better than the great views from the boat . We swam there & at the time of our visit both the beach & water were clean .Our boat owner warned us about the prices - they have a monopoly of area so what would you expect . They even wanted to charge for the toilet . The monkeys are few in number at our time of visit & we saw no trouble , but they are definitely not native to Cat Ba & are there purely for the tourists who according to other reviews , mistreat them .All in all , nothing great . A quite pleasant stopping point on a tour , but we feel that it would be extremely boring to spend any length of time there at all . DEFINITELY NOT WORTH A SPECIAL TRIP .

the monkeys are few in number and are not native to Cat Ba

the great views from the boat

author: Hannah L
title: Wear trainers and leave the monkeys alone!
original_content: This is a lovely little island of white shores and calm seas, though it’s pretty busy and lots of boats visit. There are some monkeys here and they’ll let you get up close but they’re pretty riled up as they’re taunted all day by some tourists, so they seem to be quite aggressive - you can hardly blame them! There’s a ‘hike’ here, but it’s more of a rock climb to the top, we did it ill-advisedly in flip flops but it’s slippy with sand and very jagged in places which makes it quite treacherous! The views are fantastic and it’s not a long hike but definitely take your trainers and take it slow.

author: Beatrice Ferrari

author: Stephanie B

author: Kayla K

author: Becky W
title: Bit disappointed

The climb to the top is quite tricky (wear trainers). The monkeys are jacked up on energy drinks and junk that tourists feed them and they are aggressive. author: Tom M
title: For climbers rather than wildlife enthusiasts
original_content: If you like a challenging climb (and I mean climb, not walk), this is for you, as there's a great view from the top of the rocky hill.  However, it's unlikely you'll see any indigenous monkeys (apparently they import some other monkeys to satisfy visitors) and if you're not a climber, there's little else to do.  We had to go as it was part of a bigger tour but I'd say avoid if possible.
drawbacks: little else to do if not a climber

author: Ian S

author: RoperT
title: Mobbed with tourists--and monkeys
original_content: We stopped here as part of a day-long tour of Cat-Ba island, and while a cool drink and some shade were welcome, the beach and the climb were just too crowded to be enjoyable.  I first got a drink at the bar/veranda, and watched a monkey take a person's phone.  So I drank up, and headed to the climb to the top for some views.  But it's a little steep and rocky, and too many people coming down made it too perilous for me to continue to the top.  I'd already been to the Canon Fort back on Cat Ba island, which has wonderful views (including on the way up), so why risk it?  Overall, it's a nice beach, just too crowded. I wish we would have used the valuable time out on the water to stop someplace else.

author: Pilottok

author: Francis Martino
title: View is nice

Not many areas to go except the beach and viewpoints, I recommend booking ahead and staying a night or two at monkey island resort, it's definitely worth it.Most monkeys are seen at the beach. They tend to be on the aggressive side. I've been bitten and chased into the sea as well as seen many attacks. Just keep your wits about you.Be careful as the monkeys will take anything and everything they can from you,stones are very sharp and the way gets harder, the further you walk! author: Rob
title: DONT INTERACT WITH THE MONKEYS 🐒
original_content: I didn’t really want to come to this island from what I’d heard from other reviews. However it was part of a tour so I went along and did the short hike to the top. Unfortunately at the top, where you get a fantastic view of the scenery, you also get a nightmare scene of tourists inappropriately feeding and holding the monkeys. The top of the hike it’s self is steep with jagged rocks and you have to walk slowly to climb down. It’s an easy hike but when there are so many people allowed to climb up at once there was a big back log of tourists trying to safely climb down and all were cramped at the top with monkeys taking water bottles right out of peoples hands. Please note that its deeply inappropriate to feed wild monkeys as it changes their natural behaviour and encourages them to be dominant and aggressive towards us (hence why people have been bitten in the past). Sad to see many adults my own age from my tour boat  feeding the monkeys and laughing about it; instead of listening to the advice of the guide. You can walk the hike in flip flops if you’re careful but don’t bring food and try to hide your water from the monkeys or it will be taken. Shame that people would rather get close and take a selfie with a monkey than just view the beautiful animal from an appropriate distance.
extracted_times: a big back log of tourists trying to safely climb down

big back log of tourists trying to safely climb down
practical_tips: walk the hike in flip flops if you're careful
don't bring food and try to hide your water from the monkeys

author: Mr. Mike
title: Animal Exploitation Needs To Stop
original_content: These sorts of attractions were outlawed in the West 50 or 60 years ago. author: Kali
title: Worst treatment of animals I've seen traveling
original_content: First off, the monkeys are not native to the area and were brought in some time ago for tourist. There are wayyy too many monkeys living on a small island because they are just fed by tourists. Secondly, I personally watched a guide hurl rocks as hard as possible at some monkeys that he decided were mean or stealing from the other monkeys (easily enough to hurt the monkeys) and when confronted about it, we nearly got into a fight for his abusive mistreatment and his severe lack of empathy or remorse. author: CMImum
title: Horrible- don’t support venues that allow animals to be exposed like this
original_content: Our boat made its usual stop here and we went ashore without giving it much thought but quickly regretted it. Monkeys were being fed chips by tourists who thought it was a real hoot until the monkeys started fighting over them and snatching the packet from their hands. Once a large group of tourists left the monkeys started circling us and eyeing off our backpacks, baring their teeth at us, hissing and waiting to attack. author: Kieran A
title: PLEASE LISTEN TO REVIEWS - DON'T GO TO MONKEY ISLAND
original_content: One of my least favourite parts of my entire trip to South East Asia with my wife. First off, the hike up the hill has WAY too many people, not a nice hike at all if you don't like waiting for 15 minutes to move a couple of feet. Even without the jagged rocks, it just isn't that great of experience. The view is beautiful but honestly head over to Cat Ba island for better hikes and better views. NOW TO THE MONKEYS. I really wish they would shut this down or regulate it. It's not out of the realm of reality to say there is a good chance you can get your stuff stolen or you can get bit. Just look at the reviews on here. I saw a monkey lash out at an unsuspecting couple, trying to take there stuff - so I tried to help them by scaring it away. So the monkey decided to come at me, so I kicked him in the face. That seemed to stun him and he stopped. It's not nice but that's how animals learn. Point is that people are stupid and the monkeys are vicious. I'm well aware of how monkeys can act since coming from Africa but many people don't know. My advice is to stay the hell away from this island at all cost and if you absolutely need to go. Arm yourself and watch your back.
drawbacks: good chance you can get your stuff stolen or you can get bit

author: SangreYLeche
title: Attacked by the monkeys, changed my whole itinerary. Stay away.
original_content: Nobody really warns you for them but the monkeys here are among the most agressive I have met in SE Asia. The tourist spoil them by feeding them. I visited Monkey Island at the beginning of the low season, which makes them agitated, as they don't get as much food from the tourists as they are used to. Even though I am always VERY careful around monkeys, I got attacked by two of them and this changed my whole trip, as I had to go through a rabies post-infection treatment and from that day on, had to stay close to hospitals for the multiple injections. When I spoke the doctor in Hanoi, he told me that many people get attacked at Monkey Island. The tourguides tell you that they are safe and that they are vaccinated against rabies themselves, but the doctor could not confirm this. If one bites or scratches you, you really need to go to the hospital in Hanoi. Let no-one tell you different, as the touroperators are simply protecting their name, and you should protect your life. People still die from Rabiës in Vietnam. After a bite or scratch, you have to visit a hospital as soon as possible, preferably within 24 hours. Rabiës, once the virus becomes active, WILL kill you. One more warning: I saw people let their children feed the monkeys, This is very, very dangerous. One look at their teeth says enough. Aside from the agressive monkeys, the only thing on Monkey Island is a view after a big exhausting climb, and some lazing on the beach.
drawbacks: got attacked by two of them
had to go through a rabies post-infection treatment
practical_tips: go to the hospital in Hanoi if bitten or scratched

And the rocks and sharp and spikey, making me fear that I would die or have bad injuries once I lose my grip. Some parts are also super tough for my short legs; at one moment I had to jump over to another 90 degrees wall because I couldn't stretch my legs out enough to test my footing first. Luckily I met a local guide who was with other tourists, and he kindly assisted and supported me to get to the top and to climb back down safely. It was so scary that I didn't bother taking pictures at the top; all I could think of was how to get down 😂If given a chance again, I probably wouldn't risk my life to climb it. Came back with a few 'battle scars' on my legs and hands. However, if you are an Eurasian, it will probably be easy for you. All the other Eurasian tourists looked so stable and calm and even offered their hands as a support for me. For that, I'm really grateful. Thanks guys!

I looked at one (about two metres away) and it ran and me and bit my leg. I yelped in pain then two more came and bit me on the other leg and bum while the first monkey jumped on my back. Do not come here it is a disgrace.

author: Youri van den Hurk

author: Ellen G
title: Stay away from the monkeys

I didn't do things like that, and in the end I got bitten by 2 Monkeys, after they tried to steal things out of my friends bellybag. People throw sand on the monkeys
practical_tips: Don't do things like throwing sand on the monkeys or giving them beer and junk food
Be careful with your belongings, especially in crowded areas

author: Rob S
title: Not bad - a tourist stop over
original_content: Monkey Island is known for the monkeys that bother tourists for food. There is a nice beach and a hike to a view, but this is strictly a tourist stop. Buy anything and the prices are silly for Vietnam.

author: Bernard B
title: Sad case of touristic overexploitation
original_content: The beach is nice and the view from the hilltop stunning BUT the climb is challenging and can turn dangerous if the monkeys attack you! Do NOT bring any food! While I was there some people got chased by monkeys and one lady got bitten and scratched. Sad...

author: Jennifer B
title: Great view!
original_content: I came to the island with a tour group. The moment I arrived on the island I saw a monkey on the beach! He stole a water bottle from someone and was braking it open, really cool to see but please listen to your guides and drivers to the island when they say do not carry things onto the island lol. I did bring a small 2kg dry bag but I made sure it was around Me, closed and had no snacks in it. The monkeys will steal from you, they arnt super friendly haha. The beach itself was beautiful and covered in super very small shells. I hiked, more like climbed, to the top of the island for the view it was amazing! But seriously a climb with sharp rocks. practical_tips: listen to your guides and drivers

author: larstravel05
title: Nice View and funny monkeys
original_content: Bring some snacks to feed the monkeys (you can buy some there but it's expensive), they eat out of your hand but be careful since they can get aggressive. The viewpoint is really nice but you need normal shoes (no flip flops) to get up to the top, as the rocks are a bit sharp sometimes

author: DiegoAGuzman
title: Pretty nice beach
original_content: It's nothing out of this world, but it is a pretty nice island with some 40+ monkeys running around. Compared to the monkeys in Thailand and Indonesia these are quite docile but still beware, because they do tend to get angry as most monkeys do. I would recommend a stop at this island if you're in the area.

author: Rayne K
title: Upsetting - disregard for animal wellbeing
original_content: It was the last stop of our day boat trip. We visited in low season and there were still half a dozen boats at the island at the same making the trek up to the viewpoint quite crowded. Watching my fellow tourists give junk food to the monkeys was upsetting. Despite the warnings people found it amusing to watch a monkey drink a beer or pop. Then when the animal was done the garbage is just left on the beach.

author: Farahhsuziee
title: Challenging hiking for a great view
original_content: For a view overlooking lan ha bay, you have to hike for about 30++ minutes to the peak. The view is stunning but you have to be extra careful since there is no safety features at all and the rocks are really pointy and there is no proper trails available. It will be worse during weekends since there will be crowd going up and down. Expect around 1 hour to go up and down.
practical_tips: go early to avoid weekend crowds

author: Ray Babin
title: Be prepared
original_content: It's worth the excursion, but be prepared by bringing good climbing shoes, because the trek is dangerous. Sharp rocks and sand don't mix well. The tour organizers should warn the tourists more. Also the monkeys can get agressive.
drawbacks: tour organizers should warn the tourists more

author: jkcal
title: The climb!
original_content: Money Island is worth a visit and do climb the mountain.  The climb to the top is a little challenging.  It is like rock climbing, so better be a little fit and ready to climb.  I did not make it all the way to the top because feel it was a little too dangerous for me.  I was so close to the top.  It is a very nice view of the beach from the top.  There are monkeys on the beach, don't give them food because if you do they will follow you every where.  They are not afraid of people.
drawbacks: The climb to the top is a little challenging
felt it was a little too dangerous for me
highlights: It is a very nice view of the beach from the top
There are monkeys on the beach
practical_tips: Don't give them food because if you do they will follow you every where

author: Simon Boots
title: A must see
original_content: This place is must see on any trip to Kat Ba. The monkeys are terrific and terrorise the entire island, staff and visitors.Getting on and off the island is not the easiest and the path up from the beech is pretty torcherous but it is well worth the effort.
drawbacks: Getting on and off the island is not the easiest
the path up from the beech is pretty torcherous
highlights: it is well worth the effort

author: SabineDV
title: Part off most tours
original_content: Monkey Island is part of most Halong Bay tours. There are a bunch of tame monkeys on the beach and some coats on the hill. You can climb to the top,  but this is quite dangerous and difficult since you are practically rock climbing a lot of the time.  So wear decent shoes. The view is stunning.

author: SQLRTD
title: Hike is challenging
original_content: Unfortunately we were ripped off by our hotel which promised English speaking tour guide.  Instead we got local boat who motioned to us to jump off boat into the sand.  I jumped and hurt my knee badly so could not hike.  I did see monkeys.  My partner went on the hike but he was by himself and there was no one else on the hiking trail.  It was not well marked so he did not go all the way since he was afraid of getting lost or injured with no one around.  Interestingly we met a girl on the bus a couple of days later who told us she did not get to the top because the hike was so crowded with people.  So it changes.
drawbacks: got local boat who motioned to us to jump off boat into the sand
hike was so crowded with people

author: Maria-Victoria S
title: Be prepared for a trip to the hospital
original_content: 558623085I am writing this review from the French Hospital in Ha Noi. Three injections around the bite wound, one in my arm, one in my gluteus maximus. Plus two to test for allergic reactions to the shots.I visited Monkey Island yesterday as part of the one-day tour.The guide warned us that the monkeys bite so I sat on a rock away from them. Or so I thought. I was looking out to sea and moved my backpack from my back to my lap. Quite suddenly, a monkey jumped on my shoulder and tried to get into my backpack. No sudden movements, I tried to remain calm. I was afraid it might bite me near my head or face. The monkey found no food and hoped off my shoulder and then I was quite suddenly biten on the leg by another monkey I hadn't seen. I felt panic, shock, and intense pain all at once. I could say don't sit anywhere and stay well away but if they find your movements interesting enough, and especially with the possibility of food attached, my advice is to watch out. This is not a place for children!I needed a place to sit to clean the wound. I thought of the cafe but in the cafe the monkeys were grabbing food out of people's hands.My advice is to stay on the boat. Stay away! It isn't worth the risk. I had no idea how dangerous such a wildlife encounter can be.The monkeys are expecting food. If you dont have any, stay very clear from them. If you have food, they WILL surprise you. Another tourist got slapped in the face when she ran out of food. It could have easily been a bite.They will grab anything out of your hand to inspect the edibility, including your telephone.I now have to get a full rabies vaccination series over 28 days (seven shots total just today including the two to test for an allergic reaction to the vaccines) in addition to antibiotics. Additional shots required on day 3, 7, 14 and 28 after the day of the bite. Yes, they SAY rabies isn't present on this island but the hospital and insurance companies have to treat precautionary. Please be careful.
drawbacks: monkeys grab food out of people's hands

author: navtombros
title: Beautiful Place to Spend a Few Hours
original_content: I can't believe there's so many negative reviews here. First off lets get things straight.- The monkey's are not native. Better to know this going in so you're not disappointed.- That being said this isn't a petting zoo, the monkeys are wild animals. Put your loose items away, don't feed them, don't try and touch them or get in their personal space to take a selfie. Come on people, all it takes is a little common sense.Most boats stop here as part of their itinerary and it's easy to see why.The island is small, but has a really nice beach where you can get a beautiful view of the bay. A quick hike up will give you even more AMAZING 360 degree views of the area. Some of my favorite pictures were taken from the top, it's gorgeous. Also getting to the top is a fun excursion in itself, you pretty much have to do some amateur rock climbing, thankfully the shape of the rocks give you plenty of hand/footholds to use.Loved this stop, even with the number of tourists, we could've spent another hour at the top of the hike.
drawbacks: don't try and touch them or get in their personal space
practical_tips: come on people, all it takes is a little common sense

author: Arhan E
title: monkey can bite!
original_content: small island with a lovely beach and yes, a few monkeys :)they look small and cute, but be careful, they can bite (and one of them did when we were there)!

author: jaypep1
title: Not Impressed

Very disappointing.
extracted_spaces: the top of the very small mountain
drawbacks: lots of rubbish on the beach
highlights: good view from the top of the mountain

author: Jocelyn S
title: Ok as part of your 1-day boat tour
original_content: Wouldn't make a special effort to go there separately - saw 3 rsther bored monkeys, hiked up the roughest rock 'trail' ever and saw a nice ciew from the top - followed by a difficult scramble down.

author: iidaaaaa
title: Great rock climbing for beginners
original_content: Went there as a part of a tour even though our guide sat in the cafe whilst we explored the island... Still had fun climbing up the hill and spotting the monkeys. There were some other tourists with a guide telling about the monkeys and from what I heard it sounded interesting.
drawbacks: our guide sat in the cafe whilst we explored the island

author: DavidRedDevil
title: Nice views from the top but dangerous monkeys !
original_content: We did monkey island with a tour. The views were absolutely worth the visit. But my friend was bited by one on the aggressive monkey there. She was serious scared.You can do monkey island but make sure don't stay close to the monkeys or don't give them any food.. A terrible day with the aggressive monkey.. My girlfriend still remember about them...

author: Arun C
title: lots of monkeys

author: Sheena A

author: Anika v

author: Adam J
title: Beautiful view

author: Antoniojb85
title: Nature is always nature !!
original_content: Absolutely nice experience with the crew had in that island having fun with monkeys , full of monkeys .... the only negative things is that there is not a small bar to have a coffe...the government should update the spot and sure can be more attractive.

author: moderntraveler
title: Over populated, every tour goes there.

author: Mili B

author: christineflanagan278
title: nice place for a visit
original_content: stopped off here for about an hour, climbed a cliff which had great views from the top and saw monkeys on the island.

author: Mike C
title: Very nice. Monkeys not that friendly
original_content: Nice island. You can feed the monkeys however they are not too friendly. Nice walk up to a viewpoint which is a great view. Worth a visit.

author: Ashton Tessier
title: Monkey island fun
original_content: We were on a boat tour that finished with a couple hours at Monkey Island. I wasnt really sure what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised.The trek up the mountain for the view is incredible, but be careful it gets steep towards the top. Once you start climbing higher, it feels like you're rock climbing and much harder if you don't bring proper shoes (but u can still go with sandals). Even if you decide you don't want to go all the way to the peak, it's still worth going part way up, it's a nice little climb.The monkeys are cute, but watch your stuff when you go swimming as they will go and try to steal your things!Definetly recommend, enjoy!
drawbacks: they will go and try to steal your things

author: Lancy f
title: Aggressive monkeys
original_content: The monkeys are very cute but accustomed to being fed. I do not condone feeding them and just walked and watched at a distance. Some people nearby were feeding them and I believe one of the monkeys thought I was the one with food and attached me and bit me twice tearing through two layers of pants and my skin! Afterwards I was shaken and went to the little sitting place. The monkeys stole 3 packs of Oreos, hold on to your snacks!

author: Laura_96Dyer
title: Risky, touristy and not so fun !
original_content: Did monkey island by taxi boat rented from the Cat Ba wharf. We came there and there were many boats and tourists there. We even saw some of them were attacked by the aggressive red-bum monkeys and they had to run away to the beach. Did a little hiking to the top hill and it was quite risky with sharp stones even the view was amazing. Not much thing you can do here, and we couldn't recommend !
drawbacks: not much thing you can do here

author: Mayank Agarwal
title: Worth it for the interesting and scary climb
original_content: It’s a small strip of beach about 75-100 meters long with a single restaurant serving beers n chips, normally most tours of Lan Ha Bay makes a stop here. The monkeys are there not as an attraction but a nuisance, they are bold and ready to snatch your belongings ever from inside the restaurants. The main purpose to visit the place is to climb to the top of the island. At least we didn’t find any monkeys ones we left the restaurant area.  The climb itself is on the difficult side as the trail is namesake only, most of the walk is over sharp rocks, some places you have to climb heights of 3-4 feet’s. I am obese and was still able to do it, so while it's difficult it’s still manageable. While going up we met with lots of bottlenecks and had to wait for about 20-30 minutes to let others climb down first. By the time we reached the top we were the only ones there and that added to the charm of the place. The fabulous view from the top along with the sense of achievement of climbing this scary trail gave us a great feeling. It was a total waste of time for half our group as they were not able to make the climb and spent time getting harassed by monkeys at the restaurant.  For those planning to climb the correct footwear would make the difference as I saw many people climbing down with cuts on their sole.
drawbacks: monkeys are bold and ready to snatch your belongings
highlights: sense of achievement of climbing this scary trail
practical_tips: wear correct footwear to avoid cuts on the sole

author: Jeanette P
title: The monkeys are naughty
original_content: Some tours including ours take you to the lovely beach on the island.  There is a trail you can climb to a fabulous lookout.  The trail is not for everyone as you must climb with your hands on sharp rocks to get there.   Because some tourists feed and tease the monkeys they come towards you expecting food.   The guide warned us they can be aggressive.  Wasn't wild on them.

author: Kelly O
title: Super crowded. Wear closed toed shoes for the hike!
original_content: Crowded and, frankly, quite sad to see how people (including the workers in the restaurant on the island) were treating the monkeys. They will get aggressive and bite! We were glad we took a long private boat trip and got dropped off here at the end of the day rather that take a tour boat out here with 20 other people. The hike to the top is beautiful, but be prepared with closed toed shoes and be prepared for bottlenecks, as the route is rather treacherous and a lot of people are not quite fit to climb!
drawbacks: people were treating the monkeys aggressively
a lot of people are not quite fit to climb
highlights: the hike to the top is beautiful
practical_tips: be prepared with closed toed shoes

author: Paul H

author: HasilRoshni

author: ameliaaria180
title: gold monkey
original_content: When you are a very intelligent animals threatening the knife when watching the natural life they have to buy a half-day tour.

author: margaridavc
title: Amazing morning! Cute monkeys! Outstanding views in the mountain top!
original_content: Our visit to Monkey Island was a port of a half day tour around ha long Bay and cat Ba island.As soon as we were left in the beach we could see that not much was going on there, a big 'souvenir' and kayak rental shop and that's it. Next to this shop is where you can find the huge amount of monkeys! They are really used to humans what makes them really friendly- BRING SOME PEANUTS OR FUIT WITH YOU to make sure you can make them come as close as possible from you and they will be glad to allow you to take pictures with them. Just be careful, don't try to call them to you by pretending you have some food in your hand, if you don't give them something after calling them up like this, they will be mad! The babies are the cutest and the mothers won't be scared os coming closer to you even with the baby hanging in their chest! The best and most adventure you will have will be by going up the rocky Mountain top, it will take you about 45 min to get to the top, the first 15 min are easy walking through the huge trees but the last 30min will make your legs shake... but the views... WHAT AMAZING VIEWS of the same beach you were left and the cutest little island Bay in one side and huge islands and no one to be found in the other side! You will love it!
drawbacks: Not much going on at the beach
Monkeys can get mad if you call them without giving them food
highlights: Amazing views from the top of the rocky mountain
practical_tips: Bring peanuts or fruit to make the monkeys come close
Don't try to call the monkeys without giving them food

But don't get super excited for monkey island in particular. Enjoy the beach and relax :)
drawbacks: groups of people trying to go up and down at the same time
highlights: boat through the bay is worth it

Cheers

highlights: spectacular hike to the view point

author: Peter G
title: DO NOT GO

author: Alex W

author: Dianne BM

best time with friends and meeting new people

author: Samuel W

We also arranged transfer from the airport in Hanoi to Cat Ba the day prior as well as transfer to Ha Long City the day after our climbing trip through Cat Ba Climbing, and everything went very smoothly. They were easy to work with over Whatsapp for planning an itinerary that would work with the rest of our trip. Super fun experience, 10/10 would recommend.

author: Otis A
title: Cat ba rock climbing free solo and kayaking
original_content: Tinh was the best guide super friendly and great to chat to. The rock climbing is amazing, beginner, intermediate and advanced friendly. Beautiful scenery and jumping off the cliff after your climb is heaps of  fun. Kayaking is very peaceful also
practical_tips: jumping off the cliff after your climb is heaps of fun

author: Calvin D
title: Awesome
original_content: Mr T was the best guide super cool guy. Started off with the rock climbing which has accessible difficulties for everyone and then ended with the kayaking which had amazing views

author: Jacob D
title: WOULD DO AGAIN!
original_content: Hai and Mik were phenomenal guides and the area was perfect for all levels of climbing! The water was very warm and the views can’t be beat. I can’t recommend this tour or company enough!
highlights: perfect for all levels of climbing

author: Jon G
title: Best adventure activity of my trip to Vietnam!
original_content: Brilliant guides & boat captain. Super chill group and fun climbing. I'm a 60 year old novice. The easy routes were great, and watching the experienced climbers on the touger routes was cool. Dropping into the sea makes for a sofe, warm landing. All in all a great trip (40 minute cruise each way to & from the climbing site is also a good way to see Lan Ha bay and the fisherman village - if you doing have time for a separate cruise then this is a good alternative)Definitely recommend. Hope to come back and do this again.
highlights: Super chill group and fun climbing

author: Harry L
title: A Must-Do Adventure for Climbers in Cat Ba
original_content: I’ve wanted to try deep water solo climbing for a long time, and this trip was everything I hoped for and more. We couldn’t have asked for a better guide and instructor than Hai — he was fantastic at encouraging us to push ourselves and also respecting people’s comforts zones, letting us explore a variety of climbs at our own pace. I was grateful to try the 7b, although I had no chance at topping it! The free beer at the end was also a nice touch!Climbing over turquoise waters surrounded by stunning scenery was a truly unique and unforgettable experience.We went in off season, so were a group of 4. However would have had plenty of time for many climbs with a group twice the size. I’d highly recommend this to anyone with at least a bit of climbing experience. Just be aware you do have to jump off what you climb into the sea, which I found great fun! If you’ve never climbed before, I’d suggest visiting their office first to try out their indoor wall and see if it’s right for you. If not, they also offer other amazing activities, like nighttime kayaking with bioluminescent plankton.
drawbacks: jumping off what you climb into the sea
practical_tips: visit their office first to try out their indoor wall
try nighttime kayaking with bioluminescent plankton

author: Harry L
title: From Langurs to Glowing Plankton — An unexpected highlight
original_content: My partner and I tried the bioluminescent kayaking, a little skeptical at first about whether it was real. It turned out to be one of the absolute highlights of our trip!It was just the two of us, our guide, and the captain — a wonderfully personal experience. We started off spotting golden langurs by chance, then visited Monkey Island to see brown langurs and enjoy a beautiful beach walk and swim.After that came a lovely meal at a floating restaurant, followed by kayaking and swimming among the glowing plankton. Photos can’t capture it — the water truly sparkled with light. We’ve never seen anything like it.Our captain and guide were great company throughout. They went out of their way to really show off the bay. Excellent value for money and an unforgettable way to spend an evening!

author: Sean V
title: Beautiful, unique experience
original_content: Awesome! So much fun, great teacher, beautiful experience. Lots of different options for beginner to advanced, relaxed and adrenaline

author: llewsor
title: Cat Ba Deep Water Solo Adventure
original_content: Mikey and Ting were great guides. Super friendly and professional. Perfect day of climbing, highly recommended for beginners and advanced.

author: Thanh
title: BEST adventure in the most beautiful place ever
original_content: Our family of 6 signed up for the 2-day 1-night package that included transportation, swimming, deep water soloing, kayaking, night on boat, top roping, night kayaking to see bioluminescent plankton, meals and professional guide. It was the most amazing time we had as a family. Anh Dung stayed in close communication during the planning months before our trip and our guide, Hai, was phenomenal! We felt always felt aafe and Hai gave us opportunities to challenge ourselves at every level for our entire family ranging from 60 to 18 years old!

author: paul t
title: I have never written a review before but I feel this calls for it
original_content: Broken back;Whilst I am aware that climbing has potential be a dangerous sport, after having an accident I would have expected more care from this company.On my second ever climbing trip with this company (Cat Ba climbing) I initially thought they were good, however when I jumped into the sea from around 14m I immediately knew I'd hurt myself on impact.When they said are you ok, I said no and continued to say no as I was in a lot of pain over the next two hours - no one helped, they just didn't take it seriously.When I arrived back at their office I asked for a taxi to be taken to the hospital, they initially didn't want to do it but eventually said the only way was by motorbike (!!!).They had no idea where to go at the hospital and then eventually we found some guy who the guide said, he wasn't even sure if he was a doctor. The guy poked my back in three places, said you'll be fine you just need a good meal (!). Catba Climbing did take me to a chemist but the voltarol pills were grainy and old an had v little impact so also speaks to a lack of planning.Left the island in a great deal of pain and took a long flight home. Quote from UK hospital after x-ray showed I had fractured my spine wow, that borders on gross negligence, you could have been paralysed at any point on your journey home and shouldnt have been travelling".I did contact one of the guides, he said they would look at improving their process! Not saying don't climb with them, just saying make sure you are aware of the risks
drawbacks: they just didn't take it seriously
practical_tips: make sure you are aware of the risks

author: Nicolas G
title: Deep Water Solo: Awesome experience with great guide and wonderful people
original_content: TLDR: we did deep water soloing with wonderful guide and people, it was an awesome experience! Would always do it again with Cat Ba Climbing and strongly recommend them:)Long story:While my girlfriend and I were staying in Cat Ba during a Vietnam round trip, we took the chance to explore the crags and deep water solo opportunities around the island. We rented gear for an unsupervised trip to hidden valley and booked a deep water solo tour in lan ha bay. The owner of Cat Ba Climbing Mr. Zoom took it upon himself to check whether we were able to safely lead climb and belay. We very much appreciated this sanity check, which was not performed by another tourist tour organiser. The next day we booked a deep water solo (DWS) trip right away and it was awesome!We were a small group of 5 tourists plus guide and staff. The guide (Hai, sorry if I misspell you) was in his element he speaks English well and has a profound knowledge of the DWS crags of the bay. He did a very good warm up and introduction at an easy climb up to roughly 6m above the water (I chickened out and down climbed 2m on my first try, then send it the second time) to get us used to the exposure und rock quality. After warm up we moved to different walls which had harder climbs and higher ones to test our skill and confidence. Hai even joined in on the fun and gave us a lesson in some of the harder routes. We had blast!Big thanks to Cat Ba Climbing! If you have a slight interest in climbing and are able to swim, you should definitely give DWS with Cat Ba Climbing a go!
highlights: profound knowledge of the DWS crags
practical_tips: book a deep water solo trip with Cat Ba Climbing

title: A challenging, rewarding and breathtaking day

author: Andrea
title: Good experience, could do with some clarifications and tips
original_content: Good experience, had a fun time, went top roping at Fisher Valley.Some improvements:1. The first day we went to ask for information, we were told Moody Beach is great for beginners and was basically highly recommended to us. A few days later, we went to ask again, someone else helped us and basically told us not to go (because access is difficult during low tide). I was so surprised by the difference in response for that climb, and although everyone of course is entitled to their own opinion, it's very confusing for customers to be told completely different things.2. When I was doing my first climb, one of the guides asked if I wanted to get off (and essentially quit that climb). I was struggling a bit (fell off once or twice at the same section already) but I never thought about quitting. The positive side of this is that the guide who was belaying me told the guide who made that comment that I wanted to continue and try again. So I did and eventually got it on the third try.3. I wanted to leave early, and I was told by one person the first day we went that we would leave at noon (and arrive back around 12:25PM). The second time we went back, another person told us 12:45PM. I asked if I could leave early to catch a bus back to Hanoi, and I was told that I wouldn't have the full experience - I also sensed judgment. I don't think I had to explain myself for why I wanted to leave early, and if I'm paying you for the full experience, then it shouldn't matter when I leave. And, based on the information I was given the first time, I would only be leaving 15 minutes early (I wanted to leave at 11:45AM), which is barely enough time for one climb if I even decided to do a climb at that time. One less climb for 3-4 extra hours in Hanoi is worth it to me, and I don't need anyone's judgment for why I need to leave early.Despite all that, the experience was overall quite good and fun. Wasn't really given many tips on how to actually climb though, and as beginners, we were basically tied to rope and then told to go with some pointers here and there about where to put our hands and feet. Towards the end, one of the guides said good technique is: keeping arms straight and hips (and thus body) close to the wall. That was very helpful, could've done with some "beginner tips" from the start.As the only climbing company in Cat Ba, it's a good experience if you want to try climbing. Everything is safe, people are friendly, groups aren't too big (there were 6 clients and 3 guides when I went).
drawbacks: Different responses from guides about Moody Beach
Guide asked to quit climb without permission
practical_tips: Ask for clear information about departure time

author: Soph1202
title: Experienced or professional climber AVOID! – Unprofessional, unhelpful and inappropriate owner with a big ego. Mr Zoom -
original_content: We went to Cat Ba Island to try some of the beautiful climbs. Because we were travelling by scooter, we decided not to bring our own equipment and rent some from the local Climbing business CAT BA CLIMBING. This way, we thought it would also be a good way to invest money with the locals and help the economy.Julie who works there was very lovely, but the owner Mr Zoom (Nguyen Manh Dung) had a very bad attitude towards us and seemed to take an instant dislike to us and we had no idea why. He told us we had to do “a test” before renting his equipment which is understandable. However, his short practice wall in his business is not suitable for the test as it is very cramped when you get to the top with a low ceiling and you can’t even lean back to do your set up, as Mr Zoom told us himself it is not solid enough to take weight, so you have to do everything one handed – impossible! He then started shouting at us in front of all his staff who looked embarrassed and refused to hire us his equipment instead of having a rational discussion about different ways of operating and why my partner did what he did when attempting to set up/lower off. Mr Zoom has a very big ego, with a poor and unprofessional attitude. It seems that he can’t cope with people having the same or more experience than him or doing things differently.This guy really had a bee in his bonnet. I would not recommend climbing with him or his company if you have some experience. Just do it by yourself!
drawbacks: Owner Mr Zoom had a bad attitude towards us and seemed to take an instant dislike to us
Equipment rental test was not suitable for the test as it is very cramped and has a low ceiling
Owner Mr Zoom shouted at us in front of his staff

author: Carolimo
title: Highly recommended
original_content: The tour was well organised, professional, safe and great fun. Thu was our guide, he was great at ensuring that everyone had a good time, even though we had a big mix of climbing skills in the group. I highly recommend this. Novice climbers will enjoy the day as well.We had a cloudy day in winter, the water was a bit cooler but not very unpleasant, I did swim for a bit. Don't let the weather deter you from booking.Something to note: book as soon as possible! The tides dictate when and on which days you will be able to go out. If we had booked one day later we would not have been able to go. Practice jumping into the water from a lower height on your first climb. Leaning too far back as you hit the water results in a bit of a shock on your lower back which can hurt a bit.

author: MrChadC
title: Local Climber grows the climbing community through Cat Ba Climbing
original_content: I wanted to let my trip set in before writing a review to see if my feelings were still the same, or were they just travel excitement?As I sit back in Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam which is about a 2 hr flight from Cat Ba Island.  I am still full of happiness with my trip to Cat Ba Climbing. I have been on a work trip in the bustling city of Ho Chi Minh and was in desperate need of a peaceful quick trip, Cat Ba Climbing delivered just that on the 2 days 1 night floating homestay.I did the Deep Water Solo 2 day 1-night tour guided by the famous Mr. ZOOM himself Mr. Zoom from cat ba delivered a secret climbing spot for DWS even though other companies said it the tide was good until a week later. The climbing grades are as marked and the rock is good. Mr. Zoom takes you through a warm-up traverse, then puts you your requested climbing grade. To my fellow boulder friends, he has a few good problems waiting for you! and to those who top rope "just enjoy the view".The floating homestay: Peacefully ran buy Mr. Zooms family and their 2 dogs. Beds are nice rooms are clean and the Home cooked family-style meals are amazing!  Don't expect AC and Hotel Amenities.. it's like camping on the water.  If you want to escape the crowds and want an experience to tell the grandkids book this trip. Be nice.  Bring the fam or dogs a small nice thank you gift. Mr. Zoom: Zoom is passionate about his business and very knowledgable about climbing. While on the wall he can give you beta from the boat and plays a major roll in growing this fairly new climbing community. The Beta: If you have never been to cat ba for climbing. Contact Mr. Zoom on Whatsapp prior to booking for detailed instructions on how to arrive at the island.The Crux: I flew into HPH airport, caught a "Grab" (similar to uber) to Ben Binh Pier to ride the hydrofoil boat to cat ba. Unfortunately, upon arrival it was closed (or the taxi driver brought me to a closed one). Beware taxis will scam you, plan well.  Then the taxi driver said he take me to cat ba climbing which was not true. He brought me to the next ferry landing 30 min away and charged me 300k VND + 100VND for the airport ride. I ended up hopping on the local ferry to cat ba, waited an hour in an unfamiliar area s the only tourist, caught the ferry to Cat Ba island then was hassled by taxis again for a longer ride into Cat Ba Town. KEEP IT SIMPLE. support local climber and Let Mr. Zoom plan your pickup and arrival from the airport. PS: I wish i would have known this was a fairly new climbing community, I would have brought some spare gear to donate to cat ba climbing business.
highlights: Home cooked family-style meals are amazing!
practical_tips: Bring the fam or dogs a small nice thank you gift
Contact Mr. Zoom on Whatsapp prior to booking for detailed instructions on how to arrive at the island
Support local climber and Let Mr. Zoom plan your pickup and arrival from the airport

author: Michael D
title: Deep water soloing
original_content: As a group of 3 friends we booked to go half day deep water soloing, which we were all excited to do, but none of us had done before. We were quite lucky as we were the only ones booked for that afternoon so it was like having our own private adventure!The trip started with a 30 min boat ride from Cat Ba town out into Halong Bay. We started climbing 4As working our way up to 6Bs. There are lots of routes for varying climbing abilities. The first jump into the water from the cliffs was slightly nerve-wracking, but after the first jump was much easier. The whole experience was amazing fun and was one of the highlights of our trip to Vietnam. We would definitely recommend it if you like climbing!

author: schwam
title: Great DeepWaterSolo climbing
original_content: Did the 1/2 day DWS tour.Ha Long is probably the best place in the world to do DWS. Everyone who likes climbing will also love DWS.We went 40min by boat to a north facing wall where the water is deep enough for DWS. Routes from range from 4 to 7a with max heights of ~10m. So great fun for all levels of experience. If you don't like to climb to the top you can jump of at any place. The boat driver and guide know what they do, so it's save. The rock is quite sharp so you might get some scratches if you don't pay attention. Maybe bring tape. Chalk and shoes are included but I brought my own stuff. For me half a day was more than enough. We were a group of six and everyone had enough time to could climb until you were completely done. Mr Zoom is a great and fun guide.
highlights: great fun for all levels of experience

Mit Beach is a great beach to chill, swim, climb and camp in tents that are put on sturdy platforms built into the rock formations. This beach can only be booked and visited through Cat Ba Climbing, but put it high on your list of things to do in Cat Ba. They do offer deep water solo tours too.
