author: George Fox-Edwards
title: BEST activity in Vietnam
original_content: Mr Zoom is a legend, he suits the best routes to your capabilities and means you have a lot of fun on the climbs. The price is also very reasonable for how memorable your day is.
practical_tips: suit the best routes to your capabilities

author: CMWstyle
title: Really Amazing Day Climbing in the Bay
original_content: My husband and I really enjoyed our outing with Cat Ba Climbing in Lan Ha Bay! It was our first time in Vietnam, and only our second time climbing outside - couldn't have been better. The routes were really fun and unique, especially some of the cave-like climbs. The guides stuck with me as I worked through routes, and we felt safe, happy to hang with the other climbers in our group, and even were fed delicious Bahn Mi ;) Bonus points: there were beach dog friends!

author: Carl M
title: Phenomenal overnight climbing trip
original_content: Had a full day of sport climbing on a remote island, entirely tailored to the group's ability and requests.This was followed by an overnight stay in comfy tents and a basic, yet wholesome meal on the beach.The next morning we were up early for some DWS, a bucket item list of mine!Mr Zoom and the entire team were great - would highly recommend!
highlights: entirely tailored to the group's ability and requests
basic, yet wholesome meal on the beach
DWS, a bucket item list of mine

author: Siobhan P.
title: Fantastic day climbing!
original_content: We had a great day top rope climbing in Hidden Valley, which has some spectacular views even before you start scaling the limestone cliffs! The climbing staff were incredibly helpful and professional. The experience is tailored to the various levels of everyone in the group, with (on the day we visited) one climbing instructor to every three climbers, so no one was waiting around for too long in between climbs. Of the group of nine who were climbing, only two of us had opted to stay for a full day, which meant that for the after-lunch climbing segment, we had one-to-one attention and guidance from our highly experienced and friendly climbing guides (unfortunately their names escape me, but he was from Vietnam and she was from Mexico!). By the end of the day, we were truly exhausted but very, very happy. Highly recommended!
practical_tips: opt to stay for a full day

author: Faycal D
title: Best adventure - climbing experience
original_content: We took the half day climbing trip from catba with a friend. For what it is it s super cheap and the staff is so friendly and experienced in climbing. You have all levels from 4 to 7 routes.Will definitely come back to catba just for some more climbing.Thanks guys.Fayçal & Vincent

author: Nadav K
title: Great Day Climbing !!
original_content: Had a fantastic day climbing with Cat Ba Climbing early March 2019.  They were quite flexible in what I wanted to climb so matched routes to my interests and ability. As the tides weren’t right for deep water solo, we went to Hidden Valley and climbed both multi-pitch and single pitch. The guide was great with instruction and encouragement.  He taught me the basics of lead climbing so not only did I get to climb a bunch of fun and challenging routes, but I also learned a lot. This operation is very safety-oriented, and they have also been working hard to develop and bolt new routes. I would love to climb with them again if I have a chance to get back to Cat Ba !
practical_tips: check tides for deep water solo

author: Toni B
title: Ha Long Bay Boat tour
original_content: We booked the Ha Long Bay day tour as they were offering it at a cheaper price than other places. It was a great day and we had a lot of fun so would definitely recommend. It’s done through a local guide and went the exact same places as all the other tours. However we firstly had an issue with our transfer, not sure if it was a communication issue, but we weren’t picked up from our hostel like they said, we waited 35 minutes but no one came. Our hostel rang them and they immediately sent a taxi through to us which was a good save and we made it just in time! The other issue we had was the tour boat had ‘run out’ of bottles of water (but had plenty of cans of beer and pop). Luckily other guests were kind enough to share!
drawbacks: tour boat had 'run out' of bottles of water
practical_tips: go early to avoid transfer issues

author: gusilmom
title: fantastic company if you are passionate about climbing
original_content: we are a family with young children and we climb indoors mostly.  we visited in December 2018.  We stayed in Cat Ba town(3 nights) near the office to catch the action and it was a great idea for it was off season in Cat Ba we had no issue with booking the tours.  But summer months could be different and you may benefit from booking the entire thing(lodging and all) from Hanoi.  Cat Ba Climbing was our first outdoor climbing experience and it was amazing.  This company compared to the other company(who is bigger a few steps from each other) climbs for longer and is dedicated to climbing experience.  the staff is passionate about climbing and my young children were encouraged and cherished through the experience.  we did hidden valley half day climbing, deep water solo half day, and lan ha bay/ha long bay  boat tour.  the first two were offered by the catba climbing company staff and I believe the third one was consolidated with another agency.  but it was a great tour and price was as cheap as it gets.  we are so touched by their great care and dedication.  we would love to come back and climb some more on Cat Ba island and would not hesitate to contact this company again.  ps.  we are intermediate level climbers.  the area does offer great options for beginner/intermediate level climbers.  if you are advanced you may enjoy private tour.
practical_tips: book the entire thing (lodging and all) from Hanoi
consider booking private tour for advanced climbers

author: יובל ג
title: Half day in the hidden valley
original_content: We went 5 friends to do climbing in the hidden valley with 2 guides from cat ba climbing , I really recommend on them they are true professional , and made our day great and satisfying, and also the price was really good
practical_tips: Recommend guides from Cat Ba Climbing

author: YRT
title: Free Solo Climbing half day
original_content: After a beautiful boat ride, we arrived at Mr. Zoom’s floating house where he met us and took us to the climbing routes. He gave great instructions, including how to fall safely, and then started us on our first route. He was really good at meeting us at our climbing level, starting us out on an easy route to warm up and get accustomed to the really unique terrain (and water below!) and then took us to more advanced route that challenged us as climbers. We had really limited time in Vietnam, and couldn’t swing a full day/night in Cat Ba. We really didn’t want to miss out on this, and I’m glad we didn’t - but it meant a 7:30 bus from Hanoi and a 4:00 bus out of Cat Ba (apparently it was the latest we could leave the island). We were supposed to climb 11-3, but bus delays made it more like 11:45-3:00. If you can, spend a full day out there because it’s gorgeous. But if all you have is a half day, it is possible to do! Can’t rave enough about this incredible experience set against a stunning landscape! Mr. Zoom and his tours are exceptional.
practical_tips: spend a full day out there
if all you have is a half day, it is possible to do

author: eliott h
title: Great DWS Trip
original_content: Had a great trip on a boat to do some deep water soloing. Guides were super helpful and did a great job of getting everyone a chance to climb at their skill level. They drove the boat right up to the cliff, making it easy and fast to climb into the rock.

author: Daniela R
title: Suuuuper good!
original_content: So my boyfriend and I did some research before booking a tour in Cat Ba but in the end the company we chose didn’t convince us at all so as we were walking we saw the Cat Ba Climbing office and I am so glad that happened! Mr. Zoom (manager/owner) was super open, we explained what we both wanted, my boyfriend trekking and I more chilling in the beach, kayak, etc. so we managed to book a tour with a little bit of both and with a night stay on a floating house with a fishing Vietnamese family! I cant tell you how amazing it was, from beginning to end. The trekking was super good and then we arrived to this lovely family to spend a night with them, the food was always delicious. I truly recommend this tour office, Mr. Zoom will find something for you!
highlights: lovely family to spend a night with
practical_tips: book a tour with a little bit of both
go to the Cat Ba Climbing office for a tour

author: Jan R
title: Sick. Definitely do it
original_content: We started today (sunday) with the morning tour of Deep Water soloing. Our guide/instructor Paige was the most down to earth Californian guy we have ever met. We weren't that experienced (climbed a few times over the last couple of years but nothing major) and it did not matter. If you are a bit fitter, you will easily get up to 5a-b difficulty with the right tips. The best thing was, Paige did not explain the whole route at the beginning, but just yells tips up if you seem to be stuck somewhere. So you challenge yourself and not everything gets handed to you on a silver platter (but you can probably get that to if you want to) Deep water soloing is without ropes, so if you fall or are finished you just jump down. Cliff jumping from like up 15m in height is of course included and sometimes necessary. The rock can be quite sharp on a few occasions, but he will point them out to you. But you wont get around a few little nicks here and there. So if you are a bit fitter, can swim, are not afraid of heights and jumping off from those heights this tour will definitely pump you out and the feeling of accomplishment will stay with you for a while.Just do it. The cuts will fade the memories will stay. Definitely ask for Paige!See ya 🤙🏼
drawbacks: rock can be quite sharp on a few occasions
you wont get around a few little nicks here and there
highlights: feeling of accomplishment will stay with you for a while

author: veronicap88
title: So much fun and great value
original_content: Deep water soloing and rock climbing with Cat Ba Climbing was fantastic. Mr Zoom and his team are real professionals - from belaying to coaching and strict safety checks, they provide great experiences for novice and experienced climbers alike. Deep water soloing is exhilarating and pretty photogenic too, and the climbing in hidden valley is outstanding (from 4a-7b). 10/10 would go with these guys again.

author: Tullipilli
title: Fantastic for advanced, suboptimal for beginners
original_content: I have to say I am a total beginner in climbing and my boyfriend is advanced. But I do a lot of other sports and can learn very quick. He always wanted me to try so we asked if it is ok for beginners as well. They said it‘s no problem and there are different routes. It was a great trip and everybody was very nice. I climbed at last, but not as much as I had hoped. The first route was the easiest and after that we did routes even my boyfriend couldn’t end most of the time. So I was a little bit defeated at the end. It would have been nice to at least try another easy route after getting the feeling. I thought they would explain more about how to climb correctly or what to do better. For the price it‘s not what I expected, but it‘s a great experience.
drawbacks: For the price it's not what I expected
I thought they would explain more about how to climb correctly or what to do better
I climbed at last, but not as much as I had hoped

author: PeterSams89
title: Great experience!
original_content: I have done the deep water solo with Cat Ba climbing and it was an amazing experience. The guide is very knowledgeable about the routes and gives everyone something to do that fits well with their experience and comfort level. Would recommend!

author: Jeff
title: Fantastic deep water solo trip
original_content: Our guide, Mr. Zoom was a fantastic guide who was fun and catered to the groups needs. We went on a deep water solo trip.  We had a group of four people of varying skill levels and he was able to not only cater to everyones climbing ability but was able to efficiently keep everyone engaged with minimal down time between climbs.
practical_tips: go with a guide who can cater to varying skill levels

author: RebeccaJD01
title: Mr. Zoom was able to cater to what we wanted including harder climbs
original_content: We booked a half day of deep water soloing, kayaking in Halong Bay, a night on the floating fish farm, half a day of roped climbing, and half a day of trekking through Cat Ba Climbing, which is a locally owned company owned by Mr. Zoom.  We had looked into the competitor, Asia Outdoors, but Cat Ba Climbing seemed better able to cater to our particular needs and we liked using a locally-run business.  My daughter and I are both experienced rock climbers with my daughter interested in harder climbs, including leading sport climbs, and Mr. Zoom was able to accommodate us.  Mr. Zoom did a thorough safety check before sport climbing, and the gear all seemed solid.  (We recommend bringing your own climbing shoes if you are picky b/c his selection was a bit limited.  We did use his climbing shoes for DWS.)  We had a lot of fun on our stay on the floating fish farm, although the family who runs it spoke no English.  Their 7 year old daughter, Kim Ahn, was so much fun to hang out with though, and she actually went on the boat with us to DWS and kayak.  Mr. Zoom had a couple nephews along to assist with belaying, etc. during the climbing portion of the trip.  There were definitely climbs suitable for all levels both on DWS and the roped climbing.  The kayaking in Halong Bay was also very fun.  It was a bit hot and humid in July so the rock wasn't in ideal conditions, but we still had a blast.  Mr. Zoom was also able to accommodate us when we were really pretty tired on our last afternoon when we were supposed to do a trek.  Instead, he got two motorbike drivers to take us all around the island (my daughter was very keen to get on a motorbike!), and we went to Hospital Cave.  All in all we had a great experience with Cat Ba Climbing on all of our activities with them.
highlights: fun on the floating fish farm

author: Therealellbee
title: Great experience
original_content: Sorry it's taken a while to write the review but here it is.... We did a private 2 day top-roping course with Cat Ba Climbing and absolutely loved it. The first day was at the office, which, although not the best environment for learning as it is shared premises with a hotel and quite a small cramped space, we learned a lot and the tuition we felt, was excellent. A few hours was spent with Jade and Mr. Zoom, getting familiar with the equipment, learning knots, belaying and practicing cleaning anchor.The second day was out at the crag at Hidden valley where we climbed various routes, again with excellent tuition and supervision from Mr Zoom, who clearly loves his climbing and enjoys teaching and wants everybody to enjoy themselves as well.Very reasonably priced, I am now hooked on climbing thanks to our experience with Cat Ba Climbing. Very strong recommendation from us! Hope to see you guys again some day,  Thanks for an amazing couple of days.

author: theniece
title: Fun day out, but be mindful of the timing
original_content: We took the half day rock climbing session. Husband and myself have outdoor climbing experience, but there was a newbie. 3 pax to 1 guide - not a bad ratio.Started at 9am, but it took an hour to get ready, equipment, and driving/walking to the site. Each route had to be setup cos the guide didnt want us leading. So it was quite time consuming and over 2 hours, we climbed 5 (short; 6 bolts at most) routes each. This was the only disappointing part. If I had known, would have gone with a whole day session. But the guide was knowledeable, friendly and patient. So, good for beginners!
practical_tips: go with a whole day session
consider the guide to client ratio

author: jco631
title: Trek + floating fish farm
original_content: The trek on the morning was very great, a stop on a cute lake with the possibility to chill on a small boat, and a finish with the best view you can find on cat ba island!Then we went on a floating fish farm to eat a very good and big meal, before to go kayaking with a stunning scenery! The guide / staff is very nice.Very good day with cat ba climbing!

author: Yuki D
title: Have fun in a safe and family-size environment!
original_content: We enjoyed our climbing, deep water soloing and trekking activities very much thanks to the dynamic, safety-conscious team! They were very adaptable (could pay in euros, exchange some dollars), gave good pieces of advice while climbing, brought us to spots adapted to our climbing level and not crowded. The deep water soloing was adapted both to beginners and confident climbers. Be on time (or they will leave without you :p)! Thanks again :)

author: Rockycorners
title: The highlight of my trip
original_content: Came to Cat Ba Island hoping to deep water solo cause it looks so fun, and I was not disappointed.  I travelled solo, but lucky for me Cat Ba Climbing managed to find three other people so we could do the half-day activity (6 Jun 2018). The guides, Adrian and Robin, were professional, helpful, and great climbers - They ensured our safety and recommended routes to cater to everyone's different climbing abilities. Our group ended up climbing till the sun set and we couldn't see the rock/route. The boat ride back to the harbour in the dark was smooth, quiet and peaceful. Overall, it was an incredible experience and I recommend it to anyone who wants to try something new!

author: Andy C
title: Amazing Time!! Good People Running an Honest Business!
original_content: I went deep water soloing with Mr. Zoom and had a blast. Their guides Adrian and Chao (aka Gecko) speak English and are extremely helpful / fun. We all went out to dinner afterward too.Mr. Zoom runs an honest business. It's a pity they can't offer access to certain crags in the guidebook because of the way Asia Outdoors likes to conduct business, but Mr. Zoom was able to take us to gorgeous DWS destinations not in the guidebook. I've climbed for 7 years and across 6 continents, and I can confidently say Mr. Zoom's gear and safety is top notch.10 out of 10 would climb with Mr. Zoom and his guides again!
drawbacks: can't offer access to certain crags
highlights: guides Adrian and Chao are extremely helpful / fun
gear and safety is top notch
practical_tips: go with Mr. Zoom and his guides

author: Vera S
title: So much fun!! And great price too
original_content: They are professional and such great people that you cannot not have a great time with them. You can really see how much they love climbing and they go out of their way to make sure you enjoy it as much as they do. Thank you guys!
highlights: enjoy it as much as they do

author: agtravels2018
title: Cat Ba Climbing
original_content: I went to Cat Ba Island hoping to climb. The day before I arrived, my climbing guide canceled that I was scheduled with. I reached out to Cat Ba Climbing, they responded quickly and said the group needed one more person but they would try to help. I was desperate and explained “Please, I just want to climb, can me and my friend pay the additional amount?” They were happy to arrange it, but still tried to get another climber. The next day my friend was sick and I showed up solo saying, I know you need at least 3 but it’s just me... I paid the trip cost happily, (which was fair, and they even lowered the price from the additional amount) and spent the day with two amazing guides. They were incredibly fun, safe, and experienced. I felt like I was climbing with friends, and was so happy they found a way to make the day happen. After climbing the staff genuinely wanted to hang out and share a meal and fun. The experience was so positive, if you want to climb with *climbers* as guides, I 100% booking with them- they make it so personalized to your style!
practical_tips: book with Cat Ba Climbing for personalized climbing experience

author: Khabiri
title: Deep water solo half day
original_content: It was great! They took good care of us and were accommodating to different skill levels in the group. A highlight of our trip for sure!
highlights: They took good care of us
A highlight of our trip for sure!

author: Prairiepancake
title: Great shop
original_content: Went on a climbing trip to Vietnam and didn't realize how New of a sport it was in the country. By just taking your sport rack and thinking you can just go climb anywhere you might be disappointed. But don't fret because the climbing shops on cat ba are very accommodating and with a simple skills test and some passes to the climbing areas you can enjoy the comfort of climbing the beautiful limestone karst's. I have to give the utmost credit to these shops for the effort they have put in to making climbing a positive impact to the tourism industry in a place that doesn't quite understand why you would just climb up rock faces for no reason. I highly recommend dealing with cat ba climbing if you are ever on the island.

author: Stefan D
title: Deep water soloing
original_content: Our first time climbing outdoors. So beginners with a little experience. We really enjoyed the half day trip, our guides were lovely and very knowledgeable. Climbing in a beautiful setting with 5 others, a few different routes to suit all levels. I think you would get more out of this with more experience but plenty to keep us entertained. We had a really good experience and would definitely recommend.

author: Jana K
title: The best experience from Cat Ba
original_content: We took the 1/2 deep water solo and it was just perfect! If you like climbing or if you want to just try go for it! Don’t be scared that there is not enought time for climbing during the 1/2 day. There is space for everybody! Mr. Zoom is very friendly and nice person and always makes sure everyone is happy!!! Thank you once again!
highlights: Mr. Zoom is very friendly and nice person

author: dwapril
title: Best thing I did in Cat Ba!
original_content: This was by far the best trip I did on Cat Ba island (deep water solo climbing). The instructors were all great - very patient and supportive as this was my first time trying this activity! Couldn't recommend it anymore!

author: Sara F
title: Great climbing for all!
original_content: Cat Ba Climbing was the most friendly pack of people you can meet! Jade was very helpful and accommodating when we booked the tour, and Adrian and Theo were great climbing instructors. It's a great activity even when it rains, the cliffs are overhanging but still offer both vertical and slab climbing. Good for both beginners and more advanced climbers. Awesome surroundings and just beautiful altogether. Highly recommended!
practical_tips: good for both beginners and more advanced climbers
great activity even when it rains

author: Jamie M
title: Rock Climbing Paradise
original_content: Spent a week in Cat Ba, and Mr. Zoom and his wonderful staff took us to so many beautiful valley crags, deep water solo crags and pointed us in the right direction for a great meal. They really put in the effort to show us routes which were challenging for us, and even during Vietnamese National holidays they secured a basket boat to take us out to streak lightning. More than just a tour company, these are great people who treat you like family.
highlights: showed us routes which were challenging for us
secured a basket boat to take us out to streak lightning
practical_tips: go to Mr. Zoom and his wonderful staff for a great tour experience
ask for routes that are challenging for you

author: michaelzhangcheng
title: A wonderful group of guides and climbers that makes Cat Ba feel like home
original_content: After showing up in Cat Ba with no climbing partner, I made fast friends with the all of the staff and climbers at Cat Ba Climbing and started my week with the half day tour. Hidden Valley was an incredible crag with many easy and challenging routes, and the half day tour was extremely well run and efficient. Everyone got to climb more than 10+ routes each, packing the tour with value!Even after the tour was over, one of the guides (a handsome swede named Adrian) stayed back with me to work on some more challenging routes. Despite the tour being over, he spent time showing me the harder routes and giving me beta. We ended climbing together every day for the next 3 days. (It's OK, we always wore socks).Cat Ba Climbing also acts as a nexus for traveling climbers to hang out, network, and find partners. I met a couple more wonderful people over the next few days, and got a lot of great climbing in, while having dinner every night with the Cat Ba Climbing crew. I became so attached to the climbing community here that I checked out of my much nicer accommodations in order to stay at the hostel with the other climbers and staff.This place is exactly what I hope for and expect from the best of the climbing community. Friendship through a shared love for climbing.
practical_tips: stay at the hostel with the other climbers and staff

author: Lucy H
title: Great range of routes, brilliant people
original_content: My friend and I had a great time climbing for half a day in hidden valley. There was a really good range of routes suitable for beginners and experienced climbers alike. The rock is really nice and not polished at all, and they kept setting up harder routes throughout the day as we completed easier ones. Shout out to the lovely Jade for being so encouraging!
highlights: Good range of routes for beginners and experienced climbers
practical_tips: Go early to climb harder routes

author: tvigijs
title: I want to go back
original_content: Best time of my two weeks Vietnam trip was with these guys - amazing team and very friendly people. I did toprope climbing, tried deep water solo and had a trek and changed my travel plans to stay one evening longer  because I just didn't want to leave..The company is rather small which means personalised approach and not too big groups. That also means booking couple of days in advance is recommended (especially for deep water solo).All levels of climbing are suitable, and beginners will be very well taken care of.
practical_tips: book couple of days in advance

author: Nico A
title: Amazing deep water solo
original_content: I had tried DWS before, but this one was by far a much better experience!!They have different grade of Boulder problems to try on the DWS spot (from 4 and 5 until 6c),you can try the same route several times if you keep falling, and every time you try again you start from the boat so your hands are dry and not slippery. The team was amazing, we all had a great time!!Thank you so much cat ba climbing team!!
highlights: Different grade of Boulder problems to try
practical_tips: Try the same route several times if you keep falling
Start from the boat to keep hands dry

author: Emelie U
title: Fantastic first rockclimbing experience!
original_content: We did the half day rock climbing with Cat Ba Climbing and I have zero complaints! Me and my friends were thinking of doing it with Asia outdoor at first, but as it was fully booked we decided to go this place instead and I do not regret it! It’s a small company with 5-6 employees, everyone very friendly, fun and has a great passion for climbing. Jade, Theo and Adrian were amazing! The climbing was excellent and we did a lot of it, good for both beginners and the ones that are bit more experienced. The best thing is that the groups are really small, which makes the experience and the atmosphere so much better. Would definitely recommend.
practical_tips: book in advance to avoid fully booked
consider small group sizes for better experience

author: Saga B
title: Superb!!
original_content: We did a half day top rope course and had such a blast! Three instructors with six customers - which meant A LOT of climbing per person. Adrian, Jade and Teo were great instructors! Safe and fun routes too. I really recommend it!

author: Julien S
title: Awesome time
original_content: We had an amazing time on this trip, they took us to some awesome climbing spots, and were really accommodating to everyone's skill level. Even if you just want to hang out on the boat I would highly recommend it over any of the other tour services. Really beautiful, fun, and relaxing.

author: tseyong
title: Great climbing in Cat Ba
original_content: Took us out to Hidden Valley after weather prohibited climbing on the beach. Jade and Theo were awesome and appreciate their help in convincing my daughter to climb!
highlights: help in convincing my daughter to climb

author: groff2018
title: Graham
original_content: I went to CatBa climbers after being recommended them by some fellow climbers in Vietclimb (Hanoi). I had an amazing time and did both deep water solo and a day of climbing at hidden valley. They are one of the two options for climbing tours on CatBa but they have a very local and friendly vibe. I wanted to do a third day and they knew it and went as far to come get me from my hotel in the morning when they had enough confirmed guests ! Highly recommend !
practical_tips: go to CatBa climbers for climbing tours

author: Sammy W
title: Great day of climbing
original_content: Had a wonderful day out climbing with Adrian from Sweden and a gentleman from France whose name escapes me.  They were very professional, enthusiastic, and really gave our group- three of us- a special tailor made experience.  It was my first day of outdoor climbing and they provided the right amount of soft coaching with motivation to give you that drive to push yourself to the limits.  Safety protocol was stringently observed at all times and they were even patient while I ached my way through a climb that was well above my grade level.  Had a great day out!  Thank you!
practical_tips: go with a guide who can provide a special experience
be prepared for a challenging climb

author: Youri A
title: Best Climbing place ever in Asia !!!
original_content: Cat Ba Climbing it’s a wonderful place to stay and climb.They got good dorm and private room very cheap, always hot water for the shower at night when it’s get cold ! Here the staff is fabulous, they will bring you to some awesome places to climb (on the mountains and on Deep water solo), to trek, kayak ... you will just visit the all Island with them ! If you spend longer time with them they will also show you the good places to eat in Cat Ba Island, well, this 10 days trip here was just amazing for me, I definitely recommend this place ! Cheers
practical_tips: spend longer time with the staff to get more recommendations

author: asafho3
title: My best experience in Cat Ba
original_content: We went with Cat Ba Climbing for both the half day trek and the half day rock climbing. The trek in the gidden valley was beautiful and quiet, not crowded at all (we were the only group) unlike the other treks in the national park, where all other companies go to. Cat Ba climbing are the only ones to hike in the hidden valley. The real gem though is the bakery at the end of each visit to the hidden valley! The best croissants we've had!The rock climbing was amazing and challenging. Different routes for all levels, you finish the half day when your hands are numb. The staff was kind and professional. Cat Ba Climbing made my stay in cat ba unforgettable!
practical_tips: Go with Cat Ba Climbing for a unique experience
Try the bakery at the end of the hidden valley trek

author: Toni H
title: Best Crew Best Climb Best Everything
original_content: We did 3 tours ( and a lot of Buddha Belly Evenings ) with the guys from Cat Ba Climbing and were soooo happy. In fact we stayed longer on Cat Ba just because of them. The legendary Mr. Zoom and his team are the best if you look for a place to go climbing and not feel like a customer but like a friend. Had the best time. We love you guys!!! Thank you for everything!
highlights: Legendary Mr. Zoom and his team
practical_tips: Go to Cat Ba Climbing for a great experience

author: Jennifer B
title: So cool!!
original_content: I went deep water solo climbing today for the first time! I have indoor climbed before but never outside. The guides were very helpful and safety oriented which was wonderful. I did a half day and I loved It!

author: Kim T
title: Amazing first experience
original_content: We went in a small group to the secret valley and had such an amazing time. Our guide was super helpful and enthusiastic. Safety came first, but fun was the name of the game. I've never climbed before but by the end of the session I was able to experience the full exhilaration of climbing. Maybe now I know why my niece likes climbing so much. One tip if you're like me and mosquitos find you irresistible - bring the deet spray!
highlights: guide was super helpful and enthusiastic
able to experience the full exhilaration of climbing

author: EddieShimshit
title: Grate climbing day with grate guys
original_content: Went with 4 kids for a climbing day at the secret valley.We had a real fun day, climbing from beginners and went up all the way to 25-30 meters wall (looks much higher...).The guys are professionals, very nice and fun (“F” for fun 😉).We finished the day with climbing to s view point high above the bay with a spectacular view of the bay.

author: Alexander H
title: Do the Deep Water Soloing + Kayaking Tour!!
original_content: We did the Full Day Tour with DWS and Cayaking, and it was one (if not THE) highlight of our Vietnam trip.It startet with Deep Water Soloing, that's basically climbing on the beautiful rocks of Halong Bay. You don't need a rope because you just jump (or drop) into the sea. We had beginners as well as more experienced climbers in our group and Jade and Theo knew the right routes for every skill level. It was totally amazing!! The boat tour to the climbing spot took about 30 min and led through the amazing scenery of Halong Bay. The tour included lunch on a floating house, which was very good! We then spent the afternoon kayaking. Therefore, the boat took a further into Halong Bay where we then got on kayaks. The kayak tour took as through beautiful parts of Halong Bay and Jade+Theo guided us into amazingly quit lagoons. Don't miss this tour when you're on Cat Ba Island! Forget all the other boat tours (which just take you around!). You will see a lot of Halong Bay while taking the boat to the climbing and kayaking spots, so that the tour somehow includes sightseeing in Halong Bay.But the climbing is just amazing! And Jade and Theo make the day simply perfect!
practical_tips: Forget all the other boat tours

author: Joe K
title: DWS / Lead climbing
original_content: Emailed the company before we had even decided if we would come to Cat Ba to go climbing . Spoke to Jade via email. She couldn’t have been more helpful. Her emails explained everything and it was easy to book . We did a half day deep water solo which was excellent. It catered for everyone in the group . I have done quite a lot of climbing and am quite happy to jump of huge rocks where as my girlfriend is quite the opposite . I didn’t feel like I couldn’t do big jumps and she didn’t feel like she had to. It was a brilliant experience and we got to see Mr Zooms floating guest house and have a beer at the end of the day. Yan was a brilliant guide and really helped my  Alex with her fear of jumping in. The next day we went rock climbing at Hidden Valley which is beautiful . It has so many different grades so something for everyone . Beginner or expert . I did some lead climbing and felt like I was in very safe hands and was shown some exciting routes in my grade range . Theo the French climbing botanist was brilliant . He was funny safe and knowledgeable. Alex did some top roping and really enjoyed herself. All in all we really enjoyed the two days and highly recommend these guys .  Thank you .
highlights: catered for everyone in the group
practical_tips: ask for Jade or Yan as guides

author: M0ny_75
title: Very friendly and professional staff, amazing climbing and boat trip off the beaten track!
original_content: First I went on the half day rock climbing tour, it was amazing! The guides were very knowledgeable and explained everything very nicely and professionally (in English and in French). At first I didn't really know what to expect, but even for total beginners, it was no problem, as they took care of everything and made the whole tour feel very safe and fun (a lot of good advices and encouragements!). Hidden Valley is a beautiful place where we could relax in the hammocks and play with the slackline when not climbing! There were many different levels of difficulty of climbing for everyone. It was a small group with many guides, so everyone managed to climb 6 or 7 routes in a half day!The next day we did the private boat trip, so no big boat full of tourist, but a more authentic experience, with a visit of the captain's family floating house, with a delicious lunch on the floating house and a visit of thei fish farm!We did some kayaking in a peaceful lagoon all by ourselves and helped cleaning the bay (so much garbage!) as part of a cleaning contest the guides organised (prizes were pretty shells ^^). I though it was a great eco-friendly idea!I also spent a lot of time at the office, hanging out with the cool staff, drinking lots of free tea, having fun with their indoor small climbing wall and talking about everyone's travels and tips! We went for dinner all together sometimes and got lots of good info on hotels and what to see in Vietnam.Thanks again for the awesome time, I really felt as part of a family and it definitely was my holidays highlight! Good luck with everything! I will definitely come back!! :D

author: stian o
title: Amazing company, climbing and guides!
original_content: We decided to go with Cat Ba Climbing instead of Asia Outdoors, because AO only seem to offer mass top-rope tours for complete beginners or expensive equipment rental to go on your own. CBC offers a more tailored experience, and even though we are experienced climbers, we still  learned new teqnuices and skills from the very including and skillfull guides. No matter if you are a complete beginner or a very seasoned climber, they will make the tour fit your needs. We had a great lunch at a local familys floating house, where we also stayed the night (xinh floating house, sleep here!).  You can book a room on booking.com or through CBC, who can take you directly from climbing to the floating house. Very easy! The CBC office is also a great place to just hang out, drink some tea and talk climbing with likeminded people. The whole experience was one of the highlights during a 3 month trip i asia.
drawbacks: AO only seem to offer mass top-rope tours for complete beginners or expensive equipment rental

Moreover, being the low season, there were very few boats, and this made the landscapes even more enjoyable. author: Winnie Jane
title: Magical Views, Crowded Attractions
original_content: Ha Long Bay itself was beautiful. The limestone formations looked almost magical to me, so picturesque and unlike anything I’ve seen before. Cruising through the bay and seeing all those unique rock formations was definitely the highlight of the trip.After that, we went to Luon Cave. It was very crowded, although I understand that it’s one of the popular tourist attractions in Ha Long Bay. Still, it was a fun experience taking the boat through the low natural tunnel over the water and entering the enclosed lagoon surrounded by limestone cliffs. It was something different and definitely worth experiencing at least once.Next, we visited Sung Sot Cave (Surprise Cave). The cave was huge, and there was quite a long walk through it. The cave itself was beautiful, but unfortunately, it was also very crowded. With so many tourists stopping to take photos and blocking the pathways, it was quite difficult to really enjoy the surroundings. You also need to watch your steps as you walk through the cave.We also stopped at Ti Top Island. Personally, I didn’t find the beach to be the kind of place where you can relax, swim, sunbathe and enjoy some peace and quiet. It was packed with people, with many just standing around taking photos, so it felt a little awkward and crowded rather than relaxing.Overall, witnessing Ha Long Bay was a great experience and I’m glad I got to see it. The natural scenery is truly beautiful and something I won’t forget. However, if you ask me whether I would go again, I would probably have to think twice, mainly because the crowds made it difficult to fully enjoy some of the attractions.
drawbacks: Difficult to enjoy surroundings due to many tourists
Need to watch steps while walking through the cave
highlights: Cruising through Ha Long Bay and seeing unique rock formations
Taking the boat through the low natural tunnel over the water and entering the enclosed lagoon
Witnessing Ha Long Bay's natural scenery
practical_tips: Be prepared for crowds and long walks

author: Jean-Emmanuel R
title: A place of great beauty, unforgettable
original_content: The postcard and the most iconic place in Vietnam. A landscape of great beauty that you will be able to discover during a 1 to 3-day cruise that you will have no trouble booking online or directly through an agency or your accommodation in Hanoi.If prices start at around thirty euros, it is better to opt for a two-day, one-night cruise and choose a luxury ship. The rates remain reasonable (around €200/person all-inclusive) and the experience will be unforgettable.While staying in Vietnam in July 2026 (during the rainy season and potentially typhoons), we were strongly hesitant to book this cruise. In the end, even if there was a generally cloudy sky and 2-3 showers during the stay, this does not take anything away from the beauty of the site. We even had the right to some beautiful sunny spells. No worries to have regarding safety because in case of rough seas, the authorities prohibit navigation in the bay.
practical_tips: Book online or through an agency

author: sannamoo
title: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that's a must-see
original_content: Halong Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in northern Vietnam, is famous for its emerald waters and nearly 2,000 limestone karst islands that rise dramatically from the sea. Known as the "descending dragon," it is celebrated globally for its breathtaking landscapes, natural caves, and floating fishing villages. Highlights include impressive caverns such as Sung Sot Cave and scenic viewpoints such as Ti Top Island. We visited on a day trip from Hanoi, and the experience was eye-opening. Although popular spots were crowded and smokers were frequently encountered despite clear no-smoking signs, the site's overall beauty and uniqueness make it a must-see tourist destination with potential for further improvement.

author: Salem E
title: Breathtaking nature and sustainable beauty
original_content: Ha Long Bay is Vietnam's iconic destination, famed for its stunning natural scenery and pristine waters. The vast ocean and dramatic limestone karsts are visible even from space—and it's impressive to see nature and development coexist so harmoniously.

author: Eadie Duo

author: Hunfredo D
title: Harmony between nature and development

author: Webster Liechtenstein
title: Essential vietnam stop, despite the crowds

author: Ale
title: Postcard scenarios, nightmare tourism
original_content: Over the years Vietnam has learned to enhance certain areas and to “squeeze” certain tourist sites; the latter is the case of Ha Long Bay, one of the most visited natural sites in the nation, and, precisely because Instagrammabilissimo, over the years has seen an increasingly mass tourism.The bay deserves, as the many islands that make up the scenery deserve, but the amount of small cruise ships and boats is really exaggerated, never seen such a thing.Organized tours almost always beat the usual routes, and Ha Long is among the first stops marked in them.Nice, but too many people take the magic away from these places. Try to visit the bay and the islands by bypassing the most popular tourist area
drawbacks: Too many people take the magic away from these places
Exaggerated amount of small cruise ships and boats
practical_tips: Try to visit the bay and the islands by bypassing the most popular tourist area

author: Tobias Lam
title: Stunning scenery & activities

An overnight cruise was one of my best travel decisions—waking up surrounded by serene, majestic scenery is truly unforgettable. Beyond sightseeing, you can kayak, explore Sung Sot Cave, or climb Titop Island for panoramic views. Pro tip: always book with a reputable operator for the best service and safety.

author: Heath William

author: bfvermont
title: Sadly the Venice of Southeast Asia
original_content: The photo of the traditional Chinese junk is hardly an apt image of what you will see. That is if the pollution does not obscure your view with a steady level of haze, matched by an orange sun in the sky. Clear signs of heavy particulate pollution. As for other boats, yes, there are many. I counted 30 when we docked overnight, including the party boat whose music we could hear. Another person on our cruise had been to Halong Bay 20 years ago when it indeed was a quiet and tranquil spot. Today I would call it the Venice of Southesat Asia, overrun with tourists and highly polluted.

author: P M
title: Alarming decline in Halong Bay
original_content: Halong bay has been ruined - words cannot give justice to the decline in this area over the past 20 years since my last visit - over tourism  is killing this pristine wonder of the world and frankly I found my trip to the caves and islands depressing - as a apart from the ridiculous amount of boats and people swarming each site / the grey water and skies / it now presents as a bleak Chaotic over crowded and sad version of its former self- there is no sun - it’s blocked by the polluted sky - the emerald water is gone it’s now also grey / I specifically wanted to photograph the region but there were no clouds or contrasting backdrops / everything is s misty grey - what a terrible shame - I witnessed 2 boat crashes at island stops such is the traffic jam of excessive boats and tourists all day - it’s a tragedy

author: Isabella W
title: 2d/1n trip: Overtourism, polluted water, too many cruise ships
original_content: First of all: the boat, the service, the food, communication with Lucas, the transport was a 11/10 everything was outstanding!The reason why we weren't able to enjoy the trip is that the overtourism and the pollution is so so bad, that we felt so bad being part of the problem. When the ship is moving you'll already see the plastic floating around now and then, but as soon as you anchor for the night all we were able to breathe was the scent of petroleum and we had to close our door as the sound of the motor of the ships was too noisy. The pollution in the water is in such stark contrast to the beauty of the landscape, it is really a crime that such a unique natural place is not better protected.We left feeling disappointed — not because of the staff or the service, which were amazing — but because the environmental situation overshadowed everything else. Ha Long Bay deserves stronger protection and more responsible tourism.
practical_tips: consider the environmental impact of tourism

author: Walter Z
title: Totally overflowing and little idyll
original_content: Halong Bay probably belongs on the top list of all visitors to Vietnam, which is now unfortunately shown by ‘overtourism’. Yeah, and I'm one of too many. The bay, often depicted in the pictures as a tranquil and picturesque seascape, is not only completely overcrowded, but unfortunately also very polluted and severely affected by the emerging economic performance in the region. On arrival, you look out over high-rises of the nearby town, between the picturesque rocks anchor tankers and drilling platforms, and hundreds of excursion boats tour from one bay to the other. At the popular stalactite cave, you stand in line for 2 hours, accompanied by diesel smoke and the scent of wastewater wafting over the beach. I had booked a round trip with several stops, but did not leave the excursion steamer after the second stop, luckily there was enough cool beer on board to drink the whole thing nicely. Once and never again!
practical_tips: book a round trip with several stops
consider the time of day to avoid crowds

author: Tasha H
title: Halong Bay without the typical cruise
original_content: We visited Hạ Long Bay as part of a cruise stop on Holland America’s Westerdam, cruising into and out of the bay rather than doing a separate Hạ Long Bay boat or day cruise. Even without a traditional tour among the limestone karsts, the sail-in itself was a highlight, with calm waters and scenic views as the ship approached port.After docking, we took the cruise shuttle into town, which dropped us near Vincom Plaza Hạ Long. From there, it was easy to explore on foot. We visited Starbucks Vincom Hạ Long (perfect for festive Christmas photos), wandered through the nearby parks and waterfront areas, including Cầu đi bộ, Công viên Lán Bè Skywalk, and Công viên Hoa Hạ Long, and stopped at WinMart for a look at local groceries.This felt like a relaxed, everyday view of Hạ Long city life, rather than a sightseeing-heavy experience. It was flat, walkable, and easy to do at your own pace, making it a good option for families, anyone wanting a low-effort port day, or those who have already done a traditional Hạ Long Bay cruise in the past.While you won’t see the famous limestone formations up close without a dedicated tour, this is still a pleasant and stress-free way to experience Hạ Long as a cruise port, with cafes, parks, shopping, and waterfront views all close together.

author: Alex J
title: You do not need to go on a cruise, to see the sights of this wonderful place!
original_content: We were on a conducted group tour of Vietnam and Cambodia, organised by the Australian tour company, Holiday Max.  As part of the itinerary, a "Ha Long Bay cruise" was included.  I had heard so much about Ha Long bay, and I was really looking forward to it, but the experience was a huge disappointment.  Let me explain:  We left our hotel in Hanoi, after breakfast, and drove to Ha Long Bay, reaching around early afternoon. Our group of 25 then transferred to the  "cruise ship", by a motor boat.  The "cruise ship" was anchored in the bay.   We made two excursions from the "ship", one the same day, after lunch, to see some rock formations, and one the next day, after breakfast to see a cave.  So, we were on the "cruise ship" for less than 24 hours, and I don't recall the "ship" moving during that period.  As the "Ha Long Bay Cruise" was part of our itinerary, we just accepted it, but if I was planning an independent tour of Vietnam, I would not do it this way.  In other words, if it is part of a conducted tour, as it was in our case....you do not have a choice.  BUT.....if you are going independently to Vietnam, my advice is DO NOT GO ON A HA LONG BAY CRUISE!  There are many wonderful things to see, in and around Ha Long Bay, but you do not need to get on to a "cruise ship" to see these sights.  It is MUCH better for you to stay in a decent hotel in a nearby town, and get the hotel to organise a guide, with a small motorboat, to take you around the bay to see the karst formations, and various other sights like the caves, rock formations, etc.... There is plenty to see in and around Ha Long Bay, but getting on board a "cruise ship" is NOT the best way to see it.   To recap:  it is NOT NECESSARY to actually sleep for one night (or two nights) in a rather cramped cabin on board a "cruise ship" and eat pretty ordinary food, to see the sights in and around Ha Long bay.  Much better to stay in a hotel, and go around Ha Long bay on your own!   In short, the damn "cruise" was a huge disappointment.  I intend going to Vietnam again, and I intend staying in a hotel, and see the sights in and around Ha Long bay, on my own.
practical_tips: stay in a decent hotel in a nearby town
get the hotel to organise a guide, with a small motorboat

title: Halong Bay: Romantic Nature Escape
original_content: Halong Bay is simply magical, a world-class destination that is perfect for a romantic getaway.​The emerald waters and thousands of towering limestone karsts create a breathtaking, almost ethereal backdrop for couples looking for an unforgettable experience. The sheer scale and raw nature of the bay, a UNESCO World Heritage site, will leave you speechless—it truly feels like stepping into a painting.​But it’s not just about the view; there are countless activities to enjoy together. Cruising on a traditional junk boat is an adventure in itself, especially waking up to the sunrise over the bay. You can spend your days kayaking through hidden lagoons, exploring stunning caves like Sung Sot (Surprise Cave), and trekking to the top of Titop Island for spectacular panoramic views. For a deeper dive into culture, you can visit floating fishing villages and see a way of life that has existed for centuries.​Whether you're relaxing on the sundeck with a cocktail, sharing a delicious Vietnamese meal on board, or simply watching the sunset paint the cliffs in gold, Halong Bay offers endless moments of intimacy and discovery. It's a journey filled with beauty, adventure, and a rich blend of nature and culture that will bring you closer. Highly recommended for any couple seeking a memorable escape.

author: Caroline WSL HYZ
title: Beautiful Halong Bay – Worth It, Just Eat Before You Go!
original_content: We did a Halong Bay day trip from the Peridot Gallery Classic Hotel in Hanoi, and it was stunning! The limestone cliffs and peaceful waters are unforgettable. We visited a pearl farm first, then boarded the cruise, and explored one of the caves—busy but beautiful.One lesson learned: don’t skip breakfast! I felt a bit seasick early on because I didn’t eat before the long bus ride and boat. The hotel serves a nice breakfast—take advantage of it!We chose a 5-star day cruise, and I highly recommend doing the same. It made a big difference in comfort—spacious seating, better food, and clean restrooms. It’s only a little more, but totally worth it.✅ Tip:	•	Eat something before departure	•	Bring motion sickness tablets just in case	•	Pay a bit extra for a premium boat—it really improves the experienceA long day, but absolutely worth it. Halong Bay lives up to the hype!

author: MauroMBrasilia
title: Only good if the boat is first
original_content: I did the tour where you sleep one night in the bay. It was very good but I got the feeling that it is only worth it if it is on a good level ship, since most of the time we are on board. The tour has only 3 stops of 1:30 hour each. In the first, there is the option of staying on a beach or climbing on a viewpoint overlooking the bay. It only gives time for one of these options. I did the mountain walk because the beach is crowded (all boats stop there) and it seemed to me not worth it. The second stop is the most beautiful because you visit a part of the bay that only has access through a hole in the rock and the entrance only and allowed by rowing boat (pay-part kayak option).  The third stop is in a cave on the second day. Beautiful and worth it. On board will be provided lunch, dinner and breakfast, in this order. So it has to be a ship with a good standard for the care to be satisfactory. I did on the ship Paradise Elegance and I recommend. Room and first-class boarding service. In the place where the boats stay overnight you can see boats of various levels. Some of them seemed precarious to me.
drawbacks: only worth it on a good level ship
practical_tips: go on a good level ship
consider the beach or viewpoint at the first stop

author: Avalon
title: Biggest disappointment of my Vietnam Trip
original_content: I thought this was going to be one of the highlights of my trip and instead was my biggest disappointment.  I envisioned sailing around the beautiful bay looking at the beautiful limestone formations.  Instead what I got was a 30 minute tender to my ship, whereby the ship moved for about 30 minutes and then dropped anchor until the following morning at which point we did have a nice visit on rowboats to the caves (the highlight of the 2 days).  However, once we returned to the ship, we then had another 30 minute tender back to shore.  If I had known then what I know now, at most I would have booked a day trip out.  The overnight portion of the trip was a total waste of money.The bay itself was very crowded with a LOT of other ships doing the exact same thing.  The water was quite polluted.  And there weren’t actually many interesting things to do on the ship itself. Hardly anyone showed up for the fishing activity on the ship where you simply dropped a pole into the water (and I never got the sense that we were going to catch any squid) and no one showed up for karaoke except for us.  The activities on the ship were basically a total bust for me.  In terms of the food, although we had a really nice lunch on the day we arrived, the rest of the meals were really subpar compared to all  the other meals we had in Vietnam.Overall, a huge disappointment.  If you feel that you must “tick it off your list”, I would recommend you do a day trip.
drawbacks: Overnight portion of the trip was a total waste of money

highlights: a nice visit on rowboats to the caves

author: Lia Moon
title: Overhyped, owercrowded, overpriced tourist trap - to be avoided by all means!
original_content: After visiting Halong Bay, I can honestly say it was one of the biggest travel disappointments of my Vietnam trip. While the limestone scenery is beautiful in photos, the actual experience feels extremely commercialized, overcrowded, and frankly, not worth the money or time.From the moment you arrive, it’s clear that Halong Bay has become a mass tourism machine. Hundreds of boats line up in the same areas, fighting for space. The “quiet” parts they promise on the tours? Filled with noise from other boats, tourists yelling, and diesel fumes. Any sense of peace or natural wonder gets drowned out quickly.The water, which looks stunning in pictures, is actually littered with plastic in many areas – a heartbreaking sight. Activities like kayaking and swimming, which should feel adventurous, end up feeling rushed, cramped, and at times, unsafe due to the sheer number of boats.To make it worse, many of the tours (even the “luxury” ones) are built around upselling you: overpriced drinks, packaged excursions to tacky caves or crowded beaches, and photo ops rather than real experiences. It all feels incredibly staged and soulless.Vietnam has so many other places where you can experience true beauty, authenticity, and peace – without the crowds, scams, and disappointment. Places like Ninh Binh (the “Halong Bay on land”), Phong Nha, or even the less-visited parts of the central coast offer stunning nature without feeling like a factory.Bottom line: Halong Bay might be a UNESCO World Heritage Site, but today it’s mostly a tourist trap. Save yourself the hassle – your time and money are much better spent elsewhere in Vietnam.
drawbacks: not worth the money or time

author: arpitam
title: One of the best cruising experiences: Off the beaten track
original_content: A serene experience of cruising through the Bai Tu Long bay. This route was chosen to avoid the general crowding that happens in the Lan Ha bay route. The weather was not sunny so we all could sit comfortably in the sun deck and enjoy the smooth sail through the limestone mounds.  We started off with the safety briefing by the tour manager. By then the crew set up table for the 7 course lunch all served on the table. The menu was elaborate and the food was delicious. After some relaxing time, we set off for a visit to the Vung Vieng floating fishing village. It takes around 30-40 mins to visit the fishing village. So if you are used to kayaking (2 person/kayak) you can opt for it else it is better to go with the bamboo boat (upto 6 ppl) ride. The journey is pleasant. We finished off with the pearl harvesting and demonstration.The sunset party could not happen due to the absence of sun. However, people went happy with the "happy hours". This was followed by cooking class by Mr. Peter "Vietnamese fried spring roll made by many countries". The day ended with a luxurious 7 course meal at dinner. Some of us were fishing enthusiasts who tried their hands on squid fishing at night. The 2nd day started at 6 am with a TaiChi session at the sun deck. Such a wonderful way to start your day, unless of course you want to sleep late and miss the morning fresh air and be surrounded by lofty hills. After a quick breakfast with traditional Vietnamese pho we set off for a short hiking to the Thien Canh Son cave. We need to hike about 90 high steps along steep mountain path to reach. The path is stone paved and very well maintained. The cave has a  very narrow entrance and tall people have to mind their head and legs. While climbing down, which I found rather difficult than climbing up, we diverted to a hidden and beautiful beach. Finally we returned to the cruise as it was time for checkout. Meanwhile the crew served us a wonderful lunch before we disembarked at the international cruise port at Halong.This will be a memorable event for all of us. We would certainly recommend this to all fellow travellers.
drawbacks: The sunset party could not happen due to the absence of sun
highlights: A serene experience of cruising through the Bai Tu Long bay

author: VieGo Travel
title: Nice Bay
original_content: By just some clicks on a website, you will easily see any information you need (cruise type, cabin size, amenities, anything). Anytime, anywhere, so convenient, right?BUT, the reason I told you to seek for a reliable agency is nowadays, there are hundreds of travel agencies want to sell your services. Not all of them can guarantee the quality they promote and advertise. Among hundreds of cruises in Halong Bay, this local can tell you that not 100% of them can serve you satisfied. Depend on many elements such as how long did the cruise run, how good their staffs are, how often the cruise maintains their facilities, etc. the quality of different cruises is different. Don’t choose too cheap prices, as you know, you buy cheap you buy twice, if not be careful, low quality and unsafe cruises (facilities, services, foods, etc.), miscellaneous additional charges will not be explicitly announced. Otherwise, the cheap prices you see might have hidden additional fees or charges, so cheap might become not cheap at all.

author: BabyBayard
title: Looks 10, Feels 3
original_content: No fault of the uniquely fascinating views, visiting and cruising Bai Tu Long Bay in late summer, early rainy season is a grueling ordeal if you are unaccustomed to saturation humidity and unvarying smoldering temperatures. The upshot is an oddly cognitive dissonant experience, with your eyes screaming magnificent beauty all around you, but your limp, sweat-soaked body whimpering like it's enduring a non-stop open-air sauna. When I look at the transcendent photos I took now, safely home, I marvel at how miserable I was at the time I gathered my waning strength to click the shutter. My recommendation: go, yes, but in the driest, coolest season.
practical_tips: go in the driest, coolest season

author: Steven U
title: Ha Long Bay

I awoke to watch the sun rise on my 60th birthday there and cannot think of anywhere more perfect to be for that occasion.

author: Dianne
title: The experience will not disappoint
original_content: In January, we completed a 3-day cruise around Bai Tu Long Bay. This wonderful trip exceeded our expectations – an outstanding experience from beginning to end and definitely value for money as no corners are cut in delivering such a quality experience. Very efficient and courteous hotel pickup and a smooth and comfortable transfer to Ha Long Bay where we were greeted by our tour leader – the truly amazing Long. Our cabin was spacious, tastefully decorated, a very comfortable bed with the best part being the clear and unobstructed views. If you didn’t feel like participating in any of the organised activities (although do not miss Jelly’s cocktail demonstration), lying back on the bed reading a book and gazing out the window at the extraordinary scenery will be a memory I keep for ever. Our meals were fantastic as were all the staff. Many companies offer a 3-day package however; you need to look carefully at their itinerary to ensure you do not end up just completing the same circuit and perhaps even needing to change boat on the second night.

author: AngelaKyn
title: Heartbreaking
original_content: We purposefully selected a “green” tour/boat as we had heard the Bay is becoming more polluted and unfortunately this is true. Its obvious as travelers we seek out the beautiful and the once in a life time experiences, but we’re killing the Bay and it’s beyond littered with everything from plastic bags, to kids juice boxes, straws, water bottles and toilet paper (yes lots of toilet paper) and loads of styrofoam.  Indochina Junk are doing their part by stressing the importance of being green to save the Bay - but it was heartbreaking to float for hours in nothing but trash.  I highly advise you DO NOT SWIM IN THE WATER!!!!  I would also advise you skip this altogether and visit other parts of Vietnam until more effort across ALL the boat tours step up to make a difference.

author: JocelynRochelle
title: Great service, amazing time
original_content: My adult daughter and I booked the 3 days, 2 night trip; which was arranged through our hotel in old quarter Hanoi. We were picked up by a/c bus for about about a 3 hour drive. We both thoroughly enjoyed our stay.  The room was very comfortable, and quiet with a large shower and a  balcony.  All of the service and meals were excellent.  We are vegetarians and had no problem finding food to meet our need.  I am also a great lover of good red wine, and I was able to find that as well.  Drinks are an additional cost, but after a week in Hanoi, this was the first time I easily found good wine.  When we woke up the next morning, we were surprised to find that we were the only ones at breakfast (which we were told was later on the second day).  Everyone else was packing to leave, as we were the only ones staying the additional night! We wondered what we were missing that everyone else was checking out.  Their loss, as day 2 was simply amazing!  We were transferred to a smaller boat where 2 other couples were ( also the only people staying 2 nights on their boat).  We spent a couple hours with a guide kayaking through Bai Tu Long and going to a private beach for awhile to swim. We went back to the smaller boat for an amazing lunch (More vegetarian options). The only other people we saw all day was the occasional fisherman. Very peaceful and great opportunity for photos.  But bring bug spray!  Lots of sand fly bites.  If you can arrange the 2 night trip, I highly recommend it. I have done a fair amount of travelling and stayed in some pretty amazing hotels. I have no complaints about this trip.

title: Smaller scale & less visitors-- but spectacular!
original_content: This Bay, with its 40 "islands/Karsts", is near the better know and much larger Ha Long Bay.  Its "National Park" has been designated an "Asian Heritage attraction" ... and, is ranked as the #1 attraction in the Ha Long Bay region, and, has been awarded TripAdvisor's "Certificate of Excellence".  It is much less crowded than Ha long Bay--- and is not as "overpowering"!!   "Experienced Travellers" find that, while it is "off the beaten track" it is every bit as beautiful!  Its definitely very worthwhile for those who appreciate the nature and serenity!I hope that this Review has been helpful!

I highly recommend this bay as compared to Halong Bay- which we heard was overpacked on the same day!The views and density of hills are about the same except the height might be less.

author: Jester0479
title: Great place but overvisited
original_content: Great views that you can see in few, if any, other places in the world. Good overnight cruise options with all kinds of excursions. Worth the trip up from Hanoi to visit for sure. I took a 2d1n cruise and am glad I did, as I enjoyed the easy pace and extra down time to relax on the boat, swim, kayak, and just chill for a couple days.But, don't be fooled by the crystal-clean air and water in those cover photos. That wasn't my experience anyway. The bay itself is beautiful and remote, but it is also a little polluted and crowded with boats, even in the farther reaches. The air seemed hazy, and that does obstruct the picturesque-ness of the views from the boat. Worth a visit, yes, but don't expect it to be the remote slice of pristine wilderness it perhaps once was.

author: David F
title: So much better than Halong Bay
original_content: I’m really glad I did my research on this part of our trip. Cruising in Bai Tu Long & not Halong Bay is to be recommended if you want to miss the masses. We stayed on Dagon Legend 2 which had a very high specification ( unlike many others which look as though they have had better days). The rooms are high quality with very comfortable beds. The service we received throughout the trip from all the staff was fantastic. Long was the main guide, spoke impeccable English & offered brilliant service through the trip, guiding us in the kayaks & in the local caves On the first day after a lovely lunch we traveled to Bai Tu Long & upon arrival we had the options to kayak ( great fun), swim or just rest around the junk. There are plenty of loungers to sit / lie on. The food was of a high quality ( probably to much !) & Phuong the head chef did a great job with his team. We were served at dinner in the pm by T- Small who was incredibly nice. The pm entertainment was run by the staff who played local instruments/ music - of note was Phong ( head housekeeper) who played a Viet guitar. On day 2 there is an earlyTai Chi class & then a visit to the local caves on one of the islands - very interestingIt’s really worth paying the premium to see this stunning part of Vietnam The one regret - only 1 night !

We did not see another boat close to us till the next morning when we neared a cave that we were going to explore. The staff on Dragon Legend was incredible. They paid attention to details. Surprised me with a cake and a gift for my birthday though it wasn't the reason for taking the cruise. They must have paid attention to the passport information we were asked to send in. Great food and great crew. Highly recommend touring Bai Tu Long Bay on Dragon Legend!

practical_tips: Choose Bai Tu Long Bay instead of Halong Bay for less crowds

title: UNESCO world heritage area on the “Red Dragon” Indochina junk
original_content: What a restorative and yet exhilarating trip with eight close friends and two new friends, on the Indochina Junk “Red Dragon”. Our ten berth boat was a 9 year old replica and very authentic. We enjoyed 2 nights and 3 days cruising from Ha Long Bay to the peaceful area of Bai Tu Long Bay, under the attentive and knowledgeable care of tour guide Mr Thi and crew. We enjoyed 7 local cuisine courses at lunch and dinner, on the upper open deck. We loved our guided kayaking to quiet lagoons and limestone caves. The seafood BBQ on the beach was fabulous. The weather gods were kind to us. The companies focus on Halong green is admirable to ensure eco sustainability. Well done. Highly recommend.

title: Completely overrated
original_content: In the low season (we visited in October), there was barely any tourist infrastructure available. For example, it was a real challenge to even find one restaurant that was open and could serve us some food. Moreover, there was nothing to do and the beaches were not kept clean.Initially, we wanted to spend 4 days there, however, we decided to leave the island after 1 day. Amongst others, the boat schedule was different to the high season and we were forced to wait for 5 hours at the harbor.To sum it all up, in our opinion, the island was not worth the journey to get there and the beaches looked very different (less spectular) than the pictures suggest.

author: Camper12670280459
title: Bad experience with squid fishing service.
original_content: My family and I rented a squid fishing boat. Price 1 million 7. Agree with the boat owner to fish for about 3 hours or if you're bored, it's okay to spend the night. But I only fished for 30 minutes, after the boat owner heard a phone call. I told my group that there was going to be a tornado, bad weather and we had to go home. Everyone knows that there are no tornadoes or bad weather. And it was confirmed by the people there. The boat owner accepted another group and went to pick up another group to get a new hoe. And lied to the group that we had to go ashore after less than 1 hour of fishing. What do you think?In this review, I want to let those who want to experience squid fishing services in Co To take precautions, and boat owners learn from the experience. You can't make a living doing tourism services. I lost a lot of customers, there won't be a second time.
drawbacks: Boat owner lied to the group
Boat owner accepted another group while we were still fishing
Boat owner didn't respect the agreed time
practical_tips: Take precautions when experiencing squid fishing services in Co To
Boat owners should learn from this experience

original_content: It's 50 km far from Van Don pier. nice place for relaxing and living far from the mordern life. There are 02 nice beaches (Van Chai is calm and clear when Hong Van beach is long with nice sand and strong waves). Should not miss seeing the sunrise from the Dragon nail stone area. The infrastructure of Co To is not good and need to be improved. Especially, the problem happen with electric in summer period.
drawbacks: The infrastructure of Co To is not good and need to be improved
The problem happen with electric in summer period
