practical_tips: Should not miss seeing the sunrise from the Dragon nail stone area

author: Candy C
title: Nice and beautiful Hong Van beach in Coto Island
original_content: We visited Coto island at the end of May, nice weather and less tourist that time. You should avoid to come in summer time from June - August, it will be crowed and weather is not nice at all. Renting a motorbike o visit around Island, we discovered a very beautiful beach on the island called Hong Van Beach- clean and free to relax there, only 15 minutes driving from town. Also you should not miss to visit Lighthouse where you can take overview of Coto Island

author: lien n
title: Memorable trip
original_content: Firstly, many people come to this place so the trip may be harder to travel there, I took one day to come and half of the day to come back to Hanoi. No booking room in advance, exhausted of sea sickness, at that time I regretted to come there, but luckily this people here so kind, one barber shop owner ̣(Tay Do) he allowed me to stay one night there and the next day his family accommodated one available room for guest.The first place I visited is Co To Reef; the air is extremely fresh. Water is so clean with vivid and various rocky formations; I can see through the shallow bottom. Though some visitors do not have high awareness, drink some bottle and throw rubbish here.The second place is Van Chay Beach, it is very funny and exciting with different activities. I wish I could see the dawn here, I used to  read one paragraph about the dawn in Co To, very beautiful and charming.The food here is special for seafood; But very expensive if you can not make a bargain e.g one kilogram how much?You must bring enough cash yourself if you dont want broke here because the ATM doesnt work well, and there is only one ATM at this island.
drawbacks: expensive if you can not make a bargain

author: Katie J
title: Unapologetically Vietnamese
original_content: Depending on the time of year you go, you'll either be greeted with sleepy rural local life or 'Vietnam on-holiday' karaoke party. Both of which are awesome in their own way. Westerners expect to be invited into family dinners on the beach, hustled into photos with teenagers and greeted with an enthusiastic welcome into your homestay. Seafood here is incredible and as fresh as can be. Stay in a basic beach hut on the waters edge - high season needs to be booked in advance, and hire a motorbike along the main strip when you first arrive to make the most of the island's lesser known parts (watch out for spiders weaving webs across your path in the back-country spots). Do your research and go with the flow. In bad weather there will be some trouble getting off the island so be flexible. Had an authentic and incredible time here which I will never forget.

author: Đỏ R
title: Great!
original_content: Great! the place that must come. Sea, sun, shine, sand, seafood... all deffirent. i will come back with my dear friend next chances
practical_tips: come back with my dear friend

author: Shane
title: DIRTY!
original_content: This island COULD be a real paradise, unfortunately it is affected by a common issue which plagues much of Vietnam's societies outlook on the environment- the lack of respect for their environment, nature and cleanliness. First I want to say that I really do like VN people. Love their good hearted nature. On Co To Island some are trying to make a difference by constructing new buildings to attract tourists. Unfortunately it's all about the tourist dollars vs environment. Buildings don't come before a clean environment. What they don't seem to realize is the goldmine they sit on! Co To could be an incredible island paradise. Nice sand beaches which could attract many and KEEP them her for a week or two at a time. Those same beaches are covered with garbage.....and I mean COVERED! I am not exaggerating when I say I saw three seperate pig carcasses on one beach, and even found a syringe and many used medication bottles washed up on shore. The beach was so covered in garbage that it was gross! We drove the whole island visiting the beaches and each one was much the same theme. We left after a day, it was that bad!Vietnam you have beautiful people and what could be a beautiful country. You need to change your attitudes about your environment and REALIZE that your environment comes before the dollar. Soon it will be so dirty and polluted that tourists will no longer come to visit and your children's futures will become limited. I write this in an effort to get the message across.....you have no where to go. Make a positive and beautiful change for your future.
drawbacks: Lack of respect for the environment, nature, and cleanliness
Garbage and pollution on the beaches
Pig carcasses and used medication bottles on the shore
practical_tips: Prioritize environmental cleanliness over tourist dollars

author: srihariananth
title: For friends/couples/solo . . .Rent a bike(be bold-explore Co To). For family-rent electric car(golf cart)
original_content: Wow ! ! !...great place to explore. As my title says....if you are going with friends OR SOLO or couples, try being bold and explore. If you chose a particular destination in Co To to go to and rent a bike take the roads which are not on google, just to explore. You wont get lost. . and you will find out the experience to be more adventurous. . .this is how we found out the lake from which water for daily needs for Co To is supplied from. Apart from off road experience, Co To offers good beaches, short treks like the dragon nail (Bai Bien Da Mong Rong) and bridge of rocks (Bai Da Cau my co to). Before going to Co To I had not planned a itenerary as I was somehow not able to find out much information from internet either due to lack of information or my search methodology was ineffective. Same applied to finding good hotels prior to leaving. Upon arriving at Co to, went to a restaurant for lunch and asked them about attractions and only then made a list of places. Co To Con, Bai Tam Hong Van, Bai Tam Van chay, Hai Dang Co To, Bai Tam Tinh Yeu, Bai Bien Da Mong Rong, Bai Da Cau My Co To are the places I visited and had a great experience.Regarding hotels there are quite a few hotels but availability is subjected to the season. I was told April till July are peak seasons for local Vietnamese for summer holidays and difficult to find a vacant hotel. I was told it gets so busy during this period, that locals at Co To offer rooms in their homes for rent too. I went at end of August for 4 days. Usually rains are expected at this time but I was lucky to have sunny days. For hotels, try contacting any locals who know about Co To as I booked an average hotel and I am sure there are better hotels which I found out only after arriving at Co To. Some how was not able to find out information about those hotels on popular search engines and travel websites. Getting there - most common route is via Van Don - need to take a speed boat from Van Don to Co To which takes 1.5 hours. To get to Van Don from Hanoi or other places, can take a bus. Lots to write but will address them in individual attractions....All the best ! ! !
extracted_spaces: Bai Da Cau my co to
drawbacks: Difficult to find a vacant hotel during peak seasons (April till July)
Lack of information about hotels on popular search engines and travel websites
practical_tips: Rent a bike and take the roads which are not on google
Contact locals who know about Co To for hotel information

author: Phungnm
title: Very nice island
original_content: Don't go to this island during June - Aug to avoid typhoon. The beachs are very nice with many activities. The price is a bit hgher because everything must be brought from the land.

author: Duc N
title: Pure island with epic views.
original_content: It is a great place for relaxing and having beach activities. Long beach, white sand, clear water. Cotopark is the place to visit with water sports activities, nice beach and very good restaurant. I can also book a beach view bungalow here. Stunning time here.

author: 42Manuela
title: Discover Co To but not for the beaches !
original_content: I stayed in Co To island during 4 days at the end of October (perfect weather). There are many speed boats in the morning from the pier in Cai Rong on Van Don island, every hour till 2 pm at least (ticket costs 180'000 dong). To reach Cai Rong from Halong City (Bai Chay and Hon Gay) take bus nbr 1. From the bus stop in Cai Rong, the pier is one km away. As a foreign tourist you DO NOT need anymore any special permit to visit : right at the pier you'll have to show you passport and they will register you.One would think that Co To island is an ultimate escape from the world : it's not ! It is more developed than Quan Lan, there is a big covered market, few restaurants with fresh fish and seafood (no english menu) and many hotels : in low season (from October) all rooms are virtually empty so you have a huge choice to find a very beautiful room with a/c, wifi and seaview for a bargain price (250'). Internet is working very well. Many people live in Co To but it is still a very quiet place. In these 4 days I was the only tourist !You do not go to Co To for the beaches (there are only two) as these are absolutely disgusting, especially Van Chay, full of rubbish carried by the sea. Walking and discovering the island is pretty nice, distances are around 20 km per day, or you can rent a motorbike. Go up to Hai Dang, a white military fort on top of a hill from where you have nice views. It's very interesting to watch women and children scratch and dig the sand at low tide to find clams.
highlights: beautiful room with a/c, wifi and seaview for a bargain price

author: Minh_Hai_BN
title: Cheap and valuable tour
original_content: When I was a student, I heard about Co To island from Nguyen Tuan a famous writer. In my image, it is heaven beach with blue ocean water. Finally I had opportunity to visit there with my team in this summer. This was really awesome and cheap tour ( 50$ /1 person for 2 days and 1 nights). Boat is the only way to get in Co To. You also have chance to see  Bai Tu Long Bay and Quan Lan Island. From my point of view, Co To is the most valuable place in the North of Vietnam. The environment is wild and the ocean water is very pure, clean and blue. One more attractive thing is fresh seafood. In the morning, fishing men returns from sea with many kinds of fresh seafood. You can buy and ask your motel or hotel to help you cook the lunch.
highlights: pure, clean, and blue ocean water
practical_tips: go early to see fishing men return with fresh seafood

author: Dennisfuna
title: Exciting experience
original_content: I realize that Vietnam owns a large number of stunning islands. In the trip to Quang Ninh province, I explore almost all the destinations here including Halong Bay, Bai Tu Long, Quan Lan  and Co To. There are not so many tourists in Co To; therefore, my friends and I have chances to sit on white sand beach to enjoy vast space, fresh atmosphere and admire beautiful landscape here. In the afternoon, we together hire some bicycles and ride around a small road surounded by lines of trees. Local people call it "con duong tinh yeu". For dinner, we also sit on th beach to enjoy baked food. It's really great feeling!

author: NgocMai
title: Heaven beach
original_content: If u want a peaceful, clean, wide beach Coto island is the best. The water is definitly blue and clarity :3 however the service here isnt developed so there is  few restaurant, hotels, no taxi. No supermarket and find the drugstore is quite difficult. Travelling in island by electric vehicle. The food is a lot and fresh but the people dont know how to cook delicious, just boil, steam and grill. This place is absolutely wide because of its new tourism discovery. There has CoTo Lodge, the small woden room in the beach, quite amazing experience!!

author: Bruandet N
title: Hidden charm in Bai Tu Long bay
original_content: It was our second trip to Halong and Bai Tu Long bay, so we would love to make it differently. We booked a private junk boat with Sails of Indochina, our trip started from Cai Rong, Von Don, a fishing port in northern part of Halong bay. We enjoyed much our cruise in this part of the world because there are no tourists in here and the landscape was breaktaling and pittoresque. Being foreigner, we need to have a special permit to visit Co To island the day after. It was a fun experience

author: milanvagner
title: Foreigners need a special permit
original_content: All foreigners must have a special permit to enter CoTo that is issued by Immigration Office in Quan Ninh City but not in one day.
drawbacks: Foreigners must have a special permit to enter

author: Nga Nguyen
title: One of the must-goes in Vietnam
original_content: The island is one special unit. The journey was exciting from the very beginning as you step on the ship to get to the island. Water was blue all the way and you feel like being in a small Ha Long Bay. On the island, there're several unique places like Cau My beach with magnificant rock layers, Lighthouse (can see the whole island from here) and a mountain peak perfect for sunrise watching. No words can describe how amazing the place is, have a look at my photos. And FYI, free wifi all over the island!!!
practical_tips: free wifi all over the island

author: Cuc B
title: Beautiful island, nice people, we will come back again.
original_content: Beautiful island. People are very friendly, very kind. I love seafood, it is very fresh and delicious. Everything is cheap. We were here 2 days 1 night but we think it is not enough for us to explore this amazing island. should be here at lest 3 days. One thing is amazing, wifi is free all of the island.

author: DeRubi
title: Natural of island.

We slept on Cái rồng harbor 1 night and wakeup in the morning , buy a ticket boat and take 3 hours on the sea go to thế Cô Tô island. When i arrival Cô Tô island, first moment , i was shock. This island really beautiful, natural , blue ocean. Everything good about seafood , friendly local person , beach ... I love that. I hope back soon in next year.

author: AnnaCandy
title: Wonderful island
original_content: We travel to CoTo 3 months ago when the weather is hot.I love everything here: friendly people, beautiful beaches, long and clean beach and fresh seafood with cheap price.In the afternoon, we have a BBQ on the beach. So fantasticAlthough it quite tired to go their, when you stay in Coto, you wil not want to go anywhere

author: Cleo B
title: Nice place and Excellent food
original_content: Co To Island in Quang Ninh Province is probably the most beautiful and romantic beach of Vietnam with blue clean seawater and clean white smooth sand. As a group of 7, we have a great experience there. Before departure, we had prepared a BBQ grill cooker. As soon as landing on the island, we went to the market and chose a lot of fresh seafood as: cuttlefish, many types of oyster, shrimp…On the way back to the hostel, we prepare for a BBQ dinner on the seaside. We should have gone to the market earlier, at around 5- 6 o’clock in the early morning. However, there is no refrigerator in the hostel, so we decided to go to market in the afternoon, at 4-5 PM. Without a doubt, there is not as much seafood as in the morning. In the evening, we set up barbecue at the seaside Nam Hai, one of which is to make a deal for electricity from seaside restaurants with 100.000 VND. The seafood here is much more delicious than any other sea city I have ever been. Cuttlefish, the most appetizing, is so tasty when becoming chewier. The price is quite cheap, about 140.000 – 180.000 VND only for one kilo. For transportation around the island, taking a trip by motorbike with 200.000 VND per day is much more interesting than booking a tour in advance. If you take motorbike taxi “xe om” around the centre of island, it costs only 10.000- 20.000 VND. According to my own experience, I advise you to have a big meal and take some pills before arrival in case of seasick. You should book a room in advance and make a deal in details for eating, staying, fee for picking up and other extra cost to avoid overcharged fee.
drawbacks: there is no refrigerator in the hostel
without a doubt, there is not as much seafood as in the morning
highlights: cuttlefish is so tasty when becoming chewier
practical_tips: go to market early in the morning
make a deal in details for eating, staying, fee for picking up and other extra cost to avoid overcharged fee

author: Huyen Trang Tran
title: Wonderful place for nature lovers
original_content: The word "amazing" is used to describe Co To. Its wild impressed me the most. We hired motorbikes to ride to discover the island. We rode along the path through the moutain and discoverd a very wild beautiful beach. The sand was white and the water was a clear turquoise. It is difficult to find out this color of water in the North. Only our group was there. So great. Besides, riding motorbike up to the mountain to reach the lighthouse and having a great view of the island from it were  exciting experiences. The road’s condition was good but at some turns, the slope was high, we had to stop the engine and pushed up by ourshelves. The lighthouse was not large, we went up the staircase to reach the top. On the top, the green of the forest and fields, the blue of the ocean, the white of the sand, the brown of the soil were in our view. We felt the ocean wind on our faces. At that moment, I felt myself so tiny and lost in the giant nature. Local people were friendly and hospitable. Following local people's instruction, we found out the expand of rock. An imposing scene! Food, especially, seafood was very fresh and cheap. We enjoyed a BBQ beach party with a very good price for 1 person. Beers were free. But local chefs didn't have many receipes and the way spices were used in preparing dishes were not fine. Maybe this was the only one thing I was not satisfied. I love this island.
drawbacks: local chefs didn't have many recipes
the way spices were used in preparing dishes were not fine
highlights: riding motorbike up to the mountain to reach the lighthouse
having a great view of the island from the lighthouse
the friendly and hospitable local people
practical_tips: be prepared for steep slopes on the road to the lighthouse

author: Ineke P
title: Too much noise from visitors
original_content: Interesting museum but the noise of visitors is unbearable. The guides to cover this noise, use microphone and speaker. Which makes you want to run away as soon as possible. Too bad, the museum itself is worth a visit.

author: Patrice G
title: Good but a little busy
original_content: Museum on Quang Ninh Province. Nice effort to have gathered so many pieces and information on various topics related to the province: colonial period, revolution etc. But it is probably too busy, misinformed. He probably lacked expertise in designing the layout of the different rooms

author: RoverP
title: Coal mining and culture
original_content: This is a much better option than sloshing around the islands through polluted water.  This is a modern and welcoming museum.  The top floor is devoted to coal mining which is much more interesting than it sounds.  Much of the commentary is in relation to the need to boost coal production during the war.  It is fascinating to see the language used with the miners referred to as "heroes in the struggle against American imperialism".  The lower floors relate to various cultural aspects of the region.  It is both well laid out and informative.  It was an unexpected treat.
highlights: fascinating to see the language used

author: Cao Son
title: "Must see" in Halong
original_content: Quang Ninh Museum:The unique design, close location to the beach, and beautiful surroundings make this museum a must-visit attraction in Ha Long and Quang Ninh. With an entrance fee of only 40,000 VND, visitors can explore a wide range of invaluable ancient artifacts. The enthusiastic and dedicated tour guides provide in-depth historical and cultural knowledge, making the visit even more enriching. Overall, Quang Ninh Museum is a fantastic destination for tourists looking to learn more about the history and culture of the region.Recommend to visit!!!

author: Steve R
title: Interesting if you're already in the area
original_content: An interesting place to find out about the area and it's industrial, artistic and cultural heritage.  It's a good way to enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours if you have time to spare.
highlights: enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours
practical_tips: good way to enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours

author: Darema D

original_content: The entire museum closes at 12 for one-hour lunch. The ticket is not reusable, and if you arrive around 11am no one will tell that you have one hour to see it. I was disappointed about that, but what I saw in that time was okay. If you have some free time  and seen most of other stuff this is a place to go. I’m giving it 3 as they should mention schedules at the ticket office!
drawbacks: They should mention schedules at the ticket office!

author: Anne S
title: Museum of popular arts and traditions
original_content: Monumental museum on the banks of Halong Bay with very modern architecture. There are a lot of Vietnamese objects there. Moving passage through the galleries reserved for the Vietnam War. Magnificent objects of art and popular traditions.

author: Kate W
title: Okay way to kill some time on a rainy day
original_content: I did not have the greatest expectations about the museum with the reviews I read on Google and they were pretty accurate. It is 3 floors and you can get around the museum in about an hour. It was cheap entry at 40,000 dong per person, but if it was a sunny day and we weren’t escaping the rain I don’t think we would have bothered going
drawbacks: not worth going on a sunny day

author: Paul R
title: A surprisingly good regional museum
original_content: Most international tourists do the bus from Hanoi to cruise and back to Hanoi. Which is a shame as Ha Long city itself is a nice town with several attractions in itselfOne of which is the Bao Tang Quang Ninh (the Museum of Quang Ninh). While the focus is on the local area, many of the exhibits talk of Vietnam and the importance of Quang Ninh to VIetnam history and culture. Some say all the exhibits are labelled in English but the expansive Geology, Zoology and Marine areas are not. Which is a shame as the geology, fauna and flora are definitely strong reasons why many visitors come here in the first place. I also found the marine and botanical sections a little dated with many of the exhibits faded to a ubiquitous white (or brown for the botanicals). But they have really done a good job overall, with many different sections covering the history, archeology, musical, artistic, industrial and warfare contribution this extremely rich province has made to Vietnamese history.The top floor is given over to the coal mining industry and initially this might seems strange. However, not far to the north of Ha Long is Bai Tu, the site of the largest coal seam in Vietnam. It is ironic that the same geology that produced the natural wonder of the Ha Long - Bai Tu coast line has also given us the huge mineral deposits that are now, due to illegal and disastrous mining practices pouring millions of liters of polluted water into that self same bay. The museum is modern, airconditioned, wheel chair friendly. I did two visits - one at 8 am on a Thursday morning where I had the whole place to myself! Utterly fantastic. I visited again the following Sunday and while the hoards of vistors were a distraction, it was a tour guide who insisted on using an amplifier to pontificate to her small group of Vietnamese and whose voice could be heard clearly from all three floors. Hardly what you would expect in a museum where one is bent on studing and appreciating culture. The idiot guide made it seem more like a marketAs others have mentioned, the nearby shoreline is also scenic, with several of the iconic karst pinnacles within meters of the wide, well paved walk way.  Several hundred meters further on is the huge, mushroom like Expo center that looks like an alien spaceship. Free entry but it does not always open at the posted times Well worth a visit!
extracted_spaces: Bao Tang Quang Ninh (the Museum of Quang Ninh
Ha Long - Bai Tu coast line
drawbacks: exhibits are not labelled in English in the expansive Geology, Zoology and Marine areas
exhibits are faded to a ubiquitous white (or brown for the botanicals)
tour guide using an amplifier to pontificate to her small group of Vietnamese

the nearby shoreline is also scenic
the huge, mushroom like Expo center that looks like an alien spaceship
practical_tips: visit early in the morning to avoid crowds
check the opening hours of the Expo center

author: Fred T
title: Top floor is simulated coal mine; other floors are history of area
original_content: This cube looking museum was much better than I expected.  The top floor is a simulated coal mine, along with many displays about coal mining.  The next floor has several rooms, each with different topics.  Not sure what the ground floor had as I ran out of time and the place was mobbed with school children.

author: Adriel Avishai
title: Amazing history
original_content: This was one of the highlights situated near the amazing entertainment centre, this museum told the many histories of Vietnam through excellent exhibits. Thoroughly enjoyable experience.

author: Mortred N
title: A short summary of Quang Ninh and Vietnam's history
original_content: The museum was not very big so it could not show you the most descriptive details in the history of Quang Ninh, but the place was organized with disciplines so it was easy for us to understand the timelines of the area's history. There were also English explanations so international tourists might not need a guide here. The ticket price was very cheap (40,000 VND / adult) compared to what inside the museum so the visit was worth it for us. The scenery outside of the museum was also a nice photography spot.
drawbacks: The museum was not very big
highlights: the place was organized with disciplines
the ticket price was very cheap

author: sarsdow
title: Great to see a little of the history of the area.
original_content: So often you see the real touristy areas, and don’t get to see outside of that.  I’d recommend going here, for an hour or two, to get an idea of the history of the area, and what industries happen in the area (coal mining in this case), rather than just the usual natural history.  Also gives an insight into Vietnamese culture.  It’s about a 15 minute walk from the Vincom shopping centre which is where most taxi’s will drop you, if you don’t mind the walk.  Well worth the visit, you don’t need a guide here.
highlights: get an idea of the history of the area
practical_tips: go for an hour or two
walk from the Vincom shopping centre

author: MinhLQ
title: Maverlous! QuangNinh Museum is the most modern museum in Vietnam you should visit.
original_content: Very nice museum about Vietnamese nature, culture and history! A great translation work has been done so that everything is translated into English and French.
extracted_spaces: Vietnamese nature, culture and history museum
highlights: Everything is translated into English and French

author: Chris M
title: Relaxing and informative
original_content: We visited the museum as part of the half-day city tour with Vietnam Cheap Packages.  Our guide, Mr Khang, picked us up at our hotel and returned us there afterwards, having shown us the city with a long stop at the museum where he proved to be very knowledgeable about Ha Long city and Vietnam in general.  The museum covered all aspects of life in Vietnam, from history to culture, to lifestyle, to fauna.  A very relaxing and informative visit.
practical_tips: book a guided tour with Vietnam Cheap Packages

author: Angie R
title: A fascinating museum
original_content: This is a light airy modern museum that gives a fascinating insight into Vietnam, it’s culture, history, people and animal life.It is on three floors, with both lifts and escalators.There is also a lovely little shop with very reasonably priced momentos, I bought a lovely cashmere pashmina for the equivalent of around 10 pounds.  There is also a little cafe area with nice coffee, cold drinks and ice creams....Well worth a visit....

author: GlobalGypsy_13
title: Prime Location & Look
original_content: This museum has it all -- extensive collections, a super modern building, a café, & a prime location adjacent to the Halong Bay (stunning views) and with an open green plaza on one side, the visual connection with the nearby, modern  Quang Ninh Exhibition of Planning & Expo Center. Plan a morning or afternoon visit as they close for a long mid-day lunch or enjoy the museum café that opens to the plaza or other food stalls along the bay.

drawbacks: They close for a long mid-day lunch
practical_tips: Plan a morning or afternoon visit
enjoy the museum café that opens to the plaza or other food stalls along the bay

author: LincolnlassLincoln
title: Well worth a visit
original_content: This is a very big museum. It is clean and airy with lots of very interesting exhibits. You might need a guide unless you understand written Vietnamese. Ranges from pre history to coal mining and Ho Chi Minh.
drawbacks: You might need a guide unless you understand written Vietnamese
practical_tips: You might need a guide unless you understand written Vietnamese

author: Agi94
title: A gogo museum explaining the local type of living and the mines around the place.
original_content: Interesting museum about local culture and way of living of these people, one of the few places in Vietnam not crowded and therefore plenty of space and time for every body to see well all the goods exposed.

author: Shannon B
title: Best Museum in Vietnam
original_content: This museum is epic! Three gigantic floors full of everything you could possibly ever want to know about Vietnam. A MUST Do if you come to  Halong.
highlights: everything you could possibly ever want to know about Vietnam

author: Derek Y
title: History of Halong Area
original_content: if you like to know the geographical, history and commerce of the Halong Area and also Vietnam, this is an interesting museum to visit. It consists of several floors and also gives the visitor an insight into the coal industry that is one of the major industries of this area.

author: Daniel Norton
title: Excellent tour guide and well presented museum
original_content: We really enjoyed our time at the museum, the collection is well organised on three floors, covering natural history, ancient artefacts, local culture and the wars with the French and Americans. Of course, the highlight is the coal mining exhibit, including a walk through mock-up of a mine!Our tour guide (I think arranged by the museum) was excellent - she was well informed on all the exhibits and spoke excellent English.

author: QUQQQ
title: Good to see if you have time
original_content: Nice to have a look. The walkway from Vincom plaza to the Museum is beautiful with Halong Bay seaview. There is a library nearby, it's in white colour, looks nice with the Museum building in black colour. There's a cafe there too. But the entrance ticket costs 30000VND.
highlights: walkway from Vincom plaza to the Museum is beautiful

author: Chau-Minh P
title: Really cool museum with lots of photo opportunities!
original_content: This museum is cool to walk through. Surprisingly there are a lot of beautiful photo spots here! We came during a weekday so there weren't a lot of people :)

author: Navine C
title: Illuminating for Curious Minds
original_content: A modern, well-resourced, brilliantly-planned, interesting and large installation on Halong bay. This multi-level architectural monolith houses several different themes and demonstrates Vietnamese origin  specific to the region, by displaying archaeological, biological, geological and cultural artefacts. The building is surrounding by thought-provoking sculptures and war artefacts. There is something of interest for everyone, including children, who playfully enjoy larger exhibits of coal-mining, musical instruments and animals ; scores of lively 7-year-olds lit up my second visit to the museum. For the more serious observer, stone and bronze-age, as well as ceramic artefacts depict the history of the area. Television screens and viewing rooms are available in some spaces, providing a much-needed break from being on your feet. The museum is next to the convention centre and with a short walk in the other direction, one gets to a public park and the city centre. The fresh market, also along the bay, provides some interesting (if unknown) foods, which are always worth trying - the "calamari cakes" fried in front of you, are well worth it ... I do not know the Vietnamese name. A modern shopping mall is right next to the market, if that environment is more suitable. This is a useful way to spend the lunch break because the museum closes from 11:30 to 2pm. The museum will appeal to those who are academically inclined, is a good way to spend a few hours to get a feel of the place and can keep children busy for an hour or so. The location is convenient and one could spend half-a-day there and in the surrrounding area. Enjoy it.
practical_tips: try the 'calamari cakes' fried in front of you

author: JewelTours
title: Good to know about Quang Ninh
original_content: The museum will give you an overview of Quang Ninh and Halong bay and Hill Tribe People who live in the region

author: PTP111
title: Old Vietnam
original_content: This museum focuses on the Halong bay area. There are numerous exhibits displaying the indigenous tribes of the area and some of the more modern aspects of the town. I had not realized coal mining was, and remains, such a huge part of life in Halong Bay.
drawbacks: coal mining is a huge part of life in Halong Bay
highlights: exhibits displaying the indigenous tribes of the area

author: Nathan S
title: So cool
original_content: Only 20 minutes from the Halong city, this is such a cool one for me. I was shock of huge coal right in front of museum which is around 2 tons in weight. The sea life and marine fauna display  is great as well. Coming here you know more about Halong history.
highlights: great sea life and marine fauna display

author: Denise L
title: Don't go between 11.30 - 2pm it is closed!!
original_content: We were lucky to get here when it was open as it is closed for 2.5 hours a day for lunch!! Very interesting museum & well laid out. Ground level is natural history oriented, Second level has pots & artefacts dating back a very long time. There was a very, for me, disconcerting American wartime display including clothing of people who were killed on both sides of the conflict. My American friends were a bit surprised to read some of the commentary and see some of the display material. Top floor was interesting with a very good coal mining display plus displays of how families would have lived & this includes on the ground floor some of the boats that are similar to those lived on today.This whole area is being developed with an enormous Sheraton going up close by & in the nearby town a very modern shopping centre next to a very old & rather pungent market!!We walked along the boardwalk from one to the other. Very picturesque with the boats & the Karsts in the background.
drawbacks: some of the commentary and display material was surprising

author: theproudmary
title: Very interesting history lesson
original_content: We attended the museum twice on the same day as we got there the first time at 11am & it closes from 11.30am-1.30pm every day. Adult ticket price 30,000 dong. Ground level is all about flora & fauna of the region with some impressive sized moths & butterflies! 2nd floor has some ancient artefacts dating back 2000BC. Also impressive display of US wartime military artefacts & photos. 3rd floor is predominantly about the coal industry in this region & its history (very detailed displays of coal minors & historical artefacts used for digging etc). Also has a dedicated area to Ho Chi Minh himself which was very well presented. We thoroughly enjoyed both visits & would recommend to anyone.

author: lightupthedarkness
title: some very interesting artifacts in what in a couple of years will be a stunning location
original_content: The building itself is very modern, black glass and you can see several developments in progress next door including a Guggenhiem Bilbao type edifice in stainless steel and right next door a Sheraton hotel. The area will be buzzing in 2018/9 so make sure to tim your visit and not be disappointed

right next door a Sheraton hotel

author: citruscyanide
title: Much potential?
original_content: This museum is formidable on the outside, and has some really good displays, but the information is often lacking. The translations to English all seem to have been run through Google Translate from French - there are often occasional French words in the text. The information is also in large part audiovisual, with subtitles in English also similarly hard to follow. The big display signs are better overall, but even they start to make less sense on the third floor. By all means, come and have a look at the artifacts, but be prepared to be very persistent and patient if you actually want to learn anything useful.I am a museum bunny, and managed to spend 3.5 hours here despite the quality of presentation of the available information, but I suspect most people would be through here in an hour tops. OK for the price, but the museums in Hanoi were far better for the same.What this museum adds: information regarding the geology of the region, the local coal mining industry, and the way of life of the people in Ha Long Bay, particularly regarding fishing. Also some concerning the Vietnam War, and the local flora and fauna.Note also that the museum closes over lunchtime, and is closed on Mondays.

author: Gertjan Hollema... I
title: Biggest museum with modern and unique design!
original_content: The reception at Paradise Suites Hotel had told us there wouldn’t be any boat trips in the bay because of the windy weather, so we decided to book a city trip to Ha Long Highlight Tour for our second day. It was only 4 degrees celsius and had not be that cold since 30 years!After a great breakfast we left for the city centre. First we went to the Quang Ninh Museum, the biggest museum in North Vietnam, with the most modern and unique design. The three floors showed us the history of Vietnam, all species of animals, fish and plants from the area, an exposition of the coal mines and how Vietnamese people had lived in the past and what they were wearing. Our guide told us about their Communist revolutionary leader Ho Chi Minh and the the wars with Japan, China and The United States.After the one and a half hour tour through the Quang Ninh Museum we had coffee at the museum bar, overlooking the first limestone islands of the bay.
highlights: guide told us about their Communist revolutionary leader Ho Chi Minh

go to the Quang Ninh Museum

title: Stunning display and concept

better understanding of the Quang Ninh province's importance to Vietnam

author: Bolt T
title: A Little Known Treasure in Ha Long City!
original_content: When visiting Ha Long everyone, of course, goes to and raves about the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Ha Long Bay! However, if you have an extra day please visit this beautiful and state of the art museum. There are three floors of wonderful exhibits on the natural, cultural and economic history of Quang Ninh Province.  We especially enjoyed the mining exhibit. A beautiful display of sculptures surrounds the museum as well as excellent views of the bay and it's famous land formations. This museum is worth extending your time in the beautiful Ha Long area!
practical_tips: extend your time in the beautiful Ha Long area

author: Ineke P
title: Too much noise from visitors
original_content: Interesting museum but the noise of visitors is unbearable. The guides to cover this noise, use microphone and speaker. Which makes you want to run away as soon as possible. Too bad, the museum itself is worth a visit.
highlights: museum itself is worth a visit

author: Patrice G
title: Good but a little busy
original_content: Museum on Quang Ninh Province. Nice effort to have gathered so many pieces and information on various topics related to the province: colonial period, revolution etc. But it is probably too busy, misinformed. He probably lacked expertise in designing the layout of the different rooms

author: RoverP
title: Coal mining and culture
original_content: This is a much better option than sloshing around the islands through polluted water.  This is a modern and welcoming museum.  The top floor is devoted to coal mining which is much more interesting than it sounds.  Much of the commentary is in relation to the need to boost coal production during the war.  It is fascinating to see the language used with the miners referred to as "heroes in the struggle against American imperialism".  The lower floors relate to various cultural aspects of the region.  It is both well laid out and informative.  It was an unexpected treat.
highlights: fascinating to see the language used

author: Cao Son
title: "Must see" in Halong
original_content: Quang Ninh Museum:The unique design, close location to the beach, and beautiful surroundings make this museum a must-visit attraction in Ha Long and Quang Ninh. With an entrance fee of only 40,000 VND, visitors can explore a wide range of invaluable ancient artifacts. The enthusiastic and dedicated tour guides provide in-depth historical and cultural knowledge, making the visit even more enriching. Overall, Quang Ninh Museum is a fantastic destination for tourists looking to learn more about the history and culture of the region.Recommend to visit!!!

author: Steve R
title: Interesting if you're already in the area
original_content: An interesting place to find out about the area and it's industrial, artistic and cultural heritage.  It's a good way to enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours if you have time to spare.
highlights: enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours
practical_tips: good way to enjoy an air conditioned couple of hours

author: Darema D
title: Good museum but no clear schedule
original_content: The entire museum closes at 12 for one-hour lunch. The ticket is not reusable, and if you arrive around 11am no one will tell that you have one hour to see it. I was disappointed about that, but what I saw in that time was okay. If you have some free time  and seen most of other stuff this is a place to go. I’m giving it 3 as they should mention schedules at the ticket office!

title: Museum of popular arts and traditions
original_content: Monumental museum on the banks of Halong Bay with very modern architecture. There are a lot of Vietnamese objects there. Moving passage through the galleries reserved for the Vietnam War. Magnificent objects of art and popular traditions.

title: Okay way to kill some time on a rainy day

drawbacks: not worth going on a sunny day

author: Paul R
title: A surprisingly good regional museum
original_content: Most international tourists do the bus from Hanoi to cruise and back to Hanoi. Which is a shame as Ha Long city itself is a nice town with several attractions in itselfOne of which is the Bao Tang Quang Ninh (the Museum of Quang Ninh). While the focus is on the local area, many of the exhibits talk of Vietnam and the importance of Quang Ninh to VIetnam history and culture. Some say all the exhibits are labelled in English but the expansive Geology, Zoology and Marine areas are not. Which is a shame as the geology, fauna and flora are definitely strong reasons why many visitors come here in the first place. I also found the marine and botanical sections a little dated with many of the exhibits faded to a ubiquitous white (or brown for the botanicals). But they have really done a good job overall, with many different sections covering the history, archeology, musical, artistic, industrial and warfare contribution this extremely rich province has made to Vietnamese history.The top floor is given over to the coal mining industry and initially this might seems strange. However, not far to the north of Ha Long is Bai Tu, the site of the largest coal seam in Vietnam. It is ironic that the same geology that produced the natural wonder of the Ha Long - Bai Tu coast line has also given us the huge mineral deposits that are now, due to illegal and disastrous mining practices pouring millions of liters of polluted water into that self same bay. The museum is modern, airconditioned, wheel chair friendly. I did two visits - one at 8 am on a Thursday morning where I had the whole place to myself! Utterly fantastic. I visited again the following Sunday and while the hoards of vistors were a distraction, it was a tour guide who insisted on using an amplifier to pontificate to her small group of Vietnamese and whose voice could be heard clearly from all three floors. Hardly what you would expect in a museum where one is bent on studing and appreciating culture. The idiot guide made it seem more like a marketAs others have mentioned, the nearby shoreline is also scenic, with several of the iconic karst pinnacles within meters of the wide, well paved walk way.  Several hundred meters further on is the huge, mushroom like Expo center that looks like an alien spaceship. Free entry but it does not always open at the posted times Well worth a visit!

Ha Long - Bai Tu coast line

title: Top floor is simulated coal mine; other floors are history of area

The next floor has several rooms, each with different topics.  Not sure what the ground floor had as I ran out of time and the place was mobbed with school children.

author: Adriel Avishai
title: Amazing history
original_content: This was one of the highlights situated near the amazing entertainment centre, this museum told the many histories of Vietnam through excellent exhibits. Thoroughly enjoyable experience.

author: Mortred N
title: A short summary of Quang Ninh and Vietnam's history
original_content: The museum was not very big so it could not show you the most descriptive details in the history of Quang Ninh, but the place was organized with disciplines so it was easy for us to understand the timelines of the area's history. There were also English explanations so international tourists might not need a guide here. The ticket price was very cheap (40,000 VND / adult) compared to what inside the museum so the visit was worth it for us. The scenery outside of the museum was also a nice photography spot.

the ticket price was very cheap

author: sarsdow
title: Great to see a little of the history of the area.
original_content: So often you see the real touristy areas, and don’t get to see outside of that.  I’d recommend going here, for an hour or two, to get an idea of the history of the area, and what industries happen in the area (coal mining in this case), rather than just the usual natural history.  Also gives an insight into Vietnamese culture.  It’s about a 15 minute walk from the Vincom shopping centre which is where most taxi’s will drop you, if you don’t mind the walk.  Well worth the visit, you don’t need a guide here.
highlights: get an idea of the history of the area
practical_tips: go for an hour or two
walk from the Vincom shopping centre

title: Maverlous! QuangNinh Museum is the most modern museum in Vietnam you should visit.

author: Chris M
title: Relaxing and informative

Our guide, Mr Khang, picked us up at our hotel and returned us there afterwards, having shown us the city with a long stop at the museum where he proved to be very knowledgeable about Ha Long city and Vietnam in general.  The museum covered all aspects of life in Vietnam, from history to culture, to lifestyle, to fauna.  A very relaxing and informative visit.
practical_tips: book a guided tour with Vietnam Cheap Packages

author: Angie R
title: A fascinating museum
original_content: This is a light airy modern museum that gives a fascinating insight into Vietnam, it’s culture, history, people and animal life.It is on three floors, with both lifts and escalators.There is also a lovely little shop with very reasonably priced momentos, I bought a lovely cashmere pashmina for the equivalent of around 10 pounds.  There is also a little cafe area with nice coffee, cold drinks and ice creams....Well worth a visit....

author: GlobalGypsy_13
title: Prime Location & Look
original_content: This museum has it all -- extensive collections, a super modern building, a café, & a prime location adjacent to the Halong Bay (stunning views) and with an open green plaza on one side, the visual connection with the nearby, modern  Quang Ninh Exhibition of Planning & Expo Center. Plan a morning or afternoon visit as they close for a long mid-day lunch or enjoy the museum café that opens to the plaza or other food stalls along the bay.
